docs.title: Locations and Systems
docs.text: Covers the concept of a FLOWCAL system (with "enterprise" as the default) and how locations are set up so that one or more meters can be added to them.

docs.title: Systems and Enterprise
docs.text:
FLOWCAL has a default system called enterprise. A customer may set up additional systems - for example, a separate system using a different set of units - alongside the default enterprise system.

  • The default FLOWCAL system is called enterprise.
  • Additional systems can be configured, such as one using a different unit set, alongside enterprise.

docs.title: Adding Meters to a Location
docs.text:
A location represents a physical or logical grouping in FLOWCAL, and it is possible for multiple meters to belong to the same location. Meters are added to a location as part of setting it up.

  • A single location can contain multiple meters.
  • Meters are attached to a location during location setup.

docs.title: Meter Fundamentals
docs.text: Explains what a meter represents physically in FLOWCAL, how a FLOCON filter attaches to it to capture raw data, and how meter type and characteristics (such as base pressure and base temperature) affect how flow is calculated.

docs.title: What Is a Meter
docs.text:
In FLOWCAL, everything originates from meter data. A meter is a physical device installed where product is pulled from the ground or transferred through a pipeline, and it measures volume - how much product is moving. A FLOCON filter is attached to the meter and captures the raw data based on the meter's pressure base at the time of measurement.

  • A meter is a physical device that measures product volume as it is pulled from the ground or transferred through a pipeline.
  • A FLOCON filter attaches to the meter and captures raw measurement data.

docs.title: Meter Types and Characteristics
docs.text:
Different meter types - such as Coriolis or turbine - calculate flow differently, so each meter's characteristics must be defined. Two key characteristics are the pressure base and the temperature base: the temperature of the product, the meter's own temperature, and the pressure base together determine how raw data is converted into flow.

  • Meter types include Coriolis and turbine, each with its own calculation method.
  • Pressure base and temperature base are core characteristics assigned to a meter.
  • Both product temperature and meter temperature feed into the flow calculation.

docs.title: Rollup Viewer Basics
docs.text: Introduces the Roll Up Viewer, which shows how a location's meter data aggregates (e.g. minute, super, and monthly) once a location has meters attached.

docs.title: Viewing Rolled-Up Data for a Location
docs.text:
After a location has one or more meters attached, the Roll Up Viewer shows how that location's data rolls up - for example at a minute, super, and monthly level. For a liquid meter/location, the rollup view reflects the liquid-specific data captured for that location.

  • The Roll Up Viewer aggregates a location's meter data at levels such as minute, super, and monthly.
  • Rollup output reflects the type of meter (e.g. liquid) attached to the location.

docs.title: Tickets Overview
docs.text: Explains how a ticket differs from a meter's flowing data and how a new ticket is created for a single point in time.

docs.title: What Is a Ticket
docs.text:
A ticket is similar to a meter in that it belongs to a meter, but where a meter has flowing data captured continuously (for example, each hour), a ticket represents data for a single point in time rather than a periodic record.

  • A meter captures flowing data continuously, e.g. each hour.
  • A ticket represents a single point-in-time record rather than a periodic one.

docs.title: Creating a New Ticket
docs.text:
To create a ticket, click on the meter to see its empty data grid, then choose the option to create a new ticket. Because a ticket is a one-time record rather than a periodic one, the product and applicable temperature (and similar fields) must be selected manually for that entry.

  • New tickets are created from the meter's empty grid via a "create new ticket" option.
  • Ticket entries require manually selecting fields such as product and temperature, since there is no periodic record to draw from.

docs.title: Liquid Meter and Product Setup
docs.text: Walks through creating a liquid meter and its product in FLOWCAL, how product density and units feed the meter, how meter factor and pressure/temperature base default from the product, and the difference between periodic (e.g. hourly) and batch data entry, including the contract hour/day setting.

docs.title: Creating a Liquid Meter
docs.text:
A meter is created either from a shortcut or by going to Setup > Create Meter, where the type is chosen as either a gas meter or a liquid meter. Once the meter is created, its characteristics are set up, after which the Volume Editor can be used to see how flow data is calculated.

  • Meters can be created via a shortcut or through Setup > Create Meter.
  • At creation, a meter is chosen as either a gas meter or a liquid meter.
  • After characteristics are set up, the Volume Editor shows how flow data calculates for that meter.

docs.title: Product Setup and Density
docs.text:
Creating a liquid meter requires selecting or creating its product. A common choice is a Table E product, which prompts for a density value - density does not need to be filled in if not required, but the unit for the product must still be selected.

  • A liquid meter is tied to a product (e.g. a Table E product).
  • Table E products prompt for density, though a value is not always required.
  • The product's unit selection is still required.

docs.title: Meter Factor and Pressure/Temperature Base
docs.text:
Once a product is selected for the meter, FLOWCAL pulls the pressure base and temperature base from the product automatically; any remaining fields must be filled in manually. Meter factor is usually left at its default value of one.

  • Pressure base and temperature base default from the selected product.
  • Meter factor defaults to one in typical setups.

docs.title: Periodic vs Batch Data and Contract Hour
docs.text:
Data entry can be periodic (e.g. hourly, where the grid shows one row per hour) or batch, where liquid data arrives less frequently, such as every two or fifteen days, rather than on a fixed period. A related setting is the contract hour and day, which defines the start of the operating day (for example, starting at 9 o'clock on the first day of the month) - this selection determines how the data grid is displayed.

  • Periodic (e.g. hourly) entry shows one grid row per period.
  • Batch data arrives at irregular intervals (e.g. every two or fifteen days) rather than on a fixed period.
  • Contract hour and day define when the operating day/month starts and control how the data grid displays.

docs.title: FLOWCAL Data Journey Overview
docs.text: A high-level walkthrough of how a new user moves through FLOWCAL end to end: security setup (users and groups), creating a liquid product/meter, building out locations and tickets, validating incoming meter data, resolving exceptions, closing meters, routing changes through PPA approval, manually importing data, and rolling up results into reports.

docs.title: Security: Users and Groups
docs.text:
Access to FLOWCAL is controlled through users and groups. Administrators create groups, each with a different privilege level, and then assign individual users to the group that matches the access they need.

  • Users are created individually and then assigned to one or more groups.
  • Groups are created with distinct privilege levels to control what a user can access or do in FLOWCAL.

docs.title: End-to-End Data Flow
docs.text:
After security is configured, the basic FLOWCAL workflow is: create a liquid product and meter (with a base pressure and base temperature), create the meter's location and tickets, assign characteristics to the meter, receive meter data, and validate whether the incoming data is good. Data that fails validation closes on an exception, which must be resolved. Once data looks good, the meter is closed for the period; any later change to a closed meter (such as an equation change) requires approval through the PPA (post-processing approval) workflow. Data can also be brought in through manual imports, after which results are rolled up and viewed in reports.

  • Liquid product/meter setup requires a base pressure and base temperature.
  • Core setup order: meter -> location -> tickets -> characteristics -> meter data -> validation.
  • Data that fails validation closes on an exception and must be resolved before the meter can be closed.
  • Changes to an already-closed meter (e.g. an equation change) require PPA approval.
  • Manual imports bring data into FLOWCAL outside of automated collection.
  • Rolled-up data is the basis for FLOWCAL reports.

docs.title: Change Password
docs.text:
All users can change their own passwords (this does not apply to FLOWCAL Instant Login users). You will need to log in with your existing password to update this information.

Passwords must conform to the requirements established for your Oracle profile by your database administrator.

To change your password:  1. Go to **Settings**, and select **Change Password**. 2. Enter your old password. Passwords must contain a minimum of three characters. 3. Enter your new password. 4. Enter the password again to confirm the change. 5. Click **OK**. If desired, you can set an expiration time limit for the password, configurable from the [User Access](../Settings%20Manager/Security/User%20Access.md) screen.

If you have forgotten your password or did not change it before the expiration date, an administrator can log in and change the password by going to the User Access screen and clicking the "Edit Password" option.

docs.title: Configure File Imports
docs.text:
The File Import service is a Windows service that must be installed on the application server where FLOWCAL is installed. Depending on operation size (number of meters, locations, hardware specifications), customers may have multiple application servers, each server having the capacity to run one or more import services.

Running multiple import services allows FLOWCAL to distribute the work of importing data across multiple services instead of a single service.

Example If a customer has 60,000 meters, instead of one service processing 60,000 meters on one server, they could run eight services across two servers (four on each server). Running multiple services would divide the workload by eight, so each service is handling no more than 7,500 meters at any time.

Contact Customer Support for recommendations on how many file import services to run for the FLOWCAL installation.

Common Import File Types

Most files imported into FLOWCAL are in Quorum’s proprietary CFX file format. The service can also be used to import meter and quality source text files for gas or liquid meters, as well as other meter file types. Windows does not allow the \\ / : \* ? " \< \> \| characters in import file names. CFX Files A CFX (Common File Exchange) file is a proprietary binary file format used to bring meter flow data and configuration information into FLOWCAL. It is used to import data from a variety of meter manufacturers. SCADA systems generate CFX files using one of the following formats: - **Datetime Stamped CFX File Names within a Folder Structure** - A folder structure must be created with each meter number as a folder name. CFX files are created within each folder with the datetime stamp as the file name, where file name format is “YYMMDDSQ.CFX” or “YYYYMMDDSQ.CFX” where SQ is a sequence number. The sequence number is only used when multiple files are generated for the same day. Note that the year, month, and day in the file name does not have to match the year month and day of data in the CFX file. If a file contains data for an entire month, the "DD" value will be "00". > FLOWCAL will only process 35 days of data, regardless of how many files have been read. - **CFX File Names by Meter Number** - A CFX file with the meter number as the file name does not need meter subfolders. The CFX files can be imported from a main directory and there will be an individual file for each meter. Each time a CFX file is created, it must have the same file name as the previous file created for that meter. > The system creating the CFX files will typically overwrite an existing file when new data comes in. As a result, a process for saving files for audit purposes may be necessary. The FLOWCAL file import service will rename or relocate processed files. - **Combination** - You may see a combination of both methods if you have multiple SCADA systems; some systems may create the folder structure and others may generate files using the meter number (see figure above). This is an acceptable practice as long as files for a given meter are created using the same method every time. See also: [Import Meter Data](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Data.md) TFX Files A TFX (Ticket File Exchange) file is a proprietary binary file format used to import volume and accounting information from run tickets and gauge tickets (such as pipelines, LACTs, trucks, railcars, marine vessels, or tank tickets) into FLOWCAL. Each ticket record in a TFX file is mapped to a FLOWCAL ticket by the ticket ID contained in the record. A folder named “TFXFiles” must be created in the main import directory defined in the FLOWCAL Service Configuration screen. This folder is where the File Import service will import the TFX files from. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\TFXFiles" See also: [Import Ticket Data](../Imports/Import%20Ticket%20Data.md) PFX Files A PFX (Prove Report File Exchange) file is a proprietary binary file format used to import liquid product prover data. The format encompasses prove results, prove run, and pass data, and prover and product identification. PFX files are mapped to a meter by the meter number. The directory for the File Import service to import PFX files from is set on the Liquids tab of the FLOWCAL Service Configuration screen. See also: [Import Prove Data](../Imports/Import%20Prove%20Data.md) Gas Meter Text Files Text files can be used to import gas meter data in the format specified by FLOWCAL (contact Customer Support for the file format). These files can be used to import data for one or more meters. A folder named "MeterTextFiles" must be created in the main import directory. This folder is where the File Import service will import the text files from. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\MeterTextFiles" When importing gas meter data text files by meter import ID, a folder named “MeterTextFilesByImportID” must be created in the main import directory. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\MeterTextFilesByImportID" See also: [Import Meter Text File (Gas)](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Text%20File%20-%20Gas.md) Liquid Meter Text Files Text files can be used to import liquid meter data in the format specified by FLOWCAL (contact Customer Support for the file format). These files can be used to import data for one or more meters. A folder named “LiquidMeterTextFiles” must be created in the main import directory. This folder is where the File Import service will import the text files from. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\LiquidMeterTextFiles" When importing liquid meter data text files by meter import ID, a folder named “LiquidMeterTextFilesByImportID” must be created in the main import directory. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\LiquidMeterTextFilesByImportID" See also: [Import Meter Text File (Liquid)](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Text%20File%20-%20Liquid.md) Liquid Ticket Text Files Text files can be used to import liquid ticket data in the format specified by FLOWCAL (contact Customer Support for the file format). These files can be used to import data for one or more tickets. A folder named “TicketTextFiles” must be created and in the main import directory. This folder is where the File Import service will import the text files from. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\TicketTextFiles" See also: [Import Ticket Data](../Imports/Import%20Ticket%20Data.md) Quality Source Files Text files can be used to import analysis data in the format specified by FLOWCAL (contact Customer Support for the file format). These files can be used to import data for one or more quality sources. A folder named “GQSourceTextFiles” must be created and in the main import directory. This folder is where the File Import service will import the text files from. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\GQSourceTextFiles" When importing analysis data text files by quality source import ID, a folder named “GQSourceTextFilesByImportID” must be created in the main import directory. **Example:** "C:\\FCImport\GQSourceTextFilesByImportID" See also: [Import Source Analysis Text File](../Imports/Import%20Source%20Analysis%20Text%20File.md)

Folder Security

Folder security must be configured to allow the File Import service read/write access to the import directory. To set the folder security on the main import directory: 1. Go to the folder where the import files will be imported from (example: "C:\\FCImport"). 2. Right-click the folder and select **Properties**. 3. Click the **Security** tab and click **Edit**. 4. Select the Windows account used for the service logon (configured on the service in Windows Services console). The account permissions should include all options excluding Special Permissions and Full Control. If the folder is shared, it must also have read and execute permissions. 5. Click **Apply** and close the window.

FLOWCAL Service Configuration

The Service Configuration screen is used to configure the FLOWCAL services installed on the application servers. Before starting the File Import service, a FLOWCAL service account must be configured, which the service will use to log onto the database. Most companies create a user name called "FCSRV" to easily identify the credentials. The administrator defines the network location where FLOWCAL imports files from. Typically, there is a directory specified on the same server where FLOWCAL is installed (Example: "D:\\FCImport"); however, a directory on another server can also be specified. Do not start the File Import service until all setup and configuration is complete. To configure a service account: 1. Right-click the **FLOWCAL.exe** file as select **Run as Administrator**. 2. Log in to FLOWCAL and open the Service Configuration screen from the Settings Manager (**Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Service Configuration**). 3. Click **Edit** and enter your login credentials. 4. Click the **File Imports** tab at the bottom of the screen. Use the **Folder to Check** field to specify the folder to import from. 5. Click **Save**. If the File Import service is currently running, you must restart it for the new settings to take place. When determining the Total FLOWCAL Installations value, consider the number of File Import services installed against the highest number of other services, and enter the highest number of the two. For example: If you are running four File Import services, three Meter Rollup services and one of each of the other services, enter "4". Count each service on all machines collectively, regardless of whether they are on separate servers. This helps maintain efficiency across services that require more resources.

Configuring Meter Imports for CFX

If you are importing meter data using CFX files, each meter must be configured. This can be done manually in the Meter Editor or in bulk using the Bulk Changes screen or the FcLoader utility. To configure meter imports from the Meter Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Editor**. 2. Select a meter. 3. Click the **Imports** tab, and click the **Edit** button. 4. Choose a driver under the **File Options** section. Most users will import CFX files, so most will select the STNDCFX driver. 5. Browse to the import directory to select an import path (folder), or copy and paste the import path. 6. If you are receiving CFX files using datetime stamped file names, select an import file sub-folder. If you are selecting CFX files named by meter name, select a file name. A file path is not required on the Meter Editor for FLOWCAL’s standard text file imports; however, when using an import ID, the import ID must be defined on each meter.

Configuring Meter Imports For Text Files

A file path is not required at the meter level for FLOWCAL’s standard text file imports; however, when using an import ID, this must be defined on the Imports tab of the Meter Editor for each meter. See Common Import File Types.

Configuring Source Quality Imports for Text Files

A file path is not required at the source quality level for FLOWCAL’s standard text file imports; however, when using an import ID, this must be defined on the Main tab of the Quality Source Editor. See Common Import File Types.

Running the File Import Service

Once the File Import service is installed and configured, a Windows administrator can start the service. To run the service: 1. Click the Windows **Start** button. Type “Services” in the find field, and press **Enter**. This launches the Windows Services console. 2. Scroll down the services list to find the File Import service (FcSrvFileImport). 3. Right-click the service name and select **Start**. You can view the status of the service from the [Service Monitor](../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Monitor.md).

Renaming Processed Files

The File Import service scans each subfolder and file in the specified import folder (Ex. C:\\FCImport), and then searches FLOWCAL for a matching path and file name (see Meter Editor \> Imports tab: "Import Path (Folder)" and "Subfolder or Filename") to establish a mapping. If a file is not mapped to a meter within FLOWCAL, it will not be processed. The File Import service utilizes control files to minimize "hanging" instances during which the import of a corrupt file is repeatedly attempted. Once a file or folder is locked for processing, a local control file is created (upon first import attempt) or updated. The control file tracks the attempts made to import the file by recording an informational entry on each attempt. The entry consists of the date and time of the attempt and the service executable that made the attempt. If the configurable number of retries is reached (Settings Manager \> Service Configuration \> File Imports \> Number of retries) and the file has not imported, then no further attempts are made, the file or folder is marked as failed, and the failure is reported via a system message. #### File Extensions Import file extensions will be updated to include the state of the file and the processing date and time. File Status New file extension Example File cannot be mapped to an existing meter within FLOWCAL _U_YYMMDDHHMMSS MyDataFile.cf_U_220501082430 File is successfully imported following any attempt _R_YYMMDDHHMMSS MyDataFile.cf_R_220501082430 File fails to process _F_YYMMDDHHMMSS

MyDataFile.cf_F_220501082430 MyDataFile.ctl_F_220501082430 (control file)

Advanced Configuration & Troubleshooting

FLOWCAL debug options are additional options used for troubleshooting and advanced configuration. For example: You can use the FcDebugOptions.cfg file (located in the FLOWCAL installation directory) to configure the File Import service to import from multiple folders, archive processed files, and more.

docs.title: Configure Report/Export Scheduling
docs.text:
During new implementations or installation in a new environment, you may need to configure the application to enable report and export scheduling. Scheduling provides the ability to create recurring jobs that can email reports/exports to one or more contacts, print to a network printer, or save the report/export files to a network location.

The administrator will need the following account credentials:

  • FLOWCAL services account created specifically for the FLOWCAL services to connect to the database and process data. (See: Create Users)
  • Company email account for emailing from FLOWCAL. This is the email address recipients will see on emails originating from FLOWCAL.
  • Company network account with elevated privileges, which will allow the Reports service to create report/export files at different network locations based on the user’s schedule settings.
To configure the ability to schedule or email: 1. Confirm the FLOWCAL services account is set up within the Service Login section of the Service Configuration screen. (See: [Install & Configure Services](Install%20%26%20Configure%20Services.md)) 2. Confirm the company email account credentials are configured within the Email Information section of the Report Scheduler Configuration. 3. Install the Reports service (FcSrvReports.exe). 4. Within the Microsoft Windows Services console, right-click the reports service and configure the logon to use the designated company network account so that the service can write to the network.

The Report Scheduler Configuration screen is used to set up necessary information for emailing and printing. Failure to properly set up the system will result in reports not being sent correctly. The report service will identify any errors; these error messages will then be available in the Report Scheduler Status screen to help troubleshoot the problems.

Email Information

To configure email: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Report Scheduler** \> **Configuration**. 2. Click the **Edit** button. 3. Enter the SMTP server name. The FLOWCAL reports service uses SMTP rather than MAPI to send emails because MAPI is prone to stalling. The SMTP server name (e.g., smtp.companyname.com) can also be an IP address. The Reports service also supports using SSL/TSL authentication. Check the **Enable SSL/TSL** checkbox and enter the port that is required (usually found through the user's Exchange server). If SMTP does not require this level of authentication, leave the checkbox and **Port** field blank. 4. Enter your username, password and password confirmation. When sending email through the FLOWCAL Reports service, the service will try to connect with the username and password provided. When first entering the username, the password should be specified if there is one. After saving the changes, if you open the screen again, the SMTP server name and username will display, but the password will not. You do not need to re-enter the password. It is not displayed for security reasons, but it is saved. 5. Enter the sender email address (the full email address for the username that will display in outgoing emails). Not doing so may result in an error message regarding an unknown sender. 6. Click **Save**.

Output Printers

When creating report or export schedules to print, FLOWCAL will display the printers that have been defined within Output Printers. To configure printers: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Report Scheduler** \> **Configuration**. 2. Click the **Edit** button. 3. Click **Edit Output Printers**. 4. The printers available for selection will appear on the left. Double-click a printer to add it to the Selected Printers list. Only printers known to the local server will display. If you need to access another printer on the network, the printer must first be installed on the local server. 5. Click **OK**. 6. The printers will now be available from Report Scheduling. The functionality behind the **Print Orientation** button is no longer supported.

docs.title: Configure Transaction Queue Imports
docs.text:
This feature requires the Online Transaction Processing module.

The Transaction Queue service allows FLOWCAL to provide a near-real time interface to SCADA systems and can be used as an alternative to file imports. This service permits a polling system to send information records to FLOWCAL one at a time, diminishing the need to save EFM data within the SCADA system and to write a “formal” CFX file.

Transaction Queue uses a Windows service (FcTrans.exe) and several database tables:

Liquids Gas

FC_TQ_MANAGER

FC_TQ_METER_CONFIG

FC_TQ_METER_EVENT

FC_TQ_METER_ALARM

FC_TQ_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES

FC_TQ_METER_BATCH_REPORT

FC_TQ_TICKET_METER

FC_TQ_TICKET_SCALE

FC_TQ_TICKET_TANK

FC_TRANSACTION_QUEUE

FC_TRANSACTION_SNAPSHOT

SCADA systems, data polling engines, or third-party data collection solutions insert records that represent EFM periodic and batch flow data, source analysis, events, alarms, current configuration, and liquid tickets. The Transaction Queue service reads the records provided by SCADA systems and imports them into FLOWCAL. The data is fully validated and recalculated according to the settings in FLOWCAL.

Database Security

The database security must be configured to allow the SCADA system to write transactions to the Transaction Queue tables.

Transaction Queue Service

The Transaction Queue service is a Windows service that must be installed on the application server where FLOWCAL is installed. Depending on operation size (number of meters, locations, hardware specifications), customers may have multiple application servers, each server having the capacity to run one or more import services. Running multiple import services allows FLOWCAL to distribute the work of importing data across multiple services instead of a single service. Example If a customer has 60,000 meters, instead of one service processing 60,000 meters on one server, they could run eight services across two servers (four on each server). Running multiple services would divide the workload by eight, so each service is handling no more than 7,500 meters at any time. Once the Transaction Queue service is installed and configured, a Windows administrator can start the service. To run service: 1. Click the Windows **Start** button. 2. Type “Services” in the find field, and press **Enter**. This launches the Windows Services console. 3. Scroll down the services list to find the Transaction Queue Service (FCSrvTrans.exe). 4. Right-click the service name and select **Start**. See: [All Services](../Settings%20Manager/Services/All%20Services.md)

Service Configuration

Configure the Transaction Queue service within [Service Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Configuration.md).

Service Monitor

View the current activity on the service using the [Service Monitor](../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Monitor.md).

Transaction Queue Monitor

View the status of each record in the Transaction Queue tables in the [Transaction Queue monitor](../Settings%20Manager/Services/Transaction%20Queue.md).

docs.text: To create a new contact type:  1.  Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2.  Select **Contact Types** in the **Contacts** group. 3.  Click **New**. 4.  Enter a new contact type and click the checkboxes to enable associated devices. 5.  Click **Save**.

docs.title: Associate Contacts to Contact Types
docs.text:

FLOWCAL

These steps assume a meter object is being updated. To associate a contact to a contact type: 1. Open the Meter Editor and select a meter number. 2. Select **Contact Selection** from the **Tools** menu. 3. Select the Contact Type from the list and click **Edit**. Only the contact types enabled for this object type will be available. 4. Select one or more Contacts or Distribution Lists from the Select Contact screen and click **OK**. 5. Click **Save**.

Some devices in TESTit such as Test Reports and Calibration Devices may have Contact Types associated with them. Contact Types can be used to assign these devices to a contact or group of contacts. This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 Integrated. TESTit 3 Integrated is not supported.

Test Reports

Select a device and click **New** to create a new test report. 3. In the Contacts area of the test report, set the contact for each contact type displayed. One or more contacts can be added. 4. Click **Save**. Only the contact types enabled for TESTit will be available.

Calibration Devices

1. From the main screen, go to **Setup** \> **TESTit Manager** \> **Calibration Device**. 2. Select **Contact Relationships** from the **View** menu. 3. In the Contacts area of the screen, set the contact for each contact type displayed. One or more contacts can be added. 4. Click **Save**. Only the contact types enabled for TESTit will be available.

docs.title: Create Security Groups
docs.text:
A FLOWCAL security group is a list of users that receive all the privileges that have been granted to the group. A user ID can be added to multiple groups to provide that user additional privileges.

User access is determined by the privileges specified for the user or their group. If access is granted at either the group or the user level, the selected users will have that access.

Security groups can only be created from the Group Access screen. User IDs must exist before they can be associated to a security group.

To create a security group: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **Groups** within the **Security** group. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter a new unique group ID and grant the applicable privileges. 4. Edit the password; otherwise, the user will log in with the default password and will be prompted to change the password on initial log in. 5. Click **Save**.

docs.title: Create Systems
docs.text:
Systems can only be created from the System Manager. The system creation process typically proceeds as follows:

Administrators must have Application Process - System privileges, granted from the User or Group Access screen, to create, edit, and delete systems.

To create a new system: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **System Manager** within the **Security** group. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter a system name. 4. Enter a system code if needed (this data is optional and is not displayed elsewhere in the application). 5. Grant system access to the appropriate users and/or groups. 6. Assign one or more managers to the system. Each system must have at least one manager. A manager can add or remove user or group system access from the System Manager screen. 7. Click **Save**. The administrator can then grant users and/or groups access to the system from the User or Group Access screen. Meters, locations, source analyses, lists, and other objects can then be assigned to the system. (Each object can only belong to one system.) In the Settings Manager, the System group contains system-specific settings, whereas the Application group contains settings that are application-wide and affect all systems.

Edit Approval Limits

Edit approval limitsThe maximum amount by which volume, energy, gross standard volume, or mass values can be changed through manual edits without requiring approval. Manual edits that exceed this limit will need to be approved before the edits are applied. can be set on a per-system basis. These limits are set in the System Manager screen under the Options tab, or in the System Configuration screen under the PPA and Approval Options tab. After edit limits have been set, if a user tries to save an edit to meter data that is greater than the approval limit set for that system, a message will display informing the user of the exceeded amount, and the edit will have a status of "Pending". The limit applies to the total edit amount for the month. Example An edit approval limit for volume is set at 1000 units. An edit is then made to the volume amount that varies 950 units from the original amount. The variance of 950 is below the 1000-unit limit, so no approval is required. The volume is then edited by an additional 60 units. The total variance of the edits (950 + 60) now exceeds the 1000-unit limit, so the second edit of 60 units will require approval. The edit will need to be approved by a user or group with edit approval limits greater than the system-level limit of 1000 units (defined in System Manager or System Configuration).

docs.title: Define Custom Field Labels
docs.text:
The Custom Fields screen allows an administrator to designate labels for custom fields available in screens throughout the FLOWCAL application, such as the Meter Editor, Source Analysis Editor, and Location Editor. Custom fields are also available for history records, such as flow data (periodic) and source analysis.

Custom fields accommodate data that is specific to a user’s company and that may not be standard in FLOWCAL.

Example In the Meter Editor, many fields on the Custom Fields tab can be edited, as well as other fields available on the General tab. To access the Custom Fields screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Custom Fields** within the **Application** group.

Administrators must have Application Process – FLOWCAL Options privileges, granted from the User or Group Access screen.

Button and Tab Details

The following options are available on the Custom Fields screen: - **Edit** - Enable edit mode and specify field names. - **Save** - Save changes to field names. - **Table** - Create drop-down values for custom field tabs where drop-downs are supported. - **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not save changes. - **Exit** - Exit the Custom Fields screen. Each tab in the Custom Fields screen corresponds to a screen in the FLOWCAL application: Tab Description Audit

Visible from: Tools > Audits > select a meter > double-click audit row > Custom button

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-15 are text fields

Batch Report

Visible from: Open > Volume Editor > Flow Data > Batch tab > Custom Fields sub-tab > Batch section

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-8 are text fields; Custom Fields 9-16 are numeric fields; Custom Fields 17-20 are date fields

GQ Source

Visible from: Setup > Source Analysis > Gas Quality > Main tab; or Setup > Source Analysis > Liquid Quality > Main tab

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-5 are numeric fields; Custom Fields 6-10 are text fields

GQ Source Analysis

Visible from: Setup > Source Analysis > Gas Quality > Source Analysis tab > Custom sub-tab; or Setup > Source Analysis > Liquid Quality > Source Analysis tab > Custom sub-tab

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-6 are numeric fields; Custom Fields 7-11 are text fields

GQ Source Characteristics

Visible from: Setup > Source Analysis > Gas Quality > Characteristic tab > Characteristic 2 sub-tab; or Setup > Source Analysis > Liquid Quality > Characteristic tab > Characteristic 2 sub-tab

Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-5 are numeric fields; Custom Fields 6-10 are text fields

Location

Visible from: Setup > Location > Editor > Tools > Info (includes other similar screens such as Comparison Location Editor, Inventory Editor and Tank Editor)

Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-10 are text fields.

Location Characteristics

Visible from: Setup > Location > Editor > Characteristics tab

Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-30 are text fields

Meter > General Tab

Visible from: Setup > Meter > Editor > General tab

Data format:  Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Field 1 – City; Custom Field 2 – County; Custom Field 3 – State; Custom Field 4 – County

Meter > Custom Fields Tab

Visible from: Setup > Meter > Editor > Custom Fields tab

Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-60 are text fields

Meter Characteristics

Visible from: Open > Volume Editor > Characteristic > Periodic or Daily tab > Custom Fields sub-tab

Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-30 are text fields

Meter Edit Approval

Visible from: Review > Approvals

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-4 are Yes/No (Y/N) fields

Meter Periodic Values

For meter periodic values, the administrator can also define the rollup action to be performed by the Meter Rollup service for the custom fields. If a rollup action is not defined, the Meter Rollup service will roll up the last available value by default. If a meter is configured as a helium meter (Meter Editor > General tab), the Meter Rollups service will always sum Custom Fields 1-5, regardless of the rollup action defined for those fields.

Note

Visible from: Right-clicking in various screens, such as Volume Editor, Exception Resolver, Meter Editor, Location Editor, Source Editor, and selecting Add or View Notes

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-4 are text fields

Ticket Periodic Values

Visible from: Open > Tickets > Ticket Editor > Custom Fields tab; or Open > Tickets > Ticket Search > Custom Fields tab

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-8 are text fields; Custom Fields 9-16 are numeric fields

Create Custom Field Labels

To create a custom field label: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **Custom Fields** within the **Application** group. 2. Select a tab and click **Edit**. 3. Click in the **Field Name** field and enter the label. 4. Click **Save**.

Create Custom Drop-Down Fields

To create a custom drop-down field: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **Custom Fields** within the **Application** group. 2. Select a tab and click **Edit**. 3. Click the **Use Drop-Down?** field to enable the option. 4. While the field name is selected, click **Table**. The associated database table and field name will display in the title bar. 5. Click **New**. 6. Enter the drop-down value in the **User Choice** field. 7. Click **Save**. 8. Repeat steps 5 through 7 for each drop-down value. 9. To edit or delete a drop-down value, select the item from the grid and click **Edit** or **Delete**. 10. Click **Exit** to return to the Custom Fields screen.

docs.title: Create Users
docs.text:
After installing FLOWCAL, one of the first things a company must do is create usernames and define privileges to grant users access to features and functions within the application.

Default User

The default username is "FCADMIN". This user name does not appear in the User Access screen and has no other privileges except to create and maintain security access (users, groups, objects) for other users. The FCADMIN password is initially set when the database is created. Check with your DBA to obtain access to this account. When FLOWCAL is installed for the first time or when a new database is created, the "FCADMIN" profile must be used to create the first new user. While creating the FLOWCAL schema, change the FCADMIN password by modifying the \_createDB.sql script, which is provided as part of the installation package. Otherwise, the FLOWCAL administrator should change this password once FLOWCAL has been installed.

New User

Users can only be created from the User Access screen. To create a new user: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **Users** within the **Security** group. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter a new unique user ID and grant the applicable privileges. 4. Edit the password, if desired. If you do not edit the password, the account will be created with the default password "newuser". You will then be prompted to change this password upon initial log in. 5. Click **Save**.

Administrator Account

Quorum recommends using the FCADMIN account to create the initial administrator account with User Security privileges, then using the administrator account from that point forward to create other users and manage access.

Service Account

All FLOWCAL services require a user account to log on to the database and process data and requests. This account can be any name, but it should be easily identifiable when viewing the audit trail (for example: "FCSRV"). This service account does not require any privileges granted from the User Access screen, but it should be set up without password expiration. The services are configured to use this account by setting the username, password, and database to the service account within the Service Login section of the Service Configuration screen.

docs.title: FLOWCAL Data Condenser
docs.text:
The FLOWCAL Data Condenser utility condenses datetime effective records to help maintain database stability and performance. Occasionally, daily characteristics or analysis records are created even if parameter values did not change. This utility finds all records with matching parameter values and creates one record for the span. The utility can also be used on periodic data when multiple revisions were created but no data was changed.

The FLOWCAL Data Condenser utility should only be used under the direction of product Support staff.

The FC Username and Password should be that of a FLOWCAL user, such as a service account user.

Runtime Options

- **Meter Number and GQ Number** - {Blank} – Do not review any meters/GQ sources. - \[ALL\] – Review every meter/GQ source and condense data if possible. - Specific meter or GQ source numbers can also be specified so that condensing is only performed for the meter/GQ source in question. - **Start Date** - Date of first data to be condensed. - **Do Meter Periodic** - Check this flag if you would like to condense history records (FC_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES) - **Mtr Per Special** ‐ Only use this flag if directed by your Flow‐Cal technical support representative. - **Do Mtr Char** - Check this flag if you would like to condense Meter Characteristic records (FC_METER_CHARACTERISTIC) or Meter Analysis records (FC_METER_ANALYSIS) - **Do Meter Exceptions** - Check this flag if you would like to condense Meter Exceptions. This will only condense duplicate exception (in a case where FLOWCAL incorrectly created duplicates). - **Reverse Alphabetic order** - Check this flag if the \[ALL\] setting is used and you have two utilities running in parallel. This allows the utilities to begin work at opposite ends of the meter/GQ source list. This setting can be used to reduce the time it takes the utility to look at all meter/GQ sources. - **Stop on Errors** - Check this flag to make the utility to stop if an error is encountered; the utility will wait for the user to click OK to acknowledge the error. - **Fix Gaps Overlaps Only** - Check this flag to only fix gaps and overlaps for specified items. This is similar to running the duration fix utility.

Scheduling FLOWCAL Data Condenser

The FLOWCAL Data Condenser utility can be scheduled via Windows Scheduled Tasks. Select the FcDataCondenser.exe file and append ‘CMDLINE’ as the parameter. When the schedule runs, the utility uses the database login specified in FLOWCAL Service Configuration and the runtime options specified in FcDebugOptions.cfg.

FLOWCAL Data Condenser FcDebugOptions

\[FCDATACONDENSER\] condense_meters = Y, N, or blank condense_gq_sources = Y, N, or blank time_frame_type = A - all of time, C - current month, M ‐ months, W - weeks number_of_time_frames = 1 to 120 (weeks or months) condense_meter_periodic = Y, N, or blank meter_periodic_special = Y, N, or blank condense_characteristic = Y, N, or blank condense_analysis = Y, N, or blank condense_meter_exceptions = Y, N, or blank reverse_alphabetical_order = Y, N, or blank fix_gaps_overlaps_only = Y, N, or blank (when set to Y, only gaps and overlaps are fixed)

docs.title: FcDebug Options
docs.text:
FLOWCAL Debug (FcDebug) Options provide additional capabilities for troubleshooting and advanced configuration. Options related to the File Import service are often used for moving or archiving files after being processed. Troubleshooting options are sometimes provided by Customer Support to temporarily enable when investigating issues.

These options are configured in the FcDebugOptions.cfg file in the FLOWCAL installation directory. You can open and modify the file using any text editing tool, such as Notepad.

The CFG file is initially named "FcDebugOptions_Template.cfg". You will need to remove the word "Template" from the file name when configuring options in the file. It is shipped with FLOWCAL with "Template" in the name so that your settings will not be overwritten during an upgrade or re-installation.

docs.title: File Format
docs.text:
Debug options are organized into sections in the FcDebugOptions file. Each section begins with a designated service name, user name, or other generic entries.

Example \[ALL_USERS\] \[JOHN.DOE\] \[FCSRVFILEIMPORT\]  

Section designators must appear on lines by themselves, in square brackets, with the associated parameters listed below it. Each associated parameter has a name and a value separated by an equal sign. The name is specified on the left and the value on the right.

Example \[FCSRVFILEIMPORT.EXE\] FileImportPath = \\server1\C\FCMeterFileImport  

Sections do not have designated end points, but new sections can be started at any point.

docs.title: File Import Options
docs.text:
The FcDebugOptions.cfg file is used to configure various File Import service options, such as importing from multiple directories and archiving processed files. These supported options are listed below.

To create a section in FcDebugOptions.cfg for a file import service to use these options, enter an open bracket, the exact file name of the service, and a closed bracket. Enter the applicable options on the subsequent lines.

Example If you are running two file import services, FcSrvFileImport.exe and FcSrvFileImport2.exe, you can configure options for the first service by entering “\[FcSrvFileImport.exe\]”, and listing the required parameters. You could then configure options for the second service by entering “\[FcSrvFileImport2.exe\]”, and listing the required parameters.

FileImportPath_1

Specify a file path for the file import service to look for files to import other than the path specified on the Service Configuration screen (e.g., \\server1\C\FCMeterFileImport). Example \[FCSRVFILEIMPORT2.EXE\] FileImportPath_1 = \\server1\C\FCMeterFileImport   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

FileImportPath_2

Specify an additional file path for the file import service to look for files to import other than the path specified in the Service Configuration screen (e.g., E:\cfxfiles). Example \[FCSRVFILEIMPORT2.EXE\] FileImportPath_1 = \\server1\C\FCMeterFileImport FileImportPath_2 = E:\cfxfiles   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

Successfully_Processed_File_Action

Specify how to handle processed files. By default, the File Import service will leave the files where they are once they are processed. Other options are: - **A** - Move files to default archive folder (this will automatically create a folder in the file import path called zzzProcessedFiles) - **M** - Move files to specified target folder (see successfully_processed_files_target_folder option) - **D** - Delete the file Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = A   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

Successfully_Processed_Files_Target_Folder

If the option successfully\_ processed\_ file_action = M is used, use this option to define where the files will be moved to once they are successfully processed. If no location is specified, then the default location will be used. Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = M successfully_processed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\processed_files\\   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must not have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

Target_Folder_Plus_Day

This option will create a folder per day (YYYY_MM_DD) in the target folder. Options are: - **Y** - Enabled - **N** - Disabled Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = M successfully_processed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\processed_files\\ target_folder_plus_day = Y/N   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must not have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

Unmapped_File_Action

When a file is unable to import because it is not mapped to a meter, use this option to specify a file extension as an identifier on the file. Options are: - **U** - Change extension to \_U_xxx - **F** - Change extension to \_F_xxx (default behavior for failed files) Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = M successfully_processed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\processed_files\\ target_folder_plus_day = Y/N unmapped_file_action = U  

Unmapped_Files_Target_Folder

When a file is unable to import because it is not mapped to a meter, use this option to specify a folder where the file will be moved to. Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = M successfully_processed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\processed_files\\ target_folder_plus_day = Y/N unmapped_file_action = U unmapped_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\unmapped_files  

Failed_File_Action

Specify how to handle failed files after renaming them. By default, the File Import service will leave the files where they are once they are processed. Other options are: - **A** - Move file to default archive folder (\zFailedFilesArchive) - **M** - Move to specified target folders Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = M successfully_processed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\processed_files\\ target_folder_plus_day = Y/N unmapped_file_action = U unmapped_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\unmapped_files failed_file_action = A   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must not have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

Failed_Files_Target_Folder

If the option failed_file_action = M is used, use this option to specify where failed files will be moved to. If no location is specified, the default location will be used. Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = M successfully_processed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\processed_files\\ target_folder_plus_day = Y/N unmapped_file_action = U unmapped_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\unmapped_files failed_file_action = M failed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\failed_files\\   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must not have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

Process_Single_File_Per_Folder

This option allows the File Import service to independently process each CFX file in a subdirectory. This means that files are not merged into a composite CFX during processing. The results are not representative of a typical folder import; however, the process does mimic the import process that would have occurred had the SCADA system provided the files one-by-one instead of in bulk. Options are: - **Y** - Enabled - **N** - Disabled Example \[FcSrvFileImport.exe\] successfully_processed_file_action = M successfully_processed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\processed_files\\ target_folder_plus_day = Y/N unmapped_file_action = U unmapped_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\unmapped_files failed_file_action = M failed_files_target_folder = \\svr_001\failed_files\\ process_single_file_per_folder = Y/N   To use this option, the designated service name parameter must not have the executable (.exe) extension designator following the service name.

docs.title: Location Rollup Options
docs.text:
To create a section in the FcDebugOptions.cfg file for a location rollup service to use these options, enter an open bracket, the exact file name of the service, followed by a closed bracket. Enter the applicable options on the subsequent lines.

rollup_id_processing_instance

Defines the service instance in which the fc_location_time_frame.rollup_report_id columns are calculated. If the defined service is not running, locations that have been edited and now have NULL fc_location_time_frame.rollup_report_id values will not roll up. The default value is 2 when the service count is 2 or greater.

rollup_child_locations_first

Enables location rollups optimization that rolls up child locations with queue entries before rolling up the current location. The default value is "Y"; set to "N" to disable the option.

rollup_child_location_limit

Sets the maximum number of child location rollups.

max_location_child_rollup_depth

Sets the maximum depth level for child location rollups. Defaults to a depth of 3.

rollup_parent_after_hidden_sublocation

When a hidden sub-location is rolled, its parent real location will be rolled next. If sibling hidden sub-location queue entries exist, they will be rolled before the parent when the rollup_child_locations_first option is enabled. The default value is "Y"; set to N to disable the option.

output_tieover_members

Log calculated canceling tieover time frames to file (default is "N").

show_performance_messages

Display timing messages for the service. When this is "N" (default), only the location being rolled and any error or warning messages will be displayed.

old_tieover_processing_instance

Indicates the location rollups service instance that will perform the legacy tieover handling used to hide canceled tieover and transfer members in FLOWCAL. The default is the service instance count, which is effectively the last service.

docs.title: Miscellaneous Options
docs.text:
password_expire_warning_threshold

Specifies the number of days to receive the warning stating the user’s password is expiring. By default, the number of days is set to 14 from the date of expiration. Example \[ALL_USERS\] PASSWORD_EXPIRE_WARNING_THRESHOLD = 14

docs.title: FcLoader
docs.text:
FcLoader is a standalone utility used for new implementations or new assets. This utility imports tab-delimited files in a proprietary format, allowing you to create different types of data in bulk, such as companies, contacts, locations, meters, and quality sources.

The FcLoader utility can run from a command prompt or batch file. It is shipped with FLOWCAL and is executed from the FLOWCAL install folder.

The FcLoader file format is proprietary and requires a non-disclosure agreement (NDA). Contact Customer Support to obtain this file format.

docs.title: Install & Configure Services
docs.text:
After installing FLOWCAL, the system administrator will need to install the applicable FLOWCAL services. Most services are related to a FLOWCAL module, an add-on, or TESTit Integrated, depending on the software purchased. Only services purchased and the functionality to be utilized should be installed.

Depending on operation size, customers may have one or more application servers, and each server has the capacity to run one or more services. Balancing services across servers and running multiple instances of the same service allows FLOWCAL to divide the work of processing data across multiple servers and services.

Example | Server A - User Access Only | Server B - Services Only | Server C - Services Only | |:--:|:--:|:--:| | \- | FcSrvLcnRollup.exe | FcSrvLcnRollup3.exe | | \- | FcSrvLcnRollup2.exe | FcSrvLcnRollup4.exe | | \- | FcSrvMtrRollup.exe | FcSrvMtrRollup2.exe | | \- | FcSrvImports.exe |   |

Install Services

This FLOWCAL installation folder includes all FLOWCAL services. Most FLOWCAL services can be easily identified because the application file names begin with "FcSrv." FLOWCAL services must be installed manually and do not come pre-installed with the system. At a minimum, the FcSrvMtrRollup.exe service and the FcSrvLcnRollup.exe service must be installed. If the file import service is being utilized to import data files automatically, the FcSrvFileImport.exe service must be installed. If the Source Analysis module has been purchased, the GQTrans.exe service must be installed. The Oracle client must be installed and the FLOWCAL services account must be configured within the Services Login section of the Service Configuration screen before FLOWCAL services are installed and started. To install services: 1. Locate the **\_installServices.bat** file in the FLOWCAL installation folder. This is a Windows batch command script that lists all the services provided by FLOWCAL. 2. Right-click the **\_installServices.bat** file to edit it using Notepad. 3. Each line item begins with "rem" ("remark") which tells Windows to ignore that line item. Remove the remarks indicators from the services to be installed. For example: to install the file import service, delete the "rem" indicator from the "rem FcSrvFileImport.exe /install" line. 4. Save and close the batch command script. 5. Double-click the **\_installServices.bat** batch command script to install the designated services. If the install is successful, a window displays with a "Successfully Installed" indicator for each service. If the install fails, the window displays a "Failed" instead.

Install Multiple Copies of a Service

Most standard services can be installed in multiples to distribute the processing of data across multiple services. To install a copy of a service: 1. Create a copy of the applicable service from the FLOWCAL installation directory. For example: to run a copy of the FcSrvLcnRollup service, copy the service and name the copy FcSrvLcnRollup2. 2. Login to FLOWCAL and set the Total FLOWCAL Installations field within the Service Configuration screen to the maximum number of any given service. For example: If there are two Meter Rollups services installed and three Location Rollups services installed, set this value to 3. 3. By default, the \_installServices.bat script contains only one of each FLOWCAL service. Copy and paste a command line (e.g., “FcSrvLcnRollup.exe /install”) within the script and append the incremental number to service name (e.g., “FcSrvLcnRollup2.exe /install”). The numbering must match the executable name exactly. 4. When all edits are complete, save and close the batch command script. 5. Double-click the **\_installServices.bat** batch command script to install the designated services. Contact Customer Support for a recommendation of how many services to run for the FLOWCAL installation. This will vary per customer depending on variables such as number of meters, locations, and hardware specifications.

Service Security

The Reports and File Import services may require that the service log use a network account with elevated privileges, configured in the Microsoft Services console, if accessing other servers on the network. To configure the log on for the File Import service: 1. Click the Windows Start button, type “Services” in the find field, and press **Enter**. This launches the Services console. 2. Scroll down in the list of services until you find **FcSrvFileImport**. Right-click **FcSrvFileImport** and select **Properties**. 3. Click the **Log On** tab. 1. Select **This Account**. 2. Enter the account name and password, which will be used by the file import service when determining permissions to the network import folder. 3. Click **OK**. 4. Repeat steps 1 through 6 for the Reports service.

Uninstall Services

The FLOWCAL installation folder contains a corresponding "\_uninstallServices.bat" file that is used to uninstall the services. Stop the services and follow the service installation steps; note however that the batch command script contains commands to perform uninstalls for each designated service. When uninstalling copies of any given service, remember to adjust the Total FLOWCAL Installations field within the Service Configuration screen accordingly. You do not have to be an administrator on the server to uninstall services.

docs.title: Transaction Queue Extraction
docs.text:
The TQ Extraction utility allows users to connect to a FLOWCAL database and extract Transaction Queue data in the form of text files containing SQL statements that can then be shared with support staff.

This data can then be used to troubleshoot issues or reproduce and test activities related to transaction processing or the data in question.

## Running TQ Extraction The TQ Extraction utility contains a single self-contained executable (TQRecExtraction.exe). To run the TQ Extraction utility: 1. Copy the executable into the FLOWCAL Installation folder containing the flowcal.exe file. 2. Double-click the **TQRecExtraction.exe** file. 3. Enter a FLOWCAL user name, password and database name. 4. Select the object type (Meter, Source, or Tickets) for which data will be extracted. 5. Select the object number from the drop-down box in the top left corner. 6. Use the **From** and **To** fields to designate a date range. 7. Configure the remaining options as needed: - **All Gas Transactions** – When this is checked, all gas transactions will be extracted and saved as a single SQL file. The From and To dates are still used to limit the time frame. - **All Liquid Transactions** – When this is checked, all liquid transactions will be extracted and saved as a single SQL file. The From and To dates are still used to limit the time frame. - **Unprocessed Records Only** – This option, when selected in conjunction with any of the other extract options, will only allow for the extraction of records that have not been processed. For gas records this means that FC_TRANSACTION_QUEUE.UNAVAILABLE = 0 and for liquid transactions FC_TQ_MANAGER.STATUS = 0. - **Source ID** - The utility will extract all transactions with a specific source ID and ignore the object number. - Upon completion of the extraction, the utility will create the following SQL text files: - For meter data, there will be two files with the following naming format: \_TQ_Recs_Meter\_\.sql \_TQ_Snapshot_Recs_Meter\_\.sql - For quality source data, there will be a single file with the following naming format: \_TQ_Recs_GQ\_\.sql These SQL files can then be shared with support staff, along with FcDabaBoss transfers for the purposes mentioned above.

Export Meter Transactions

To export meter transactions, the ‘Meter’ radio button must be selected. The drop-down list will be populated with all available gas and liquid meter numbers. This does not take into account a user’s security permissions. A meter may be selected from the list or a source id may be provided in the ‘Source ID’ text box. The ‘From’ and ‘To’ date may be adjusted to fit the time span of the data that is being extracted. Populating Source ID will override the meter number selection from the drop-down. The Source ID is used if there is a source ID to be extracted that does not match a meter number in the database. This would be the case if auto creating a meter or if importing by Source ID rather than meter number. When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.

Export Source Transactions

To export source analyses transactions, the ‘Source’ radio button must be selected. The drop-down list will be populated with all available gas and liquid quality source numbers. This does not take into account a user’s security permissions. A source may be selected from the list or a source id may be provided in the ‘Source ID’ text box. The ‘From’ and ‘To’ date may be adjusted to fit the time span of the data that is being extracted. Populating Source ID will override the quality source number selection from the drop-down. The Source ID is used if there is a source ID to be extracted that does not match a quality source number in the database. This would be the case if auto creating a quality source or if importing by Source ID rather than source number. When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.

Export Ticket Transactions

To export Ticket transactions, the ‘Tickets’ radio button must be selected. The drop-down list will be populated will all available locations that can have a ticket attached to it. Comparison locations, for example, will not be in the drop-down. A location may be selected from the drop-down or a source id for the specific ticket may be provided in the ‘Source ID’ text box. The ‘From’ and ‘To’ date may be adjusted to fit the time span of the data that is being extracted. When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.

Export Standalone Tickets and Sample Analyses

Standalone Tickets and Sample Analysis records exist independently of any quality source or location. To extract these transactions, the user needs to enter the specific source id into the ‘Source ID” field in the extraction tool and select the appropriate date range. When the tool is run, messages will populate the application window that show the number of transactions that are being extracted. Those extracted transactions are formatted into insert statements and saved as a SQL file in the same location as the TQ Extraction Tool.
