docs.title: Auto Edits Editor
docs.text:
The Auto Edits Editor allows you to specify automatic edits that can be applied to applicable data on one or more meters. This is especially useful if you have data imported or entered every month for which you know you have to change specific detail(s), characteristic(s), or analysis.

Auto edits apply to all applicable data, regardless of the status of the record; that is, if the data is closed, an auto edit still applies if the data meets the condition of the auto edit and a PPA is also created. Auto edits do not apply to meter data that is created or edited from the Auto Estimate service or Master Allocations.

To set up an auto edit: Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Auto Edits Editor**. When Auto Edit criteria are defined on more than one tab, the Auto Edits are applied in the following order: - Auto edits defined on tabs that do not trigger a recalculation - Auto edits defined on tabs that trigger a recalculation of the correlation factors applicable to that meter; correlation factors are then recalculated - Auto edits defined on tabs that trigger a recalculation of volume and mass; volume and mass are then recalculated

docs.title: Gas Auto Edits
docs.text:
Upon import of meter data, FLOWCAL attempts to apply the Auto Edit to each periodic record that is imported. On edits, FLOWCAL attempts to apply the Auto Edit to each periodic record that is within the Contract Month of the data that is modified.

For meter characteristic Auto Edits, the Auto Edit only applies to characteristic records within the Contract Month. Additionally, Auto Edits are not applied to time frames where no periodic records exist. Meter Characteristic records are split by the Auto Edit process as needed.

Requires the FLOWCAL Gas module.

docs.title: Liquid Auto Edits
docs.text:
On import of meter data, FLOWCAL attempts to apply the Auto Edit to each periodic record that is imported. On edits, FLOWCAL attempts to apply the Auto Edit to each periodic record that is specifically modified by the user.

For meter characteristic Auto Edits, the Auto Edit only applies to characteristic records within the Contract Month that are tied to a periodic record that is imported or specifically modified by the user. Additionally, Auto Edits are not applied to time frames where no periodic records exist. Meter Characteristic records are split by the Auto Edit process as needed and an exception will be generated to alert the user. If the Product is changed from an Auto Edit, then the batch is split at the effective date of the characteristic record affected before calculations take place.

If the FLOWCAL Option ‘Reconcile Volume’ is enabled, the Auto Edit Editor menu item is disabled and any Auto Edit that attempts to be processed is skipped.

For liquid meter periodic data, the user has the ability to set a data point to a numerical value or to choose from a list of data points to copy the value from. For example, if Gross Standard Volume (GSV) > 0, then set Meter Temperature = Observed Temperature. To set a data point to a numerical value, choose the Action ‘New Value’ so that a numerical value can be provided.

Requires the FLOWCAL Liquids module.

docs.title: Auto Edit Editor Tabs
docs.text:
The tab that the Auto Edit criteria are defined on determines the type of recalculation that occurs after the Auto Edit is applied. If an Auto Edit is defined on the ‘Vol. and Mass’ (Liquids) or ‘Volume’ (Gas) tab, then that Auto Edit triggers FLOWCAL to perform a recalculation of Volume and Mass. If an Auto Edit is defined on the ‘CF’ (Liquids) or ‘VCF’ (Gas) tab. then that Auto Edit triggers FLOWCAL to perform a recalculation of all Correlation Factors applicable to that meter. If an auto edit is defined on the ‘Operations’, ‘Other’, or ‘Customer and Other Fields’ tab, then no recalculation occurs.

Periodic

Use this tab to set conditions that the meter periodic data must meet in order for the specified action to apply. Gas Meters #### Condition & Action Values - Diff. Press. - Stat. Press. - Temp - C-Prime - Ext - Flow Hour - Volume - Mass - Energy - Pulses - Corr. Factor - Raw Volume - Liquid Meters #### Action Operators = Configure an Auto Edit to set the current value exactly equal to a constant. +/-

Configure an Auto Edit to add or subtract a constant from the current value.

To add, a positive constant must be provided. To subtract, a negative constant must be provided. If the data point configured to be added or subtracted by a constant is not provided on import, then FLOWCAL assumes 0 for the data point.

For example: If an Auto Edit is configured to set Volume = Volume + 1000, but Volume is not provided on import, then Volume is set to 1000 = 0+1000.

Certain values that would not logically go below zero such as differential pressure and pressure will only be set to 0 if subtracting the specified amount will take it below zero. For instance: If an auto edit is to subtract 10 from the pressure, but the pressure is 9, the pressure will be set to 0.

This operator will only be applied to imported data.

*

Configure an Auto Edit to multiply the current value by a constant. If the data point configured to be multiplied by a constant is not provided on import, then FLOWCAL assumes 1 for the data point. For example, if an Auto Edit is configured to set Volume = Volume * 1000, but Volume is not provided on import, then Volume is set to 1000 = 1*1000.

This operator will only be applied to imported data.

/ Configure an Auto Edit to divide the current value by a constant. If the data point configured to be divided by a constant is not provided on import, then the division will not occur. This operator will only be applied to imported data. /VCF Configure an Auto Edit to divide the Volume by the Correlation Factor (/VCF) in order to set the data to what FLOWCAL calculates for the Volume. Only available if the specified value is Volume. Liquid Meters #### Condition Values - Unc. Density - Obs. Density - Obs. Temperature - Obs. Pressure - Obs. EVP - Meter Temp. - Meter Press. - EVP - Pulses - Diss. Press. - Flow Time - Base Density - Meter Density - CTPL - CTL - CPL - CCF - CSW - Mass - IV - GSV - NSV - Summed Vol. - Net Allow. - S&W% - SWV - Theo. Prod. #### Action Values - Unc. Density - Obs. Density - Obs. Temperature - Obs. Pressure - Obs. EVP - Meter Temp. - Meter Press. - EVP - Pulses - Diff. Press. - Flow Time - Mass - IV - GSV - NSV - Summed Vol. - Net Allow. - SWV - CF = 1 This option is only available from the left Action drop down on the Vol. and Mass sub tab. When selected, if the conditional criteria for this row are met, all CF values for a given record are set to 1. - New Value This option is only available from the right Action drop down. When this option is selected, the text box to the right of the drop down will become enabled so that the user may input a numerical value. #### Action Operators | | | |:--:|----| | = | Configure an Auto Edit to set the current value exactly equal to a constant or data point. | | +/- | Configure an Auto Edit to add or subtract a constant or data point from the current value. This operator will only be applied to imported data. | | \* | Configure an Auto Edit to multiply the current value by a constant or data point. This operator will only be applied to imported data. | | / | Configure an Auto Edit to divide the current value by a constant or data point. This operator will only be applied to imported data. | For Action Operators other than "=", if a data point that is configured to be manipulated by an Auto Edit is not available on import, then the Auto Edit is not applied. For example: If an Auto Edit is configured to set Mass = Mass \* 1000 but Mass is not provided on import, then the Auto Edit is not applied.

Characteristics

Use this tab to change information such as orifice diameter, plate size, meter factor, temperature base, units.

Analysis

Use this tab to change information regarding composition values such as carbon dioxide, nitrogen, helium, specific gravity, etc. This is only available for auto edits with a gas fluid phase.

docs.title: Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Compliance
docs.text:
FLOWCAL includes several features available to help operators meet the requirements of 43 CFR §§ 3170, 3173, 3174 and 3175—the replacement rules for BLM Orders 3, 4 and 5.

BLM Tab

Each editor in FLOWCAL contains a BLM tab to capture data for meters, locations, tanks and caverns that are under BLM jurisdiction. To designate an item as a BLM property, click the BLM tab and select "Yes" from the BLM Property drop-down. Several regulatory identification fields on the BLM tab become active when the meter or location is designated as a BLM property. These include Facility Measurement Point (FMP) Number, Lease Number, and CA and PA Numbers. You can also set the BLM Property designation and other BLM-specific fields using FcLoader. The following meter reports include the BLM identification fields: - [BLM GVS](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/BLM%20Reports.md#BLM) - [Meter Sample and Analysis](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#MeterSampleAnalysis) - [Meter Edit Reasons](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#MeterEditReasons) - [Meter Characteristic](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#MeterCharacteristics) - [Meter Alarm Detail](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#MeterAlarmDetail) - [Meter Events](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#MeterEvents)

FMP Tier

The daily average flow for a facility measurement point (FMP) determines the required frequency for inspection and permissible measurement uncertainty, and influences several other applicable practices. Each FMP is assigned to a volume tier based on the daily average flow calculated from the previous 12 months of data. The FMP tier is calculated in FLOWCAL as part of the close process. You can also initiate the calculation from the [Toolbox](../Tools/Toolbox/Toolbox.md). An override is also available so that you can manually set the tier when a BLM variance has been granted. FMP Tier calculations are displayed on the [BLM tab](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/BLM%20Tab.md) of the Meter Editor. For additional details about the calculation process, see: [FMP Tier Calculation](FMP%20Tier%20Calculation.md). The [BLM FMP Tier report](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/BLM%20Reports.md#BLM2) compiles a list of all designated BLM properties.

Meter Sample and Analysis Report

Several fields have been added to the gas quality sample and analysis details, including spot sample method, install and removal dates of a composite sample, and lab analyzer make, model and last calibration date. All fields may be imported to a gas quality source and are reported in the [Meter Sample and Analysis report](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#MeterSampleAnalysis).

Gas Quality Validations

Several gas quality validations have been added in accordance with the new rules. Missing components, an incorrect C6+ split definition, and past due C6+ characterizations are all validated and will generate meter exceptions if violated. FLOWCAL will report the C6+ characterization age before the past due date. Exceptions will be generated after 135 days (instead of six months) for a very high volume meter and after 255 days (instead of one year) for a high volume meter.

Heating Value Uncertainty

BLM regulations require that measured heating value must have an annual average uncertainty of 1% or less for very high volume meters and 2% or less for high volume meters. FLOWCAL calculates heating value uncertainty when a source analysis is applied to a BLM gas meter, and generates exceptions if the uncertainty is not within range. The calculated heating value uncertainty is visible on the Meter Analysis detail within the Volume Editor. FLOWCAL provides two heating value uncertainty reports: - **[Heating Value Uncertainty](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/BLM%20Reports.md#Heating)** - Reports heating value, uncertainty and FMP tier for all meters in a list, highlighting FMPs that are out of tolerance - **[Heating Value Uncertainty Exceptions](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/BLM%20Reports.md#Heating2)** - Reports only FMPs that are out of tolerance #### See also: [Heating Value Uncertainty Details](Heating%20Value%20Uncertainty%20Details.md)

BLM Audit Package

FLOWCAL provides BLM Audit Package report group to assist in providing information required to satisfy BLM audit requirements. The BLM Audit Package report group includes the following reports: - BLM Audit Package Cover Page - BLM Gas Volume Statement - Daily - Meter Characteristic - Meter Events - Meter Sample and Analysis #### See also: [BLM Reports](../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/BLM%20Reports.md)

docs.title: FMP Tier Calculation
docs.text:
This feature requires the Monthly Close Functions and Service module.

The FMP tier is determined by evaluating the daily average volume for an averaging period. "Averaging period" is defined by the BLM (43 CFR, subpart 3170.3) as the previous 12 months or the life of the meter, whichever is shorter.

For FMPs that measure production from a newly drilled well, the averaging period excludes any production from that well that occurred in or before the first full month of production.

Example  If an FMP was installed to measure the production from a new well that first produced on April 10, the averaging period for that FMP would not include the production that occurred in April (partial month) and May (full month) of that year.

FLOWCAL interprets "previous" as "closed". As a result, when the calculation runs, FLOWCAL starts with the most recent closed month. Within the averaging period, FLOWCAL will also:

  • Exclude time frames for which the meter status is "Inactive" or "Disconnected". The averaging period is not extended to "make up" for these time frames.
  • Include zero flow days where the meter status is "Active".

First Flow Date: 1/1/2017

Per BLM rules, 1/2017 and 2/2017 are not used in the averaging period.

Scenario Expected Results

Run on 2/15/2018

Closed for January

The calculation will use the months 3/2017 through 1/2018, a total of 10 months.

Run on 4/15/2018

Closed for March

The calculation will use the months 4/2017 through 3/2018, a total of 12 months.

Run on 4/15/2018

Closed for March

Zero Flow for month of June

The calculation will use the months 4/2017 through 3/2018, a total of 12 months.

Run on 4/15/2018

Closed for March

Inactive for month of June

The calculation will use the months 4/2017, 5/2017, and 7/2017 through 3/2018, a total of 11 months.

Note that the inactive period does not need be on a month boundary as used in this example. It is the days that are inactive that are excluded.

The First Flow field on the Misc. tab of the Meter Editor is used to calculate the Calculated Tier when a meter started flowing within the last 12 months.

BLM regulations prescribe that heating value uncertainty must be within +/- 2% for a high volume FMP and within +/- 1% for a very high volume FMP. FLOWCAL performs this calculation for BLM properties as part of the source apply process and generates an exception if the uncertainty is not within range. If the calculation is unsuccessful, an error exception will be written. (See: Exceptions 9021 - 9024)

docs.title: Business Month Editor
docs.text:
The Current Business Month is usually defined as the open production month currently being processed. The business month is used in areas of such as PPAs. This business month concept also allows users to explicitly set the current business month for a given system within the application. By explicitly setting a business month, there could be one or more open production months, but the user has control over which month is the current business month. In addition, some data has the current business month recorded as part of the audit trail.

Each FLOWCAL system is set to use an explicit business month. For liquid meters, Tickets now have an explicitly recorded Business Month as part of the audit trail. Tickets that belong to a Location use the Location's System to establish the Business Month. Standalone tickets or tickets that do not belong to a Location do not have a Business Month.

To access the Business Month Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **Business Month**. An application administrator must initially set the current business month. After the initial setup, any user with Meter Close privileges can set the business month. Once set, the business month may only be incremented by one month, every ten days.

Business Month Editor Screen Details

The following items are available on the Business Month Editor: - **Use the First Open Month** - Use the first open month as the Current Business Month. - **Use the Business Month** - Use the specified business month as the Current Business Month.

The following items are available on the Calculated Meter menu:

  • New - Create a new meter.

A fluid phase of liquid is only available with the FLOWCAL Liquids module.

  • Edit - Enable edit mode.

  • Delete - Delete the selected meter. Calculated meters can only be deleted from the Calculated Meter Editor.

  • Security - View or edit users that have access to the calculated meter.

User/group access to calculated meters is only relevant for companies that maintain object level security. Most companies do not restrict access at the object level.

  • Exit - Exit the screen.

docs.title: Calculated Meter Editor
docs.text:
Currently, FLOWCAL only supports gas calculated meters.

A calculated meter (also called a virtual or pseudo meter) is a meter that does not physically exist but is calculated from known meter values. The total volume, mass and energy for a calculated meter are determined based on meter member contributions during the period in which they were added. You can also set up a conditional statement with basic arithmetic operations and absolute values to specify member contributions.

A calculated meter may also be used to determine how much analysis component volume is lost in a balanced system. This application is important because the amount of certain gases emitted into the environment must be documented and submitted to the government.

Example Texas is a segment location within a system, comprising many meters. You want to know the volume entering Harris County where a physical meter does not exist. You can calculate that volume using upstream meters as data points (a calculated meter). To access the Calculated Meter Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Calculated Meter**.

Calculated Meter Editor Details

The following items are available in the Calculated Meter Editor screen: - **Calc Meter/Name** - Calculated meter number and name - **System** - FLOWCAL System the calculated meter is associated with - **Unknown Volume** - A user may find that the sign on an unknown value, once calculated, is negative. To correct this, FLOWCAL has created an option called Unknown Volume, which simply changes the sign of the result of the unknown volume equation. While a value yielded from an unknown volume calculation may be accurate as a negative number, some accounting departments require that figures be entered with positive numbers and identify whether the value is inlet or outlet via the configuration. - **Fix PPAs** - Every PPA record written (table fc_ppa_accounting_info) for a meter is also written for any parent calculated meters. Before the ability to purge PPAs was introduced, this was often done with SQL scripts. At times the calculated meter was overlooked. This button does a force delete and re-copy of the calculated meter’s PPA from its members when backing out PPAs for member meters. This feature is usually only requested by FLOWCAL Support. - **Reference Meter** - Used to ensure common pressure base, temperature base, contract hour and contract day for all meters in a calculated meter. The reference meter is dependent on the From/To Date values and can change for each relationship time frame. - **From/To** - Start and end datetime, which represents each time frame the members have been included within the calculated meter. In the To field, the maximum date can be entered by pressing **Ctrl+E** and the minimum date in the From field can be entered by pressing **Ctrl+S**. The end date must be greater than the start date. - **Formulas** - Read-only field that displays whether the formula is enabled for the current datetime span. (See: [Formulas tab](Formulas%20Tab.md)) - **Find** - Open the find tool to search members of a calculated meter - **Refresh** - Refresh the screen - **Security** - View or edit users that have access to the calculated meter. User/group access to calculated meters is only relevant for companies that maintain object level security. Most companies do not restrict access at the object level. - **Delete** - Delete a calculated meter. - **Edit** - Enable edit mode for the calculated meter. - **New** - Create a new calculated meter. When you click the **New** button, the fluid phase is set to the user-defined default fluid phase configured within User Preferences. To set the fluid phase manually, click the drop-down on the **New** button and select "Gas" or "Liquid". - **Exit** - Close Calculated Meter Editor. - **Query** - Open the Query Editor to populate the Calculated Meter based on a query. To add members based on a query, run the query from the Query Editor and select the members from the list of query results by clicking the right arrow button. - **Save** - Save your changes. - **Cancel** - Discard your changes.

docs.title: Custom Fields Tab

The Custom Fields tab has 60 user-definable fields that can be used to add the user's company specific information about a meter such as Division or Field Technician. All fields listed are custom definable, meaning the labels are user-defined and the edit fields can be converted to drop-downs with a defined list of options.

Custom field labels and drop-down options are managed from the Custom Fields screen within the Settings Manager and requires the FLOWCAL Options privilege.

docs.title: Formulas Tab
docs.text:
The Formulas tab is used to configure two calculated meter rollups functions: The averaging pool and conditional formulas.

Averaging Pool

**Calculate average of members with base direction of** - Include or exclude member values from average calculations based on their base directions. When calculating the average values of the calculated meter, the Calculated Meter Rollups service will only include members with the selected base direction. By default, both Inlet and Outlet are checked. This option is not datetime effective; it is effective for all of time.

Formulas

In the Formulas section of this screen, you can customize how to calculate quantities such as volume, energy, and mass that are usually summed from member values. You can specify a condition under which the customized calculation is to take place using a simple if-then-else format. Formula configuration is effective only for the datetime span specified by the From and To dates. From and To dates can only be deleted from the Relationship tab.

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Formulas tab of the Calculated Meter Editor: - **Enable Formulas** – Click this checkbox to enable the formulas functionality for the current datetime span so that the Calculated Meter Rollup service uses the specified expression when calculating summed values for the calculated meter. Expressions may be edited and saved for a datetime span that has formulas disabled. Calculated meter data will be rolled up normally during a datetime span that has formulas disabled even if there is an expression stored for the span. - **Edit ** – Click this button to access the edit form for each If, Do, and Else Do statement. This button is enabled when you are in edit mode. (For additional details, see: [Formula Statement Editors](Formulas/Formula%20Statement%20Editors.md)) The statement edit button only provides access to the Statement Editor. Use the screen Edit button to put the Calculated Meters screen in edit mode. - **Validate** – Click this button to validate the formulas. The formulas must pass validation to be saved. If the validation fails, a message displays with a list of errors that need to be corrected. (For additional details, see: [Formula Validation and Error Messages](Formulas/Validation%20and%20Error%20Messages.md))

docs.title: General Tab
docs.text:
The General tab shows basic information about the meter, such as where it is located and what Close Group it belongs to. The fields that are shaded in gray such as Meter Type and Meter Direction are read-only and are retrieved from the meter’s characteristics. These read-only fields are editable in the Volume Editor.

The following items are available on the General tab of the Calculated Meter Editor:

  • Meter Type - Read-only field that displays the type of meter, which is a Calculated Meter.

  • Alt. Meter Number - Informational field used to document an alternate meter number. This typically references a third party or contract meter number.

  • Meter Direction - Read-only field that displays whether a meter is classified as Inlet, Outlet, Throughput, Balance Check, Transfer, Tieover, or Off System for balancing purposes. This value is retrieved from the meter’s characteristics and can be edited from the Volume Editor.

  • Customer - The customer the meter belongs to.

  • Cust. Meter Number - Informational field used to document the customer's meter number.

  • Check Meter Exists - Specifies whether an existing check meter is associated to the meter; commonly used if data from another meter is being measured at the same measurement point.

  • Helium Meter - Designates whether a meter is a helium meter. This option would be set to “Yes” for the member meters within the Meter Editor. Helium is calculated at the member meter level. However, the user could set this option “Yes” in order to run the Helium reports for a calculated meter.

  • Close Groups - Close Groups only appear if the close schedule type is set to Close Group in the FLOWCAL Configuration screen.

  • Fluid Phase - Defines the meter phase conditions as gas or liquid. The fluid phase is defined on meter creation and cannot be changed once the meter is created.

  • Meter Status - Indicates whether the meter is active; pulled from meter’s characteristics and applicable to the current system time.

  • Business Status - This status is not datetime effective and can be updated manually via the Calculated Meter Editor. This status overrides the Meter Status.

Meters that have any Business Status other than "On" are treated as out of service and will not be included when running reports for a list.

  • System - Informational field that indicates which system the meter is assigned to, typically set during meter creation.

  • Notes - Additional notes about the meter; up to 320 characters.

The notes stored on the General tab are only available from the Calculated Meter Editor. For notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., Volume Editor), right-click on the Calculated Meter Editor screen to add or view notes.

  • City - City the meter is in; up to 50 characters.

  • County - County the meter is in; up to 20 characters. Options are defined in the County Editor.

  • State - State the meter is in; up to 50 characters. Options are defined in the State Editor.

  • Country - Country the meter is in; up to 50 characters. Options are defined in the Country Editor.

  • Time Zone - Time zone the meter is in; up to 80 characters. Options are defined in the Time Zone Editor.

  • Quarter - Each section is divided into quarter sections, which are each further divided into quarter sections, for a total of 16 parts per section; up to 25 characters. Example "NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4" refers to the northwestern-most quarter of the southeastern quarter.

  • Section - The basic unit of a township and range; each section refers to an area of a square mile; up to three characters.

  • Township - A measure of the distance north or south from the baseline, six miles in length; up to four characters.

  • Range - A measure of the distance east or west from the principal meridian, six miles in length; up to four characters.

  • Meridian - A geographical north to south reference point; up to 25 characters.

  • Latitude - A geographic coordinate specifying a north-south location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Equator; up to 12 characters.

  • Longitude - A geographic coordinate specifying an east-west location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Prime Meridian; up to 12 characters.

docs.title: Integration Tab
docs.text:
The Integration tab contains data points required for linking a meter with the Quorum ecosystem via the Quorum Enterprise Integration (QEI) platform.

You can use the FcLoader utility to import the following values in bulk:

  • Integrated
  • Facility (code)
  • Integration ID

Data Field Details

- **Integrated** - When set to "Yes", the meter is designated as being integrated or linked to the Quorum ecosystem. Data is expected to flow from FLOWCAL automatically and transparently to other Quorum integrated applications. An example of this integration is data flowing from FLOWCAL to TIPS. When set to "Yes", the following data will be automatically sent to the Integration Platform when data changes due to imports or edits: - Meter Header/Configuration - Volumes (Hourly, Daily, Monthly) - Analysis (Hourly, Daily, Monthly) The following Meter Editor data points must be populated before an Integrated meter can be saved: - Facility - Integration ID - State - County This option must be set to "Yes" for other options on this tab to be enabled. - **Facility** – Allows the user to select a facility from the list of facilities designated as Integrated. This data point is necessary to properly identify a meter across the Quorum ecosystem. - **Integration ID** – Allows the user to enter a unique ID that is necessary to properly identify a meter across the Quorum ecosystem. - Must be a unique value among all other existing Integration IDs - Maximum length is 10 characters

docs.title: Misc. Tab
docs.text:
Most of the items listed are informational fields about the meter. Meter Type, Meter Make, and Default Temperature are retrieved from the meter characteristics table for the current characteristic and are read-only. The user can enter other details about the meter such as the Serial Number, Site ID, Power Source, Pressure Mode, and Temperature Mode.

  • Last Modified - Read-only field that shows the last user that edited the meter within the Meter Editor and the datetime that it was edited. This could be something as simple as a Custom Fields update.

  • Existing Data - Read-only field that shows the meter’s Creation Date (first date that the meter's data was imported into FLOWCAL), Unarchived Data Start (date of the first data record in the database for the meter) and Unarchived Data End (date of the last data record in the database for the meter).

The Unarchived Data End should not exceed the current datetime.

  • First Flow - These fields are utilized to notify a contact when the meter begins to flow. The analyst manually enters the date once they have confirmed real flow within the Volume Editor. A notification email is then sent to the Contact Type set up in the Notify field.

docs.title: Operations Tab
docs.text:
The following items are available on the Operations tab of the Calculated Meter Editor:

Meter Direction - Meter or location direction (e.g., Inlet, Outlet). The directions for a calculated meter determine the math that will be used.

For inlet meters: Inlets - Outlets

For outlet meters: Outlets - Inlets

For throughput meters: Positive Quantities* - Negative Quantities

*Specified in the Relationship tab

Meter Class - A meter class or "meter purpose" used to provide FLOWCAL categories for grouping meters within viewers and reports (e.g., Sales, Receipt, Delivery).

Calculate Component (Calculated Meter Type) - A calculated meter is normally set to calculate the net total for the members based on the defined arithmetic or it can calculate the volume for one specific component as configured in the Calculated Meter Type section. If configured to calculate the volume for a given component, the mole % of each member is applied to the member volume and those totals are used to arrive at the net. That is FLOWCAL does not total a net and then apply a calculated mole %.

Meter direction and class can be defined from the Calculated Meter Editor when in new mode. Once a calculated meter is created, direction and class can only be edited from the Volume Editor.

docs.title: Relationship Tab
docs.text:
The relationship tab displays the meters and/or locations that make up the calculated meter for the time frame selected.

Click any column header to sort the data by that column, in ascending or descending order.

  • X - Multiplier

This function is available for any member/direction type.

  • System - System associated with the meter or location

  • L/M - Indicates whether a member is a location or meter

  • Number - Meter or location number

  • Name - Meter or location name

  • Class - A meter class or "meter purpose" used to provide FLOWCAL categories for grouping meters within viewers and reports (e.g., Sales, Receipt, Delivery).

  • Direction - Meter or location direction (e.g., Inlet, Outlet). The meter member directions allowed are dependent on the direction of the calculated meter. If the calculated meter has a direction of "Throughput", the meter members must have a direction of "Throughput" as well. If throughput meters are added as members of a calculated meter, the contribution must be specified (positive or negative) before the calculated meter is saved.

  • Type - Meter or location type (e.g., Orifice, Turbine, Station)

docs.title: Reports Tab
docs.text:
The Reports tab contains various meter level report options that are associated to and affect the behavior of several standard reports. In addition, contract hour, contract day, and data span are displayed as read-only fields from the meter’s most recent characteristic record.

The following items are available on the Reports tab of the Calculated Meter Editor:

  • Print Customer Name - If set to Yes, the customer name will be printed at the top of all meter reports (that display one meter per page), such as the Hourly and Daily Gas Volume Statements. The customer is selected on the General tab of the Meter Editor. If set to Yes, the customer name will take precedence over a company name or logo defined in FLOWCAL.
  • Print Edit Reasons on Gas Volume Statement - By default, Daily and Hourly Gas Volume Statements identify each record as edited or not, but do not print the edit reasons. With this option, you can choose to:
  • Show Codes and Reasons
  • Indicate Edited Data, No Reasons
  • No Edit Indicators
  • Print Interval or Fixed Factor on Gas Volume Statement - Determines whether the interval or fixed factor will be displayed on the Gas Volume Statement. For charts, this is the rotation and for EFMs, this is the data resolution as defined in the meter’s characteristics.
  • Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - On most meter reports where the meter name is displayed, the Alternate Meter Number can be displayed in its place. The Alt. Meter Number is set on the General tab of the Meter Editor.
  • Print Volume at Optional Pressure Base - If set to Yes, the volume will be recalculated at the pressure base specified in the Use Pressure Base of field. This recalculated volume will then be printed at the bottom of the Daily Gas Volume Statement, along with the optional pressure base. The value entered for the optional pressure base must be between 9.000 and 20.000 psi.
  • Use Pressure Base of - Used in conjunction with the Print Volume at Optional Pressure Base option.
  • Print Measurement Area - If set to Yes, the Measurement Area will be printed at the top of most meter reports that display one meter per page.
  • Measurement Area - Select a Measurement Area from the drop-down or, with the correct privileges, click the New button to create a new Measurement Area. Measurement Areas are managed from the Measurement Area Editor.
  • Chart Change Schedule - Chart labels can be created for scheduled chart routes. A schedule is used to specify the on and off dates for the charts, which is used when printing the Bar Code Labels report.
  • Skip Closing Data - Any meter can be closed, but the closing of a meter can be prohibited by setting this option to Yes. The default is No.

docs.title: Tools Menu
docs.text:
Menu items under the Tools menu are available when in edit mode. The Info menu item is available from both edit and new mode.

The following items are available on the Tools menu in the Calculated Meter Editor:

  • Contact Selection - Contact Relationships can be designated for meters, sources and locations.

The user can associate specific contacts (email addresses) to a calculated meter. Exceptions and messages logged for the meter will automatically be emailed to the associated contacts for exceptions and messages set up for the contact type.

  • Validations* - When a calculated meter is rolled up, if validations are enabled, an exception will be logged if the value comes in outside the range defined.

  • Info - Contains user-definable fields and an additional notes section.

The notes stored on the Info screen are only available from the Calculated Meter Editor Info menu. For notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., Volume Editor), right-click on the Calculated Meter Editor screen to add or view notes.

  • Validate Hierarchy* - The Validate Hierarchy tool assists users in troubleshooting issues. The user opens the Validate Hierarchy tool from the Calculated Meter Editor, then chooses the validation options to run: Show Invalid Tieover, Show Invalid Transfers, Validate Throughput as Tieover, and Show Unused Meters.

  • Find Parent Locations* - The Find Parent Locations tool can be used to find a meter within a large hierarchy, or find all locations that a meter belongs to. From the Calculated Meter Editor Tools menu, select Find Parent Locations and enter part or all of the meter number into the filter. Select the meter number you are looking for from the left pane. The Right pane will show the locations that the meter is a member of.

  • Product Conversion* - Not applicable for calculated meters.

* These values are carried over from the Location Editor and do not apply to calculated meters.

docs.title: Calculated Meter Rollup Process
docs.text:
The Calculated Meter Rollup service performs calculations as follows:

  1. Gathers final form data for meter and location members. If Component Calculation is configured for a particular component, the selected component total data from the members are gathered.
  2. For non-quantity flow parameters, calculates averages of final form hourly values of members according to the selected Averaging Pool option and populates into the final form hourly record of the calculated meter.
  3. If the Formulas option is enabled, then for each measurement hour of the calculated meter:
    1. Reads the IF statement for the calculated meter.
    2. Retrieves the specified data point from each member that appear in the IF statement, from the final form record of the specified resolution.
    3. Substitutes in the retrieved member values into the IF statement and evaluates it.
    4. According to the evaluation result, reads either the DO or the ELSE DO statement of the calculated meter.
    5. For each quantity, such as volume, energy, and mass, calculates as specified by the statement using the final form hourly data of the members that appear in the statement, and adds the data to the final form hourly record of the calculated meter.
  4. If the Formulas option is not enabled, calculates the hourly values of the calculated meter following standard FLOWCAL rollup processes. The rollup arithmetic is determined by directions of the calculated meter and the members. See: Calculated Meter Direction
  5. Rolls the final form hourly data of the calculated meter up to the daily and monthly resolutions following the standard FLOWCAL rollup processes.

docs.title: Formula Statement Editors
docs.text:
Use the formula statement editors to enter calculated meter formulas consisting of calculated meter members, numbers, and basic arithmetic operators. To ensure consistency, editing is done using buttons to insert components, rather than manually typing in components. This helps users adhere to the syntactical rules required by the parser of the Calculated Meter Rollup service.

For details about how the Calculated Meter Rollup service applies the formula entered in these editor, see: Calculated Meter Rollup Process.

IF Statement Editor

An IF statement contains a left side, right side, and an inequality operator. An IF statement determines whether a DO and ELSE DO calculation will take place if the conditions are met; it does not specify how the calculation is performed. The calculation method is specified by DO and ELSE DO statements. To configure an IF statement: 1. Select a resolution and data point to specify what the condition will be based on. The default selections are Hourly (resolution) and Volume (data point). The following resolutions and data points are supported: > > > > Resolutions > Data Points > > > > > Hourly > Volume > > > Daily > Energy > > > Monthly > Mass > > > > Flow Time > > > Differential Pressure > > > Pressure > > > Temperature > > > Pulses > > > Raw Volume > > > Heating Value > > > 1. Select a side to edit. Click the display boxes located on either side of the inequality drop-down. The activated side will be white; the deactivated side will be grey. 2. Select an inequality operator to be used for the IF evaluation using the drop-down. The following operators are supported: > - **\>** (is greater than) > - **\<** (is less than) > - **=** (is equal to) > - **\>=** (is greater than or equal to) > - **\<=** (is less than or equal to) > - **\<\>** (is less than or greater than) 1. Refer to Common Edit Form Components for details about the other features on this screen.

DO Statement Editor

Use the DO Statement Editor to specify how the calculated meter values will be calculated when the IF statement is determined to be true. For each measurement hour where the IF statement is true, quantities of the calculated meter will be calculated as specified. See: [Calculated Meter Rollup Process](Calculated%20Meter%20Rollup%20Process.md) Refer to Common Edit Form Components for details about the other features on this screen.

ELSE DO Statement Editor

Use the ELSE DO Statement Editor to specify the calculation to be performed when the IF statement is determined to be false. For each measurement hour where the IF statement is false, quantities of the calculated meter will be calculated as specified. See: [Calculated Meter Rollup Process](Calculated%20Meter%20Rollup%20Process.md) Refer to Common Edit Form Components for details about the other features on this screen.

Common Edit Form Components

To ensure consistency, statements cannot be manually typed in; they are edited using textboxes and buttons on the edit form. Components are enabled only when it is syntactically appropriate to use them. Insert the following items into your statement: - **Arithmetic components** - Click the buttons to enter the necessary components. - **Members** - Select the Meter or Location radio button. Members of the calculated meter will display in the drop-down. Select the number in the drop-down and click the **Insert** button. Each statement can contain up to 10 members. When a member is inserted, “M.” or “L.” is added to the beginning of the object number to indicate the object type (meter or location, respectively) for parsing. - **Constants** - Enter the value in the textbox and click the Insert button. ### Statement Display Box The statement display box concatenates the specified components and displays the result. This text box is read-only; you cannot type in the statement to edit. Editing occurs only at the end of the statements. The content can be selected and copied into other text editors. The following function buttons are available: - **Backspace** - Delete the element entered last in the current display box. - **Clear** - Delete all elements entered in the current display box. - **Validate** - Trigger a validation of what has been currently entered for the statement for syntactical errors. (See: [Validation and Error Messages](Validation%20and%20Error%20Messages.md)) - **Apply** - Store the statement and close the edit form. Clicking this button applies the same syntax validation as the Validate button. The statement must pass the validation in order for the form to be closed and the statement to be stored. - **Cancel** - Discards edits made during the current session and close the form.

docs.title: Formula Validation and Error Messages
docs.text: A formula expression consisting of three statements cannot be saved to the database unless the syntax is correct and all member relationships are correct. Otherwise, the Calculated Meter Rollup service cannot perform correctly.

docs.title: Syntax Validation
docs.text:
Syntactical validation is triggered from the Calculated Meter Editor by:

  • Clicking the Validate button in an edit form
  • Clicking the Apply button in an edit form
  • Saving data in the Calculated Meter Editor

In the first two events, only the current statement being edited is validated. When saving the edit session and exiting the Calculated Meter Editor, IF, DO, and ELSE DO statements are validated together as an expression.

All validations are syntactical only and will not validate whether the mathematical expression is a valid operation. If an expression leads to an invalid operation, the Calculated Meter Rollup service will log an exception message when it evaluates the expression for processing. See: Formula Exception Messages

When the validation is complete, a Validation Results window will display. If there are any errors, they will be listed here. All errors must be resolved before the statement can be saved.

Syntax Validation Error Messages

The following error messages can be generated during syntax validation. | Error Message | Description/Notes | |:---|:---| | The left/right side of the statement should not be empty. Please provide information for the left/right side. | IF statement cannot be populated only on one side (IF statement only). | | Statement must contain at least one location or meter. | IF statement only | | The left/right side of the statement did not end properly. Please complete the left/right side. | Each side must end with either a member, a constant, or closing parenthesis (IF statement only). | | Statement did not end properly. Please complete the statement. | Statement must end with either a member, a constant, or closing parenthesis (DO and ELSE DO statements only). | | \ is not a member of the calculated meter. | This error occurs when a member is removed from the calculated meter, either by editing in the Relationship tab or by deleting it from FLOWCAL. The calculated meter edit session following the removal cannot be saved until the formulas are edited to exclude the removed member. | | If and Do statements should not be empty simultaneously. | This error occurs when an ELSE DO statement is provided but IF and DO statements are not. | | Do and Else Do statements should not be empty simultaneously. | This error occurs when IF statement is provided but DO and ELSE DO statements are not. | | Statement guarantees a division by zero. Please remove division by zero. | \- | | Parser experienced an error when processing “\". | \- | | “\” is an invalid statement component. | \- | | Unknown compiler error. | \- | | Parenthetical structure is invalid. Please review the opening and closing parentheses. | DO and ELSE DO statements only | | Left/Right Side - Parenthetical structure is invalid. Please review the opening and closing parentheses. | IF statement only | | Statement is invalid. Please review for mathematical validity. | \- | | Statement includes invalid arithmetic operation. Please review for mathematical validity. | \- | | Parser does not recognize "\". | \- |

Statement Editor Syntax Errors

Some syntax errors are validated at the time the edit is made. Error messages in these cases are displayed in the status bar of the edit form. | Statement Editor Error Message | Description/Notes | |:---|:---| | Number of members cannot exceed 10. | \- | | Constant cannot be greater than 1000000000. | \- | | Constant cannot be less than -1000000000. | \- | | Number of characters cannot exceed 1024. | Character count includes spaces between components and other hidden special characters added for parsing. |

Formula Exception Messages

If the Calculated Meter Rollup service evaluates a formula statement and fails to produce a valid result, an exception message will be logged to the service log file for the measurement hour. Evaluation of the IF statement takes place for each hour of the calculated meter, but all hours for an entire day or an entire month could possibly have same result, depending on the resolution of the IF statement configured on the Formulas tab. When the evaluation of the IF statement does not yield a valid value and the IF statement cannot be determined to be true or false, an exception message is logged for all applicable hours per the statement resolution. Evaluation of the DO or ELSE DO statement takes place for each of the summed values for each hour of the calculated meter. Although an invalid result might be produced for any and all of the summed values, an exception message is logged only if the adjusted total volume (FC_FFMTR_HOURLY.adjusted_total_volume) and the adjusted total energy (FC_FFMTR_HOURLY.adjusted_total_energy) result in an invalid value. Results for other summed values are irrelevant to the exception logging. An invalid result, or a null value, is different from a blank statement. Exception messages are not logged for blank statements. This could happen for a variety of reasons, including but not limited to: - **Unintended division by zero** **For example:** 1 / (METER1 - METER1) will be evaluated as Not a Number, regardless of the METER1 value. Another example is 1 / (METER1 - METER2) where METER1 and METER2 happen to have the same values. - **Unintended division by null** **For example:** 1 / METER1 will be evaluated to be null when METER1 has no value. The Calculated Meter Rollup service currently supports three exception messages: | Exception Message | Description/Notes | |:---|:---| | 1201 CV – Evaluation failed for the IF statement of the calculated meter | The evaluation of the IF statement fails to produce a valid value for any reason and the evaluation result is null. All summed values of the final form hourly record for the calculated meter being processed will be null. This message is logged for each hour and each calculated meter with the error. | | 1202 CV – Evaluation failed for the DO statement of the calculated meter | The IF statement is true and the evaluation of the DO statement fails to produce a valid value for adjusted total volume and adjusted total energy for any reason and they are both null. This message is logged for each hour and each calculated meter with these results. | | 1203 CV – Evaluation failed for the ELSE DO statement of the calculated meter | The IF statement is false and the evaluation of the ELSE DO statement fails to produce a valid value for adjusted total volume and adjusted total energy for any reason and they are both null. This message is logged for each hour and each calculated meter with these results. |

docs.title: Close Dates Editor
docs.text:
The Close Dates Editor displays the following close status information for a specified meter:

  • Months for which the meter is closed
  • Whether the meter is still closed or has been reopened
  • Whether PPAs have been applied
  • The start and end of the closed month
  • When the month was last closed or opened
  • Who last closed or opened the meter for that month
To view meter close dates: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Close Dates**. 2. Select a meter number or meter name from the drop-down menu. 3. To view data for the meter for a range of months, select **Contract Month** and select the time frame to be displayed; otherwise, select **All Dates**. 4. Click **Refresh**.

Meter Close Date Considerations

Once a meter’s information is displayed in the editor, if a month has been closed, but no PPAs have been applied, the user can select the row for that month and click Open Data. This will open the month and any edits to the data will be saved as regular edits, not as PPAs. Who opened the data and when they opened it will be recorded and displayed under Open/Closed By and Open/Closed On, respectively. If a meter has been opened for a month, it can be closed by selecting the row for that month and clicking Close Data. This will close the month and any edits to the data will be saved as PPAs. The meter can only be closed for the month in this manner if it was already previously closed and subsequently opened. Who closed the data and when they closed it will be recorded and displayed under Open/Closed By and Open/Closed On, respectively. By default, any meter can be closed as long as the user has appropriate permissions (see: [User Access](../Settings%20Manager/Security/User%20Access.md)).

Disallow Closing of Meters

To disallow the closing of meters: 1. Go to the [Meter Editor Reports tab](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Reports%20Tab.md). 2. Set the "Skip Closing Data" option to "Yes". 3. Return to the Meter Data Close Dates Editor. "Disallowed" will display under the "Closes of this Meter are" label. 4. To override this setting, click the **OK** button under "Change?". This setting will not impact data that has already been closed.

docs.title: About Close Groups
docs.text:
Lists or close groups allow users to close multiple meters together according to the close schedule requested. Whether a company uses lists or close groups is determined by how the Close Schedule Type option selected in the FLOWCAL Configuration screen. "List" is the default close schedule type.

Consider the following when determining whether to use lists or close groups for close schedules:

Functionality Lists Close Groups A meter can only belong to one at any point in time No Yes Datetime effective No Yes A meter must be assigned to one during meter creation before the meter can be saved No Yes, if the Require on Meter Create option is enabled

docs.title: Close Group Implementation
docs.text:
The process of implementing the use of close groups is as follows:

After setting the close schedule type to "Close Group", the Close Groups drop-down will be available in the Meter Editor and Meter Quick Create screen. The Close Schedules screen will also be set to use close groups instead of lists.

In addition to close schedules, close groups can also be used to generate reports and exports, import data, and view data. Locations can also be assigned to close groups. A Close Group tab is available in the Location Editor for liquids to allow you to close tickets associated with the location. For gas, if you associate a location with a close group and close it, all the meters within the location will be closed automatically.

docs.title: Assign Locations to Close Groups
docs.text:
After assigning a meter or group of meters to a location, you can assign that location to a close group. You can also assign locations to close groups in bulk from the Bulk Changes screen.

To assign a location to a close group: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Editor**. 2. Select a location, and click the **Edit** button. 3. Select the **Close Group** tab. 4. Double-click on a row in the table to open the Select Close Group screen. 5. Select a close group. 6. Enter a start and end month and year. 7. Click **OK** to return to the Location Editor. 8. Click **Save** to apply the changes.

You can also use the Close Group tab to assign a location to more than one close group during different time periods.

A Close Group tab is available in the Location Editor for liquids to allow you to close tickets associated with the location. For gas, if you associate a location with a close group and close it, all the meters within the location will be closed automatically.

docs.title: Assign Meters to Close Groups
docs.text:
Meter Close Group assignments take place in the Meter Editor, creating a new meter from Meter Quick Create, or in bulk from the Bulk Changes screen.

For the Close Groups option to be available, the close schedule type within the FLOWCAL Options screen must be set to "Close Group".

To assign a meter to a close group from the Meter Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter Editor**. 2. Select a meter, and click **Edit**. 3. Select a close group from the Close Groups drop-down on the General tab. 4. Click **Save** to apply changes. The meter is assigned to the close group from 1/1972 through 12/2037 by default.

docs.title: Close Schedules
docs.text:
Once a list or close group has been created, data must be scheduled for closing before it can be closed, either manually or with the Close Scheduler Service. This is done in the Close Schedule screen.

To access Close Schedules: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Close Schedules**. 2. Select the List Name or Close Group Name to close from the drop-down menu. 3. Click the **New Sched** button. 4. Select the Measurement Month to close from the drop-down menu. 5. Select the close on date that the user would like the data to be closed on from the drop-down menu. This is only used by the Close Scheduler service. Once the date on the server running the Close Scheduler service has passed this date, the Close Scheduler service will try to close the data for all meters and tickets attached to Locations in the list or close group. 6. Click **OK**. The user will then be prompted that the gas month has been successfully scheduled to be closed.

Close Schedule Screen Details

The following items are available on the Close Schedule screen: - **Hold** - Place the schedule on hold and the service will ignore the scheduled Close Group until the Release Now button is clicked. - **New Sched** - Open the Close Group Schedule Date form. - **Release Now** - Close the data now with the Close Scheduler Service by updating the Close On date to be the current date and time. - **Show Open** - Display all the meters that are currently open. The user can select to view the open meters by selecting All Meters or by List/Close Groups for the month and year selected in the Meters Not Closed form. - **Close Data** - Close the selected close group immediately. The Close Data option requires **Meter Close - Can Schedule** and **Close Group - Can Schedule** privileges.

Viewing Meters That Are Not Closed

To view a list of meters that are not closed: 1. Click the **Show Open** button. 2. Select **All Meters** to view all open meters. 3. To view open meters in a particular list or close group, select the **List** or **Close Group** radio button. Then select a list name or close group name from the pull down selection. 4. Select the month and year to scan for open meters. 5. Click **Refresh**.

Close Schedule Considerations

- Only contract months can be scheduled for closing. Users cannot schedule less than a month (May 7 - May 15, for example) for closing. Each month must be scheduled individually. For example, to close March through May, the user must schedule March, then April and then May. The order can vary (you could schedule May, then March, then April, for instance), but each month must be done individually. - Once a month has been scheduled for closing, it can be done manually or by the close scheduler service. To close a month manually, select the month to close by clicking on the appropriate row and then click Close Data. Depending on how many meters and/or tickets attached to locations are in the list or close group, this may take some time. If the month is successfully closed, the user will be informed and the window will display the date the data was closed on. If not, the date of the failed attempt will be displayed along with the reason for the failure. - For data being closed by the Close Service, the success or failure of the closing of the data can be monitored from this window. If a list fails to close, the user can view the reason for the failure and correct the problem. Every time the service runs, it will try to close the data until it succeeds, so once the problem is corrected, the service will close the data. - The Release Now button is used to close the data now with the Close Scheduler Service by updating the Close On date to be the current date and time. - Additionally, the following requirements need to be kept in mind when closing meter or ticket data: - The close date must be after the selected contract month ends. - There cannot be any unresolved exceptions for a meter or ticket to be closed. - If the option to not close a meter if it has missing data has been selected, then the meter must have data for every hour. This requirement is only for meters, not tickets. - If one meter in the List or Close Group cannot be closed, all other meters or tickets in the list that can be closed will be. - If a Location has only Tickets associated with it and it is a member of a List or Close Group that is scheduled for close, then FLOWCAL's Close Data service attempts to close each ticket assigned to that Location. If a single ticket fails to close, the service continues to process all of the remaining members of the List or Close Group. Hard Closing by clicking the Close Data button in the Close Schedules Editor also closes tickets on any locations within the List or Close Group being closed. Once a ticket has been processed, the associated Location is queued to close and is processed by the Location Close Data service (FCSRVLCNCLOSEDATA.exe).

docs.title: Create Close Groups
docs.text:
A close group consists of a meter or a set of meters that should be closed together on the same date. Once a close group is created and meters have been assigned to it, you can generate automatic monthly close schedules for the group, or you can close it manually, just as with a list.

To create a close group: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Close Groups** to access the Close Groups screen. The close schedule type within the FLOWCAL Options screen must be set to "Close Group" to enable access to the Close Group screen. 2. Click **New** 3. Enter a close group number (required) and a close group name (optional). 4. Check the "Enable" option to enable the close group. 5. Click **Save**. Administrators must have the "Application Process – Close Groups" privilege, granted from the User or Group Access screen, to create and edit close groups.

docs.title: Edit Close Groups
docs.text:
After creating a close group, you can update the close group number or name by editing this data on the Close Groups screen. You can also enable or disable the close group.

To edit a close group: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Close Groups**. 2. Click **Edit**. 3. Update the close group data as needed. 4. Click **Save** to apply changes.

Close groups cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Manage Close Groups
docs.text:
Once a meter is assigned to a close group, the button to the right of the drop-down becomes enabled which provides access to the Manage Close Groups screen.

The Manage Close Groups screen displays all the close groups a meter belongs to. You can use this screen to assign a meter to more than one close group during different time periods.

To assign a different close group to a meter: 1. From the Meter Editor, click button next to the Close Groups drop-down on the General tab, or go to **Tools** \> **Manage Close Groups**. 2. Click **Edit**. A new row will display. 3. Select a start month and end month. Click in each field to manually type in a year. 4. Click **OK** to apply the changes. The start and end month for the other close group assignments are automatically adjusted based on the changes. 5. Click **Save** and **Exit** to return to the Meter Editor. To discard the changes, click **Cancel** and **Exit**.

docs.title: View Close Groups
docs.text:
You may need to see a list of all close groups that have been created in FLOWCAL, or a list of all close groups assigned to a meter.

To view all available close groups: Go to Setup > Close Groups.

To view the close groups assigned to a meter: Go to the Meter Editor, and click button next to the Close Groups drop-down on the General tab, or go to Tools > Manage Close Groups.

docs.title: Comparison Location Editor
docs.text: << Back | Configuration | Validation

docs.title: Configuration Tab
docs.text:
The following items are available on the Configuration tab:

  • Check and Custody object selectors - Select designations for the check and custody measurements. They may be meters, locations or a mix of the two.

  • Calculation - Define the calculation used to provide the comparative amount and percentage. This is not an absolute value.

To define the comparison calculation, set the numerator to determine the difference. The choices are either: (Check - Custody) or (Custody - Check). This essentially determines the sign of the result. Positive values represent the user's maximum validation, while negative values represent the user's minimum validation. Set the denominator to determine if the result is a percentage of the check measurement or a percentage of the custody measurement.

Meter and location directions will not be factored into the comparison. An inlet can be compared to another inlet or to an outlet. The sign will be determined by this definition.

  • Reference Meter - A comparison location requires a reference meter to determine contract day and hour. The reference meter does not have to be a meter that is used in the calculation.

docs.title: Comparison Location Editor
docs.text: << Back | Configuration | Validation

docs.title: Validation Tab
docs.text:
Monthly, Weekly, and Daily Resolution Sub-Tabs

The resolution tabs contain the user-configurable minimum and maximum limits. Daily and monthly resolutions are supported for all locations. If the Calculate Weekly Totals system option is enabled, the Weekly tab will display.

FLOWCAL validates the net quantity in the given unit and does not perform unit conversions.

Validations are run by the Location Rollup service. They can also be initiated from the Toolbox.

docs.title: Comparison Location Editor
docs.text: << Back | Comparison Location | Tools

docs.title: Comparison Location Menu
docs.text:
The following options are available on the Comparison Location menu:

  • New - Create a new comparison location. The fluid phase will be set to the user-defined default fluid phase configured within User Preferences. To set the fluid phase manually, click the drop-down on the New button and select Gas or Liquid.

The gas and liquid fluid phases are only available with the FLOWCAL Gas and Liquid modules, respectively.

  • Edit - Enable Edit mode.

  • Save - Save changes.

  • Delete - Delete the selected location.

  • Cancel - Cancel edits and do not save changes.

  • Exit - Exit the screen.

docs.title: Comparison Location
docs.text:
A comparison location is a type of location used to compare the measurement quantities of two entities. The entities to be compared can be meters, locations or one of each. A comparison location is typically used when a metering site has both check and custody measurement. This allows users to easily compare the two and ensure any differences fall within user-determined validation limits.

The ability for a user to define a comparison scenario provides additional capability for proactive anomaly detection. By creating a comparison location and constantly tracking the variance between the two sets of measurement points, anomalies can be promptly detected and resolved. In addition, with a history of comparisons on record, the check data can be confidently substituted if the custody measurement is unavailable.

Comparison locations calculate differences and percent differences for gas volume and gas energy; liquid GSV, NSV, summed volume, and net allowable; and mass (for both gas and liquids). The difference and percent difference is calculated for each quantity at daily, weekly, and monthly data resolutions.

docs.title: Comparison Location Editor
docs.text:
The Comparison Location Editor consists of a main window, a Configuration tab, and a Validation tab.

To access the Comparison Location Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Comparison Location**.

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Comparison Location Editor screen: - **Comparison** (group box) - This selector is used to pick the comparison location to be edited. - **New** - Create a new comparison location. The fluid phase will be set to the user-defined default fluid phase configured within [User Preferences](../Settings%20Manager/User%20Settings/User%20Preferences.md). To set the fluid phase manually, click the drop-down on the **New** button and select **Gas** or **Liquid**. The gas and liquid fluid phases are only available with the FLOWCAL Gas and Liquid modules, respectively - **Edit** - Enable Edit mode. - **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not save changes. - **Save** - Save changes. - **Delete** - Delete the selected location.

docs.title: Tools Menu
docs.text:
The following items are available on the Tools menu:

  • Info
  • Alt ID - Not used anywhere else, this is an FYI field.
  • Fluid Phase - The fluid phase for the location (gas or liquid) determines which columns to initially display in the Meter/Location Rollup Viewer. This is defined on location creation and cannot be changed once the location is created.
  • Meas. Area - Select a measurement area from the drop-down or, with System Information privileges, click New and create a new measurement area.
  • Custom Fields - Labels can be user-defined. (See: Define Custom Field Labels)
  • Notes - Open area for storing comments and information about this location.
  • Contact Selection - Contact relationships can be designated for meters, sources, and locations.

Users can associate specific contacts (email addresses) to a location. Exceptions and messages logged for the location can be configured to trigger an email to the associated contacts.

docs.title: Arranging and Customizing Tiles
docs.text:
The quick launch tiles can be arranged on the dashboard in any order. Simply drag and drop a tile into a new location. While you are moving the tile, it will display as semi-transparent.

Arrange tiles starting at the top left corner and working your way down, two columns at a time.

Tile Groups

Groups are denoted by increased space between tiles or tools. To create a new group of tiles or tools: 1. Click the desired tile or tool and drag it to an open area on the right side of the dashboard. This will create a new group area where other items can be added. 2. Add more items to the group as needed.

Tile Size

Reducing tile size increases available dashboard space. To change the size of a tile: 1. Right-click a tile. 2. Hover over **Size**. 3. Select the appropriate option.

Tile Color

Tiles and widgets can be color-coded to denote priority or data groupings. To change a tile color: 1. Right-click the tile. 2. Hover over **Color**. 3. Select the desired color.

docs.title: Dashboard Manager
docs.text:
Use the Dashboard Manager to configure the following dashboard tools (widgets):

  • Quick Launch Tiles
  • "Did you know?" Tips
  • Exception Resolver Widget
  • Gain/Loss Balance Widget
To configure your Dashboard items:  1. Go to **Settings** \> **Dashboard Manager**. 2. Click each item to access the corresponding settings screens.

docs.title: "Did you know?" Tips
docs.text:
The “Did you know?” widget displays information and tips about application features and functions. These messages will cycle automatically. To manually advance to a new message, click the “Did you know?” box.

Change Message Cycle Time

By default, the messages in the "Did you know?" widget will cycle automatically. You can adjust the cycle frequency to be every 5 seconds, 30 seconds, 1 minute, or 5 minutes, or you can elect to refresh the messages manually. To change the cycle time for the "Did you know?" widget: 1. Click the gear icon in the top right corner of the main screen to open the Settings menu. 2. Click **Dashboard Manager**. 3. Click **Did you know?**. 4. Select a cycle time from the **Message Interval** drop-down list.

Add or Remove "Did you know?" Widget

You may elect to remove the "Did you know?" widget from your dashboard, or add it back. To add or remove the “Did you know?” widget: 1. Open the Dashboard Manager and click **Did you know?**. 2. Click the "X" icon to remove the widget from your dashboard, or click the **Add Widget** link to add it back.

docs.title: Exception Resolver Widget
docs.text:
The FLOWCAL dashboard includes an Exception Resolver widget that displays the number of "Unresolved" and "Pending" exceptions associated with a given list.

By default, a single Exception Resolver widget displays on the dashboard, using the first list from the default system specified on the User Preferences screen.

The Exception Resolver widget will display the exact number of exceptions up to 9,999. If the number of exceptions is 10,000 or higher, the amount will be abbreviated with a decimal (example: 10,289 exceptions will display as 10.2K).

Click the More link in the bottom right corner of the widget to open the Exception Resolver. After resolving exceptions, click the refresh button

to update the exception count.

When you access the Exception Resolver by clicking the More link, exceptions with a status of Pending or Unresolved will display by default. Otherwise, the Exception Resolver will display exceptions based on your user preferences or session settings.

Change Lists

You can change the list for an Exception Resolver widget directly from the dashboard. To change a list: 1. Click the list name at the top of the widget. A drop-down will display the available lists. 2. Select the desired list from the drop-down list.

Add or Remove an Exception Resolver Widget

You can display up to 10 Exception Resolver widgets on your dashboard. To add or remove a widget: 1. Click the gear icon in the top right corner of the main screen to open the Settings menu. 2. Click **Dashboard Manager**. 3. Click **Exceptions**. 4. Click the "X" icon to remove the widget from your dashboard, or click the **Select to add a new widget** link to add a new widget.

Configure an Exception Resolver Widget

Use the Dashboard Manager to specify the system and list associated with an Exception Resolver widget. You can also assign specific colors to widgets to help make your data easy to view. To set up an Exception Resolver widget: 1. Click the gear icon in the top right corner of the main screen to open the Settings menu. 2. Click **Dashboard Manager**. 3. Click **Exceptions**. 4. Add a new widget if necessary. 5. Click the **System** and **List** fields to select a system and list for your widget. You can also begin typing in these fields to search for a name. 6. Assign a specific color to the widget (optional).

docs.title: Gain/Loss Balance Tool
docs.text:
The FLOWCAL dashboard includes a Gain/Loss Balance widget to help you keep track of location gain/loss balances.

By default, a single widget will display on the dashboard, using the preferred location set on the User Preferences screen.

Two views are available within the widget:

  • Table view shows the actual value of the data
  • Graphical view shows the percentage gain or loss for the location, with an upper and lower bound of 2 and -2, respectively

Click the widget to toggle between views.

Click the More link in the bottom right corner of the widget to open the Rollups Viewer. Click the Refresh button to update the data in the widget.

docs.title: Data Types
docs.text:
The data displayed in the Gain/Loss Balance widget varies based on the fluid phase of the location:

  • Gas Location - Volume, energy, mass
  • Liquid Location - NSV, mass
  • Gas and Liquid Location - Volume, energy, mass (gas), NSV, mass (liquid)

For gas or liquid locations, the Gain/Loss Balance widget defaults to the table view. You can click the widget to see the graphical view.

For mixed locations (locations that are both gas and liquid), the initial table view will display values for gas and liquid. When you click the widget, the graphical view will display the gas data. When you click the widget again, the graphical view will display the liquid data.

Add or Remove a Gain/Loss Balance Widget

You can display up to four Gain/Loss Balance widgets on the dashboard. To add or remove a Gain/Loss Balance widget: 1. Click the gear icon in the top right corner of the main screen to open the Settings menu. 2. Click **Dashboard Manager**. 3. Click **Gain/Loss Balance**. 4. Click the "X" icon to remove the widget from your dashboard, or click the **Add a new widget** link to add a new widget.

Configure a Gain/Loss Balance widget

Using the Dashboard Manager, you can specify the system and location associated with a Gain/Loss Balance widget. To set up a Gain/Loss Balance widget: 1. Click the gear icon in the top right corner of the main screen to open the Settings menu. 2. Click **Dashboard Manager**. 3. Click **Gain/Loss Balance**. 4. Add a new widget if necessary. 5. Click the **System** and **Location** fields to select a system and location for your widget. You can also begin typing in these fields to search for a name. 6. Select a unit of measure for the balance data.

docs.title: Quick Launch Tiles
docs.text:
Use the Dashboard Manager to select which tiles will display on your main screen.

To add or remove a dashboard tile: 1. Click the gear icon in the top right corner of the Main Screen to open the Settings menu. 2. Click **Dashboard Manager**. 3. Click **Quick Launch Tiles**. 4. A list of tiles is available in the left column of the screen. The tiles currently on your dashboard are in the right column of the screen. Drag and drop items from one column to the other to add or remove tiles from your dashboard. The order of tiles in this window does not reflect the order in which they will display on your dashboard. You can arrange the tile order directly from the main screen.

The TESTit tile is available for both TESTit 2 and TEST 3 Integrated. For TESTit 2, the database must be set to TESTit 2 and the associated files must be available within the FLOWCAL directory. For TESTit 3, the database must be set to TESTit 3 and the install path must be defined in the TESTit_Config.cfg file in the FLOWCAL directory. For the TESTit 3 tile to display, the path in the TESTit_Config.cfg must include the Bin folder that contains the TESTit.exe file (example: C:\Apps\TESTit\Bin).
