docs.title: Densitometer Editor
docs.text:
The Densitometer Editor allows users to create densitometers that can be assigned to meters.

Densitometers can be set up to either apply a particular density meter factor (DMF) to a meter or validate the meter’s DMF at import time. The densitometer can also be set up to validate that edited DMF values are within a certain tolerance and the edited value does not vary from the value being replaced by a certain percentage.

Using the densitometer to apply a DMF at import time is useful if the DMF is not being kept up to date in the flow computer in the field. You can create a date time effective DMF entry on a per product basis. As data is imported, FLOWCAL will apply the DMF.

At import time, applying a DMF to a meter will set the DMF characteristic of that meter to the specified value. If a DMF is applied to a meter from the FLOWCAL densitometer and the Uncorrected Observed Density is present and NO Corrected Observed Density is present, a corrected observed density will be calculated from the Uncorrected Observed Density and the applied DMF. If an Uncorrected Observed Density is not available at import, it will be calculated from the Corrected Observed Density and the applied DMF. No action will take place if both the Uncorrected and Corrected Observed Densities are imported, other than updating the DMF. Newly calculated values will be used in calculations for volume and mass accordingly.

Note that the densitometer DMF will only be applied at import. If the product on a batch is edited in the volume editor to a different product, the densitometer will not correct the DMF. The user will need to do that as a manual edit.

The user can choose to validate the DMF at import instead of applying it. When this option is selected if the imported DMF does not match the DMF in the densitometer out to the number of decimal places set in the product editor, FLOWCAL will generate exception 40000.

Creating a Densitometer

When an entry for a product is created, only a start date is specified. The entry for that product will be used until the end of time or until a new entry for that product is entered. For example: We have created an entry for Crude with a DMF of 0.9500 with an effective date of 1/1/1972 00:00:00. This value will be applied to meter data assigned to this densitometer where the imported product is Crude and the effective date is after 1/1/1972 00:00:00. If a second entry is created with an effective date of 1/1/2012 00:00:00 for Crude, then all data with a product of Crude imported into meters assigned to this densitometer will have this DMF used, provided that the record effective date is 1/1/2012 00:00:00 or later. To create a densitometer: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**. 2. Click **New** or press **Alt+N**. 3. Enter a densitometer name. 4. Click **Save**. 5. Right-click and select **New Periodic** to add a new periodic record. 6. Click **Save**. Additional product entries can be created for a densitometer. For instance, there might be a different crude product that flows on a meter such as Light Crude. Creating an entry for Light Crude at 1/1/2012 01:00:00 will cause all Light Crude data on meters assigned to this densitometer with an effective date on or after 1/1/2012 00:00:00 to apply the specified DMF. Meter data with a product of Crude will still use the entry for Crude. For a given date there can be only one entry in the densitometer. If a pyc is done for multiple products at the same time, each product entry must be entered at least one second apart from the other.

Editing a Densitometer

To edit a densitometer: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**. 2. Select a densitometer. 3. Click the **Periodic** tab and double-click a periodic record. 4. Make changes to the densitometer data as needed. 5. Click **Save**.

Deleting a Densitometer

To delete a densitometer: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**. 2. Select a densitometer. 3. Go to **Densitometer** \> **Delete**.

Densitometer Assignment

Use the Densitometer Assignment screen to assign meters to the densitometer so that the DMF can either be applied or validated during import. ##### Applying a DMF to Meter Data 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**. 2. Select a densitometer. 3. Click the **Assignment** tab. 4. Right-click and select **New Assignment**. 5. Select a meter from the drop-down menu. 6. Select an apply option. If you choose Apply DMF to meter you must also select a recalc method. If you choose Validate meter DMF, then the DMF wil not be applied to the meter, but the meter’s imported DMF will be validated against the DMF in the densitometer. If you choose Unspecified, then no action will take place. If the Apply option for a densitometer assignment is set to "Apply DMF to meter", the DMF is applied to the meter batch on import. An observed density is calculated from the unobserved density and the DMF is applied to the meter and calculations proceed accordingly. 7. Enter an effective date. 8. Click **Save**.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: • Densitometer Validations

docs.title: Densitometer Validations
docs.text:
Manually entered (user edit) DMF values can be validated. This is done through the Densitometer Validations screen. Users can enter a minimum and maximum value and a variance for the DMF value. When manually entering data, the user will be warned through a dialog box if the value entered for the DMF is out of the validation range conditions set in the densitometer. The variance is used to validate DMF changes for like products; exceptions are generated if a DMF change exceeds the validation variance for a given product.

Creating Validations

To create a validation: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Densitometer**. 2. Select a densitometer. 3. In the Densitometer Editor, go to **Densitometer** \> **Validations**. 4. Click **New**. 5. Select a product from the drop-down list. 6. Enter a minimum, maximum, and variance value for the product. 7. Click **Save**. Multiple validation criteria can be created on a per-product basis.

Editing Validations

To edit validations: 1. From the Densitometer Validations screen, click **Edit**. 2. Edit the desired variables. The product cannot be changed once created. 3. Click **Save**.

Deleting Validations

To delete validations: 1. From the Densitometer Validations screen, select the validation to be deleted. 2. Click **Delete**.

docs.title: Edit Approvals
docs.text:
Use the Edit Approvals screen to approve, reject, or un-reject pending edits, prior period adjustments, and applied test reports.

  • When edit approval limits are defined under System Configuration, monthly adjustments that exceed the specified volume or energy limit will require approval before the edit can be applied. Quality source apply and auto edits are not considered during calculation if edits have exceeded the edit approval limit.
  • When the PPA options are set to "Approval Required", any prior period adjustments will require approval before they are applied.
  • When test reports using TESTit Integrated are applied, approval is required before any edits are applied.

Viewing Records

To view records: 1. Go to **Review** \> **Approvals**. 2. Select a list, location, or meter. 3. Select a time filter. 4. Select the status filter. 5. Click the **Refresh** button.

Approving or Rejecting Edits

To approve, reject, or un-reject an edit: 1. Right-click a record and select **Approve** or **Reject**. A meter message is generated when an edit is approved or rejected. 2. If you select **Approve**, you will be prompted to provide a reason for the edit and a comment. A confirmation screen will display. 3. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor** to view the edit. You will need **Edit/PPA Approval - Can Approve** privileges to approve, reject, or un-reject an edit.

docs.title: Exception Directory

0 System constants not available for this period

This exception is most often created when the system encounters a gap in time in the [System Factors](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Factors.md) form while performing calculations.

1 Event old value does not match previous event new value

This exception will be generated when the system identifies unmatched old and new values while importing a CFX file. For example: The following CO2 events are imported: | Event | Old Value | New Value | |:-----:|:---------:|:---------:| | \#1 | 12.4983 | 12.4 | | \#2 | 12.505 | 12.506 | In this case, an exception is generated because the Event \#2 old value does not match the Event \#1 new value.  FLOWCAL expected the Event \#2 old value to equal 12.505.

2 Unknown transaction type

This exception is generated from the transaction queue if FLOWCAL receives a transaction type that does not correspond with the following known transaction types: | Number | Transaction Type | |:------:|:--------------------------------------------------------| | 1 | Meter Event - Instantaneous & Static Meter Transactions | | 2 | Meter Alarm | | 3 | Meter History - Periodic Measurement Transaction | | 4 | Meter Configuration Snapshot | | 5 | GQ Gas Quality - Periodic Gas Quality Transaction | | 6 | GQ Event - Instantaneous & Static GQ Transactions | | 7 | GQ Snapshot | | 10 | Meter Ultrasonic Data |

4 Meter identified in transaction failed to load

This exception is generated if data was loading for a meter and the transaction queue service or the FLOWCAL database lost connectivity. It could also be triggered by a meter that is locked by another user.
6 Failed reasonable test (deprecated)
8 Data received for out-of-service meter (deprecated)

9 Characteristic or analysis changed without corresponding event

This exception is generated when FLOWCAL receives data but does not have an event that matches the change in value. For example: If a liquid meter has a product of propane on the meter for all of the time, but the product is changed to butane through an import and there is not an event corresponding to the product change, this exception will be generated. This indicates that the user is not receiving events from their flow computer.
10 Meter number does not exist (deprecated)
12 Required value not given (deprecated)
14 Value out of range (deprecated)
16 Required value too high (deprecated)
18 Required value too low (deprecated)
19 Volume not given; will attempt to calculate it (deprecated)
20 Volume present but no differential pressure (deprecated)
22 Volume present but no pulses (deprecated)

24 Temperature base out of range

This exception is generated for a meter characteristic record that has a temperature base value that is less than or equal to -100 or greater than 1000.
26 Pipe diameter out of range (deprecated)
29 Orifice out of beta (small) (deprecated)
31 Orifice out of beta (large) (deprecated)
32 Fixed factor too small (deprecated)
33 Extreme relative density (deprecated)

34 Pressure base out of range

This exception is generated when the pressure base identified in the Meter Characteristics form is out of range. FLOWCAL uses a 12-16.1 (psi) hard-coded value for its pressure bases. Common triggers for this exception are base pressure values outside of the 12-16.1 range or incorrect pressure units. (See: [Unit Assignment](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/Unit%20Assignment.md))
35 Viscosity out of range using 6.9e-6 (deprecated)
36 Analysis is not available for this period (deprecated)
37 Specific heat ratio out of range using 1.3 (deprecated)

38 AGA-8 detail Fpv calculation has incomplete analysis

This exception applies to imported and edited Gas Flow Data when the Meter is Configured with a FPV Method of AGA-8 Detail. If the meter analysis on a flow data record has mole % values totaling anything other than 100%, then this exception will be generated.
40 Nitrogen (N2) is out of range (deprecated)
41 Total analysis composition is not within range (deprecated)

45 Unable to close data (meter has unresolved exceptions)

This exception is generated when FLOWCAL attempts to close a meter manually or via service and the meter has unresolved exceptions. To close the meter, the exceptions must be addressed in the Exception Resolver.

46 Unable to close data (meter has missing data)

This exception is generated when FLOWCAL attempts to close a meter with missing data, and the "Do Not Close if Missing Data" option is enabled in [System Configuration](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration.md).

47 Unable to close data (meter held from closing)

This exception is generated when FLOWCAL attempts to close a meter that meets the requirements to be closed (no missing data or unresolved exceptions), but is being held from closing, often due to pending exceptions. (See: Exception 50)

48 Auto estimated data replaced (import create revision)

This exception is generated when a meter has been configured for auto estimates and the ‘Log Exception on Replacing Auto Estimate’ and the ‘Replace Estimated Data on Import’ options are enabled within the Auto Estimate tab of the Meter Editor. Data that has been auto estimated will be overwritten as data is imported and the exception will be generated.

49 Missing or inhibited analysis; used prior data

This exception is generated when a Quality Source Assignment has been configured with the ‘Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited’ option enabled. As quality source analysis is imported or edited, that data is validated. If an exception is encountered, the record will become inhibited and the prior analysis record will be applied as configured in the Quality Source Assignment.

50 Unable to close data (meter has pending exceptions)

This exception is generated when FLOWCAL attempts to close a meter with pending exceptions and the "Do Not Close if Pending Exceptions" option is enabled in [System Configuration](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration.md).
51 Invalid exception number (deprecated)

52 Purged all data; keep original

This exception is generated when a meter purge is initiated using the "All Date/Time" date range and the "Keep Original Data" option.

53 Purged all data

This exception is generated when a meter purged is initiated using the "All Date/Time" date range.

54 HAS_RTD is different than USE_RTD

Total Flow flow computers have two flags: "HAS_RTD" and "USE_RTD". When a probe is connected to the computer, it registers with the "Has_RTD" flag, but the technician must manually enable the “Use_RTD” option, or the manual value will be used. This is a validation to check for a probe that is connected but not in use. This can be found in the CFX format on offset 426 and 427 for configuration. When these two values do not match the exception is generated.

55 Source assignment missing

This exception is generated for a gas meter that does not have a source assignment set up when the Source Assignments Required option in System Configuration is enabled. This exception is generated when the meter is saved in the Meter Editor with the First Flow date of the meter entered in the Misc. tab; the exception will be effective as of the First Flow date. This exception is automatically resolved when an assignment is created.

56 Default source assigned

This exception is generated for a gas meter upon apply of a GQ source that has been set as a default analysis, with the Source Assignments Required option in System Configuration enabled. This exception is generated for the effective date of the GQ assignment. (See: [Default Analysis](../../../Source%20Analysis/Gas%20Quality%20Source%20Editor/Main%20Tab.md#DefaultAnalysis))

57 Purged all data; keep original

This exception is generated when a liquid or gas quality source purge is initiated using the "All Date/Time" date range and the "Keep Original Data" option. FLOWCAL will keep the original imported values but purge any manually entered data or edits to original data. (See: [Purge Source Analysis](../../../Tools/Purge/Purge%20Source%20Analysis%20Data.md))

58 Purged all data

This exception is generated when a liquid or gas quality source purge is initiated using the "All Date/Time" date range. (See: [Purge Source Analysis](../../../Tools/Purge/Purge%20Source%20Analysis%20Data.md))

59 Discrepancy in full wellstream usage between meter and source

This exception is generated for a gas meter upon apply of a GQ source through an assignment. Upon analysis apply, if the meter characteristic and the source analysis record that is applied do not agree on whether full wellstream factor is used, this exception is generated on the meter characteristic record. Full wellstream usage is indicated on the Meter tab of the characteristic detail of Volume Editor for a meter, and on the Liq. Content tab for a GQ source analysis record. (See: [Full Wellstream Factor](../../../Source%20Analysis/Gas%20Quality%20Source%20Editor/Full%20Wellstream%20Factor.md))

60 Data point value does not equal the difference between starting and ending index

This exception is generated when the difference between the end index and start index of a value does not equal the value that is imported. For example: If a flow computer reads 1 as a start index and 11 for the end index, FLOWCAL (or the flow computer) will calculate the flow as 1. If a flow value other than 1 is imported, FLOWCAL will generate this exception.

61 Source record marked as "inhibited"

This exception is generated when a sample is missing and the "Use Prior when Current is Missing or Inhibited" option is enabled (Source Assignments). The sample time frame that is missing will generate an exception for the first time frame it would have been applied to the meter.

62 Missing source analysis; all or part of the data within the date range used prior analysis

This exception is generated for a meter periodic record if: - There is no applicable GQ source analysis record specified in the "Apply GQ At" option on the Assignment editor; and - The "Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited" option is enabled (Setup \> Source Analysis \> Quality Source Assignment Viewer). For example: the "Apply GQ At" option is set to "Effective Date/Time" on an assignment between a gas meter and an hourly chromatograph GQ, and the "Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited" option is enabled. The GQ contains three analysis records (note that the 14:00:00 record is missing): |   | Effective Date | Effective End Date | |:---:|:-----------------:|:------------------:| | A | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | | B | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | | C | 1/1/2016 15:00:00 | 1/1/2016 16:00:00 | The GQ analysis records are applied to the meter as follows: | Meter Periodic Record Effective Date | Applied Analysis | |:------------------------------------:|:----------------:| | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | A | | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | B | | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | B | | 1/1/2016 15:00:00 | C | The exception is generated on the meter periodic record at 1/1/2016 14:00:00.

63 Inhibited source analysis; all or part of the data within the date range used prior analysis

This exception is generated for a gas meter upon apply of a GQ source through an assignment. Upon analysis apply, if the analysis record on the assigned GQ that is applicable to a meter periodic record according to the Apply GQ At option on the Assignment editor is inhibited and as a result no analysis is applied to the meter periodic record, this exception is generated on the meter periodic record. This is applicable only is the User Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibition option on the Quality Source Assignment editor (Setup \> Source Analysis \> Quality Source Assignment Viewer \> *select a gas meter and a record*) is unchecked. For example, the Apply GQ At option is set to Effective Date/Time on an assignment between a gas meter and an hourly chromatograph GQ, and the Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option is unchecked. The GQ has following analysis records: |   | Effective Date | Effective End Date | Note | |:---:|:-----------------:|--------------------|:---------:| | A | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | \- | | B | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | Inhibited | | C | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | 1/1/2016 15:00:00 | \- | GQ analysis records are applied to the meter as follows: | Meter Periodic Record Effective Date | Applied Analysis | |:------------------------------------:|:----------------:| | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | A | | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | No Analysis | | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | C | Then this exception is generated on the meter periodic record at 1/1/2016 13:00:00.

64 Inhibited analysis; used prior data

This exception is generated for a gas meter upon apply of a GQ source through an assignment. When setting up the assignment on the Quality Source Assignment editor (Setup \> Source Analysis \> Quality Source Assignment Viewer \> *select a gas meter and a record*), the Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option is checked. Upon analysis apply, if the analysis record on the assigned GQ that is applicable to a meter periodic record according to the Apply GQ At option on the Assignment editor is inhibited and a prior analysis record is applied instead per this option, this exception is generated on the meter periodic record. For example, the Apply GQ At option is set to Effective Date/Time on an assignment between a gas meter and an hourly chromatograph GQ, and the Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option is checked. The GQ has following analysis records: |   | Effective Date | Effective End Date | Note | |:---:|:-----------------:|--------------------|:---------:| | A | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | \- | | B | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | Inhibited | | C | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | 1/1/2016 15:00:00 | \- | GQ analysis records are applied to the meter as follows: | Meter Periodic Record Effective Date | Applied Analysis | |:------------------------------------:|:----------------:| | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | A | | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | A | | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | C | Then this exception is generated on the meter periodic record at 1/1/2016 13:00:00.

65 Missing analysis

This exception is generated for a gas meter upon apply of a GQ source through an assignment. When setting up the assignment on the Quality Source Assignment editor (Setup \> Source Analysis \> Quality Source Assignment Viewer \> *select a gas meter and a record*), the Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option is unchecked. Upon analysis apply, if there is no analysis record on the assigned GQ that is applicable to a meter periodic record according to the Apply GQ At option on the Assignment editor, this exception is generated on the meter periodic record.  For example, the Apply GQ At option is set to Effective Date/Time on an assignment between a gas meter and an hourly chromatograph GQ, and the Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option is unchecked. The GQ has following analysis records: |   | Effective Date | Effective End Date | |:---:|:-----------------:|:------------------:| | A | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | | B | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | | C | 1/1/2016 15:00:00 | 1/1/2016 16:00:00 | The GQ analysis records are applied to the meter as follows: | Meter Periodic Record Effective Date | Applied Analysis | |:------------------------------------:|:----------------:| | 1/1/2016 12:00:00 | A | | 1/1/2016 13:00:00 | B | | 1/1/2016 14:00:00 | No Analysis | | 1/1/2016 15:00:00 | C | The exception is generated on the meter periodic record at 1/1/2016 14:00:00.

66 Percent/unit minimum exceeded

This exception has severity of 0 and hence disabled by default. Adjust the severity of this exception before use in the Exception Description Editor (Settings \> Settings Manager \> Exception Description). This exception is generated for a meter when the Calibration Adjustment Apply service applies a TESTit test report to a meter and the difference between the volume or energy values before and after the adjustment is greater than the values entered in the Min Cal Adj Pct field or the Min Cal Adj Unit Diff field for the test report in the Review Test Report editor (Tools \> Review Test Report). For example, for a test report, the Min Cal Adj Pct value is 1 and the Min Cal Adj Unit Diff is 1. Before the test report is applied to the meter, volume is 136.597 and energy is 147.917. After the test report is applied, the volume becomes 138.113 and the energy becomes 14403.377. Then the differences in volume and energy are as follows: |   | Percent Difference | Unit Difference | |:------:|:-----------------------------------------:|:-------------------------:| | Volume | (137.535 / 136.597 – 1) \* 100 = 0.6867 % | 137.535 – 136.597 = 0.938 | | Energy | (148.932 / 147.917 – 1) \* 100 = 0.6862 % | 148.932 – 147.917 = 1.015 | Percent differences for both volume energy are less than 1 % Min Cal Adj Pct value. Unit difference for volume is less than 1 Min Cal Adj Unit Diff, but the energy unit difference is greater than 1. Therefore this exception is generated.

67 Unable to close data (meter has unaccepted auto estimates)

This exception is generated when a meter cannot be closed because there is auto estimated data within the month that have not been accepted. The autoestimated data has to be accepted from the context menu in the Volume Editor, or by using the Toolbox before the month can be closed for the meter.

68 GPA 2172 - Incomplete analysis sample

This exception is generated on a gas meter with GPA 2172 adjustment enabled when a meter analysis record has the component total mole % that falls outside of the system limits set in System Factors (Admin \> System Options \> System Factors). For example, Component Totals \[Hi Limit\] is set to 100.10 and Component Totals \[Lo Limit\] is set to 99.90. A meter analysis record has the following component mole %: Since the total mole % is 99.88 which is less than the Lo Limit of 99.90, this exception is generated and the GPA 2172 adjustment does not go forward.

69 GPA 2172 - Failed to calculate relative density

This exception is generated on a gas meter with GPA 2172 adjustment enabled when relative density cannot be calculated due to HC Properties calculation failures. For example, if an error is experienced while loading the DLL for the HC Properties calculation, this exception would be generated.

70 No correlation factor; unable to apply source analysis

This exception is generated on a gas meter periodic record upon apply of a GQ source through an assignment. If the Recalc. Method on the assignment (Setup \> Source Analysis \> Quality Source Assignment Viewer) is set to Volume so that the analysis apply process would need VCF for calculation and a meter periodic record does not have a VCF, the recalculation process necessary to apply the source analysis cannot proceed and this exception is generated. For example, an assignment between an orifice meter and a GQ source is set up with Recalc. Method of Volume. User enters temperature and pressure data into a blank periodic record manually, expecting FLOWCAL to calculate volume using the assigned source analysis. The Recalc. option in the Volume Editor for the periodic record edit is set to Vol Use VCF. Since there is no VCF on this periodic record, the calculation does not go forward and this exception is generated.

71 No correlation factor; unable to calculate volume

This exception is generated on a gas meter periodic record when a calculation of the record takes place if the calculation process is configured to use VCF stored in the database for the record and the record does not have a VCF. For example, user enters temperature and pressure data into a blank periodic record and full analysis data into the associated meter analysis record manually, expecting FLOWCAL to calculate volume using the assigned source analysis. The Recalc. option in the Volume Editor for the periodic record edit is set to Vol Use VCF. Since there is no VCF on this periodic record, the calculation does not go forward and this exception is generated.  This exception only generates for gas meters configured with the AGA-3 2013 or AGA-7 calculation method.

72 Partially saturated sample has no H2O mol% or water content

This exception is generated on a gas meter with GPA 2172 adjustment enabled when a meter analysis record has no value for water mole % with the Flowing Gas Condition set to Partially Saturated @ Flowing Conditions on the GPA 2172 tab in the Volume Editor. If the Reporting Condition on the GPA 2172 tab is set to Dry, as the process continues, 0 will be calculated for water mole %, which resolves the exception.

73 Meter indicated volume exceeds line fill volume

This exception is generated during the import of a line fill liquid meter if the indicated volume on the import record is greater than the line fill volume set in the meter characteristic.

74 Unable to close meter (batches not finalized)

This exception is generated when an unfinalized batch is available when attempting to close, and the "Allow Preliminary Tickets" option is enabled. This option allows meters and tickets to be finalized before they are closed.

75 Number of periodic revisions has exceeded the limit specified

This exception is generated when the number of revisions to the Meter Periodic table exceeds a specified limit, in order to notify users of abnormally high numbers of record revisions. The default alarm limit is 20, but this can be altered using the revision_limit_meter_periodic FcDebugOption. To enable the FcDebugOption, paste the following into the FcDebugOption.cfg file and enter an alarm limit: revision_limit_meter_periodic = 20 Once a single periodic record exceeds the number of revisions specified, the exception will be generated.

76 Number of characteristic revisions has exceeded the limit specified

This exception is generated when the number of revisions to the Meter Characteristic table exceeds a specified limit, in order to notify users of abnormally high numbers of record revisions. The default alarm limit is 10, but this can be altered using the revision_limit_meter_characteristic FcDebugOption. To enable the FcDebugOption, paste the following into the FcDebugOption.cfg file and enter an alarm limit: revision_limit_meter_characteristic = 10 Once a single characteristic record exceeds the number of revisions specified, the exception will be generated.

77 Number of analysis revisions has exceeded the limit specified

This exception is generated when the number of revisions to the Meter Analysis table exceeds a specified limit, in order to notify users of abnormally high numbers of record revisions. The default alarm limit is 10, but this can be altered using the revision_limit_meter_analysis FcDebugOption. To enable the FcDebugOption, paste the following into the FcDebugOption.cfg file and enter an alarm limit: revision_limit_meter_analysis = 10 Once a single analysis record exceeds the number of revisions specified, the exception will be generated.

78 Unable to close data (meter has unprocessed live oil queue entries)

This exception is generated when a user attempts to close a dead oil or flash gas meter if there are unprocessed entries in the live oil queue for the given meter and close month. To close the meter, please wait for the entries to process.

79 Import meter number does not match FLOWCAL meter number

This exception is generated when the import service imports a CFX file that contains a meter number that does not match the meter it is mapped to. The effective date of the exception can be used to identify the CFX file with the mismatched meter number. This exception will not be generated for any manual import or for import formats other than CFX. This exception can only be set to Acknowledged or Pending; it will not be resolved automatically or by the user. The default severity is 0, which prevents the exception from generating.
Exception Directory

100 SV - Standard values

Standard values (SV) exceptions are related to the limits and constants that are defined in [System Factors](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Factors.md). FLOWCAL will generate SV exceptions to alert users if a constant is outside of a calculation range, or if the flow data is not within the limits defined at the system level.

103 SV - System constant base pressure out of range

This exception is generated when the pressure base identified in [System Factors](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Factors.md) is out of range. FLOWCAL checks that the system pressure base is within the range of 12–16.1 psi, converting for units when the pressure base unit is not in psi. Common reasons for this exception to be generated would be for the base pressure to be outside of the 12–16.1 psi range or the pressure base unit to be incorrect. You can check your pressure base unit in the Settings Manager under [Unit Assignment](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/Unit%20Assignment.md).

104 SV - System constant base temperature out of range

This exception is generated when the temperature base identified in [System Factors](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Factors.md) is out of range. FLOWCAL checks that the system pressure base is within a range of 50–70°F, converting for units when the temperature base unit is not in degrees F. Common reasons for this exception to be generated would be for the base temperature to be outside of the 50–70°F range or the temperature base unit to be incorrect. You can check your temperature base unit in the Settings Manager under [Unit Assignment](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/Unit%20Assignment.md).

105 SV - Analysis total less than system constant low limit

This exception is generated when the mol% total on a meter periodic record is lower than the limit set in Component Totals (Lo Limit) field in [System Factors](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Factors.md). For example: If the Component Totals (Lo Limit) is set to 99.90, but the analysis that is applied to a meter periodic totals to 98% for the mol% components, then this exception will be generated.

106 SV - Analysis total greater than system constant high limit

This exception is generated when the mol% total on a meter periodic record is higher than the limit set in Component Totals (Hi Limit) field in [System Factors](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Factors.md). For example: If the Component Totals (Hi Limit) is set to 100, but the analysis that is applied to a meter periodic totals to 100.01% for the mol% components, then this exception will be generated.
Exception Directory

201 Flow time too high for hourly record

This exception is generated for a gas or liquid orifice meter with hourly data resolution, when the flow time on an imported record is larger than the Pct. Flow in 1 Hour value set in [System Configuration](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration%20-%20General%20Tab.md#ExceptionValues). This exception is resolved for a no-flow record.

202 Flow time too high for daily record

This exception is generated for a gas or liquid orifice meter with daily data resolution when the flow time on an imported record is larger than the Pct. Flow in 1 Day value set in [System Configuration](../../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration%20-%20General%20Tab.md#ExceptionValues). This exception is resolved for a no-flow record.

203 Warning - Water vapor correction is applied to dehydrated gas (EFM)

This exception is generated when Water Vapor Correction Factor is set to be used in the Meter Characteristics; the Dehydrated Gas field is also set to "Yes"; and at least one of the Water Vapor Technique and the Water Vapor Method fields is null. This exception is generated upon saving such Characteristic record.

204 Warning - Water vapor correction is applied to dehydrated gas (FC)

This exception is generated when Water Vapor Correction Factor is set to be used in the Meter Characteristics; the Dehydrated Gas field is also set to "Yes"; and neither of the Water Vapor Technique and the Water Vapor Method fields is not null. This exception is generated upon saving such Characteristic record.

205 Differential = 0; volume = 0; flow time > 0

This exception is generated upon import of gas orifice or gas cone meter data, for periodic records that have differential pressure of 0 or less, volume of 0, and flow time (or flow %) that is non-null and greater than 0. This exception is resolved when the periodic record is saved with a flow time of 0, including a calculated flow time of 0.

206 Differential = 0; volume = 0; flow time not given

This exception is generated upon import of gas orifice or gas cone meter data, for periodic records that have 0 differential pressure, 0 volume, and null flow time (or flow %). This exception is resolved when the periodic record is saved with a flow time of 0, including a calculated flow time of 0. As FLOWCAL calculates flow time of 0 upon import of differential pressure and volume of 0, this exception is resolved when the periodic record is recalculated after import. This exception also gets resolved during the import process (status “RD”) if Flowing Parameters validations are enabled.

207 Prove overdue (operational time allowed between proves exceeded)

This exception is generated on periodic records if the time elapsed between the last prove date and the periodic record effective date is greater than the operational limit. When this validation is enabled, there must be manual prove adjustments applied to batches. To enable this validation, an operational limit for Maximum Time Between Proves must be configured for the meter on Contractual Limits. The operational limit configuration must be effective for the date of data being validated. For example, liquid meter PROVE_METER has two batches in August 2017 with effective dates 8/1/2017 7:00:00 and 8/15/2017 7:00:00. There is a contractual limit record for this meter with effective dates 1/1/2017 7:00:00-1/1/2018 7:00:00. On the contractual limit record, the operational limit for Maximum Time Between Proves is set to 15 (days). A prove adjustment is made to the 8/1/2017 batch with the prove date of 8/3/2017 09:17:44. Then, periodic records with effective date greater than 8/18/2017 9:17:44 are more than 15 days past the prove date. Hence exception 207 is generated for all periodic records starting on 8/18/2017 10:00:00.

208 Prove overdue (contractual time allowed between proves exceeded)

This exception is generated on periodic records if the time elapsed between the last prove date and the periodic record effective date is greater than the contractual limit. When this validation is enabled, there must be manual prove adjustments applied to batches. To enable this validation, a contractual limit for Maximum Time Between Proves must be configured for the meter on Contractual Limits. The contractual limit configuration must be effective for the date of data being validated. For example, liquid meter PROVE_METER has two batches in August 2017 with effective dates 8/1/2017 7:00:00 and 8/15/2017 7:00:00. There is a contractual limit record for this meter with effective dates 1/1/2017 7:00:00-1/1/2018 7:00:00. On the contractual limit record, the contractual limit for Maximum Time Between Proves is set to 15 (days). A prove adjustment is made to the 8/1/2017 batch with the prove date of 8/3/2017 09:17:44. Then, periodic records with effective date greater than 8/18/2017 9:17:44 are more than 15 days past the prove date. Hence exception 208 is generated for all periodic records starting on 8/18/2017 10:00:00.

209 Prove overdue (operational volume allowed between proves exceeded)

This exception is generated on periodic records if the volume accumulated since the prior prove until the periodic record effective date is greater than the operational limit. When this validation is enabled, there must be manual prove adjustments for batches. To enable this validation, an operational limit for Accumulated Vol Between Proves must be configured for the meter on Contractual Limits. The operational limit configuration must be effective for the date of data being validated. Totalizer Digits in the meter characteristics must be specified. The accumulated volume for the periodic record since the prior prove on the meter is calculated as (Indicated Volume Start Index for the periodic record - Current Index for the prove). If IV start index is less than the current index, the calculation takes Totalizer Digits into account for index rollover calculations. For example, liquid meter PROVE_METER has Totalizer Digits of 5. There are 2 batches in August 2017 with effective dates 8/1/2017 7:00:00 and 8/15/2017 7:00:00. There is a contractual limit record for this meter with effective dates 1/1/2017 7:00:00-1/1/2018 7:00:00. On the contractual limit record, the operational limit for Accumulated Vol Between Proves is set to 8000. A prove adjustment is made to the 8/1/2017 batch with the prove date of 8/1/2017 09:17:44 and current index of 305. Periodic record at 8/14/2017 17:00:00 has an Indicated Volume Start Index of 8424. The accumulated volume since prior prove for the periodic record is then calculated as 8424 – 305 = 8115. This is greater than the operational limit of 8000, so exception 209 is generated for the periodic record. Another prove adjustment is made to the 8/15/2017 batch with the prove date of 8/15/2017 8:44:21 and current index of 2503. Periodic record at 8/28/2017 23:00:00 has an Indicated Volume Start Index of 1229. The current index is smaller than the IV start index, so Totalizer Digits of 5 is used for the accumulated volume calculation which yields 10000 + 1229 - 2503 = 8726. This is greater than the operational limit of 8000, so exception 209 is generated for the periodic record.
Exception Directory

400 Operational meter factor variance limit exceeded

This exception is generated upon import of prove reports into FLOWCAL through PFX files when the prove data violates the Operational limit configured for Meter Factor Change Between Proves on Contractual Limits. To enable this validation, the Operational field for Meter Factor Change Between Proves must be populated. The operational limit configuration must be effective for the date of the batch the prove data is applied to. This exception is generated when the meter factor in the prove report is different from the existing meter factor for the batch date by more than the operational limit. This exception is generated for all batches the violating prove data was applied to. For example, liquid meter PROVE_METER has 4 weekly batches in August 2017 with effective dates 8/1/2017 7:00:00, 8/8/2017 7:00:00, 8/15/2017 7:00:00, and 8/22/2017 7:00:00. There is a contractual limit configuration for this meter with effective dates 1/1/2017 7:00:00-1/1/2018 7:00:00. On the contractual limit configuration, the operational limit for Meter Factor Change Between Proves is set to 0.0010. Before prove reports are imported for August, the meter factor is 0.9999 for all four August batches. Then 3 prove reports each dated 8/1/2017 10:35:22, 8/8/2017 09:14:53, and 8/15/2017 9:45:44 are imported and applied as follows: Batch Effective Date Existing MF Before PFX Import Updated MF After PFX Import MF Change Exception 400 Generated 8/1/2017 7:00:00 0.9999 0.9801 -0.0198 Yes 8/8/2017 7:00:00 0.9801 0.9803 0.0002 No 8/15/2017 7:00:00 0.9803 0.9975 0.0172 Yes 8/22/2017 7:00:00 0.9803 0.9975 0.0172 Yes

401 Contractual meter factor variance limit exceeded

This exception is generated upon import of prove reports into FLOWCAL through PFX files when the prove data violates the Contractual limit configured for Meter Factor Change Between Proves on Contractual Limits. To enable this validation, the Contractual field for Meter Factor Change Between Proves must be populated. The contractual limit configuration must be effective for the date of the batch the prove data is applied to. This exception is generated when the meter factor in the prove report is different from the existing meter factor for the batch date by more than the contractual limit. This exception is generated for all batches the violating prove data was applied to. For example, liquid meter PROVE_METER has 4 weekly batches in August 2017 with effective dates 8/1/2017 7:00:00, 8/8/2017 7:00:00, 8/15/2017 7:00:00, and 8/22/2017 7:00:00. There is a contractual limit configuration for this meter with effective dates 1/1/2017 7:00:00-1/1/2018 7:00:00. On the contractual limit configuration, the contractual limit for Meter Factor Change Between Proves is set to 0.0010. Before prove reports are imported for August, the meter factor is 0.9999 for all four August batches. Then 3 prove reports each dated 8/1/2017 10:35:22, 8/8/2017 09:14:53, and 8/15/2017 9:45:44 are imported and applied as follows: Batch Effective Date Existing MF Before PFX Import Updated MF After PFX Import MF Change Exception 400 Generated 8/1/2017 7:00:00 0.9999 0.9801 -0.0198 Yes 8/8/2017 7:00:00 0.9801 0.9803 0.0002 No 8/15/2017 7:00:00 0.9803 0.9975 0.0172 Yes 8/22/2017 7:00:00 0.9803 0.9975 0.0172 Yes

402 Invalid calculation method in import

This exception is generated upon meter data import if both the meter characteristic in effect and the configuration data being imported have NULL calculation method. The exception is generated for periodic records to which the violating characteristic record applies. For example, a gas meter has a characteristic record from 5/16/2017 12:00:00 to 9/1/2017 9:00:00 that has turbine meter type but NULL calculation method by mistake. A CFX file with configuration data enabled and periodic records dated 6/1/2017 9:00:00 and 7/1/2017 9:00:00 are imported. The configuration section of the CFX file has NULL for calculation method. When the import is done and data is saved, a characteristic record is split at 6/1/2017 9:00:00 that has NULL calculation method. Exception 402 is generated for 6/1/2017 9:00:00 and 7/1/2017 9:00:00 periodic records as the 6/1/2017 9:00:00 characteristic record applies to periodic records.
Exception Directory

1000 - Calculation validation

Calculation validation (CV) exceptions will be generated when a data point needed for calculations is either not provided or goes outside of the acceptable limits for a calculation to occur. These limits are hard-coded within FLOWCAL.

1001 CV - Static pressure not given

This exception applies to imported and edited gas flow data. Before performing calculations, FLOWCAL will validate that the data needed for calculations to occur is provided and valid. If a non-zero DP or pulses value is given but static pressure is not provided, this exception will be generated. 1042 CV - Differential > 0 but no volume

The cutoff limit for Differential Pressure is defined using the following precedence: - Cutoff limit defined on the Ranges tab in Meter Characteristics - Low Flow Cut-Off defined in System Configuration - 0.00001 For example, with the cutoff limits within FLOWCAL defined as follows: - Meter Characteristics Cutoff = 0.75 - System Configuration Low Flow Cut-Off = 0.5 A Gas Orifice periodic record imported with a Volume of 0 and a Differential Pressure of 0.6 will not generate this exception because the Differential Pressure is lower than the Meter Characteristics Cutoff. 1048 CV - Calculated raw volume does not match expected raw volume (Type P)

This exception applies to imported and edited Gas Flow Data using a Calculation Method of AGA-7 or Line Pack. For meters configured with a Calculation Method of AGA-7, this exception will generate when the absolute value of the difference between the provided Raw Volume and the FLOWCAL calculated Raw Volume (\|provided Raw Volume – calculated Raw Volume\|) is greater than the maximum difference allowed. The maximum difference allowed is as follows: | Provided Raw Volume | Maximum Difference Allowed | |:-------------------:|:--------------------------:| | \< 100 | 2 | | \< 1000 | 20 | | \< 10000 | 200 | | \> 10000 | 500 | For example, a Gas Turbine is configured with a Calculation Method of AGA-7 and periodic record is created with Pulses = 1000, K Factor = 1, and Raw Volume = 1050. The FLOWCAL calculated Raw Volume = 1000 (Pulses / K Factor). The maximum difference allowed is 200 because the provided Raw Volume is greater than 1000 but less than 10000. The absolute value of the difference is 50 (\|1050-1000\|), which is less than the maximum difference allowed, so this exception will not be generated. However, if the K Factor was imported as 10, then the FLOWCAL calculated Raw Volume = 100 (Pulses / K Factor). The absolute value of the difference is 950 (\|1050-100\|), which is greater than the maximum difference allowed, so this exception will be generated. For meters configured with a Calculation Method of Line Pack, this exception will generate when the Percent Difference between the provided Raw Volume and the FLOWCAL calculated Raw Volume exceeds the Max Deviation on the Validations \> Flowing Parameters tab in the Meter Editor. The Max Deviation Type must be set to Percent. Percent Difference is calculated as: \|Calculated Raw Volume – Provided Raw Volume\| / Provided Raw Volume For example, a Line Pack Meter has the Max Deviation set to 10 Percent in the Meter Editor and is configured with a Pipe Diameter of 24 Inches and Pipe Length of 28 Miles. The FLOWCAL calculated Raw Volume ≈ 464 MCF (V = π\*r\*h\*unit conversions). A record is created that has Raw Volume = 550. The Percent Difference ≈ 15.6%, which is greater than the Max Deviation, so this exception will be generated.

1049 CV - Pipe length too small

The Max Deviation Type must be set to Unit. Unit Difference is calculated as: \|Calculated Raw Volume – Provided Raw Volume\| For example, a Line Pack Meter has the Max Deviation set to 10 Units in the Meter Editor and is configured with a Pipe Diameter of 24 Inches and Pipe Length of 28 Miles. The FLOWCAL calculated Raw Volume ≈ 464 MCF (V = π\*r\*h\*unit conversions). A record is created that has Raw Volume = 500. 1111 CV - Observed density does not equal uncorrected time DMF

This exception applies to imported and edited Liquid Meter and Ticket Data. When the “Observed Density Tolerance” option is defined in System Configuration, FLOWCAL will compare the provided Observed Density to the FLOWCAL calculated Observed Density using the provided Uncorrected Density and DMF. If the difference between the provided Observed Density and FLOWCAL calculated Observed Density is greater than the Observed Density Tolerance defined in the FLOWCAL Options, then this exception will be generated. For example, the Observed Density Tolerance is set to 0.0001 and a Meter Ticket is created that has an Uncorrected Density of 0.5050 REL, Observed Density = 0.5050, and DMF of 1.0005. The FLOWCAL Calculated Observed Density is 0.5052525 REL (0.5050\*1.0005). The difference between the provided and FLOWCAL calculated is 0.0002525, which is greater than the Observed Density Tolerance so this exception will be generated.

1112 CV - Pressure compensated (CPL is not equal to 1.0 on file import)

This exception applies to imported Liquid Meter and Ticket Data. For Meters, if the meter is configured with Pressure Compensated set to Yes in Meter Characteristics, or the import file has Pressure Compensated = Y, and a CPL value other than 1 is imported, then this exception will be generated. For Tickets, if the import file has Pressure Compensated = Y and a CPL value other than 1 is imported, then this exception will be generated. For example, a TFX file containing a Meter Ticket is imported with Pressure Compensated = Y and CPL = 1.0062. Calculations will assume a CPL value of 1 and this exception will be generated to alert the user.

1113 CV - Temperature compensated (CTL is not equal to 1.0 on file import)

This exception applies to imported Liquid Meter and Ticket Data. For Meters, if the meter is configured with Temperature Compensated set to Yes in Meter Characteristics, or the import file has Temperature Compensated = Y, and a CTL value other than 1 is imported, then this exception will be generated. For Tickets, if the import file has Temperature Compensated = Y and a CTL value other than 1 is imported, then this exception will be generated. 1121 CV – DPY not available on import for AGA-3 2013 with API 21.1 (2013)

This exception is generated upon import for a gas orifice meter with calculation method set to AGA-3 2013 and DP usage set to API 21.1 (2013). DPY can be imported using the CFX format. If a flow data periodic record imported into an applicable meter does not include DPY value, this exception is generated. This exception gets resolved when DPY is calculated and is not null anymore.

1122 CV – DPY undefined; unable to perform Y-factor calculation

This exception is generated for a gas orifice meter with calculation method set to AGA3-2013 and DP usage set to API 21.1 (2013) upon import or edit, when calculation is triggered. Cutoff alarm limit is not defined. API 21.1 (2013) calculation uses DPY to calculate expansion factor (Y). If DPY is not defined so that calculation is not able to calculate a Y factor, this exception is generated. This exception is also generated when DPY is calculated to be less than 0. If DPY is calculated to be less than 0, DPY is not stored or displayed, and no further calculation takes place. This exception gets resolved when DPY is a positive value. For example, a meter is set with AGA-3 2013 calculation method and API 21.1 (2013) DP usage. The pressure is absolute pressure. The extension definition is SQRT(DP\*P). From the EFM, following flow parameters are imported: - DP: 0.210326 inches of water - P: 485.34 psia - T: 74.06 °F - Flow time: 3456 seconds - Extension: 21.7863 Then DPIV is calculated to be 0.97795 … inches of water. Using the DP and DPIV value, DPY calculation is then attempted, and the result is -0.16694 … inches of water. This negative value is not valid as DPY. Therefore, the exception 1122 is generated and calculation is stopped.

1123 CV – Unable to calculate DPY; DPIV undefined or below cutoff, DP above cutoff

This exception is generated for a gas orifice meter with calculation method set to AGA-3 2013 and DP usage set to API 21.1 (2013) upon import or edit, when calculation is triggered. Cutoff alarm limit is defined. API 21.1 (2013) calculation calculates DPY from DP and DPIV. If DP is valid and above cutoff alarm limit and DPIV is null for any reason, or if DP is valid and above cutoff, and DPIV is less than cutoff alarm limit, no further calculation takes place and DPY is not calculated. For example, a meter is set with AGA-3 2013 calculation method and API 21.1 (2013) DP usage. The pressure is absolute pressure. The extension definition is SQRT(DP\*P). Cutoff alarm limit is 0.40 inches of water. From the EFM, following flow parameters are imported: - DP: 49.785 inches of water - P: 485.34 psia - T: 74.06 °F - Flow time: 3456 seconds - Extension: 9.5873 Then DPIV is calculated to be 0.18938 … inches of water. DP of 48.785 inches of water is above the cutoff alarm limit of 0.40 inches of water. However, DPIV of 0.1894 inches of water is below the cutoff alarm limit. Therefore, the exception 1123 is generated and calculation is stopped.

1124 CV – Unable to calculate DPY; DP is undefined

This exception is generated for a gas orifice meter with calculation method set to AGA-3 2013 and DP usage set to API 21.1 (2013) upon import or edit, when calculation is triggered. API 21.1 (2013) calculation calculates DPY from DP. If no value is provided for DP, calculation cannot take place and this exception is generated.

1125 CV – DP is below the back flow limit

This exception is generated for a gas orifice meter with calculation method set to AGA-3 2013 and DP usage set to API 21.1 (2013) upon import or edit, when calculation is triggered. Back flow alarm limit is defined. This exception is generated if DP is less than the back flow alarm limit. This does not stop the calculation.

docs.text: These exceptions are part of the Scheduled Movement Reconciliation add-on.

docs.title:
1401 - SMR - Schedule not found for batch

A scheduled movement could not be found for the meter batch. If a meter is configured to Reconcile Volume (Meter Editor \> Liquids tab \> Setup sub-tab), each batch must have a corresponding scheduled movement. This exception will auto-resolve if the batch is later matched to a new or updated schedule.

1402 - SMR - Sum of matched batches exceeds scheduled quantity

When a batch is matched to a schedule, a check is made to determine if the scheduled quantity, plus a tolerance amount, has been exceeded by the sum of all currently matched batches. This exception indicates that the sum of the currently matched batched exceed the scheduled amount. This exception will not auto-resolve.

1800 QRC - Quality radical change

Quality Radical Change exceptions are related to the limits that are defined in the Quality Source Validations (Setup \> Source Analysis \> Gas/Liquid Quality) for both Gas and Liquid Sources. FLOWCAL will compare the specified sample values to the prior sample values. If the value changes by more than the limit that the user defines, then an exception will be generated.

1801 QRC - High relative density

FLOWCAL will compare the Relative Density on the current sample to the Relative Density on the prior sample. An exception will be generated if the Relative Density has increased by more than the limit defined in the Radical Change validation for Relative Density. For example, the current sample has a Relative Density value of 0.6. The limit defined in Radical Change validation for Relative is 0.01. If the prior sample’s Relative Density is less than 0.59, then this exception will be generated.

1999 Single run validation

Single Run Validation exceptions are related to the limits that are defined in the Meter Editor (Set-Up -\> Meter -\> Editor) for both Gas and Liquid Sources. Meter Single Run validations allow the user to specify whether to look for excessive variations, to compare the current record to the previous record or previous day, to compare using percentage or unit difference, when to compare, and minimum and maximum limits for each value, which serves as a tolerance level within which values will be treated as having excessive variation.

This exception is only generated when an Audit is setup on a meter. The exception will be generated when the Audit/Sales meter is missing Volume data for 30-59 days. 11419 TKT - Low level

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users if the imported or manually entered value is below the minimum level limit. If the Tank Level Fill % Required flag is checked and a minimum level is specified in the Ticket Validation Template Editor, this exception will be generated when the level falls below the specified minimum limit. The tank level units specified in the [Tank Configuration \> Units & Options tab](../../../Tank%20Editor/Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Units-Options%20Tab.md) are the units that are used for this validation. Examples **Example 1:** - Tank level unit: Inches - Tank level minimum: 15 A gauge ticket is entered with a level of 2’ 0”. Because the tank level unit is inches, the gauge ticket is converted to 24 inches. This exceeds the tank level minimum of 15, so the exception is not generated. **Example 2:** - Tank level unit: Feet - Tank level minimum: 15 A gauge ticket is entered with a level of 2’ 6”. Because the tank level unit is feet, the gauge ticket is converted to 2.5 feet. This is below the tank level minimum of 15, so the exception is generated. Only the Gauge ticket type is associated with this exception.

11420 TKT - High level

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users if the imported or manually entered value is above the user-defined maximum level limit. If the Tank Level Fill % Required flag is checked and a maximum level is specified in the Ticket Validation Template Editor, this exception will be generated when the level exceeds the specified maximum limit. The tank level units specified in the [Tank Configuration \> Units & Options tab](../../../Tank%20Editor/Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Units-Options%20Tab.md) are the units that are used for this validation. Examples **Example 1:** - Tank level unit: Inches - Tank level maximum: 15 A gauge ticket is entered with a level of 2’ 0”. Because the tank level unit is inches, the gauge ticket is converted to 24 inches. This exceeds the tank level maximum of 15, so the exception is generated. **Example 2:** - Tank level unit: Feet - Tank level minimum: 15 A gauge ticket is entered with a level of 2’ 6”. Because the tank level unit is feet, the gauge ticket is converted to 2.5 feet. This is below the tank level maximum of 15, so the exception is not generated. Only the Gauge ticket type is associated with this exception.

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. If the Free Water Fill % Required flag is checked and a minimum level is specified in the Ticket Validation Template Editor, this exception will be generated when the level falls below the specified minimum limit. The tank level units specified in the [Tank Configuration \> Units & Options tab](../../../Tank%20Editor/Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Units-Options%20Tab.md) are the units that are used for this validation. Examples **Example 1:** - Tank level unit: Inches - Free Water Fill % Min: 2 A gauge ticket is entered with a free water level of 1’ 0”. Because the tank level unit is inches, the free water level is converted to 12 inches. This exceeds the free water fill % level minimum of 2, so the exception is not generated. **Example 2:** - Tank level unit: Feet - Free Water Fill % Min: 2 A gauge ticket is entered with a free water level of 1’ 6”. Because the tank level unit is feet, the free water level is converted to 1.5 feet. This is below the free water fill % level minimum of 2, so the exception is generated. Only the Gauge ticket type is associated with this exception.

11477 TKT - High movement level change

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tank run tickets. This exception notifies users that the change in level from open to close is above the user-defined maximum movement level change limit. If the level change is specified in the Ticket Validation Template Editor, this exception will be generated when the level change exceeds the specified limit. The tank level units specified in the [Tank Configuration \> Units & Options tab](../../../Tank%20Editor/Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Units-Options%20Tab.md) are the units that are used for this validation. Examples **Example 1:** - Tank level unit: Inches - Level change: 5 An open level of 0' 6" and a close level of 3' 0" are entered. Because the tank level unit is inches, the movement change is calculated as: 36" - 6" = 30". This result exceeds the level change limit of 5, so the exception is generated. **Example 2:** - Tank level unit: Feet - Level change: 5 An open level of 0' 6" and a close level of 3' 0" are entered. Because the tank level unit is feet, the movement change is calculated as: 3' - .5' = 2.5'. This result is below the level change limit of 5, so the exception is not generated. Only the Tank Run ticket type is associated with this exception.

11801 TKT - Observed EVP percent difference exceeded

This exception is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users that the imported or manually entered value differs from the calculated observed EVP value by more than the user-defined limit for observed EVP percent difference.

11802 TKT - Meter EVP percent difference exceeded

This exception is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users that the imported or manually entered value differs from the calculated meter EVP value by more than the user-defined limit for EVP percent difference.

This exception is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users that the imported or manually entered value has exceeded the user-defined limit for CTL percent difference.

11804 TKT - CPL percent difference exceeded

This exception is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users that the imported or manually entered value has exceeded the user-defined limit for CPL percent difference.

11805 TKT - CTPL percent difference exceeded

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users that the imported or manually entered value has exceeded the user-defined limit for CTPL percent difference. The ticket types associated with this exception are: Gauge, Run, and Vessel Tank.

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. 11855 TKT - Current seal off does not match previous seal on
