This exception notifies users that the imported or manually entered value for the current seal off does not match previous seal on. The ticket types associated with this exception are: Gauge, Run, and Vessel Tank.

11856 TKT - Current seal 2 off does not match previous seal 2 on

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users that the imported or manually entered value for the current seal 2 off does not match previous seal 2 on. The ticket types associated with this exception are: Gauge, Run, and Vessel Tank.

11857 TKT - New open level is not within tolerance of prior close level

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users if the imported or manually entered value is not within tolerance of the prior close level. If the Tank Level Tolerance is defined in the Ticket Validation Template Editor, then this exception will be generated when the tolerance between new open level and prior close level exceeds the limit specified in the "Level Tolerance" field. The tank level units specified in the [Tank Configuration \> Units & Options tab](../../../Tank%20Editor/Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Units-Options%20Tab.md) are the units that are used for this validation. Examples **Example 1:** - Tank level unit: Inches - Level tolerance: 6 The prior run ticket close level is set to 10’ 0” and the new run ticket open level is entered as 12’ 0”. The difference between the prior close level and the open level is 2’ 0”. Since the tank level units are in inches, the difference is converted to 24 inches. This is above the level tolerance of 6, so the exception is generated. **Example 2:** - Tank level unit: Feet - Level tolerance: 6 The prior run ticket close level is set to 10’ 0” and the new run ticket open level is entered as 12’ 0” The difference between the prior close level and the open level is 2’ 0”. Since the tank’s level units are in feet, the difference is converted to 2 feet. This is below the Level Tolerance of 6, so the exception is not generated. Only the Tank Run ticket type is associated with this exception.

11858 TKT - New gauge level is not within tolerance of prior gauge level

This exception is a user-defined exception in the Ticket Validation Template Editor and is generated on import and edit of tickets. This exception notifies users if the imported or manually entered value is not within tolerance of the prior gauge level. If the Tank Level Tolerance is defined in the Ticket Validation Template Editor, then this exception will be generated when the tolerance between new gauge level and prior gauge level exceeds the limit specified in the "Level Tolerance" field. The tank level units specified in the Tank Configuration \> Units & Options tab are the units that are used for this validation. Examples Example 1: - Tank level unit: Inches - Level tolerance: 6 The prior gauge ticket level is set to 10’ 0” and the new run ticket open level is entered as 12’ 0”. The difference between the prior gauge level and the new gauge level is 2’ 0”. Since the tank level units are in inches, the difference is converted to 24 inches. This is above the level tolerance of 6, so the exception is generated. Example 2: - Tank level unit: Feet - Level tolerance: 6 The gauge ticket level is set to 10’ 0” and the new gauge ticket level is entered as 12’ 0”. The difference between the prior close level and the open level is 2’ 0”. Since the tank’s level units are in feet, the difference is converted to 2 feet. This is below the Level Tolerance of 6, so the exception is not generated. Only the Gauge ticket type is associated with this exception.

11859 TKT – Level is below leg height

This gauge ticket exception is generated when the gauge level in a floating roof tank is lower than the floating roof leg height in the capacity table. When this happens, it indicates that the product level is in or below the critical zone and FRA should be 0. Floating roof leg height must be set in order to generate the exception.

11860 TKT – Open level is below leg height

This tank run ticket exception is generated when the open level in a floating roof tank is lower than the floating roof leg height in the capacity table. When this happens, it indicates that the open level is in or below the critical zone and FRA should be 0. Floating roof leg height must be set in order to generate the exception.

11861 TKT – Close level is below leg height

This tank run ticket exception is generated when the close level in a floating roof tank is lower than the floating roof leg height in the capacity table. When this happens, it indicates that the close level is in or below the critical zone and FRA should be 0. Floating roof leg height must be set in order to generate the exception.

11862 TKT - Ticket location is not an inventory (line pack ticket)

This exception is generated on import of line pack meter tickets. The exception notifies the user that the location the ticket is attached to is not an inventory location as is required.

11863 TKT - Ticket direction is not an outlet (line pack ticket)

This exception is generated on import of line pack meter tickets. The exception notifies the user that the ticket direction is something other than outlet.

docs.title: Exception Directory

15201 Source apply conversion not possible (heating value condition)

This validation and exception applies on sample apply from a GQ Source to gas meter data. This exception will be generated if: - The Heating Value Saturation on the GQ Source Assignment is set to Meter Condition, but neither the Heating Value Saturation on the Meter Analysis or the EFM Heat Value Condition for GPA 2172 is set on the Meter. - The Heating Value Saturation on the GQ Source Assignment is set to As Delivered, but the BTU Base on the Sample that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply is a value other than As Delivered (Wet, Dry, etc.).

15202 Source apply conversion not possible (pressure base)

**For Gas Meter Data or Gas Loss Tickets:** If a sample that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply to a record has a Pressure Base less than or equal to 0, or is empty, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated. **For Liquid Meter Data or Tickets:** If the sample apply is configured to apply density and the sample that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply to a record has a Pressure Base less than or equal to 0, or is empty, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated.

15203 Source apply conversion not possible (heating value)

This validation and exception applies on sample apply from a GQ Source to gas meter data or a gas loss ticket. If a sample that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply to gas meter data or a gas loss ticket has a Heating Value less than or equal to 0, or is empty, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated.

15204 Source apply not possible (products do not match)

This validation and exception applies on sample apply from a GQ Source to gas meter data or a gas loss ticket. If a sample that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply has a Product defined, FLOWCAL will validate that the sample and record have the same Product before applying the sample. If the Products are different, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated. For example, if the sample has a Product of “Propane”, but the ticket that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply the sample to has a Product of “Ethane”, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated.

15205 Source apply not possible (temperature base)

For Gas Meter Data or Gas Loss Tickets: If a sample that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply to a record has a Temperature Base less than or equal to 0, or is empty, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated. For Liquid Meter Data or Tickets: If the sample apply is configured to apply density and the sample that FLOWCAL is attempting to apply to a record has a Temperature Base less than or equal to 0, or is empty, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated.

15206 Source apply not possible (unit set discrepancy)

**For Gas Meter Data or Gas Loss Tickets:** FLOWCAL will compare the Pressure Base Unit and Temperature Base Unit on the sample to the Pressure Base Unit and Temperature Base Unit on the record. If either of the unit values is different, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated. **For Liquid Meter Data or Tickets:** If the sample apply is configured to apply density, FLOWCAL will compare the Pressure Base, Pressure Base Unit, Temperature Base, and Temperature Base Unit on the sample to the Pressure Base, Pressure Base Unit, Temperature Base, and Temperature Base Unit on the record. If any of the values are different, then the sample will not apply and this exception will be generated. The units for Tickets will be pulled from the System units for the System that the Location on the Ticket is a member of. If the Gas Loss Ticket does not have a Location set, then the units will be pulled from the System units for the Default System. FLOWCAL currently supports the following units for US and SI units for the temperature and pressure base: - US Units: - Pressure Base: PSIA - Temperature Base: Fahrenheit - SI Units: - Pressure Base: Kilopascal and Bar - Temperature Base: Celsius

15207 Density values not copied to meter analysis (unit set discrepancy); only sample percentages copied

This exception is generated when there's a discrepancy between sample unit and liquid meter/ticket data unit. For example, if the pressure base unit in the sample is psi, and temperature base unit is Fahrenheit, but the meter has kilopascal and Celsius, respectively, then this exception will be generated when attempting to apply the sample.
15208 Measured HV not pressure base adjusted (unit set discrepancy) (deprecated)

15209 Source calculation not possible (unit set discrepancy)

This validation and exception applies on Gas Meter data for meters that have the Quality Calculations enabled on the Calculations \> Quality sub-tab in the Meter Editor. When attempting to perform a quality calculation on meter analysis data, FLOWCAL will compare the units for Pressure Base, Temperature Base, Heating Value, and Mass Heating Value on the meter characteristic to the units on the HC Properties tied to that meter. If any of the unit values differ, then quality calculations will not be performed and this exception will be generated. For gas meters configured to use GQ Calc at the meter level. FLOWCAL will compare units for Pressure Base, Temperature Base, HV, and Mass HV. If any differ, this exception should be generated. FLOWCAL currently supports the following units for US and SI units for the mentioned data points: - US Units: - Pressure Base: PSIA - Temperature Base: Fahrenheit - Heating Value: BTU/scf - Mass Heating Value: BTU/Lbm - SI Units: - Pressure Base: Kilopascal - Temperature Base: Celsius - Heating Value: MegaJoule/Cubic Meter - Mass Heating Value: MegaJoule/Kg

15210 Source apply - Density selected by user not applied; fallback density used

This validation and exception applies on sample apply from a LQ Source or Standalone Sample to liquid meter data or a ticket. If the sample apply is configured to apply density, but the density chosen to apply is not found on the sample, then FLOWCAL will use the next available density on the sample and this exception will be generated. For example, a sample has a value provided for Relative Density, but not API Gravity. The sample is configured to apply to a ticket with the Apply Density Option set to API Gravity. Since API Gravity is not available on the sample, FLOWCAL will fail over to applying the Relative Density from the sample and generate this exception. The density apply will fail over to using a sample density value in the order depicted in the table below. | Apply Density Option | 1st Failover | 2nd Failover | |:---------------------|:-----------------|:-----------------| | Relative Density | API Gravity | Absolute Density | | API Gravity | Relative Density | Absolute Density | | Absolute Density | Relative Density | API Gravity |

15211 Source apply - Fallback density not applied

This validation and exception applies on sample apply from a LQ Source or Standalone Sample to liquid meter data or a ticket. If the sample apply is configured to apply density, but no density values are found on the sample, then FLOWCAL will not apply a density from the sample and this exception will be generated. For example, a sample has no value provided for Relative Density, API Gravity, or Absolute Density. The sample is configured to apply to a ticket with the Apply Density Option set to API Gravity. Since API Gravity is not available on the sample, FLOWCAL will attempt to fail over to applying the Relative Density or Absolute Density from the sample. Since values are not available for these densities on the sample either, FLOWCAL will not apply a density from the sample and this exception will be generated.

15212 Source Apply conversion not possible (standard heating value)

If Flowing Gas Condition is left blank on the GPA 2172 tab in the Volume Editor, FLOWCAL will calculate a standard heating value using a conversion factor to account for going from one heating value condition on the meter such as Dry to a different heating value condition at the system level such as Wet when applying an assigned source. When FLOWCAL attempts to apply the assigned source to the gas meter data, if FLOWCAL cannot apply a conversion factor to account for this, such as going from Dry to Partially Saturated, then the standard heating value will not be calculated and this exception will be generated. To resolve exception 15212, set the Flowing Gas Condition field on the GPA 2172 tab in the Volume Editor to allow the GPA 2172 method to calculate the standard heating value or adjust the meter heating value saturation and/or source assignment to match the system heating value condition.

15213 Source apply not possible (missing sample pressure or temperature)

This exception is generated if a sample density is selected for the liquid assignment option "Apply Density" and if either the sample pressure or sample temperature is not provided on the applied analysis. Both are required as well as the pressure gauge/absolute indicator and atmospheric pressure.

16000 TRANS - Transactions

This exception is a Header exception and will not be generated by FLOWCAL. This group of exceptions has to do with the Transaction Service and potential issues around the import of data via the Transaction Service.

16001 TRANS - Meter was automatically created by transaction processing

This exception is generated when importing a .sql file via the Transaction Service into a FLOWCAL database, and the meter being imported does not exist on the FLOWCAL database.  For the auto-creation to occur, the Service Configuration Option, in the Transaction Queue Options group box, must be enabled for Auto Create Meters. This exception is to let the user know that the meter was automatically created.
16002 TRANS - History older than (deprecated)

16003 TRANS - Duplicate history effective date with new data

This exception is generated when a Transaction Queue record is imported for an effective date, and another record with different data is imported on the same meter for the same effective date. In this case FLOWCAL will increment the second imported record by 1 second and both records will be displayed in the Volume editor. Users may see this, for example, if they did not take into account Daylight Savings Time within FLOWCAL and allowed two records to be imported in the Fall when time changes.   Another example, would be when a user resets time on a Flow Computer.  It is 9:07am on the Flow Computer and a user realizes it’s really 8:57am so they set the time back to 8:57am on the Flow Computer. This would cause two 9am records to be imported and would also generate this exception.

16004 TRANS - Automatically replaced auto estimated data with original

This exception is generated when a Transaction Queue record is imported over auto estimated data. This is to let the user know that that auto estimate service has been overwritten.

16005 TRANS - Inactive meter

This exception is generated when a Transaction Queue record is imported on to an Inactive Meter.

16006 TRANS - Disconnected meter

This exception is generated when a Transaction Queue record is imported on to a Disconnected Meter.

16007 TRANS - Late import of char/analysis caused recalc of original correlation factor (ignore only)

Generated by Transaction Queue service imports. If an event or configuration record is received that when applied is applied to a time frame that has existing imported periodic data, the revision 0 correlation factors for all imported records will be recalculated based on the updated meter configuration. (Liquid TQ only.)

16008 TRANS - Late import of char/analysis caused recalc of revised correlation factor (ignore only)

Generated by Transaction Queue service imports. If an event or configuration record is received that when applied is applied to a time frame that has existing periodic data, the correlation factors for all imported records for the most current revision will be recalculated based on the updated meter configuration. (Liquid TQ only.)

17000 EXTVOL - External volume

This is a header exception; it is never generated in FLOWCAL. These exceptions primarily address text file imports and meter status.

17001 EXTVOL - Meter was automatically created by external volume import

This exception is generated when importing a Meter Text File into a FLOWCAL database, and a Meter within the Text File does not exist on the FLOWCAL database.  For the auto-creation to occur, the Service Configuration Option in the Text File Import group box must be set to Auto Create for Meters. This exception is to let the user know that the meter was automatically created.

17002 EXTVOL - Replaced previous data

This exception is generated when importing a Meter Text File into a FLOWCAL database, and Revision 0 exists for the meter. This newly imported data will replace the Revision 0 data that was originally there.

17003 EXTVOL - Inactive meter

This exception is generated when data is imported or manually entered into a meter where the status of the meter is Inactive. This is set in Meter Characteristics in the Operations tab and can be manually changed to Active (if desired) to resolve the exception. Often this is falsely generated because the meter is set to Inactive on the CFX File (when it should not be). Users would need to get in contact with their Measurement Manager to update the Flow Computer settings so this status comes in properly.

17004 EXTVOL - Disconnected meter

This exception is generated when data is imported or manually entered into a meter where the status of the meter is Disconnected. This is set in Meter Characteristics in the Operations tab and can be manually changed to Active (if desired) to resolve the exception. Often this is falsely generated because the meter is set to Disconnected on the CFX File (when it should not be). Users would need to get in contact with their Measurement Manager to update the Flow Computer settings so this status comes in properly.

17005 EXTVOL - Record rejected due to import rule

This exception is generated when a user has set up an Import Rule in the Import Rule Editor. In the Import Rule Editor, user may create rules to reject the import of specific periodic records. Users may then apply these rules to a specific meter via the Meter Editor (Imports tab; Conditional Import Rules). If the Import rule prevents any records from being successfully imported, then the exception will be generated to let the user know their record was attempted to be imported, but was prevented by the import rule set on the meter.

17006 EXTVOL - Meter has no flow computer assigned for product mapping/cross reference

This exception is generated when a file is imported into a Meter, and has the Flow Computer Mapping set to Yes in the Meter Editor, Imports Tab. However, there is not a Flow Computer mapping setup for the meter in the Flow Computer Editor.

17007 EXTVOL - Assigned flow computer ID is different than ID in CFX file

This exception is generated when the Computer ID on the CFX file that was generated is different than the Computer ID that was input into the Flow Computer Editor. For this exception to have been generated, a user would have to create a Flow Computer via the Flow Computer Editor and map products to the index associated with the Flow Computer. Then the user would have to assign the Flow Computer to a Meter via the Meter Editor, Imports tab. Once that is done, the Computer ID that is generated on the CFX file must then not match the Number on the Flow Computer in the Flow Computer Editor.

17008 EXTVOL - CFX product number/code must be between 1 and 32

This exception is generated when the Product Number/Code on the CFX file that was generated is not between 1 to 32. For this exception to have been generated, a user would have to create a Flow Computer via the Flow Computer Editor and map products to the index associated with the Flow Computer. Then the user would have to assign the Flow Computer to a Meter via the Meter Editor, Imports tab.

17009 EXTVOL - CFX product number/code is not mapped to flow computer

This exception is generated when the Flow Computer ID matches the Flow Computer in FLOWCAL but the product mapping set in the Flow Computer editor does NOT match. To resolve this exception, it would be ideal to add the mapping to the Flow Computer in the Flow Computer Editor so future imports with that product will come in easily.

17010 EXTVOL - Nonexistent meter

This exception is generated when data is imported or manually entered into a meter where the status of the meter is Nonexistent. This is set in Meter Characteristics in the Operations tab and can be manually changed to Active (if desired) to resolve the exception. Often this is falsely generated because the meter is set to Nonexistent on the CFX File (when it should not be). Users would need to get in contact with their Measurement Manager to update the Flow Computer settings so this status comes in properly.

17011 EXTVOL - Batch split due to product change

This exception occurs when a product is imported into a batch time frame that contained another product. For example, if a meter had a Product of Propane for all of August 2016 and a product of Ethane was imported on to that meter, because FLOWCAL cannot have two products for one batch, a batch split will occur. This exception lets the user know that this has occurred.

18125 FFRC - COSTALD density variation

This exception is generated for a batch on a liquid meter that uses a COSTALD product. The meter needs to have the Density Variance value of analysis validation set, and the analysis validations enabled (Run on Imports and Edits: Yes). If the batch’s average observed density calculated from the periodic data varies from the COSTALD density calculated based on the batch temperature, pressure, and analysis by more than the density variance limit, this exception is generated. For example, the Density Variance limit is set as 1% for a meter that uses a COSTALD product. FLOWCAL has observed density of 0.600000023841858 REL for a batch that has observed temperature of 77°F, observed pressure of 500 psi, and 100% propane. The COSTALD density is calculated to be approximately 0.501218048561296 REL for the flow parameters and analysis. The difference between the observed density and the COSTALD density is: (0.600000023841858 – 0.501218048561296) / 0.600000023841858 \* 100% = 16.4636619% Since this is greater than the 1% limit, exception 18125 is generated for the batch.

18126 FFRC - Location hourly volume variance failure

This exception is generated by the Location Rollup service when Adjusted Total Volume in the measured unit on an hourly location Final Form record varies from the average of previous records by more than the limit set in the Final Form Expert Systems validation configuration in the Location Validations Editor. For example, in the Location Validations Editor Expert Systems tab, Volume/Energy is set to Measured; Expert Systems validation is enabled; and the Averaging Method is set to Running. 18201 LQA - Out of tolerance sample found; not used

This exception is generated when a valid sample is found on the liquid source, but it is not within the time frame that is able to be applied to that record. Example A liquid meter has a batch with a product of "propane" from 06/01/2016 07:00:00 to 06/14/2016 07:00:00, and an LQ source has a sample for 6/28/2016 07:00:00. Within the Meter Editor of the liquid meter, the tolerance is set to seven days before the start of batch and three days after the end of batch. Within the Source Assignment editor, the "Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited" option is not enabled. The exception would then be generated because there is a sample on the LQ, but FLOWCAL cannot apply it because it is out of the tolerance range.

2049 Frozen value check

This is a header exception; it is never generated within the application. Frozen value exceptions are related to the limits that are defined in the Meter Editor (Setup \> Meter \> Editor). If a meter continues to report the same value for a particular data point over a number of hours, it is possible the reading is inaccurate and the results are caused by a frozen value that is not being updated. Meter frozen value validations allow the user to specify whether to look for frozen values, the number of hours for which each value must persist before it is considered frozen, and the limit for each value, which serves as a tolerance level within which values will be treated as identical.

2050 FVC – Frozen differential pressure

This validation and exception applies only to imported data on orifice and cone meters. If the value on the specified records does not change by more than the user-defined limit, then an exception will be generated. For example, if the Frozen Value comparison window is set to 2 hours and Differential Pressure Deadband is set to a difference of 1. 2075 Multi-run validation

Multi-run validation (MRV) exceptions are related to the limits defined in the Multiple Run subtab of the Meter Editor Validations tab for gas and liquid meters. Multiple run validation enables the user to perform a comparison of the meter’s record to as many as four other meter’s records for multi-tube locations, check meters versus sales meters, or upstream and downstream comparisons.

2076 MRV - Low differential pressure

This exception is generated when the Differential Pressure on a periodic record falls below the lower bound calculated according to the values set in the Meter Editor. For example, for Meter One, the When field is set to Always; the Using field to Unit Difference; and the Min value to 0.1000 for Differential Pressure. If the Meter One’s periodic record at 8/1/2016 12:00:00 has Differential Pressure of 15.3 psi, the lower bound for the current meter’s differential pressure at 8/1/2016 12:00:00 is 15.3 - 0.1000 = 15.2 psi. If the differential pressure for that record is less than 15.2 psi, this exception will be generated for the periodic record. The full Description of this exception will be: “MRV – low Differential Pressure as compared to Meter \#: \[comparison meter number\], \[current meter’s differential pressure\] -\> \[comparison meter’s differential pressure\]” The validation field Differential Pressure and therefore this exception will be available only for Orifice and Cone meter types.

2230 Expert systems

Expert systems (ES) exceptions are related to the limits defined in the Expert Systems subtab of the Meter Editor Validations tab. Expert systems statistically analyze historical data to identify uncharacteristic changes in the meter’s data flow pattern.

2231 ES - Differential pressure failed

This exception is generated when the Differential Pressure on a periodic record falls outside of the lower and upper bounds calculated according to the Expert Systems validation configuration in the Meter Editor. For example, Average Method is set to Running; Exclude E/S Exception is set to No; Average Count is set to 5; Check is set to Yes; Method is set to Std Deviation; and the ES Limit is set to 1.000 for Differential Pressure. The mean differential pressure for five previous periodic records is 15.2 and the standard deviation is 0.1673. Then the lower bound is 15.2 – (1 \* 0.1673) = 15.3673 and 15.2 + (1 \* 0.1673) = 15.0327. If the differential pressure for the current periodic record is less than 15.3673 or greater than 15.0327, this exception will be generated for the periodic record. The validation field Differential Pressure and therefore this exception will be available only for Orifice and Cone meter types.

2232 ES - Pulses failed

This exception is generated when the Pulses on a periodic record falls outside of the lower and upper bounds calculated according to the Expert Systems validation configuration in the Meter Editor. For example, Average Method is set to Running; Exclude E/S Exception is set to No; Average Count is set to 10; Check is set to Yes; Method is set to Std Deviation; and the ES Limit is set to 2.000 for Pulses. The mean pulses for 10 previous periodic records is 116.92 and the standard deviation is 2.2382. Then the lower bound is 116.92 – (2 \* 2.2382) = 112.4436 and 116.92 + (2 \* 2.2382) = 121.3964. If the pulses for the current periodic record is less than 112.4436 or greater than 121.3964, this exception will be generated for the periodic record. The validation field Pulses and therefore this exception will be available only for Coriolis, Positive Displacement, Turbine, and Ultrasonic meter types.

For example, Average Method is set to Running; Exclude E/S Exception is set to No; Average Count is set to 10; Check is set to Yes; Method is set to Std Deviation; and the LO Limit is set to 20.000 for Static Pressure. The mean Temperature for 10 previous periodic records is 74.22. Then the Hi Limit is 74.22 - 20 = 54.22. If the Temperature for the current periodic record is less than 54.22, this exception will be generated for the periodic record. For liquid meters, Meter Temperature is the field that is applied with this validation and exception.

2300 QFV - Quality frozen value

Quality Frozen Value exceptions are related to the limits that are defined in the Quality Source Validations for both Gas and Liquid Sources. If a Source continues to report the same value for a particular data point over a number of consecutive samples, it is possible the reading is inaccurate and the results are caused by a frozen value that is not being updated. Quality Frozen Value validations allow the user to specify whether to look for frozen values, the number of records for which each value must persist before it is considered frozen, and the limit for each value, which serves as a tolerance level within which values will be treated as identical.

FLOWCAL will compare the current sample’s Relative Density to the Relative Density value on a specified number of prior samples. 2401 FWV - Water correction not possible (gas is already dehydrated)

This exception is generated for a gas meter if the Dehydrated Gas field in the Volume Editor is set to "Yes" when FLOWCAL calculates the water vapor correction factor.

2402 ANLC - Low observed temperature

This exception is generated when the Observed Temperature on a liquid meter periodic record falls below the minimum value set in the Meter Editor. For example, the Min value for Observed Temperature is set to 50.000 but the value on the periodic record is 0.000.

2403 ANLC - High observed temperature

This exception is generated when the Observed Temperature on a liquid meter periodic record exceeds the maximum value set in the Meter Editor. For example, the Max value for Observed Temperature is set to 85.000 but the value on the periodic record is 85.6.

2404 ANLC - Low observed pressure

This exception is generated when the Observed Pressure on a liquid meter periodic record falls below the minimum value set in the Meter Editor. For example, the Min value for Observed Pressure is set to 10.000 but the value on the periodic record is 0.

2405 ANLC - High observed pressure

This exception is generated when the Observed Pressure on a liquid meter periodic record exceeds the maximum value set in the Meter Editor. For example, the Max value for Observed Pressure is set to 200.000 but the value on the periodic record is 213.

2406 ANLC - Low S&W percentage

This exception is generated when the Sediment and Water % on a liquid meter analysis record falls below the minimum value set in the Meter Editor. This exception is generated for the violating meter analysis record and will be displayed in the Volume Editor for all meter periodic records that are associated with the meter analysis record. For example, the Min value for S&W % is set to 0.005 but the value on the analysis record is 0.000.

2407 ANLC - High S&W percentage

This exception is generated when the Sediment and Water % on a liquid meter periodic record exceeds the maximum value set in the Meter Editor. This exception is generated for the violating meter analysis record and will be displayed in the Volume Editor for all meter periodic records that are associated with the meter analysis record. For example, the Max value for S&W % is set to 2.000 but the value on the analysis record is 4.128.

2408 ANLC - Low S&W volume

This exception is generated when the Sediment and Water Volume on a liquid meter periodic record falls below the minimum value set in the Meter Editor. For example, the Min value for S&W Volume is set to 1.00 but the value on the periodic record is 0.03.

2409 ANLC - High S&W volume

This exception is generated when the Sediment and Water Volume on a liquid meter periodic record exceeds the maximum value set in the Meter Editor. For example, the Max value for S&W Volume is set to 20.00 but the value on the periodic record is 23.67.

2410 ANLC - Low mass heating value

This exception is generated when mass heating value on a gas meter analysis record falls below the minimum value set in the Min/Max Values group box in the Meter Editor. This exception is generated for the violating meter analysis record and will be displayed in the Volume Editor for all meter periodic records that are associated with the meter analysis record. For example, the Min value for mass heating value is set to 22500.000 but the value on the analysis record is 22496.096.

2411 ANLC - High mass heating value

This exception is generated when mass heating value on a gas meter analysis record exceeds the maximum value set in the Min/Max Values group box in the Meter Editor. This exception is generated for the violating meter analysis record and will be displayed in the Volume Editor for all meter periodic records that are associated with the meter analysis record. For example, the Max value for mass heating value is set to 23500.000 but the value on the analysis record is 23502.417.

2412 ANLC - Low shrinkage factor

This exception is generated when a shrink factor value imported into a liquid meter is 0 or less. This exception is generated for the meter analysis record the shrink factor is imported into and will be displayed in the Volume Editor for all meter periodic records that are associated with the meter analysis record.

2413 ANLC - High shrinkage factor

This exception is generated when a shrink factor value of a liquid meter analysis is greater than 1.

2414 ANLC - Missing shrinkage factor

This exception is generated when the shrink factor on a live oil liquid meter is null. The shrink factor value must be greater than 0 or £ 1. This exception does not apply to live oil meters that are marked as stabilized oil. (See: [Live Oil Management](../../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Tools%20Menu.md)) If the value for the shrink factor is 1 or \[NULL\], the value for the flash gas factor must be 0 or \[NULL\]. If the meter is a live oil meter and is not "Stabilized Oil", the shrink factor cannot be NULL.

2415 ANLC - Missing flash gas factor

This exception is generated when the flash gas factor on a live oil liquid meter is null. The flash gas factor must be ≥ 0. This exception does not apply to live oil meters that are marked as stabilized oil. (See: [Live Oil Management](../../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Tools%20Menu.md)) If the value for the shrink factor is 1 or \[NULL\], the value for the flash gas factor must be 0 or \[NULL\]. If the meter is a live oil meter and is not "Stabilized Oil", the flash gas factor cannot be \[NULL\].

2416 ANLC - Invalid flash gas factor

This exception is generated when the flash gas factor of a liquid meter is less than zero.

2417 ANLC - Flash gas factor must be zero because shrinkage factor is 1

This exception is generated when one of the following is true for a liquid meter: - The shrink factor is one and the flash gas factor is not zero or null - The shrink factor is null and the flash gas factor is not zero or null

2451 MKF - Variance between meter factor and baseline exceeds allowable unit difference

This exception is written when a liquid meter factor is outside the acceptable range of the established baseline meter factor. The acceptable range is calculated as: ("Baseline Meter Factor" - "Unit Difference") to ("Baseline Meter Factor" + "Unit Difference").

2452 MKF - Variance between meter factor and baseline exceeds allowable percent difference

This exception is written when a liquid meter factor is outside the acceptable range of the established baseline meter factor. The acceptable range is calculated as: "Baseline Meter Factor" \* (1 - "Percent Difference"/100) to "Baseline Meter Factor" \* (1 + "Percent Difference"/100)

2453 MKF - Variance between K-factor and baseline exceeds allowable unit difference

This exception is written when a liquid k factor is outside the acceptable range of the established baseline k factor. The acceptable range is calculated as: ("Baseline K Factor" - "Unit Difference") to ("Baseline K Factor" + "Unit Difference")

2454 MKF - Variance between K-factor and baseline exceeds allowable percent difference

This exception is written when a liquid k factor is outside the acceptable range of the established baseline k factor. The acceptable range is calculated as "Baseline K Factor" \* (1 - "Percent Difference"/100) to "Baseline K Factor" \* (1 + "Percent Difference"/100)
Exception Directory

2500 US - Ultrasonic UFM diagnostic

Ultrasonic (US) exceptions are related to the limits defined in the Meter Editor Flowing Parameters Validations tab for gas and liquid meters. These validations are available only for ultrasonic meters as they check ultrasonic meter parameters such as speed of sound, profile, and symmetry. Path Gain validation generates exceptions 2600-2659 . These validations are performed against the data displayed in the UFM Diagnostic tab in the Volume Editor for ultrasonic meters.

2501 US - Speed of sound is not constant

This exception is generated when the Speed of Sound for a UFM Diagnostic record of a ultrasonic meter differs from previous Speed of Sound values by more than the percent difference limit set in the Ultrasonic 2 validation in the Meter Editor. For example, in the Speed of Sound group box on the Ultrasonic 2 sub-tab of the Meter Editor, the Duration (Hours) is set to 5 and the Percent Difference is set to 0.25. For a UFM Diagnostic record for the meter, the Speed of Sound is 399.241149. The Speed of Sound values for the 5 previous records are 397.6949768, 397.8718872, 397.2702636, 398.3409118, and 398.4650268. The percent difference from each record is 0.3888, 0.3441, 0.2438, 0.2260, and 0.1948.  Two exceptions will be generated on the current UFM Diagnostics record since 0.3888 and 0.3441 are greater than 0.25. This validation and exception are not applicable where the number of records available for the comparison with the current record is less than the Duration (Hours) value.

2502 US - Speed of sound exceeds variance validation limit

This exception is generated when the imported Speed of Sound for a UFM Diagnostic record of a ultrasonic meter differs from the Speed of Sound value calculated by FLOWCAL by more than the limit set in the Ultrasonic 2 validation in the Meter Editor. For example, in the Speed of Sound group box on the Ultrasonic 2 sub-tab of the Meter Editor, the Variance Amount is set to 0.0005 and the Compare Using field is set to Unit Difference. For a UFM Diagnostic record for the meter, the Speed of Sound of Path 1 is 400.08813; the Speed of Sound of Path 2 400.08841; the Speed of Sound of Path 3 400.15152; and the Speed of Sound of Path 4 400.31750; and the imported Speed of Sound is 400.1601. FLOWCAL calculates the Speed of Sound to be the average of the four paths: (400.08813 + 400.08841 + 400.15152 + 400.31750) / 4 = 400.1614. The unit difference between the imported value and the calculated value is 400.1614 – 400.1601 = 0.0013 which is greater than 0.0005, and this exception is generated.

2503 US - Flow velocity profile exceeds baseline limit

This exception is generated when the Profile of path velocities for a ultrasonic meter can be calculated and the calculated value varies from the Baseline by more than the Percent Difference Allowed set in the Ultrasonic 2 validation in the Meter Editor. The Profile is defined as (Path 2 Velocity + Path 3 Velocity) / (Path 1 Velocity + Path 4 Velocity). For example, in the Profile group box on the Ultrasonic 2 sub-tab of the Meter Editor, the Baseline is set to 0.9990 and the Percent Difference Allowed is set to 0.1000. For a UFM Diagnostics record, the Path 1 Velocity is 1.14496028; the Path 2 Velocity 1.12940907; the Path 3 Velocity 1.16436565; and the Path 4 Velocity 1.15422022. The Profile is then (1.12940907 + 1.16436565) / (1.14496028 + 1.15422022) = 0.99764882. The variance from the Baseline value is abs(0.99764882 / 0.9990) – 1) \* 100 = 0.1353 %. This exceeds the Percent Difference Allowed value of 0.1000, so the exception is generated.

2504 US - Flow velocity symmetry exceeds baseline limit

This exception is generated when the Symmetry of path velocities for a ultrasonic meter can be calculated and the calculated value varies from the Baseline by more than the Percent Difference Allowed set in the Ultrasonic 2 validation in the Meter Editor. The Symmetry is defined as (Path 1 Velocity + Path 2 Velocity) / (Path 3 Velocity + Path 4 Velocity). For example, in the Symmetry group box on the Ultrasonic 2 sub-tab of the Meter Editor, the Baseline is set to 0.9820 and the Percent Difference Allowed is set to 0.1000. For a UFM Diagnostics record, the Path 1 Velocity is 1.14496028; the Path 2 Velocity 1.12940907; the Path 3 Velocity 1.16436565; and the Path 4 Velocity 1.15422022. The Profile is then (1.14496028 + 1.12940907) / (1.16436565 + 1.15422022) = 0.980929534. The variance from the Baseline value is abs (0.980929534 / 0.9990 – 1) \* 100 = 1.8089 %. This exceeds the Percent Difference Allowed value of 0.1000, so the exception is generated.

2505 US - Unable to calculate profile

This exception is generated when the Profile of path velocities for a ultrasonic meter cannot be calculated and the returned value is null. The Profile is defined as (Path 2 Velocity + Path 3 Velocity) / (Path 1 Velocity + Path 4 Velocity). This exceptions is applicable when the Profile validation values are configured properly on the Ultrasonic 2 validation in the Meter Editor, and the Ultrasonic 2 validation is set to Run on Imports and Edits.

2506 US - Unable to calculate symmetry

This exception is generated when the Symmetry of path velocities for a ultrasonic meter cannot be calculated and the returned value is null. The Symmetry is defined as (Path 1 Velocity + Path 2 Velocity) / (Path 3 Velocity + Path 4 Velocity). This exceptions is applicable when the Symmetry validation values are configured properly on the Ultrasonic 2 validation in the Meter Editor, and the Ultrasonic 2 validation is set to Run on Imports and Edits.

2700 Flowing parameters check (high-high low-low)

FLOWCAL supports 'High-High' and 'Low-Low' limits for additional flowing parameter validations with appropriate exception descriptions. A 'Max Unresolved Severity' can be tracked in the Final Form Tables. By setting the severity of these exceptions to an elevated level, the exports and downstream systems can examine the Max Severity Value and determine if a record is ready to be processed. Any unresolved High-High or Low-Low exceptions present will prevent the meter data from being sent downstream. If a High and High-High or Low and Low-Low limit are both exceeded, FLOWCAL will only generate a single exception for either the High-High or the Low-Low. An exception will not be generated for the High or Low limit being exceeded.

2701 FPC - Low-low volume

This exception is generated when a record’s Volume exceeds the user defined limit for minimum volume. For example, the minimum volume is set to 100.0000, but the meter’s volume is calculated at 90.0000.

2702 FPC - High-high volume

This exception is generated when a record’s Volume exceeds the user defined limit for maximum volume. For example, the maximum volume is set to 1000.0000, but the meter’s volume is calculated at 1090.0000.

2703 FPC - Low-low energy

This exception is generated when a record’s Energy exceeds the user defined limit for minimum energy. For example, the minimum energy is set to 100.0010, but the meter’s energy is calculated at 90.0000.

2704 FPC - High-high energy

This exception is generated when a record’s Energy exceeds the user defined limit for maximum energy. For example, the maximum energy is set to 1000.0000, but the meter’s energy is calculated at 1090.0500.

2705 FPC - Low-low static pressure

This exception is generated when a record’s Static Pressure exceeds the user defined limit for minimum static pressure. For example, the minimum static pressure is set to 10.0000, but the meter’s static pressure is calculated at 0.1000.

2706 FPC - High-high static pressure

This exception is generated when a record’s Static Pressure exceeds the user defined limit for maximum static pressure. For example, the maximum static pressure is set to 475.0000, but the meter’s static pressure is calculated at 485.0500.

2707 FPC - Low-low temperature

This exception is generated when a record’s Temperature exceeds the user defined limit for minimum temperature. For example, the minimum temperature is set to 32.0000, but the meter’s temperature is calculated at 28.0000.

2708 FPC - High-high temperature

This exception is generated when a record’s Temperature exceeds the user defined limit for maximum temperature. For example, the maximum temperature is set to 175.0000, but the meter’s temperature is calculated at 186.0500.

2709 FPC - Low-low differential pressure

This exception is generated when a record’s Differential Pressure exceeds the user defined limit for minimum differential pressure. For example, the minimum differential pressure is set to 10.00, but the meter’s differential pressure is calculated at 0.10.

2710 FPC - High-high differential pressure

This exception is generated when a record’s Differential Pressure exceeds the user defined limit for maximum differential pressure. For example, the maximum differential pressure is set to 475.0000, but the meter’s differential pressure is calculated at 485.0500.

2711 FPC - Low-low pulses

This exception is generated when a record’s Pulses exceeds the user defined limit for minimum pulses. For example, the minimum pulse count is set to 10.0000, but the meter’s pulse count is calculated at 3.0000.

2712 FPC - High-high pulses

This exception is generated when a record’s Pulses exceeds the user defined limit for maximum pulses. For example, the maximum pulse count is set to 3600.0000, but the meter’s pulse count is calculated at 3690.0000.

2713 FPC - Low-low average extension

This exception is generated when a record’s Average Extension exceeds the user defined limit for minimum extension. For example, the minimum extension is set to 30.000, but the meter’s average extension is calculated at 25.000.

2714 FPC - High-high average extension

This exception is generated when a record’s Average Extension exceeds the user defined limit for maximum extension. For example, the maximum extension is set to 260.000, but the meter’s average extension is calculated at 269.000.

2715 FPC - Low-low raw volume

This exception is generated when a record’s Raw Volume exceeds the user defined limit for minimum raw volume. For example, the minimum raw volume is set to 100.000, but the meter’s raw volume is imported at 90.000.

2716 FPC - High-high raw volume

This exception is generated when a record’s Raw Volume exceeds the user defined limit for maximum raw volume. For example, the maximum raw volume is set to 1000.000, but the meter’s raw volume is imported at 1001.000.

2717 FPC - Low-low correlation factor

This exception is generated when a record’s Correlation Factor exceeds the user defined limit for minimum correlation factor. For example, the minimum correlation factor is set to 0.995, but the meter’s correlation factor is calculated at 0.90.

2718 FPC - High-high correlation factor

This exception is generated when a record’s Correlation Factor exceeds the user defined limit for maximum correlation factor. For example, the maximum correlation factor is set to 1.005, but the meter’s correlation factor is calculated at 1.01.

2800 Meter master characteristic comparisons differences

Meter Master Characteristic Comparisons Differences exceptions are related to the limits that are defined in Master Data Validation for both Gas and Liquid Meters. Master Data Validation (also known as Contract and Inspection Comparisons) defines how a meter's characteristics should look when brought in from the field. Master Characteristics are typically created based on the last test report for a meter. The master characteristics can be configured to generate exceptions if there is a difference between the meter’s master characteristic and the meter characteristic.

2801 MMCCD - Plate diameter changed

FLOWCAL will compare the Orifice Plate Diameter on the Meter Characteristic record to the Orifice Plate Diameter on the Master Characteristic record for that meter defined in Master Data Validation. If the value differs between the meter and master characteristic record, then an exception will be generated. For example, if the Orifice Plate Diameter is set to 6 on the Meter Characteristic record, but the Master Characteristic record has Orifice Plate Diameter set to 6.25, then this exception will be generated.

For example, if the Orifice Plate Temperature is set to 68 on the Meter Characteristic record, but the Master Characteristic record has Orifice Plate Temperature set to 70, then this exception will be generated.

2900 FPC - Static pressure falls below low calibration limit

Exception 2900 is an exception that defaults with a severity of 0. A user will need to go the Exception Description editor and set the severity to a value between 1 and 5 for this exception to be generated. This exception is also unique in that it can be enabled on a per meter basis in the Meter Editor, Exceptions tab. Once a severity is set, a user will need to set a Static Pressure Low Calibration limit in the Volume Editor. A user will need to navigate to the Characteristics, and double click the desired record. Then they will need to navigate to the Ranges tab. When the Static pressure goes below the low limit (in this case 0), then the exception will be generated.

Exception Directory

20000 INV - Mass exceeds fill limit

This validation and exception applies to Cavern and Inventory (created from Inventory Editor) Locations. For each hour, FLOWCAL will compare the Mass Inventory amount on the Location to the Total Mass that is defined in the Validations on the location. If the Mass Inventory amount for the hour is greater than the Total Mass defined on the Location, then this exception will be generated. For example, if the Total Mass on a Cavern Location is set to 100,000 and a Cavern Level Ticket is created with Mass set to 150,000, then this exception will be generated on the location.

20001 INV - Volume exceeds fill limit

This validation and exception applies to Cavern and Tank Locations. **Cavern Locations:** For each hour, FLOWCAL will compare the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount on the Cavern to the Total Volume that is defined in the Validations on the location. If the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount for the hour is greater than the Total Volume defined on the Cavern, then this exception will be generated. For example, if the Total Volume on a Cavern Location is set to 100,000 and a Cavern Level Ticket is created with Gross Standard Volume set to 150,000, then this exception will be generated on the location because the Gross Standard Volume on the Ticket exceeds the Total Volume for that Cavern. **Tank Locations:** For each hour, FLOWCAL will compare the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount on the Tank to the Total Volume that is defined on the Capacity Table Data tab for the tank. If the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount for the hour is greater than the Maximum Volume defined on the Capacity Table for the Tank, then this exception will be generated. For example, if the Maximum Volume on the Capacity Table for the Tank is set to 200,000 and a Tank Gauge Ticket is created with Gross Standard Volume set to 205,000, then this exception will be generated on the location because the Gross Standard Volume on the Ticket exceeds the Maximum Volume for that Tank.

20002 INV - Mass below low fill percentage

This validation and exception applies to Cavern and Inventory (created from Inventory Editor) Locations. A Total Mass and Min Fill % is defined on the validations for the location. A Minimum Fill amount for the Location is determined by multiplying the Total Mass by the Min Fill %. For each hour, FLOWCAL will compare the Mass Inventory amount on the Location to the Minimum Fill amount for the Location. If the Mass Inventory amount for the hour is less than the Minimum Fill amount for the Location, then this exception will be generated. For example, the Total Mass on a Cavern Location is set to 100,000 and the Min Fill % is 10 %, so the Minimum Fill on the Cavern is 10,000 (100000\*10%). If a Cavern Level Ticket is created with Mass set to 5000, then this exception will be generated on the location because the Mass Inventory is lower than the Minimum Fill for the Cavern.

For example, the Total Volume on a Cavern Location is set to 100,000 and the Min Fill % is 10 %, so the Minimum Fill amount on the Cavern is 10,000 (100000\*10%). If a Cavern Level Ticket is created with Gross Standard Volume set to 5000, then this exception will be generated on the location because the Gross Standard Volume Inventory is lower than the Minimum Fill amount for the Cavern. **Tank Locations:** A Min Fill % is defined on the validations for the tank, and the Total Volume is defined on the Capacity Table Data tab for the tank. A Minimum Fill amount for the Tank is determined by multiplying the Total Volume by the Min Fill %. For each hour, FLOWCAL will compare the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount on the Tank to the Minimum Fill amount for the Tank. If the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount for the hour is less than the Minimum Fill amount for the Tank, then this exception will be generated. For example, the Total Volume on the Capacity Table for the Tank is set to 200,000 and the Min Fill % for the Tank is 10%, so the Minimum Fill amount on the Tank is 20,000 (200000\*10%). If a Tank Gauge Ticket is created with Gross Standard Volume set to 15,000, then this exception will be generated on the location because the Gross Standard Volume Inventory is lower than the Minimum Volume amount for that Tank.

A Maximum Fill amount for the Tank is determined by multiplying the Total Volume by the Max Fill %. For each hour, FLOWCAL will compare the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount on the Tank to the Maximum Fill amount for the Tank. If the Gross Standard Volume Inventory amount for the hour is greater than the Maximum Fill amount for the Tank, then this exception will be generated. For example, the Total Volume on the Capacity Table for the Tank is set to 200,000 and the Max Fill % for the Tank is 90%, so the Maximum Fill amount on the Tank is 180,000 (200000\*90%). If a Tank Gauge Ticket is created with Gross Standard Volume set to 185,000, then this exception will be generated on the location because the Gross Standard Volume Inventory is greater than the Maximum Volume for that Tank.

20006 INV - Total changed when inventory not active

This validation and exception applies to Caverns, Inventory (created from Inventory Editor), and Tank Locations. If the Gross Standard Volume Inventory or Mass Inventory value on the Location changes while the Location Status is set to Inactive, Long-Term Monitoring, or Plugged and Abandoned on the Characteristic tab for that Location, then this exception will be generated.
Exception Directory
21001 TANK - Calculated GSV does not match given GSV (deprecated)

21002 TANK – Capacity table not given for ticket period

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets. This exception is generated for a tank ticket with an effective date that is not covered by the tank’s active capacity table data. In this scenario, calculation of total observed volume (TOV) will not take place for the ticket. To resolve the exception, capacity table data needs to be provided for the period, or a different capacity table must be selected.

21003 TANK – Construction material not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved on a tank that does not have Construction Material set to one of the options available on the Main tab of the Tank Editor. If the Use Steel Temperature Correction (CTS) for Calculations option on the Capacity Table editor is enabled, CTS (liquid) and CTS (vapor) will not be calculated. If the Use Steel Pressure Correction (CPS) for Calculations option on the Capacity Table editor is enabled, Shell Pressure Correction will not be calculated. To resolve the exception, the Construction Material field needs to be populated in the Tank Editor.

21004 TANK - Run splitting process failed (effective date collision)

Generated when the splitting process fails due to the presence of a gauge ticket with the same effective date as the (unsplit) run ticket.

21005 TANK - Run splitting process failed (failed to obtain external ticket number)

Generated when the custom external ticket numbering feature is in use and system was unable to retrieve a ticket number for the newly split record. The split will not occur when this happens.

21006 TANK – Capacity table not configured

This exception indicates that a capacity table has not been configured in the tank characteristic for the effective date of the ticket. Calculation of total observed volume (TOV) will not take place for the ticket. To resolve the exception, a capacity table must be set on the tank’s characteristic.

3000 BI - Batch imports

This is just a header exception; it is never generated within the application.
3001 BI - Data contains sum of duplicate records (effective date) (deprecated)

3002 BI - Imported original data obscured by existing edited data

This exception is generated for two specific cases: - If a record is auto-estimated and edited, and then the original record comes in, and the flag to replace Auto Estimated data is set to Y. - If a record is estimated, and then the original record comes in, and the auto estimate flag to replace Auto Estimated data is set to N.

3003 BI - Duplicate record detected

This exception is generated during the Daylight Saving Time period for “Fall Back.” This exception will be generated if a meter is not “Adjusted for DST” (Meter Editor; Imports tab) and duplicate records are imported which is very likely to happen for Fall back. When Adjusted for DST is enabled, FLOWCAL will also flag the first chronological hour where a fall back time change took place so that if a second instance of duplicate records is found within the Fall Back time frame exception 3003 will be generated appropriately.

3004 BI - Imported data does not match database original data

This exception is generated with Batch Snap functionality in the Meter Editor, Imports tab. Using the snap functionality to adjust a batch start date or a batch end date may cause the batch to conflict with a batch record that is already in the database. The comparison will be based on the following fields: - Batch Start Date - Batch End Date - Indicated Volume (IV) - Gross Standard Volume (GSV) - Net Standard Volume (NSV) - Mass If IV, GSV, NSV or mass in the file is undefined, then it will not be included in the comparison. All fields must otherwise match.  When this happens, the batch will not be imported and the exception will be generated.

3005 BI - Original periodic data not Imported due to existing overlapping periodic data

This exception is generated to inform the user that a liquid meter periodic record in time trails record span was not imported because it overlaps with an existing original periodic record. One exception is generated for each periodic record that was not imported in this fashion, on the existing periodic record that was already in database. This exception is generated to prevent overlapping periodic records from causing erroneous virtual batches to be displayed in the Volume Editor. This exception is most often caused by getting late periodic records.

3006 BI - Batch import failed; batch snapped to an effective date of existing batch

Using the snap functionality to adjust a periodic record’s date may cause the record to conflict with a periodic record already in the database from a previous import. If this happens, this exception will be generated, indicating that the record cannot be imported.

This exception is generated if a sample density is included on a liquid source or standalone analysis record and the sample pressure, the pressure on the liquid when the sample density was determined, is not provided.

3502 GQ/LQ - Sample temperature must be provided if sample density is given

This exception is generated if a sample density is included on a liquid source or standalone analysis record and the sample temperature, the temperature of the liquid when the sample density was determined, is not provided.

3503 GQ/LQ - Sample pressure requires an indicator of gauge or absolute units

This exception is generated if the sample pressure associated with a sample density on a liquid source or standalone analysis record does not include a gauge/absolute indicator.

3504 GQ/LQ - Atmospheric pressure must be provided if sample pressure is provided in absolute units

This exception is generated if atmospheric pressure has not been provided for a sample pressure that is indicated to be an absolute measurement. This applies to liquid source and standalone analysis records that include a sample density. In order calculate other density values at sample conditions, the pressure must be in gauge conditions.

30000 PROD - Imported product base density does not match FLOWCAL product

This validation and exception applies on import of liquid meter data and tickets. FLOWCAL will compare the Base Density value defined for the Product on the import file (Liquid Product Tab on CFX and TFX) to the Base Density value on the Characteristic tab for the product. If the values differ, then this exception will be generated. For example, the Base Density for Product “Demeth” is set to 0.6500 on the Liquid Product tab of a CFX File. The product “Demeth” is configured with a Base Density of 0.6501 in the Product Editor within FLOWCAL. The value for Base Density differs between the import file and the Product, so this exception will be generated.

30001 PROD - Imported EVP does not match FLOWCAL product

This validation and exception applies on import of liquid meter data and tickets. FLOWCAL will compare the EVP value defined for the Product on the import file (Liquid Product Tab on CFX and TFX) to the EVP value on the Characteristic tab for the product. If the values differ, then this exception will be generated. For example, the EVP for Product “Demeth” is set to 500 on the Liquid Product tab of a CFX File. The product “Demeth” is configured with an EVP of 515 in the Product Editor within FLOWCAL. The value for EVP differs between the import file and the Product, so this exception will be generated.

30002 PROD - Imported table type does not match FLOWCAL product

This validation and exception applies on import of liquid meter data and tickets. This exception is only valid for certain products that require specifying a Table Type, such as products set to use Product Table Aromatics & Cyclohexane (2004). FLOWCAL will compare the Table Type defined for the Product on the import file (Liquid Product Tab on CFX and TFX) to the Table Type on the Characteristic tab for the product. The Table Type differs between the import file and the Product, so this exception will be generated.

30041 PROD - Imported density engineering unit does not match FLOWCAL product

This validation and exception applies on import of liquid meter periodic records for meters that have the option “Import CFX Units” on the Imports tab in the Meter Editor set to Yes and the Product is configured with a Density Import Option of Engineering Units. FLOWCAL will compare the Density Unit defined on the Configuration \> Units 2 tab on the CFX file to the Density Unit defined for the Engineering Units on the Characteristic tab for the product. If the Density Unit differs, then this exception will be generated. For example, the Density Unit for Product “Propane” is set to REL on the Configuration \> Units 2 tab of a CFX File. The product “Propane” is configured with a Density Unit of Grams/CC in the Product Editor within FLOWCAL. The value for Density Unit differs between the import file and the Product, so this exception will be generated.

30042 PROD - Imported density is undefined for API degrees specified on FLOWCAL product

This validation and exception applies on import of liquid meter periodic records where the Product is configured with a Density Import Option of API Degrees. When the Density Import Option on a Product is set to API Degrees, FLOWCAL will import the Observed Density value from the Observed Density in API Degrees field in the History section of a CFX file. If this field is blank in the CFX file, then an Observed Density will not be imported and this exception will be generated.

30043 PROD - Imported density is undefined for relative density specified on FLOWCAL product

This validation and exception applies on import of liquid meter periodic records where the Product is configured with a Density Import Option of Relative Density. When the Density Import Option on a Product is set to Relative Density, FLOWCAL will import the Observed Density value from the Observed Density in Relative Density field in the History section of a CFX file. If this field is blank in the CFX file, then an Observed Density will not be imported and this exception will be generated.

4087 GQA - Comparison variance

An option is available in the Liquid Quality Source Editor to compare a new source (Source B) with a pre-existing source (Source A). When this comparison is established and a source record for Source B is imported into FLOWCAL, Source B’s newest record will be compared to Source A’s most current record. If there is any variance between the two analyses, FLOWCAL will generate exception 4087 on Source B.

4088 GQA - C6+/C7+ not applied

This exception is generated when a source analysis’ Component Configuration Method is configured to “Use C6+ and C7+ Splits” and C6+ Split and C7+ split does not equal 100.000 and the imported or manually entered source record has a value other than 0 for C8, C9, or C10. If only C6+ Split is not equal to 100 but C7+ Split is 100, then this exception will be generated if the source record has a value other than 0 for C7, C8, C9 or C10.

4089 GQA - Unnormalized total = 0

This exception is generated when the Unnormalized Volume Total is equal to 0 or not within the appropriate min/max limits set under Source Validations. This can occur in one of two ways: - **Upon Import:** If a Source Analysis Text File is imported with a record containing an Unnormalized Total = 0 - **Run Validations:** If the Minimum for Unnormalized Total is something other than “0.000” and source validations are run for a source with an Unnormalized Total = 0

4102 MD - Data has been auto estimated

This exception is generated for a meter when the data for the period missing data is auto-estimated by the Auto Estimate service. This exception is generated only for the first effective date of the auto-estimated data. Auto Estimate is enabled for the meter, and the Log Missing Data In Exceptions Log is set to Yes on the Auto Estimate sub-tab in the Meter Editor.

4103 Rescan - SCADA request has been queued for the meter

This exception is generated for a meter by the Auto Rescan service when the service processes a SCADA Request for a meter. SCADA Request is enabled for meter, and the Log Rescan Data In Exceptions Log is set to Yes on the SCADA Request sub-tab in the Meter Editor.

4104 Rescan - Missing (late) data detected

This exception is generated for a meter by the Auto Rescan service when the service finds missing periodic records prior to the current record being processed. Late Data Exception is enabled, and Generated Late Data Exception After values are set in the Meter Editor Late Data Services tab. For example, Generate Late Data Exception After values are set to 1 Day. As the Auto Rescan service processes the 1/10/2016 12:00:00 record, it will check records from 1/9/2016 12:00:00 to 1/10/2016 11:00:00. As soon as it finds the first periodic record missing, it will generate this exception for the 1/10/2016 12:00:00 record.

5001 VAR - Percent variance high ethane (C2) GPM

This exception is generated on a gas quality source for each sample that has the Ethane C2 GPM value that varies from the value calculated by FLOWCAL by more than the Percent limit set in the Variance validations for the quality source. For example, the current sample has Ethane C2 GPM value of 3.8624. Ethane C2 GPM calculated by FLOWCAL based on the sample values is 3.8597. The limit defined in Variance validation is 0.05%. 5500 Test report and FLOWCAL data differ

‘Test report and FLOWCAL data differ’ is based on field mappings set in the Data Map Editor. An exception is generated for each mapped field that differs between FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics and the data in the imported .tsx TEST report. Once this exception is generated, it must be ignored for it to no longer be unresolved.

5501 Trouble ticket received (low priority)

The Trouble Ticket Exceptions are generated anytime a Trouble Ticket task is imported via .tsx file. Priority is a field within the task that can be Low, Medium, High (not a required field, so that’s why Unknown Priority is available). Trouble Tickets are created in TESTit whenever there is an abnormal condition at the meter site like vandalism, broken equipment, weather damage etc. Once this exception is generated, it must be ignored for it to no longer be unresolved.

5601 PFX - Duplicate prove import with different meter factor

This exception is generated when a duplicate prove report is imported and the meter factor in the prove report being imported does not match the meter factor of the previously imported prove report. For example: The previous prove report has a meter factor of ".998" and a new PFX file is imported with a meter factor of "1.02". The two meter factors do not match, so an exception is generated.

5603 PFX - Duplicate prove import with different product

This exception is generated when a duplicate prove report is imported and the product in the prove report being imported does not match the product of the previously imported prove report. For example: The previous prove report has a product of "NGL" and a new PFX file is imported with a product of "Propane". The two products do not match, so an exception is generated.

5604 PFX - Composite Meter Factor is missing from PFX file

This exception is generated when “Pressure Compensated” is Yes and the PFX file does not contain a composite meter factor. For example, if the meter characteristic “Pressure Compensated” is Yes, the application will attempt to import the composite meter factor (‘Composite MF’ in the Prove Report section) from the file. If the composite meter factor field is null then this exception is generated.

5605 PFX - Meter Factor is missing from PFX file

This exception is generated when “Pressure Compensated” is No and the PFX file does not contain a meter factor. For example, if the meter characteristic “Pressure Compensated” is No, the application will attempt to import the meter factor (‘Resultant Meter Factor’ in the Prove Report section) from the file. If the resultant meter factor field is null then this exception is generated.

50100 ANLC - Relative density exceeds variance validation limit

This exception is for Gas meters only. It is driven off of Calculation Variance Validations in the Meter Editor. Users can import/edit a relative density. When this is filled out and imported, FLOWCAL will calculate a relative density based off of the Mole %’s given. If the difference between the FLOWCAL calculated relative density and imported/edited relative density exceeds the Calculation Variance Validation point then Exception 50100 will be generated. Comparisons for unit differences are done by rounding both the calculated and the measured values to 4 decimal places. Comparison calculations for percent difference use unrounded calculated and measured values, but the percent difference calculated are rounded to 4 decimal places before comparing to the specified limit.

docs.text: Exceptions 6301 Custom exception 1 through 6400 Custom exception 100 are custom exceptions that are for specific customers based on specific requirements. These exceptions will not be generated in a FLOWCAL environment, regardless of the severity level set, unless custom code has been written for that particular customer.

docs.title: Exception Directory

docs.text: String event and alarm (SEA) exceptions are unique in FLOWCAL in that they have an editor to set the parameters for the generation of each exception. These exceptions have a default severity set to 0. If this exception is being generated, criteria has been created for the exception and the severity level has been raised.  Exceptions  6501 – 6600 have the same functionality as other exceptions in the Exception Description Editor. Users can:  - Modify the description - Set the severity from 0 (do not generate) to 5 - Assign a contact group to notify when the exception is generated  Users can also click the **Edit Criteria** button to launch the Exception Criteria Editor and configure the criteria required to generate the custom exceptions for string events and alarms.  Multiple events or alarms may be attached to a periodic record that will generate the exception; however, only one record for a given exception number will be generated for any periodic record. For example: A string of low battery may trigger 60 alarms within an hour, but if exception 6501 is set to generate when this occurs, then only one exception 6501 will be generated for the hour.

60000 TKT - Calculated TOV does not match given TOV

This validation and exception applies on edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for all Tank Types other than Horizontal. If the TOV value is manually entered, FLOWCAL will compare the manually entered TOV to the FLOWCAL calculated TOV. If the values do not match out to product discrimination, then this exception will be generated on the ticket. For example, the Volume unit on the Tank is set to Bbl and has a Product Discrimination of 2 decimals. If the manually entered TOV value on a Tank Gauge ticket is 1000.35 and FLOWCAL calculates that TOV should be 1000.36, then this exception will be generated on the ticket.
