60004 TKT - Current seal off does not match previous seal on

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of a Tank Run ticket. FLOWCAL will compare the Seal Off on the current Tank Run ticket to the Seal On from the previous Tank Run ticket on that Tank. If the values do not match, then this exception will be generated. For example, a Tank Run ticket is created with an effective date of 09/01/2016 09:25:34 that has a Seal On of 135. A Tank Run ticket is then created with an effective date of 09/15/2016 16:13:51 that does not have a value set for Seal Off. Since the Seal On from the previous Tank Run ticket does not match the Seal Off from the new Tank Run ticket, this exception will be generated.

60005 TKT - Invalid odorant unit imported

This validation and exception applies on import of a ticket. The Odorant Unit on the Ticket Data tab of a TFX file is validated on import. If the Odorant Unit has a value other that is not a valid unit, then this exception will be generated on the ticket. The values are case sensitive. Valid values: - g = gallons - p = pounds per 10,000 gallons (lbm/10,000g) - C = g/cc - K = kg/m3 - G = pounds per gallon (lbm/gallon )

60006 TKT - Inactive from facility

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of all ticket types other than Cavern Level, Inventory Empty, and Product Conversion Tickets. When a Facility was previously configured to be a From Facility in the Facility Editor, but is then changed to no longer be a valid From Facility, FLOWCAL will mark that Facility as an Inactive From Facility. If a ticket is imported that has a From Facility that FLOWCAL considers to be an Inactive From Facility, then this exception will be generated on the ticket.

60007 TKT - Inactive to facility

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of all ticket types other than Cavern Level, Inventory Empty, and Product Conversion Tickets. When a Facility was previously configured to be a To Facility in the Facility Editor, but is then changed to no longer be a valid To Facility, FLOWCAL will mark that Facility as an Inactive To Facility. If a ticket is imported that has a To Facility that FLOWCAL considers to be an Inactive To Facility, then this exception will be generated on the ticket.

60008 TKT - Facility created on import

This validation and exception applies on import of a ticket. If the "Create Facilities" option is enabled and a ticket has a From Facility Code or To Facility Code that does not currently exist within FLOWCAL, then FLOWCAL will automatically create the Facility on import. If the ticket is attached to a location and a Facility is automatically created, then this exception will be generated on the location.

60009 TKT - Invalid movement dates

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of all ticket types other than Tank Gauge, Inventory Empty, and Product Conversion. If a ticket is imported that has a Movement Start Date that is greater than the Movement End Date, then this exception will be generated on the ticket. For example, if a Meter Ticket is imported with a Movement Start Date that is set to 09/01/2016 09:00:00 and a Movement End Date of 09/01/2016 08:59:59, this then exception will be generated because the Movement Start Date has a later date than the Movement End Date.

60042 TKT - Close level difference between tank run and gauge ticket exceeds capacity table resolution

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets. If a Tank Run and Tank Gauge ticket exist on a Tank for the same Effective Date, then FLOWCAL will compare the Close Level on the Tank Run ticket to the Level on the Tank Gauge ticket. If the level differs by more than the Table Entry Resolution defined on the Capacity Table, then this exception will be generated.

60043 GQA - High sediment and water percent

This exception is generated for Liquid Quality Sources when the S&W% (on the Additional tab) exceeds 100%. This exception will be validated on Import and Edits. If a user wants to set different min/max validation points for Sediment and Water then the user would need to set a validation on the Product (in the Product Editor).

60044 GQA - Low sediment and water percent

This exception is generated for Liquid Quality Sources when the S&W% (on the Additional tab) is below 0%. This exception will be validated on Import and Edits. If a user wants to set different min/max validation points for Sediment and Water then the user would need to set a validation on the Product (in the Product Editor).

60045 GQA - High sediment and water correction

This exception is generated for Liquid Quality Sources when the CSW (on the Additional tab) exceeds 1. This exception will be validated on Import and Edits. The acceptable range for CSW is anywhere between 0 and 1.

60046 GQA - Low sediment and water correction

This exception is generated for Liquid Quality Sources when the CSW (on the Additional tab) is below 0. This exception will be validated on Import and Edits. The acceptable range for CSW is anywhere between 0 and 1.

60047 GQA - CSW does not correspond to sediment and water percent

This exception is generated for Liquid Quality Sources when the S&W% and CSW (on the Additional tab) do not correlate with each other. For example, if a user set S&W% of 1% and a CSW of 0.98000 (indicative of S&W% set to 2%), this exception would generate since the data doesn’t correlate together.

60048 TKT – Level not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with no value in the Level field. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Level is missing, and will not be resolved until both are provided.

60049 TKT – Liquid temperature not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with no value in the Liquid Temperature field. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Liquid Temperature is missing, and will not be resolved until both are provided. If the Use Steel Temperature Correction (CTS) for Calculations option on the Capacity Table editor is enabled, CTS (liquid) and CTS (vapor) will not be calculated. CTL will not be calculated.

60050 TKT – Liquid pressure not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with no value in the Tank Pressure field. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Tank Pressure is missing, and will not be resolved until both are provided. If the Use Steel Pressure Correction (CPS) for Calculations option on the Capacity Table editor is enabled, Shell Pressure Correction will not be calculated.

60051 TKT – Observed temperature not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with no value in the Observed Temperature field. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Observed Temperature is missing, and will not be resolved until both are provided. CTL, Base Density, and Vapor Density will not be calculated.

60052 TKT – Observed density not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with no value in the Observed Density field. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Observed Temperature is missing, and will not be resolved until both are provided. CTL, Base Density, and Vapor Density will not be calculated.

60053 TKT – Valid analysis (liquid volume %) not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved without a value in the Vapor Density field; and without a valid analysis, specifically Liquid Volume %, so that Vapor Density could not be calculated. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Vapor Density is missing, and there is no valid analysis on the ticket. For a run ticket, it will not be resolved until both Vapor Density values are provided or a valid analysis is provided.

60055 TKT – Base density too high

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. Vapor Density calculation method is limited to the base density range of 0.4 to 0.65 Relative Density. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with data that results in a base density greater than 0.65 REL. For example, a tank gauge ticket has a Table E product; Observed Density of 0.6388 REL; Observed Temperature of 86°F; and Observed Pressure of 130 psig. When the ticket is saved, the base density is calculated to be 0.6506 REL. This is greater than 0.65 REL, and this exception is generated. Vapor Density will not be calculated. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Base Density is greater than 0.65 REL, and will not be resolved until both base densities are below the limit.

60056 TKT – Base density too low

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. Vapor Density calculation method is limited to the base density range of 0.4 to 0.65 Relative Density. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with data that results in a base density less than 0.4 REL. For example, a tank gauge ticket has a Table E product; Observed Density of 0.4205 REL; Observed Temperature of 33°F; and Observed Pressure of 105 psig. When the ticket is saved, the base density is calculated to be 0.3863 REL. This is less than 0.4 REL, and this exception is generated. Vapor Density will not be calculated. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Base Density is less than 0.4 REL, and will not be resolved until both base densities are above the limit.

60057 TKT – Observed pressure too high

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. The Vapor Density calculation uncertainty increases when the observed pressure is above 280 psia. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with an observed pressure greater than 280 psia. For example, a tank gauge ticket has an observed pressure of 267 psi. The pressure gauge is Gauge and the atmospheric pressure is 14.7 psi. Then the observed pressure is 281.7 psia. This is above 280 psia, and this exception is generated. Vapor Density will not be calculated. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Observed Pressure is above 280 psia, and will not be resolved until both pressures are below the limit.

60058 TKT – Observed temperature too high

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. Vapor Density calculation method is limited to the product temperatures of -40°F to 140°F. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with an observed temperature higher than 140°F. Vapor Density will not be calculated. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Observed Temperature is higher than 140°F, and will not be resolved until both base temperatures are below the limit.

60059 TKT – Observed temperature too low

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. Vapor Density calculation method is limited to the product temperatures of -40°F to 140°F. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with an observed temperature lower than -40°F. Vapor Density will not be calculated. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Observed Temperature is lower than -40°F, and will not be resolved until both base temperatures are above the limit.

60060 TKT – Correction for shell temperature not available

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with either CTS (vapor) or CTS (liquid) fields having no value. If the Use Steel Temperature Correction (CTS) for Calculations option on the Capacity Table editor is not enabled, CTS (liquid) and CTS (vapor) will be set to 1 so that this exception will not be applicable.

60061 TKT – CTL not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved and CTL value is not imported and cannot be calculated. For example, a tank gauge ticket is imported and the import data does not include observed temperature and CTL. FLOWCAL will not be able to calculate CTL with observed temperature missing. Since CTL is not imported or calculated, this exception will be generated.

60062 TKT – Total observed volume not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with no value in the Total Observed Volume. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Total Observed Volume is not imported or cannot be calculated, and will not be resolved until both are imported or calculated.

60063 TKT – Vapor density not given

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. This exception is generated when a tank ticket is saved with no value in the Vapor Density. For a gauge ticket, it is labelled Vapor Base Density. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Vapor Density is not imported or cannot be calculated, and will not be resolved until both are imported or calculated.

This validation and exception applies on import and edit of Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets for the Spherical Tank Type. For a run ticket, this exception will be generated if either Open or Close Vapor Temperature is not provided, and will not be resolved until both are provided. Exception Directory

70000 ALLOC - Master allocation

This is a header exception; it is never generated within the application.

70001 ALLOC - Master meter has multiple products assigned for allocation day

This exception is generated when the Master Meter has more than one product assigned for the allocation contract day(s) selected. For example, in location MA_LIQ_EXC_LOC, there are two meter members: - MA_LIQ_EXC_1 - MA_LIQ_EXC_2 In the month of November, MA_LIQ_EXC_1 has two different products on the same contract day, 11/15/2015. When attempting to perform the allocation from 11/14/2015 – 11/16/2015, the allocation cannot be completed because of the conflicting products on 11/15/2015 and this exception is thrown.

70002 ALLOC - Master meter products do not match

This exception is generated when a location has multiple master meters and the product on those meters does not match. For example, in location MA_LIQ_EXC_LOC, there are two meter members: - MA_LIQ_EXC_1 - MA_LIQ_EXC_2 For the month of February 2016, MA_LIQ_EXC_1 has a single product for the entire month labeled PROPANE; whereas MA_LIQ_EXC_2 has the same product until Feb. 15, 2016 0:00:00 where the product in the pipeline changes to CRUDE. When allocating to a third meter \[MA_LIQ_EXC_3\], this exception will be thrown and the allocation will not take place:

70003 ALLOC - Allocation meter has multiple products assigned for allocation day

This exception is generated when the meter that is being allocated to has more than one product for the contract days that it is being allocated too. For example, the meter being allocated \[MA_LIQ_EXEC_3\] to has two different products on contract day 10/15/2015. When attempting to perform the allocation from 10/14/2015 – 10/16/2015, the allocation cannot be completed because of the conflicting products on 10/15/2015 and this exception is thrown.

70004 ALLOC - Allocation meter product does not match master meter product

This exception is generated when the product on the meter being allocated to does not match the product on the Master Meter(s). For example, meter MA_LIQ_EXC_3 is the meter being allocated to for the month of December 2015 and its product for the entire month is Propane; however, the Master Meters, MA_LIQ_EXC_1 and MA_LIQ_EXC_2, both have a product of Crude. When the allocation is attempted for the contract month of December 2015, the process will stop not be possible and this exception will be thrown.

70005 ALLOC - Master meter components cannot be allocated to allocation meter

This exception is generated when the components from the analysis on the Master Meter(s) are different from the components on the Allocation Meter for the allocation time frame selected. The allocation cannot happen because the corresponding component values on the Allocation Meter are null. For example, the following component values are on the Master Meters \[MA_LIQ_EXC_1\] and \[MA_LIQ_EXC_2\] as well as on the Allocation Meter \[MA_LIQ_EXC_3\]: | | | |:--:|:--:| | Master Meters | Allocation Meter | | | | When attempting to perform an allocation for the month of January, the following exception thrown and the allocation process will not be able to take place.

70006 ALLOC - Master meter data set type does not match other master meter data set

This exception is generated when the data set type on one meter within the Master location does not match the data set type of another or the other meter members within the same location. There are two possible data set types: - Data Set Type 1 = Batch and/or Periodic Data only - Data Set Type 2 = Batch and/or Periodic Data and Component Data To resolve this exception, confirm all member meters have either Data Set Type 1 or Data Set Type 2.

70007 ALLOC - Allocation meter data set type does not match other allocation meter data set

This exception is generated when the data set type on one meter within the Allocation location does not match the data set type of another or the other meter members within the same location. There are two possible data set types: - Data Set Type 1 = Batch and/or Periodic Data only - Data Set Type 2 = Batch and/or Periodic Data and Component Data To resolve this exception, confirm all member meters have either Data Set Type 1 or Data Set Type 2.

70008 ALLOC - Allocation meter data set type does not match master data set type

This exception is generated when the data set type on one meter within the Allocation location does not match the data set type of the meter members within the Master location. There are two possible data set types: - Data Set Type 1 = Batch and/or Periodic Data only - Data Set Type 2 = Batch and/or Periodic Data and Component Data To resolve this exception, confirm all member meters in the Allocation location and the Master location have either Data Set Type 1 or Data Set Type 2.
Exception Directory

8001 LCN - Location ready for close approval

This exception will only be generated when the Location is set for Close Approval. This is set in the Location Editor in Tools \> Info. If the option Requires Close Approval is checked, then this exception may be generated. This is generated by the Location Close Service. If the location meets the requirements to be closed (all meter and ticket data is closed), then the Location Close Service will generate this exception. The user can then go to the Close Approvals form to Approve their location for close.

8002 LCN - Location close approved

This exception will only be generated when the Location is set for Close Approval. This is set in the Location Editor in Tools \> Info. If the option Requires Close Approval is checked, then this exception may be generated. After all meters are closed, the user will navigate to the Close Approvals form. A user will select their desired location for the desired month and then Approve the Close. When a user approves the close, it sets the location to closed for that month. This exception is informational in that it is generated when the Location is approved for close successfully.

8004 LCN - Line fill volume exceeded

This exception is generated when the FC_FFLCN_HOURLY.raw_volume value exceeds the Line Fill Volume set in the Location Editor Characteristics. This data for this exception is most typically driven from Line Fill meter data. This can be accessed by choosing a location, and then going to the Characteristics tab. The user may then double click a record and set a Line Fill Volume. When FLOWCAL rolls up the meters in that location, if the sum of the meters exceeds the Line Fill Volume then this exception will be generated.
8005 LCN - Unable to close location (data not finalized) (deprecated)

These exceptions address discrepancies identified when values in the TESTit task do not match corresponding values present in the FLOWCAL characteristic record as of the date the task was performed.

These exceptions are generated for TESTit 3 Integrated only.

docs.title:
80001 TI – Static pressure calibration range low does not match

This exception is generated when the imported Static Pressure Calibration Range Low value from TESTit does not match the corresponding value in the FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics record. For example: the TESTit value for Static Pressure Calibration Range Low is 0, but the FLOWCAL value is 14.6.

For example: the TESTit value for Tap Location is Upstream, but the FLOWCAL value is Downstream.

80028 TI – Measurement type does not match TESTit

This exception is generated when the imported Measurement Type value from TESTit does not match the current value in FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics. The value on the FLOWCAL characteristic record that is in effect as of the Date Performed of the TESTit Meter Inspection task will be compared to the value on the TESTit task. For example: the TESTit value for Measurement Type is EFM, but the FLOWCAL value is Chart.

80029 TI – Cone diameter does not match TESTit

This exception is generated when the imported Cone Diameter value from TESTit does not match the current value in FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics. The value on the FLOWCAL characteristic record that is in effect as of the Date Performed of the TESTit Meter Inspection task will be compared to the value on the TESTit task. For example: the TESTit value for Cone Diameter is 3, but the FLOWCAL value is 2.

80030 TI – K-factor does not match TESTit

This exception is generated when the imported K Factor value from TESTit does not match the current value in FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics. The value on the FLOWCAL characteristic record that is in effect as of the Date Performed of the TESTit Meter Inspection task will be compared to the value on the TESTit task. For example: the TESTit value for K Factor is 1000, but the FLOWCAL value is 1200.

80031 TI – Meter factor does not match TESTit

This exception is generated when the imported Meter Factor value from TESTit does not match the current value in FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics. The value on the FLOWCAL characteristic record that is in effect as of the Date Performed of the TESTit Meter Inspection task will be compared to the value on the TESTit task. For example: the TESTit value for Meter Factor is 1, but the FLOWCAL value is 0.99.

80032 TI – Number of dials does not match TESTit

This exception is generated when the imported Number of Dials value from TESTit does not match the current value in FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics. The value on the FLOWCAL characteristic record that is in effect as of the Date Performed of the TESTit Meter Inspection task will be compared to the value on the TESTit task. For example: the TESTit value for Number of Dials is 6, but the FLOWCAL value is 5.

80033 TI – Meter type does not match TESTit

This exception is generated when the imported Meter Type value does not match the current value in FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics. The value on the FLOWCAL characteristic record that is in effect as of the Date Performed of the TESTit Meter Inspection task will be compared to the value on the TESTit task. For example: the TESTit Meter Type is Orifice, but the FLOWCAL Meter Type is Turbine.
Exception Directory

9000 BLM - Bureau of Land Management (BLM) related validations

This is just a header exception; it is never generated within the application.

9001 BLM - Methane (C1) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. The BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that methane is missing.

9002 BLM - Ethane (C2) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that ethane is missing.

9003 BLM - Propane (C3) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that propane is missing.

9004 BLM - Isobutane (i-C4) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that isobutane is missing.

9005 BLM - n-Butane (n-C4) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that normal butane is missing.

9006 BLM - Isopentane (i-C5) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that isopentane is missing.

9007 BLM - n-Pentane (n-C5) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that normal pentane is missing.

9008 BLM - Hexanes+ (C6+) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that hydrocarbon components C1 through C6 always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that hexane, or the hexanes plus, is missing.

9009 BLM - Carbon dioxide (CO2) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that carbon dioxide always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that carbon dioxide is missing.

9010 BLM - Nitrogen (N2) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that nitrogen always be included in an analysis. This exception indicates that nitrogen is missing.

9011 BLM - Assigned GQ uses splits for component characterization when hexanes+ (C6+) mol% exceeds 0.5%

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that if the C6+ of an analysis exceeds 0.5%, then a C6+ split cannot be used to calculate heating value and other properties. BLM requires either a C9 analysis or the use of a C6+ characterization in these cases. This exception indicates that a C6+ split is inappropriately being used and that one of the two alternatives is required.

9012 BLM - C6+ split is not 60-30-10

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. In the calculation of heating value and other analysis properties, BLM requires that, when a C6+ split is permitted, the split ratio must be 60-30-10. This exception indicates that a split ratio other than 60-30-10 has been used.

9013 BLM - C6+ characterization date is approaching the six-month limit for a very high volume meter

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM permits the use of a C6+ characterization (as determined from a prior C9 or greater analysis), rather than a fixed C6+ split ratio, for the calculation of heating value and other analysis properties. The C6+ characterization must be updated at least every 6 months for very high volume meters. This exception indicates that the current C6+ characterization is approaching its six-month expiration date.  This exception will begin generating when the characterization is 135 days old, rather than 180 days old, to allow for a 45-day grace period (15 days before a monthly analysis would be due).

9014 BLM - C6+ characterization is approaching the one-year limit for a high volume meter

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM permits the use of a C6+ characterization (as determined from a prior C9 or greater analysis), rather than a fixed C6+ split ratio, for the calculation of heating value and other analysis properties. The C6+ characterization must be updated at least every 12 months for high volume meters. This exception indicates that the current C6+ characterization is approaching its one-year expiration date. This exception will actually begin generating when the characterization is 255 days old, rather than 365 days old, to allow for a 105-day grace period (15 days before a quarterly analysis would be due).

9015 BLM - Heptane (C7) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that the hydrocarbon components C7, C8 and C9 always be included when a C9 analysis is used. This exception indicates that heptane is missing from such an analysis.

9016 BLM - Octane (C8) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that the hydrocarbon components C7, C8 and C9 always be included when a C9 analysis is used. This exception indicates that octane is missing from such an analysis.

9017 BLM - Nonane (C9) mol% is missing

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM requires that the hydrocarbon components C7, C8 and C9 always be included when a C9 analysis is used. This exception indicates that nonane is missing from such an analysis.

9018 BLM - C6+ characterization is incomplete

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM permits the use of a C6+ characterization (as determined from a prior C9 or greater analysis), rather than a fixed C6+ split ratio, for the calculation of heating value and other analysis properties. This exception indicates that one of the characterization values is missing. The required C6+ characterization values are molar mass, gas relative density, gas/liquid volume ratio and gross heating value.

9019 BLM - C6+ characterization date is older than the six month limit for a very high volume meter

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM permits the use of a C6+ characterization (as determined from a prior C9 or greater analysis), rather than a fixed C6+ split ratio, for the calculation of heating value and other analysis properties. The C6+ characterization must be updated at least every six months for very high volume meters. This exception indicates that the current C6+ characterization is older then the allowed six-month period.

9020 BLM - C6+ characterization date is older than the one year limit for a high volume meter

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. BLM permits the use of a C6+ characterization (as determined from a prior C9 or greater analysis), rather than a fixed C6+ split ratio, for the calculation of heating value and other analysis properties. The C6+ characterization must be updated at least every 12 months for high volume meters. This exception indicates that the current C6+ characterization is older then the allowed one-year period.

9021 BLM - Heating value uncertainty exceeds designated limit

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. The BLM requires uncertainty to be calculated for heating values. This exception indicates the calculated uncertainty value is higher than the maximum uncertainty allowed. For meters with an FMP Tier of Very High, the limit is 1%. For meters with an FMP Tier of High, the limit is 2%.

9022 BLM - Heating value uncertainty cannot be calculated (calculation requires at least five analyses)

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. The BLM requires uncertainty to be calculated for heating values. For uncertainty to be calculated at least five analyses must be present, each with a unique lab date. This exception indicates there are less than five analyses or the analyses do not have at least five unique lab dates.

9023 BLM - Heating value uncertainty cannot be calculated (multiple heating values with same lab date)

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. The BLM requires uncertainty to be calculated for heating values. This exception indicates that uncertainty calculation cannot be performed due to different heating values with the same lab date.

9024 BLM – Heating value uncertainty cannot be calculated (cause unknown)

This exception can only be generated for a BLM-enabled meter. The BLM requires uncertainty to be calculated for heating values. This exception indicates that uncertainty calculation cannot be performed for an unknown reason.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
The Exception Resolver Settings screen contains several configuration options to help you organize and access exception data. Click the gear icon

on the main toolbar to access the Settings screen. The following options are available:

User Preferences

The User Preferences screen contains options for configuring the following: - **Date Selector** - Select a date range display option for exception data: - **Current Month** - Display data from the first day of the month at 00 hours to the current date and next hour. - **Previous Month** – Display data from the first day of the previous month at 00 hours to first day of current month at 00 hours. - **Both Current and Previous Month** – Display data from the first day of previous month at 00 hours to current date and next hour. - **Status Filter** - Select statuses to filter exceptions by. - **Load exceptions when window opens** - Enable this option to automatically populate exceptions upon entering the Exception Resolver based on the settings you have defined. When this option is disabled, you will need to click the Refresh button to populate the exceptions list based on your settings. - **Color detail rows** - Enable this option to color the rows in the exception grid based on status. - **System** - Select a system associated with the exceptions you want to view. - **List** - Specify a default list for the Exception Resolver. These options vary based on the system selected.

Column Selector

Use the Column Selector to specify which columns to display in the Exception Resolver grid. To modify columns:  - Drag and drop items from the Available Columns list to the Current Columns list, or vice versa. The order of the columns will dictate the order in which the columns display on the grid. While dragging a column into either list, a pop-up will indicate the position of the column in the list it is going into. - Click **Select All** to move all columns to the Current Columns list. Required columns (such as Description, Exception Count and Status) cannot be removed from the Current Columns list. Device Name and Device Number are conditionally required; you can remove one or the other from the Current Columns list, but not both. If a column cannot be removed, a pop-up will display. You can also change the order of the columns by dragging and dropping column headings within the grid itself, or remove columns by dragging and dropping them outside of the grid, but FLOWCAL will not save that layout when you exit the Exception Resolver.

Grouping Selector

Use the Grouping Selector to specify groupings for the Exception Resolver grid. To modify groupings: - Drag and drop items from the Available Groupings list to the Current Groupings list, or vice versa. While dragging a column into either list, a pop-up will indicate the position of the column in the list it is going into. - Click **Select All** to move all columns to the Current Groupings list. The order of the columns dictates the sort order. By default, the grouping is by Device Number, Description, and then Status. Not all columns from the Exception Resolver grid are available for grouping. Those columns will not display in the Grouping Selector. If a column cannot be removed, a pop-up will display.

docs.title: Apply Changes
docs.text:
Click Done when you are ready to apply your changes to the Exceptions Resolver. If you click the close button

, a dialog box will display, prompting you to save the changes. Three options are available:

  • Yes - Save the changes and apply the settings to the Exception Resolver.
  • No - Discard the changes and close the Settings window.
  • Cancel - Return to the Settings window and make changes as needed. Clicking the close button will also perform this function.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires Data Exceptions - Can View permissions.

Exceptions flag suspect data that has been imported or manually added to a meter, location, source, or ticket. Running validations for a meter after data has been added can also create exceptions. A complete list of FLOWCAL exceptions is available in the Exception Description Editor.

FLOWCAL typically generates exceptions when it detects:

  • Differences between an imported characteristic and a master characteristic.
  • Imported (original) or edited data that lies outside established set points.
  • Missing data that it needs for performing a calculation.
  • Missing data where it expected data.

The Exception Resolver lists all exceptions for a selected object, allowing you to investigate causes and determine how to resolve the issues.

FLOWCAL cannot retrieve more than 500,000 exceptions from the database at a time. It retrieves meter exceptions first, followed by location and source exceptions.

To access the Exception Resolver: - Click the **Exception** tile on the main screen; - Go to **Review** \> **Exception Resolver**; or - Click **More** on an [Exception Resolver widget](../../Dashboard%20Manager/Dashboard%20Manager_Exception%20Resolver.md) on the main screen (if configured). If you access the Exception Resolver from an Exception Resolver widget, the data grid displays the exceptions for the selected list and follows the user preferences for filters.

Filter Options

The following filter options are available in the Exception Resolver: - **System** - Contains the FLOWCAL systems where you are a member. - **Object Type** - Determines the type of data that displays in the exception grid. This selection determines the items that will be available in the Object Search box. Available object types are: - **Meter** - Displays exceptions for specific meters. - **Location** - Displays exceptions for a location, including exceptions for all associated meters, locations, and tickets in the location hierarchy. You can further filter location objects by location type (balance, liquid cavern, comparison, inventory, segment, station, and tank). - **List** (default) - Displays exceptions for meter/location lists. Location lists display location exceptions, including exceptions for immediate associated meters, locations, and tickets. FLOWCAL does not display exceptions for members that are not immediate members. - **Close Group** - Displays exceptions for associated meters. FLOWCAL does not display exceptions for locations in close groups. - **Source** - Displays exceptions for sources. - **Source List** - Displays exceptions for source lists. - **Ticket** - Displays exceptions for standalone tickets (tickets not associated with a location). Object Search is not available. - **Sample** - Displays exceptions for standalone samples (samples not associated to an LQ source). Object Search is not available. - **Object Search** - Select an object for which to view exceptions. The list contains the 10 most recently used objects of a given type, followed by the remaining list of objects you have access to based on security. For example, if you select Meter as the object type, the list contains the 10 most recently used meters, followed by the rest of the meters to which you have access. You can expand the Object Search drop-down list by clicking and dragging the bottom-right corner. You can also manually search for items within this list. - **Show Quality Source Object Selector** - Includes exceptions for an associated quality source. This link is only available after you select an object. - **Date Selector** - Select a datetime range for exceptions you want to display, if necessary. Three date options are available: - **None** - Displays exceptions for all of time. - **Effective Date** - Displays exceptions based on the effective date of the associated data. - **Generated Date** - Displays exceptions that were generated on a specific date. By default, the Date Selector is set to Effective Date with the First Date being the beginning of the previous month at 00 hour (for example, if the current date is April 10, then the First Date is March 1) and the Last Date being the current date and the start of the next hour from the system time. The First and Last Date/Hour are inclusive. Select the start time for the First Date by clicking in the field to access the calendar, and then clicking the **Start of Time** button or pressing **Alt+S**. Select the end time for the Last Date by clicking in the field to access the calendar, and then clicking the **End of Time** button or pressing **Alt+E**. If the **First Date** value is later than the **Last Date** value, the Date Selector displays in red, indicating that there is an issue with the dates. - **Legend/Status Filter** - Click the checkboxes next to each status type to filter the exceptions by status (Acknowledged, Resolved by Late Data, Resolved by User, Pending, Unresolved). FLOWCAL retains status filter changes that you make from the Exception Resolver screen until you close FLOWCAL, even if you exit the Exception Resolver. To save status filter selections across sessions, go to **Settings** \> **User Preferences**.

Toolbar Options

The following options are available on the Exception Resolver toolbar: - **Reset** - Clears the grid and restores the settings to the user preferences that are defined in **Settings Manager** \> **User Preferences**. - **Email** - Opens the email dialog box and populates the email with the selected exceptions. This option is also available when you right-click an exception in the grid. - **Export to Excel** - Exports all data from the Exception Resolver (excluding summary rows). The Excel export might include exceptions that are not currently visible in the grid due to column filtering. Exceptions filtered out through parameters at the top of the form are not included in the export. - **Add Note** - Adds a note to objects for the selected exception. This option is also available when you right-click on an exception in the grid. (See: [Notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md)) - **Settings** - Opens the Settings screen so that you can specify user preferences. (See: [Exception Resolver Settings](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md)) A **Refresh** button is also available beneath the Status Filter checkboxes. Click this button to refresh the grid based on the filters/settings that you defined. The total number of exceptions displays in the bottom right corner of the screen, labeled **Count=**. If you change any settings after FLOWCAL populates the data grid, the data grid clears and you will need to click the **Refresh** button again.

Function Buttons

The following function buttons are available to change the status of exceptions: - **Acknowledge** - Update the status of selected exceptions to "Acknowledged". This button is only enabled when you select one or more unresolved or pending exceptions. Use this status for exceptions that have been reviewed and deemed acceptable. - **Pending** - Update the status of selected exceptions to Pending. This button is only enabled when you select one or more unresolved exceptions. Use this status for exceptions that require resolution at a later time. - **Unresolve** - Update the status of selected exceptions to "Unresolved". This button is only enabled when you select one or more acknowledged or pending exceptions. Use this status for exceptions that have not been addressed and need attention. - **Resolve** - Access the flagged data for selected exceptions so that you can investigate or resolve the issue. This button is enabled when you select any exception. Double-clicking an exception will also direct you to the flagged data. - Meter exceptions open the Volume Editor to the hour the exception occurred. - Location exceptions open the Location Close Approval screen for the appropriate record. - Source exceptions open the Source Analysis Editor for the appropriate record. - Ticket exceptions open the Ticket Detail Editor. - Sample exceptions open the Sample Analysis Editor. The Resolve button is only available if you have **Data Exceptions - Can Edit** privileges and the **Exception Resolver - Linkages** module. You cannot resolve event-generated exceptions, such as a purged all data exception; you can only acknowledge them. You can only update an exception status for an exception, not a summary (group) row. - **Done** - Close the exception resolver. To require an edit reason for exception status changes, enable the Require Edit Reason for Exceptions option in the [System Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration%20-%20General%20Tab.md) screen.

docs.title: Exception Grid
docs.text:
The exception grid displays all of the exceptions that meet the filter parameters that you have specified. Several options are available for sorting, organizing and managing exceptions.

If you double-click a location exception in the exception resolver, the Balance Explorer will open and will be preset with the following:

  • Object Selector = Location
  • Location Number = Location that the exception was generated for
  • Date Range = Contract Month
  • From = Month/Year of exception
  • To = Month immediately following the month of exception

Grid Columns

The following columns are available in the exception grid: - **Device Number** - Numeric identifier assigned to the object when it was created in the application (example: meter number). - **Device Name** - Identifier assigned to the object when it was created in the application (for example, meter name). - **Effective Date** - Date or date range associated with the exception data. - **Generated Date** - Date or date range when the exception was initially generated. - **Description** - Actual exception text explaining the issue and cause. - **Exception Number** - Unique numeric identifier associated with the exception. - **Exception Count** - Total number of exceptions in the group (summary rows only). (See: [Grouping Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Grouping)) - **Edit Reason\*** - The reason given for changing the exception status. - **Edit Code\*** - The numeric code associated with the edit reason. - **Comment\*** - Additional information regarding changes to an exception status. \* These items are required if the Require Edit Reasons for Exceptions option is enabled under **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **System** \> **System Configuration**. - **Field Value** - Data value that the validation process tested against. - **Alarm Level** - Value limit defined for the data. - **Status** - Current status of the exception (example: Unresolved). - **Type** - Type of device or object (defined under **Object Types**). - **Severity** - Priority level defined for the exception. Modify severity levels in the [Exception Description Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Exception%20Description%20Editor.md). - **Modified By** - User ID that last modified the status of the exception. - **Modified Date** - Date when the exception status was last modified. - **Field Name** - Name of the database field that contains the flagged data (example: Temperature). - **Table Name** - Name of the database table that contains the flagged data (example: FC_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES). - **Machine** - Name of the computer that last accessed the data. - **User Name** - User ID that last accessed the data.

Column Options

Right-click any column header to access the following configuration options: - **Full Expand** - Expands all exception groups. - **Full Collapse** - Collapses all exception groups. - **Sort Ascending** - Sorts exceptions by the selected column in ascending order. - **Sort Descending** - Sorts exceptions by the selected column in descending order. - **Show Column Chooser** - Opens the Column Selector so that you can select which columns display on the grid. (See: [Column Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector)) Easily remove a column by dragging and dropping the column header outside of the grid. FLOWCAL retains changes that you make from the grid until you close the Exception Resolver. Use the [Column Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector) to save a column layout. - **Best Fit** - Expands the selected column to completely display the contents. - **Best Fit (all columns)** - Expands all columns to completely display the contents. - **Filter Editor** - Launches the Filter Editor so that you can create conditional statements. The statements can include any column or value within the column. ![](data:image/png;base64,) ##### Column Order To change the column order, click a column header and drag and drop the column to the new location.

Sorting Exceptions

By default, FLOWCAL groups and sorts exceptions by device number, then exception description, and then status. To sort exceptions by an individual column, click the column header or the up/down arrow in the header. The arrow might be hidden because of column width. You can only sort columns within the grouping order. For example, if the grouping order in Settings is device number, description, and status, then status will only be sorted ascending/descending with a specific device number and exception description. To sort by number and then status, in the Group Selector, device number must be at the top, followed by status. Sorting by exception count applies to groups only—not individual exceptions. If you click the **Exception Count** column heading, FLOWCAL sorts the summary rows (groups) by the number of exceptions they contain.

Filtering Exceptions

You can filter exceptions by a single column or by multiple columns. To filter by a single column: 1. To display the filter icon, hover over a column header. 2. To open the Filter dialog box, click the filter icon. The box contains two tabs: > - **Filter Values** - Select the values you want to display. > - **Filter Rules** - Apply a conditional rule (for example, "Is greater than" or "Is less than"). First select a condition, and then specify a value. 1. To close the Filter dialog box, click on the grid. After FLOWCAL applies the filter, you can use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter. To filter using multiple columns, right-click on a column header and select **Filter Editor**.

Grouping Exceptions

By default, FLOWCAL groups exceptions by device number, exception description, and status. A summary (or group) row includes the device number, device name, effective date range, exception description, exception number, exception count, and status. (See: [Grouping Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Grouping)) You cannot update exceptions in bulk by selecting a group. To update multiple exceptions, expand the group and then select the exceptions individually, or press **Ctrl+A**.

Other Menu Options

Right-click an exception or group of exceptions to access the following options: - **Add Notes** - Write [notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md) for objects associated with an exception. - **View Notes** - View [notes](Exception%20Resolver_Notes.md) for objects associated with an exception. - **Email** - Open the email dialog box so that you can populate the email with the selected exceptions. - **Reschedule Sample** - Reschedule samples for Source Analysis exceptions (TESTit 2 Integrated users only). To use this feature, you must enable the **Allow Reschedule of Analysis Samples** option (**Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **System** \> **System Configuration**).

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
Exceptions may require supplemental documentation to provide additional status information.

Example Validations for a meter are set so that exceptions are generated when the flow data temperature falls below 55°F. An analyst can change the status of these exceptions to "Acknowledged" during the time frames that fall outside of the validation range, and provide an edit reason for doing so. A senior analyst would like to see some documentation inside FLOWCAL that describes the meter data conditions and provides context for why FLOWCAL reports data discrepancies.

Creating Notes

You can add notes to objects that exceptions are associated with directly from the Exception Resolver grid. To add a note to an object in the Exception Resolver: 1. Highlight the desired exceptions. 2. Click the **Add Note** icon on the toolbar. You can also right-click one of the highlighted exceptions and select **Add Note** or **View Notes**. When the View Notes screen displays, you can then click the **Add Note** button. 3. When the Add Note screen displays, provide the required data: - **First Date** - The beginning effective date for the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the minimum effective date of the exceptions selected in the exception grid. - **Last Date** - The ending effective date for the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the maximum effective date of the exceptions selected in the exception grid. - **Visibility** - Designation to determine who can view the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the user’s visibility settings in User Preferences window. Other options are: - **Everyone** - All FLOWCAL users can access the note. - **Internal** - All FLOWCAL users can access the note, but the note will not display on any standard reports. - **Private** - Only the user who created the note can view it. - **Expiration Date** - Date after which the note will no longer be visible in FLOWCAL. (The record of the note will still be stored in the database.)  The Expired Notes report can be used to view a list of expired notes in FLOWCAL. - **Custom Fields** - Four custom text boxes are available for capturing additional data. (If custom fields are configured on the Notes tab of the [Custom Fields Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Custom%20Fields.md), those fields will be generated when you first open the Add Note screen.) - **Note Text** - The documentation portion of the note (required). - **Object Information** - The number, name and type of any objects associated with the selected exceptions.  If you click the delete button on any of the object rows, the note will no longer be included on that object. - When you have finished entering the note date, click **Done**. After a note is saved, a note icon will display next to the exception(s) you selected if the effective date for the exception(s) falls within the date range of the note.

Viewing Notes

To view notes associated with an object: Right-click an exception with a note icon and select **View Notes**. When the View Notes screen displays, you will be able to view the full body of the note, as well as the following Object History details: - **Modified Date** - GMS date when the note was last edited. - **Modified By** - Name of the user who last edited the note. - **First Date\*** - Effective starting date of the note. - **Last Date\*** - Effective ending date of the note. - **Expiration Date\*** - Date after which the note will no longer be available. - **Visibility\*** - Designation indicating who can view the note. - **Custom 1–4** - Editable fields used to capture additional data. (If custom fields are configured on the notes tab of the [Custom Fields Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Custom%20Fields.md), the column headers in the View Notes screen will match those custom fields.) \* These items are read-only; they are only editable in the Add Note screen.

Deleting Notes

Notes are deleted from the Object History grid. To delete a note: 1. Hover over a note in the Object History grid. 2. Click the delete button when it displays. Deleting a note removes the note from the object. Any exceptions for the object within the effective date range of the note will no longer include the note icon.

Column Options

Right-click any column header to access the following configuration options: - **Sort Ascending** - Sort items in ascending order for the selected column. - **Sort Descending** - Sort items in descending order for the selected column. - **Show Column Chooser** - Open the Column Selector to select the columns to display in the grid. (See: [Column Selector](Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector)) - **Best Fit** - Expand the selected column to display the complete contents. - **Best Fit (all columns)** - Expand all columns to display the complete contents. - **Filter Editor** - Open the Filter Editor to create conditional statements based on any column or value within the column. ##### Column Order To change the order of the columns, click a column header and then drag and drop the column to the new location. You can remove a column by dragging and dropping it outside of the grid, but FLOWCAL will not save this layout when you exit the screen.

Sorting Notes

By default, notes are sorted by modified date, in descending order. To change the sort order of notes: - Click any column header to sort notes by that parameter. - Click a header again to reverse the list order (ascending or descending). - Right-click a column header and select **Sort Ascending** or **Sort Descending**.

Filtering Notes

You can filter notes by a single column or by multiple columns. To filter by a single column: 1. Hover over a column header to display the filter icon. 2. Click the filter icon to open the Filter dialog box. The dialog box contains two tabs: - **Filter Values** - Select the values that you want to display. - **Filter Rules** - Apply a conditional rule (for example: "Is greater than" or "Is less than"). Select the condition, and then specify a value. 3. Close the Filter dialog box by clicking on the grid. 4. After FLOWCAL applies the filter, you can use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter. To filter by multiple columns, right-click a column header and select **Filter Editor**. The following example shows a filter that uses multiple columns:

All users can change their own passwords (this does not apply to FLOWCAL Instant Login users). You will need to log in with your existing password to update this information.

Passwords must conform to the requirements established for your Oracle profile by your database administrator.

docs.title: Instant Login
docs.text:
The Instant Login feature mimics Single Sign On capabilities and allows users to log in to pre-defined FLOWCAL databases using Windows credentials, either through command line or a shortcut.

Vault Configuration Utility

The standalone Vault Configuration utility (FlowCal.VaultConfiguration) allows users to create .fcvault files that securely store one or more sets of login credentials. This utility is part of the FLOWCAL install set. A FLOWCAL installation will point to the vault file for use by the Instant Login process. Only members of the Windows Active Directory group FLOWCAL-VAULT-USER will be allowed to run and access the utility. To configure utility access, the network administrator must first create the Active Directory group. The following items are available on the Vault Configuration utility: - **Vault File** - The Windows path where the vault file is saved to. - **Database** – Must be unique for the current fcvault file. - **Username** – The username for the given database. - **Password** – The password for the given username (password is case sensitive). - **Add Row** – Add additional rows for more sets of login credentials. For the utility to save: - At least one record is required. - Duplicate databases are not allowed. - All fields (Database, Username, and Password) must be populated.

Instant Login Vault Location

To set a vault file location in FLOWCAL, or edit an existing location: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Security** \> **Instant Login Vault**. Users must have **User Security - Can Create Application Process** or **User Security - Can Edit Application Process** privileges to access this screen. 2. Click **Browse**. 3. Select the file location and click **Save**. 4. Click **Done**.

Access Configuration

Instant User Designation Options for configuring instant users are available on the [User Access](../Settings%20Manager/Security/User%20Access.md) screen. Security Group Association Associate Windows Active Directory groups with FLOWCAL security groups through the [Group Access](../Settings%20Manager/Security/Group%20Access.md) screen. - Instant users do not need to belong to any AD security groups if the users are manually created; however, they will first need to be given permissions to access various FLOWCAL functions. - If a new instant user belongs to at least one AD group, the AD group can be mapped to a FLOWCAL security group, which will give the user group-level security privileges upon logging in. - When a Windows user who belongs to at least one AD group with FLOWCAL group mapping attempts to log in to FLOWCAL for the first time, FLOWCAL automatically creates an instant user with no user-level security privileges. The user will be granted group-level privileges based on the mapped FLOWCAL group. - When instant users who belong to at least one AD group log in to FLOWCAL, their FLOWCAL group membership will be adjusted based the current AD/FLOWCAL group mapping. This only applies to automatically created instant users.

User Login

Once set up, instant users may log in using the command line or a FLOWCAL.exe shortcut. To log in through command line: 1. Open a command prompt. 2. Navigate to the FLOWCAL install folder. 3. Enter "FLOWCAL.exe" followed by the command line argument "/instant" and the database name. 4. Press **Enter**. To log in through a FLOWCAL.exe shortcut: 1. Create a FLOWCAL.exe shortcut. 2. Right-click the shortcut and select **Properties**. 3. Click the **Shortcut** tab. 4. Add the argument "/instant" and database name to the end of the **Target** field. 5. Save the change. 6. Double-click the shortcut.

Setup Instructions

1. The IT department will need to create a Windows Active Directory group called "FLOWCAL-VAULT-USER". 2. When this AD group has been created, add all Windows users who will be using the Vault Configuration Utility feature (FlowcalVaultConfiguration.exe) to this group. If additional AD groups are desired (see examples in Access Configuration), create the groups and add members. 3. In FLOWCAL, create a standard user to be used in the Vault Configuration Utility; this username credential will be used by the instant login functionality to connect all instant users to FLOWCAL. - This user will need **User Security** \> **Can Create** and **Can Edit** privileges, as well as any other permissions where an instant user that logs in through this vault standard user would require. - An existing standard user that meets this requirement can also be used for the utility. 4. Create the fcvault file with the login credentials via the Vault Configuration Utility. 5. Log in to FLOWCAL as a standard user and set up the vault path (see Instant Login Vault Location). 6. Create users. - **Auto create instant users:** 1. 1. Set up the FLOWCAL security group/AD group association (see Access Configuration). 2. Place the Windows users in the appropriate Windows AD group. 3. Create a FLOWCAL shortcut (see User Login) and log in. The new instant user is created during the first login and should be presented with the FLOWCAL main screen. Instant users created this way will inherit all security permissions from the assigned AD group. These instant user’s AD group membership will be updated automatically if the FLOWCAL security group/AD group association is changed. - **Manually create instant users** in the FLOWCAL User Access screen and assign appropriate user security permissions. Create a FLOWCAL shortcut (see User Login). Double-click the shortcut. The user should be logged into FLOWCAL automatically. If customers want to log in as instant users with an existing FLOWCAL username, their FC username and Windows username must match. No method exists for converting existing standard users into instant users if these usernames do not match.
