docs.title: Tips for New Users
Common FLOWCAL Terminology
Time-Related
docs.text:
Business Month

The business month is the first month after the last close. If the last month closed is April and it is July 10, the business month is May (last month after close in April).

Data Resolution

Defines whether the flow data will be captured in 15-minute, hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly records. This is defined at the meter level, by setting the Data Resolution field within the meter’ characteristics.

Datetime Effective

Records with a start date and time and an end date and time; may span all of time.

Effective Date / Effective End Date

Time stamp that signifies when the meter acquired the data. The effective date is the beginning time for which the record is effective. The end date indicates the end time for which the record is effective.

GMS Date

Gas measurement system day on which a database record was created or last modified.

Measurement Month

A one-month period with start and end dates defined by a contract day and contract hour; generally, offset from the corresponding calendar month because of the contract day and hour. Example A meter has a contract day of 5 and a contract hour of 7; in this case, the measurement month begins January 5th at 7 a.m. and ends February 5th at 7 a.m.; note that the first four days of February are included in the January measurement month.

Start / End date

Datetime for when the data starts and ends.

Time Leads vs. Time Trails data

Proprietary term indicating where an interval of time is recorded within the beginning and ending timestamps. This is defined at the meter level, by setting the Data Span field within the meter characteristics. Example The period of 1:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. is either labeled at the 13:00 hour (time leads data) or the 14:00 hour (time trails data) in the computer logs.

Timestamp

A date and time expressed as an integer and representing the number of seconds elapsed since 12/31/1969 @ 18:00:00. Time zones and Daylight Saving Time are not considered.

docs.title: Data-Related
docs.text:
Correlation Factor (also known as VCF and CF)

A factor used to compensate for the inherent inaccuracy associated with calculating volumes from averages of the flowing parameters as opposed to the actual instantaneous values used by the original flow-computing device. This factor is only required for recalculation purposes, but it is also useful as a validation parameter and is a term unique to the FLOWCAL system. Ideally, the VCF calculated by FLOWCAL will be at or near 1.0. For more information, see: Understanding Correlation Factors for Liquid Meters and Understanding Volume Correlation Factors for Gas Meters.

Exception

Exceptions are created when suspect data for a meter, location or quality source is imported or added as an edit.

Measured Conditions versus Standard Conditions

**Measured** - Volume is shown at the meter pressure base and temperature base. **Standard** - Volume shown at the system pressure base, temperature base, and system units.

Original Data versus Current Data

**Original** - Original data import from the field, which imports into FLOWCAL as revision 0. **Current **- Current data is the most current record revision. Example A record is imported and is original data from the field, which is stored as revision 0. The user applies an analysis to the record and it is recalculated. The edited record is stored as revision 1. Revision 1 is the current data record. Revision 0 remains the original data record.

Rollups or Final Form Data

Process by which hourly or 15-minute numbers are summed or averaged to get an hourly, daily, and monthly total or average used for reporting. This is done by FLOWCAL's meter and location rollups services.

docs.title: Feature-Related
docs.text:
Fluid Phase

Refers to the type of product the meter measured. FLOWCAL supports two fluid phases: gas and liquid. Gas is used for meters flowing products such as natural gas and helium. Liquid is used for meters flowing products such as crude oil, NGL, Y-grade, and refined products.

Lists versus Locations versus Close Groups

Lists are used to create logical combinations of meters, locations, and quality sources for importing, viewing, and exporting data, and generating reports. Lists are not datetime effective. Locations are used in FLOWCAL for many reasons, including calculating total volume, energy and mass for multiple meters; calculating lost and unaccounted for volume, energy, and mass such as on a pipeline segment; calculating inventory. Locations are the basis for tanks, liquid caverns, and gas inventory locations; comparison locations allow for comparing a meter to another meter, a location to another location or a location to a meter. Close groups are date-effective groups of meters that allow the user to close meters in bulk. Meters can only belong to one close group at a time.

Reports versus Exports

Reports are created with Crystal Reports and are access from the Standard Reports screen. Reports can be previewed in the Crystal Viewer that is standard with FLOWCAL and can be exported to several different formats, such as PDF. Exports are typically made available through DLL files to export data. Running an export often generates a file such as XLS, which can be further manipulated. FLOWCAL ships with several standard exports, which can be accessed from the Export menu.

System versus Application

System-level settings allows a user to manage security for users, groups, and objects within each system independently. Users can also configure many system- specific settings such as System Factors, System Units, System Options, and Rollup Options. This is a powerful tool that allows a user to have several systems within one database. By default, FLOWCAL ships with one system called Enterprise. There is no limit as to the number of systems that can be created and because security is defined within each system, one user could have full access to one system and its objects and no access or read-only access to another. The application settings are a level higher than systems in that application settings affect all systems, like Service Configuration.

docs.title: Import-Related
docs.text:
CFX

Proprietary binary file format to bring flow data and configuration information from meters into FLOWCAL.

PFX

Proprietary binary file format used to bring meter prove data from liquid meters into FLOWCAL and PROVEit.

TFX

Proprietary binary file format to bring volume and accounting information from run tickets and gauge tickets (pipelines, LACTs, trucks, rail cars, marine vessels, or tank tickets) into FLOWCAL.

Transaction Queue (TQ)

The Transaction Queue service (FcSrvTrans.exe) is a Windows service that can be installed on the application server to import data into FLOWCAL on a near real-time basis. The Transaction Queue consists of two database tables (FC\_ TRANSACTION_QUEUE and FC_TRANSACTION_SNAPSHOT) to which external processes insert rows corresponding to various transactions.

docs.title: User Preferences
docs.text:
Users can configure personalized settings that are used throughout the application. For example: If you set a default system, then when you access a screen that requires a system selection, the System field will already be populated with the default system you specified.

Settings are specific to each user.

To access the User Preferences screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **User Preferences** in the **User Settings** group.

User Preferences Screen Details

The following items are available on the User Preferences screen: - **Message Path** - The location of import messages created during the manual import process. Click the **Browse** button to select a folder where the file will be saved (example: D:\Flow-Cal\Logfiles). Each time a location or list is imported, a file is created with the list or location name and a .txt file extension. If you do not define a message path, the import messages will not be stored in a permanent file. - **Graph Centric** - If enabled, the Volume Editor will automatically display the data in graphical form instead of in a tabular grid. You can also switch between tabular and graphical mode from the Volume Editor **File** menu. - **Batch Import Mismatch Pause** - If enabled, a manual list or location import will pause if a meter number in the CFX import file does not match the FLOWCAL meter number it is being imported into. During this pause, you can review the discrepancy and elect to cancel or continue the import. (This feature only applies to manual import of CFX files.) - **Volume Editor Auto Open** - If enabled, FLOWCAL will remember the value of the Auto option in the Volume Editor for the duration of your FLOWCAL session. This option is enabled by default. - **Remember UI Filter Values** - If enabled, FLOWCAL will remember your filter settings in the Exception Resolver, Meter/Location Rollups Viewer, Volume Editor, and Standard Reports for the duration of your FLOWCAL session. Area Filters Remembered Exception Resolver
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Date range type and selection
  • Type filters, time filter, status filters, sort by, severity filter, and max rows
Meter/Location Rollups Viewer
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Date range type and selection
  • Data resolution, options, by location, by meter, revision, quantity, closed, conditions, net allowable and inventory
Volume Editor
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Object number (meter number is not remembered)
  • Auto
  • Month and year
  • FLOWCAL explorer (pinned or unpinned)
Standard Reports
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Date range type and selection
  • Report list selection, level, resolution, volume/energy, revision, and number of decimals
- **Hide Virtual Batches** - If enabled, virtual batches will be hidden. - **Virtual Batch Hide Duration** - If the Hide Virtual Batches option is enabled, you can specify a minimum batch length to hide. This allows users to hide short gaps, but show longer gaps where data may be missing. The time period is denoted in hours, minutes and seconds, defaulted to 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 0 seconds. - If you leave the default value at 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 0 seconds, all virtual batches are hidden. - If you change the value to 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 5 seconds, only virtual batches less than or equal to five seconds in length are hidden, but virtual batches greater than five seconds in length are shown. - **Default System** - Selecting a default system automatically populates the System drop-down field on any FLOWCAL screen that requires a system to be specified. - **Notes Visibility** - This designation sets the default visibility for notes that a user creates. Options are: - **Everyone** - Anyone in the FLOWCAL application can see the note and it can be printed on reports such as Batch Ticket. - **Internal** - Anyone in the FLOWCAL application can see the note and it can be printed on reports such as Batch Ticket when the option to print internal notes is enabled. - **Private** - Only the person who entered the note can see it in FLOWCAL. It will not be printed on any reports. - **Preferred Location** - Selecting a preferred location makes the selected location the default location when entering the Location Tree Editor. - **Default Personality** (TESTit 2 Integrated only) - Defines the default application personality to be used upon initial login. - **Default Fluid Phase** - Defines the default fluid phase (gas or liquid) to be used upon creation of a new meter, location, or source analysis.

docs.title: What Is FLOWCAL?
docs.text: FLOWCAL Enterprise was developed as a corporate solution for demanding system requirements, minimizing the efforts required for managing a complex measurement department. Throughout the measurement industry, companies in the exploration and production, midstream, pipeline, and local distribution sectors use this integrated system to validate, balance, store, and report gas and liquid measurement data.

docs.title: Consolidation
docs.text: The FLOWCAL system is a comprehensive, integrated software package that manages electronic gas and liquid measurement data from the field to the corporate accounting system. FLOWCAL displays all your data in one place, providing a single location for you to review and edit information, and a complete audit trail compliant with all industry standards.

docs.title: Data Quality
docs.text:
FLOWCAL interfaces with all major SCADA systems, polling engines, and flow computer manufacturers to automate the import process from your field devices. With more than 150 configurable validation set points, FLOWCAL identifies even the smallest flow anomalies out of massive amounts of data, and alerts the measurement team of potential errors.

Additionally, FLOWCAL’s advanced system balancing and inventory management feature displays gain/loss data so you can put those dollars back where they belong.

docs.title: Distribution Schedules
docs.text: FLOWCAL offers a built-in report scheduler so that you can automatically distribute tickets, volume statements and other reports to management, customers or accounting without lifting a finger.

docs.title: Customer Support
docs.text: For more information, visit the Quorum Software website or contact Customer Support (281-956-4500).

docs.title: Additional Import Drivers
docs.text:
FLOWCAL provides drivers for many manufacturer native file formats. The table below shows the typical configuration of these drivers. Some driver types require additional information.

Two generic option fields, Option 1 and Option 2, will display in FLOWCAL depending on the driver selected and should be populated as noted below.

All import configurations require Import Path.

Driver Notes Details Applied.dll

Driver for Applied Automation TotalFlow flow computers

Typical collection files have CFX extension

Filename: The name portion of the collection file

Option 1: n/a

Option 2: n/a

Bristol.dll
  • Driver for Bristol TeleFlow flow computers
  • There are typically three collection files with extensions of CFG, AUD and HLY
  • This driver uses a mapping file with the extension FCS to map Bristol signal names to FLOWCAL data points

Filename: The name portion of the collection files

Option 1: The name of the FCS file

Option 2: The name portion of the CFG file if different

ChartAtf.dll
  • File is output by Chart-32 chart integration software
  • One file per meter
  • Extension is typically ATF, any extension will work

Filename: The name and extension of the import file

Option 1: n/a

Option 2: n/a

CtrlWave.dll
  • Driver for Bristol ControlWave RTUs
  • There are typically three collection files with extensions of CFG, AUD and HLY
  • This driver uses a mapping file with the extension FCS to map ControlWave signal names to FLOWCAL data points

Filename: The name portion of the collection files

Option 1: The name portion of the FCS file

Option 2: The name portion of the CFG file if different

FcLiq01.dll

  • A minimal driver for simple liquid periodic flow data, no characteristics
  • One file per meter

Filename: The name and extension of the import file

Option 1: n/a

Option 2: n/a

OMNIs can output a text file called a 701 report that can be configured to match our FcLiq01 format.

Fisher.dll
  • Driver for Fisher ROC flow computers
  • The import file will typically have an extension of AGA or DET, depending on the version of EFM

Filename: The name and extension of the import file

Option 1: Run or tube number within the file

Option 2: n/a

If the flow computer uses AGA7 calculation, then Option 1 may also include an asterisk (*) which will adjust the pulse count by a factor of 1000. For example, Option 1 = 3* would mean run 3 and adjust the count by a factor of 1000.

FlowAuto.dll
  • Driver for Flow Automation brand flow computers. Common models include SuperFlo, AutoPILOT and AutoMATE
  • This driver requires that either the Import ID or Meter Number in FLOWCAL match the Meter Name in the flow computer
  • The usual collection file names are MBS##.DIR and MBS##.DAT
  • The files can contain data for multiple meters and multiple data sets for each meter
  • To see a list of meters and datasets in a file, set Option 1 to "LIST" in the override section of the manual import screen; this will display a list of meter names. FLOWCAL will only look for and import Periodic data, not Daily

Filename: The last node in the path to where the import files are located, or the DAT file prefix if not MBS##; do not repeat the last node in the path

Option 1: Unused in normal use

Option 2: Entry number; if blank, the last/latest data set in the file for this meter is used

LQTicket.dll
  • Driver for liquid meters set up in run ticket mode (See: [Meter Editor > Liquids tab > Setup sub-tab](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Liquids%20Tab.md#Setup))
  • The import files can contain data for multiple meters
  • The file extension is LQT; any extension will work for manual imports
  • This driver requires that the meter numbers in the file match the meter numbers in FLOWCAL; import IDs are not used
  • The driver requires the file to use encoding UTF-8

Filename: The name and extension of the import file

Option 1: n/a

Option 2: n/a

Mercury1.dll
  • Driver for Mercury Mini-Max and Mini-AT correctors
  • There are typically two collection files with extensions ATM and ADT
  • ADT files contain the flow data for one meter
  • ATM files contain meter specific values

Filename: Name portion of the ATM/ADT files

Option 1: n/a

Option 2: n/a

Mercury2.dll*
  • Driver for Mercury Mini-Max and Mini-AT correctors
  • This must be configured in the [Meter Editor](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Imports%20Tab.md); cannot use overrides during manual import
  • There are typically two collection files with extensions CSD and ITM
  • CSD files contain flow data and may contain data for multiple meters
  • ITM files contain meter specific values. The ITM file name must match the FLOWCAL meter number or must be specified in either Option 1 or import ID

Filename: Name portion of the CSD file

Option 1: Name portion of the ITM file if different from meter number

Option 2: n/a

Reynolds.dll*
  • Driver for Reynolds Pro flow computers
  • There are typically two collection files with the same file name and the extensions PRO and IDB
  • The files contain data for one flow meter

Filename: Name portion of the PRO/IDB files.

Option 1: n/a

Option 2: n/a

Stndcfx.dll A CFX (Common File Exchange) file is a proprietary binary file format used to bring meter flow data and configuration information into FLOWCAL. It is used to import data from a variety of meter manufacturers.

* These drivers are not supported by the File Import service. They are only available when manually importing data using the Import > Meter Data screen.

The Stndtfx and Stndpfx drivers cannot be loaded. These import drivers are automatically used by FLOWCAL when importing tickets or PROVEit files, respectively.
