docs.title: Import Capacity Table
docs.text:
This function requires the Liquids add-on.

A capacity tableA table showing the capacities or volumes of a tank for various liquid levels measured from the reference gauge point; also known as a strapping table, tank capacity table or calibration table. (strapping table) can be manually entered from the Tank Editor or imported from a tab-delimited file available from Customer Support.

The import process supports import of a single or multiple tanks, and a single capacity table or multiple tables in the same file.

Each capacity table belongs to a specified tank and is datetime effectiveDatetime effective records have a defined start date and time and a defined end date and time.. Capacity tables are identified by name, and a tank may have more than one capacity table. Reasons for having multiple capacity tables include separate tables for high-leg and low-leg roof configurations, and alternate tables that depend on product density.

FLOWCAL does not automatically switch between available capacity tables. Users must manually maintain the active table via the Tank Editor Characteristics tab.

Tanks are not auto-created during the capacity table import process, so the tank associated with the table must exist in FLOWCAL prior to importing a file.

To import a capacity table: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Capacity Table**. 2. Click the browse button next to the **Import File** field to select the text file to import, or type the file path into the field. 3. Click the **Import** button. A dialog box will display, providing information about the import. 4. When the import is complete, go to **Setup** \> **Tank Editor** \> **Tools** \> **Capacity Table** to view the imported data.

If capacity tables already exist for a tank, they will be split as needed to account for the date and time of the imported tables. If the date and time of an imported table encompass existing gauge tickets and tank run tickets, these tickets will not be automatically recalculated. Each ticket will need to be manually edited and confirmed when the import is complete and validations have been performed.

A capacity table can be entered or imported manually. The file import service does not support the import of capacity tables.

Capacity Table File Format

Contact Customer Support to obtain the Capacity Table file format. The following is additional information regarding the import of capacity tables: - When importing a capacity table for a tank, the first record must be a header row, followed by the table rows for the tank. If there is no header record, the capacity table will not import. Header records contain general information about the capacity table. - After the header record, any number of table records can be imported. Table records contain tank levels and volumes. Each table record must have a level and either the volume at the given level, or the volume per increment and the number of increments per zone. If a record has incomplete parameters, an error message will be generated. - If values for **Total Volume for the Tank at Specified Tank Level** and **Volume per Increment for the Zone/Increments in the Zone** are imported, the imported volume at level will be validated against the calculated volume at that level, based on the incremental volumes. If a record has inconsistent volumes, an error message will be generated. - A shell temperature correction must be applied to all tanks with volumes greater than 5,000 bbl. If the total calculated volume for the tank exceeds 5,000 barrels, the **Apply Shell Temperature Correction, CTSh** field in the Capacity Table Setup screen will automatically be set to "true" regardless of the original import value.

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: Import Contractual Limits
docs.text:
Contractual limits can be manually entered from the Master Characteristics screen* or from a tab-delimited file (contact Customer Support to obtain the file format).

* This method requires the Master Characteristics module.

The import process supports the import of data for a single meter or multiple meters in the same file.

Contractual limits belong to a specified meter and are datetime effectiveDatetime effective records have a defined start date and time and a defined end date and time.. Meters are not auto-created during the contractual limit import process, so the meters associated with the data must exist in FLOWCAL prior to importing a file.

To import a contractual limits file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Contractual Limits**. 2. Click the browse button next to the Import File field to select the import file (example: C:\data\ContractualLimits.txt), or type the file path in the field. 3. Click the **Import** button. The process bar next to the Import button will display the percentage of the file completed as it is processed. Any errors generated during the import process will be displayed in the messages window. 4. Go to **Setup**\> **Meter** \> **Master Data Validation** to view the imported data. Contractual limits can be entered or imported manually. The file import service does not support the import of contractual limits.

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: Import Prove Data
docs.text:
This function requires the Liquids add-on.

Importing Manually

Use the Manual Prove Import screen to import prove data created by PROVEit or an external SCADA system. The import process uses a PFX file to import data for a single prove or multiple proves. Prove data belongs to a specified meter and is date effective. Meters are not auto-created during the prove data import process, so meters associated with the prove data must exist in FLOWCAL prior to import. To import a PFX file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Prove Data**. 2. Select a meter. 3. Click the browse button beside the **File Name** field to select the PFX file, or type the file path into the field. Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit. 4. Click the **Import** button. If the PFX file includes a PDF of the prove report, the PDF will be imported and displayed in the Volume Editor. An "R" will display on a batch or periodic to indicate that a prove report is attached. If the PFX Recalc Method option in the Meter Editor is not set to **None, Import Prove PDF Only**, the resultant meter factor from the prove report will be applied back to the start of the batch that encompasses the meter prove, and the periodic records will be recalculated.

Importing Using the File Import Service

PFX files can be imported into FLOWCAL using the File Import Service. In order for FLOWCAL to map the prove reports to the correct meters the Proving Import ID for the meter must match the device number in the PFX file. The path to the folder that holds the PFX files must also be specified in [Service Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Configuration.md). If the PFX file includes a PDF of the prove report, the PDF will be imported and displayed in the Volume Editor. An “R” will display on the batch or periodic to indicate that the prove report is attached.

Importing into Multiple Meters

Users can import a single prove report into multiple meters using the File Import service. To support this type of import, the device number in the report is mapped to the Proving Import ID in the Meter Editor. When a PFX file is imported, the prove report will be saved to every meter that bears the corresponding Proving Import ID. To apply a prove report to multiple meters, all of the meters must have the Proving Import ID populated with the device number in the PFX file. If all prove reports are successfully applied, then the file will be marked with "\_R\_\" to indicate that the import was successful. If the prove report fails to import into any of the meters, the file will be marked with "\_F\_\" to indicate that the import failed. ##### Meter Factor & Product Validation If an attempt is made to import a prove report into a meter where one already exists, FLOWCAL will compare the meter factor and product of the prove report in the database to what is in the PFX file. If the meter factor in the database does not match the meter factor in the file then an exception is generated (5601) and the file is renamed as failed. If the product in the database does not match the product in the file then an exception is generated (5603) and the file is renamed as failed. ##### Meter Locking If an attempt is made to import a PFX file into a meter that is locked, that meter import will be skipped and the PFX will be applied to the any other meters that it can. The file will not be marked as failed or successful; an attempt will be made to import the meters that were locked and skipped in a subsequent cycle.

docs.title: Import Source Analysis Text File
docs.text:
This function requires the Source Analysis module.

Use the Source Analysis Text File Import screen to import source analysis data for one or more sourcesThe basis of gas or liquid quality analysis as defined by the user; a source could be a physical sample or online chromatograph; it is a representative sample either manually entered or imported into FLOWCAL and utilized to calculate volumes, mass, components, and gas equivalent values in the form of a text file in the format specified by Quorum (contact Customer Support to obtain the file format). The imported source data can then be applied directly to one or more meters.

Refer to the appropriate text file import format document for additional information on the order of fields in the file and whether or not they have any restrictions or are required.

To import a source text file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Source Analysis Text File**. 2. Click the browse button next to the Import File field to find the import text file (ex. C:\data\01301-July.txt), or type the file path into the field. 3. Select **Specify Start Time** if the start time is different than what is in the file. If the start time in the file is correct, you do not need to select this option. 4. The **Specify End Time** option is not required for characteristic records. If the end time is omitted, the characteristic data will be applied until the end time specified in the file. If no end time is specified in the file, it will default to the end of time (1/18/2038) or until the next characteristic is uploaded. 5. If applicable, select **Source Analysis Number Field is Import ID**. If you are importing data from a third party and the source analysis number in the file is different than the source analysis number in FLOWCAL, you can set up the source analysis number as the import ID in the Quality Source Editor. This will designate the source to import the data into. 6. Select an edit reason from the **Reason** drop-down or manually enter an edit reason. 7. Click the **Import** button. 8. When the import is complete, go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Gas** or **Liquid Quality** to view the analysis data. If the source number in the import file is different from the source number in FLOWCAL, you must use the Import ID field to import your data. If the source number does not exist in FLOWCAL, the import fails unless the Auto Create option has been enabled for text file imports under the Service Configuration screen.

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: Import Ticket Data
docs.text:
This function requires the Liquids add-on.

Use the Manual Ticket Import screen to import ticket data using a TFX fileA proprietary binary file format used to import volume and accounting information from run tickets and gauge tickets (pipelines, LACTs, trucks, rail cars, marine vessels, or tank tickets) into FLOWCAL. or liquid text file.

The import process can import data for a single ticket or multiple tickets of different types using the same TFX or text file. The tank or location associated with the ticket data must exist in FLOWCAL prior to import.

A prior period adjustment (PPA) is automatically created when an imported ticket is attached to a Location and the ticket effective date is contained in a measurement month in which the location is closed. If a PPA is automatically created for the ticket, a location message will be generated upon import. If the PPAs Not Allowed option is enabled (Settings > Settings Manager > System > System Configuration > PPA Options), and a ticket is imported for a location that is closed for the month of the effective date of the ticket, the ticket will fail to import and a location message will be generated.

To import a TFX file or text file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Ticket Data**. 2. Click the browse button beside the **Folder or File Name** field to locate a TFX file or text file to import. 3. Use the drop-down menu in the lower right corner of the File Explorer window to specify whether the import will use a TFX file or text file. 1. Select the import file and click the **Open** button. 2. Click the **Import** button. A dialogue box will display the status of the import. When the import is complete, the data will be available in the Ticket Editor. Use the Ticket Search function to locate the imported ticket data.

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: Import Lab Analysis
docs.text:
If you do not have the Source Analysis module, you can use the Import Lab Analysis screen to import gas analysis sample data that uses Quorum's text file format.

The text file must be in the FLOWCAL lab analysis import format.

FLOWCAL will read the gas analysis sample contained in the text file, apply the gas sample to the meter and re-calculate volume and energy values as applicable. This process is often used to apply spot and/or composite samples received from a lab.

To import a lab analysis file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Lab Analysis**. 2. Click **Browse Files** to locate a text file to import (example: C:\data\01301-July.txt), or type the file path into the **File Name** field. 3. Specify an alternate file name if applicable. (See: [Alternate File Format](Lab%20Analysis%20Import%20Format.md#Alternate)) 4. Select **Specify Start Time** and **Specify End Time** to override the start time and end time in the analysis import file (if applicable). The import file end time is effective until the next calendar month, unless another analysis exists with a start time later than the first. If not overridden, the start and end dates will be the dates specified in the import file. If this option is used, it is recommended that both dates be overridden. Start Time and End Time Formats Three date and time formats are available when specifying start and end times: - For a specific date and time, use **mm/dd/yyyy hh:mi:ss**.\* - For a specific date with an implied time for the meter contract hour, use **mm/dd/yyyy**.\* - For a specific month and year with an implied date for the meter contract day and an implied time for the meter contract hour, use **mm/yyyy**. \*These formats are used most frequently. 5. Select **Force Recalc** to force a recalculation of the meter data with the analysis (if applicable). 6. Select a recalculation method (Recalculate Volumes or Recalculate VCFs) from the drop-down list. 7. Click **Import**.

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: Lab Analysis Import Format

docs.title: Lab Analysis Import Format
docs.text:
Two lab analysis import file formats are available in FLOWCAL.

Lab Analysis Import Format V1

Items are listed in a line in the following order: Meter Number Effective Date/Time Sample Date/Time Heating Value Relative Density CO2 mole% N2 mole% C1 mole% C2 mole% C3 mole% Isobutane mole% n-Butane mole% Isopentane mole% N-Pentane mole% Neopentane mole% C6 mole% C7 mole% O2 mole% H2O mole% H2S mole% He mole% Viscosity Specific Heat Ratio C8 mole% C9 mole% C10 mole% Ar mole% CO mole% H2 mole%

Lab Analysis Import Format V2

This file includes a header and the file body. The header ("VERSION=2") must be present for FLOWCAL to recognize and understand the file contents. The body is the same as Lab Analysis Import Format V1, but it also includes Btu condition and Pressure Base fields. Any analysis containing a Btu condition of "A" (as delivered) will be discarded if the station setup is anything other than "as delivered" (e.g., Dry, Wet, Calc). FLOWCAL will convert the analysis record Btu condition and pressure base to those reflected by the station description in the FLOWCAL database. Items are listed in the following order: Meter Number Effective Date/Time Sample Date/Time Heating Value Heating Value condition ('W'- Wet Saturated 'D'- dry 'A'- As delivered) Pressure Base Relative Density CO2 mole% N2 mole% C1 mole% C2 mole% C3 mole% Isobutane mole% n-Butane mole% Isopentane mole% n-pentane mole% Neopentane mole% C6 mole% C7 mole% O2 mole% H2O mole% H2S mole% He mole% Viscosity Specific Heat Ratio C8 mole% C9 mole% C10 mole% Ar mole% CO mole% H2 mole%

docs.title: Format Parameters
docs.text:
All lab analysis import files will use the following format:

  • The lab analysis import file should not exceed 255 characters.
  • There is one meter gas sample analysis record per line.
  • Blank lines and lines that start with #, ; or / are discarded as comments.
  • Each data point in a line is separated by spaces or commas. If commas are used as separators, extra spaces are ignored. When using the space-separated format, use a minus sign (-) to indicate a blank or skipped field.
  • Any field may be left blank. Additionally, all fields do not have to be present. Missing trailing fields are assumed to be blank or NULL.
  • Values for gas analysis mole percent fields should be a percentage in the range of 0 to 100.
  • Other special characters are the carat (^) or tilde (~), which are used to indicate numeric blank value, and the double quote (""), which is used to indicate that a field has the same value as the corresponding field on the previous line.
Example ; this is how a file containing gas analysis import information ; would look / The next record will update the CO2 and N2 / components to 5% and 3.25% respectively STA_NUM 10/1/2001 7:00 - - - 5 3.25 ; the next record does the same using a comma-delimited format STA_NUM,10/1/2001 7:00, , , ,5,3.25 ; the above 2 records also demonstrate skipped fields ; for sample date, btu, and gravity.

docs.title: Alternate File Format
docs.text:
This file contains a cross reference of meter numbers which must be updated with the lab analysis information of a meter found in the primary file (File Name). For every lab analysis record for a meter in the primary file, a corresponding record will be created and applied for every meter which references the meter found in the primary file.

  • This is a text file composed of lines of up to 255 characters in length.
  • Each line contains meter numbers separated by commas or spaces.
  • The first meter number in a line is a meter number which may be in the primary file.
  • The remaining meter numbers will use any gas analysis information found in the primary file which belongs to the first meter number mentioned above.
Example Primary file record: MET_NUM,2/1/2005,1/30/2005,,,,,, Alternate file line: MET_NUM, MET1, MET2, MET3 The record for MET_NUM will be used to update meters MET1, MET2, and MET3.

docs.title: External Volume Default Values Editor
docs.text:
Use the External Volume Default Values Editor to set up editing preferences and default meter values for the External Volume Interface. The default values will be used if values are not provided.

To access the External Volume Default Values Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter**. 2. Click **Default Values**. 3. Select a meter number from the drop-down menu. 4. Click the **Edit** button. 5. If applicable, select the preferences for volume/energy/mass and raw data/pulses.  For volume/enery/mass, you can select accumulation for the period (total volume/energy/mass) or the beginning volume index. The ending index will be the start index for the next period. This setting determines whether you will enter total raw volume or pulses or index values for raw volume and pulses. The meter will default to "Accumulation" for the period and "Pulses". These selections are only applicable to linear meters.  6. If applicable, enter default values for static pressure, heating value, and temperature. The meter will use these values initially, but they can be overridden manually. 7. Set the default seasonal temperatures. Specify season start dates on the [General tab](../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration%20-%20General%20Tab.md) of the System Configuration Options screen. 8. Click the **Save** button.

docs.title: Manual Meter Input
docs.text: This functionality is only available for gas meters.

docs.title: External Volume Interface
docs.text:
Use the External Volume Interface to manually enter data for any gas meter, including external volume meters. (A meter is defined as an External Volume meter by enabling this option from the Imports tab of the Meter Editor.) Once the data is imported, you can exit the External Volume Interface and view the data from the Volume Editor.

This import screen differs from other meter import screens because users can manually enter energy values.

The meter drop-down defaults to "External Volume Meters Only." To select a gas meter from the meter drop-down, the "Can enter data for any meter" System Configuration option must be enabled.

Manually Entering Data

To manually enter data using the External Volume Interface: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Manual Entry** \> **Meter Input**. 2. Select the **External Volume Meters Only** option to filter the meter drop-down by external volume meters only. 3. Click the **Browse** button to find a text file to import (example: C:\data\01301-July.txt), or type the file path into the edit box. 4. Select the meter number or meter name from the drop-down. 5. Select **Contract Month** or **Contract Day(s)** for the date range. 6. Click **OK**. 7. To enter daily data, check the **Enter daily data** option. To enter monthly data, leave the **Enter daily data** option unchecked. 8. Enter the volume, energy, heating value, differential pressure, static pressure, and/or temperature. For positive displacement meters, enter the appropriate data for the applicable dates. 9. Leave the **Do not calculate heating value** option unchecked to have FLOWCAL calculate a heating value automatically. 10. Select the **Enter Mass** option to enter mass. 11. Select values for the contract day and hour. 12. Select the data resolution (15-minute, 1 hour, or 1 day). 13. Select **Leading** or **Trailing** for the data span. 14. Click the **Analysis** tab to manually enter analysis data. 15. Click the **Characteristics** tab to manually enter characteristics data. 16. Click **Import**.

Manual Data Entry Screen Details

The following items are available on the Manual Data Entry screen: - **Analysis** – Click this button to open the source assigned to the meter for the date range selected. - **Change** – Click this button to change meter number or data range. - **For DP, Pres., and Temp.** - **Fill blanks with monthly value** – When a range total differential pressure, pressure, and/or temperature is entered, select this option and click Fill In to automatically populate the same values for all daily records containing volume or pulses. - **Fill blanks with previous day’s value** – When a differential pressure, pressure, and/or temperature is entered for a daily record, select this option and click Fill In to automatically populate the same values for all subsequent daily records containing volume or pulses. - **Tab Order** - **Full Row** – Select this option to tab across the entire row, left to right, from Volume to Temperature. - **Half Row** – Select this option to tab across the left side of the row, from Volume to Heating Value. Upon reaching the last row or daily record, pressing Tab will navigate to the right half of the row, from Differential Pressure to Temperature.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: External Volume Import Options

docs.title: Manual Planimeter Entry
docs.text:
This functionality is only available for gas meters.

Use the Planimeter Entry screen to calculate the process variable for differential pressure, static pressure, and temperature for a specific meter for a specified date. You can provide manual values for the process variables, or, if the transducer ranges are set within the meter’s characteristics, you can provide a planimeter read. The process variable will then be calculated based on the planimeter read and ranges.

Before entering planimeter data, transducer low and high ranges for differential pressure, static pressure, and temperature must be set in the Volume Editor (Characteristics > Ranges tab).

Manually Entering Data

To manually enter planimeter data: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Manual Entry** \> **Planimeter**. 2. Enter the planimeter reads to calculate the process variables ((read\*read)/100\*(high-low)+low); otherwise, enter the manual values to populate the process variables. When all three process variables are populated, the Import button will be enabled. 3. Click **Import** to import the process variables to the meter flow data or analysis.

Planimeter Entry Screen Details

The following items are available on the Plaimeter Entry screen: #### Ranges - If the transducer low and high ranges for differential pressure, static pressure, and temperature have not been set up in Meter Characteristics, the ranges will display as "0 – X" in red. - If the transducer low ranges for differential pressure, static pressure, and temperature have not been set up in Meter Characteristics, but the high range has, the ranges will display as "0 – configured high range" in red. - If the low and high ranges for differential pressure, static pressure, and temperature have both been set up in Meter Characteristics, the ranges will display the associated ranges in black. #### Planimeter Read - If the transducer low and high ranges for differential pressure, static pressure, and temperature have not been set up in Meter Characteristics, the Planimeter Read edit boxes are disabled. - If the Manual Value edit boxes have been entered, the Planimeter Read edit boxes are disabled. - Planimeter read values must be numbers between 0 and 10. #### Manual Value - The Manual Value edit boxes are enabled only if corresponding Planimeter Read edit boxes are empty.

docs.title: Import Meter Data
docs.text:
FLOWCAL has the ability to import gas or liquid meter data using a CFX fileA proprietary binary file format used to bring meter flow data and configuration information into FLOWCAL.. A flow computer or SCADA system will generate a CFX file that can contain meter flow history, meter configuration, events, alarms, product information and/or analysis data. This data is brought into FLOWCAL for calculation and balancing purposes. The data can be validated on import to see if there are any discrepancies and/or exceptions on the imported data.

To manually import a file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Meter Data**. 2. Choose a meter, location or list to import data into. 3. If you choose a list or location, you can select **Use Start Date** and enter a starting date for data. This filters out data recorded prior to the selected time. By default, FLOWCAL only imports the last 35 days of data it finds for each meter. When importing for a single meter, you can preview the data in the Volume Editor before saving any data. When importing by list or location, all meters in the list or location will be imported. You will then need to review data in the Volume Editor and purge or edit any incorrect data. 4. Click the browse button beside the **Folder or File Name** field to select the CFX file, or type the file path into the field. 5. **Optional:** Select a driver (typically STNDCFX). If the meter has already been set up in the Meter Editor with the correct import path and import driver, this is not necessary. 6. Click the **Import** button. 7. When the Volume Editor displays, review the data to make sure it has imported correctly. 8. Go to **Data** \> **Save** and close the Volume Editor.

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: Additional Import Drivers

docs.title: Import Gas Meter Text File
docs.text:
Use the Text File Import screen to bring in data from a text file that uses Quroum's text file format (contact Customer Support for the file format). The file can be used to import gas meter data for one or more meters.

To import a gas meter text file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Gas Meter Text File**. 2. Click the **Browse** button to locate a text file to import (example: C:\data\01301-July.txt), or type the file path into the **Import File** field. 3. Select the data resolution (Meter Characteristic, 15 Minute, 1 Hour, or 1 Day). If you select "Meter Characteristic", FLOWCAL uses the resolution defined in the meter characteristic data. 4. If applicable, select **Treat records with same start and end date as daily record**. With this option enabled, a record with the same start and end date will be imported as a daily record for that date. Example If a record starts on 3/1/2016 and ends on 3/1/2016, the data will be imported for 3/1/2016. If this option is not enabled, an error message will display, stating that the end date cannot match the start date. 5. If applicable, select **Meter number field is Import ID**. If you are importing data from a third party, and the meter number in the file is different from the meter number in FLOWCAL, you can set the third-party meter number as the import ID within the Meter Editor.  If the meter number does not exist in FLOWCAL, the import will fail unless the Auto Create option has been enabled for text file imports. (See: [Service Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Configuration.md))

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: Import Liquid Meter Text File
docs.text:
This function requires the Liquids add-on.

Use the Text File Import screen to bring in data from a text file that uses Quorum's text file format (contact Customer Support for the file format). The file can be used to import liquid meter data for one or more meters.

To import a liquid meter text file: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Liquid Meter Text File**. 2. Click the **Browse** button to locate a text file to import (example: C:\data\01301-July.txt), or type the file path into the **Import File** field. 3. If applicable, select **Meter number field is Import ID**. If you are importing data from a third party, and the meter number in the file is different from the meter number in FLOWCAL, you can set the third-party meter number as the import ID within the Meter Editor.  If the meter number does not exist in FLOWCAL, the import will fail unless the Auto Create option has been enabled for text file imports. (See: [Service Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Configuration.md))

You can also use the File Import Service to import text files manually or automatically. (See: Configure Imports)

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: Positive Displacement Entry - Daily
docs.text:
This functionality is only available for gas meters.

Use the PD Entry Daily screen to quickly enter positive displacement and turbine meter index readings, single or daily pressures and temperatures, and daily pulse counts or uncorrected volumes from which FLOWCAL will calculate the corrected volume if characteristics and analyses are in place.

Upon creating a new entry, the previous "Off" information (off date, off hour, and off reading) is used as the "On" information for the new entry.

Data Entry Formats Date

Six-digit MMDDYY format; includes leading zeroes

Example: February 4, 2007 = 040207

Hour

Two-digit, 24-hour HH format; includes leading zero

Example: 9 am = 03; 9 pm = 21

Reading

Number-of-dials digits; includes leading zeroes

Example: Number of dials = 6 ® index reading is six digits: 004321

Entering Data Manually

To enter data in the PD Entry Daily screen: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Positive Displacement** \> **Daily Entry**. 2. Select a meter. If the meter is not a positive displacement meter or turbine meter, a warning will display. 3. Click **New** to enter new index readings. 4. If no data exists for the meter, the first empty cell will be **On Date**. If there is existing data for the meter, the first empty cell will be **Off Date**. 5. Enter an on date and on hour. 6. Enter the on reading. 7. Enter the three off values the same way you entered the on values. The difference between the on and off readings is automatically calculated. Rollover values are handled by the calculations. By default, the reading values and the difference are stored as pulses. To store the readings and differences as raw volume, select that option in **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Default Values**. 8. To enter a daily pressure, check the "Daily Pressure" option. To enter a daily temperature, check the "Daily Temperature" option. 9. Based on the On Date and Off Date values, the row for each day in the date range becomes available for entering daily values. The first column is for pulse count/raw volume entry. Depending on the options selected, the second column is for pressure and the third column is temperature. 10. As daily data is entered, the Daily Volume Running Total field will contain a running sum of the on reading plus each day's pulse count/raw volume. 11. Click **Save** to import the pulse count/raw volume, pressure, and temperature data. To use this function, the Transaction Queue service must be installed and running.

Data Entry Parameters

| Field | Format Requirements | |----|----| | On Date/Off Date | 6 numeric digits (MMDDYY) | | On Hour/Off Hour | 2 numeric digits (HH); use a leading 0 for single-digit hours | | On Reading/Off Reading | Number of digits corresponds to the number of dials on the meter; this value is set in Meter Characteristics; if no value is specified, the default number is 6 |

Read Tolerances

Read tolerances (in days) may be set for monthly records on the **Meter Editor** \> **Reports** tab. Records with an actual (entered) on date within the read tolerance will be snapped to contract start of month. Records with an actual (entered) off date within the read tolerance will be snapped to the contract end of month. PD Entry Daily will not save: - Long records with on or off dates outside the read tolerances. - Records dated in the future. Both the on and off dates must occur before the date of entry. Off dates must occur after on dates.

docs.title: Positive Displacement Entry - By List
docs.text:
This functionality is only available for gas meters.

Use the PD Entry by List screen to quickly enter index readings for positive displacement and turbine meters from which FLOWCAL will calculate the net raw volume and distribute it evenly across the date range.

The previous removed (Off) information is used as the current placed (On) information.

Tip - Keyboard Entry The PD Entry by List screen is designed to be used with your keyboard's numeric key pad. You can type values into the grid and press the **Enter** key to navigate to the next cell. Real-time validations will occur when you follow this process. You can also navigate the grid using the mouse, but in this case, the data will not validate until you click the **Import** button.

Entering Data Manually

To enter data in the PD Entry by List screen: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Positive Displacement** \> **Entry by List**. 2. Select a list, location, or individual meter. - If you select a meter that is not a positive displacement or turbine meter, a beep will sound and a message ("Not a turbine or displacement meter") will display at the bottom of the screen. - If you select a list or location, all of the positive displacement meters and turbine meters that you have access to will display in the grid. 3. By default, meter/location numbers are used in the drop-down and on the grid. Click the **Use Names** checkbox beneath the grid to display meter/location names instead of numbers. 4. After selecting your meter/location number, press **Tab** to navigate to the first empty grid cell to enter your data. If no data exists for the meter, the first empty cell will be **On Date**. If there is existing data for the meter, the first empty cell will be **Off Date**. 5. The difference between the on and off readings is automatically calculated. Rollover values are handled by the calculations. By default, the reading values and the difference are stored as pulses. To store the readings and differences as raw volume, select that option in **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Default Values**. 6. FLOWCAL provides the ability to set default pressures and temperatures. You can specify these values in **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Default Values**. If these values are set up, the grid will display them for new entries. You may overwrite them with updated values or skip over them as desired. If these value are not set up, the grid fields will be empty and you must provide the values. 7. The resolution (Daily, Hourly, or As Is) will display based on the meter's characteristic data resolution for the specified time frame. As Is resolution will write one record for the specified time frame. Daily resolution will split the difference in readings across the appropriate number of days and write daily records for the specified time frame. 8. When you press **Enter**, the data will validate and your cursor will navigate to the next row. 9. If there are no more rows with meters, click **Import** or press **Enter** to import the data. Additional validations are performed on the data before writing it to the database. Any errors found during these validations will display on the Messages tab and written to the log file. To use this function, the Transaction Queue service must be installed and running.

Data Entry Parameters

| Field | Format Requirements | |----|----| | On Date/Off Date | 6 numeric digits (MMDDYY) | | On Hour/Off Hour | 2 numeric digits (HH); use a leading 0 for single-digit hours | | On Reading/Off Reading | Number of digits corresponds to the number of dials on the meter; this value is set in Meter Characteristics; if no value is specified, the default number is 6 | If a value does not have the correct number of digits, the system will beep and a message will display in the status bar. The cursor will not advance, and the invalid data will be highlighted.

Read Tolerances

Read tolerances (in days) may be set for monthly records on the **Meter Editor** \> **Reports** tab. Records with an actual (entered) on date within the read tolerance will be snapped to contract start of month. Records with an actual (entered) off date within the read tolerance will be snapped to the contract end of month. PD Entry by List will not save: - Long records with on or off dates outside the read tolerances. - Records dated in the future. Both the on and off dates must occur before the date of entry. Off dates must occur after on dates.

docs.title: Positive Displacement Entry - With History
docs.text:
This functionality is only available for gas meters.

Use the PD Entry with History screen to quickly enter index readings for positive displacement and turbine meters from which FLOWCAL will calculate the uncorrected and corrected volume, and distribute it evenly across the date range.

The PD Entry with History function is similar to PD Entry by List, but it also displays the history of entries for the selected meter.

The previous removed (Off) information is used as the current placed (On) information.

Tip - Keyboard Entry The PD Entry With History screen is designed to be used with your keyboard's numeric key pad. You can type values into the grid and press the **Enter** key to navigate to the next cell.

Entering Data Manually

To enter data in the PD Entry with History screen: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Positive Displacement** \> **Entry with History**. 2. Select a meter. If the meter is not a positive displacement meter or turbine meter, a warning will display. 3. Select a time filter to view the history for the meter. 4. Click **New** to enter new index readings. 5. Enter the required data. If no data exists for the meter, the first empty cell will be **On Date**. If there is existing data for the meter, the first empty cell will be **Off Date**. 6. The difference between the on and off readings is automatically calculated. Rollover values are handled by the calculations. By default, the reading values and the difference are stored as pulses. To store the readings and differences as raw volume, select that option in **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Default Values**. 7. FLOWCAL provides the ability to set default pressures and temperatures. You can specify these values in **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Default Values**. If these values are set up, the grid will display them for new entries. You may overwrite them with updated values or skip over them as desired. If these value are not set up, the grid fields will be empty and you must provide the values. The As Is resolution will write one record for the specified time frame. Daily resolution will split the difference in readings across the appropriate number of days and write daily records for the specified time frame. 8. Click **Save** to import the new index readings. To use this function, the Transaction Queue service must be installed and running.

Data Entry Parameters

| Field | Format Requirements | |----|----| | On Date/Off Date | 6 numeric digits (MMDDYY) | | On Hour/Off Hour | 2 numeric digits (HH); use a leading 0 for single-digit hours | | On Reading/Off Reading | Number of digits corresponds to the number of dials on the meter; this value is set in Meter Characteristics; if no value is specified, the default number is 6 |

Read Tolerances

Read tolerances (in days) may be set for monthly records on the **Meter Editor** \> **Reports** tab. Records with an actual (entered) on date within the read tolerance will be snapped to contract start of month. Records with an actual (entered) off date within the read tolerance will be snapped to the contract end of month. PD Entry with History will not save: - Long records with on or off dates outside the read tolerances. - Records dated in the future. Both the on and off dates must occur before the date of entry. Off dates must occur after on dates.

docs.title: Scheduled Batch Movement
docs.text:
Pipeline companies typically match meter batches to scheduled batch movements when scheduling batches to be injected into a pipeline at a given point (the receipt point). Pipeline operations will also schedule those same batches to come off the pipeline at a different point (the delivery point). These schedules can then be imported into FLOWCAL.

As the meter batches are imported or manually entered, FLOWCAL can then match the meter batches to the scheduled batch movement based on delivery and receipt point, and the time and amount of the batch. FLOWCAL will model a single batch movement between delivery and receipt points by comparing the batches of meter members within two locations based on product, origin, destination, start time (both origin and destination), and the batch size (configured as GSV, NSV, or mass).

A single batch movement will be associated to at least two meters in two locations.

The purpose of having two different locations is to create an association to a batch movement between two different FLOWCAL meters that exist physically at the delivery and receipt points. This gives FLOWCAL enough information to narrow down a batch product and match on criteria as it travels from one location in the pipeline (the origin), to the delivery point in the pipeline (the destination).

The delivery and receipt points being at the location level within FLOWCAL allows for multiple meters to be located where batches are being injected into or coming off the pipeline.

The meters located at the receipt and delivery points represent the start and end points (respectively) of the batch movement from the left to the right in the diagram. The area enclosed on the left is the Origin location to be configured and the area enclosed on the right is the Destination location to be configured.

Example The origin of a batch movement is Location 1 and the destination of the movement is Location 2. A scheduled batch movement is imported with a start and end date at the origin of 12/01/2018 09:00:00 – 12/01/12:00:00 for a batch size of GSV = 2000. The scheduled batch movement also defines the start and end date for the destination to be 12/1/2018 13:00:00 – 12/1/2018 16:00:00. Since the origin and destination of the batch movement correspond to Location 1 and Location 2, FLOWCAL will attempt to find batches within the meters on each of the locations that match the criteria defined on the batch movement schedule. The Batch Schedule Matching service will search through all meters within Location 1 to find a batch that matches the product, batch size, and origin start date from the schedule. Similarly, the Batch Schedule Matching service will search through all meters within Location 1 to find a batch that matches the product, batch size, and destination start date from the schedule.

Scheduled batch movements can be entered into FLOWCAL manually or imported from an Excel (.xls) file in the FLOWCAL-specified format. As batches are imported for meters with the Reconcile Batches option enabled, FLOWCAL will try to match each batch to a scheduled batch movement via the Batch Schedule Matching service (FcSrvBatchScheduleMatching.exe). If a batch is unable to be matched, exception 18205 will be generated and the queue entry will fail to be processed.

This method requires the Liquids add-on.

Manually Import a Scheduled Batch Movement

To import a scheduled batch movement manually: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Scheduled Batch Movement**. 2. Click the **Browse** button to find a .xls file or type the file path into the edit box. 3. Click **Import**. 4. When the import is complete, go to **Tools** \> **Batch Movement Reconciliation** to view the scheduled batch movements.

Automatically Import a Scheduled Batch Movement

To import a scheduled batch movement automatically, use the File Import service. Specify the folder to check for scheduled batch movements in the [Service Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Service%20Configuration.md) screen within the Liquid Imports tab. Any .xls files in the specified folder or its sub-directories will be imported. If an imported meter batch cannot be matched to a scheduled batch movement, exceptions will be generated to alert the user.

Manually Enter Scheduled Batch Movements

To manually enter scheduled batch movements: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Liquids** \> **Batch Movement Reconciliation**. 2. Click **New**. The Scheduled Batch Movement Editor will open. 3. Define the criteria for the scheduled batch movement desired and click **Save**. 4. Click **Match** to manually associate batches to the schedule. (See: [Manually Associate Scheduled Batches](#Associate)) The product on the scheduled batch must match the product on the meter batch. For additional information on field definitions, see Scheduled Batch Movement File Format.

Batch Schedule Matching Service

Queue entries on the Batch Matching tab of the Service Queues will be processed by the FcSrvBatchScheduleMatching.exe service. FLOWCAL will then attempt to associate meter batches to the scheduled batch movements defined in the Batch Movement Reconciliation Viewer. If the service is unable to associate a batch to both the origin and destination specified on the scheduled batch movement, the queue entry status will be set to "Failed". If the service associates a batch to the origin and destination specified on the scheduled batch movement, the queue entry will be cleared from the list and the meter batches will now be associated to the scheduled batch movement.

Location Setup for Scheduled Batch Movements

To set up location information for scheduled batch movements, the following must be configured in the Location Editor (**Setup** \> **Location** \> **Editor** \> **Tools** \> **Info**): - The meter containing the batch, matching the origin within the schedule, must belong to the location that has the origin defined in Custom Field 1. - The meter containing the batch, matching the destination within the schedule, must belong to the location that has the destination defined in Custom Field 1. - Set the tolerance for the batch’s volume or mass and start time on the location, so that they fall within the range for the scheduled batch movement. - The total volume or mass for the actual meter batch must match the scheduled batch movement amount within the tolerance setup on the location. The tolerance is defined using the **Volume or Mass Must Be Within** value. - The start date and time of the actual meter batch must match the start time of the scheduled batch movement within the tolerance setup for the location. The tolerance is defined using the **Start Time Must Be Within** value.

Manually Associate Scheduled Batches

If a meter batch fails to be associated with a scheduled batch movement and does not fall within the scheduled batch movement tolerances defined in the [Location Editor](../../Locations/Location%20Editor/Location%20Editor.md), you can manually associate a meter batch to the scheduled batch movement. To manually associate a meter batch: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Liquids** \> **Batch Movement Reconciliation**. 2. Specify the location, where the match should occur, and date range criteria that fits the schedule you want to modify. 3. Double-click the schedule to bring up the Batch Movement Association Editor. 4. Select **Batches Filtered**. 5. Change the filter criteria for origin date, destination date, and batch size to meet the criteria for the meter batch. 6. When meter batch appears, click **Edit**. 7. Right-click the batch and select **Associate**, then **Save**.

Scheduled Batch Movement File Format

The import file is an Excel (.xls) file with the following columns for each line of data. Blank lines in the file will be ignored. The first line in the file may be a header line, which will be ignored on import. Column Notes Shipper Name Up to 50 characters; must match a valid company within FLOWCAL that is marked as a shipper (Settings > Settings Manager > Contacts > Company Manager) Product ID or Commodity Code Must match a Product Code or Product Alias within FLOWCAL (Settings > Settings Manager > Liquids > Products) Batch Start Date and Time at Origin - Batch End Date and Time at Origin - Origin Up to 50 characters; must match exactly to a custom field 1 on a location within FLOWCAL (Setup > Location > Editor > Tools > Info) Destination Up to 50 characters; must match exactly to a custom field 1 on a location within FLOWCAL (Setup > Location > Editor > Tools > Info) Batch Size - Estimated Flow Rate - Estimated Arrival Date and Time at Destination - Movement ID Up to 50 characters; must be unique Comments Up to 500 characters Volume Type "G" - GSV; "N" - NSV; "M" - Mass

Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: CALCit Integrated
docs.text:
CALCit is an intuitive application that assists field and office personnel in performing gas and liquid flow measurement calculations. This application uses the latest industry standard calculations, allowing users to perform spot calculations for gas volume, plate size, liquid correction factors, speed of sound, and more. CALCit also assists in validating other systems, and allows users to view, save, and print the results of multiple calculations based on different input values.

CALCit Integrated makes CALCit accessible from FLOWCAL, including all of its calculators and associated functionality, depending on purchased licensing. The integrated package also includes the ability to populate a calculator from a selected gas meter's configuration.

For additional information, and to learn about all available CALCit calculators, please visit the CALCit product page or contact Customer Support.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: CALCit Integrated Installation

docs.title: Analysis to TESTit
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit Integrated (Version 2.14.2 or later and Version 3.3 and later).

The service FcSrvTestITAnalysisSync copies the current gas meter analysis in FLOWCAL to TESTit gas analysis database table. Meters need to be enabled for TESTit and rolled up in order for their analysis data to be copied to TESTit. Meter analysis data that is a part of autoestimated records are not copied by this service.

The FcSrvTestITAnalysisSync service is installed in the same manner that any other FLOWCAL service is installed. (See: Install and Configure Services)

The flowcal.enterprise.integration.service must also be installed and running for this service to work.

Once installed, the service is started from the Windows Service Monitor. The service runs at 7:00 AM every day by default.

The hour and port for this service can be adjusted by directly updating values stored in the database. Configuration of this service is not available on the Service Monitor screen.

  • FC_APPLICATION_OPTIONS.FCSRV_TIANASYNC_HOUR - The hour at which the service should run. If null, the default setting is 7.
  • FC_APPLICATION_OPTIONS.FCSRV_TIANASYNC_PORT - The port the service should use.

This service processes all meters that are enabled for TESTit (See: Enabling a FLOWCAL Item for TESTit) and are not on the meter rollup queue when it runs. It searches the final form hourly meter data table (FC_FFMTR_HOURLY) for the most recent hourly record for the meter before the current system time, and checks whether there are values in SPECIFIC_GRAVITY, C1, C2 and C3 columns. If the record does not have these columns populated or if the record is auto estimated, it does nothing. If the record contains non-null values in the checked columns, it copies the analysis values to corresponding columns of FC_TRANALYSIS table.

For TESTit 3 integration, the FC_TRANALYSIS table is no longer used. Analysis data is instead transmitted to the TESTit 3 Server database and stored in the FA_SOURCE_ANALYSIS table there.

docs.title: Associating TESTit Devices to Contact Types
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 Integrated.

Some devices in TESTit, such as test reports and calibration devices, may have contact types associated with them. Contact types can be used to assign these devices to a contact or group of contacts.

Two contact types ("Technician" and "Witness") are created by default; more can be added and managed from the Contact Type Editor. The Contact Type Editor is used to define these Contact Types for use in the various Contact Selection screens under the device related editors. The contacts set up for each device are notified by email when changes are made to that device and saved.

To set up contacts for test reports: 1. From the FLOWCAL main menu, go to **Setup** \> **TESTit Manager** \> **Quick View Report**. 2. All TESTit enabled meters are available in the **Device** drop-down selection list. After selecting the appropriate device, click the **New** button to create a new test report. 3. In the **Contacts** area of the screen, set the contacts or contact group for each contact type displayed. One or more contacts can be set for each contact type. Only the contact types enabled for test reports are available to be set up. 4. Click the **Save** button. To set up contacts for calibration devices: 1. From the FLOWAL main menu, go to **Setup** \> **Calibration Device**. 2. Go to **View** \> **Contact Relationships**. 3. In the **Contacts** area of the screen, set the contacts or contact group for each contact type displayed. One or more contacts can be set for each contact type. Only the contact types enabled for calibration devices are available to be set up. 4. Click the **Save** button.

docs.title: Calibration Adjustments
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 3 integration.

FLOWCAL has the ability to adjust data based on TESTit Test Reports through edits or Prior Period Adjustments (PPAs). The adjustments can be made automatically on import of a Test Report or through the Review Test Report screen. For details, refer to: Review Test Report.

For an adjustment to be applied, the adjustment amount must be greater than a specified error tolerance level and minimum unit difference. Error tolerance is a percentage difference of volume or energy for the month that must exist between the current monthly volume or energy and the adjusted monthly volume or energy. Minimum unit difference is volume or energy (in units) for the month that must exist between the current monthly volume or energy and the adjusted monthly volume or energy.

Applying a test report means that adjustment values are calculated, and adjustments are made if the adjustment value was greater than the error tolerance and the minimum unit difference. If the calculations yield an adjustment amount less than or equal to that required by the error tolerance or minimum unit difference no adjustment to the data will be made.

Logical flow for applying a test report to a meter:

For Error Tolerance set to "%" and Minimum Unit Difference set to "Unit":

If volume adjustment > % AND volume adjustment > unit

Result: Applied test report. An edit or PPA will be made.

Else if energy adjustment > % AND energy adjustment > unit

Result: Applied test report. An edit or PPA will be made.

Else

Result: Attempted test report. No edit or PPA will be made.

docs.title: Auto Calibration Adjustments
docs.text:
Error tolerance and minimum unit difference are set within the Master Characteristics section on the Operational tab.

These values need to be in place before the import of test reports or the user will have to manually apply the adjustment. Error tolerance (the Min Calibration Adjustment Pct) is a percentage and should be entered as a whole number (ex. Two percent = 2). If the monthly adjustment value exceeds the error tolerance and minimum unit difference (the Min Calibration Adjustment Unit Diff), the adjustment will be applied and meter data will be adjusted.

Auto calibration adjustments can be made on open or closed data. PPAs must be allowed at the system level for auto adjustments on closed data or open data.

The date span for a calibration adjustment is based on the date of the test and the last test date. For this reason, at least test report is required in the system before auto adjustments can be made.

docs.title: Enabling a FLOWCAL Item for TESTit
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit Integrated.

To specify a meter, source analysis, or list as TESTit-enabled, access the Meter Editor, Source Analysis Editor, or List Editor, and click the Enabled for TESTit drop-down.

With TESTit 3 Integrated service, FLOWCAL allows users to synchronously create, modify, and delete meters in the TESTit Server application. Managed meters are protected from certain edits within the TESTit Server application; however, changes made to managed meters in FLOWCAL are also made within the TESTit Server database.

To enable a meter for TESTit: 1. From the FLOWCAL main menu, go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Editor**. 2. Select the desired meter and click the **Reports** tab. 3. Click **Edit**. 4. At the bottom of the Reports tab, set the **Enable for TESTit** option to "Yes". 5. The **Test Reports** button is now available in the Meter Editor. The Enabled for TESTit option can be set back to "No". This functionality sends an update to TESTit 3 to indicate that the meter should no longer be protected from edits in TESTit 3. This setting cannot be reversed with TESTit 2. To enable a source analysis for TESTit (TESTit 2 only): 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Gas Quality**. 2. Select the desired source analysis. 3. Click **Edit**. 4. At the bottom of the Main tab, set the **Enable for TESTit** option to "Yes". 5. The **Test Reports** option is now available in the Tools menu. To enable a list for TESTit (TESTit 3 only): 1. Go to **Setup** \> **List**. 2. Select the desired list. 3. Click **Edit**. 4. In the upper-right corner of the editor, set the **Enable for TESTit** option to "Yes". 5. Click **Save**. The list can now be sent to a TESTit 3 server for integration. TESTit-enabled lists are protected from edits within the TESTit Server application. Any changes must be made in the FLOWCAL List Editor and pushed to the TESTit 3 server. Dynamic lists are transmitted to the TESTit server as static, but updates are periodically sent to TESTit as changes occur to the lists in FLOWCAL.

docs.title: Export Data Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

TESTit allows users to export information about meter tests. You can choose to export test report data, meter definitions, list definitions, configuration data, contact data, etc. You can then upload your data to TESTit Enterprise and share your information with other TESTit users.

  1. From the menu bar, choose the Export button.

  2. Click the New button.

    You can either choose one of the following to export: Device, Lists, Locations, Test Reports, Schedules, Contacts, Configuration data, or export multiple items by selecting more than one of the options.

  3. Click the Continue button.

  4. You can set the export name and file name in this window.

    Click … to select a directory and file name where you would like to export the data to.

    You can email the export by selecting Email Export and then entering an email address.

    If Email Export is selected, the export will not be saved locally.

    The contact creating the export can also be emailed by selecting Notify Me On Import.

    Depending on the type of export option was selected, click Export Now or Email Now. Once the data is exported, you will see the file located in the directory specified or in the email specified. The file will have a .tsx extension (e.g., testreports.tsx).

docs.title: Export Jobs
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

TESTit has the ability to allow users to create export jobs containing test report data, meter definitions, list definitions, configuration data, contact data, etc. These export jobs can then be scheduled to be exported on a recurring basis. These exports can then be uploaded to other TESTit users.

To access the Export Jobs screen: From the main **TESTit Integrated** menu, go to **File** \> **Export Jobs**. All current export jobs, including the export name, status, next scheduled run time, previous status, and previous run time will display on this screen. To export the current jobs listed: Click **Export Now**. To create a new export job: 1. Click **New**. 2. Enable options to configure what is included in the export. If you select Export Test Reports, Export Schedule Definitions, or Export Schedule Entries, and no devices are selected on the left side of the screen, all devices will be selected. If you select a particular device for export, it will display in the grid below the device selection area. If you have selected devices of a particular type, such as Meter, and then select to export all meters, the previously selected meters will be removed from the grid. - **Last Number of Test Reports** - Export only the last number of test reports specified by the user. This option can be combined with the date range option to export only the last number of test reports in a date range. - **By Date Range** - Specify a date range for which to export the test reports. You can select the current month, a previous number of months, the current week, a previous number of weeks, a previous number of days, and an exact date range. When selecting either previous Months, Weeks, or Days the user will select how many Months, Weeks, or Days to go back and will also have the option to include the current Month, Week, or Day - **Schedule Definitions** - Export the most current definition along with the most current schedule entry for the selected devices. - **Schedule Entries** - Export completed entries or canceled entries that are unlinked. Unlinked entries are completed or canceled schedule entries that do not have a test report linked to them. - **Contact Export** - Export all contacts and distribution lists. - **Agency Export** - Export all agencies. - **Brands and Models Export** - Export all brand and model definitions. - **Configuration Export** - Export field property values, drop-down lists, tasks, system defaults, state lists, schedule frequencies, and unit templates. 3. When you have configured the options, click **Continue**. 4. On the next screen, you will be able to enter the export job name, the export file name, the export path, as well as the export schedule. 5. Check the **Scheduled Export** checkbox to schedule the export job. 6. Click **Save Export Job** to save the export, or click **Export Now** to run the export. 7. Click the **Review Export** button to review the export options. 8. Click the **Edit** button to edit the currently selected schedule.

docs.title: Flow Averages to TESTit
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 3 Integrated.

The Flow Averages utility (FlowCal.Integration.FlowAverages.exe) allows users to synchronize meter flow averages between FLOWCAL to TESTit 3. Previously, meter flow averages were synchronized by the Meter Rollup service, which frequently overwhelmed the transfer process with unnecessary updates. This new utility provides better control of the data transfer via scheduling and a data selection filter.

  • The utility is scheduled via Windows Scheduler, which permits daily or less frequent execution.
  • The data selection filter allows users to limit the transfer to closed or complete months only, significantly reducing the transfer workload.

The Flow Averages utility is part of the FLOWCAL and TESTit 3 Integrated suite.

Compatibility

The Flow Averages utility works with TESTit 3 Integrated services between FLOWCAL Version 10.1.1 and higher and TESTit 3.

Installation

The utility is installed by the standard FLOWCAL installer and is available in the main installation folder.

Running the Utility

Users can run the Flow Averages utility as follows: - Manually by double-clicking the executable; - Manually in a command console window; or - Automatically via a Windows Scheduled Task. The recommended execution interval is once per day or less frequently. The utility uses the FLOWCAL service login credentials to connect to the database. Any errors encountered by the utility will be written to the \_FC_DB_ERROR.LOG file (located in the LOGFILES subfolder of the FLOWCAL installation directory). Running the Utility with Status Filter By default, the utility will sync all TESTit-enabled meters for which the process flag (FC_FFMTR_MONTHLY.EXTERNAL_PROCESS_FLAG_7) is null. The utility will set the flag to “Y” after processing. A meter rollup resulting in new data will clear the flag. To improve control over the amount of data transferred, users can run the utility with a filter to only sync meters with completed or closed statuses. To run the utility with a filter, append the command line argument “/STATUS=\” where the \ variable is either “Complete” or “Closed”. Do not insert any spaces between the **/status** switch and its argument. **Example:** Flowcal.Integration.FlowAverages.exe /STATUS = Closed If the status is “Complete”, the utility will only send completed monthly records, i.e., records where FC_FFMTR_MONTHLY.COMPLETION_STATUS = “Y” and the process flag is null). If the status is “Closed”, the utility will only send closed monthly records, i.e., records for which: - There is a corresponding row in FC_METER_CLOSE_DATES for the meter and measurement month of interest; - The STATUS column of the FC_METER_CLOSE_DATES record is “Y”; and - The process flag is null. If the command line argument is malformed, the service will not process any meters and will write a message to the \_FC_DB_ERROR.LOG file. To use a filter when scheduling the utility, create and schedule a .bat or .cmd file containing the complete command line with the filter.

docs.title: Meter Characteristics from TESTit
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 3 Integrated.

When a new meter test is received from TESTit, any new Meter Characteristics will be brought in for validation. An exception is generated whenever a field in the TESTit Meter Characteristics differs from a field in the current FLOWCAL Meter Characteristics. For any unwanted validations, the user may set the Exception severity for that particular field to 0 to avoid displaying it in the Exception Resolver.
