docs.title: Model Type Editor
docs.text:
The Model Type Editor is used to define custom model types. All model types must be of a base type, which can be a: meter, GQ source, transmitter, recorder, or RTU.

This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

To add a new model type: 1. From the main **TESTit Integrated** menu, go to **Set-up** \> **Brand/Model**. 2. Create new model and on the button to the right of the Model Type heading to access the Model Type Editor screen. TESTit comes installed with a default model for each type. 3. Click **New** and enter the new model type (meter, calibration device, recorder, or RTU). 4. Enter the model type name. 5. Click **Save**. Edit existing model types by selecting an existing type and clicking **Edit**. If necessary, click the **Undo** button to revert changes you have made.

docs.title: Orifice Meter Test Report - Manual Entry
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

FLOWCAL allows users to manually enter data into a TESTit test report through TESTit Integrated.

To set up a report for manual entry: 1. Go to **View** \> **Tree View**. 2. Select a meter. 3. Select **New** \> **Create/View**. 4. Select **Orifice Meter Test** from the drop-down menu. Enter the following data to make the manually entered test report available on the Review Test Report screen: 1. Enter the plate information and tube information on the **Orifice** tab. 2. Enter the **Before Calibration** and **Test Points** data on the **Differential Transmitter** tab. If there are not any test points, then enter 0 in the **As Found** and **As Left** fields and change the **Number of Test Points** value to 1. 3. Enter the **Test Points** data on the **Static Transmitter** tab. If there are not any test points, enter 0 in the **As Found** and **As Left** fields and change the **Number of Test Points** value to 1. 4. Enter the **Test Points** data on the **Temperature Transmitter** tab. If there are not any test points, enter 0 in the **As Found** and **As Left** fields and change the **Number of Test Points** value to 1. 5. On the **Meter** tab, select the **Volume Calculations** sub-tab and select a calculation method and FPV method from the drop-down menus. When "AGA-8 Detail" is selected for the FPV method, the **Detail** section will need to be completed in addition to the **Calculation Data** section. If "AGA-8 Gross 1" or "AGA-8 Gross 2" is selected for the FPV method, then data will only need to be entered in the **Calculation Data** section. 6. Select the **Meter** sub-tab, click both calculator buttons in the **Calc. Flow Rate** section. 7. Save your changes. 8. Start the FcSrvTestITCalAdjApply service. The test report will now be available for viewing in FLOWCAL under **Review** \> **Review Test Report**.

docs.title: Reassign Scheduled Tasks
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

Scheduled tasks can be reassigned to different users in TESTit.

To reassign a scheduled task: 1. Open Schedule Definition Viewer by clicking the Schedule Definition Editor button. 2. Click the \> to expand the object (meter, lists, etc.) and see the currently scheduled tasks related to the object. 3. Right-click an object and select **Reassign**. 4. Select the user to reassign the task to and click **Select**. The task has now been reassigned.

docs.title: Schedule Frequency Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Scheduling Frequency Editor is used to define frequencies that are used in the schedule definitions.

To add a new schedule frequency: 1. Click the **Schedule Definition Editor** button. 2. Click the **New** button. 3. From the Schedule Definition Editor window and after setting up the device information to be Recurring, click the button to the right of the **Frequency** drop-down list to open the Schedule Frequency Editor. 4. Click **New**. 5. Enter the frequency name. 6. Enter the value for the number of days, weeks, or months. 7. Select the unit type from the drop-down list. 8. Click **Save**.

docs.title: Scheduled Tasks Calendar View
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 Integrated.

The Calendar View shows the scheduled tasks on a calendar much like Microsoft Outlook. From this view you can easily see tasks for the selected day, week, month, or year.

To access the calendar view: 1. From View \> Schedules View or by clicking on the quick access toolbar icon\[Schedules button.PNG\]. 2. The calendar view uses different colors to represent the state of the different tasks. - **White** – The task is not yet due - **Yellow** – The task is due - **Red** – The task is over due - **Green** – The task has been completed - **Gray** – Tasks that have been canceled - **Turquoise** – Represents reoccurring entries 3. The view can be easily filtered to show all tasks or any combination of scheduled, due, overdue, completed, and canceled. The tasks can also be filtered for all users or a specific user. 4. Scheduled items can be moved around the calendar (within their grace period) simply by clicking and dragging an item from one day to another. 5. The task can be performed by double-clicking on the scheduled item. New tasks can be added by double-clicking a day on the calendar. 6. Schedule entries can be exported to Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Excel, Plain Text, HTML, and XML. 7. To export click File \> Export Calendar and click on the format to export the schedule to.

docs.title: Scheduled Tasks Grid View
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 Integrated.

The Grid View shows the scheduled tasks in a grid with powerful filters and sorting options. From this view you can easily find information about scheduled tasks.

To access the grid view: 1. To access the Grid view, in the Schedules window, select the Grid option under the Views section in the left side of the window. 2. The view can be easily filtered to show all tasks or any combination of scheduled, due, overdue, completed, and canceled tasks. 3. The tasks can also be filtered for all users or a specific user. Filtering can also be done on the Device Name, Device Task Name, and Description. The tasks can be sorted quickly by Status, Duration, Scheduled Date/Time, Due Date/Time, and Completion Date/Time. 4. The task can be performed by selecting a task and clicking Edit. 5. New tasks can be added by clicking New.

docs.title: TESTit 3 Config File
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 3 Integrated.

The FLOWCAL install directory contains a file named ‘TESTit_Config_template.cfg’. This file is used for configuring key information in accessing TESTit 3 Server from FLOWCAL and remote integration services. This file must be renamed to ‘TESTit_Config.cfg’ before it can be used. The template appended to the end is to prevent this file from being overwritten every time a new version of FLOWCAL is implemented.

Example text from a .cfg file:

Install Path: C:\FA\testit3\server\Bin

Service Scheme: http

Service Host: localhost

Service Port: 53879

docs.title: Config File Details
docs.text:
• Install Path - The file path of the TESTit 3 Server the user wishes to be launched from within FLOWCAL.
  • Service Scheme - This does not need to be modified if the user is running the FLOWCAL Integration Services on the same machine as the FLOWCAL application.
  • Service Host - This does not need to be modified if the user is running the FLOWCAL Integration Services on the same machine as the FLOWCAL application.
  • Service Port - This does not need to be modified if the user is running the FLOWCAL Integration Services on the same machine as the FLOWCAL application.

If the user is running the services on a separate machine, Service Scheme, Service Host (computer name), and Service Port must be specified to point to that server.

docs.title: TESTit Analysis Viewer
docs.text:
The analyses brought over from FLOWCAL to TESTit can be viewed by navigating to the Analysis Viewer while in TESTit personality. Users may also manually input analyses for meters from this viewer. Both analyses originating from FLOWCAL and manually entered analyses can be edited and deleted in the Analysis viewer.

This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration (Version 2.14.2 and later).

To access the TESTit Analysis Viewer: 1. From the main **TESTit Integrated** menu, go to **Set-up** \> **Meter**. 2. Select the **Analysis** option. The FcSrvTestITAnalysisSync service must be installed for this functionality to be available.

docs.title: TESTit Import Service
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

To import test reports from the field, the TESTit Import Service will need to be installed and configured. This service is used to automatically import data from TESTit into FLOWCAL. The service name that will need to be installed is called FcSrvTESTItSchedulerImport.exe. This service is located in the FLOWCAL installation directory on the server where FLOWCAL is installed. To install this service the administrator can utilize the _installservices.bat within the FLOWCAL installation folder.

Once the service is installed, the service will need to be configured in FLOWCAL by going to the Settings Manager > Services > Service Configuration menu. At the bottom of the screen you will see the configuration for the TESTit Imports. The TESTit options within FLOWCAL will appear if the TESTit module has been purchased from FLOWCAL.

The ‘Folder to check’ is the main import folder for TESTit data. After the service processes each TESTit (.TSX) file it will be moved to a folder under the import directory, labeled with the timestamp, indicating when it was processed. A Success or Failed folder will be created within the main import folder so that it is easy to see what files have processed successfully and which ones have failed. The main import folder may also contain additional folders for saved mapping configurations

Meters and/or source analyses that do not exist in FLOWCAL will be created by the TESTit Import Service using a default mapping; however, it is strongly recommended that the meters and/or source analyses are setup in FLOWCAL before any TESTit data is imported.

docs.title: TESTit 2 Integrated
docs.text:
TESTit integration into FLOWCAL provides a central repository for equipment calibration results and access to the TESTit Scheduler. This allows measurement office staff to oversee field operations and verify compliance.

Integrating the functionality of TESTit into FLOWCAL helps coordinate field operations and measurement office operations by making test reports available to office personnel and providing additional methods for validating test reports. It also allows for test reports to be edited at the office, includes a complete audit trail of field-entered data, and allows reports to be scheduled and distributed as needed.

  • Complete details about TESTit 2 Integrated with FLOWCAL are available here:

TESTit 2 Integrated Overview

  • Instructions for installing the TESTit 2 Integrated with FLOWCAL plugin are available here:

TESTit 2 Integrated with FLOWCAL Plugin

  • Complete details about TESTit 3 Integrated with FLOWCAL are available here:

docs.title: Calibration Device Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Calibration Devices Editor is used to create calibration devices in TESTit.

To access the Calibration Device Editor and create a new device: 1. From the main **TESTit Integrated** menu, go to **Set-Up** \> **Calibration Device**. 2. Click **New**. 3. Select the type of calibration device (Temperature, Static Pressure, Differential Pressure, Static Differential Pressure Combo, Test Measure, Gravity, Electronic Device, or Mechanical Device).  4. Enter the model name, manufacturer, and serial number. If the calibration device type is "Static Pressure" or "Static Differential Pressure Combo", you will need to select a pressure unit. 5. Confirm whether the calibration device is a current active calibration device.  6. Click **Save**. 7. Upon saving, you will be prompted to set up schedule definitions for the new device. If you click **Yes**, the Schedule Definition Editor screen will appear. To edit an existing calibration device: 1. Select the device and click **Edit**. 2. While editing, you can configure all aspects of the calibration device, including the option to add or edit schedule definitions. Click **Add/Edit Schedule Definitions** to access the Schedule Definition Editor. 3. If necessary, click the **Undo** button to revert changes you have made.

docs.title: Data Map Editor
docs.text:
The Data Map Editor allows the user to set up and save data mappings between TESTit and FLOWCAL fields to be used during imports of test reports with TESTit 2 Integrated. This feature is useful in determining if a TESTit value should update a FLOWCAL value on import or generate an exception. For example, by mapping the TESTit meter name to the FLOWCAL meter name, the FLOWCAL meter name will be updated during the import of TESTit data.

By default, none of the fields are mapped.

This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 Integrated.

To access the Data Map Editor:  Go to **Setup** \> **TESTit Manager**.

Data Map Editor Details

The following items are available on the Data Map Editor screen: - **Default Mapping** - A change to the Default Mapping will affect all meters or sources. The user can create additional data maps that can be used on specific sources or meters as defined by the user. - **Create Meters Pending** - Meters that are created as a result of a test report import will be created with a Business Status of Pending New. Meter Status is not affected by this option. If a meter is created by TESTit import, Meter Status will default to Active. - **New** - Create a new data map. A new map cannot be named "Default Mapping." Once a new mapping has been created, a folder with the same name will be created in the TESTit import path defined within Service Configuration. - **Save** - Save changes. - **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not save changes. - **Exit** - Exit the Data Map Editor screen.

Table Objects

There are four FLOWCAL table objects within the Data Map Editor: Meter, GQ Source, Contact, and Company. A table object can be configured to Report, Create, or Ignore within the Update column. - The **Report** option will create a system message when an object (e.g., meter, source, contact, or company) is encountered that did not exist during a TESTit import. The object will not be created in FLOWCAL. - The **Create** option will create the object in FLOWCAL if it does not exist. - The **Ignore** option will ignore the object and will not create a system message. #### Meter and GQ Source TESTit fields can be mapped to FLOWCAL fields within the Meter and GQ Source table objects. The left side of the grid contains TESTit fields and the right side contains FLOWCAL fields. To map a field: 1. Expand the table associated objects. 2. Drag and drop a TESTit field from the left to a FLOWCAL field on the right. 3. Check the **Compare** checkbox to create an exception when the TESTit field value differs from the FLOWCAL field value. 4. Select an option from the Update drop-down list. > The Update options are Values Only, Values & NULL, and Ignore. > > - The **Values Only** option will not copy over null values. A value must exist. > - The **Values & Null** option will copy over values including null values. > - The **Ignore** option will ignore the imported value and is often used in conjunction with the Compare checkbox. When combined, a system message will be created when the values differ, but the data in FLOWCAL will not be modified. 1. Click **Save**. TSX files to be imported should be placed in the folder that corresponds to the appropriate data map. To use the Default Mapping, place the files in the TESTit import path configured within Service Configuration. #### Contact and Company This feature is no longer supported.

docs.title: Data Map Editor
docs.text:
The Data Map Editor allows the user to set up and save data mappings of TESTit fields into FLOWCAL fields when TESTit Test Reports are imported into FLOWCAL.

This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

To access the Data Map Editor: 1. From the FLOWCAL main menu, go to **Setup** \> **TESTit Manager** \> **Data Map Editor**. 2. Note that the FLOWCAL objects on the right (Meter, GQSource, Contact, and Company) only have the following update options: - **Create** - Create the object in FLOWCAL if it does not already exist Users can select to have the business status set to Pending Create for meters that are created by the TESTit Import service. Meter status is not affected by this option. If a meter is created by TESTit Import, the meter status will default to "In Service/Active". - **Ignore** - Ignore the object (will not be created) - **Report** - Create a system message indicating that the unknown meter was not created 3. Contacts and customers can also be imported from TESTit, but individual columns are not mapped. You can set customers/contacts to either report, ignore, or create. 4. Drag and drop TESTit fields from the left side onto the destination FLOWCAL field on the right side. Supported fields include those from the FC_METER, FC_METER2, FC_METER_CHARACTERISTIC, FC_GQ_SOURCE, and FC_GQ_SOURCE_CHARACTERISTIC tables. 5. After a field is mapped, the user needs to choose import options for each field mapped. On the far right is the update option. TESTit data can update the field it is mapped to by replacing data with values or values & nulls. The ignore option will allow the field to be compared without updating any information in FLOWCAL. When the Compare checkbox is selected, the FLOWCAL values will be compared to those being imported from TESTit. If the values do not match an exception is created

docs.title: Additional Mappings
docs.text: The default mapping affects any import in the main import path. Users can create multiple mappings by clicking new at the top of the data map editor. All user created mappings must be named something other than Default Mapping. The import service will create a sub folder in the main import path with the same name as the user-created mapping configuration in FLOWCAL. The import service will import TSX files from these subfolders using that mapping configuration.

docs.title: Quick View
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Quick View allows users to quickly select a single device, Meter, GQ Source, Calibration Device, Prover, or Miscellaneous Device, and view all completed tested associated with the device. By only displaying one device at a time it allows the user to focus only on the selected meter and better control over which data is displayed. The quick view gives the user the ability to filter by the completed task name and date range.

To access the Quick View screen: Go to **Test Reports** \> **Create/View Test Reports** \> **Quick View**, or click the quick view button on the quick access toolbar.

docs.title: Tree View
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Tree View allows users to see all of the available devices, Meters, GQ Sources, Calibration Devices, Provers, Miscellaneous Devices, Lists, and Locations, in hierarchical view. Each device in the tree view can be expanded to reveal any completed tests, if any exists, and collapsed again to hide the revealed tests.

Since the tree view has the ability to display large amounts of data at one time TESTit provides the user with different order and filter methods that can be used to make specific data easier to find.

Lists, Locations, Meters, and GQ Sources can all be ordered by number or name. Calibration Devices and Provers can be ordered by type, model, or manufacturer. Tests can also be filtered by a date range. Only tests that fall into the specified date range are displayed making it even easier to find the test the user is looking for.

To access the Tree View: Go to **Test Reports** \> **Create/View Test Reports** \> **Tree View**, or click the tree view button on the quick access toolbar.

docs.title: Review Test Report
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit integration.

Users can apply edits or PPAs to data using TESTit test reports. These adjustments can be applied automatically upon import of a test report, or manually through the Review Test Report screen.

PPAs must be allowed in order to make calibration adjustments on open data from a test report. PPAs via Test Reports must be enabled for auto calibration adjustments on closed data.

To manually apply data from a TESTit test report: 1. Go to **Review** \> **Review Test Report**. 2. Select a list, location, or meter to view imported test reports for. 3. Select a time filter to locate the desired test reports. When the "Use Date Range" option is enabled, the "From" date defaults to one month prior to the current date; this can be set to any date range. You can also select a status filter when looking for a specific test report or perform a full text search to locate a test summary. A list of test summaries created from TESTit test reports that match the filter criteria will display. 4. If you need to change the From or To date or the Error Tolerance or Min Unit Difference, then select a row and click the **Edit** button. Click **Save** to save your edits. 5. If you want to bypass the error tolerance and minimum unit difference checks and calculate a calibration adjustment anyway, enable the "Force" option on the applicable rows. 6. To preview the results of the calibration adjustment before actually applying and saving the results, click the **Preview** button. (See: Calibration Adjustment Preview) 7. Select the rows on which you want to apply the calibration adjustment and click **Apply**. Double-click a row to view an individual test report. If TESTit 3 Integration is enabled, the task report PDF will display in your PDF reader.

Screen Details

The following columns are available on the Review Test Report screen: - **Meter Number** - **Test Date** - The date the test was performed - **Status** - **Applied** - Test report was applied and an edit or PPA was made (actual edit may not have been made) - **Not Applied** - Test report not been applied yet - **Failed** - Test report failed to apply - **Partial** - Test report did not successfully apply to the specified time frame - **Attempted** - Test report port was applied but no adjustment was necessary based on tolerance set - **From/To Date** - Defines the span for which the test report will be applied - **Error Tolerance** - Limit - **Minimum Unit Difference** - Low limit - **Force** - Temporarily sets error tolerance and minimum unit difference to values that will force the adjustment, effectively bypassing error tolerance and minimum unit difference checks

Calibration Adjustment Preview

Users can preview calibration adjustments without saving the results. The preview function executes the calibration adjustment process and displays the corresponding results. When the preview screen is dismissed, the results are discarded and no edits or PPAs are created. The Preview button is only enabled when a single test report is selected and its status is "Not Applied", "Failed", or "Partial". The Preview button is a multi-function "split" button, which provides a default action (the main portion of the button labeled Preview), or a drop-down selection of actions (the down arrowhead on the right side of the button). For this button, the default and selectable actions determine the layout of the preview screen. The drop-down options are "Compact" and "Detailed". The default action is determined via the "Show Individual Transmitter Corrections" TESTit option (Settings \> TESTit Integration Configuration \> Test Report Preview). The **compact layout** provides a view of volume, energy, and mass adjustments. The current value, revised (new) value, percent difference, and unit difference are shown for each quantity. Other columns indicate whether a PPA will be created and display a notation of errors encountered that may prevent successful adjustment when the test report is applied. Each month that will be affected by the adjustment is shown separately. The **detailed layout** adds the individual impact of each transmitter on the volume. The percent differences and unit differences are shown.

docs.title: Application Options Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Application Options Editor is used to configure different system options, including whether to display the flow/total flow rate error, plate size tolerance, com device setup, and configuration of test points.

To access the Application Options Editor: From the main **TESTit Integrated** menu, go to **Application** \> **Application Options**.

docs.title: Brands & Models Editor
docs.text:
The Brands & Models Editor is used to set up brands and models of equipment used by your company. The interface has a hierarchical view. You can expand a particular brand to see associated models.

This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

To add a new brand: 1. From the main **TESTit Integrated** menu, go to **Set-up** \> **Brand/Model**. 2. Click **New** and select **Add New Brand**. 3. Enter a brand name. 4. Click **Save**. To add a new model: 1. Click **New** and select **Add New Model**. 2. Select a model type such as a GQ source, meter, RTU, recorder, static pressure transmitter, differential transmitter, or temperature transmitter. 3. Enter a model name. 4. Click **Save**. Edit existing brands and models by selecting an existing brand or model and clicking **Edit**. If necessary, click the **Undo** button to revert changes you have made.

docs.title: Custom Tab Editor
docs.text:
The Custom Tab editor allows administrators to create custom tabs that can be configured and used in test reports to display additional information.

This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

To create a custom tab: 1. From the main TESTit Integrated menu, go to **Administrator** \> **Custom Tab**. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter a tab name. 4. Select a tab type. 5. Click **Save**. To edit a custom tab: 1. Select a custom tab and click the **Edit** button. 2. Edit the tab name and type as needed. 3. If necessary, click the **Undo** button to revert changes you have made.

docs.title: Custom Task Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Custom Task Editor allows administrators to create custom tasks that they can configure and use in test reports for additional information that they might require their meter technicians to retrieve.

To create a custom task: 1. From the main TESTit Integrated menu, go to **Administrator** \> **Custom Task**. 2. You can view all current device tasks and the tabs associated with them by selecting them from the device task name drop-down lists. The available tabs are located on the left and the tabs associated with the task are on the right. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Enter a task name and description. 5. Select a task type: - **Meter Test Report** – Only Meters will be able to have this task preformed on them. - **GQ Source Test Report** – Only GQ Sources will be able to have this task preformed on them. - **Calibration Device Test Report** – Only Calibration Devices will be able to have this task preformed on them. - **Miscellaneous Event** – Task for Miscellaneous events. - **DISABLED** – Use this option to disable a task from being used. 6. Select the type of report that you would like to be associated with this task. 7. Add tabs to the task by selecting the task and clicking the add arrow. 8. You can also remove tabs by clicking the remove arrow. 9. Custom tabs that you created will also be available for you to add to the tasks. 10. Click **Save**. 11. To edit a custom task, select the custom task you wish to edit and click **Edit**. 12. You can edit the task name, task description, task type, task report file, and the tabs that are associated with the task. 13. To undo changes you have made while in edit mode click **Undo**. You can now use these custom or updated tasks for test reports. If you edited a standard test report the changes will cascade to all of the existing test using that test report so you will not have to reschedule any tasks.

docs.title: Drop-Down List Setup
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

Setting a field to be a drop-down list helps control data is that entered in that certain field. Drop-down lists can be created from the Drop-Down List Editor.

To change a field to a drop-down list: 1. Select the field you want to change. 2. Hover over **Form Configuration** on the right side of the screen and check the **Drop-Down List** check box. 3. After the field has been changed to a drop-down list, the administrator can select the drop-down list type that will be used. All of the lists that have been created in the Drop-Down List editor will appear as options. 4. The field has been successfully changed to a drop-down style list. To remove this setting, right-click and deselect the drop-down option.

docs.title: Unit Template Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Unit Template Editor allows you to create templates to use for unit conversion for various factors affecting the calculations. For convenience you can click either the All “Units to US” or “All Units to Metric” buttons to quickly change all of the units at once.

To create a unit template: 1. From the main **TESTit Integrated** menu, go to **Test Reports** \> **Unit Template**. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter the template name and units to be used with each of the items listed. 4. Click **Save**.

docs.title: Schedule Definition Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 integration.

The Schedule Definition Editor is used to set up schedules for tasks to be performed.

To access the Schedule Definition Editor: 1. Open Schedule Definition Editor by clicking the Schedule Definition Editor button. Then click New. 2. Next to the Device field, click the Device tree view button to select the device to schedule from the tree view. The option to create schedule definitions was chosen after creating a device such as a meter or GHQ source. When then New button is clicked the device that is currently being created will be populated in the device field. 3. Select the Device Task to schedule. 4. Select the person to whom this will be Assigned To. 5. Enter the Grace Period, or number of days after the tests due date a user has to complete the test. 6. Check whether this task will be Recurring. If so, select the Frequency. If the frequency you would like to use it not available you can open the [Schedule Frequency Editor](../Schedule%20Frequency%20Editor.md) by clicking the ellipses. 7. Select the Next Due Date. 8. Click Save. 9. The scheduled definition will now be added to the Calendar and Grid View the next time the Scheduler Service runs.

docs.title: Scheduling Miscellaneous Tasks
docs.text:
This functionality is only available with TESTit 2 Integrated.

Miscellaneous tasks cannot be scheduled until a custom task had been created to be used with the miscellaneous tasks.

  1. Add a link to custom task + tab creation.
  2. Miscellaneous Task can be scheduled form the Schedule Definition Editor.
  3. These tasks will be viewable from both the grid view and calendar view.

docs.title: Liquid Cavern Editor
docs.text:
The Liquid Cavern Editor requires a Liquids Inventory Module license.

Liquid caverns can be added to locations to track total inventory and perform gain/loss calculations. Use the Liquid Cavern Editor to calculate inventory totals for liquid volumes.

To access the Cavern Editor: Go to **Open** \> **Liquid Cavern Editor**. When you create a new liquid cavern, a reference meter, along with either an injection or withdrawal point, must be specified before the meter can be saved. - **Reference Meter** - A reference meter is required upon creation of a new cavern. The contract day and hour from the reference meter will be used to calculate the rollup IDs for cavern tickets. - **Injection Point** - An existing station location specified as the inlet to the cavern. - **Withdrawal Point** - An existing station location specified as the outlet to the cavern.

docs.title: Cavern Configuration
docs.text:
Cavern Status

If a cavern is no longer active, you can change the cavern status to reflect this. To change the cavern status: 1. Open the Cavern Editor. 2. Select the **Configuration** radio button and click the **Characteristics** tab. 3. Click **Edit Status**. The Location Characteristic Editor will open. Because location status can be datetime effective, users can specify the start and end times for which a cavern will fall under a particular status. This allows a cavern to be classified with different statuses over its lifetime. If the cavern level then changes on a cavern with a status of "Inactive", "Long-term Monitoring", or "Plugged and Abandoned", an exception will be generated.

Liquid Cavern Units

User-defined liquid cavern units display on all Liquid Cavern tickets. To access and configure liquid cavern units: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Tank Editor**. 2. Select the **Configuration** radio button. 3. Click the **Units** tab. 4. Use the drop-down menus to configure your unit settings. When units are not set or are left blank in the Liquid Cavern Editor, the units defined in System Settings are displayed in the Ticket Editor. 5. Click the **Save** button.

Cavern Site Details

Details about the liquid cavern site, including legal information and geographic details, are available on the Site tab in the Liquid Cavern Editor. To access cavern site information: 1. Open the Liquid Cavern Editor. 2. Select a liquid cavern. 3. Select the **Configuration** radio button. 4. Click the **Site** tab. The following data fields are available on the Site tab: - **City** - Indicates the city the liquid cavern is in; up to 20 characters - **County** - The county the liquid cavern is in; drop-down options are defined in the County Editor - **State** - The state the liquid cavern is in; drop-down options are defined in the State Editor - **Country** - The country the liquid cavern is in; drop-down options are defined in the Country Editor - **Time Zone** - The time zone of the liquid cavern; drop-down options are defined in the Time Zone Editor - **Section** - The basic unit of a township and range; each section refers to an area of a square mile; up to three characters - **Quarter** - Each section is divided into quarter sections, which are each further divided into quarter sections, for a total of 16 parts per section; up to 25 characters Example "NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4" refers to the most northwestern quarter of the southeastern quarter. - **Township** - A measure of the distance north or south from the baseline, six miles in length; up to four characters - **Range** - A measure of the distance east or west from the principal meridian, six miles in length; up to four characters - **Meridian** - A geographical north to south reference point; up to 25 characters - **Latitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying a north-south location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Equator; up to 12 characters - **Longitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying an east-west location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Prime Meridian; up to 12 characters

docs.title: Cavern Inventory
docs.text:
Liquid Cavern Inventory Levels

You can manually enter an inventory level and FLOWCAL will use the specified volume and mass to initialize the cavern inventory level. The inventory level entered will be used from the effective date forward, and batches following will be added or subtracted from that level. To set a cavern to a specific level: 1. Open the Liquid Cavern Editor. 2. Click the **Flow Data** radio button. 3. Go to **Periodic** \> **New**. Units for set level volume and mass are specified on the Units tab under the Configuration section.

docs.title: Reports & Tickets
docs.text:
Inventory Reports

Two reports are available from the Inventory menu on the Flow Data screen. These options will vary depending on whether you are on the Inventory tab or the Batch tab. To access the reports: Go to **Inventory** \> **Print**. If you're on the Inventory tab, a report displaying all set level records will be generated. If you're on the Batch tab, a report displaying all batches will be generated.

Inventory Empty Tickets

Inventory Empty tickets zero out the volume, mass and component levels for the cavern. You can choose a date to run the inventory empty, and FLOWCAL will calculate the empty amount for GSV, NSV, Mass and Net Allowable per product and determine the gain/loss percentage. The percentage is calculated as: GSV Percent gain/loss = GSV empty amount/((GSV in since last empty + GSV amount out since last empty)/2) \* 100. An empty may be performed at the end of a batch accounted for within a cavern or a manual date may be specified. If a manual date is specified, you will be prompted to perform an advanced batch split. If the "Ignore Batch Split" option is enabled, the empty will be performed without splitting batches. To perform an inventory empty: 1. Open the Liquid Cavern Editor. 2. Go to **Periodic** \> **Inventory Empty**. Double-clicking a record will open the [Ticket Details](../Tickets/Ticket%20Details/Ticket%20Details%20Editor.md) form; from there, you can view or edit ticket data as needed. Inventory Empty tickets can only be generated through the inventory empty process and cannot be manually edited or deleted.

Product Conversion Tickets

Product Conversion tickets can be used to convert the product accounted for within a cavern into a new product. To create a Product Conversion ticket: 1. Open the Liquid Cavern Editor. 2. Go to **Periodic** \> **Convert Product**. You can select the product to convert from and the product to convert to and specify the relevant measurement data for both sides of the conversion. When saved, two associated tickets will be created to correct the volume, mass and components for each product. Double-clicking a record will open the [Ticket Details](../Tickets/Ticket%20Details/Ticket%20Details%20Editor.md) form; from there, you can view or edit ticket data as needed. Data must be rolled up for the cavern and its members before a conversion may be initiated. The product to convert from and to must also be set up in the Product Editor as a valid product conversion.

Cavern Editor Table View

The Inventory tab in the Cavern Editor shows manually entered inventory levels, inventory empty tickets and product conversion tickets. Double-click an Inventory Empty or a Product Conversion record to review ticket data in the Ticket Editor (see Tickets from the Cavern Inventory Editor). Double-click a Set Level record to view or edit an entry that was used to define the amount in storage at a given point in time. You can also specify the initial amount in a cavern. Under the Batch tab in the Flow Data section, all of the batches from the meters in each injection and withdrawal location are displayed. The injection batches will add to the inventory; the withdrawal batches will decrease the inventory. When a location is closed, the cavern inventory at that point is saved in the Closed Inventory columns of the database. Any edits made to a closed record are accounted for in the Adjusted Total Inventory columns.

docs.title: Cavern Editor Tools
docs.text:
Contact Selections

Assign contacts to a cavern to be notified if messages or exceptions are generated.

Show Tools

When the Show Tools option is enabled, the menu icons at the top of the Liquid Cavern Editor are displayed. When it is not enabled, the menu icons are not visible.

Validations

FLOWCAL will validate specified volume or mass quantities against user-defined limits upon import of cavern-level tickets.

Info

The Cavern Info screen allows users to configure information and import options for a cavern. To access the Cavern Info screen: 1. Open the Liquid Cavern Editor. 2. Select a cavern. 3. Go to **Tools** \> **Info**. The following options are available on the Info screen: - **Fluid Phase** - The fluid phase of a cavern is always "Liquid". - **Requires Close Approval** - Caverns that require close approval have to satisfy a set of conditions before they can be closed, and are closed manually in [Location Close Approval](../Locations/Close%20Approval/Close%20Approval.md). - **Weekly Schedule** - This drop-down will list schedules created using the [Annual Schedule Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md). Location rollups will calculate totals for the cavern according to the date spans defined by the schedule selected here. Checking the Calculate Weekly Totals option in System Configuration will make the Weekly Schedule option visible for the locations, tanks, and caverns in that system. - **Ticket Import** - Ticket import options are used to enable adjustment of ticket dates for daylight savings time or for time zone. When these options are enabled, dates on all cavern-level tickets that are imported into the location via TFX are adjusted. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md)) - **Time Zone Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times are adjusted bu the offset amount defined for the selected time zone. (Time zones are created using the [Time Zone Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Geographic/Time%20Zone%20Editor.md).) For these purposes the time zone offset is to be user-configured based on the offset from the company's standard business time zone rather than offsets from UTC. - **DST Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times occurring during daylight saving time are shifted forward one hour. All dates and times that occur outside of daylight saving time are imported. - **Time Zone** - This read-only field displays the current time zone of the cavern.

docs.title: About Lists
docs.text:
FLOWCAL lists are logical groupings of locations, meters or sources, used for generating reports and exports, importing data, and viewing data.

Three types of lists are available in FLOWCAL:

  • Static - A static list only changes if you access the list through the List Editor, click the Edit button, and modify the list members.
  • Dynamic - A dynamic list is based on a user-defined query created in the Query Editor. This list changes based on returns from the associated query.
  • Ordered - An ordered list contains members listed in the order in which they were added. Typically, ordered lists are used for printing chart labels for gas meters in the order that the technician pulls the charts.

By default, static and dynamic lists are sorted by object number (i.e., meter, location or source number).

docs.text:
• Create & Delete Lists

  • Query Editor

docs.title: List Editor
docs.text:
FLOWCAL lists allow you to create logical groupings of like data points for meters, locations, and sources (such as grouping all meters in a given drilling basin, or all sources assigned to a given analyst). These lists can then be used to generate reports and exports, or to import, view, or edit data.

FLOWCAL supports static, dynamic and ordered lists. Static lists can only be edited through the List Editor, whereas dynamic lists are updated based on queries created in the Query Editor.

By default, static and dynamic lists are sorted by the object number (i.e., meter, location, or source number). Ordered lists display members in the order they were added. Typically, these are used for printing chart labels for gas meters in the order that the technician pulls charts.

To access the List Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **List**.

Creating Static or Ordered Lists

To create a static or ordered list from the List Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **List** to access the List Editor. 2. Click the **List** button, and select "List" to create a list of meters and/or locations, or select "Source List" to create a list of sources. 3. Click **New** and enter a name for the list. List names must be unique. They can be mixed case, and up to 50 characters. 4. Select whether the list will be static or ordered. If you are creating an ordered list, the assets will display in the order they are selected. 5. Populate the list. On the Lists tab under **Select from Available**, select members from the left side to add to the new list. To select more than one member, double-click a member, or hold the **Ctrl** key while clicking multiple items. 6. Click the arrow buttons to add your selection(s) to the list. Click in the **Select from Available** grid or the **Selected** grid and press **Ctrl+F** to quickly search through the grid. You can also select **Search** from the menu. To merge members from another list into the new list, select an existing list from the **Merge With** drop-down and click the **Merge** button. You can also copy a list of members from another program, such as Excel, if the members already exist in FLOWCAL. Right-click the grid and select **Paste** to add the items to the list. By default, items are displayed in order by number. Click a column header to sort data by that column. 7. Click **Save**.

Creating Dynamic Lists

To create a dynamic list from the List Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **List** to access the List Editor. 2. Click the **List** button, and select "List" to create a list of meters and/or locations, or select "Source List" to create a list of sources. 3. Click **New** and enter a name for the list. List names must be unique. They can be mixed case, and up to 50 characters. 4. Select **Dynamic** and choose a query from the **Query** drop-down to base the list on. The Selected grid will populate based on the query results. To create a new query, click the **Query** button or go to **Tools** \> **Query** to open the [Query Editor](../Tools/Query%20Editor.md). Once the query is created, click **OK** to return to the List Editor, and select the new query from the drop-down. 5. To include or exclude specific members from a dynamic list, click the **Included** or **Excluded** tab as appropriate and use the arrow buttons to include or exclude available items from the list. Including or excluding query result members will not alter the query. 6. Click **Save**.

Converting a Dynamic List to Static

Use the merge function to quickly convert a dynamic list to a static list. To convert a dynamic list to a static list: 1. Click the **Merge With** drop-down. 2. Select a list and click the **Merge** button to compile members from the existing list into the new list. All members from the list being merged will display in the grid under the list of selected locations, meters, or sources.

Deleting Lists

Lists can only be deleted from the List Editor. To delete a list: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **List** to open the List Editor. 2. Click the **List** button to select list or source list. 3. Select the list from the drop-down. 4. Click the **Delete** button.

docs.title: Set List Permissions
docs.text:
Provide certain groups and users access to the list using the Group and User Access tab. By default, the user creating the list will have access. Any other groups or users must be added if they are to have access.

While in Edit mode, use the arrow buttons to set access for specific users and groups, or use the Select All and Reject All buttons to grant or restrict access to the list for all users or groups.

Only users or groups with the List View privilege can be assigned to a list.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text:
• Create & Delete Lists
  • View Lists
  • Query Editor

docs.title: View Lists
docs.text:
You can view the members of a list from the List Editor.

To view lists: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **List** to open the List Editor. 2. Click the **List** button and select "List" or "Source List". 3. The members of the list will display under the Selected grid. For meter and/or location lists, you can elect to see locations only, meters only, or both. 4. The user to last modify the list, and the date of the last change, are displayed at the bottom of the screen.

You can also use the List Editor to find members in a large list or to find other lists that a given member belongs to.

  • Tools > Reverse Lookup - Select a list member to see the lists the member belongs to. Select a list and click Delete to remove the member from the selected list.
  • Search > Find - Launches a text box to allow you to quickly search through the grid. You can also press Ctrl+F or right-click the grid and select Find.

docs.title: List Notes
docs.text: Select a list in the List Editor and right-click the top half of screen to view or add notes associated with the list.

docs.title: About Locations
docs.text:
A location is a collection of one or more meters and/or other locations. Locations are used for balancing, determining pipeline efficiency and reporting (such as producer total volumes, fuel by area, or emissions reporting). Within a location, member data is totaled or averaged, and is available at an hourly, daily, or monthly basis.

In the following example, five meter members have been added to a location. When the location is rolled up, the volume and energy values are totaled, and the values for pressure and heating are averaged using weighted averaging.

Volume Energy Pressure Heat Value MET_1 100.0 105.0 150.0 1050.0 MET_2 100.0 105.0 175.0 1050.0 MET_3 100.0 105.0 125.0 1050.0 MET_4 200.0 220.0 165.0 1100.0 MET_5 200.0 220.0 145.0 1100.0 LOC1 700.0 755.0 152.9 1078.6

docs.title: Location Types
docs.text:
Locations can be used to model stations, laterals, segments, balances, and inventories, as indicated in the following table:

Legend

Meter Segment Station Balance

Segment

A segment is a physical or logical section of a pipeline; made up of meters and/or other locations. #### Data Considerations All segments require a base direction. The segment’s direction represents its general contribution to the overall system and dictate how the total is calculated: - **Inlet**: Total = \[(Sum of Inlets) – (Sum of Outlets)\] - **Outlet**: Total = \[(Sum of Outlets) – (Sum of Inlets)\] Segment locations with a "Throughput" direction can only have throughput meters as members. Each meter member will designated as having a positive or negative contribution to the location. Those specifications are used in calculating the total: - **Throughput:** Total = \[(Sum of Positives) – (Sum of Negatives)\]

Station

Station locations are used to total all meter runs associated with a meter station, such as multiple tubes delivering to a power plant, multiple wellheads at a pad location, or large volume interconnects between pipelines. #### Data Considerations The station location can be classified as an inlet or outlet; however, member meters are all additive to the station location. The following rules are true of stations: - A station can contain only meter members, therefore neither a segment nor another station can be a member of a station. - A meter cannot belong to two stations at the same time. - A station is a physical location. - Meter members are all additive to the station location whether they are classified as an inlet or outlet.  

Balance

A balance is a segment with properties for balancing a pipeline system; consists of a closed system of inlets and outlets; can contain any type of member (meters, stations, segments, and other balances). ![](data:image/png;base64,) #### Data Considerations The expectation of a balance system is that everything is accounted for and the total product received into the system will equal the total product delivered out of the system. No direction is needed since results are expected to equal zero. However, these totals never completely reach zero; this difference is termed "gain" or "loss." The default calculation in FLOWCAL is: (Outlets - Inlets)/Inlets The sign of the result depends on how the balance arithmetic is set up within the Rollup Configuration screen. You can define the numerator and denominator according to operational needs and preferences. The balance location total will result in a loss if there are more inlets than outlets, or a gain if there are more outlets than inlets. To successfully balance a system of piping, all inlets and outlets need to be represented. This includes not only conventional meters, tanks, batches, and line pack, but also accounts for items such as fuel used, flared volumes, shrinkage due to treating or processing, and third-party volumes. Balances at the top of the hierarchy will typically have the "Root Location" option set.

Inventory

An inventory refers to a segment with properties for inventory tracking. This location aggregates total inventory and calculates changes in inventory. It consists of inventory objects such as line pack meters and other inventory locations, and can be added to balance locations.

docs.title: Create & Delete Locations
docs.text:
Locations can be created in FLOWCAL manually from the Location Editor. Following a new implementation of FLOWCAL or other type of data acquisition, many locations may need to be created in bulk.

Manually Creating Locations

To create a location: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Editor**. 2. Click the **New** button or go to **Location** \> **New** from the Location Editor menu. 3. Click the arrow next to the **New** button to select a fluid phase; otherwise, the new location will use the default fluid phase specified in the User Preferences screen. Once the new location has been saved, the fluid phase cannot be changed. The liquid fluid phase is only available if you have the **FLOWCAL Liquids** module. 4. Enter a location number and name. 5. Select a location type. If you select "Station" or "Segment", you will also need to select a direction. (See: [About Locations](About%20Locations.md)) 6. Select a reference meter. A reference meter is datetime effective and is used to help ensure that location members have a common pressure base, temperature base, contract hour and contract day. By default, the reference meter is the first meter added to the location. You can also specify a reference meter that is not in the location. It is recommended that you create one or more reference meter templates, so that all locations can use the same reference meter. 7. Select a date range in the upper right corner of the screen. Meter/location membership within the location is datetime effective. 8. Select location members. - Click in the **Select from Available** grid or the **Selected** grid and press **Ctrl+F** to quickly search through the grid. You can also select **Search** from the menu. - Enter multiple meter IDs or location IDs copying and pasting the ID numbers from an Excel spreadsheet or text editor. Ensure the radio button selection on the left matches the member types to be pasted. Select **Data** \> **Paste** from the top menu bar. If you are pasting IDs from Excel or a text file, you can paste only meters or only locations with each paste. You cannot paste a combination of meter and location IDs. Membership will only apply to the date range selected in Step 7. 9. Enter any additional location information and click **Save**. The location will be queued to roll up the location data. By default, items are displayed in order by number. Click on the column headers to sort data by that column.

Bulk Creating Locations

A new FLOWCAL implementation for data acquisition can require the creation of hundreds or thousands of locations. The [FcLoader utility](../Admin%20Options/FcLoader.md) is available for creating locations in bulk. FcLoader ships with FLOWCAL and is available in the installation folder. A signed non-disclosure agreement (NDA) must be on file to receive the FcLoader file format. Contact Customer Support to obtain the appropriate NDA.

Deleting Locations

Locations can only be deleted from the Location Editor. Deleting a location requires **Location Edit – Can Delete** privileges. To delete a location: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Editor**. 2. Select a location using the Location drop-down. 3. Click the **Delete** button. 4. When prompted, confirm the deletion. When a location is deleted, FLOWCAL will generate a message logging the deletion. This message is available in the Message Viewer.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text:
• About Locations
  • Location Editor
  • View Location Data
  • Comparison Locations

docs.title: Edit Location Data
docs.text:
Meter members can be added to or removed from a location based on a datetime effective relationship. This keeps rollup totals accurate over time and maintains the membership history.

The reference meter and the meter/location membership within the location are date effective. When the location members need to be edited due to changes, such as new meters being placed in service, or a change in pipeline configuration occurring, a new date range should be created. This assures that the existing historical rollup data remains unchanged prior to these edits.

When editing existing locations, failing to create a new effective datetime will cause a new rollup for the existing balance to show results for the entire date period shown. This could result in many months of historical data being submitted to the Location Rollup Queue, which could create a backlog and impact system performance.

The Service Configuration screen offers rollup options that can limit the lookback period for rollups. If this option is enabled, data prior to the configured data is not rolled up.

To edit a location: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Editor**. 2. Select a location using the Location drop-down. 3. Click the **Edit** button. 4. Enter a date range that the changes apply to. 5. Make necessary changes and click **Save**. The changes will be applied and the location will be queued to roll up the location data based on the changes. You can delete a specific time frame for a location by selecting the time frame in the upper right corner and clicking the **Delete** button while in View mode.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text:
• Location Editor
  • Service Queues

docs.title: Section Editor
docs.text:
Sections identify parts or segments of a pipeline. Sections are populated with meters and behave much like locations. The Line Fill Service calculates the line fill on these sections.

Use the Section Editor to create, edit, and delete sections.

To access the Section Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Section Editor**. When creating a section, users must specify a section name, water capacity, water capacity units, product, and reference meter prior to saving. A section resembles a location in that it has date-effective members that are used to construct the section results. Sections can include meters or other sections as members. They cannot have locations as members; however, sections can be members of inventories or balance locations. The **Delete** button at the bottom of the Section Editor screen will delete the section in its entirety. The **Delete** button under the **To** date field will clear all data from the section for the selected time frame.

docs.title: Location Tree View
docs.text:
The location Tree View provides a visual structure for all locations that are a root location or are a member of a root location. This is ideal for keeping track of locations that are nested within larger locations.

To access the location Tree View: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Tree View**. 2. Select a location in the left-hand panel. 3. The location members as of the date in the Date field will display. If the location membership has changed over time, change this date to see the membership as it was on different dates. Clicking the up/down arrow at the top next to the **Number** heading to sort members in ascending order (up arrow) or descending order (down arrow). When you have selected a root location, you can drill down to see meter and location members. As you click on members of the location, the members of that member will display in the right-hand panel. By default, the left-hand panel does not show meter members. To display meter numbers in the meter members, click **Show** on the menu bar and select **Meters**. The Path field displays the path to the top of the selected root location. Click the **Search** button to the right of the **Path** field to access the Path Finder. In the Path Finder, select items (left column) to display their membership in root locations (right column). To find a specific meter or location, enter information in the search field at the top and click **Filter** to find items that match your criteria.

docs.title: View Location Data
docs.text:
All meters and locations under a parent location are rolled up to the parent location (i.e., everything totals upward in a tree). Several viewers display this rollup data, including the Meter/Location Rollups, Daily, Monthly, and NGL Balance Viewers.

To access the rollup viewers: Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers**.

docs.title: Close Approval
docs.text:
Use the Location Close Approval screen to evaluate the performance and efficiency of a location, acknowledge PPAs and exceptions, view the open members of a location, and close the location manually.

It displays energy and volume data for the current month in addition to the past five months. You can select a location that requires manual close approval and view various totals with volume and energy data viewed in either standard or measured mode.

Closing a Location Manually

To access the Close Approval screen: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Close Approval**. 2. Select the desired location from the drop-down menu. 3. Click the **Approve** button. The location will be marked as closed. The Approve button will only be available if all of the requirements have been satisfied. If any of the location members are still open, the Approve button will be disabled and the Open Items button will be visible. Click this button to view a list of location members that are still open. If PPAs have been applied to any location members, the **Approve** button will be disabled until the **PPAs Outstanding** option is enabled. If any monthly values exceed the validation limits, the **Approve** button will remain disabled until a comment has been entered. Upon closing a location: - The name of the person who closed the location, and the date and time of the close are recorded in the database and display in the Close Approval screen. - The Status field will auto update to show that the location has been closed. - A **Show Revisions** button becomes visible once the selected month for the selected location has been closed. (See: [Location Close Revisions](Location%20Close%20Revisions.md))

Requirements to Close a Location

Locations created with Requires Approval to Close enabled are placed in the Location Rollup Queue. After the location rolls up, the Location Close Data Service writes an exception stating that this location requires approval to close. For a location to be closed manually, four conditions must be met: - The location must be rolled up. - All location members (meter and location) must be closed first. - Any PPAs rolled up from members must be acknowledged by setting a checkbox. - A comment must be made if any values are outside of the validation limits. To create a location that requires approval to close: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Editor**. 2. Click **New** and enter a location name and number. 3. Set the location type to "Balance." 4. Go to **Tools** \> **Info** and check the **Requires Approval to Close** checkbox. 5. Click **OK**. 6. Add meter and/or location members. 7. Click the **Save** button.

Data Columns

The data columns will adjust depending on which Values radio button is selected (Gas or Liquid). Gas - If you select "Gas" for a non-inventory location, the values will be displayed as gain/loss and percent difference of volume and energy. - If you select "Gas" for an inventory location, the values will be displayed as total inventory for volume and energy. Liquid - If you select "Liquid" for a non-inventory location, the values will be displayed as gain/loss and percent difference of sum of component volume and mass. - If you select "Liquid" for an inventory location, the values will be displayed as total inventory of sum of component volume and mass.

docs.title: Location Close Revisions
docs.text:
Volume, mass, volume and mass inventory, and component volume and mass inventory data are stored whenever a location is closed through the location Close Approval screen. This allows for a closed location to have a revision number stored and manually incremented by a user.

When it first opens, the Location Close Revisions screen displays the stored volume, mass, inventory, and component data in the units that are selected on the Location Close Approval screen. The user may then select to have the values displayed in either Measured or Standard units.

In the top row, the current rolled-up data for the selected location and month is displayed. In the bottom grid, all revision records for the selected location and month are displayed, including the revision number for each record.

Users can select and right-click on a single row in the bottom grid to bring up a pop-up menu from which they can choose to print the Location Inventory Ticket report for that row to display the appropriate data for the revision.

Generating a Revision Number

The New Revision button on the Location Close Revisions screen is enabled when all rollup operations for the selected location and month are complete and the current rolled-up values differ from the latest revision in any of the stored fields, e.g. due to a PPA. The user privilege required for this button is the same as for approving a location to be closed. When the button is clicked, the current values are stored in the database with a revision number.

Locations Messages for Inventory Changes after Close Approval

When the Location Rollup Service rolls up a location month that has been closed, and if the values that have just been rolled up differ from the latest revision stored in the database, a location exception message is generated. When multiple data columns differ, FLOWCAL decides which column data to display using the following priority: - Sum of component volume - NSV - GSV - Mass - Individual component volume and mass The location exception message is generated effective the beginning of the month at contract hour with a default priority of 0. The user can adjust the priority of the exception message as desired. A new message is generated only when there are no unacknowledged messages for the same measurement month. Upon creating a new revision, any existing unacknowledged messages for the location and measurement month becomes acknowledged.

docs.title: Efficiency Definition Editor
docs.text:
Users must have the Location Balancing module in order to access the Efficiency Definition Editor.

The Energy Efficiency calculation allows the user to view their useful deliveries as a percent of their total receipts. By viewing the trend in calculated efficiency percentages, the user can easily notice any month to month differences in operating efficiency.

Defining an efficiency equation in FLOWCAL allows users to manage assets and identify bottom line impacts. This calculation divides the total useful energy delivered by the total energy received. Users can then determine their efficiency level to compare changes from month to month.

Before accessing the Efficiency Definition Editor, users must enable the subtotaling configuration options and enable efficiency calculation options for the location.

Enable Subtotaling Options

To enable subtotaling: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Application** \> **FLOWCAL Configuration**. 2. Enable the "Subtotal by Meter Direction" and "Subtotal by Meter Class" configuration options. (See: [FLOWCAL Configuration](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#Subtotal))

Enable Efficiencies on Locations

To enable efficiency calculation options for locations: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Location Editor**. 2. Select a location from the Location drop-down menu. 3. From within the Location Editor, go to **Tools** \> **Info**. 4. Under **Options**, the select the check box for **Calculate Energy Efficiency**, **Calculate Plant Recovery Efficiency**, or **Calculate System Recovery Efficiency**. System or Plant Recovery Efficiency will be displayed, but not both. If both options are enabled in the Location Editor for a given location, the System Recovery values will be displayed rather than the Plant Recovery values. To configure the Energy Efficiency equation in the Efficiency Definition Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Efficiency Definition**. 2. Select **Energy Efficiency** from the **Equation** drop-down menu. 3. Click the **Edit** button. 4. Under the **Numerator** panel, select all outlets to be calculated. These outlets are the total energy received. 5. Under the **Denominator** panel, select all inlets to be calculated. These inlets are the total useful energy delivered. 6. Click **Save**. 7. Select **System Recovery** or **Plant Recovery** from the **Equation** drop-down list to define those calculations. Example Energy efficiency can be calculated as: (NGL + Refined Product + Residue) / (NGL +Wet Gas) In this example, NGL, refined product and residue outlets are selected for the outlet energy efficiency definition. NGL and wet gas inlets are selected for the inlet energy efficiency definition.

View Energy Efficiency Results

Energy efficiency results are displayed on the Balance-Meas and Balance-Std tabs in the [Meter/Location Rollups Viewer](../../Rollup%20Viewers/Meter-Location%20Rollups/Meter-Location%20Rollups.md). To access energy efficiency results: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers** \> **Meter/Location Rollups**. 2. Click the **Balance - Meas** or **Balance - Std** tabs. If the efficiency definition selections are changed after initial setup in the Location Editor, users must restart location rollups and re-queue locations to roll up in order to change the data. You can also view results in the Balance Explorer using the Recovery Analysis View Template: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers** \> **Balance Explorer**. 2. Click **Templates** \> **Default Template** \> **Recovery Analysis View**. 3. Select your location in the tree view on the left side of the screen. 4. Set the date range. 5. Click **Refresh**.

docs.title: Inventory Editor
docs.text:
Use the Inventory Editor to create, edit, and delete gas inventory locationsInventory locations, such as underground sotrage caverns, are used to track storage amounts. An initial amount is added to or subtracted from the inventory. The results can then be viewed and reported in FLOWCAL..

The Inventory Editor has two primary tabs: Flow Data and Configuration. The Flow Data tab lists all Inventory Periodic records. The Configuration tab contains details and configuration options for injection and withdrawal points, characteristics, and site information.

Inventories can be viewed in the Meter/Location Rollups Viewer.

To create a new inventory location: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**. 2. Click the **New Inventory** button or go to **Inventory** \> **New**. 3. Enter an inventory location number. 4. Enter an inventory name (optional). 5. Select an injection point and/or withdrawal point (station locations). Entering at least on of these location points is required. If the items you need are not in the menu, you will need to add them through the [Location Editor](../Location%20Editor/Location%20Editor.md). 6. Click the **Characteristics** tab to edit the status. 7. Click the **Edit Status** button to change the status. Options are "Active", "Inactive", "Long Term Monitoring", and "Plugged and Abandoned". If the status is set to "Inactive", "Long Term Monitoring", or "Plugged and Abandoned", exceptions will be generated if the inventory changes during that time period. 8. Complete the applicable information on the Site tab. 9. Click the **Save** button.

The following options are available on the Inventory Editor screen:

  • Inventory Location Number - A unique identifier that the user sets for the inventory location. This field is required to create the inventory location.
  • Inventory Location Name - Optional field to identify a name for the inventory location.
  • Flow Data/Configuration - Select whether to view the location by all flow data for the Inventory or by the inventory's configuration setup
  • Injection Point - An existing station location set as an inlet that acts as the injection point for gas coming into the inventory location.
  • Withdrawal Point - An existing station location set as an outlet that acts as the withdrawal point for gas leaving from the inventory location.

Inventory Periodic Records

Set the inventory to a specific value using an inventory periodic record. To create an inventory periodic record: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**. 2. Go to **Periodic** \> **New**. 3. If the inventory location is a liquid type, enter the gross standard volume, net standard volume, and/or mass. If the inventory location is a gas type, enter volume, energy and/or mass. 4. Select a date and hour. 5. Click the **Save** button. To edit or delete a periodic record, select a row, and click **Periodic** \> **Edit** or **Periodic** \> **Delete**.

Inventory Validations

FLOWCAL can validate specified volume or mass quantities against user-defined limits. To view the Inventory Validations screen: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**. 2. Select a gas inventory. 3. Go to **Tools** \> **Validations**. The following options are available on the Validations screen: - **Total Volume/Mass** - Select volume or mass as the quantity to track, and specify the total quantity amount the inventory can hold. If the FLOWCAL-calculated inventory amount for any given hour exceeds this amount, an exception will be generated. - **Max/Min Fill** - If the FLOWCAL-calculated inventory amount exceeds or falls below the percentage of the total quantity amount, an exception will be generated. This provides a warning to users when nearing the bottom or nearing the overfill limit for the inventory.

Inventory Info

Details about the inventory contents are available in the Inventory Info screen. To access the Inventory Info screen: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Inventory Editor**. 2. Select a gas inventory. 3. Go to **Tools** \> **Info**. The following options are available on the Inventory Info screen: - **Fluid Phase** - The fluid phase of a gas inventory is always "Gas". - **Requires Close Approval** - Gas inventories that require close approval have to satisfy a set of conditions before they can be closed, and are closed manually in [Location Close Approval](../Close%20Approval/Close%20Approval.md).

Inventory Tools

The Inventory Tools screen provides access to several inventory configuration options: - **Contact Selections** - Contacts can be assigned to a gas inventory. These will allow for notification for messages and exceptions. - **Show Tools** - When this option is enabled, the menu icons at the top of the inventory editor are displayed. When it is not checked, the menu icons are hidden. - **Validations** - FLOWCAL will validate either volume or mass, against a user-defined limit. - **Info** - User can configure FYI information and import options for the inventory.

docs.title: Active Status Tab
docs.text:
Indicates whether a location is active or disconnected and is determined by the status of the meter members. The status is datetime effective and is split based on the status changes of its members during the meter rollup process.

The status can be seen on the Location Editor form and the history can be seen on the Active Status tab. The following are examples of what the user can expect for a location Active Status based on different scenarios:

  • If the user has a location with 1,000 meter members and even one is active, the location status is Active.
  • If the user has a location with 1,000 meter members and none are active, but even one is inactive, the location status is Inactive.
  • If the user has a location with 1,000 meter members with no active or inactive members, the location status is Disconnected.
  • If the user has a location with no members, the location status is Disconnected.

docs.title: BLM Tab
docs.text:
The BLM tab contains BLM-specific data points. The options on this tab determine how FLOWCAL handles verifications and reports generated for this location.

  • BLM Property - Designates the location as a BLM property. When set to “Yes”, the other fields available on this tab become visible and editable.
  • FMP Number - The BLM-approved facility measurement point (FMP) where oil or gas produced from a Federal or Native American lease, unit PA, or CA is measured; this measurement affects the calculation of the volume or quality of production on which royalty is owed. Required field if the BLM Property identifier is set to "Yes".
  • Lease Number - The number assigned to the lease location where the production occurs.
  • CA Number - Communitization agreement (CA) number identifying an agreement to combine a lease or a portion of a lease with other tracts for purposes of cooperative development and operations, when the initial lease cannot be independently developed and operated in accordance with established well spacing or well development programs.
  • PA Number - Participating area (PA) number representing a combined portion of the unitized area that BLM determines to be reasonably proven to produce geothermal resources or that supports production in commercial quantities, such as pressure support from injection wells; the size and configuration of all participating areas and revisions are not effective until BLM approves them.
  • FMP Tier - A volume rate designation for this location; higher volume rates have more stringent operating requirements.

Designations for locations are as follows:

  • High Volume: ≥ 30,000 bbl/month (default)
  • Low Volume: \< 30,000 bbl/month

FMP Tier dictates how validations are triggered; locations are defaulted to High Volume as this is the most stringent designation and will require the most attention from the producer, therefore ensuring compliance.

FMP Number, Lease Number, CA Number, and FMP Tier are shown on select reports designed specifically for BLM reporting requirements.

Once a meter or group of meters have been assigned to a location, the user can assign that location to a close group. The Close Group tab allows the user to assign a location to more than one close group during different time periods. Close groups can also be assigned in bulk from the Bulk Changes screen.

Locations can be assigned to close groups. The Close Group tab was added to the Location Editor for liquids to close tickets associated to the location. For gas, if the user associates a location to a close group and closes it, all the meters within the location will be closed automatically.
