docs.title: Edit Reasons Tab
docs.text:
FLOWCAL can be configured to require an edit reason when editing a location. By default, this feature is disabled. To enable it, select the location type to enable on the System Configuration screen. Once enabled, an edit reason is required before saving edits to a location. Edit reasons are filtered according to the date range selected for the location.

  • Effective Date - The datetime to which the edit reason applies
  • Comment - The edit/comment entered during a location edit
  • Username - The username of the user that made the edit
  • GMS Date - The datetime at which the edit was applied

docs.title: Location Editor
docs.text:
Use the Location Editor to create logical groups of meters and/or locations for specific time periods. Locations are especially useful for summing multiple meter tubes and performing system balancing.

Once a location is created, the Location Rollups service creates hourly, daily, and monthly records for the location by totaling volume, energy, and mass, and averaging fields like pressure, temperature, and analysis. All meters and locations under a parent location are totaled to the parent location.

When creating a new location you must select a fluid phase ("Gas" or "Liquid"). This is done by clicking the arrow on the right side of the New button. If you just click the New button, rather than the drop-down, the fluid phase for the location will be based on the default fuid phase defined in User Preferences.

The selected fluid phase does not affect which data is rolled up or calculated at the location level. All data is calculated and rolled up the same way, regardless of Fluid Phase. The location’s fluid phase only affects how the Meter/Location Rollup Viewer initially displays the location. If you select "Gas", the location will initially display with the Measured tab selected. If you select "Liquid", then the location will initially display with the Liquid Flow Data tab selected. Some tabs displayed in the Meter/Location Rollups Viewer will also vary depending on which fluid phase is selected.

All location types (except station locations) require the System Balancing Functions module.

To access the Location Editor:  Go to **Setup** \> **Location** \> **Location Editor**.

Location Editor Details

Use the panes on the lower half of the Location Editor screen to add or modify members of a location. The radio buttons at the top left pane provide a list of all available meters or locations. The right pane lists the current members of the location. Add or remove a member from the location by clicking the member and using the arrow buttons. The following items are available in the Location Editor: - **System** - FLOWCAL system associated with the location. - **Location** - Location number. The location number cannot contain any of the following symbols: (&, \|, \<, \>, ^). Spaces will be converted to underscores. - **Name** - Location name. Non-unique, optional identifier for each location. It has a 50-character maximum. Location name is not datetime effective. - **Type** - Station, Segment, Balance, or Inventory. See: [About Locations](../About%20Locations.md) - **Active Status** - Indicates whether a location is active or disconnected and is determined by the status of the meter members. The status is datetime effective and is split based on the status changes of its members during the meter rollup process. - **Reference Meter** - Used to ensure common pressure base, temperature base, contract hour and contract day for all meters in a location. This field is required to create a new Location. - **From/To** - Locations have a Time Span (start and end datetime) which represents the time frame each set of members should be included with the location. In the To field, the latest date can be entered by pressing **Ctrl+E**; in the From field, the earliest date can be entered by pressing **Ctrl+S**. The end date must occur later than the start date. - **Rollups** - Location rollups may be controlled per location. - **Enabled** - Locations are set to Enabled by default. The location will automatically roll up every time an edit is made. - **On Demand** - Selecting the On Demand option allows the user to declare when the Location will roll up. Clicking the On Demand button on the Unrolled Locations tab of the Service Queues screen makes these records visible and updates the status of these entries to "In Queue". - **Disabled** - If a location is set to Disabled, then it will not be rolled up. Disabled is useful if the location totals are not needed, but the organizational hierarchy of locations is still helpful. - **Root Location** - The Root Location check box is used to indicate that a location is at the top of a balance hierarchy. Other locations can be placed in it as members, as well as meters. A Root Location cannot be added as a member of another location without having Root Location unchecked. - **Find** - Launch a text box for data entry to quickly search through the grid. You can also press **Ctrl+F**. - **Refresh** - Reload the location from the database - **Security** - View or edit users that have access to the location. User/group access to the location is only relevant for companies that maintain object level security. Most companies do not restrict access at the object level. - **Delete** - Deletes a location. - **Edit** - Enter Edit mode to edit a selected location. - **New** - Create a new location. When you click the **New** button, the fluid phase is set to the user-defined default fluid phase configured within User Preferences. To set the fluid phase manually, click the drop-down on the **New** button and select Gas or Liquid. - **Exit** - Close the Location Editor. - **Query** - Open the [Query Editor](../../Tools/Query%20Editor.md) to populate the Location based on a query. To add members based on a query, the user must run the query from the Query Editor and select the members from the Query Results by clicking the right arrow button. - **Save** - Save changes. - **Cancel** - Cancel changes.

docs.title: Members Tab
docs.text:
The Members tab displays the meters and/or locations that make up the location for the time frame selected. All the meters and locations that are members of a location are totaled to the parent location during rollups.

Click any column header to sort in ascending or descending order.

The following items are available on the Members tab:

  • X - Multiplier.

This value cannot be edited for members that have a direction of "Tieover" or "Transfer".

  • System - System that the meter or location is associated with.

  • L/M - Indicates whether a member is a location or meter.

  • Number - Meter or location number.

  • Name - Meter or location name.

  • Class - A meter class or "meter purpose" used to provide FLOWCAL categories for grouping meters within viewers and reports (e.g., Sales, Receipt, Delivery).

  • Direction - Meter or location direction (e.g., Inlet, Outlet).

  • Type - Meter or location type (e.g., Orifice, Turbine, Station).

docs.title: Site Tab
docs.text:
The Site tab contains the legal description and information about the location site. The following items are available on the Site tab:

  • City - City the location is in; up to 20 characters.
  • County - County the location is in. Options are defined in the County Editor.
  • State - State the location is in. Options are defined in the State Editor.
  • Country - Country the location is in. Options are defined in the Country Editor.
  • Time Zone - Time zone the location is in. Options are defined in the Time Zone Editor.
  • Section - The basic unit of a township and range; each section refers to an area of a square mile; up to three characters.

  • Quarter - Each section is divided into quarter sections, which are each further divided into quarter sections, for a total of 16 parts per section; up to 25 characters. Example "NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4" refers to the northwestern-most quarter of the southeastern quarter.

  • Township - A measure of the distance north or south from the baseline, six miles in length; up to four characters.

  • Range - A measure of the distance east or west from the principal meridian, six miles in length; up to four characters.
  • Meridian - A geographical north to south reference point; up to 25 characters.
  • Latitude - A geographic coordinate specifying a north-south location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Equator; up to 12 characters.
  • Longitude - A geographic coordinate specifying an east-west location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Prime Meridian; up to 12 characters.

docs.title: Location Validations
docs.text:
Location validations allow you to validate that certain values (such as gas volume, energy, mass, and GSV) fall within the set points that you specify.

To specify minimum and maximum set points for location validations:  In the Location Editor, select **Tools** \> **Validations**.

After you specify minimum and maximum values, FLOWCAL prompts you to specify a time range and run validations. If a value is above or below the set points that you specified, FLOWCAL generates an exception.

The Location Rollup service automatically runs validations. You can also initiate them from the Toolbox (Tools > Toolbox).

For all location types, FLOWCAL validates the net quantity in the given unit and does not perform unit conversions. For balance locations, FLOWCAL also validates the calculated percent difference:

GSV, NSV, Summed Volume, and Net Allowable are only available with the Liquids module.

docs.title: Ticket Validations
docs.text:
Ticket validations allow you to attach validation templates to a location to validate attached tickets.

Add a Validation

To add a ticket validation template: 1. Click **Edit**. 2. Select a validation template from the drop-down menu. 3. Click the **add** button next to the drop-down menu. 4. Use the up and down arrows to the side of the main window to change the order the validations will be run in. 5. Click **Save**. The validations will be run in the order in which the templates appear in the Ticket Validations screen. Tickets will be validated when they are imported, manually created, or edited. If the ticket values fall outside the ranges set in the validations, an exception is generated.

Remove a Validation

To remove a validation template: 1. Click **Edit**. 2. Select a validation template. 3. Click the **remove** button in the lower-right corner of the window. 4. Click **Save**.

The following options are available on the Tools menu in the Location Editor:

  • Contact Selection - Contact Relationships can be designated for meters, sources, and locations.

The user can associate specific contacts (email addresses) to a location. Exceptions and messages logged for the location will automatically be emailed to the associated contacts for exceptions and messages set up for the contact type.

  • Location Validations - When a location is rolled up, if validations are enabled, an exception will be logged if the value is outside the range defined. (See: Location Validations)
  • Ticket Validations - If validation templates are attached to a location, all tickets attached to that location will be validated and exceptions will be logged if a value is outside of the range defined. (See: Ticket Validations)
  • Info
  • Fluid Phase – This field is set when the location is created and cannot be changed.

The selected fluid phase does not affect which data is rolled up or calculated at the location level. All data is calculated and rolled up the same way, regardless of Fluid Phase. The location’s fluid phase only affects how the Meter/Location Rollup Viewer initially displays the location. If you select "Gas", the location will initially display with the Measured tab selected. If you select "Liquid", then the location will initially display with the Liquid Flow Data tab selected. Some tabs displayed in the Meter/Location Rollups Viewer will also vary depending on which fluid phase is selected.

  • Measurement Area - Select a Measurement Area from the drop-down or, with System Information privileges, click new and create a new Measurement Area.

  • Custom Fields – These fields are not datetime effective. Labels can be user-defined. (See: Define Custom Field Labels)

  • Notes - The notes stored on the Info screen are only available from the Location Editor Info menu. For notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g. Volume Editor), right-click on the Location Editor screen to add or view notes.

  • Requires Close Approval - Indicator that flags locations that must satisfy a set of conditions before they can be closed; these locations are then closed manually through the Location Close Approval screen.

For a location to be closed manually, all location members (meter and location) must be closed first.

  • Weekly Schedule - This drop-down contains schedules created in the Annual Schedule Editor; location rollups will calculate totals for the location according to the date spans defined by this schedule. Although called Weekly Schedule, the span does not have to be for a week.

Example

A ticket schedule can be assigned to a location, tank, inventory, liquid cavern, or comparison. This allows for location rollups to calculate values that span multiple days, but less than a month per the defined schedule.

Enable the Calculate Weekly Totals option in System Configuration to make the Weekly Schedule option visible for the locations in that system. Turning on this functionality will greatly increase the size of the user's database.

  • Efficiency Options – Determine how location rollups calculate efficiency for segment or balance locations; efficiency definition must be configured in the Efficiency Definition Editor, and Subtotal by Meter Direction and Subtotal by Meter Class options must be enabled in FLOWCAL Configuration.

  • Calculate Energy Efficiency - Energy efficiency is calculated and displayed in Rollup Viewer, Daily Location Rollups Viewer, and Monthly Location Rollups Viewer.

  • Calculate Plant Recovery Efficiency - Plant recovery efficiency is calculated and displayed in the Recovery Analysis Viewer.
  • Calculate System Recovery Efficiency - System recovery efficiency is calculated and displayed in the Recovery Analysis Viewer.

If both plant and system recovery efficiencies are calculated, the system recovery values will be displayed.

  • Ticket Import - Ticket import options are used to enable adjustment of ticket dates for daylight savings time or for time zone. When these options are enabled, dates on all tickets that are imported into the location via TFX or FLOWCAL text file format are adjusted. (See: Date and Time Adjustments During Import)
  • Time Zone Shift - When enabled, all dates and times are adjusted by the offset amount defined for the selected time zone. (Time zones are created using the Time Zone Editor.) For these purposes the time zone offset is to be user-configured based on the offset from the company's standard business time zone rather than offsets from UTC.
  • DST Shift - When enabled, all dates and times occurring during daylight saving time are shifted forward one hour. All dates and times that occur outside of daylight saving time are imported.

  • Time Zone - This read-only field displays the current time zone of the location as defined on the Site tab of the Location Editor.

  • Scheduled Batch Movements – See: Scheduled Batch Movement

  • Validate Hierarchy - The Validate Hierarchy tool assists users in troubleshooting issues. The user opens the Validate Hierarchy tool from the Location Editor, then chooses the validation options to run: Show Invalid Tieover, Show Invalid Transfers, Validate Throughput as Tieover, and Show Unused Meters.
  • Find Parent Locations - The Find Parent Locations tool can be used to find a location/meter within a large hierarchy, or find all locations that a location/meter belongs to. From the Location Editor Tools menu, select Find Parent Locations and enter part or all of the object number into the filter. Select the object number you are looking for from the left pane. The Right pane will show the locations that the meter is a member of.
  • Product Conversion - Product Conversion opens the Ticket Editor with Ticket Type defaulted to Product Conversion to allow entry of conversion products, quantity converted, and accounting and analysis information. The result is two tickets, one which reduces the inventory of the “From” product and one that increases the inventory of the “To” product.

docs.title: Messages
Message Viewer
docs.text:
Messages form an organized audit trail of changes made to FLOWCAL settings, device creation and deletion, and informational messages regarding process statuses.

All messages can be viewed, acknowledged, and configured for automatic notification by email.

Four types of messages are generated:

  • System
  • Location
  • Meter
  • Source
To access the Message Viewer: Go to **Review** \> **Messages**. View a complete list of FLOWCAL messages in the Message Description Editor.

Message Viewer Details

The following items are available in the Message Viewer: - **Message** - Filter the messages for system, location, meter, or source. - **Select** - Select items used to filter the message grid. Options are Meter, Location, List, Source, Source List, Calc Meter, and Close Group. - **Priority** - Filter priority is user-defined based on the needs of IT and the business structure. - **Time Filter** - Datetime filtering applied to records, based on the time the message was generated. - **Class Filter** - Filters include Error, Warning, Information, or Security. These user-defined fields are based on the needs of IT and the business structure. - **Status Filters** - The status of the message in the system. - A message with a priority 1 through 10 is written with a default status of "Logged". - A message with a priority greater than 10 is written with a default status of "Unacknowledged". - **Acknowledge** - Indicates that a message has been reviewed and is considered acceptable. - **Unacknowledge** - Reverts the status of an acknowledged message to "Unacknowledged". Acknowledge and Unacknowledge options only apply to messages with a priority designation of 11 or higher. - **Print** - Generates the Messages report, using the filters defined in the Message Viewer.

Viewing Messages

To view a message: 1. Select the appropriate filters to reduce the number of messages displayed. 2. Double-click a message. The Message Detail screen will display, listing all additional information related to the message.

Emailing Messages

You can manually email messages directly from the Message Viewer, or configure contacts to be notified automatically when certain messages are generated. To manually email a message: 1. Highlight one or more rows. Right-click the highlighted items and select **E-mail**. 2. Select a contact and click **Send**. To set up automatic notifications, you will need to set message parameters and designate recipients in the [Message Description Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Application/Message%20Description%20Editor.md).

1200 - Invalid gas master allocation (allocated delta)

This informational message is generated when the total value for the denominator is \<= 0 or NULL. This value is comprised of the difference between the Inlet and outlets being allocated to. This error can occur when the same amount going in the pipe is equal to the amount exiting the pipe or if no product is flowing in the contract month selected through the meters being allocated to. For example, a Master Meter has a direction of Outlet and has three meter members: METER.IN (Inlet), METER.OUT.1 (Outlet) and METER.OUT.2 (Outlet). The denominator for determining the volume allocation amount per meter will always be: Allocation for METER.IN = {*METER.IN*/\[(*METER.OUT*.1 + *METER.OUT*.2) - *METER.IN*\]} \* MASTER.METER If The Sum of the Outlet Meter Members = 150 and METER.IN = 150, then the denominator would = 0 and FLOWCAL would produce this error message to alert the user that the allocation was unsuccessful.

This informational message is generated when a Master Allocation could not be processed completely. An example of the master allocation failing would be selecting a contract month that contains no flow data for either the master meter or its meter members.

About Meters
docs.text: A meter is a physical device used in the field to measure the flow of gas and liquid products. Each meter type has unique identifiers and characteristics. FLOWCAL supports several meter types, including cone, Coriolis, orifice, positive displacement, turbine, and ultrasonic.

docs.title: Meter Types
docs.text:
Cone Meter

Cone meters use a conical position inside of the pipe to cause a pressure drop. The amount of the pressure drop is used to calculate the amount of mass and volume being moved.

Coriolis Flow Meter

Coriolis flow meters use vibrating tubes to calculate the mass and density of the product passing through it.

Line Pack

Line pack meters are used to monitor pipeline inventory. Line pack meter periodics reflect pipeline inventory at a particular time period. The meter rollup process calculates changes in pipeline inventory from one period to the next. See: [Line Pack Meters](Line%20Pack%20Meters.md)

Orifice

Orifice meters use a plate in a pipe to cause a pressure drop. The amount of the pressure drop is then used to calculate the amount of mass and volume being moved.

Positive Displacement

Positive displacement meters are a type of rotary meter. The container is filled with fluid and rotates from supply side to distribution side. Each rotation creates a pulse which correlates to a fixed amount of volume.

Turbine

Turbine meters have a fan blade in the pipe that rotates as product passes through it. Each rotation results in a pulse. These pulses are used to calculate the amount of volume passing through the pipe.

Ultrasonic

Ultrasonic meters use ultrasonic transmitters and receivers to calculate the velocity of the liquid passing through. This is used to calculate the volume.

docs.title: Create & Delete Meters
docs.text:
Meters can be created in FLOWCAL manually or automatically via file imports. Following a new implementation of FLOWCAL, merger, or other type of data acquisition, many meters may need to be created in bulk. Other times, analysts may need to create a handful of meters every month.

Manually Creating Meters

In FLOWCAL, you can manually create meters from the [Meter Editor](Meter%20Editor/Meter%20Editor.md) or the Meter Quick Create screen. Each screen has specific benefits: | Functionality | Meter Editor | Meter Quick Create | |:---|:--:|:--:| | Copy feature allows user to copy from an existing meter | Yes | Yes | | Limited data set | No | Yes | | Support for gas meters | Yes | Yes | | Support for liquid meters | Yes | No | | Can edit characteristic fields such as Meter Type | No | Yes |   To create a meter from the Meter Editor: 1. Open the Meter Editor, and click the **New** button or go to **Meter** \> **New** from the Meter Editor menu. Click the arrow next to the **New** button to select a fluid phase; otherwise, the new meter will use the default fluid phase specified in the User Preferences screen. Once the new meter has been saved, the fluid phase cannot be changed. The liquid fluid phase is only available if you have the **FLOWCAL Liquids** module. 2. Populate required data fields (highlighted in green). These fields must be populated before you can save the meter record. By default, the only required field to save a new gas meter is Meter Number. For liquid meters, Operation Type is also required, which is defaulted to "Batch". Additional fields may be required based on how FLOWCAL options are configured. Your new meter may have required Meter Characteristics data fields. You will be able to create and save the new meter without populating those fields; however, when you edit the Meter Characteristics under the Volume Editor screen, you will need to populate the remaining required fields before you can save your changes. 3. Enter any additional meter information and click **Save**. The Meter Number field can contain up to 16 characters. The Meter Name field can contain up to 60 characters.

Automatically Creating Meters

The "Auto Create Meters" options allow you to automatically create meters during data import using Quroum’s proprietary meter text file format or Transaction Queue. These options must be configured under the Service Configuration screen. Auto Create for meters is not supported for CFX files. #### Text Files When the "Auto Create" option for meters is enabled, meters imported by text file using the **Import** \> **Meter Text File** screen will be created automatically if they do not already exist. #### See also: - [Text File Import - Gas Meters](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Text%20File%20-%20Gas.md) - [Text File Import - Liquid Meters](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Text%20File%20-%20Liquid.md) You can also use the File Import service to automatically import meter text files and create meters. #### TESTit Integrated Meters can also be created automatically using TESTit Integrated. - **TESTit 3** - When you enable the "Auto Create on Import" option through the TESTit Integration Configuration screen, meters will be created automatically when test reports are imported. - **TESTit 2** - When you set the Update column on the Data Map Editor to Create for Meter, meters will be created automatically when test reports are imported. This feature requires TESTit Integrated.

Bulk Creating Meters

A new FLOWCAL implementation or data acquisition can require the creation of hundreds or thousands of meters. The FcLoader utility is available for creating meters in bulk. FcLoader ships with FLOWCAL and is located in the installation folder. A signed non-disclosure agreement (NDA) must be on file to receive the meter text file, FcLoader, and Transaction Queue file formats. Contact Customer Support to obtain the appropriate NDA.

Copying Meters

You can also create a meter by making a copy of an existing meter. Users will often create a set of default meters to use as the basis for new meters, so that meter properties, such as close group, custom field values and validation ranges, are automatically specified in the new meter. You can copy an existing meter through either the [Meter Editor](Meter%20Editor/Meter%20Editor.md) or the Meter Quick Create screen. To copy a meter from the Meter Editor: 1. Open the Meter Editor, and select a meter to copy using the Meter drop-down. 2. Click the **Copy** button, or select **Meter** \> **Copy** from the Meter Editor menu. 3. Enter a new meter number and name. 4. Make any required edits and click **Save**.

Deleting Meters

Meters can only be deleted from the Meter Editor. Deleting a meter requires the **Meter Edit - Can Delete** privilege. To delete a meter: 1. Open the Meter Editor, and select a meter to delete using the Meter drop-down. 2. Click the **Delete** button, or select **Meter** \> **Delete** from the Meter Editor menu. 3. When prompted, confirm the deletion. When a meter is deleted, FLOWCAL will generate a message logging the deletion (available in the [Message Viewer](../Messages/Message%20Viewer.md)).

docs.title: Import Meter Data
General Data
docs.text:
General meter information as seen on the Meter Editor can be populated using the following methods:

  • Manual entry through the Meter Editor
  • Bulk edits through the Bulk Changes screen
  • Bulk imports using the FcLoader utility

docs.title: Flow Data
docs.text:
Meter volumes, characteristics, and analysis can be imported using the following methods:

  • Manual or automatic file imports (such as text file, CFX, or other FLOWCAL supported file type)
  • Manual data entry
  • Transaction Queue import

Manual File Imports

The following table lists the various screens available for importing meter volumes, characteristics and analyses: | Screen | Description | |:---|:---| | [Meter Data](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Data.md) | Import gas or liquid meter data in the form of a CFX file, which can contain meter flow history, meter configuration, events, alarms, product information and/or analysis data. Access other FLOWCAL meter import drivers from the Driver drop-down on this screen. | | [Meter Text File](../Imports/Meter%20Data/Import%20Meter%20Text%20File%20-%20Gas.md) | Import gas or liquid meter data for a single meter or multiple meters using Quroum’s proprietary text file format. | | [Prove Data](../Imports/Import%20Prove%20Data.md) | Import prove data in the form of a PFX created by PROVEit or an external SCADA system. | | [Lab Analysis](../Imports/Lab%20Analysis/Import%20Lab%20Analysis.md) | If you do not have the Source Analysis module, use the Import Lab Analysis screen to import gas analysis sample data that uses the lab analysis text file format. |   Most files imported into FLOWCAL are in Quorum’s proprietary file format. A signed non-disclosure agreement (NDA) must be on file to receive these file formats. Contact Customer Support to obtain the appropriate NDA.

Automatic File Imports

The File Import service is a Windows service that can be installed on the application server where FLOWCAL is installed. The service automatically processes import files based on the file path specified within FLOWCAL. The service can be used to import different file types, such as meter text files and CFX files.

Manual Data Entry

Flow data, meter characteristics, and meter analyses can be entered manually in the Volume Editor. You can also manually enter data for other types of meters from various Import screens. This data is rolled up into hourly, daily and monthly records, which can then be seen from the Meter/Location Rollup Viewer. This rolled data is primarily used for reporting externally and internally to other departments and downstream systems. The following table lists the various screens available for manually entering meter volumes, characteristics or analyses: | Screen | Description | |:---|:---| | Manual Entry \> [Meter Input](../Imports/Manual%20Entry/Manual%20Meter%20Input.md) | Manually enter data for external volume meters (designated within the Meter Editor). | | Manual Entry \> [PD Entry By List](../Imports/Positive%20Displacement/Positive%20Displacement%20Entry%20by%20List.md) | Quickly enter index readings for positive displacement and turbine meters. | | Manual Entry \> [Planimeter](../Imports/Manual%20Entry/Manual%20Planimeter%20Entry.md) | Calculate the process variable for differential pressure, static pressure, and temperature for a specific meter for a specified date. |

Transaction Queue

Transaction Queue provides an alternative to file imports and can be used to import data into FLOWCAL on a near real-time basis. The data is written to the database from SCADA or other intermediate solution. Contact Customer Support for additional information about Transaction Queue.

docs.title: Line Pack Meters
docs.text:
Pipeline inventory, or line pack, is managed in FLOWCAL via a meter type called “Line Pack”. Line pack meter periodics reflect pipeline inventory at a particular time period. The meter rollup process calculates changes in pipeline inventory from one period to the next.

To create a line pack meter in FLOWCAL, set the meter type to “Line Pack” in the meter’s characteristics.

Gas Line Pack Meters

Gas line pack meters in FLOWCAL use the same parameters as AGA-7 meters, except that users can either provide the raw volume (provided with each periodic) or let FLOWCAL calculate it based on pipe length and diameter (meter characteristics). Temperature, pressure, and an analysis that satisfies the selected Z Method are required to calculate volume and energy. To create a gas line pack meter: 1. Create a new gas meter in the Meter Editor. 2. Go to the Volume Editor and open the meter characteristics. 3. Set the meter type and calculation method to “Line Pack”, and set the Z Method. 4. If you want FLOWCAL to calculate raw volume, enter the pipe diameter and pipe length. 5. Enter the pressure base, temperature base, pressure gauge, atmospheric pressure, and other information as needed. Pipe diameter and pipe length units default to the FLOWCAL system units. The default units for the meter can be changed on the Units tab of the meter’s characteristics.

Liquid Line Pack Meters

For liquid line pack meters, if you need FLOWCAL to calculate the mass and volume, the calculation method must be set to API 12.2 (Liq Volumetric) and a product must be selected. You can choose the Data Only calculation method if you will be providing mass and volume. Observed temperature, observed pressure, observed density, meter temperature and meter pressure are required to calculate GSV, NSV, and mass. If an analysis is applied, gas equivalent volume, energy, component volume, and component mass are calculated. Indicated volume can be entered for each record, or you can set the line pack volume on the Operations tab of the meter’s characteristics. The calculation for each record will use a volumetric calculation based on a water volume for the pipe that the meter represents. A water volume can be specified on the Operations tab of the meter’s characteristics. This will be the default uncorrected volume, although each record can be imported or edited with its own uncorrected volume. To create a new liquid line pack meter: 1. Create a new liquid meter in the Meter Editor. 2. From the Volume Editor, go to the meter’s characteristics. 3. Set the meter type to “Line Pack” and the calculation method to “API 12.2 (Liq Volumetric)” or “Data Only”. 4. Select a product. 5. Set the meter factor, pressure gauge and atmospheric pressure. If the meter factor is not set, a value of 1.0 will be used.

Line Pack Batches

Line pack batches are typically created via the [Batch Scheduler utility](../Settings%20Manager/Liquids/Batch%20Scheduler%20Utility.md). ACBI batches will be created for periods in which no defined batches exist. Line pack batches can only be rolled up from periodics. Consequently: - Line pack batches cannot be imported; and - Line pack batch flow data cannot be edited.

Meter Data Rollups

The Rollup Viewer displays changes in line pack data between the current record and the previous record as well as the inventory. FLOWCAL uses the latest value of each period for the inventory, so the change represents the activity during the period, and the line pack inventory represents the total line pack inventory at the end of the period. When viewing monthly data for the current month, for example, the values will represent the net change since the end of last month and the latest known total line pack of the segment or section. Similarly, the last hour of each day is taken as the value for that day, and the last day of the month is taken as the value for that month. The following table demonstrates this calculation using a three-hour day and a three-day month: ![](data:image/png;base64,)

Line Pack Meters in Inventory Locations

Inventory locations, created within the Location Editor, are also available for line pack meters to calculate the total amount of inventory as well as the change in that inventory. The rollup action for hourly data sums the line pack inventories and change amounts from the corresponding hours of all location members (members may be line pack meters or other inventory locations). The rollup action for daily and monthly inventory data takes the latest chronological value for each period to the next resolution level and calculates the difference from the previous record. Location rollups include the change volume from a line pack meter or inventory location when calculating the gain/loss for a segment or a balance. The Rollup Viewer displays the changes in volume, energy, and mass from one record to the next. The total inventory is also displayed for volume, energy, and mass. When adding multiple line pack meters into one inventory location (created in the Location Editor), the meter data resolutions must match.

docs.title: Non-Physical Meters
docs.text:
FLOWCAL supports certain non-physical meter types that represent volumes derived from physical meters.

Calculated Meters

Calculated meters contain meter or location members that all contribute to the calculated meter total, based on direction and contribution factor. On the front end, calculated meters are treated the same as regular meters in that they will appear on reports when run by meter list. On the back end, calculated meters are handled like locations, maintaining the member relationships, and only displaying flow data from the Meter/Location Rollup Viewer. (See: [Calculated Meter Editor](../Calculated%20Meter%20Editor/Calculated%20Meter.md))

Dead Oil Meters

This meter type is part of the [Live Oil Management add-on](Meter%20Editor/Tools%20Menu.md). It can only be created as a child of a designated live oil meter. The calc method for dead oil meters is “Data Only”; data cannot be directly imported into a dead oil meter.

Flash Gas Meters

This meter type is part of the [Live Oil Management add-on](Meter%20Editor/Tools%20Menu.md). It can only be created as a child of a designated live oil meter. The calc method for flash gas meters is “Gas Data Only”; data cannot be directly imported into a flash gas meter.

docs.title: Analysis Tab
docs.text:
Analysis is the global analysis setting which meters utilize for calculations. They are datetime effective and are used to warn the user when a meter analysis is imported for the meter that does not match the known master analysis.

To create a master analysis: 1. Select the **Analysis** tab and click **New**. 2. Check the **Compare to Analysis** option. When checked, the meter analysis will be compared to the master analysis on import. If unchecked, validations against the master analysis will not occur. 3. Enter the **Effective From** and **Effective To** dates, which defines the dates for which the master analysis will be effective. There can be multiple master analysis for any meter, but their date ranges will not overlap. If the date range of a master analysis is set so that it overlaps an existing master analysis, the existing analysis will be modified (or deleted if the new analysis completely overlaps the existing analysis) so that there is no overlap. 4. Flag fields of interest by checking **Compare** or **Autocreate**. 1. When **Compare** is checked, FLOWCAL will compare the master analysis against the meter analysis imported. If the values differ from one another, then an exception will be generated. 2. When **Autocreate** is checked, the existing master analysis record will be split at the date of the new meter analysis containing the new value for that field. This will help keep the Master Analysis up-to-date and minimize the number of exceptions generated when a new meter analysis is imported. 5. Click **OK** to save.

docs.title: Master Characteristics
docs.text: << Back | Characteristic | Analysis | Contractual/Operational

docs.title: Characteristic Tab
docs.text:
Characteristics are a set of standards by which a meter is operated. They are datetime effective and are used to warn the user when a meter characteristic is imported for the meter that does not match the known master meter configuration.

When creating a new master characteristic, it will appear pre-populated with data from the current meter characteristic, including the start and end date. All fields can be edited. If values are selected which are different from the current meter characteristic, the user will be warned when the user saves.

The fields displayed will change based on the selected meter type.

Meter characteristics are compared to master characteristics upon import and edit.

To create a master characteristic: 1. Select the **Characteristics** tab and click **New**. 2. Enter the **Effective From** and **Effective To dates**, which defines the dates for which the master characteristic will be effective. There can be multiple master characteristics for any meter, but their date ranges will not overlap. If the date range of a master characteristic is set so that it overlaps an existing master characteristic, the existing characteristic will be modified (or deleted if the new characteristic completely overlaps the existing characteristic) so that there is no overlap. Example Suppose that for meter number 01000, there is a master characteristic that runs from midnight on January 1, 2000 through midnight on January 1, 2003. Now suppose that the user creates a new master characteristic with a start date of midnight on June 1, 2002. Since this overlaps the original master characteristic from midnight on June 1, 2002 to midnight on January 1, 2003, the effective date of the original master characteristic will be changed to midnight on January 1, 2000 to midnight on June 1, 2002. 3. Check the **Compare to Characteristic** option. When checked, the meter characteristic will be compared to the master characteristic upon import or edit. If unchecked, validations against the master characteristics will not occur. 4. Flag fields of interest by checking **Compare** or **Autocreate**. 1. When **Compare** is checked, FLOWCAL will compare the master characteristics against the imported or edited meter characteristics. If the values differ from one another, then an exception will be generated. 2. When **Autocreate** is checked, the existing master characteristic record will be split at the date of the new meter characteristic containing the new value for that field. This will help keep the Master Characteristics up-to-date and minimize the number of exceptions generated when a new meter characteristic is imported or edited. This is useful for fields such as the orifice plate where changes are expected. 5. Click **OK** to save.

Characteristic Tab Details

The following items are available on the Characteristic tab: - **Data Source** - The Data Source field is an FYI field and is similar to an edit reason. In general, Master Characteristics are manually maintained from paper reports. You may receive paper Equipment Change reports, Annual Equipment Inventory reports, Meter Test reports, etc. Based on these paper reports, the Master Characteristics data will be edited; this field tracks the source of information used to make the edit. When EFM data comes in, if an exception is generated, it either means that a change was made in the EFM and not reported, or a change was reported on paper but not entered into the EFM. - **Sample Taken** - Check this field to indicate that a sample has been taken. This indication can be used to manually verify that the analysis is eventually received from the lab.

docs.title: Contractual/Operational Tabs
docs.text:
Contractual limits are regulatory requirements defined in a tariff and/or operational agreements, maintenance agreements, and standard operating procedures and include items such as test frequency and sample frequency. These limits can be used to define correction limits, test and sample frequencies for meters, and PPA thresholds.

Operational limits represent limits set by the actual operation of the meter, which may or may not match Contractual limits. Operational limits can be validated against contractual limits to ensure operations meet or exceed contractual limits.

The record has an effective date and an effective end date, but these data points are not used. These records are for all of time. When a new record is created, these fields will be populated with the start and end of time. These values are not editable.

Contractual limits can be manually entered from the Master Characteristics screen or imported from a tab-delimited file (contact Customer Support to obtain the file format). See also: Import Contractual Limits

To add contractual or operational limits: 1. Select the **Contractual** or **Operational** tab and click **New**. 2. Update fields of interest. 3. Click **OK** to save.

Copy Data Button - Copy the contractual limits to the operational limits.

Schedule Sub-Tab

The Schedule tab allows you to define frequencies for tests, samples and gravity tests. Each of these fields are validations that are run between meter tasks. You can set the maximum amount of time, the first month of test, sample or gravity test, and the tiering options to schedule tasks if volume reaches certain time-based thresholds. If any of these limits are exceeded an exception will be thrown to notify you that a new task should be scheduled. #### Schedule Sub-Tab Details The following items are available on the Schedule sub-tab: - **Test Frequency** - The Test Frequency defines how often the meter should be tested for accuracy. - **Sample Frequency** - Sample Frequency defines how often a gas stream should have a sample analyzed. The last three fields (Accumulated Vol Between Proves, Maximum Time Between Proves, and Meter Factor Change Between Proves) on the Schedules tab are for liquids. Each of these fields are validations that are run between proves. A user can set the maximum amount of volume, maximum amount of time and maximum delta for the meter factor between proves. If any of these fields go above what is set between proves, then an exception will be generated to alert the user.

Sample Sub-Tab

The Sample tab allows you to store a set analysis for the meter. This analysis can then be used as a reference when working elsewhere in FLOWCAL. #### Sample Sub-Tab Details The following items are available on the Sample sub-tab: - **Methane (% of Ethane)** - This limit is only applicable to liquid meters. If you have a contractual limit for methane (C1) as a percentage of ethane (C2), you would enter that limit here. When an analysis is applied to liquid meters, FLOWCAL will calculate component volume values. If the component volume for methane exceeds this limit, the amount of methane over the limit, in gallons, will be stored in excess_c1 in FC_BATCH_REPORT and FC_BATCH_TOTAL. If the limit is exceeded, this value will be displayed on the batch ticket report in the comments section. - **Carbon Dioxide (% of Ethane)** - This limit is only applicable to liquid meters. If you have a contractual limit for Carbon Dioxide (CO2) as a percentage of ethane (C2), you would enter that limit here. When an analysis is applied to liquid meters, FLOWCAL will calculate component volume values. If the component volume for carbon dioxide exceeds this limit, the amount of carbon dioxide over the limit, in gallons, will be stored in excess_co2 in FC_BATCH_REPORT and FC_BATCH_TOTAL. If the limit is exceeded, this value will be displayed on the batch ticket report in the comments section.

Thresholds Sub-Tab

#### Thresholds Sub-Tab Details ##### Calibration Adjustment The first four fields (Correction Time Limit (days), Calibration Adjustment Rule, Min Calibration Adjustment Pct, and Min Calibration Adjustment Unit Diff) define test report correction limits used with TESTit Integrated. Requires TESTit Integrated. ##### PPA Thresholds The fields in the PPA Thresholds group allow users to set thresholds for PPAs performed on the selected meter. If the threshold criteria is not met, the PPA is automatically rejected and a meter message is generated. The rejected PPA can then be manually unrejected and then approved from the [Edit Approvals](../../Edit%20Approvals/Edit%20Approvals.md) screen. FLOWCAL gives priority to operational limits. If the operational limits are null, the contractual limit will be enforced. If the operational and contractual Limits are both null, the system limits will be enforced. FLOWCAL will enforce the same limit type for all data points. Example A user only sets an Operational Limit for Gas Volume and leaves the other data points as null. FLOWCAL will not consider Contractual or System thresholds for the remaining data points since it already encountered an Operational Limit for Gas Volume. - **Max PPA Time Frame (Months)** - Maximum time frame beyond which PPAs will be automatically rejected. For example, If the threshold is set to 6 months and in August 2018 a PPA is made to the closed production month of January 2018, the PPA will be auto-rejected since the difference between the production month and current business month is 7 months, which is greater than the threshold. - **Gas Data Point Thresholds** - Gas meter minimum thresholds for PPAs. When one or more PPA amounts do not exceed the minimums, the PPA will be automatically rejected and a meter message (number 705) will be written. The rejected PPA can be manually unrejected and then approved from the Edit Approvals window (Review \> Approvals). FLOWCAL will first look to see if Operational thresholds have been set. If none are set, then Contractual thresholds will be examined. Finally, if no meter-level thresholds have been set, then system-level thresholds will be examined. Only threshold values for Gas Volume or Energy will be considered for gas meters. VCF edits, which are sometimes used to correct data values shown on final reports, do not alter volume but are still saved as PPAs. Such PPAs will be automatically rejected if the thresholds have been set and will need special attention by the user. - **Liquid Data Point Thresholds** - Liquid meter minimum thresholds for PPAs. When one or more PPA amounts do not exceed the minimums, the PPA will be automatically rejected and a meter message (number 705) will be written. The rejected PPA can be manually unrejected and then approved from the Edit Approvals window (Review \> Approvals). FLOWCAL will first look to see if Operational thresholds have been set. If none are set, then Contractual thresholds will be examined. Finally, if no meter-level thresholds have been set, then system-level thresholds will be examined. Only threshold values for Mass, GSV, or Summed Volume will be considered for liquid meters. CF edits, which are sometimes used to correct data values shown on final reports, do not alter volume or mass but are still saved as PPAs. Such PPAs will be automatically rejected if the thresholds have been set and will need special attention by the user. The thresholds will only be enforced if the Approval Required PPA Option is selected in System Configuration.

docs.title: Master Characteristics
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires the Master Characteristics module and System Process – Master Data privileges.

Master Characteristics define how a meter’s characteristics should look when brought in from the field and are typically created based on the last meter test report.

Like Meter Characteristics, Master Characteristics are datetime effective. Master Characteristics can be set up to create exceptions if there is a difference between the meter’s master characteristic and the meter characteristic. You can also have the master characteristic updated automatically to reflect the meter characteristic in the field. Both exception creation and automatic master characteristic updates can be toggled on or off for each field in Master Characteristics. You can also validate the imported analysis to look for differences in the imported analysis.

To access the Master Characteristics screen: Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Master Characteristics**.

Master Characteristics Screen Details

The following items are available on the Master Characteristics screen: - **Navigation Buttons** - Click the following when a list is selected: > - **Back to Beginning** - Navigate to the first meter number in the list. > - **Back One** - Move back in the list to the previous meter. > - **Launch Tree View** - Open the Tree View for the list selected. > - **Forward One** - Move forward in the list to the next meter. > - **Forward to End** - Navigate to the last meter number in the list. - **Effective From/Effective To** - The dates for which the master characteristic data is effective. The grid is filtered based on these dates. - **All Dates** - Sets the Effective From date to the start of time and the Effective To date to the end of time. - **Refresh** - Refreshes the grid. - **New** - Create a new Master Characteristics record. - **Edit** - Edit an existing master characteristic record. - **Delete** - Delete an existing master characteristic record. - **Exit** - Exit Master Characteristics and return to main screen.

docs.title: Screen Tabs
docs.text:
Three tabs are available within the Master Characteristics screen:

  • Characteristic Tab
  • Analysis Tab
  • Contractual/Operational Tabs

docs.title: BLM Tab
docs.text:
The BLM tab contains BLM-specific data points. The options on this tab determine how FLOWCAL handles verifications and reports generated for this meter. The FMP Number, Lease Number, CA Number, and FMP Tier fields are displayed on select reports designed specifically for BLM reporting requirements.

You can use the FcLoader utility to import the following values in bulk:

  • BLM Property
  • FMP Number
  • Lease Number
  • CA Number
  • PA Number
  • FMP Tier

Data Field Details

The following items are available on the BLM tab: - **BLM Property** - When set to "Yes", the asset is designated a BLM property. This option must be set to "Yes" for other options on this tab to be enabled. - **FMP Number** - A BLM-approved facility measurement point (FMP) where oil or gas produced from a Federal or Native American lease, unit PA or CA is measured, and the measurement affects the calculation of the volume or quality of production on which royalty is owed (required field if BLM Property is set to "Yes"). - **Lease Number** - The number assigned to the lease location where the production occurs. - **CA Number** - Communitization agreement (CA) number identifying an agreement to combine a lease or a portion of a lease with other tracts for purposes of cooperative development and operations, when the initial lease cannot be independently developed and operated in accordance with established well spacing or well development programs. - **PA Number** - Participating area (PA) number representing a combined portion of the unitized area that BLM determines to be reasonably proven to produce geothermal resources or that supports production in commercial quantities, such as pressure support from injection wells; the size and configuration of all participating areas and revisions are not effective until BLM approves them. The BLM tab for liquids will only contain fields for BLM Property, FMP Number, Lease Number, CA Number and PA Number - **FMP Tier** - A volume rate designation for the meter; higher volume rates have more stringent operating requirements. In FLOWCAL, this value determines the limits for [heating value uncertainty](../../BLM/Heating%20Value%20Uncertainty%20Details.md) and C6+ characterization age. Tier designations for gas meters are as follows: - **Very High Volume:** \> 1,000 Mcf/day (default) - **High Volume:** \> 200 and ≤ 1000 Mcf/day - **Low Volume:** \>35 and ≤ 200 Mcf/day - **Very Low Volume:** ≤ 35 Mcf/day FMP Tier dictates how validations are triggered; meters are defaulted to "Very High Volume" as this is the most stringent designation and will require the most attention from the producer, therefore ensuring compliance. - **AO Tier Variance on File** - This indicates that the BLM Area Office (AO) has issued a variance letter setting the Tier designation of this FMP to a specific level despite the calculated level. It is manually maintained. When set to Yes, the FMP Tier field may be manually set and the calculated level will not update it. - **Calculated Tier** - The volume rate designation as calculated by FLOWCAL. If "AO Tier Variance" is No, this calculated tier will be copied to the the FMP Tier field. If "AO Tier Variance" is Yes, this calculated tier will not be copied to the FMP Tier field. - **Daily Avg. Volume** - The daily average volume calculated by FLOWCAL and used to determine the Calculated Tier value. (See: [FMP Tier Calculation](../../BLM/FMP%20Tier%20Calculation.md)) - **Calculation Date** - The date and time that FLOWCAL performed the most recent tier calculation. - **Calculation Result** - A short message describing the success or failure of the most recent tier calculation. Available messages are: - Success - FMP tier not calculated (database error occurred accessing meter) - FMP tier not calculated (meter has no first flow date) - FMP tier not calculated (meter has insufficient flow data) - Unknown error in FMP tier calculation - FMP tier updated by calculation All messages except "Success" correspond to [meter messages 801 through 805](../../Messages/Meter%20Messages/Meter%20800.md), respectively.

docs.title: Calculations Tab
docs.text:
The Calculations tab displays the meter characteristics as read-only. These fields are datetime effective and can be edited within the Volume Editor. The current or most recent values are displayed for all fields.

General Sub-Tab

The following items are available on this sub-tab: - **Pressure Base, Temperature Base, Heating Value Base Condition, Calculation Method and Z Method** - Read-only, datetime effective fields retrieved from the meter’s characteristics. These data points are initially configured during setup or are updated during meter import; they can be edited within the Volume Editor. - **Heating Value Base Condition** - Read-only, datetime effective field retrieved from the meter’s analysis. This is initially configured during setup or updated during a meter import; it can be edited within the Volume Editor. - **Ignore Bogus Pulses** - Setting this field to “Yes” has the following implications: - It is assumed that the data for this kind of meter uses the AGA-7 calculation. - The data set may be incomplete or invalid, preventing FLOWCAL from performing a full recalculation of volume and energy. Example Invalid data set: Pulses = 0, Volume = 5 Pulses = 5, Volume = 0 Incomplete data set: K-factor is missing - When the user edits and/or manipulates this kind of data set, FLOWCAL will only re-calculate energy if possible and/or applicable. - Some validation checks are bypassed to prevent an overwhelming number of exceptions. Example If the volume is zero, but pulses are non-zero, exception 1043 (CV - Pulses \> 0 but no volume) would normally be generated. However, by setting the Ignore Bogus Pulses option to "Yes", the exception will not be generated. This flag is automatically set to "Yes" if the import driver is Mercury1 or Mercury2. - **Create PPAs** - These meter-level options determine which methods can be used to generate prior period adjustments through edits performed on closed data sets from a source other than manual edits within the Volume Editor. These options work in conjunction with the PPA options on the [System Configuration Approvals tab](../../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration%20-%20Approvals%20Tab.md). - When PPA options are set to “Apply Immediate”, the Allow Auto PPAs option must be checked to enable the use of the Create PPAs option in the Meter Editor. - When PPA options are set to “Approval Required”, the Allow Auto PPAs option is automatically set to "Yes" and the Create PPAs option in the Meter Editor must be checked to allow PPAs to be created for the meter.

Quality Sub-Tab

This sub-tab contains configuration options for the Relative Density, Heating Value, Mass Heating Value, Mole %, Mass % and GPMs fields. Configuration options are: - **No Action** - Null values or imported data will remain as-is. - **Fill In** - Null values will be populated with FLOWCAL-calculated values based on the analysis sample. Previously calculated values that were propagated from the prior meter analysis record will be replaced with FLOWCAL-calculated values based on the current analysis sample. - **Replace** - Imported values will be replaced with FLOWCAL-calculated values based on the analysis sample. The C6+ and C7+ splits are used when performing hydrocarbon calculations such as density, heating value, mass heating value and others based on the analysis sample. These options only apply when importing and editing data.

docs.title: Meter Editor
Create & Delete Meters
docs.text:
To create a meter from the Meter Editor: 1. Open the Meter Editor, and click the **New** button or go to **Meter** \> **New** from the Meter Editor menu. Click the arrow next to the **New** button to select a fluid phase; otherwise, the new meter will use the default fluid phase specified in the User Preferences screen. Once the new meter has been saved, the fluid phase cannot be changed. The liquid fluid phase is only available if you have the **FLOWCAL Liquids** module. 2. Populate required data fields (highlighted in green). These fields must be populated before you can save the meter record. By default, the only required field to save a new gas meter is Meter Number. For liquid meters, Operation Type is also required, which is defaulted to "Batch". Additional fields may be required based on how FLOWCAL options are configured. Your new meter may have required Meter Characteristics data fields. You will be able to create and save the new meter without populating those fields; however, when you edit the Meter Characteristics under the Volume Editor screen, you will need to populate the remaining required fields before you can save your changes. 3. Enter any additional meter information and click **Save**. The Meter Number field can contain up to 16 characters. The Meter Name field can contain up to 60 characters.

Copy a Meter

You can also create a meter by making a copy of an existing meter. Users will often create a set of default meters to use as the basis for new meters, so that meter properties, such as close group, custom field values and validation ranges, are automatically specified in the new meter. To copy a meter from the Meter Editor: 1. Open the Meter Editor, and select a meter to copy using the Meter drop-down. 2. Click the **Copy** button, or select **Meter** \> **Copy** from the Meter Editor menu. 3. Enter a new meter number and name. 4. Make any required edits and click **Save**.

Delete a Meter

Meters can only be deleted from the Meter Editor. Deleting a meter requires the **Meter Edit - Can Delete** privilege. To delete a meter: 1. Open the Meter Editor, and select a meter to delete using the Meter drop-down. 2. Click the **Delete** button, or select **Meter** \> **Delete** from the Meter Editor menu. 3. When prompted, confirm the deletion. When a meter is deleted, FLOWCAL will generate a message logging the deletion (available in the [Message Viewer](../../Messages/Message%20Viewer.md)).

docs.title: Custom Fields Tab

The Custom Fields tab has 80 user-definable fields, 20 of which are datetime effective. They can be used to accommodate company-specific meter information, such as division or field technician. All of the labels are user-defined and the data format can be converted to drop-downs with defined lists of options.

Custom field labels and drop-down options are managed from the Custom Fields screen within the Settings Manager.

You will need the FLOWCAL Options privilege to customize data fields.

docs.title: Date and Time Adjustments During Import
docs.text:
FLOWCAL’s standard import drivers can apply three types of adjustments to datetimes contained in meter and ticket data import files:

  • Convert time trails data to time leads prior to import
  • Adjust for Daylight Saving Time prior to import
  • Adjust by the offset defined for the meter or location time zone prior to import

Time Trails to Time Leads (TT→TL) Conversion

When Time Leads Shift is enabled, meter import records with time trails data spans are converted to and then imported as time leads records. - The Time Leads Shift option applies only to gas meters. - As liquid meters can only have record span of Time Leads in FLOWCAL, TT→TL conversion upon import happens for liquid meters when needed regardless of any option. - Ticket data is not designated as time trails or leads; therefore, this adjustment is not applicable to ticket data. - Among data points that represent datetime, TT→TL adjustments are applicable only to those data points that represent a span of time, not a point in time. - In a CFX file, two Meter Configuration section fields are used to determine whether to do a TT→TL adjustment. - If the Time Span value is T (time trails), timestamps of History records are adjusted. - If the Alternate Time Span value is T (time trails), timestamps of Alternate Periodic Values records are adjusted. The following factors are considered when calculating the effective date of the converted time leads record (not in order): - Beginning of the periodic defined by record resolution, contract day, and contract hour - Duration, if specified for the import record - End effective date of preceding record in the current import file - Start and end effective dates of any existing data in the same periodic

Daylight Savings Time (DST) Adjustment

When the DST shift is enabled, all dates and times that occur during Daylight Saving Time will be shifted forward an hour. All time stamps outside of DST will be imported as-is. ### Standard Time to Daylight Saving Time (Spring Forward) Adjustment If import records are time trails, import records with timestamps of 2:00:00 AM or earlier of the start date of DST are imported as-is. The import records with timestamps later than 2:00:00 AM of the start date of DST are imported with one hour added. | In Import File (Before Shift) | In Database (After Shift) | |-------------------------------|---------------------------| | 3/14/2021 1:30:00 | 3/14/2021 1:30:00 | | 3/14/2021 1:59:59 | 3/14/2021 1:59:59 | | 3/14/2021 2:00:00 | 3/14/2021 2:00:00 | | 3/14/2021 2:00:01 | 3/14/2021 3:00:01 | | 3/14/2021 2:30:00 | 3/14/2021 3:30:00 | | 3/14/2021 3:00:00 | 3/14/2021 4:00:00 | If import records are time leads, import records with timestamps earlier than 2:00:00 AM of the start date of DST are imported as is. The import records with timestamps of 2:00:00 AM or later of the start date of DST are imported with one hour added. | In Import File (Before Shift) | In Database (After Shift) | |-------------------------------|---------------------------| | 3/14/2021 1:30:00 | 3/14/2021 1:30:00 | | 3/14/2021 1:59:59 | 3/14/2021 1:59:59 | | 3/14/2021 2:00:00 | 3/14/2021 3:00:00 | | 3/14/2021 2:00:01 | 3/14/2021 3:00:01 | | 3/14/2021 2:30:00 | 3/14/2021 3:30:00 | | 3/14/2021 3:00:00 | 3/14/2021 4:00:00 | ### Daylight Saving Time to Standard Time (Fall Back) Adjustment This adjustment will continue until 1:00:00 AM on the end date of DST. If import records are time trails, the import records with timestamps later 1:00:00 AM on the end date of DST are imported as-is. | In Import File (Before Shift) | In Database (After Shift) | |-------------------------------|---------------------------| | 11/7/21 0:30:00 | 11/7/21 1:30:00 | | 11/7/21 0:59:59 | 11/7/21 1:59:59 | | 11/7/21 1:00:00 | **11/7/21 2:00:00** | | 11/7/21 1:00:01 | 11/7/21 1:00:01 | | 11/7/21 2:00:00 | 11/7/21 2:00:00 | If the import records are time leads, the import records are imported as-is, starting with 1:00:00 AM on the end date of DST. | In Import File (Before Shift) | In Database (After Shift) | |-------------------------------|---------------------------| | 11/7/21 0:30:00 | 11/7/21 1:30:00 | | 11/7/21 0:59:59 | 11/7/21 1:59:59 | | 11/7/21 1:00:00 | 11/7/21 1:00:00 | | 11/7/21 1:00:01 | 11/7/21 1:00:01 | | 11/7/21 2:00:00 | 11/7/21 2:00:00 |

Business Time Zone (BTZ) Adjustment

When Time Zone Shift is enabled, all dates and times will be adjusted by the offset amount defined for the selected time zone. For example, if Central Standard Time (CST) has an offset of +1, a CFX record with a date and time of 1/1/2017 12:00:00 will be imported into a meter in the CST time zone as 1/1/2017 13:00:00.

Enable Adjustments

To enable these options, set each item to "Yes". These options are disabled by default. - **Meter Data** - For meter data, the options can be enabled at the meter level through the Meter Editor Imports tab. - **Ticket Data** - For ticket data, the options can be enabled at the location level (tank, cavern, or location) through the corresponding editor for the tickets belonging directly to the locations to be adjusted and imported.

Order of Adjustments

Adjustment types may be combined. When combined, adjustments are processed in the following order: 1. BTZ 2. DST 3. TT→TL

Import File Formats

The following table lists the file formats supported for each type of adjustment along with associated data points. docs.text:

On this tab, you can control the severity settings of designated flowing parameter validations. You can also disable an exception by setting the severity to zero.

Meter message 313 "Exception severity changed" is generated when a severity is changed on this tab. If a contact type is set at the application level, that setting is reflected in the Contact Type column.

docs.title: General Tab
docs.text:
The General tab in the Meter Editor shows basic information about the meter, such as where it is located and what Close Group it belongs to. The fields that are shaded in gray such as Meter Type and Meter Direction are read-only and are retrieved from the meter’s characteristics. These read-only fields are editable in the Volume Editor.

By default, the only fields required to save a new meter are Meter Number and Fluid Phase, and for liquid meters, Operation Type, which is defaulted to Batch.

Data Field Details

The following items are available on the General tab: - **Meter Type** - Read-only field that displays the type of meter. This value is retrieved from the meter’s characteristics and can be edited from the Volume Editor or updated during a meter import. - **Alt. Meter Number** - Informational field used to document an alternate meter number. This typically references a third party or contract meter number. - **Meter Direction** - Read-only field that displays whether a meter is classified as Inlet, Outlet, Throughput, Balance Check, Transfer, Tieover, or Off System for balancing purposes. This value is retrieved from the meter’s characteristics and can be edited from the Volume Editor. - **Customer** - The customer the meter belongs to. This name can be printed on reports if enabled under the **[**Reports** tab](Reports%20Tab.md)**. - **Cust. Meter Number** - Informational field used to document the customer's meter number. - **Check Meter Exists** - Specifies whether an existing check meter is associated to the meter; commonly used if data from another meter is being measured at the same measurement point. - **Helium Meter**\* - Designates whether a meter is a helium meter. If "Yes" is selected, FLOWCAL will calculate the following: - Total net helium - Gross 50% to 65% helium - Net 50% to 65% helium - Gross less than 50% helium - Net less than 50% helium These calculation results will be stored in user-defined fields 1 through 5 for meter periodic records. The Meter Rollups service will always sum user-defined fields 1 through 5 in the meter periodic values, regardless of the rollup action configured for those fields (**Settings Manager** \> **Custom Fields** \> **Meter Periodic Values** tab). - **Account for DST**\* - Indicates whether to compensate for Daylight Saving Time. If "Yes" is selected, the DST time change table is used to establish when to adjust for time changes to avoid generating missing data exceptions and duplicate data and/or high periodic flow time exceptions. - **Close Groups** - Only visible if the close schedule type is set to "Close Group" in the FLOWCAL Configuration screen. - **Fluid Phase** - Defines the meter phase conditions as gas or liquid; the fluid phase is defined on meter creation and cannot be changed once the meter is created. - **Meter Status** - Indicates whether the meter is active; pulled from meter’s characteristics and applicable to the current system time (all other meter characteristic values displayed on other tabs are applicable to the last meter periodic record). - **Fluid Service** - Defines the meter fluid service as "Hydrocarbon" (default) or "Nonhydrocarbon" for liquid meters. The fluid service is specified when creating a new liquid meter and cannot be changed once the meter is created. - **Business Status** - The current or proposed meter status that can be influenced by test reports from TESTit. This status is not datetime effective and can be updated manually via the Meter Editor or, when mapped, TESTit imports. This status overrides the Meter Status. Meters that have a business status other than "On" are treated as out of service and will not import data or be included when running reports for a list. - **System** - Informational field that indicates which system the meter is assigned to, typically set during meter creation. - **Notes** - Additional notes about the meter; up to 320 characters. The notes stored on the General tab are only available from the Meter Editor. Right-click the Meter Editor screen to add or view notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Volume Editor). If additional notes are needed, click the **Notes** button in the right side of the form for an additional 2,000 characters. - **City** - City the meter is in; up to 50 characters. - **County** - County the meter is in; up to 20 characters; options are defined in the County Editor. - **State** - State the meter is in; up to 50 characters; options are defined in the State Editor. - **Country** - Country the meter is in; up to 50 characters; options are defined in the Country Editor. - **Time Zone** - Time zone the meter is in; up to 80 characters; options are defined in the Time Zone Editor. When a time zone is selected for a meter and the Time Zone Shift in enabled on the Imports tab, dates contained in the import data will be adjusted according to the offset associated to the time zone. - **Quarter** - Each section is divided into quarter sections, which are each further divided into quarter sections, for a total of 16 parts per section; up to 25 characters. Example "NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4" refers to the northwestern-most quarter of the southeastern quarter. - **Section** - The basic unit of a township and range; each section refers to an area of a square mile; up to three characters. - **Township** - A measure of the distance north or south from the baseline, six miles in length; up to four characters. - **Range** - A measure of the distance east or west from the principal meridian, six miles in length; up to four characters. - **Meridian** - A geographical north to south reference point; up to 25 characters. - **Latitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying a north-south location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Equator; up to 12 characters. - **Longitude** - A geographic coordinate specifying an east-west location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Prime Meridian; up to 12 characters. **\***Not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.
