docs.title: Imports Tab
docs.text:
This tab is not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.

The Imports tab contains information about how data should be imported for meters. Setting these options helps streamline the meter import process. For instance, you can specify an import driver and import path (file and folder name) so that you do not have to enter it every time you import meter data. You can also assign auto edits based on known routine occurrences for a meter; FLOWCAL will then make these adjustments automatically.

Import Options

- **Compare to Master Characteristics** - When set to "Yes", FLOWCAL will verify if the meter’s characteristics matches the master characteristics. If the master characteristics are different from the meter characteristics, an exception will generate. Exceptions and updates of master characteristics are managed within the Master Data Validation screen. - **External Volume** - An external volume meter is usually a meter whose “official measurement” or custody volume is managed by a third party outside of FLOWCAL; data corrections or edits are not expected to take place in the application. Examples of external volumes are chart volumes and third-party measured volumes. Data for external volume meters can be imported via normal imports such as CFX files, text files, or Transaction Queue processing, or entered manually. Defining a meter as an external volume meter makes the meter available for selection within the External Volume interface. - **Update Meter Name**\* - When set to "Yes" (default), the meter name is updated on import with the meter name from the field. Set this option to "No" to prevent the meter name from being updated on import. - **Inhibit Default Exceptions** - When set to "Yes", FLOWCAL will not generate default exceptions. User-configured validations will still generate exceptions. - **Sync Operational to Contractual** - When set to "Yes", FLOWCAL will update the meter with the contractual limits that have been set on the Master Data Validations screen. This is for items such as calibrations, tests, and samples that are set to standard operating procedures and/or government requirements. - **Ignore Contract Hour**\* - When set to "Yes", the contract hour will not be updated on file import or through Transaction Queue. - **PFX Recalc Method** - Recalculation method used on PFX imports. Choose between the standard liquid recalc methods or select “None. Import Prove PDF Only”. The “None. Import Prove PDF Only” option is used by companies who are retroactively recalculating volume and mass in the flow computer and do not want FLOWCAL to calculate a new volume and mass on top of the new one calculated by the flow computer. Only the import of the PDF is performed. This feature is only available with the Liquids add-on and requires PROVEit. - **Flow Computer Product Mapping** - When set to "Yes", the Flow Computer Editor is enabled. The Flow Computer Editor is used when a SCADA system knows which product position is being used for calculations, but not the product name or product code. For example: the SCADA system may be able to tell that the batch flowing is for product position 2, but it does not know what the product is. SCADA will report this position as the product name in the CFX file, rather than a FLOWCAL product code. You can then use the Flow Computer Editor to update the products when the products in the field flow computer are modified. This feature is only available with the Liquids add-on. - **Auto Edit Criteria** - An auto edit (see: [Auto Edits Editor](../../Auto%20Edits/Auto%20Edits%20Editor.md)) can be assigned to the meter to address routine occurrences for that meter. FLOWCAL will automatically make these adjustments on imports or edits. Check the "Apply on Import Only" checkbox to apply the auto edits only when the data is imported. - **Import ID** - The meter number in the system sending data to FLOWCAL may not match the meter number in FLOWCAL. In this case, defining an Import ID will ensure the data is imported to the appropriate meter. When using the Import ID for text file or Transaction Queue imports, the option to use Import ID must be enabled on the Service Configuration screen. When importing MBS## files, there is a requirement that the meter name in FLOWCAL match that in the MBS## file. To use a different meter name in FLOWCAL, set the meter name of the meter in the MBS## file in the Import ID field. The use of Import ID is supported by text file, Transaction Queue, and Flow Automation MBS## file imports. See: [Configure Imports](../../Admin%20Options/Configure%20Imports.md) - **Proving Import ID** - The meter number in the PROVEit PFX file being imported may not match the meter number in FLOWCAL. In this case, defining a Proving Import ID will ensure the data is imported to the appropriate meter. This feature is only available with the Liquids add-on. - **Periodic Snap/Batch Snap** - These fields are used to snap incoming data to the start of the resolution period (such as the top of the hour for hourly resolution). If a time stamp falls within the range specified, the time stamp will snap to the top of the hour. If multiple records meet time frame criteria, the first record will be flagged at the top of the hour, and the next record will be flagged for one second after (or one second before for time trails data). The adjustment of the time stamp occurs during import, without a revision being created. The total of the time before the start of the hour and after the end of the hour cannot exceed the number of seconds specified for data resolution in the meter characteristics (3600 for hourly data, 900 for 15-minute data). - **Time Zone Shift**\* – Applies only to gas and liquid CFX and text file imports, as well as liquid TFX files. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md)) - **DST Shift**\* – Applies only to gas and liquid CFX and text file imports, as well as liquid TFX files. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md)) - **Time Leads Shift**\* – Applies only to gas CFX and text file imports (not supported for monthly data resolution). (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md)) \* These options are not supported by Transaction Queue.

Pressure/Temperature Source

If a meter does not have associated pressure or temperature, you can use the Pressure/Temperature Source options to assign a source meter to provide its pressure or temperature for calculation purposes. The pressure and/or temperature must be available on the source meter for it to apply to the destination meter during import. If the data for the source meter is imported after that of the destination meter, the pressure and/or temperature from the source will not be applied.

File Options

- **Driver** - Import driver selection based on the type of file expected during imports. If the driver is not installed, select the button to install the appropriate driver from the Import Driver Editor. Most users import CFX files and select the STNDCFX driver. - **Import Path (Folder)** - Select the import directory or copy/paste the file path from Windows Explorer. Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit. - **Subfolder or Filename** - Select a subfolder or file name for importing CFX files. - Select a subfolder if you are importing CFX files with a datetime stamped file name, as the import file name will be different for every import. - Select a file name if you are importing CFX files with a meter ID as the file name, as the import file name will remain constant. - **Import CFX Units** - When set to "Yes", units specified in the CFX file will be imported. - **Ignore Configuration Snapshots** - By default, meter configurations specified in a CFX file are imported. CFX meter configurations are automatically associated with the latest flow data record included in the file. At times, the configuration data provided is not in sync with the periodic data and should be ignored. When this option is set to "Yes": - Import of meter configuration snapshots will be prevented, including analysis. - Meter characteristic records in the Volume Editor need to be updated manually or via events from the flow computer. - Meter analysis records in the Volume Editor need to be updated manually, via events from the flow computer, or from analysis provided as part of the History record. - **Create Revisions** - By default, data imported from CFX will not overwrite existing data. When this option is enabled, if differences are found between the time stamp, differential pressure, pulses, pressure, temperature, volume, or energy values, the data will be imported as a new revision (for closed data, a prior period adjustment will be created). If the data being imported is the same as the existing data, the import will be ignored. This is commonly used to track revisions of third-party data that is not being edited locally and does not have source analysis being applied via a source assignment. Applying analysis to recalculate the imported volume and energy must be done after all imports for the time frame are complete; subsequent imports will not recalculate based on the quality source data. - This field is available for gas meters only. - **Import Alternate Periodics** - By default, alternate periodic information is not imported. Alternate periodic information is generally flow data represented at another resolution. For example, CFX typically will import hourly periodic data. Daily periodic data from the EFM could be provided via the alternate periodic section of CFX. Alternate periodics are stored but not validated or used in any way. Setting this option to "Yes" enables the import of alternate periodic records from CFX imports and allows this data to display in the Volume Editor.

Conditional Import Rules

Conditional import rules are available to allow rejection of data that does not meet specific criteria, such as temperature that is out of range. That hour's record is discarded, but additional records that import with the flagged record are kept. Conditional import rules are supported for all files types; however, they are not supported for Transaction Queue imports.

docs.title: Integration Tab
docs.text:
The Integration tab contains data points required for linking a meter with the Quorum ecosystem via the Quorum Enterprise Integration (QEI) platform.

You can use the FcLoader utility to import the following values in bulk:

  • Integrated
  • Facility (code)
  • Integration ID

Data Field Details

- **Integrated** - When set to "Yes", the meter is designated as being integrated or linked to the Quorum ecosystem. Data is expected to flow from FLOWCAL automatically and transparently to other Quorum integrated applications. An example of this integration is data flowing from FLOWCAL to TIPS. When set to "Yes", the following data will be automatically sent to the Integration Platform when data changes due to imports or edits: - Meter Header/Configuration - Volumes (Hourly, Daily, Monthly) - Analysis (Hourly, Daily, Monthly) The following Meter Editor data points must be populated before an Integrated meter can be saved: - Facility - Integration ID - State - County This option must be set to "Yes" for other options on this tab to be enabled. - **Facility** – Allows the user to select a facility from the list of facilities designated as Integrated. This data point is necessary to properly identify a meter across the Quorum ecosystem. - **Integration ID** – Allows the user to enter a unique ID that is necessary to properly identify a meter across the Quorum ecosystem. - Must be a unique value among all other existing Integration IDs - Maximum length is 10 characters

docs.title: Liquids Tab
docs.text:
The Liquids tab contains general setup information for liquid meters.

This feature is only available with the FLOWCAL Liquids module.

Setup Sub-Tab

Use this tab to specify products that should flow on a meter, the tolerance window at the end of a batch for finding a matching sample, and other options specific to liquid meters. Batch Options - **Operation Type**\* - **Batch** - Default option for liquid meters. When operating in this mode, a meter allows for input of both batch and periodic data. When batch data is entered or imported, the flow data is broken down and distributed to each of the periodic records that fall within its duration. When periodic data is provided, the values of a record are aggregated with the other periodic records that fall within a batch to determine the batch total. - **Run Ticket** - For meters with intermittent flow such as truck or rail car loading or unloading. When operating in this mode, flow data may only be entered under the periodic tab in the Volume Editor. All records created in this manner are restricted to one second in duration. Records may be created under the Batch tab, but only the start and end dates may be specified; these records behave purely as a container for the underlying periodic records. Run Ticket essentially allows users to enter meter data that imitates tickets. - **Create Batch on New Analysis** - This option enables automatically creates a new batch upon a new analysis being manually created or imported to this meter. - **Create Batch on Off Hour Record** - This option splits a batch if a periodic record is imported with an effective date that does not fall at the meter’s specified data resolution as defined in the meter characteristics in the Volume Editor. For instance, if a meter is set up with daily data resolution and it has a contract hour of seven, any record that comes in with a time that is not at 07:00:00 would cause a batch split. If a meter is set up with hourly data resolution, any record that comes in with a time not at the top of the hour would cause a batch split. - **Reconcile Batches**\* - Enables the Batch Movement Reconciliation functionality. When enabled, meter batches must be scheduled (See Batch Movement Reconciliation). As the actual batches import, if they cannot be matched to a scheduled batch, exceptions will be generated to alert the user to this. **\*** Not available for dead oil meters. Sample Tolerances **Before/After End of Batch** - When a Liquid Quality Source Assignment is created using the option to apply samples at the end of a batch, the default behavior is such that a sample can only be applied to a batch if its sample date falls on the exact second that the batch ends. The Sample Tolerance settings allow a user to specify a window around the end of a batch for which a sample will be considered applicable. The maximum for both Before and End of Batch options is 365 days. If multiple samples are within the window, the last one is used. If no window is given, then a sample would only be applied to a batch if one of the following is true: - The assignment is set up to use effective date and time and a sample with a corresponding sample date exists. - The assignment is end of batch and the batch’s end date and time matches the sample’s date and time. - The assignment is end of batch and the Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option is checked. An option to use the first sample found is available in the [Quality Assignment Editor](../../Source%20Analysis/Quality%20Assignment%20Editor/Configuring%20Assignments.md) screen. Import Options This group of options is not available for dead oil meters. - **Apply Last Edited/Imported MF to the Batch** - When a new meter factor is imported or edited, FLOWCAL splits the meter characteristic record and applies the new meter factor at the effective date of the history record or the event and uses the new meter factor from that point forward. It may be desirable to have FLOWCAL apply the value back to the start of the batch. Checking this option causes FLOWCAL to update the meter factor back to the start of the current batch with the new value. Volume, mass, component volume and component mass values are recalculated for the time period the meter factor is applied to. New revisions for the meter characteristics record, the periodic data and the batch are created. An edit reason of “New MF Applied to Start of Batch” is created as well. If unchecked, then the meter factor at the date of the change is used. - **Apply Last Edited/Imported DMF to the Batch** - This option is the same as the Apply Last Edited/Imported MF to the Batch option, except it is applicable to the DMF. - **Recalc Method** - Determines the recalculation method to use when applying import options. FLOWCAL does not apply a MF or DMF of 0 as it does not consider a MF or DMF of 0 to be a valid value to apply to the batch. If the last edited or imported MF or DMF is 0, then FLOWCAL looks to the prior MF or DMF within the batch and applies that value to the whole batch. The MF and DMF are considered separately during the apply process. Validate Products - **Validate Products -** When the option to Validate Products is selected, the product drop-down in the Volume Editor will show only the products specified on this tab; no other products may be selected. On import, if a product not in the list of valid products is imported, an exception will be generated. - **Add/Edit Product** - Add or edit a product. Clicking the Add or Edit Product buttons will open the Configure Product screen. The base density and base density unit are automatically populated by the values specified in the Product Editor if available, but with the exception of products assigned a table type that has a fixed base density, these values can be edited. If the Always Use Base Conditions as Observed option is checked, the base density specified for the product in the Validate Products section of the Meter Editor and the base temperature specified in the Product Editor will replace the observed density and temperature of a record on import. Unit conversion between the density from the units specified in the Meter Editor and the units found in meter characteristics will be done. The Sample Required checkbox enables a validation when a liquid source is assigned to a meter that requires each record on that meter to be associated with a sample analysis. If a record does not have a sample applied to it, an exception will be generated. - **Remove Product** - Remove a product. Once removed, unless the Validate Products checkbox is unchecked, the product will no longer appear on the Product drop-down of the Volume Editor for the meter. Any records that have already been saved with that product will retain their product information; however, and an edit made to these records will generate an exception. Likewise, if a file is imported with invalid products, the records will still be saved, but an exception will be generated. - **Set as Default** - The selected product will become the meter's default product. When a new batch record is created, this product will automatically be selected, if there is not already a product on the record. The product can be changed to any other valid product specified for the meter, so this is a matter of convenience. A default product will not populate when entering edit mode from the Periodic tab for both Flow Data and Characteristic records.

Schedules Sub-Tab

Batch schedules can be assigned to a meter to automatically create batches for liquid meters that deliver batches on a known schedule, with known products. You can assign a different batch schedule for a meter on a month-by-month basis if the product flow or the day of the month that the batch starts on changes. The use of a batch schedule can be helpful if batches are to be hand-keyed into the system, or if the import file doesn’t contain the batch start and stop or the batch product information. When batches are created from a schedule, each batch starts and ends at the contract hour set in meter characteristics on the day specified in the schedule. Monthly batch schedules are created from the [Batch Schedule Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Liquids/Batch%20Schedule%20Editor.md) and annual schedules are created from the [Annual Schedule Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md). For FLOWCAL to create batches based on a batch schedule, the service FcBatchScheduler.exe must be installed and running. If the service FcBatchScheduler.exe runs, but cannot create batches on a meter because it is locked by another process such as meter rollups or a user performing edits, no messages will be generated. FcBatchScheduler should be run during off hours to minimize the chances of this happening and to minimize database access during peak hours. Monthly Schedule To select a monthly schedule: 1. Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**. 2. Select the Monthly Schedule option and click on the button to the right. The Batch Schedule Select screen will display. 3. Select the schedule from the drop-down and click **Select**. 4. Click **Save**. To delete a monthly schedule: 1. Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**. 2. Click the button with the red circle and minus sign in the Regular Schedule section. 3. Click **Save**. Annual Schedule To select an annual schedule: 1. Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**. 2. Select the Annual Schedule option and click on the button to the right of the Monthly Schedule label. The Annual Schedule Editor screen will display. 3. Choose the schedule from the drop-down and click **Apply**. 4. Click **Save**. To delete an annual schedule: 1. Within the Meter Editor, select a meter and click **Edit**. 2. Click the button with the red circle and minus sign in the Regular Schedule section. 3. Click **Save**. Unlike a monthly batch schedule, no product is defined for an annual batch schedule. The product must be set up in the Meter Characteristics screen or provided in the import file. When batches are created from a schedule, each batch starts and ends at the contract hour set in Meter Characteristics on the day specified in the schedule. Overrides If there is a month that should use a different schedule, a separate schedule can be set. To override a month: 1. Click the expansion button in the Overrides section of the Liquids tab. A month/year selector and Template option will display. 2. Select the month and year to override the regular schedule with. 3. Click the button next to the Template edit box. The Batch Schedule Select screen will appear. 4. Choose the schedule name from the drop-down and click **Select**. The selected schedule will now display in the Template field. 5. Click on the expansion button in the Overrides section again. The schedule will be added to the list of Overrides. 6. Click **Save**. If an override is selected for a month that has started, it will not be used to create any batches.

Facilities Sub-Tab

Use the Facilities tab to define valid facilities for a meter. Facilities can be assigned to batches in the Volume Editor. This can be useful information for downstream accounting systems to be able to match batches to contracts. A facility may not be assigned to a batch in the Volume Editor if it has not first been added as a valid facility in this section of the Meter Editor. Facilities are created in the Facility Editor within Settings Manager. Each facility can be set up as a From Facility, a To Facility or both a From Facility and a To Facility to indicate where product is flowing.

docs.title: Live Oil Info
docs.text:
This feature requires the Liquids System module and Live Oil Management add-on. The Live Oil Service (FlowCal.LiveOil.Service.exe) must be installed as well.

Live Oil Management allows users to set up meters to hold low vapor pressure (“dead”) oil quantities and associated flash gas volumes. These holding meters receive periodic flow data calculated by applying user-provided shrink and flash gas factors to the production volume of a related high vapor pressure (“live”) oil meter. The holding meters are otherwise independent and operate like typical meters: They can have analyses applied for component calculations, they can be included in balances, they can be closed and receive PPAs, and they have their own validations.

In practice, a crude oil liquid meter is designated as a live oil meter, and child meters for dead oil and flash gas are created directly from this meter (Meter Editor > Tools > Live Oil Info).

Dead oil and flash gas meters receive data from the parent live oil meter:

Dead oil NSV = live oil theoretical production * units correction

Flash gas volume = live oil theoretical production * flash gas factor * units correction * pb correction

Data is transferred from live oil to dead oil and flash gas meters using the installed Live Oil service (FlowCal.LiveOil.Service.exe). This service is available on the Service Queues and Service Configuration forms. (See: Live Oil Service)

Shrink factor, flash gas factor, and stock tank density are fully implemented and can be imported into sources and applied to meters or imported into liquid meters directly.

Default validations are available for flash gas and shrink factors. Shrink factors, if provided, must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to 1. Flash gas factors, if provided, must be greater than or equal to 0. In addition, if Live Oil Management is authorized, then exceptions will be generated if either the shrink factor or flash gas factor is missing.

A theoretical production calculation method is also available to allow users to choose between the standard API 20.1 application of shrink factor and the direct application of the shrink factor to NSV.

To access the Live Oil Management form: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Editor**. 2. Click the **Tools** menu option. 3. Select any liquid meter or a flash gas meter. 4. Select **Live Oil Management**. The **Liquid System** module and **Live Oil Management** add-on must be authorized to enable the Live Oil Management form. The Live Oil Management form is not available when the Meter Editor is in New or Edit mode.

Screen Details

- **Live Oil** - When the checkbox is selected, the liquid meter is designated as a live oil parent meter. This option must be selected for all other options on this tab to be enabled. - **Stabilized Oil** – If this checkbox is not selected, the shrink factor and flash gas factor must be assigned a value for the calculation of dead oil and flash gas meter volumes. - **Live Oil (Parent)** – This group box contains the meter number, meter name, and system for any meter that is designated as a live oil meter. These fields will be read-only and will be auto-populated with the live oil meter information. - **Dead Oil (Child)** – Use this group box to create a dead oil meter and link it to a parent live oil meter. To create a dead oil meter: 1. Click the **Edit** button at the bottom of the Live Oil Management screen. 2. Enter a system, meter number, and meter name for the dead oil meter. 3. If the dead oil and live oil meter relationship is active, select the "Active" checkbox. This checkbox selection is not datetime effective. A dead oil meter can only be assigned to one live oil meter. - **Flash Gas (Child)** – Use this group box to create a flash gas meter and link it to a parent live oil meter. To create a Flash Gas meter: 1. Click the **Edit** button at the bottom of the Live Oil Management screen. 2. Enter a system, meter number, and meter name for the flash gas meter. 3. If the flash gas and live oil meter relationship is active, select the "Active" checkbox. This checkbox selection is not datetime effective. The **Gas System** module must be authorized to create flash gas meters. A flash gas meter can only be assigned to one live oil meter.

docs.title: Meter Editor
docs.text:
Accessing the Meter Editor requires System Process – Meter Edit – Can View privileges. For additional details about Meter Editor access, see: Meter Editor Access Privileges. The Meter Editor contains much more detailed meter information than the Meter Quick Create screen.

Use the Meter Editor to create, edit, or delete a meter. You can also set the meter fluid phase, identify the import file location and set up reporting, validations, and other service functions.

The Meter Editor also includes 80 user-definable fields that can be free form entry or drop-down to accommodate data points not built into the Meter Editor.

To access the Meter Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Editor**.

Meter Selector

While creating or editing a meter, users can use the Meter Selector to edit the system, number, and name of a meter. For existing meters, this is the only location where these values can be updated. When updating a meter number and saving, the system message 8 and the meter message 8 “Meter number changed” will be generated.

Meter Editor Details

The following items are available on the Meter Editor screen: - **Refresh** - Reload the meter from the database - **New** - Create a new meter A fluid phase of liquid is only available with the **FLOWCAL Liquids** module. - **Edit** - Enable data edit mode - **Copy** - Copy the selected meter and generate a new meter, maintaining the data from the original meter - **Delete** - Delete the selected meter - **Save** - Saves changes to data; only enabled when in New or Edit mode - **Cancel** - Cancel changes; only enabled when in New or Edit mode - **Exit** - Exit the Meter Editor screen - **Notes** - Enter or edit a note for the selected meter by right-clicking the Meter Editor screen while a meter is selected. Notes that have been added through the Notes screen can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Volume Editor). When the selected meter includes a note that has been added using this method, the note icon in the Object Selector displays in color when that meter is selected. - **Src Assigns.** - Open the Quality Source Assignment Viewer with the meter number pre-populated - **Open Data** - Open the Volume Editor with the meter number pre-populated and the current month/year - **Location Info** - Display the meter’s associated location relationships - **Close Dates** - Open the Meter Data Close Dates screen with the meter number pre-populated for all dates - **User Access** - Display users and groups with access to the selected meter User/group access to meters is only relevant for companies that maintain object-level security. Most companies do not restrict access on a per-meter basis. - **Test Reports** - For TESTit enabled meters, the **Test Reports** button is available immediately below the **Exit** button. For TESTit 2 Integrated, this button will display the test reports for the meter. You can then open each one to see the details or make edits. With TESTit 3 Integrated, test reports will display when you click the **Test Reports** button, but a PDF is opened for each record. Edits must be made within TESTit 3. This feature requires TESTit Integrated.

docs.title: Misc. Tab
docs.text:
Most of the items listed are informational, read-only fields. The Meter Type, Meter Make, and Default Temperature values are retrieved from the meter characteristics table for the current characteristic. If needed, you can enter other details about the meter such as the serial number, site ID, power source, pressure mode, and temperature mode.

Additional options on this tab include:

  • Last Modified - Read-only field that shows the last user who edited the meter within the Meter Editor and the datetime of the edit.

  • Existing Data - Read-only fields displaying the following dates:

  • Creation Date - The date when data was first imported into FLOWCAL for this meter.

  • Unarchived Data Start - The date of the first meter data record in the database.

  • Unarchived Data End - The date of the last meter data record in the database.

    The Unarchived Data End date should not exceed the current datetime.

  • First Flow - The first flow date is used to calculate the BLM Calculated Tier when a meter started flowing within the last 12 months. The Notify field is used to notify a contact when the meter begins to flow. When real flow is confirmed, the analyst manually enters the date in the Volume Editor. A notification email is then sent to the contact type specified in the Notify field.

The first flow date is also used when the Source Assignment Required option is enabled in the System Configuration screen, which enables generation of exception 55. Only dates after the first flow date will be checked for assignment for the exception. The exception effective date will be the first flow date.

The Notify functionality is only available if you have purchased the Scheduled Reporting module.

docs.title: Reports Tab
docs.text:
The Reports tab contains meter-level report options that are associated with and affect the behavior of several standard reports. In addition, Contract Hour, Contract Day, and Data Span are displayed as read-only fields from the meter’s most recent characteristic record.

This tab also includes the option to enable a meter for TESTit Integrated.

Reports Tab Details

The following options are available on the Reports tab: - **Contract Hour** - Displays as read-only field using the meter’s most recent characteristic record. - **Contract Day** - Displays as read-only field using the meter’s most recent characteristic record. - **Time Leads Data/Time Trails Data** - Displays as read-only field using the meter’s most recent characteristic record. - **Read Tolerance** - Read tolerances (in days) may be set for monthly records. Records whose actual (entered) on date is within the read tolerance will be snapped to contract start of month. Records whose actual (entered) off date is within the read tolerance will be snapped to the contract end of month. - **Print Customer Name** - If set to "Yes", the customer name (selected on the [General tab](General%20Tab.md)) will replace the company name or logo defined in FLOWCAL on meter-level reports. - **Print Edit Reasons on Gas Volume Statement** - By default, Daily and Hourly Gas Volume Statements identify each record as edited or not, but do not print the edit reasons. With this option, you can choose to: - Show Codes and Reasons - Indicate Edited Data, No Reasons - No Edit Indicators - **Print Interval or Fixed Factor on Gas Volume Statement** - Determines whether the interval or fixed factor will be displayed on the Gas Volume Statement. For charts, "interval" refers to the rotation. For EFMs, "fixed factor" refers to the data resolution defined in the meter’s characteristics. - **Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name** - On many meter reports, the alternate meter number specified on the [General](General%20Tab.md) tab can be displayed instead of the meter name. - **Print Volume at Optional Pressure Base** - If set to "Yes", the volume will be recalculated at the pressure base specified in the **Use Pressure Base of** field. This recalculated volume will then be printed at the bottom of the Daily Gas Volume Statement, along with the optional pressure base. The value entered for the optional pressure base must be between 9.000 and 20.000 psi. - **Use Pressure Base of** - Used in conjunction with the Print Volume at Optional Pressure Base option. - **Print Measurement Area** - If set to "Yes", the measurement area will be printed at the top of most meter reports that display one meter per page. - **Measurement Area** - Select a measurement area from the drop-down or, with the correct privileges, click the **New** button to create a new Measurement Area. Measurement areas are managed from the [Measurement Area Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Geographic/Measurement%20Area%20Editor.md). - **Chart Change Schedule** - Chart labels can be created for scheduled chart routes. An annual schedule is used to specify the on and off dates for the charts, which is used when printing the Bar Code Labels report. (See: [Annual Schedule Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md)) - **Show Off Spec on Batch Ticket** - If set to "Yes", [exceptions 30009 - 30040](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/30000/30000-30999.md) on the batch data generated based on product specifications will display on the Meter Batch Ticket reports (liquid meters only). - **Enabled for TESTit** - This field is set to "No" by default when a meter is created. With TESTit Integrated, you can set this field to "Yes" to enable the meter for TESTit. This feature requires TESTit Integrated. - **For TESTit 2 Integrated** - Once this field is set to "Yes", it cannot be changed due to the audit trail and the ability to link TESTit tasks to the meter. - **For TESTit 3 Integrated** - This field may be set back to "No". The tasks in TESTit 3 are not affected by this change. - **Test Reports** - Click this button to access the TESTit test reports for the meter. This is only available if the meter is TESTit enabled. - **Skip Closing Data** - When set to "Yes", closing the meter will be prohibited.

docs.title: Services Tab
docs.text:
This tab is not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.

The Services tab is used for configuring the Auto Estimate, Gas Day Projection, and Rescan services, as well as the Quality and Characteristics Download processes for each meter. Note that the Rescan service controls both SCADA Request and Late Data exceptions.

Auto Estimate Sub-Tab

For FLOWCAL to auto estimate data, the service FcSrvAutoEstimate.exe must be installed and running. The Auto Estimate service allows for the estimation of missing data until data can be provided from the field. If multiple gaps are present with data interspersed between, the estimated values used to fill each gap are determined independently. Auto estimates are configured in the Meter Editor on a per-meter basis; they can also be configured for a list of meters using the Bulk Changes screen. The data collection interval should be smaller than the auto estimating interval (Time Elapsed Before Missing) to minimize unneeded estimates, which would unnecessarily grow the database and affect performance. Auto estimate should only be running when the collection interval has skipped. The Auto Estimate service is not applicable for gas line pack meters. This feature is only available with the Service to Auto Estimate Missing Data Module. - **Auto Estimate Enabled** - If set to "Yes", the Auto Estimate service is enabled for the meter. - **Replace Estimated Data on Import** - If set to “Yes”, estimated data will be replaced by original data when it is imported. Auto estimated records are created as revision 1. Data imported into a period that has been auto estimated comes in both as a revision 0 record (beneath the auto estimated record) and as a revision 2 record, which will overwrite the auto estimate data. If source analysis or an auto edit is to be applied, it will be applied at this time, and a revision 3 record will be created in meter periodic values. If this option is set to “No”, the imported data is only brought in under the auto estimated record, and an exception is generated to indicate that imported data is being obscured by the estimated data. - **Auto Estimate Record Only One Time** - If set to “Yes”, once data has been auto estimated, that data is no longer considered for estimation. This keeps the original estimate, regardless of any newer data that it might be based on. If set to “No”, changes to data used to generate the auto estimate can result in the records being re-estimated and adjusted as appropriate. - **Log Missing Data in Exceptions Log** - If set to “Yes”, an exception is generated to flag records written by the Auto Estimate service as having missing data so that they can be evaluated, and data can then be imported if needed. To clear this exception, you must manually ignore it from the Exception Resolver. This missing data exception is in addition to the missing data exceptions that may occur on import. - **Log Exception on Replacing Auto Estimate** - If set to “Yes”, an exception will be generated when an auto estimated record is replaced by imported data. To clear this exception, you must manually ignore it from the Exception Resolver. - **Estimate Resolution** - The resolution that the Auto Estimate service will use when writing new records. This should match the resolution defined by the meter's characteristics. Options are 15 Minutes, Hourly and Daily. - **Time Elapsed Before Missing** - Days or hours elapsed from the current datetime before data will be considered missing. Valid values are 0 to 30 (for days) and 0 to 23 (for hours). - **Number of Prior Days Considered** - The number of days prior to the current date that the auto estimate service will scan to create an estimate for missing data or update a previous estimate. Valid values are 1 to 60. Example If you enter 60, the service will not examine data that is more than 60 days old. Closed data within the specified time frame is not considered. - **Adjust for Daylight Savings Time** - If set to "Yes", the Auto Estimate service will allow for a missing hour in the week after Daylight Saving Time begins. When the time reverts to standard time, one record will have double volume (for double flow time). If set to "No", the Auto Estimate service will estimate for the missing hour if a time change occurs. - **Improve Estimate** - If set to "Yes", when more than one estimate technique is specified, the Auto Estimate service will re-estimate using a better technique as more information becomes available. FLOWCAL considers Estimate Technique 1 to be the best technique. Example If Estimate Technique 1 is a point-to-point estimate, and there is no data after the missing data, then this technique cannot be performed, so the service would use Estimate Technique 2, if specified. If data is later provided that occurs after the missing data, but there is still missing data elsewhere, the Auto Estimate service will see that the data was originally estimated using Estimate Technique 2, but that new data is now available, so Estimate Technique 1 can now be used. If set to “No”, once data is estimated by Technique 2 or 3, it will not be re-estimated by a "better" technique, even if new data is provided. - **Energy** - Determines how missing energy is calculated. - **Estimate from Data** - Energy will be estimated using the same technique as was used to estimate the volume. - **Calculate from Hv** - Energy is calculated by applying the heating value to the estimated volume. The heating value may come from a source assignment; if there is no source assignment, the heating value may be an estimated value. A source assignment may overwrite an energy value if the estimated data has been accepted. - **Edit Reason** - When data is estimated, this edit reason will appear with the historical data. The Code field shows the associated code to help indicate the edit reason. Auto Estimate Techniques A meter or location’s data must be rolled up, depending on the auto estimate technique selected. - **Average Data** - All records preceding a period of missing data that fall within the specified number of prior days or hours will be averaged to derive the values that will be propagated forward. - **Skip No Flow** - If checked, records indicating that a meter experienced zero flow are not included when generating the average. - **Allow Use of Auto Estimated Data** - If checked previously auto estimated records that fall within the specified window will be included when calculating the average. Consider the data resolution when specifying averaging period. - **User Data** - Missing data is populated with user-specified volume and energy or gross standard volume and mass. This is useful when a meter has gone out of service and needs to be populated with zeroes, or if a compressor has no meter on the fuel usage, but you have an estimate to use for balancing the system. Note that only volume and energy are populated; pulses, differential pressure, static pressure, temperature, and flow time will remain blank. - **Curve Data** - Specify a starting volume, energy, base date, and decline factor. The specified volume and energy will be used on the base date and start declining by the factor specified. Over time the volume and energy estimate will diminish based on the decline factor. This technique may be used when a well test is done periodically, and the volume and energy is calculated for that point in time. - **Point to Point Data** - When a gap is present, the record immediately preceding the gap and the record immediately following it will be evaluated, and the average of the difference between the two records will be determined for each data point. Starting from the first missing record, the previous value for a data point will be adjusted by the calculated value, creating a series of intermediate steps between the two field records. It will draw a straight line between the start and end points for differential pressure, pressure, temperature, volume, and energy. There must be data both prior to and after the missing data. - **Reference Meter or Location Data** - A reference meter or location must be specified for this option. Any missing data is filled in using the values available at that time on the reference meter or location. The **Multiplier** option allows you to specify a factor by which the reference meter or location's data is multiplied before being applied to the current meter or location. - **Previous Day’s Data** - This technique populates each record with data provided for the meter exactly one day prior. This technique is useful if meters are cyclical.

Gas Day Projection Sub-Tab

The Gas Day Projection service automatically projects flow values for a meter or location for the remainder of the gas day. These projected values are based upon historical data variables selected by the user and are calculated as an allocated percentage of a reference meter or location. This feature requires the Gas Day Projection Volume Service module. #### User Reference Data Estimate based on the meter, reference meter, or location data. - **Percentage Used** - The percentage of volume, energy, and mass used from the source record. This option projects any nonexistent daily data for the current day back one month. If any daily data exists that has actual hourly data and is complete or incomplete, the service does not project this record. If using a reference meter or reference location, the service only projects days where the reference has daily data. The percentage used only applies to the reference meter or location data. #### User Historical Data Estimate based on an average of previous days or hours as specified based on the meter or reference meter. This option projects current day only. Current day is the day after the contract hour; otherwise, the current data refers to the previous day.  

SCADA Request Sub-Tab

This service scans the meter periodic values looking for missing data. Missing data queues a SCADA request to poll the meter device for the missing data. Requests can be seen from the SCADA Request Viewer. The SCADA system must support this feature for it to work. - **SCADA Request Enabled** - When set to "Yes", the SCADA Request service is enabled for the meter. - **Log Rescan Data in Exceptions Log** - When set to “Yes”, an exception is generated when estimated data is written to the database. To clear this exception, you must manually ignore it from the Exception Resolver. This is a useful method for alerting office personnel to a meter not reporting in a timely fashion. - **Rescan Frequency** - Determines if the service should rescan the meter periodic values hourly or daily. - **Daily Rescan Hour** - Designates the hour of the day that the service should perform the scan. - **Number of Retries Allowed** - The number of times that the service should request SCADA to attempt to collect data for missing hours. If no data is found after the specified number of rescans, the status in the FC_SCADA_REQUEST table is set to "N". - **Time Elapsed Before Considered for Rescan** - Amount of time (days or hours) the service waits until it rescans for missing data. Valid values are 0 to 30 (for days) and 0 to 23 (for hours). Data is considered missing if it is older than the values entered. - **Number of Prior Days Considered** - The time frame for which the service processes data. Specifies the number of days prior to the current date that the service will scan for missing data. Valid values are 1 to 60. Example If you enter 60, the service will not examine data that is more than 60 days old. Closed data within the time frame specified is not considered. Make sure that you have installed and started the fcSrvAutoRecan.exe service.

Late Data Sub-Tab

Using these settings, FLOWCAL will generate exception 4104 (Missing (late) data detected) when missing data is found and the wait period exceeds the amount of time specified in the Generate Late Data Exception After field. This service searches the prior number of days/hours specified, and generates an exception if there is missing data in at least one of those hours. The late data exception indicates that data should have arrived in FLOWCAL at a given time and is now late. - **Late Data Exception Enabled** - When set to "Yes", late data exceptions are enabled for the meter. - **Generate Late Data Exception After** - The length of time (in days or hours) to wait before generating the late data exception. This determines when to generate the late data exception, not the SCADA request exception. Make sure that you have installed and started the fcSrvAutoRecan.exe service.

Quality Download Sub-Tab

This tab allows for specified analysis data to be submitted as a SCADA request to a meter's remote terminal unit (RTU). Requests can be seen from the SCADA Request Viewer. The SCADA system must support this feature for it to work. - **Data to Download** - Once a Data to Download option has been selected and saved, a grid will display with the analysis data points. The following options are available: - **Current Analysis** - Most recent source analysis record from the assigned source (database table fc_gq_source_analysis). - **Last Hourly** - Current time minus 1 hour from the hourly rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_hourly). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups and for hourly rollups. - **Last Daily** - Current day minus 1 day from the daily rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_daily). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups. - **Last Monthly** - Current month minus 1 month from the monthly rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_monthly). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups. - **Current Daily** - Current time from the daily rollups for the source assigned (database table fc_ffgq_daily). Requires that the source is enabled for rollups. - **None** - Do not download any analysis data (default). - **Send Current** - If checked, values will be provided by the current quality source, if one has been associated with the meter. - **New Value** - Specify a new value for a parameter. - **Send** - When clicked, the update request is written to the SCADA request table.

Characteristic Download Sub-Tab

This tab allows for meter configuration and alarm parameters to be broadcast back to the remote terminal unit (RTU). In this way, an event that may have been missed can be corrected through FLOWCAL. Characteristic download requests can be seen from the SCADA Request Viewer. This tab is only visible while in view mode. The SCADA system must support this feature for it to work. - **Send Current** - If checked, values will be provided by the current Master Meter Characteristic record, if one is provided for the meter. - **New Value** - Specify a new value for a parameter. - **Send** - When clicked, the update request is written to the SCADA request table.

docs.title: Snap Before/Snap After
docs.text:
When importing meter or source analysis data, some records will not come in at the top of an hour. This can cause missing data exceptions and it may appear that you have duplicate records with one hour missing and another with data.

In the meter imported below, data appears to be missing for every other hour. In this case, the data is coming in one second before the hour (ex. 16:59:59 instead of 17:00:00).

To fix this issue, go to Setup > Meter > Meter Editor and adjust the Snap Before and Snap After option on the Imports tab. Enter the number of seconds before and/or after the time frame you are trying to adjust. Usually putting 10 to 15 seconds in the Snap Before and the Snap After fields resolves most of these data cases.

To resolve the issue:

  1. Go to Setup > Meter > Meter Editor >Imports tab.
  2. Click Edit.
  3. Enter the number of seconds before and after the hour you want to adjust. It is best to enter a value in both fields to catch both scenarios.
  4. Click Save.

Once saved, any data that is imported going forward will be adjusted if the records do not start at the top of the hour.

If you set this option after importing data, you will need to purge the existing data and re-import it to reflect the changes.

To purge the data:

  1. Go to Tools > Purge > Meter Data.
  2. Select the meter and then specify the correct contract month or date range where records do not come in at the top of the hour.

Once the data is purged, re-import the data by going to Import > Meter Data.

The following example shows how this option corrected the data.

The Snap Before and Snap After option is also available for source analyses within the Source Analysis Editor. This option is used most often when collecting gas quality data from a gas chromatograph when the data is not coming in at the top of the hour. To set this option for source analyses, go to Setup > Source Analysis > Gas Quality > Main tab.

docs.title: Validations Tab
docs.text:
On this tab, you can manually set or edit validation parameters for a meter. If the Run on Imports and Edits option is set to "Yes", validations will be performed during imports and edits. If this option set to "No", validations will not be performed.

If a value is out of validation range, an exception will be generated. All exceptions generated can be viewed and edited within the Exception Resolver. Exceptions will only be generated the Run on Imports and Edits option is set to "Yes" and the item has a value to check against.

You can also use validations to track the data in the Max Exception Severity column in the Final Form (rollups) tables. By setting the severity of any exceptions to an elevated level, custom exports or other downstream systems can examine the Max Exception Severity value to determine if a record is ready to be exported.

Flowing Parameters Sub-Tab

#### General Flowing Parameters validations allow for definition of minimum and maximum limits on Flow Variable (DP or Pulses), Static Pressure, Temperature, Volume, Energy NSV, Mass, Flow Basis (Extension, Raw Volume), Volume Correlation Factor (VCF), Speed of Sound and Flow Time variables. If a liquid meter uses a volumetric measurement, then net standard volume can be validated; otherwise, mass can be validated. For gas meters only, when the system option is enabled, high-high and low-low limits are available for additional flowing parameter validations, which generate associated exceptions. When high-high/low-low limits are available in addition to high/low limits, only one exception is generated for data that exceeds the set limits. For example: If a value exceeds both the high limit and the high-high limit, only one exception will be generated for exceeding the high-high limit. A second exception for exceeding the High limit will not be generated. - **Run on Imports and Edits** - When set to "Yes", Flowing Parameter validations are enabled for the meter. - **Extension** - The extension reported by the meter, or, if FLOWCAL calculates the extension, the average flowing extension (orifice meters only). - **Raw Volume** - The actual volume, which does not have the temperature, pressure, or compressibility corrections required for standard volume (AGA-7 meters only). - **VCF** - The volume calculated by the electronic flow meter, divided by the FLOWCAL-calculated volume (gas meters only). This factor is typically close to 1 (example: .997) because of differences between the two sets of volumes. In some cases, such as intermittent flow, these differences can exceed 20%. These differences occur when significant fluctuations of the flowing parameters (DP, P, or T) happen within the record. - **Correlation Factor** - The Mass, GSV, NSV, IV, and SWV calculated by the electronic flow meter the user is editing, divided by the FLOWCAL calculated number for each value (liquid meters only). This factor is typically close to 1 (example: .997), because there will usually be small differences between the two sets of values. The same Min and Max limits are applied to all five Liquid Correlation Factors for Mass, GSV, NSV, IV, and SWV. - **Speed of Sound** - Only applicable to ultrasonic meters that import speed of sound diagnostics. - **Max Deviation** - The difference between the meter's imported raw volume and the volume FLOWCAL calculates from the pipe length and pipe diameter (line pack calculations only). The comparison can determine a unit difference or a percent difference. - For a unit difference test, the calculated value must be within the raw volume +/- the deviation amount. If the calculated value is outside of this range, exception 1050 will be generated. Example Raw volume = 10,000, unit difference = 100. The calculated volume must be within the range of 9,900 to 10,100. - For a percent difference test, the calculated value must be within the raw volume +/- the deviation percentage. If the calculated value is outside of this range, exception 1048 will be generated Example Raw volume = 10,000, percent deviation = 2. The calculated volume must be within the range of 9,800 to 10,200. - **Flow Time** - Comparison of the meter's real flow time to the set minimum and maximum values. Options are Minutes, Hours, Days, % of an hour, or No Entry/Clear. If the flow time is outside of the range specified here, an exception is generated. The No Entry/Clear option deletes any previously entered value. Setting the value to 0 will not disable the validation; it will set the minimum value to 0. If the “% of an hour” option is selected in the drop-down, values shown will display with a decimal precision of two places. Example If the previous drop-down value selected was Days (DD HHH:MM:SS) and the validation value was 00 000:45:25 = 2725 s = 75.694444444444 %, the Meter Editor will display 75.69 % if the drop-down is changed to “% of an hour”. For a daily resolution meter, it may be easier to enter and read validation limits in hours (23:55:00 and 24:05:00) rather than seconds (85100 and 86700). Even for hourly resolution, minutes (59 and 61) may be easier to interpret than seconds (3540 and 3660). - **Skip No-Flow Exceptions** - When set to "Yes", an exception will not be generated when a meter has a record that is zero flow, even if the parameter is outside of the validation limits. For orifice meters, no flow is defined as: - Volume = 0 and differential pressure \< no flow cutoff; or - Volume = 0, differential pressure not given and flow time = 0; or - Volume = 0, differential pressure not given, and flow time not given For non-orifice meters, no flow is defined as: - Volume = 0 and flow time = 0; or - Volume = 0 and pulses = 0 - **Scale for Flow Time** - If enabled, the data for accumulated fields (volume, energy, pulses, and mass) will be scaled based on flow time. #### Coriolis - **Drive Gain Min / Max** - Minimum and maximum allowed drive gain values (Coriolis meters only). #### Ultrasonic 2 Ultrasonic flow meters measure the travel time difference of ultrasonic sound waves transmitted with and against the fluid flow direction. The time difference, along with the physical configuration of the meter, is used to determine the average velocity of the flow. Speed of Sound Validation When the speed of sound differs across records (i.e., over time) more than the limit configured here, [exception 2501](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated. - **Duration (Hours)** - The number of previous UFM diagnostics records that the current record is to be validated against. - **Percent Difference Allowed** - The maximum percentage of difference allowed between the current record and the previous records. When the speed of sound variance exceeds the limit configured here, [exception 2502](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated. - **Variance** - Amount of variance allowed between FLOWCAL's speed of sound calculation and the value imported. - **Compare Using** - When performing the variance validation for speed of sound, the variance can be specified as a unit difference or a percent difference. Flow Velocity Profile Validation - **Baseline** - A user-defined target value for the calculated profile. - **Percent Difference Allowed** - A comparison between the profile baseline and the calculated baseline. This value is the maximum percentage of variance allowed before [exception 2503](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated. Example | Calculated Profile From UFM Periodic Data | Baseline | Pct. Difference Allowed | Percent Difference Calculated/Baseline | Exception Generated | |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:| | 5.02 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((5.02/5.095)-1)\*100=1.472% | No | | 6 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((6/5.095)-1)\*100=17.763% | Yes | | 4 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((4/5.095)-1)\*100=21.492% | Yes |   Flow Velocity Symmetry Validation - **Baseline** - A user-defined target value for the calculated symmetry. - **Percent Difference Allowed** - A comparison between the symmetry baseline and the calculated baseline. This value is the maximum percentage of variance allowed before [exception 2504](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2500-2599.md) is generated. Example | Calculated Symmetry From UFM Periodic Data | Baseline | Pct. Difference Allowed | Percent Difference Calculated/Baseline | Exception Generated | |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:| | 1.001 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((1.001/1.0001)-1)\*100=0.089% | No | | 0.9 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((0.9/1.0001)-1)\*100=-10.009% | Yes | | 1.1 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((1.1/1.0001)-1)\*100=9.989% | Yes |  

Analysis Sub-Tab

Analysis validations assess analysis data applied to a meter. Much like the flowing parameters, minimum and maximum values can be specified for each of the components available under the **Mole %** button. - **Quality button** - Quality-related information such as total GPM, relative density, heating value, sample pressure, and sample temperature can be validated. Available for gas meters only - **Mole % button** - Mole % validations are available for both gas and liquid meters. - **Liquids button** - Liquids validations are available for liquid meters only.

Frozen Values Sub-Tab*

Frozen Values validations are used if a meter continues to report the same value for a data point over several consecutive records. It is possible the reading is inaccurate, and the results are caused by a frozen value that is not being updated. In this section, you can specify whether to look for frozen values, the duration for which each value must persist before it is considered frozen, and the deadband for each value, which serves as a tolerance level within which values will be treated as identical. To specify a deadband value of 0, set the value to a very small number (for example, 0.001) rather than 0. Specifying 0 will not trigger validation for that data point.

Single Run Sub-Tab*

Single Run validations enable user-defined comparisons of a meter’s current record to prior records to identify excessive variation. For each flowing parameter, you can specify whether to compare the data to the previous record or to the previous day.

Multiple Run Sub-Tab*

Multiple Run validations are similar to Single Run validations, but you can also compare the meter’s record with up to four other meter records. This feature provides a comparison for multi-tube locations, check meters versus sales meters, or upstream and downstream comparisons. - **Temperature Differentiation** - This is useful if two meters have the same feed and one of them is shut in. Where the meter is shut in, the temperature should not track the temperature of the line with flow. If it does track, that indicates a leak. In this case, FLOWCAL will generate an exception to try to identify the problem.

Expert Systems Sub-Tab*

Expert Systems validations apply statistical analyses to historical data to identify uncharacteristic changes in a meter's data flow pattern. If the value in the current record being imported is outside the range of the lower and upper bounds, which are calculated using a running or weighted average (Average Count field), an exception is generated. The following options are available on the Expert Systems sub-tab: - **Average Method** - The method by which average values will be calculated. - **Running** - A straight average of all values where each value has an equal weighting. ![](data:image/png;base64,) - **Weighted** - Each value to be averaged is assigned a weight. The oldest record is assigned a weight of 1. Newer records carry more weight, increasing by an interval of 1. ![](data:image/png;base64,) - **Average Count** - The number of records used to calculate the average; this count starts with the record immediately prior to the record being validated and goes back in time. Missing data is included in the average count, but it is not included in the average calculation. A data point with no value in an existing value does get included in the average calculation. If all records in the period to be used for average calculation are missing, no validation takes place for the current iteration. The validation process moves on to the next record to be validated. - **Exclude E/S Exception** - If set to "Yes", data points with Expert Systems exceptions are excluded during the validation process. When an Expert System exception has been flagged, it is a data anomaly, which may not be desirable when calculating averages for more data points for the same meter. Example | Effective Date | Volume | Exception | |:--------------------|:------:|:---------:| | 1/1/2017 07:00:00 | 1290 | \- | | 1/1/2017 08:00:00 | 1200 | \- | | 1/1/2017 09:00:00 | 800 | 2236 | | 1/1/2017 10:00:00 | 1250 | \- | | 1/1/2017 11:00:00 | 1260 | \- | | 1/1/2017 12:00:00 | 1290 | \- | | 1/1/2017 13:00:00\* | 1350 | \- | \* Record being validated The record at 1/1/2017 13:00:00 is being validated, with an average count of 5. Typically, this would mean that the average would be calculated from the previous five records (1/1/2017 8:00:00 through 1/1/2017 12:00:00). However, note that the 1/1/2017 9:00:00 record has a validation exception (2236 ES - Volume failed). This exception is an expert systems validation, so this record is excluded from the process. The average is then calculated from the other four records: (1200+1250+1260+1290) / 4 = 1250. - **Step** - The number of consecutive records to be validated using the calculated average. Valid inputs are integers between 1 and 96. If a step value is not provided, the value will default to 1. The first step of a contract month will always start on the first period of the month. If a step spans two months, the validation process will start over at the beginning of the second month. Example - **Method** - **Percent Difference** Lower Bound = Average - (Percent Difference \* Average) Upper Bound = Average + (Percent Difference \* Average) - **Std Deviation** Lower Bound = Average - (ES Limit \* Standard Deviation) Upper Bound = Average + (ES Limit \* Standard Deviation) - **LO Limit / HI Limit** - When the Expert Systems calculation is complete, FLOWCAL validates if any data points were below or above the low and high benchmark limits. An exception is generated for any data points outside of the set limits. Expert Systems Example | Step | Effective Date | Volume | Average Used for Validation | |:----:|:-----------------:|:------:|:---------------------------:| | \- | 1/1/2017 04:00:00 | 1290 | \- | | \- | 1/1/2017 05:00:00 | 1200 | \- | | \- | 1/1/2017 06:00:00 | 1130 | \- | | \- | 1/1/2017 07:00:00 | 1250 | \- | | \- | 1/1/2017 08:00:00 | 1260 | \- | | 1 | 1/1/2017 09:00:00 | 1290 | 1210 | | 1 | 1/1/2017 10:00:00 | 1350 | 1210 | | 1 | 1/1/2017 11:00:00 | 1340 | 1210 | | 2 | 1/1/2017 12:00:00 | 1370 | 1310 | | 2 | 1/1/2017 13:00:00 | 1310 | 1310 | | 2 | 1/1/2017 14:00:00 | 1315 | 1310 | In this example, the average count value is 4 and step value is 3. The contract day is 1 and contract hour is 9. For validation of January data, the 1/1/2017 9:00:00 record is validated first. Since the step value is 3, the three records starting at 1/1/2017 9:00:00 are validated using the same average. The average is calculated from the four previous records starting with the record immediately before the beginning of the step and going back in time. This means the average of the four records starting with 1/1/2017 8:00:00 and going back in time will be used: (1200+1130+1250+1260) / 4 = 1210 The next step begins with the record after the first step (1/1/2017 12:00:00). The three records starting at 1/1/2017 12:00:00 are validated using the average calculated from the four preceding records from 1/1/2017 8:00:00 to 1/1/2017 11:00:00: (1260+1290+1350+1340) / 4 = 1310 Expert Systems Example With Missing Data | Effective Date | Temperature | Volume | Weight | |:-------------------:|:-----------:|:------:|:------:| | 1/1/2017 07:00:00 | 71 | 1100 |   | | 1/1/2017 08:00:00 | 79 | 1200 | 1 | | 1/1/2017 09:00:00 |   | 800 | 2 | | \[missing\] |   |   |   | | \[missing\] |   |   |   | | 1/1/2017 12:00:00 | 85 | 1300 | 3 | | 1/1/2017 13:00:00\* | 86 | 1350 |   | \* Record being validated **Running average of volume** - To validate volume of the 1/1/2017 13:00:00 record, records in the five-hour period of 1/1/2017 8:00:00 – 1/1/2017 12:00:00 are averaged. As two hours in the period are missing data, the average is calculated as (1200+800+1300) / 3 = 1100. **Weighted average of volume** - The oldest record in the period, 1/1/2017 8:00:00, is assigned with the weight of 1. Weight increases by 1 for each record with data until the record immediately before the record being validated. The two hours missing data are not included in the average calculation, and are not assigned a weight. **Temperature validation** - The 1/1/2017 9:00:00 record does not have a temperature value. The running average of temperature would be calculated as (79+85) / 2 = 83.

Final Form Sub-Tab*

Final Form occurs on rolled-up data at hourly, daily, or monthly resolution. Min/Max and Expert Systems validations are available for Final Form. You can flag daily and monthly values comparable to nominations for the day or month. Editing the daily and/or monthly validation ranges routinely will help you identify the in-line comparison to the marketing nominations set at the beginning of each day and/or month. This tab is also useful when trying to maintain contractual agreements between two parties. The Max monthly final form meter data validation is performed when data changes even if the month is not complete. Exceptions for high monthly values are generated as soon as a given monthly value exceeds the max validation set point even when the month is not yet complete. Validations for Min values are checked only when the month is complete. #### Min/Max Click the **Min/Max** button to access the following options: - **DE Alarm Count** - Used strictly for a specific field unit named Total Flow. This allows the user to set values that will indicate the Differential Error limit expected to see on a daily basis. - **Back Flow Percentage** - Used strictly for a specific field unit named Total Flow. Setting the Back Flow Percentage limit, the user will be able to flag when to receive an exception on typical back flow of the field unit.

MF/KF Sub-Tab*

Meter factor and K-factor (MF/KF) validations provide a comparison of a meter characteristic value to a range from an established baseline value. See Unit Diff and % Diff below to determine the range. The following items are available on the MF/KF sub-tab: - **Baseline Enable** - Enter "Yes" to enable baseline factor validations. - **Product grid** - Displays the baseline details of each configured product - **Select Product** - If the [Validate Products](Liquids%20Tab.md#ValidateProducts) option is enabled in the Meter Editor, this product selector will contain the meter's valid products; otherwise, it will contain the complete list of products. - **Baseline Date** - The date this baseline information was established. This is an informational value. The characteristic will be validated against the current baseline factors without regard to the baseline date. - **Meter Factor** - The user-determined baseline meter factor. - **K Factor** - The user-determined baseline K-factor. - **Unit Diff** - The scalar amount added to or subtracted from the baseline factor to determine an acceptable range. Example The acceptable range for a characteristic meter factor is between (Meter Factor - Unit Diff) and (Meter Factor + Unit Diff). - **% Diff** - The percent amount applied to the baseline factor to determine an acceptable range. Example The acceptable range for a characteristic K-factor is between (K-Factor \* (1 + (% Diff/100) ) ) and (K Factor \* (1 - (% Diff/100) ) ). The initial set up screen provides a General product. This baseline will apply to all products for which a specific validation has not been added. The General product cannot be removed. Values that are not configured will not cause an exception. It is not necessary to provide both a meter factor and a K-factor, or to provide both a value for Unit Diff and % Diff. If a product row is added and no other values are provided for it, no validation will take place for that product. See: [MKF Exceptions 2451 - 2454](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/2000/2400-2499.md)

* Not available for dead oil meters or flash gas meters.
