docs.title: Meter Quick Create
docs.text:
Meter Quick Create is a quick and simple way to quickly create a new gas meter or multiple gas meters that share one or more common attributes.  This allows the user to set up the import driver and import path (file and folder name) so that the user does not have to enter it every time he or she wants to import data for a meter.  This screen also allows the user to add more information about the meter such as: characteristics, units (US or Metric), the user can set validations and select information that the user would want to have on a report.

This function is not available for liquid meters and may not be available for gas meters if the administrator has set up required meter fields and disabled Meter Quick Create.

To create a meter: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Quick Create**. 2. When a meter is created or edited, some fields can be required to be populated. Failure to populate a required field will prevent a record from being saved. Required fields that are blank are highlighted in green. There are numerous fields in the Meter Attributes that are not available under Meter Quick Create and meters can thus be created without all of the required fields being populated. Once you edit the meter under the Meter Editor, then the remaining required fields must be populated before you can save any other changes. 3. Under the Imports tab, select an Import Driver (see: [Import Driver Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Import%20Driver%20Editor.md)) from the drop-down menu or click to add a new import driver. Depending on what import driver you choose, the fields may change on the screen.  For example, if you select Bristol as your import driver, the fields for an FCS File and Shared CFG will appear. If Fisher import driver is selected, the field TUBE NUMBER will appear. 4. Enter an import path. 5. Enter a file name. 6. Click the **Save** button. 7. To enter more meters, click **Clear** and repeat steps 1-6. Alternatively, the user may elect to enter only values for fields common across multiple new meter to be created and the user must only enter a new meter number and click **Save**.

Imports Tab

The following items are available on the Imports tab: - **Compare to Master Characteristics** - If Compare to Master Characteristics is checked, FLOWCAL will check to see if the meters characteristics match the Master Characteristics. If the Master Characteristics are different from the meter characteristics, an exception will occur. Exceptions and updates of characteristics will be done based on user selection within the Master Data Validation. - **External Volume** - An External Volume Meter is usually a meter whose volume is not calculated in the System.  The meter's data is imported into FLOWCAL via the External Volume Import Mechanism (Data Entry or File Import) where it can be edited and utilized with complete reporting functions. - **Update Meter Name** - Normally, the meter name from the .CFX file associated with a meter is imported into FLOWCAL, unless the user has this field set to NO. The meter name in the field is not always what is desired in FLOWCAL. By default, the meter name is updated on import with the meter name from the field. If you want to keep the meter name manually entered into FLOWCAL, set this field to "No." - **Inhibit Default Exceptions** - If set to Yes, FLOWCAL will not generate any exceptions for default validations. FLOWCAL runs an extensive suite of Default Validations to alert the user about data being out of range for a given calculation or configuration. User configured validations will still generate exceptions. By default, this field is set to Null. Null and No are treated the same. - **Auto Edit Criteria** - This option can set a particular Auto Edit at the meter level. Auto Edit Criterian= also has the ability to be enabled only at Import. - **Import ID** - Import ID is used for text file imports, Transaction Queue processing and also for imports of Flow Automation MBS## files. If importing text files or Transaction Queue data, the meter number in the system sending data to FLOWCAL may not match the meter number in the user's system. If so, put the meter number from the other system in Import ID and check the box Meter number field is Import ID when importing the text file. If Importing MBS## files, there is a requirement that the meter name in FLOWCAL match that in the MBS## file. If you want a different meter name in FLOWCAL, put the meter name of the meter in the MBS## file in the Import ID field. - **Snap Before and Snap After** - The Snap Before and Snap After fields are used to snap data to the start of an hour. When dealing with hourly data, records are expected to come in right on the hour. Sometimes the records may come in with a time stamp that is before or after the hour it is for. For example, the 9:00 record might come in with a time stamp of 9:00:03 or 8:59:19. This will cause the user's missing data report to flag data as missing and gaps will appear in the hourly view of data. If this record is supposed to be at the top of the hour, you can specify how before or after the start of the hour a record can come in and have it moved to the top of the hour. No revision is created in the hourly data, so there is no way to see the shift in data. The total of the time before the start of the hour and after the end of the hour cannot exceed the number of seconds specified for data resolution in the meter characteristics (3600 for hourly data, 900 for 15 minute data). If there are multiple records that meet the criteria, the first record will be flagged at the top of the hour, and the next record will be one second after (or before for time trails data). (See: [Snap Before/Snap After Details](../Meter%20Editor/Snap%20Before-Snap%20After.md)) - **FCS File** - This is the mapping file (3308, 3530, teleflow, etc) of how the Bristol is formed. - **Shared CFG** - Used only on a multitube where the CFG is shared among the two. - **Tube Number** - Used only with the Fisher to designate the appropriate meter run inside .AGA or .DET files (300, 400, 500 series). - **Entry Number** - Entry Number is used with Flow Automation Meters only. If the user leaves this blank it will automatically pick the last entry within the file. - **Option 1 & 2** - The user may need to enter data for options 1 and 2 (depending on what type of import driver is chosen).  These fields are used if different flow computers are configured to interface with FLOWCAL. See ‘Import Driver Settings’ for more information. - **Import CFX Units** - Units for fields such as volume, energy, temperature and pressure can be included in CFX files. Older CFX creation programs may not properly populate these fields. The user should Check Import CFX Units if his or her CFX files will have the valid units that the user wants FLOWCAL to import. - **Create Revisions** - When data is imported into FLOWCAL, if data has previously been imported for a date and time, data on subsequent imports will be ignored, even if the data is different. The only way to get this data in is to purge the record. If Create Revisions is checked, when new data is imported, the previous data is retained, but the new data will be saved in the next available revision. For example, if there is record at 9:00 and there was an edit done creating a revision 1 record, the next import with different data for the 9:00 record will cause the creation of a rev. 2 record with the new data. If a subsequent import has the same data as was previously imported, no additional records are created. - **Ignore Configuration Snapshot** - If Ignore Configuration Snapshot is selected, FLOWCAL will update the Meter Configuration based on events only; otherwise, the CFX configuration or transaction snap shots will be used as a check sum to compare to the database meter configuration. Any discrepancies will be updated to reflect CFX or transaction snapshot values. If yes is selected, a lost event will cause FLOWCAL to reflect the wrong value with no automated means of detection. This feature is to accommodate collection or "polling engines" who do not properly collect the "snapshot" when gathering the data.

docs.title: PPA Editor
docs.text:
Use the PPA Editor to apply a volume, energy and/or mass adjustment to a specific datetime range, contract day(s), or a contract month after meter data has been closed. Once the PPA is applied, the data will then be saved to the PPA columns within the database.

The PPA Editor can also be used to review PPAs for gas and liquid meters and create PPAs for gas meters.

To access the PPA Editor, go to Open > PPA Editor. A list of existing PPAs for a selected meter will display. You can select a range of rows and right-click to display the cumulative PPA amounts. Use the Time Filter radio buttons to narrow the PPAs displayed to a particular month range based on production month or accounting month.

If you select a list or location, you can scroll through the meters to see any PPAs.

To create a new PPA: 1. Click the **New** button.  2. Select the desired date range and meter.  3. When saving the PPA, the date range selected will be checked to verify that all the data in that time period is closed. PPAs cannot be applied to data that has not been closed. If some of the data is not closed, a warning will display and the PPA will not be saved. 4. Enter the volume and/or energy adjustment amount and an edit reason.  5. Select a month to account for the volume and/or energy.  6. Click **OK** to apply the PPA. To create a PPA in the Volume Editor: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor**. 2. Select a closed meter to be adjusted. 3. Make the necessary edits to the meter data and save. If the "Apply Immediate" [System Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/System/System%20Configuration/System%20Configuration%20-%20Approvals%20Tab.md) option is specified, a "P" will display in the left column of the Volume Editor. If the "Approval Required" option is specified, a "+/-" will display in the left column, indicating that approval is pending. A meter message is also generated, notifying specified contacts that a PPA is now pending approval. Users can view all PPAs pending approval by going to **Review** \> **Approvals**.

After a PPA is applied and the affected data has been rolled up, the results of the PPA can be viewed in several reports, such as the Volume Statement reports, and in the rollup viewers.

If the flow data on a closed meter is changed such that the original values are reverted following a previous PPA, a new PPA record is created with all values set to zero to indicate that the original values did not need to be adjusted.

docs.title: Add an Export
docs.text:
Quorum develops custom exports to extract data from FLOWCAL and output it into a text file, such as a TXT or CSV file, that can then feed other systems or be sent to other companies for import.

After a custom export has been created, you can add it to FLOWCAL and run it manually from the Exports menu or run it automatically by creating an export schedule from Report/Export Scheduling.

An export does not need to be added to FLOWCAL if you will only run it manually from the Reports > Exports menu. You will only need to add the export to FLOWCAL if it will be scheduled.

To add a custom export to FLOWCAL: 1. Copy the export file (**.dll**) into the **Export** directory under the FLOWCAL installation folder everywhere FLOWCAL is installed. 2. In FLOWCAL, go to **Reports** \> **Add Export**. The Select an Export screen will display. FLOWCAL will attempt to default to the Export folder; if this directory does not display, you will need to navigate to the Export folder located in the FLOWCAL installation folder. 1. When the Export Data Types screen displays, select whether the export is a meter or source export. Custom exports are typically meter exports. If you are not sure, contact Customer Support. 1. Click **OK**. The export will now be available from the **Reports** \> **Exports** menu or the Reports Scheduling screen.

All FLOWCAL installations include the Grade.dll, GasTextFileExchange.dll, LiquidTextFileExchange.dll, SourceAnalysisExport.dll, StndFieldInsights, StndTIPS, and CrossMonthBalance.dll exports in the Export sub-directory of the FLOWCAL installation folder. (See: Exports)

docs.title: Add a Report
docs.text:
Custom reports can be developed using Crystal Reports, either in-house or by Quorum on request. After a custom report has been created, you can add it to FLOWCAL so that it is available from the Standard Reports menu and from the Report Scheduler.

To add a custom report to FLOWCAL: 1. Go to the **Crystal** folder in the FLOWCAL installation folder. Create a folder called "Custom" if one does not already exist. 2. Copy your report (**.rpt**) file into the **Crystal\Custom** directory. 3. Repeat steps 1 and 2 everywhere FLOWCAL is installed. 4. In FLOWCAL, go to **Reports** \> **Add Report** to launch the Available Reports screen. The list of available reports will only contain reports that are in the Crystal\Custom directory and that have not been previously added to FLOWCAL. 1. Select the new report and click **OK**. The Add Reports screen will display. If the custom report uses any parameters that are not recognized by FLOWCAL, you will be prompted to specify what the parameter should be used for. If you are developing a custom report, contact Customer Support for a list or supported report parameters. 2. Select the orientation of your report (portrait or landscape). 3. Select the menu group (report category). This is where the report will be listed in the Standard Reports screen. (See: [Report Categories](Report%20Categories.md)) 4. Select the report type, or fluid phase (Gas, Liquid, or Both). This will determine which icon displays next to the report name in the Standard Reports screen. 5. Select the access scope: - **Public** – All users have access - **Admin Only** – Only users with **Report Scheduler** privileges have access - **Customize** – A user-defined combination of users/groups have access 6. Click **OK**. The report will now be available from the Standard Reports screen and the Reports Scheduling screen.

docs.title: Crystal Export Types
docs.text:
The following export formats are available for Crystal reports:

Character Separated Values (CSV)

This is a record-based export format. Each column is separated by a predefined character called delimiter in the export. If the delimiter used is comma, then it is called comma separated values or CSV. If **TAB** is used, then it is called TabSeparatedText (TTX). This export file can be opened in Excel or Notepad. This is a very popular method for exporting raw reports to Microsoft Excel users. **Example:** CommaSeparatedValues, TabSeperatedText

Crystal Reports (RPT)

This format saves reports as RPT files, which you can open in Visual Studio. The RPT file is saved with the data. This is the same as using the Save As feature with the Save Data with Report option selected.

Rich Text Format (RTF)

This export formats produces RTF files. The EditableRTF option creates files that contain only text and no drawing objects. The RichText option produces files that can contain text and drawing objects. Both files can be opened in word processing programs such as Microsoft Word. **Example:** EditableRTF, RichText

Microsoft Excel (XLSX)

This produces report in an Excel format. Each column in report corresponds to a column in Excel. The report is exported page-by-page and added to single worksheet with the same name as the report name. If the worksheet becomes full, then the Crystal report will create another worksheet and continue. If there are more columns in the report than Excel can support, the additional report columns are omitted from the export. The XLS format can only support 256 columns; the XLSX format can handle 16,384 columns. This option also exports report formulas (supported formulas are SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MIN and MAX). Three export options are available: - **Microsoft Excel (97-2003) (\*.xls)** - This XLS format corresponds to Microsoft Excel (97-2003) (\*.xls). This is a page-based export option that retains the original formatting, but lines and boxes are omitted from the report. - **Microsoft Excel (97-2003) Data-Only** - This is a record-based export type. Only the report data is exported; formatting is not included. - **Microsoft Excel Data-Only (\*.xlsx)** - This is similar to the Microsoft Excel (97-2003) Data-Only format, but it supports more columns. **Example:** Excel, ExcelRecord, ExcelWorkbook

HTML

Creates an HTML format that preserves the original report layout. Useful for mailing well formatted reports to customers. Crystal can export to in HTML 3.2 or HTML 4.0. **Example:** HTML32, HTML40

PDF

Export to PortableDocFormat (PDF) is a page-based export type. This export retains both layout and formatting options, so the exported report will display as it displayed on the Preview screen. PDFdocuments cannot be altered without specialized software, making this format useful if you want to email the report or save it for later viewing. **Example:** PortableDocFormat

Report Definition (RPTR)

This is a special Crystal-specific export format that generates a read-only version of the RPT file. The data, report definitions and database connection are exported. This file can only be opened from the Crystal Report Viewer. This protects the report from accidental modification. The report cannot be modified, and a new RPT file cannot be created from this file. This export retains connection to the database, so if the report is refreshed, this file will be updated.

Text (TXT)

This exports the report in plain text. This option does not retain any formatting information.

Microsoft Word

This option exports the report in Microsoft Word format. The text and drawing objects of the original report are retained. **Example:** WordForWindows

XML

This option exports the report in an XML format. This uses the SAP Crystal Reports XML schema for the export. This option is usually used for data exchange.

The following options are available on the Edit menu on the Standard Reports screen:

  • Description - Quickly identify the report’s purpose, or add a description to a custom report. You can also edit the description by right-clicking a report.

docs.title: Email a Report
docs.text: To email a report:  1.  Select one or more reports and the data to display.  2.  Click the **Email** button.  3.  Click the **To:** button to select a recipient.      If you are emailing multiple reports, a separate email will be generated for each report.  4.  Select the file format to export the report to, such as PDF. (See: [Crystal Export Types](Crystal%20Export%20Types.md))  5.  Enter a subject and a message.  6.  Check the **Compress Report Files** option to compress the files into a .zip file before emailing them.  7.  Click **OK**.

docs.title: Export Template Editor
docs.text:
You must have Can Create, Can Delete, or Can Edit privileges for the FLOWCAL Options Application Process to create, delete, or modify templates, respectively. Users who do not have these privileges will still be able to access this screen and view the export templates.

Use the Export Template Editor to view, create, modify, and delete text file export templates. The standard GasTextFileExchange export format is available as a standard template called “GasTextFileExchange”.

To access the Export Template Editor: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Exports**. 2. Select the **GasTextFileExchange.dll** export. 3. Click the browse button next to the **Export Template** field.

Creating an Export Template

To create an export template: 1. Click the **New** button to create a new template, or click the **Copy** button to copy an existing template. 2. Select an export template in the Select Template to Copy dialog. 3. Enter a name for the export template in the **Export Template** field. 4. Continue to step 2 of Modifying an Export Template below to complete the template setup.

Modifying an Export Template

To make changes to an export template: 1. Select an existing user-created template in the Export Template drop-down and click the **Edit** button. 2. Choose a delimiter: - **Tab** - A tab (→) is used as a separator between export values. - **Comma** - A comma (,) is used as a separator between export values. - **Space** - A single space ( ) is used as a separator between export values. - **Pipe** - A pipe (\|) is used as a separator between export values. - **Other** - Specify a single character to be used as a separator between export values. 3. Select a print option: - **Print Headers** - If this option is enabled, the field names are included in the first row of the export file. - **Enclosure Character** - Check this option and enter a single character to be included on both sides of each export value. Example If the Atmospheric Pressure value is 14.696 and the enclosure character is a double quote (“), “14.696” is used for the field in the export file. 4. Select fields to be included or excluded in the export file by clicking and highlighting a field in the Available Fields list or the Selected Fields list and using the left and right arrow buttons to select or deselect fields. Double-clicking a field also moves the field between lists. 5. Set the order of the selected fields. Fields are included in a export data line in the order listed in the Selected Fields list (listed from top to bottom). Highlight a field and use the up and down arrow buttons located to the right of the Selected Fields list to reorder the fields. 6. For fields in the Selected Fields list, right-click a field to display the Set Field Print Options menu. 7. Click the Set Field Print Options menu item to open the Field Print Options dialog. - **Database Value** - The value stored in the database for the selected field will be printed. - **Blank Field** - "Blank" will be printed for the selected field. - **Constant Value** - A user-specified string of up to 250 characters will be printed for the selected field. 8. Click **OK** and close the dialog. The print option will display for the selected field in the Selected Fields list under the Value column.

Viewing Associated Export Schedules

To view an existing export template: 1. Select the template in the **Export Template** drop-down. 2. Click the **Associated Schedules** button next to the Export Template drop-down to see all export schedules that currently use the selected template.

Deleting an Export Template

To delete an existing export template: Click the **Delete** button while viewing the template. You cannot delete the template if it is currently used in an export group or scheduled export. Before the template can be deleted, the template must be removed from the export group and the schedule, or the export group and the schedule must be deleted.

docs.title: Export a Report
docs.text: To export a report:  1.  Select one or more reports and the data to display.  2.  Click the **Export** button.  3.  Specify a directory where the reports will be saved.      Remember that this is the path relative to the computer FLOWCAL has been executed from. If you want a report written to the D:\\ drive on your local computer, browse to the D:\\ drive on your computer; otherwise, the Reports service will write the file to its own D:\\ drive. For report schedules, this path will be relative to the computer where the Reports service is running.  4.  Select the file format to export the report to, such as PDF. (See: [Crystal Export Types](Crystal%20Export%20Types.md) )  5.  If applicable, select options for the output file name. You can define text to append or prepend to the file name, or use one of the following variables:      - **%RUNDATE%** - The time stamp for the export using a MM-DD-YY HH-MM-SS (24-hour) format      >      >     > **For example:** If the run date is August 2, 2017, at 3:07:08 pm, the variable will translate to "08-02-17 15-07-08".     >     >       - **%SCHEDNAME%** - The name of the schedule     - **%RPTMONTH%** - The name of the reporting month  6.  Select an output file configuration option. By default, FLOWCAL creates one file for meter reports.     - **Output Common File** (default) – Export one file for the selected meter(s)     - **Output Individual File per Meter** – Export a separate file for each meter     - **Output Individual File into Meter Directory** – Export a separate file and directory for each meter  7.  Click **OK**.

docs.title: Exports
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires System Process - Meter Edit - Can View and System Process - RptScheduler - Can View privileges.

Use the Available Exports screen to select an export. Exports are used to extract data from FLOWCAL so that it can then be imported into other applications or sent to other recipients.

To access any of the exports available in FLOWCAL: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Exports**. 2. Select the desired export option.

Export Parameters

The following parameters are commonly found in standard and custom exports:

  • Object Selection - The object type and object number to be exported.

  • Resolution - The data resolution for the export. Options are: Hourly, Daily, and Monthly.

  • Data Level - The type of object data to export. Options are: Meter Data or Location Data.

This option is only enabled for the Location, List, and Close Group option types.

  • Conditions (formerly labeled "Volume/Energy) - The pressure base, temperature base, and saturation conditions to be exported. Options are: Measured or Standard.

  • Decimals - The precision to which gas volume and energy values will be displayed (0 to 3 decimal places).

  • Date Range - The date range for the export. Options are: Contract Month, Contract Day(s), and Date/Time Range. The First and Last fields are inclusive for any date range selected. Example If January 2017 is selected as the first month and December 2017 as the last month, the resulting export will contain data from the beginning of January 2017 through the end of December 2017. To run the export for one month’s worth of data, select the month as the first month and the last month.

  • Output File - The directory and file name for the output. Use browse button next to the Directory Name field to find an existing directory. Enter a name for the output file in the File Name field. These items are required for the export to run.

docs.title: Standard Exports
docs.text:
The following exports come standard with every FLOWCAL shipment (additional exports may be available if you have custom exports installed):

GasTextFileExchange

GasTextFileExchange exports gas meter data into a FLOWCAL-standard text file format. These files can be used to exchange data between two separate companies and are easily imported into any FLOWCAL system. ### Export Options - **Export Template** - Defaulted to the standard GasTextFileExchange template. Export templates can be created to define custom export file formats. When you create a template, you will be able to select it from the drop-down menu and use it to run the export. Click the **Browse** button next to the drop-down menu to open the Export Template Editor and view, create, edit, or delete templates. (See: [Export Template Editor](Export%20Template%20Editor.md)) - **Enforce Time Trails Time Stamps** - This option is only available for exports configured with daily resolution. The effective date and effective end date are printed differently for each record depending on this option and the data span of the meter. > > > > Data Span > Option Enabled > Option Disabled > > > > > Time Leads Data >

Effective Date

>

Effective End Date

>

Effective Date

>

Effective End Date

> > > Time Trails Data >

Effective Date

>

Effective End Date

>

Effective Date minus one Data Resolution

>

Effective End minus one Data Resolution

> > > > >   > > > > Example > > > > A gas meter has a time trails data span, an hourly data resolution, and a contract hour of 9. At the daily resolution, this meter would have records that start and end at 10:00:00 (e.g., the contract day 3/3/2018 would start on 3/3/2018 10:00:00 and end on 3/4/ 2018 10:00:00). > > With the Enforce Time Trails Time Stamps option enabled, the contract day 3/3/2018 would be exported with an effective date of 3/3/2018 10:00:00 and an effective end date of 3/4/2018 10:00:00. > > With the Enforce Time Trails Time Stamps option disabled, the contract day 3/3/2018 would be exported with an effective date of 3/3/2018 9:00:00 and an effective end date of 3/4/2018 9:00:00. > > > >

LiquidTextFileExchange

The LiquidTextFileExchange export exports liquid meter data to a FLOWCAL liquid meter text file. The resulting file is suitable for importing into other FLOWCAL systems. ### Export Options - **Resolution** - The data output resolution. Options are: Hourly, Daily, Monthly, and Batch. - **Conditions** - Data output units. Choices are Measured and System. Measured units are determined per meter and may differ from meter to meter. System units are determined at the system level and are consistent for all meters in that system. ### Output Data #### Hourly, Daily, Monthly Resolution - All “Liquid Meter Periodic” fields are exported except for the following: - Liquids: IV Index Start\* - Liquids: IV Index End\* - Liquids: GSV Index Start\* - Liquids: GSV Index End\* - Liquids: Mass Index Start\* - Liquids: Mass Index End\* - Liquids: NSV Index Start\* - Liquids: NSV Index End\* - Liquids: S&W Index Start\* - Liquids: S&W Index End\* - Liquids: Pulse Index Start Liquids: Orifice Extension\* - Liquids: Pulse Index End Liquids: Orifice C Prime\* - Coriolis Drive Gain\*\* - C Prime\*\* - Liquids: Observed Density in Relative Density\*\*\* - Liquids: Observed Density in API Degrees\*\*\* \* Index readings are not exported because index differences may not tie to the corresponding quantity and could cause exceptions on import. Index readings are not maintained and represent "original" data while the quantities may have been edited or recalculated at some point. \*\* The periodic column is not rolled up and, therefore, cannot be exported with Hourly, Daily or Monthly data. \*\*\* These observed density fields are used in very specific and non-typical situations. They act as an original data import directive and are not meaningful in an export record. - All products that flowed within the time span will be exported and each record will have the same effective date. For example: While exporting monthly resolution, if product A flowed for the first half of the month and product B flowed for the second half of the month, a monthly record for each product will be exported with an effective date of the 1st of the month. The product “Total Fluid” is not exported. #### Batch Resolution - All “Liquid Meter Batch” fields are exported except for the following: - Batch: IV Index Start\* - Batch: IV Index End\* - Batch: GSV Index Start\* - Batch: GSV Index End\* - Batch: Mass Index Start\* - Batch: Mass Index End\* - Batch: NSV Index Start\* - Batch: NSV Index End\* - Batch: S&W Index Start\* - Batch: S&W Index End\* - Batch: Pulse Index Start Batch: Orifice Extension\* - Batch: Pulse Index End Batch: Orifice C Prime\* - Batch: Observed Density in Relative Density\*\* - Batch: Observed Density in API Degrees\*\* \* Index readings are not exported because index differences may not tie to the corresponding quantity and could cause exceptions on import. Index readings are not maintained and represent "original" data while the quantities may have been edited or recalculated at some point. \*\* These observed density fields are used in very specific and non-typical situations. They act as an original data import directive and are not meaningful in an export record. #### Products - Products in the exporting database should already exist in the target import database. The Create Products option (see: [FLOWCAL Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md)) can be enabled to create a minimal product in the target. However, the export does not contain any product definition other than the product code.

Standard TIPS

The Standard TIPS export (StndTIPS.dll) generates two comma-delimited text files (.csv)—one for volumetric data and one for analysis data—that can be imported into TIPS. This export is intended for use with gas data. ### Export Options The TIPS export uses the standard FLOWCAL export parameters and an option to include auto estimated data: - Export Data For - Object selector - All Meters - Close Group - List - Location - Meter - Include Auto Estimated Data - This option is de-selected by default - Resolution - Daily - Only applies to volumetric data - Monthly - Volume/Energy - Measured - Standard - Date Range - Contract Month - Contract Day(s) - Available only when the resolution is set to "Daily" - Output File - Directory Name - File Name - The text specified by the user in this field will be appended with the resolution, data type, and the first exported month/day ### Standard TIPS Export Flags See: [Report/Export Scheduling > Schedule Editor Details](Report%20Scheduler/Scheduling.md) ### Export Function - Analysis data is always monthly. - If multiple meters are exported, records are first sorted by meter number alphanumerically, then by effective date. - Column headers are not printed in the output files. - See the Standard TIPS Export spreadsheet for details about exported values.

Standard Field Insights

The standard Field Insights export (StndFieldInsights.dll) generates Excel files containing metered volumes, pressure and readings, and monthly production data that can be imported into Field Insights. This export is intended to be used for gas and liquid data. - **Metered Volumes** – Daily metered volume. Only new and changed records within the selected date range are exported - **Pressure & Readings** – Daily metering pressure, hardcoded as “LINE” pressure - **Monthly Production** – Monthly metered volume. Volume will be month-to-date in the current month ### Configuration In order to be included in the Field Insights exports, meters need to be configured as “Gas”, “NGL”, “Oil” or “Condensate” meter. See the PDF documentation for details. ### Export Options The Field Insights export uses the standard FLOWCAL export parameters, as well as the following: - **Data Output** - All Three - Daily Pressure - Daily Volume - Monthly - **Data to Export** – This selection applies only to the daily metered volume output file. The option determines which records are exported for the selected meter and date range. - **All Data** – All records are ecported, regardless of whether it has exported before or changed from the original data. - **Current Volume Different from Original** – Only those records that have the current gas volume that is differenet from the original (imported) gas volume are exported. - **New and Changed Records** (default selection) – Only those records that have been added or edited since the last Field Insights export of the selected meter month are exported. The Field Insights export updates the FC_FFMTR_DAILY_EXTERNAL_PROCESS_FLAG_0 value to “Y” on exported records to track exported records for the "New and Changed Records" option. - **Directory Name** – The desired location for output files. Export file names are formatted as follows: - FI_Monthly_Volume\_\.xlsx - FI_Daily_Metered_Volume\_\.xlsx - FI_Daily_Pressure\_\.xlsx Because the output file names are predetermined, the Prepend Text, Append Text, and Overwrite values will be ignored when setting up export files for a scheduled export; however, the directory field must include a file name. Any file name can be entered, but the path itself must reflect the desired output location. ### Export Flags See: [StndFieldInsights Export Flags](Report%20Scheduler/Scheduling.md#StndFieldExportFlags)

Grade

The Gas Revenue Accounting Data Exchange (Grade) is an API-standard file format.

SourceAnalysisExport

SourceAnalysisExport exports gas or liquid quality data and standalone sample data into a FLOWCAL-standard text file format. These files can be used to exchange data between two separate companies and are easily imported into any FLOWCAL system. ### Export Options - **Process Standalone Sample Analyses within Date Range** – If this option is enabled, the export will include standalone sample analyses (Open \> Sample Analyses) within the specified date range. - **Export Last Record Only** – If this option is enabled, only the last record from the selected quality source will be exported. When it is not enabled, all analysis records for the selected time frame will be exported. This option applies only to quality source data; standalone sample analyses will always be filtered by the specified date range.

CrossMonthBalance

CrossMonthBalance exports monthly gas and liquid volume, energy, and mass values for a balance location. In addition to totals for each data point, it also exports subtotals by direction and class calculated by Location Rollups. ### Export Options - **Export Data For** – CrossMonthBalance is a location-level export. When run for a location, it will export data for the selected location. When run for a close group or a list, it will export data for each immediate member location; however, it will not process data for sub-locations of those locations. - **Volume/Energy** – Units for each data point will be printed in the column headings in the first row of the export file. If you select "Measured", units from the reference meter of the location are displayed, and values in measured conditions will be exported. If you select "Standard", units from the system the location belongs to are displayed, and values in system conditions will be exported. - **Decimals** – The precision to which gas volume and energy values are displayed. Mass, GSV, NSV, summed volume, and total net allowable will be displayed per discrimination specified on the first product for the location. If the location has no liquid data and there is no product on the location, these values will display with the number of decimals selected. - **Month Range** – The range of months if the export is being run for multiple months (first and last month selections are inclusive). For example: If you select January 2017 as the first month and December 2017 as the last month, the resulting export will contain data from the beginning of January 2017 through the end of December 2017. - **Output File** – Click the browse button next to the **Directory Name** field to specify a directory for the output file. Enter a name for the file in the **File Name** field. These items must be provided for the export to run. ### Output CrossMonthBalance generates a CSV file that can be viewed using Excel. Once opened in Excel, you can sort and filter the data as needed.

The following options are available on the File menu on the Standard Reports screen:

  • Export - Open the Choose an Export File Directory screen to specify a network path, file format, and other output options. (See: Export a Report)

docs.title: Report Access
docs.text:
Use the Report Access screen to grant access permissions to specified users or a designated group of users for individual reports or report categories.

If TESTit 3 Integrated is enabled, the TESTit category and reports will not display; these items will only be available from the TESTit application.

To grant/restrict access to reports: 1. Go to **Report** \> **Access** on the Standard Reports menu or right-click a report or category. 2. Select **Reports** or **Categories** to show the applicable list of objects. 3. Select the report or category and click **Edit**. 4. Select a scope: - **Public** – All users have access. - **Admin Only** – Users with **Report Scheduler** privileges have access. - **Customize** – A specified combination of users/groups have access. 5. Click **Save**.

docs.title: Report Categories
docs.text:
Report categories are used to create groupings of reports that will be available in the Standard Reports screen. User or group access to these categories can then be granted/restricted from the Reports Access screen.

If TESTit 3 Integrated is enabled, the TESTit category and reports will not display; these items will only be available from the TESTit application.

To create a report category: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Standard Reports**. 2. Select **Report** \> **Category** from the Standard Reports menu. Each report is labeled as "L" (liquid), "G" (gas), or "B" (both). 3. In the Report Categories screen, go to **File** \> **New** or right-click the empty space and select **New**. 4. Enter a name for the category. 5. Drag and drop one or more reports from the Available Reports list to the new category. 6. Go to **File** \> **Save** or right-click the empty space and select **Save**. The category with the associated reports will now be available from the Standard Reports screen.

docs.title: Report Display Options
Displaying Company and Customer Identification Data on Standard Reports
docs.text:
Depending on user settings, a company logo, customer name, or company name will display in the top right corner of each FLOWCAL standard report. These elements will display in the following precedence:

  • If a valid logo image path is provided in the Rollup Configuration settings, the logo image displays; or
  • For meter-level reports, if the Print Customer Name option on the Meter Editor Reports tab is set to Yes, the customer specified for the meter on the Meter Editor General tab displays; or
  • The company name specified in the System Factors settings for the selected system in the report run displays.

docs.title: Standard Reports
docs.text:
This function requires Report Scheduler privileges.

FLOWCAL provides several built-in reports created using Crystal Reports 2016. The Standard Reports screen allows you to view, print, and export data for various reports. These reports are grouped by category (e.g., Meter/Location, Source, Editor, TESTit, BLM) and display with an icon to indicate whether the report is for a gas or liquid meter, or both.

If TESTit 3 Integrated is enabled, the TESTit category and reports will not display in the Standard Reports screen; they will only be available from the TESTit application. The TESTit report category only applies to TESTit 2 Integrated.

To access the Standard Reports screen: Go to **Reports** \> **Standard Reports**.

Run a Report

To run a report from the Standard Reports screen: 1. Expand a category heading in the Report Selection menu. 2. Click a report name to select a single report, or click the checkboxes next to multiple report names to select more than one report. 3. Use the available options on the right side of the screen to select the report data you want to display. These configuration options will vary for each report. The more reports you select, the more fields will be available. 4. Click **Preview**, **Print**, **Export** or **Email** to configure the report output. The **Email** button will only be enabled if you have licensed the Scheduled Reporting module. Tip - Remember UI Filter Values If the **Remember UI Filter Values** option is enabled (see: [User Preferences](../Settings%20Manager/User%20Settings/User%20Preferences.md)), the Standard Reports screen will retain the following filter and date settings for the duration of the FLOWCAL session: - Object type (Meter, Location, List, or Close Group); object number or name (e.g., meter number) will not be retained - Date range type and selection - Report list selection, level, resolution, volume/energy, revision, and number of decimals When multiple Standard Reports screens are open, the filter and date settings from the last Standard Reports screen closed will be retained. The filter settings are cleared when you log out or close FLOWCAL.

Function Buttons

The following report functions are available on the Standard Reports screen: - **Preview** - Open the Report Viewer to view the results of your report selections and export or print reports. If you have selected multiple reports, each report will display on a separate tab. - **Print** - Select a printer and print options for the report. - **Export** - Open the Choose an Export File Directory screen to specify a network path, file format, and other output options. (See: [Export a Report](Export%20a%20Report.md)) - **E-mail** - Open the Email Reports screen and configure email and recipient options. (See: [Email a Report](Email%20a%20Report.md)) - **Exit** - Close the Standard Reports screen.

Right-Click Options

The following report functions are available in the right-click menu: - **Description** - Quickly identify the report’s purpose, or add a description to a custom report. You can also edit the description by going to **Edit** \> **Description**. - **Add** - Open the Available Reports screen to install custom reports found in the **Crystal\Custom** directory of the FLOWCAL installation folder. If you want to create a custom report, you will need to purchase a Crystal Reports Developer license. A Crystal license is not required if you are only running reports. - **Refresh** - Update the list of categories and reports. - **Category Access** - Open the Category Access screen to grant/restrict access to categories. (See: [Report Access](Report%20Access.md)) - **Report Access** - Open the Report Access screen to grant/restrict access to reports. (See: [Report Access](Report%20Access.md))

docs.title: Stored Reports
docs.text:
For archival purposes, FLOWCAL can store reports that have previously been generated. This is useful for keeping a record of reports associated with a monthly close. The stored report includes data about who created the stored report, the date and time, the associated close group and measurement month, comments, and one or more files.

Files of any type can be stored with a report; however, because the files are stored in the database, users need to be cautious of file size.

Stored reports may be edited or deleted until the associated close group and month is closed. After the close, the reports are locked for audit purposes.

A close group is not required, but without it, editing or deleting a stored report will not be restricted by the close process.

To create a stored report: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Stored Reports** from the main menu or from the Standard Reports menu. 2. Go to **Store** \> **New**. 3. Enter a name for the stored report and assign a close group. 4. Select a month and year with which the stored report is associated. 5. Go to **File** \> **Add** to add files to the stored report. 6. Enter additional comments as needed. 7. Click **Store**. Export all of the stored report files to a local or network directory by going to **File** \> **Export All** while in view mode.

BLM Audit Package Cover Page

A cover page report for the [BLM Audit Package](../../BLM/BLM%20Compliance.md#AuditPackage) that displays information of each meter and, if applicable, BLM property details. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor: - Print Customer Name - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - Print Measurement Area Schedule Editor Group Name: - BLM Audit Package Cover Page - BLM Audit Package View Sample Reports: - BLM Audit Package Cover Page - BLM Audit Package Cover Page - Non-BLM - BLM Audit Package Cover Page - Non-BLM With ME Options

BLM FMP Tier

Reports whether AO Tier Variance has been granted for a meter, its Current and Calculated FMP tier, calculated its average daily volume, and any errors FLOWCAL generates for calculation. This report is valid for gas meters that are designated as BLM property. This report enables user to review FMP tier information for multiple meters at once. Data used in this report is available on the [BLM tab of the Meter Editor](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/BLM%20Tab.md). If the meter is designated as a BLM property and hence has BLM identification fields provided in the Meter Editor BLM tab, BLM identification field values are displayed in the top right of the report. Schedule Editor Group Name: BLM FMP Tier View Sample Report

BLM Gas Volume Statement

Displays the hourly meter flow data for a month or day range, and daily meter flow data for a month range, per BLM specifications, with additional precision and extension. If the meter is designated as a BLM property and hence has BLM identification fields provided in the Meter Editor BLM tab, BLM identification field values are displayed at the top of the report, between the report header and the company logo. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Edit Reasons - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - Print Volume at Optional Pressure Base - Print Measurement Area Schedule Editor Group Name: - BLM Gas Volume Statement - Daily - BLM Gas Volume Statement - Hourly View Sample Reports: - BLM Gas Volume Statement - Daily, with BLM ID Fields - BLM Gas Volume Statement - Hourly - BLM Gas Volume Statement - Original Revision

BLM Heating Value Uncertainty

This report compiles heating value variability and heating value uncertainty for all FMP tiers. This report is valid only for gas meters designated as BLM property. FMP Number is set in the Meter Editor BLM tab. [Exceptions 9021 - 9024](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/9000/9000-9999.md) will be generated for meters with a heating value uncertainty that exceeds the specified threshold or that has not been calculated. These meters will display with "\<\<\<". For additional information, see: [Heating Value Uncertainty Details](../../BLM/Heating%20Value%20Uncertainty%20Details.md) Scheduling Group Name: BLM Heating Value Uncertainty View Sample Report

BLM Heating Value Uncertainty Exceptions

This report compiles exceptions for meters whose heating value uncertainties lie outside of their acceptable heating value uncertainty limits at the specified datetime. Meters for which heating value uncertainty at the specified datetime could not be calculated are also reported. This report is valid only for gas meters that are designated as BLM property, and only those meters with unacceptable heating value uncertainty levels and have heating value uncertainty exceptions generated are displayed. Average Analysis

Displays a weighted average of meter analysis data for a selected time frame, calculated by product or total fluid. Raw Data Count at the top right corner of the report indicates the number of final form daily records that were retrieved as the basis of average calculation according to the selected meter or location, time frame, and product. This report is available as a standard report for FLOWCAL 8.10.50.4 and 8.11.35, or above. For component mole %, mass %, and liquid volume % average calculation, if a field is null for one or more records, but not all records, the value for the record is considered to be 0, not null. However, if a field is null for all records used for calculation, the average is null and is displayed as blank. > > > Example > > > > - If Propane mole % is not measured for one out of 5 days, and there are four records with non-null mole % values and one record with null as mole %, the record with null value is considered to have 0% for propane for average calculation. > - If Decane mole % was not measured for any of the five days and all five records have null for Decane mole %, then the report will display blank for Decane mole %. > > > > If the weight value per the weighted averaging method is null or 0 for all retrieved records, then the simple average is reported instead. > > > Example > > > > If the Rel. Density field on the System Rollup Configuration form is set to “Time Weighted, Linear,” but the flow time on the retrieved records are null, Absolute Density, Relative Density, and Stock Tank Density values will be simple-averaged, instead of weight-averaged. > > The following applies to the meter version of the report only: > > - Weighted averages for various analysis properties such as Absolute Density, Relative Density, Molar Mass, Volume Ratio, Sediment and Water %,  Shrink Factor, etc. are calculated and displayed on the right side of the report. > - The averaging method for Absolute Density, Relative Density, and Stock Tank Density will depend on the Rel. Density field value on the System Rollup Configuration form (Admin \> System Options \> Rollup Configuration \> Gas Avg.). The averaging method for Molar Mass, Volume Ratio, S&W %, Shrinkage Factor, and Stock Tank S&W % will depend on the Analysis field value. > - For the Cn+ Fraction column of the Property table, the weighted averages will not be an accurate representation of the data if the retrieved records have mixed Cn+ Fractions, e.g. some records with C6+ and others with C7+. > > > > Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Customer Name - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - Print Measurement Area Schedule Editor Group Name: - Average Analysis (By Product) - Average Analysis (By Total Fluid) View Sample Reports: - Average Analysis (By Product) - Average Analysis (By Total Fluid)

Displays gas volume and energy for members of a balance location, grouped by meter direction, meter class, or both. Also displays tickets associated with the balance location according to the ticket direction and ticket class, grouped into ticket types. Meter volume and energy displayed are for the meter’s full gas month. If the meter is part of the balance location hierarchy only for a part of the reported month, the report displays the full-month quantity. For accurate accounting with regards to the time of relationship, use the Balance Detail (Calc) report. - **Meter Direction Not Set** - Members with no direction set are displayed in a separate group with the label \. - **Inventory Data** - If an inventory location such as a gas inventory, a tank, or a cavern is included in the balance location, any ticket or meter data associated with the inventory does not appear under their directions. Instead, change in the inventory amount held over the reported month in the inventory itself is displayed in a group labeled Change in Inventory. At a minimum, the Subtotal By Meter Direction option (Admin \> FLOWCAL Options \> FLOWCAL Configuration) needs to be checked when rolling up balance locations for the report to display the subtotal values associated with each meter direction. If both Subtotal By options are disabled, the subtotal values will not be calculated by the location rollups and the report will not report any subtotal values. This report displays component data for tickets of all ticket types in a location for a given time frame. Tickets are sorted by effective date and ticket number. At the end of all tickets, the totals of quantities for all movement tickets are calculated and displayed. Users must select whether they want to see components reported to C5+, C6+, or C10 for the report to run. Users must also select if they want to see liquid volume, mass or net allowable components. The report can be run for measured or standard conditions and by product or total fluid. If displayed tickets have sediment and water data, the report will display gross standard volume, sediment and water percentage, and sediment and water volume. EFM Data Reconciliation

The purpose of this report is to show changes in gas volume values due to edits. The report compares original volume to current volume and displays meters for which the difference between the original and current volumes exceeds the Max Edit Difference specified by the user. The Max Edit Difference value can be specified either as unit difference or percent difference. To indicate a percent difference, enter a % sign at the end of the value in the field. - **EFM Volume** - The original (revision 0) volume. - **Adjusted Volume** - The current volume on the meter as it appears within the Volume Editor. - **Volume Diff** - - For orifice meters, in order to only see volumes due to edits besides GQ apply, the effects of relative density changes resulting from a source apply are backed out. The Volume Diff value displayed on the report is calculated as the difference between the original volume and the volume that is calculated after backing out the specific gravity. The calculation for the volume used in the comparison to the original volume is: Current Volume \* Ö(current relative density/original relative density) - For all other meter types, this value is calculated as the difference between the Adjusted Volume and EFM Volume values. - **Volume % Diff** - Calculated as: (Volume Diff / EFM Volume) \* 100 Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: EFM Data Reconciliation View Sample Report

Only meters with a monthly average differential pressure less than 10 and a plate diameter of at least 0.5 will be displayed. - **Avg DP:** Average differential pressure from the monthly final form meter table - **DP Range:** High differential pressure transducer limit - **Pressure:** Average static pressure for gas meters and average meter static pressure from the monthly final form meter table - **Plate Size:** Current plate (orifice) diameter as of the end of the selected measurement month - **Tube Size:** Current tube (pipe) diameter as of the end of the selected measurement month - **Beta Ratio:** Beta ratio is calculated as plate size / tube size. - **Volume for Month:** Monthly total of volume for gas meters and gross standard volume for liquid meters - **Flow Time %:** Monthly total actual flow time as % of the complete month flow time Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: Plate Change Notification View Sample Report

Plate Change Summary

Displays all plate changes for a given meter during a selected time frame. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: Plate Change Summary View Sample Report

PPA Approvals by Acct Month

Displays the pending, rejected, or approved PPA edit approvals, sorted by PPA accounting month. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name View Sample Report

PPA Approvals by Prod Month

Displays pending, rejected, or approved PPA edit approvals, sorted by the data production month. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name View Sample Report

PPA Changes by GMS Date

Displays closed, adjusted total, and adjustment amounts for the hours to which prior period adjustments were applied, for the PPAs made during the selected time frame. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: PPA Changes by GMS Date View Sample Report

PPA Changes by Prod Month

Displays closed, adjusted total, and adjustment amounts for the months to which that prior period adjustments applied. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: PPA Changes by Prod Month View Sample Report

PPA Detail By Acct Month

Displays volume and energy adjustment amounts for gas, and GSV, NSV, mass, summed volume, and total net allowable adjustment amounts for liquids, for each PPA of a given accounting month. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Customer Name - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - Print Measurement Area Schedule Editor Group Name:  - PPA Detail By Acct Month (Gas) - PPA Detail By Acct Month (Liquid) - PPA Detail By Acct Month (Ticket) View Sample Report: - PPA Detail By Acct Month (Gas) - PPA Detail By Acct Month (Liquid) - PPA Detail By Acct Month (Ticket)

PPA Detail By Prod Month

Displays volume and energy adjustment amounts for gas, and GSV, NSV, mass, summed volume, and total net allowable adjustment amounts for liquids, for each PPA of a given production month. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Customer Name - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - Print Measurement Area Schedule Editor Group Name: - PPA Detail By Prod Month (Gas) - PPA Detail By Prod Month (Liquid) - PPA Detail By Prod Month (Ticket) View Sample Report: - PPA Detail By Prod Month (Gas) - PPA Detail By Prod Month (Liquid) - PPA Detail By Prod Month (Ticket)

PPA Summary By Acct Month

Displays a summary of PPAs, sorted by accounting month. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: PPA Summary by Acct Month View Sample Report

PPA Summary By Prod Month

Displays the summary of PPAs by the Production Month of the data. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: PPA Summary by Prod Month View Sample Report

Process Variable Limit Check

Displays days that are out of range according to the temporary user-defined validation set points. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: Process Variable Limit Check View Sample Report

Quick Compare Meter Daily

Displays a side-by-side daily comparison of volume and energy for two meters. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name View Sample Report

Significant Flow Change

Compares volume and energy values from the selected month to those of the previous month, and displays meters for which the change in volume or energy exceeds the value in the Max Monthly Change field specified by the user. The Max Monthly Change value can be specified either as unit difference or percent difference. To indicate a percent difference, enter a % sign at the end of the value in the field. The percent difference is always displayed with two decimal places. It uses the selected month as the denominator. The Max Monthly Change can be the difference (e.g., 20.0) or the percent difference (e.g., 2.0%) Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name Schedule Editor Group Name: Significant Flow Change View Sample Report

Station Location Verification

Compares the daily or monthly totals for each station location member of a list or location to the sums of all meter and/or ticket member data, displaying any discrepancies. The comparison is performed on volume, energy, and mass (for gas), or GSV, NSV, mass, and summed volume (for liquids). The report assumes that there are no date/time splits on the station location and that multipliers of 1 are specified for all meter members. Schedule Editor Group Name: - Station Location Verification (Gas) - Daily - Station Location Verification (Gas) - Monthly - Station Location Verification (Liquid) - Daily - Station Location Verification (Liquid) - Monthly View Sample Report: - Station Location Verification (Gas) - Monthly - Station Location Verification (Gas) - Daily - Station Location Verification (Liquid) - Monthly - Station Location Verification (Liquid) - Daily

Tank Empty Summary

Displays GSV, NSV, mass, summed volume and total net allowable, the gain/loss amount and percent since the last tank empty for an empty ticket, and a breakdown of component mass, component volume, and component net allowable for the same time frame. Gauge Receipts accounts for changes in tank inventory where a gauge shows an increase in volume that is not accounted for by a meter or ticket receipt. Gauge Deliveries accounts for changes in tank inventory where a gauge shows a decrease in volume that is not accounted for by a meter or ticket delivery. Schedule Editor Group Name: Tank Empty (Summary) View Sample Report

Tank Inventory

Displays daily GSV, NSV, and mass inventory data, grouped by product or total fluid for tank locations. Schedule Editor Group Name: - Tank Inventory (By Product) - Tank Inventory (By Total Fluid) View Sample Report: - Tank Inventory (By Product) - Tank Inventory (By Total Fluid)

Tank Run Summary

Displays all tank run tickets for a time frame, including the tank, ticket date, ticket number, transporter, TOV, GSV, NSV, SWV and observed density. Schedule Editor Group Name: Tank Run Summary View Sample Report

Test Report Summary

Displays test reports on a per-meter basis, including report status, from and to dates for the test report apply, the apply criteria, and related messages. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name View Sample Report

Theoretical Volume Statement

Displays daily or hourly flow data for liquid meters, including meter configuration and analysis for the last flow record, as well as theoretical production and shrink factor values. When running by product, each product will be displayed on a different page. Available Configuration Options in the Meter Editor: - Print Customer Name - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - Print Measurement Area Schedule Editor Group Names: - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Product) - Hourly - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Product) - Daily - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Total Fluid) - Hourly - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Total Fluid) - Daily View Sample Report: - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Product) - Hourly (No S&W; Has Analysis) - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Product) - Daily (No S&W; Has Analysis) - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Total Fluid) - Hourly (S&W) - Theoretical Volume Statement (By Total Fluid) - Daily (S&W)

Ticket Detail

This report displays detailed ticket data, including measurement data, accounting information, and component quantities, for all applicable ticket types in the selected location for a given time frame. Each ticket will be displayed on a different page. When this report is run for a ticket attached to a location or a tank that is set up as a BLM property, the report will display the FMP number, lease number, CA number, and PA number. Schedule Editor Group Name: Ticket Detail View Sample Report: Ticket Detail - Tank

Ticket Detail Allowables

This report displays detailed ticket data, including measurement data, accounting information, and net allowable quantities, for all applicable ticket types in the selected location for a given time frame. Each ticket will be displayed on a different page. When this report is run for a ticket attached to a location or a tank that is set up as a BLM property, the report will display the FMP number, lease number, CA number, and PA number. When the report is run for a ticket using US Customary units, the component volumes and net allowables values are reported in gallons, regardless of the component volume units on the ticket. The Component section contains: - All component data available for the ticket, up to the highest component. - Alkenes and neopentane if the "Show Alkenes" and "Show Neo-Pentane" options are enabled for the ticket. - Component mass data for meter tickets using the mass-based calculation method. In this case, the report displays density values for each component pulled from the HC Properties data. To determine the Density values on the report, FLOWCAL first looks at the source to determine which HC properties values to display, then the system-level HC properties. Schedule Editor Group Name: Ticket Detail Allowables View Sample Report: Ticket Detail Allowables - Location

Ticket Volume Statement

This report displays flow data for tickets of all ticket types in a location for a given time frame. Tickets are sorted by effective date and ticket number. At the end of all tickets, the totals of quantities for all movement tickets are calculated and displayed. If displayed tickets have sediment and water data, the report will display gross standard volume, sediment and water percentage, and sediment and water volume. If displayed tickets do not have any sediment and water percentage or sediment and water volume, the report will display additional component quantities such as summed volume and total net allowable. Schedule Editor Group Name: - Ticket Volume Statement (By Product) - Ticket Volume Statement (By Total Fluid) View Sample Reports: - Ticket Volume Statement - By Product (Rail Car, Without Sediment and Water) - Ticket Volume Statement - By Product (Various, With Sediment and Water) - Ticket Volume Statement - By Product (Tanks, Without Sediment and Water) - Ticket Volume Statement - By Product (Tanks, With Sediment and Water)

Volume Cross-Tab

Displays a daily or monthly cross-tab summary of volume and energy for selected meters. When run using daily data resolution, the report can be run for a range of contract days or a single contract month. When run using monthly data resolution, the report can be run for a range of contract months or a single contract month. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name (meter reports only) Schedule Editor Group Name: - Volume Cross-tab - Meter, Daily - Volume Cross-tab - Meter, Monthly View Sample Report: - Volume Cross-tab - Meter, Daily - Volume Cross-tab - Meter, Monthly

Volume Statement

The Volume Statements can be found on the report menu by selecting the Volume Statement option. These reports display daily or hourly flow data for gas or liquid meters. The report includes meter configuration and analysis data for the last flow record. Each daily (or hourly) value is displayed on the report along with any prior period adjustments that may have occurred during the month. ##### Edit Reasons Edit reasons can be displayed for a meter by selecting the Print Edit Reasons option on the Reports tab of the Meter Editor. The edit reasons will always start on the second page of the daily report. The hourly report displays the edit reasons at the bottom of the page. ##### PPA Edit PPA edits will display for every meter with PPAs for the measurement month. The PPA edit will begin after the meter edit reasons if those are set to print in the Meter Editor. If the edit reasons do not display, the PPA edits will display on page 2. ##### PPA Accounted for During the Month The PPA Accounted for section displays only if the applicable flags are setup in System Configurations on the PPA and Approvals tab. The Set Accounting Month To options needs to be checked for the Accounted for information to display on the GVS. This section displays after the PPA Edits. This accounted for section has the option to include the accounted for totals or not. If the user wants to see the totals, the Show Total on GVS report option in System Configuration must be checked. ##### Additional Report Behavior When running the report for liquid and by product, each product is displayed on a different page. - The composition section of the Volume Statement (Liquid) reports will be suppressed if the total component liquid volume percent and total mass percent are both 0 or null. - Volume Statement (Liquid) reports will not display pulses for meters that have the "Calculate from Pulses" option in Meter Characteristics set to "No". - Volume Statement (Liquid) reports will display sediment and water percentage and volume only for meters that have non-zero sediment and water. - When the selected month has PPA edits, the PPA Adjustments and Edit Reasons section will appear on the second page. - When the Accounting Month for PPAs setting is enabled, the PPAs Accounted For During the Month section will display on the second page. In addition to listing the PPAs accounted for during the month, their totals will be calculated and displayed if the Show Total On GVS Report option is enabled. Report Group "Audit Reconciliation Request - Meter" includes the Volume Statement (Gas) - Daily report in addition to the Audit Reconciliation Request. Available Configuration Options in Meter Editor:  - Print Customer Name - Print Edit Reasons - Print Interval or Fixed Factor - Print Alternate Meter Number Instead of Meter Name - Print Volume at Optional Pressure Base - Print Measurement Area Available Configuration Options in the System Configuration \> PPAs & Approvals tab: - Allow Auto PPAs - Set Accounting Month To - Business Month - Production Month - Allow Edit - Show Total On Volume Statements - Enable Daily PPA Accounting - Account for Liquid PPA Accounting in Business Month at Location Level Schedule Editor Group Name: - Volume Statement (Gas) - Daily - Volume Statement (Gas) - Hourly - Volume Statement (Liquid) (By Product) - Daily - Volume Statement (Liquid) (By Product) - Hourly - Volume Statement (Liquid) (By Total Fluid) - Daily - Volume Statement (Liquid) (By Total Fluid) - Hourly - Audit Reconciliation Request - Meter View Sample Reports: - Volume Statement (Gas) - Orifice for an Open Month - Hourly - Orifice for an Open Month - Daily - Orifice for a Closed Month with PPA - Hourly - Orifice for a Closed Month with PPA - Daily - Orifice with GPA 2172 Enabled - Measured - Orifice with GPA 2172 Enabled - Standard - Print Volume at Optional Base - Hourly - Volume Statement (Liquid) - Orifice for an Open Month - Hourly - Orifice for an Open Month - Daily - Turbine for a Closed Month with PPA - Hourly - Turbine for a Closed Month with PPA - Daily - Turbine Liquid Volumetric for NGL - Hourly - Turbine Liquid Volumetric for NGL - Daily - Coriolis Inferred Volume for Crude Oil - Hourly - Coriolis Inferred Volume for Crude Oil - Daily - Coriolis Total Fluid BLM - Daily - Coriolis Total Fluid BLM - Hourly

Volume Summary

Displays liquid flow data by product (when grouping by product); hourly data for a selected day; daily data for a selected day or month; or total fluid flow data per meter (when grouping by total fluid).
