docs.title: Audit Reports

Audit Data Request Letter

Form letter requesting audit information for a given meter. The Audit Module can generate this report automatically, or you can click **Letter** in the Audit Detail Editor to generate it manually. View Sample Report

Audit Reconciliation Request

Provides audit information for a given meter. The Audit Module can generate this report automatically, or you can click **Letter** in the Audit Detail Editor to generate it manually. You can also run this report from the **Standard Reports** menu. Schedule Editor Group Name: - Audit Reconciliation Request - Audit Reconciliation Request with Location View Sample Report

Audit Summary

Displays audit summary information as seen on the Audit Tracker grid. Run this report from the Audit Tracker. View Sample Report
Chart Reports

Bar Code Labels

Displays bar code labels for charts, ordered by route. Run this report from the Chart Reports Editor. View Sample Report See: [Bar Code Labels (Details)](../../Tools/Charts/Reports/Reports_Bar%20Code%20Labels.md)

Chart Batch Contents

Displays chart tracking information on a meter. For example, chart ID, actual on/off dates, and operator for a contract month. Run this report from the Chart Reports Editor. View Sample Report See: [Chart Batch Contents (Details)](../../Tools/Charts/Reports/Reports_Chart%20Batch%20Contents.md)

Chart Tracking Status

Displays the progress of an orifice chart or meter read. Run this report from the Chart Reports Editor. View Sample Report See: [Chart Tracking Status (Details)](../../Tools/Charts/Reports/Reports_Chart%20Tracking%20Status.md)

Operator Statistics Detail

Displays a breakdown by operator and daily chart processed count. Run this report from the Chart Reports Editor. See: [Operator Statistics Detail (Details)](../../Tools/Charts/Reports/Reports_Operator%20Statistics%20Detail.md)

Operator Statistics Summary

Displays number of charts, number of days, and average number of charts per day for each operator. Run this report from the Chart Reports Editor. See: [Operator Statistics Summary (Details)](../../Tools/Charts/Reports/Reports_Operator%20Statistics%20Summary.md)
Ticket Reports

Final Form Ticket

Compiles measurement and accounting data for the following ticket types: - Scale - Cavern Level - Tank Run and Tank Gauge - Meter - Blow Down - Flare - Conversion To run this report, open the Ticket Editor or Ticket Search and right-click a ticket. The Component Section contains: - All component data available for the ticket, out to the highest component. - Alkenes and neopentane if the "Show Alkenes" and "Show Neo-pentane" options are enabled for the ticket. - Component mass data for meter tickets using the mass-based calculation method. In this case, the report displays density values for each component from the HC Properties data. FLOWCAL first looks at the ticket for HC properties (set on the Analysis tab), then falls back to the source, then back to the system-level HC properties. View Sample Report: - Final Form Ticket - Meter (Table A) - Final Form Ticket - Meter (Table E) - Final Form Ticket - Scale - Final Form Ticket - Upright Tank Run, API 12.1.1 (2011) - Final Form Ticket - Horizontal Tank Gauge

Final Form Ticket Allowed

Compiles measurement and accounting data for the same tickets as Final Form Ticket reports, and also displays the net allowable amounts by component and net allowable total for a ticket. When the component volumes are in US customary units, the report will always display component volumes and component volume net allowable amounts in gallons. To run this report, open the Ticket Editor or Ticket Search, right-click a ticket and select **Print Ticket(s)** \> **Ticket Allowables**. This report is also available from the Ticket Detail Editor by clicking the drop-down on the Print button and choosing **Print Allowables** or **Print Allowables with Internal Notes** The Component section contains: - All component data available for the ticket, out to the highest component. - Alkenes and neopentane if the "Show Alkenes" and "Show Neo-Pentane" options are enabled for the ticket. - Component mass data for meter tickets using the mass-based calculation method. In this case, the report displays density values for each component pulled from the HC Properties data. - When the report is run for a ticket using US Customary units, the component volumes and net allowable values are in gallons, regardless of component volume units on the ticket. For density values displayed on the report, FLOWCAL first looks at the source to determine which HC properties values to display, then the system-level HC properties. View Sample Report: - Final Form Ticket Allowed - Meter (Table A) - Final Form Ticket Allowed - Meter (Table E) - Final Form Ticket Allowed - Scale - Final Form Ticket Allowed - Upright Tank Run, API 12.1.1 (2011) - Final Form Ticket Allowed - Horizontal Tank Gauge

Rail Car Ticket

Displays pertinent volume BOL data per US DOT requirements. Run this report from the Ticket Editor and Ticket Search for rail car tickets. View Sample Report

You can run some ticket reports for individual tickets while you are viewing them in the Ticket Editor or Ticket Search. You can use the context menu on the ticket or click Print on the Ticket Detail form to preview or email the reports.
Query Reports

GQ Source Query Results

Displays the selected GQ sources for a source query in the Query Editor. Run this report from the Query Editor. View Sample Report

Location Query Results

Displays the results of a location query that you run from the Query Editor. Run this report from the Query Editor. View Sample Report

Meter Query Results

Displays the results of a meter query that you run from the Query Editor. Run this report from the Query Editor. View Sample Report
Miscellaneous Reports

Cavern Batch Summary

This report matches the Inventory Batch Summary run from the Standard Reports menu. It displays net standard volume amounts on batches that are injected into or withdrawn from the selected cavern. This report is run from the Batch tab of the Liquid Cavern Editor. View Sample Report

Helium Measurement

Runs for meters defined as helium meters in the Meter Editor. Displays the following values at an hourly, daily, or monthly resolution: - Total Net Helium - Gross 50 to 65% Helium - Net 50 to 65% Helium - Gross less than 50% Helium - Net less than 50% Helium The hourly, daily, and monthly Helium Measurement reports are shipped with FLOWCAL, but are not installed by default. To install these reports, copy the reports from the Crystal folder to the Crystal\Custom folder and add the reports to FLOWCAL using the **Add Report** menu.

Inventory Location Definition

Displays volume, energy, and mass for each periodic inventory record on an inventory location (gas inventories), or GSV, NSV, and mass for each periodic inventory record on a cavern location (liquid inventories). Run this report from the Inventory Editor and Liquid Cavern Editor. View Sample Report

Location Inventory Ticket

Displays total volume and mass inventory, component volume and mass inventory, and % from the selected revision of an inventory location. To run this report, right-click on a revision in the revisions grid of the Location Close Revisions form. This report is only available for inventory locations. View Sample Report

Missing Source Data

Source Analysis

Displays information for source analysis samples, including composition, C6+ information, and C7+ information.  Each sample will be printed individually. Sample selection is based on the effective dates. If the source analysis being reported has full analysis enabled, this report will include an additional section to display the TP-17 information associated with the sample. (See: [Full Analysis - Gas](../../Source%20Analysis/Gas%20Quality%20Source%20Editor/Source%20Analysis%20Tab.md#SourceAnalysis-Gas) and [Full Analysis - Liquid](../../Source%20Analysis/Liquid%20Quality%20Source%20Editor/Source%20Analysis%20Tab.md#FullAnalysis-Liquid)) This report can also be run by clicking the **Print** button in the GQ or LQ Source Analysis Editor Detail screen. Source Analysis by Sample Date

Schedule Editor Group Name: Source Analysis by Sample Date View Sample Reports: - Source Analysis by Sample Date - Gas - Source Analysis by Sample Date - Liquid

Source Analysis Last 5 Samples

Displays sample information for the last five samples of a selected GQ source, prior to and including the selected date and time. Displays sample characteristics, pressure and temperature, heating values, Wobbe index, relative density, and component mol%. This report is for GQ sources only. Schedule Editor Group Name: Source Analysis Last 5 Samples View Sample Report

Source Exception Detail

Displays details of source analysis exceptions, including the exception name, when it was generated, the field value, and the alarm limit. Users can specify a specific exception code to look for, or, if one is not specified, all exceptions that meet the remaining criteria will be displayed. Standalone sample exceptions cannot be seen in the listing. Schedule Editor Group Name: Source Exception Detail View Sample Report

Source Exception Summary

Provides a summary count of source analysis exceptions. Users can specify a specific exception code, or, if one is not specified, all exceptions that meet the remaining criteria will be displayed. Schedule Editor Group Name: Source Exception Summary View Sample Report

Source Messages

Displays messages for source analyses that have been logged to the database, including the source, message, class, status and priority. Schedule Editor Group Name: Source Messages View Sample Report

Source Meter Assignments

Displays all meters assigned to a source analysis, the time frame for the assignment and how the assignment will apply data. Apply Density column reflects the Apply Density option chosen in the Source Assignment Editor. Schedule Editor Group Name: Source Meter Assignments View Sample Reports: - Source Meter Assignments - GQ Source - Source Meter Assignments - LQ Source

Source Notes

Displays notes entered on a source analysis and when the note will expire. Schedule Editor Group Name: Source Notes View Sample Report

Source Rollups

Displays averages for heating value, CO2, N2, C1-C10, Wobbe index and cricondentherm for chromatograph or RTU average GQ source types. To run this report, rollups must be enabled on the source analysis. Schedule Editor Group Name: - Source Rollups - Daily - Source Rollups - Hourly View Sample Reports: - Source Rollups - Daily - Source Rollups - Hourly

Configure Report/Export Scheduling
docs.text:
During new implementations or installation in a new environment, you may need to configure the application to enable report and export scheduling. Scheduling provides the ability to create recurring jobs that can email reports/exports to one or more contacts, print to a network printer, or save the report/export files to a network location.

The administrator will need the following account credentials:

  • FLOWCAL services account created specifically for the FLOWCAL services to connect to the database and process data. (See: Create Users)
  • Company email account for emailing from FLOWCAL. This is the email address recipients will see on emails originating from FLOWCAL.
  • Company network account with elevated privileges, which will allow the Reports service to create report/export files at different network locations based on the user’s schedule settings.
To configure the ability to schedule or email: 1. Confirm the FLOWCAL services account is set up within the Service Login section of the Service Configuration screen. (See: [Install & Configure Services](../../Admin%20Options/Install%20%26%20Configure%20Services.md)) 2. Confirm the company email account credentials are configured within the Email Information section of the Report Scheduler Configuration. 3. Install the Reports service (FcSrvReports.exe). 4. Within the Microsoft Windows Services console, right-click the reports service and configure the logon to use the designated company network account so that the service can write to the network.

The Report Scheduler Configuration screen is used to set up necessary information for emailing and printing. Failure to properly set up the system will result in reports not being sent correctly. The report service will identify any errors; these error messages will then be available in the Report Scheduler Status screen to help troubleshoot the problems.

Email Information

To configure email: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Report Scheduler** \> **Configuration**. 2. Click the **Edit** button. 3. Enter the SMTP server name. The FLOWCAL reports service uses SMTP rather than MAPI to send emails because MAPI is prone to stalling. The SMTP server name (e.g., smtp.companyname.com) can also be an IP address. The Reports service also supports using SSL/TSL authentication. Check the **Enable SSL/TSL** checkbox and enter the port that is required (usually found through the user's Exchange server). If SMTP does not require this level of authentication, leave the checkbox and **Port** field blank. 4. Enter your username, password and password confirmation. When sending email through the FLOWCAL Reports service, the service will try to connect with the username and password provided. When first entering the username, the password should be specified if there is one. After saving the changes, if you open the screen again, the SMTP server name and username will display, but the password will not. You do not need to re-enter the password. It is not displayed for security reasons, but it is saved. 5. Enter the sender email address (the full email address for the username that will display in outgoing emails). Not doing so may result in an error message regarding an unknown sender. 6. Click **Save**.

Output Printers

When creating report or export schedules to print, FLOWCAL will display the printers that have been defined within Output Printers. To configure printers: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Report Scheduler** \> **Configuration**. 2. Click the **Edit** button. 3. Click **Edit Output Printers**. 4. The printers available for selection will appear on the left. Double-click a printer to add it to the Selected Printers list. Only printers known to the local server will display. If you need to access another printer on the network, the printer must first be installed on the local server. 5. Click **OK**. 6. The printers will now be available from Report Scheduling. The functionality behind the **Print Orientation** button is no longer supported.

docs.title: Report/Export Groups
docs.text:
Use the Report and Export Group Editor to create a group of reports or exports to be used within the Report Scheduler.

To access the Report and Export Group Editor: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Report Scheduler** \> **Report/Exports Group**. 2. Select the group type (Exports or Reports). **Reports** is selected by default. 1. Select **Reports** for Crystal reports such as the Volume Statement or Balance Detail report to filter the **Group** drop-down by report groups. 2. Select **Exports** for custom or standard exports, such as GasTextFileExchange to filter the **Group** drop-down by export groups. 3. Click **New** to create a new group. 4. Enter a group name. 5. Double-click items in the **Available Reports** list to move them to the **Selected Reports** list. You can also click an available report and click the right arrow button. 6. Click **Save**. 7. The new group will now be available from the Schedule Editor when you click the **Group** drop-down menu. In the Schedule Editor, click the **Reports** button next to the Groups drop-down to view a list of reports in this group.

By default, a BLM Audit Package report group has been created that contains the following reports:

  • BLM Audit Package Cover Page
  • BLM Gas Volume Statement – Daily
  • Meter Characteristics
  • Meter Events
  • Meter Sample and Analysis

This group is not required by the system and can be edited or deleted.

If TESTit 3 Integrated is enabled, the TESTit reports are not displayed; these items are only available from the TESTit application.

docs.title: Report/Export Scheduling
docs.text:
Automatic scheduling and emailing reports or exports requires the Scheduled Reporting module. Administrators must have System Process – Report Scheduler – Can Schedule privileges, granted from the User Access or Group Access screen.

Use the Schedule Editor screen to create report and export schedules. Schedules are processed by the Reports service, and are then emailed, printed, or saved to a file on a daily, weekly, or monthly basis.

Before creating schedules, see: Configure Report/Export Scheduling.

Schedule Editor Details

The following items are available on the Schedule Editor screen: - **Name** - Name used to identify the schedule - **Schedule Type** - Designates whether the schedule is for reports (default) or exports. - **Run Frequency** - Defines how often the report schedule will run (daily, weekly, or monthly). For weekly frequency, select the day of the week; for monthly frequency, select the day of the month. For example: A schedule that should run on the 1st of every month, would be set to Monthly, 1st. - **Run Time** - Defines the time of day the report schedule will run. For example: A schedule that should run on the 1st of every month at 10:00am would be set to Monthly, 1st, 10:00:00 AM. - **Data Set Dates** - Defines the time frame or period the report will run for. For example: A schedule that should run every month on the 1st for the prior contract month would be set to Previous Contract Month. Data Set Date options are as follows: - **Month to Date** – The beginning of the current month up to the current date. For example: If today is October 23, the data will be from October 1 at midnight to October 23 at the current time. - **Last Full Month** – Data starting on the first of the previous month and ending on the first of the current month. For example: September 1, 12:00 AM through October 1, 12:00 AM. - **Last Full Week** – Data starting at midnight Sunday and ending on the following Sunday at midnight. For example: Sunday, October 15 12:00 AM through Sunday, October 22 12:00 AM. - **Previous X Days** – A specified number of days prior to the current date. For example: previous 30 days. - **Current Contract Month** – The beginning of the current contract month to the current date. For example: If today is October 25, the contract day is 2 and contract hour is 8, the data will be from October 2, 8:00 AM through October 25, at the current time. - **Previous Contract Month** – The beginning of the previous contract month to the end of the previous contract month. For example: If today is October 25, the contract day is 2, and the contract hour is 8, the data will be from September 2, 8:00 AM through October 2, 8:00 AM. - **Group** - A list of reports and report groups that you can select to schedule. - **Export Flags** - This option is only available when the schedule type is set to "Exports". Export flags are only used if the export has been coded to accept these values. Different export flag options are supported by each export. Review the documentation for each export format to see what options are supported. If an export format supports export flags and no values are entered in this field or a blank is given where a character is expected, default flag values will be assumed. Common Export Flags - **Data Resolution (H, D, or M)** - Indicates data resolution; H = hourly, D = daily, M = monthly. - **Data Level (M or L)** - Indicates the data source; M = meter data, L = location data. - **Rounded or Fractional (R or F)** - Determines the precision for applicable exported values. R = whole (rounded) numbers, F = fractional values before rounding. - **Character 4: Measured or Standard Units (M or S)** - M = measured unit values, S = standard unit values. GasTextFileExchange Export Flags - **Character 1: Data Resolution (H, D, or M)** - If this flag is left blank, it defaults to D. - **Character 2: Data Level (M or L)** - **Character 3: Rounded or Fractional (R or F)** - If this flag is left blank, it defaults to F. If this flag is set to F, the number of decimal places is defaulted to 6. - **Character 4: Measured or Standard Conditions (M or S)** - M = measured conditions, S = standard conditions. If this flag is left empty, it will default to M. - **Character 5: Enforce Time Trails Time Stamp (Y or N)** - Y is equivalent to checking the Enforce Time Trails Time Stamp option on the GasTextFileExchange Export screen; N is equivalent to not having the option checked. If this flag is left empty, it will default to Y. (See: [Exports](../Exports.md#FcTextFileExchange)) LiquidTextFileExchange Export Flags - **Character 1: Data Resolution (H, D, M, or B)** - Hourly, Daily, Monthly, or Batch. All other values will default to "D". - **Character 2: Unused -** Set to "X". - **Character 3: Unused -** Set to "X". - **Character 4: Measured or System Units (M or S)** - Measured or System. All other values, including null values, will default to "M". **Example:** Export flags "BXXS" will output batch-level data at system units. SourceAnalysisExport Export Flags - **Character 1: Process Standalone Sample Analyses within Date Range (Y or N)** - Y is equivalent to checking the Process Standalone Sample Analyses within Date Range option on the Export screen; N is equivalent to not having the option checked. If this flag is left empty, it will default to N. - **Character 2: Enforce Time Trails Time Stamp (Y or N)** - Y is equivalent to checking the Export Last Record only option on the Export screen; N is equivalent to not having the option checked. If this flag is left empty, it will default to N. (See: [Exports](../Exports.md#SourceAnalysisExport)) StndTIPS Export Flags - **Character 1: Data resolution (D or M)** - D = daily, M = monthly. This flag is set to D by default. - **Character 2: Measured or standard units (M or S)** - M = measured unit values, S = standard unit values. This flag is set to M by default. - **Character 3: Include auto estimated data (Y or N)** - This flag is set to N by default. - **Character 4: Output meter number designation (M, A, or C)** - M = meter number, A = alternative meter number, or C = customer meter number. StndFieldInsights Export Flags - **Character 1: Data output (A, D, P, or M)** - A = all three, D = daily volumes, P = daily pressure, M = monthly volumes. This flag must be specified for a schedule to be processed. - **Character 2: Measured or standard units (M or S)** - M = measured unit values, S = standard unit values. This flag is set to M by default. - **Character 3: Data to export (A, C, or N)** - A = all data, C = current volume different from original, N = new and changed records. This flag is set to N by default.

Function Buttons

The following functions are available on the Schedule Editor screen: - **Run Now** - Click this button while in view mode to queue the selected schedule to be processed by the Reports service at the current date and time. The schedule will also continue to run at the configured date and time. - **Reports** - This button only displays when the schedule type is set to "Reports". When you select a report group from the Group drop-down, click the **Reports** button next to the drop-down to see the reports included in the selected group. - **Exports** - This button only displays when the schedule type is set to "Exports". When you select an export group from the Group drop-down, click the **Exports** button next to the drop-down to see the exports included in the selected group. - **Data** - Configure report selections (parameters). Examples are: meter, list, measured/standard, original/current, and decimals. These parameters will vary by report. Selecting a report group will include the parameters for each report in the group. When scheduling a report group, you can click the **Replicate Data** button to use the same parameter value across all reports in the group. For example: You have created a schedule for four reports that all have a parameter called "Number of Decimals". If you set the parameter to "0" for one report and click the **Replicate Data** button, the parameter will be set to "0" for the other reports in the group. - **Email** - Specify recipients for emailed scheduled reports. - **Files** - Save scheduled reports to a file. - **Printers** - Send scheduled reports to a printer. - **New** - Create a new schedule. - **Edit** - Edit an existing schedule. - **Delete** - Delete an existing schedule. - **Save** - Save changes made to the schedule. - **Cancel** - Discard changes made to a schedule. - **Exit** - Close the Schedule Editor screen. - **Print** - Preview the scheduled report with the details specified.

Create a Schedule

Individual reports/exports or report/export groups can be scheduled to run automatically. To create a schedule: 1. Go to **Reports** \> **Scheduling**. 2. Select a schedule type (Reports or Exports). 3. Click **New**. 4. Enter a name for the schedule. 5. Select the run frequency, run time, data set dates, and group options. If you have a custom report or export that is not available from the Group drop-down, see: [Add Report](../Add%20Report.md) or [Add Export](../Add%20Export.md). 6. Define export flags, if applicable. 7. Click the **Data** button to launch the Data Editor and define report data parameters. From within the Data Editor, double-click each row in the grid (or select a row and click **Edit**) to populate each parameter value. 8. Click **OK** to exit the Data Editor. 9. Click the **Email**, **Files**, or **Printers** buttons to configure the schedule delivery method. Multiple delivery methods can be selected. For example: A scheduled report can be emailed and printed. 10. Once the schedule has been configured, click **Save**. 11. Go to **Reports** \> **Status** to review the next scheduled run and status of the report/export schedule.

Email Reports/Exports

Scheduled reports or exports can be emailed to one or more contacts or email distribution groups. To email an export, a file output must also be configured. (See: Files) If you email a report or export group consisting of more than one report/export, a separate email will be generated for each report/export. The following items are available on the Report Email Editor screen: - **To** - Email recipient(s). Recipients must exist as contacts in FLOWCAL and must include valid email addresses. - **File Format** - The file type for the emailed report (see: [Crystal Export Types](../Crystal%20Export%20Types.md)). - **Subject** - Subject line for the scheduled report email. - **Message** - Body of the scheduled report email. - **Compress Report Files** - Enable this option to compress the files into a .zip file before emailing them.

Files

Scheduled reports or exports can be saved to file. The following items are available on the File Distribution Editor screen: - **Directory** (or **File** for exports) - Directory where scheduled report/export will be saved. This path is relative to the computer FLOWCAL is running from. If you want a report written to your local computer, you will need to browse to the location on your computer; otherwise, the Reports service will write the file to its own D:\\ drive. For schedules, this path is relative to the computer where the service is running. When emailing an export, the Directory field must include the name of the file and file extension; otherwise, FLOWCAL will just create the file in the directory specified, and the export will not be emailed. - **File Format** - Several options are available for report schedules, such as PDF. (See: [Crystal Export Types](../Crystal%20Export%20Types.md)) - **Output File Naming Options** - Define text to append or prepend to the file name, or use one of the following variables: - **%RUNDATE%** - The time stamp for the export using a MM-DD-YY HH-MM-SS (24-hour) format Example If the run date is August 2, 2017, at 3:07:08 pm, the variable will translate to "08-02-17 15-07-08". - **%SCHEDNAME%** - The name of the schedule - **%RPTMONTH%** - The name of the reporting month - **Meter Reports** - Select an output file configuration option. By default, FLOWCAL creates one file for meter reports. - **Output Common File** (default) – Export one file for the selected meter(s) - **Output Individual File per Meter** – Export a separate file for each meter - **Output Individual File into Meter Directory** – Export a separate file and directory for each meter

Printers

Scheduled reports or exports can be sent to a printer. Only printers defined within Output Printers of the Report Configuration screen will be listed in the drop-down. (See: [Configure Report/Export Scheduling](Configure%20Report-Export%20Scheduling.md))

docs.title: Report Status
docs.text:
FLOWCAL allows users to monitor report and export schedules to see whether the operations were successful.

To monitor the status of report and export schedules: Go to **Reports** \> **Report Scheduler** \> **Status**.

Reports Tab Details

The following items are available on the Reports tab: - **Scheduled Reports** - The Scheduled Reports tab shows all of the report schedules that are currently configured. - **Successful Reports** - When a schedule is completed, the schedule will display under this tab. The screen displays the time when the schedule ran and when it succeeded. - **Failed Reports** - If the schedule fails, it will display on the Failed Reports tab. Common reasons for a schedule to fail are: - You do not have permissions to the directory you were attempting to write to. - An email address was not entered correctly. - **Crystal Errors** - Crystal-related errors will display on this tab. If you want to create a custom report, you will need to purchase a Crystal Reports Developer license. A Crystal license is not required if you are only running reports.

Exports Tab Details

The following items are available on the Exports tab: - **Scheduled Exports** - The Scheduled Exports tab shows all of the export schedules that are currently configured. - **Successful Exports** - When a schedule is completed, the schedule will display under this tab. The screen displays the time when the schedule ran and when it succeeded. - **Failed Exports** - If the schedule fails, it will display on the Failed Exports tab. Common reasons for a schedule to fail are: - You do not have permissions to the directory you were attempting to write to. - An email address was not entered correctly.

Function Buttons

The following functions are available on the Report and Export Scheduler Information screen: - **Delete** - Remove a schedule. - **Activate** - Enable a schedule that has been put on hold. - **Hold** - Disengage a schedule that is ready to run. - **Run Now** - Set the schedule to run during the next scheduler iteration. - **Refresh** - Update the screen to display new, successful or failed schedules. - **Exit** - Close the Report and Export Scheduler Information screen.

docs.title: Carry/Borrow Method
docs.text:
The periodic volumes that comprise an hour are totaled and stored in the measured_volume column of the Final-Form Hourly table. A rounded, integer version of this value is calculated using a carry/borrow method and is stored in the rollup_volume column.

Hourly Records

Consider a meter with volumes as shown (column A) for the first four hours of a day. Presume the rest of the hours for the day are exactly 0. | Day | Measured Volume | Current Day + Last Carry Amount | Carry/Borrow Rounded Value | Monthly Carry (Borrow) Amount | Straight Rounding | |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:| | \- | A | B = A + D | C = Round(B) | D = B - C | E = Round(A) | | 1 | 10.4 | \- | 10 | 0.4 | 10 | | 2 | 10.4 | 10.8 | 11 | (0.2) | 10 | | 3 | 10.4 | 10.2 | 10 | 0.2 | 10 | | 4 | 10.4 | 10.6 | 11 | (0.4) | 10 | Hour 1 is rounded to 10 (column C), and the leftover amount of 0.4 is noted (column D) as the carry amount. The Hour 1 carry amount is added to the Hour 2 Measured Volume (result in column B). This result, 10.8, is rounded to 11 (column C). The leftover amount of -0.2 is carried to Hour 3 (i.e., 0.2 is borrowed from Hour 3), and so on through the day. If each individual hour is rounded without attention to the carry-borrow amount (Straight Rounding, column E), the user will notice that there is not a one-to-one correspondence between the rounded hourly values (compare column C with column E).

Daily Records

Daily records are constructed as the sum of the corresponding hourly records. As shown below, the Straight Rounding total (column E) does not match the rounded Measured Volume total (column A). This is the usual problem with rounding and is the reason for FLOWCAL's carry/borrow method. By paying attention to the carry/borrow amount, the carry/borrow total for the day (column C) exactly matches the rounded Measured Volume total (column A). |   | Measured Volume |   | Carry/Borrow Rounded Value |   | Straight Rounding | |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:| | \- | A | B | C = Round(B) | D | E = Round(A) | | Total of Hours | 41.6 | \- | 42 | \- | 40 | | Rounded Total | 42 | \- | 42 | \- | 40 | At the end of each day, the remaining carry/borrow amount is discarded. By this process, the amount can never be more than +/- 0.5.

Monthly Records

Discrepancies can occur between the measured volume and the rollup volume at the monthly level. Consider a month where the first four days are exactly as shown above. Compare the rounded total shown in columns A and B. | Day | Monthly Carry (Borrow) Amount | Straight Rounding | |:-------------:|:-----------------------------:|:-----------------:| | 1 | 41.6 | 42 | | 2 | 41.6 | 42 | | 3 | 41.6 | 42 | | 4 | 41.6 | 42 | | Total of Days | 166.4 | 168 | | Rounded Total | 166 | 168 | This is not unusual and is not wrong. By policy, a company may choose to state daily volumes as integer values and, as such, it is not meaningful to compare the full precision total with the rounded total. Recall chart integrations that were broke daily. These resulted in daily integer volumes by rounding a full precision calculation result. This is the same except that the full precision results are saved. As noted, comparing them is not meaningful and can cause confusion. Because the carry/borrow amount that is discarded, daily cannot be more the +/- 0.5, the discrepancy at the monthly level will never be more than 15.5. Because of statistical fluctuations in the Measured Volume values, the discrepancy tends to be 0.

Monthly Carry/Borrow

FLOWCAL provides a system option to cause the carry/borrow method to cross day boundaries. This works as before except that the daily discard does not occur; the carry/borrow process continues through the entire month. In this case, the discrepancies in the monthly totals are alleviated (compare Rounded Totals between column A and column C), but there will now be discrepancies at the daily level (compare Day 2 between column C and column E). | Day | Measured Volume | Current Day + Last Carry Amount | Carry/Borrow Rounded Value | Monthly Carry (Borrow) Amount | Straight Rounding | |:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:| | \- | A | B = A + D | C = Round(B) | D = B - C | E = Round(A) | | 1 | 41.6 | 41.6 | 42 | (0.4) | 42 | | 2 | 41.6 | 41.2 | 41 | 0.2 | 42 | | 3 | 41.6 | 41.8 | 42 | (0.2) | 42 | | 4 | 41.6 | 41.4 | 41 | 0.4 | 42 | | Total of Days | 166.4 | \- | 166 | \- | \- | | Rounded Total | 166 | \- | 166 | \- | \- |

docs.title: Ad Hoc Data Review
docs.text:
Use the Ad-Hoc Data Review to view a desired set of data based on user-defined parameters. Data can be viewed at the meter or location level, at measured or standard conditions, and at hourly, daily or monthly resolution.

To access the Ad Hoc Data Review: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers** \> **Ad Hoc Data Review**. 2. Click the drop-down button under the **Meter** label and select **Meter**, **Location**, or **List**. 3. Based on your selection in step 2, select a meter, location or list to view data for. 4. Set the date range for the data you want to view. Example To set the date range to August 2018, select August 2018 for the **From Date** and September 2018 for the **To Date**). 5. On the **Main** tab, specify whether the data will be at the meter or location level. 6. Select the resolution for the data display (Hourly, Daily or Monthly). 7. Specify whether the view will display volume and heating values at measured or standard conditions. 8. On the **Flow**, **Mol%**, and **HCL** tabs, select the values to be displayed. 9. Click **Refresh**.

docs.title: Button Details
docs.text:
The following functions are available on the Ad Hoc Data Review screen:

  • Refresh – Query the database for the data selected in the left pane.

  • Remove – Hide selected rows in the grid.

Select rows on the grid either as a continuous block or by holding the Ctrl key and clicking rows, then click Remove to hide those rows. To show hidden rows, click Refresh.

  • Find – Users can enter a value to be searched for in the data grid. Clicking Find Next or Find Previous will take the user from one row to the next with data points that meet the specified criteria. Clicking the Highlight button will cause all cells with the specified criteria to be highlighted with a \<HI> before and a \</HI> after every data point that meets the criteria.

docs.title: File Menu
docs.text:
The following options are available on the Ad Hoc Data Viewer File menu:

  • Refresh – Refresh data on the screen (this functionality is the same as the Refresh button).

  • Export – Export all data displayed on the grid to an XLS or CSV file.

Export file includes object number, object name, date and all data points, and column headers. Data that has been hidden is not included.

  • Find – Show or hide the Find tool at the bottom of the grid.

  • Exit – Close the Ad Hoc Data Review screen and return to the main FLOWCAL screen.

docs.title: Options Menu
docs.text:
The following options are available on the Ad Hoc Data Viewer Options menu:

  • Flow Duration – Specify whether to view the flow time in hhss format or as a percentage of an hour.
  • Decimals – Specify the number of decimals displayed for volume and energy (0–4)
  • Pressure – Specify whether to display the pressure as absolute, gauge, or the field measurement condition.
  • Options – Specify the number of data rows to display ("Unlimited" is specified by default). This option allows users to set a value other than "Unlimited" when a large data set is returned, usually involving tens of thousands of meters, which can cause the application to run out of memory when attempting to display the data.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Balance Explorer combines several of the legacy rollup viewers:

  • Daily Location Rollups
  • Monthly Location Rollups
  • NGL Balance
  • Recovery Analysis Viewer
To access the Balance Explorer: Go to **Open** \> **Balance Explorer**. ![](data:image/png;base64,)

Screen Configuration

Upon initially opening the Balance Explorer, the default layout is as follows: | Open by Default | Collapsed or Hidden by Default | |-------------------|--------------------------------| | Location Explorer | Date Selector | | L&U Viewer | Location Rollup Queue | | Member Viewer |   | The L&U Viewer and Member Viewer panels can be expanded, hidden, moved, dragged out of the Balance Explorer window. Once hidden, you can reopen the panels from the Panel drop-down at the top of the screen. The Location Explorer, L&U Viewer, and Member Viewer can be pinned and collapsed to the side of Balance Explorer.

docs.title: Date Selector
docs.text:
Use the date selector to select a datetime range to display. Three date options are available:

  • Current Month – Displays results from the current contract month, from the first day of the month to the current date.
  • Previous Month – Displays results from the previous contract month, from the first day of the month to the last.
  • Effective Date - Displays results based on the effective date of the associated data.

By default, the Date Selector is set to Effective Date with the First Date being the beginning of the previous month (e.g., if the current date is April 10, then the First Date is March 1) and the Last Date being the current date based on system time.

Select the start time for the First Date by clicking in the field to access the calendar, and then clicking the Start of Time button or pressing Alt+S.

Select the end time for the Last Date by clicking in the field to access the calendar, and then clicking the End of Time button or pressing Alt+E.

The First and Last Dates are inclusive. If the First Date value is later than the Last Date value, the Date Selector displays in red, indicating that there is an issue with the dates.

Based on the datetime range selected, displayed data will be calculated as follows:

Selected Date Range Date View (L&U and Member) Range selected are full months (e.g., April 1 – June 30) In monthly columns, show monthly values from database. Range is a full month and partial month (e.g., April 1 – June 15) Full months show values from database; Partial month data are calculated by accumulation if applicable (i.e., volume, energy, mass, etc.), or displayed as NA (i.e. calculated factors, flowing parameters). Range is all partial (e.g., April 15 – May 15) Partial month data are calculated by accumulation if applicable (i.e., volume, energy, mass, etc.), or displayed as NA (i.e., calculated factors, flowing parameters). Filter days in data grid In monthly columns, the accumulation is calculated and displayed.

docs.title: Location Explorer
docs.text:
The Location Explorer is a collapsible tree view in the Balance Explorer that allows you to navigate through the location groupings for each system and view data related to specific objects. The Location Explorer will show the list of root (pinned) locations and systems (with the preferred system expanded).

  • Expanding a system will show all location types within that system.
  • Selecting a location and date and clicking the Refresh button will populate the L&U and Members data grids.
  • Location types and objects within locations are ordered alphabetically.
  • All current members of a given location will display in the Location Explorer; however, the data grid will only display current members within the selected date range.

Search Bar

Use the search bar to search for items in the tree view by name or number. When you enter criteria in the search bar, the Location Explorer returns a sorted list of items that meet the criteria.

Tree View Icons

Each object type in the tree view has a unique icon. These icons are as follows: | Icon | Object | |:--:|:---| | | Pinned location | | | Gas or liquid meter | | | Location | | | Balance location | | | Comparison location | | | Inventories | | | Gas inventory | | | Liquid inventory | | | Liquid cavern | | | Section | | | Segment | | | Station | | | Tank |

Column Options

Right-click any column header to access the following configuration options: - **Sort Ascending** - Sort items in ascending order for the selected column. - **Sort Descending** - Sort items in descending order for the selected column. - **Show Column Chooser** - Open the Column Selector to select the columns to display in the grid. (See: [Column Selector](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Resolver/Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector)) - **Best Fit** - Expand the selected column to display the complete contents. - **Best Fit (all columns)** - Expand all columns to display the complete contents. - **Filter Editor** - Open the Filter Editor to create conditional statements based on any column or value within the column. ##### Column Order To change the order of the columns, click a column header and then drag and drop the column to the new location. You can remove a column by dragging and dropping it outside of the grid, but FLOWCAL will not save this layout when you exit the screen.

Sorting

By default, items in a group are sorted by number, in descending order. To change the sort order: - Click any column header to sort items by that parameter. - Click a header again to reverse the list order (ascending or descending). - Right-click a column header and select **Sort Ascending** or **Sort Descending**.

Filtering

You can filter items by a single column or by multiple columns. To filter by a single column: 1. Hover over a column header to display the filter icon. 2. Click the filter icon to open the Filter dialog box. The dialog box contains two tabs: - **Filter Values** - Select the values that you want to display. - **Filter Rules** - Apply a conditional rule (for example: "Is greater than" or "Is less than"). Select the condition, and then specify a value. 3. Close the Filter dialog box by clicking on the grid. 4. After FLOWCAL applies the filter, you can use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter. To filter by multiple columns, right-click a column header and select **Filter Editor**. The following example shows a filter that uses multiple columns:

Class Hierarchy

The Class Hierarchy tab will display the member directions and classes of the selected location within the date range. Clicking Refresh will then display the member data of that hierarchy in the Member Viewer Data Viewer.

docs.text:
This panel displays whether the selected location is rolled up for all of time. Click the Refresh button within the panel to search for non-rolled data under that location for all of time.

  • If unrolled data is identified, the following message will display: "There is unrolled data for \<Location>".
  • If no unrolled data is identified, the following message will display: "All data is rolled for \<Location>".

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
The Balance Explorer may require supplemental documentation to provide additional status information.

Example Validations for a meter are set so that exceptions are generated when the flow data temperature falls below 55°F. An analyst can change the status of these exceptions to "Acknowledged" during the time frames that fall outside of the validation range, and provide an edit reason for doing so. A senior analyst would like to see some documentation inside FLOWCAL that describes the meter data conditions and provides context for why FLOWCAL reports data discrepancies.

Creating Notes

You can add notes to objects in the Member Viewer grid of the Balance Explorer. To add a note to an object in the Balance Explorer: 1. Right-click the desired object. 2. Select **Add Note** or **View Notes**. When the View Notes screen displays, click the **Add Note** button. 3. When the Add Note screen displays, provide the required data: - **First Date** - The beginning effective date for the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the minimum date selected in the Date Selector. - **Last Date** - The ending effective date for the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the maximum date selected in the Date Selector. - **Visibility** - Designation to determine who can view the note. By default, this field will be auto-populated with the user’s visibility settings in User Preferences window. Other options are: - **Everyone** - All FLOWCAL users can access the note. - **Internal** - All FLOWCAL users can access the note, but the note will not display on any standard reports. - **Private** - Only the user who created the note can view it. - **Expiration Date** - Date after which the note will no longer be visible in FLOWCAL. (The record of the note will still be stored in the database.)  The Expired Notes report can be used to view a list of expired notes in FLOWCAL. - **Custom Fields** - Four custom text boxes are available for capturing additional data. (If custom fields are configured on the Notes tab of the [Custom Fields Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Custom%20Fields.md), those fields will be generated when you first open the Add Note screen.) - **Note Text** - The documentation portion of the note (required). - **Object Information** - The number, name and type of the selected objects.  If you click the delete button on any of the object rows, the note will no longer be included on that object. 4. When you have finished entering the note date, click **Done**. After a note is saved, a note icon will display next to the object(s) that contain notes.

Viewing Notes

To view notes associated with an object: Right-click an object with a note icon and select **View Notes**. When the View Notes screen displays, you will be able to view the full body of the note, as well as the following Object History details: - **Modified Date** - GMS date when the note was last edited. - **Modified By** - Name of the user who last edited the note. - **First Date\*** - Effective starting date of the note. - **Last Date\*** - Effective ending date of the note. - **Expiration Date\*** - Date after which the note will no longer be available. - **Visibility\*** - Designation indicating who can view the note. - **Custom 1–4** - Editable fields used to capture additional data. (If custom fields are configured on the notes tab of the [Custom Fields Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/Custom%20Fields.md), the column headers in the View Notes screen will match those custom fields.) \* These items are read-only; they are only editable in the Add Note screen.

Deleting Notes

Notes are deleted from the Object History grid. To delete a note: 1. Hover over a note in the Object History grid. 2. Click the delete button when it displays.

Column Options

Right-click any column header to access the following configuration options: - **Sort Ascending** - Sort items in ascending order for the selected column. - **Sort Descending** - Sort items in descending order for the selected column. - **Show Column Chooser** - Open the Column Selector to select the columns to display in the grid. (See: [Column Selector](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Resolver/Exception%20Resolver%20Settings.md#Selector)) - **Best Fit** - Expand the selected column to display the complete contents. - **Best Fit (all columns)** - Expand all columns to display the complete contents. - **Filter Editor** - Open the Filter Editor to create conditional statements based on any column or value within the column. ##### Column Order To change the order of the columns, click a column header and then drag and drop the column to the new location. You can remove a column by dragging and dropping it outside of the grid, but FLOWCAL will not save this layout when you exit the screen.

Sorting Notes

By default, notes are sorted by modified date, in descending order. To change the sort order of notes: - Click any column header to sort notes by that parameter. - Click a header again to reverse the list order (ascending or descending). - Right-click a column header and select Sort Ascending or Sort Descending.

Filtering Notes

You can filter notes by a single column or by multiple columns. To filter by a single column: 1. Hover over a column header to display the filter icon. 2. Click the filter icon to open the Filter dialog box. The dialog box contains two tabs: - **Filter Values** - Select the values that you want to display. - **Filter Rules** - Apply a conditional rule (for example: "Is greater than" or "Is less than"). Select the condition, and then specify a value. 3. Close the Filter dialog box by clicking on the grid. 4. After FLOWCAL applies the filter, you can use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter. To filter by multiple columns, right-click a column header and select **Filter Editor**. The following example shows a filter that uses multiple columns:

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Users can configure several default settings of the Balance Explorer.

  • Default Date Range - Set the default Date Selector option. Options are:
  • Current Month
  • Previous Month

  • Both Current And Previous Month

  • Show L&U data in Member View data grid - When this option is enabled, L&U and L&U % rows are added to the Member Viewer data grid the L&U Viewer panel is hidden.

If you then turn on L&U Viewer from the Panels drop-down, L&U information will display in both the L&U Viewer and Member Viewer.

If you are using the Recovery Analysis template, it is best to display the L&U grid as these values are calculated only in the L&U grid.

  • Load data when window opens - When this option is enabled, the data grids will automatically load based on pre-selected templates, location, and other related options.

  • Show Location Rollup Queue panel - When this option is enabled, the Location Rollup Queue panel will display under the Location Explorer panel.

  • Default Template - Select a default template to load when the Balance Explorer is launched.

  • Default Conditions - Switch between measured and standard conditions for applicable variables.

  • Default Decimals - Set default decimal places for the following categories: Gas and Liquid Volumes, Energy, Mass, Temperature, Pressure, Heating Value, Density, Meter and K-Factors, Correction Factors, Components, L&U Percentage.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
The Balance Explorer includes four default templates:

  • Gas Default View
  • Liquid Default View
  • NGL View
  • Recovery Analysis View

Default templates cannot be modified or deleted.

docs.title: Custom Templates
docs.text:
Users can also create custom templates with preferred variables and location. Custom templates are saved on a per-user basis; users can only access their own custom templates.

To create a custom template: 1. Select desired locations and variables in the L&U Viewer and Member Viewer variable selectors. 2. Go to **Templates** \> **Save Current View as a Template**. 3. Enter a template name (optional). To manage custom templates, go to **Templates** \> **Manage Templates**. The Manage Templates screen contains all default and custom templates, associated locations (custom templates only), and variable selections. From this screen, you can: - Update the location and variables as needed. - Rename a custom template. - Delete a custom template. You cannot edit fields for a template in the Manage Templates screen.

docs.title: Viewers
docs.text:
The L&U Viewer and Member Viewer panels display lost and unaccounted for data and member data for a given location, over a selected datetime range.

L&U Viewer

Two tabs are available in the L&U Viewer panel: - **Variable Selector** - Volume, Energy, and Mass; Calculated Factors; Flowing Parameters; Component Volume/Component Volume %; Component Mass/Component Mass %; Component Net Allowable - **Data Viewer** - A graphical display represents changes in values as follows: Absolute Current Value   Graphical Display Lower than previous value Denotes a decreased imbalance (improvement) Higher than previous value Denotes an increased imbalance (no improvement) Equal to previous value No change - **Show/Hide Daily Data** - Display or hide daily L&U data cards - **Single/Multiple Row Display buttons** - Toggle between horizontal and vertical display of the cards. ##### Graphing Functionality Use the Graphing functionality to generate current L&U data in a graph. - **Chart Options** - Show data point makers - Show data point labels - Variables - Change or deselect the displayed variables in the graph Only variables selected in the L&U Variable Selectors will be shown in the drop-down. - **Show Monthly/Daily Data** - Toggle between monthly and daily data in the graph. - **Export to PNG** - Generate a PNG image of the current graph.

Member Viewer

Two tabs are available in the Member Viewer panel: - **Variable Selector** - **Show data for Recovery Analysis** - Add Recovery Eff %, Inlet GPM, and Outlet GPM rows to the data grid. - **Show Activity Codes** - Add activity codes column to the data grid - **Variable Selector** - Volume, Energy, and Mass; Calculated Factors; Flowing Parameters; Component Volume/Component Volume %; Component Mass/Component Mass %; Component Net Allowable - **Data Viewer** - Member number, name and direction are displayed in the grid, followed by monthly totals. To display daily data, click on the arrow next to Monthly Total or Partial Total. To display hourly data, click on the plus sign (+) next to the date. A Member Hourly Viewer screen will display the hourly data. - **Member drop-down** - Switch between members of the selected location. - **Export Data to Excel and Graph Hourly Data** - Export appropriate file types of the current data. Multiple Member Hourly Viewer screens can be open at the same time. - **Export Data to Excel** - Generate an Excel spreadsheet containing the current data grid. ##### Graphing Functionality Use the graphing functionality to generate current member meter and location data in a graph. - **Chart Options** - **Chart Settings** - Single variable with multiple members - Multiple variables with single member - Show data point makers - Show data point labels - **Show logarithmic scale** - Transform the Y axis based on logarithmic scale. Only available when single variable with multiple members is selected. - **Primary Axis Variable** - Change or deselect the displayed primary variables in the graph. Only variables selected in the Member Viewer Variable Selectors will be shown in the drop-down. - **Secondary Axis Variables** - Display a secondary variable. Only available when single variable with multiple members is selected. - **Members** - Select locations - **Show Monthly/Daily Data** - Toggle between monthly and daily data in the graph. - **Export to PNG** - Generate a PNG image of the current graph.

docs.title: Gas Analysis Tab
docs.text:
The Gas Analysis tab shows accumulated analysis results.

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - The date for which the data is applicable.  This is dependent on contract day, contract hour and Resolution.  For Hourly Resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for.  For Daily Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day.  For Monthly Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Codes - This column will display whether or not any of the activity codes enabled under the System Rollup Options are present for the device for a given period. The column will be highlighted an amber color if it is populated by anything and the code associated with the activity record(s) will appear. Right-clicking on a row will display the code and the associated trigger at the bottom of the context menu.

docs.title: Liquid Adjustment Tab
docs.text:
The Liquid Adjustment tab shows adjustments that were made for hydrocarbon liquid meters. These include current period adjustments (CPA) and prior period adjustments (PPA).

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - The date for which the data is applicable.  This is dependent on contract day, contract hour and Resolution.  For Hourly Resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for.  For Daily Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day.  For Monthly Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Codes - Activity codes can be meter events, alarms, analysis changes or other items as selected on the Rollup Configuration Editor. FLOWCAL calculates these at the hourly, daily, monthly and batch level. The user can choose which ones will appear by going to System Rollup Configuration and checking or unchecking options in the Activity Codes section.
  • GSV - GSV is the gross standard volume before PPAs are made.
  • Adj GSV - Adj GSV is the adjusted total gross standard volume for the period. It includes any CPAs and PPAs.
  • Mass - Mass is the mass before PPAs are made.
  • PPA Mass - PPA Mass is the prior period adjustment to the Mass. This is the amount of any proving adjustment(s).
  • Adj Mass - Adj Mass is the adjusted mass for the period. It includes any CPAs and PPAs.
  • GMS Date - GMS date is the date that the data was written to the database.

The Liquid Analysis tab shows the analysis for hydrocarbon liquid meters. All data are mole percent values.

The following items are available on this tab:

For Hourly Resolution, the effective date is the day and hour the data is effective for. For Daily Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day. For Monthly Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Codes - These can be meter events, alarms, analysis changes or other items as selected on the Rollup Configuration screen. FLOWCAL calculates these at the hourly, daily, monthly, calendar and batch level. The user can choose which ones appear by going to System Rollup Configuration and enabling or disabling options in the Activity Codes section.

  • N2 - Nitrogen

docs.title: Liquid Flow Data Tab
docs.text:
The Liquid Flow Data Tab shows data for hydrocarbon liquid meters.

This tab is not available and is not displayed for Section-type locations.

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - The date for which the data is applicable. This is dependent on Contract Day, Contract Hour and Resolution. For Hourly Resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for. For Daily Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day. For Monthly Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Codes - These can be meter events, alarms, analysis changes or other items as selected on the Rollup Configuration Editor. FLOWCAL calculates these at the hourly, daily, monthly, calendar and batch level. The user can choose which ones will appear by going to System Rollup Configuration and checking or unchecking options in the Activity Codes section.
  • Pressure - Average meter Pressure for the meter. Average static Pressure for the location.
  • Temperature - Average meter Temperature for the meter. Average Temperature for the location.
  • IV - This is the total Indicated Volume for the period.
  • GSV - This is the total Gross Standard Volume for the period, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj GSV - This is the Adjusted Total Gross Standard Volume for the period. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • NSV - This is the Total Net Standard Volume for the period, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj NSV - This is the Total Net Standard Volume for the period. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Mass - This is the Total Mass for the Period, including PPAs.
  • S&W % - Average Sediment and Water Percentage for the period.
  • SWV - This is the Sediment and Water Volume for the period, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj. SWV - This is the Sediment and Water Volume for the period. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Eqv Gas Vol - This is the Equivalent Gas Volume. This only appears for products that are Table E. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Summed Comp Volume - This is the Sum of Component Volumes, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj Summed Comp Volume - This is the Adjusted Sum of Component Volumes. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Eqv Energy - This is the Equivalent Gas Energy. This only appears for products that are Table E. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Completion - Indicates whether all data is present for a record. When viewing data for a location, if any of the members is missing data for the time frame indicated by the effective date, the status will be marked as "Incomplete".
  • GMS Date - This is the date that the data was written to the database.

docs.title: Measured Tab
docs.text:
The Measured tab shows data that was calculated based on the meter or location’s measured conditions.

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - This is the date for which the data is applicable.  This is dependent on contract day, contract hour and resolution.  For hourly resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for.  For daily resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day.  For monthly resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Code - This column will display whether or not any of the activity codes enabled under System Rollup Configuration are present for the device for a given period. The column will be highlighted an amber color if it is populated by anything and the code associated with the activity record(s) will appear. Right-clicking on a row will display the code and the associated trigger at the bottom of the context menu.
  • Volume - This is the total volume including PPAs for the meter or location for the stated time span.
  • Energy - This is the energy reported by the meter for the stated time span.
  • Mass - This is the mass reported by the meter for the stated time span.
  • Extension or Raw Volume - The Extension is reported for AGA-3 meters. Raw Volume is reported for AGA-7 meters.
  • Flow Time - This is the time (hours, min, sec) where there was flow for the stated time span.
  • Differential Pressure or Pulses - Differential Pressure is displayed for AGA-3 meters, while Total Pulses or Frequency are shown for AGA-7 meters.
  • Pressure - This is the average static pressure for the meter or location at the given time.
  • Temperature - This is the average flowing temperature for a meter or location at the given time.
  • Completion Status - Indicates whether or not there is missing data. If there is no missing data for the time span, the completion status will be complete; otherwise, the completion status will be incomplete.
  • GMS Date - This is the date that data was written to the database.
  • Projected Volume, Projected Energy, Projected Mass - For users with Gas Day Projection module. These columns will display the projected values for each data point for the selected meter or location based on the settings defined for Gas Day Projection within the Meter Editor.

docs.title: Meter/Location Rollups
docs.text:
The Rollup Viewer shows accumulated hourly, daily, monthly, batch and period totals for meters and locations as calculated by the Rollup Services. Accumulated or averaged totals for relevant fields for meters and locations are stored in the Final Form Tables.

To access the Rollup Viewer: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers**. 2. Click **Meter/Location Rollups**. To view rolled data, select a list, location, or meter. Configure parameters (Resolution, Date Range, Meter or Location, etc.), and then click the **Refresh** button to update the data in the tabs. Changing any parameter will refresh or clear the data, depending on the data resolution. Rollup Viewer for Gas Meters Rollup Viewer for Non-Hydrocarbon Liquid Meters Rollup Viewer for Hydrocarbon Liquid Meters

Rollup Viewer Screen Details

Use the By Meter or By Location radio buttons to view individual members of the selected item. Navigate through the members using the forward ![](data:image/png;base64,) or back ![](data:image/png;base64,) buttons. The ![](data:image/png;base64,) button can be used to select the last member of a list or location or close group while the ![](data:image/png;base64,) button can be used to navigate back to the first member. The ![](data:image/png;base64,) button will open the tree view, which allows you to move throughout a location or list hierarchy directly to select specific members. #### Data Options - **Revision** - **Current** - Displays the most current data, including any edits that have been made. - **Original Data** - This is the data that came in during import. This data has not had any edits (only available for gas meters). - **Quantity** - **Gas Volume** - Displays data by volume for gas meters. - **Liquid Volume** - Displays data by volume for liquid meters. - **Mass** - Displays data by mass. - **Closed** - **Adjusted** - Displays the original closed total plus any PPAs. - **Closed** - This is the final total from the closed data. - **Conditions** - **Measured** - Volume and energy calculated at the meter's pressure base. - **System** - Volume and energy calculated at the system pressure base. #### Function Buttons - **Show** - Displays the time frame where data exists in the appropriate final form table for the selected meter or location. This is useful to help determine where in time there is data to display. - **Open** - Available only when a meter is selected. It opens the Meter Editor in view only mode for the selected meter. Subsequently clicking on the Open Data button in the Meter Editor brings up the Volume Editor on the same selected meter. - **Unrolled Data** - Launches the Service Queues screen to display data waiting to be queued in the [Unrolled Meters tab](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Unrolled%20Meters%20Tab.md) or the [Unrolled Locations tab](../../Settings%20Manager/Services/Unrolled%20Locations%20Tab.md). - **Refresh** - The Refresh button updates the data in the tabs at the bottom of the Rollups Viewer for the parameters specified. Changing any parameter (Resolution, Date Range, Meter or Location, etc.) will cause the tabs to be cleared. - **Print** - Available when Resolution is set to Hourly or Daily. It will print the GVS Hourly or Daily report for the selected meter or location. If multiple months are selected, the report can be very long, especially if the resolution is set to Hourly. The maximum number of rows to display has no effect on the reports.

Filter Settings

If the [Remember UI Filter Values](../../Settings%20Manager/User%20Settings/User%20Preferences.md) option is enabled, the Rollup Viewer remembers the filter and date settings for the duration of the FLOWCAL session. The filter and date settings set in the last Rollup Viewer to be closed are retained when multiple Rollup Viewers are opened. The filter settings are forgotten once a user logs out or closes FLOWCAL. The following filter settings are remembered during a session: - Object Selector (Meter, Location, or List) - Date Range Type and Selection - Data Resolution, Options, By Location, By Meter, Revision, Quantity, Closed, Conditions, Allowables, and Inventory - FLOWCAL Explorer (pinned or unpinned)

Liquid Meters and Locations with Multiple Products

A liquid meter or location may have multiple products flowing on it within the selected time frame. To see the total of all products on each record, set Product to Total Fluid. If the user clicks the Product drop-down, the user can see all of the products that flowed on the selected meter or location for the time frame. To see the flow for a given Product, select that product and then click Refresh. If for a given time frame the selected product only flowed for part of the time, the values displayed will be for the time the selected product was flowing.

docs.title: Right-Click Menu Options
docs.text:
Add Note

Notes can be added to any record in the Rollup Viewer. Notes are datetime effective and can be made public or private. When this option is selected a new window will appear to add a note. Notes created here are visible in other places that notes are visible, such as the Volume Editor.

View Note

Click this option to view notes that were previously added to records from the Rollup Viewer, Volume Editor, or elsewhere.

Plot Data

This will bring up a graph of the data on the screen. Once on screen, the user has various options available from the menu bar such as: exporting data to a file, choosing how to display the data, picking what data is displayed on the graph, and specifying how to scale the data. On the Rollup Viewer, the user can change meters and the graph will update to show the data. Since values for Mass are generally much larger numbers than values for Volume or other flow variables, the graph plot displayed within the Meter/Location Rollup Viewer becomes unusable as only the Mass trace line is visible with the other trace lines all being "squeezed" together at the bottom of the plot. To prevent this from happening, the trace line for Mass is now defaulted to not be visible in the graph plot. Plot Data for Gas Meters Plot Data for Liquid Meters

Customize Columns and Layout

Use the Customize Column option to specify which columns are visible in the rollup viewer and the order in which they appear. This is configurable on a per user basis, by meter type (e.g., orifice, turbine) and location type (e.g., segment, liquid cavern). When the option is selected, a new window will appear called Available Column List. If visible columns have been removed, they will be listed here. To remove a column, click the column header and drag it onto the Available Column List window. To restore a column, click the column name in the Available Column List window and drag it back to the rollup viewer grid and drop it between any two columns. You can also move columns around by clicking on a column header and dragging it between two other columns to change the column order. Close the Available Column List window to save the configuration settings. You can do this for each rollup viewer tab, but you must save the column layout before moving to another tab or the changes will be lost. Click **Save Column Layout** in the right-click menu to save the column order. Click **Reset Column Layout** to revert the changes to the default settings.

Admin Options

The following options are available to users with admin privileges: - **Save As Default for All Users** - Save the current rollup viewer configuration as the default for all users. This is for each tab, each meter and location type. - **Reset Default for All Users** - Reset the rollup viewer back to the default settings for all users. This is for each tab, each meter and location type.

docs.title: NHC Adjustment Tab
docs.text:
The NHC Adjustment tab shows adjustments that were made for non-hydrocarbon liquid meters. These include current period adjustments (CPA) and prior period adjustments (PPA).

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - The date for which the data is applicable. This is dependent on contract day, contract hour and Resolution. For Hourly Resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for. For Daily Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day. For Monthly Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Codes - Activity codes can be meter events, alarms, analysis changes or other items as selected on the Rollup Configuration Editor. FLOWCAL calculates these at the hourly, daily, monthly and batch level. The user can choose which ones will appear by going to System Rollup Configuration and checking or unchecking options in the Activity Codes section.
  • GSV - GSV is the gross standard volume before PPAs are made.
  • Adj GSV - Adj GSV is the adjusted total gross standard volume for the period. It includes any CPAs and PPAs.
  • Mass - Mass is the mass before PPAs are made.
  • PPA Mass - PPA Mass is the prior period adjustment to the Mass. This is the amount of any proving adjustment(s).
  • Adj Mass - Adj Mass is the adjusted mass for the period. It includes any CPAs and PPAs.
  • GMS Date - GMS date is the date that the data was written to the database.

FLOWCAL calculates these at the hourly, daily, monthly, calendar and batch level. The user can choose which ones appear by going to System Rollup Configuration and enabling or disabling options in the Activity Codes section.

docs.title: NHC Flow Data Tab
docs.text:
The NHC Flow Data tab shows data for non-hydrocarbon liquid meters.

This tab is not available and is not displayed for Section-type locations.

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - The date for which the data is applicable. This is dependent on Contract Day, Contract Hour and Resolution. For Hourly Resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for. For Daily Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day. For Monthly Resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Codes - These can be meter events, alarms, analysis changes or other items as selected on the Rollup Configuration Editor. FLOWCAL calculates these at the hourly, daily, monthly, calendar and batch level. The user can choose which ones will appear by going to System Rollup Configuration and checking or unchecking options in the Activity Codes section.
  • Pressure - Average meter Pressure for the meter. Average static Pressure for the location.
  • Temperature - Average meter Temperature for the meter. Average Temperature for the location.
  • IV - This is the total Indicated Volume for the period.
  • GSV - This is the total Gross Standard Volume for the period, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj GSV - This is the Adjusted Total Gross Standard Volume for the period. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • NSV - This is the Total Net Standard Volume for the period, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj NSV - This is the Total Net Standard Volume for the period. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Mass - This is the Total Mass for the Period, including PPAs.
  • S&W % - Average Sediment and Water Percentage for the period.
  • SWV - This is the Sediment and Water Volume for the period, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj. SWV - This is the Sediment and Water Volume for the period. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Eqv Gas Vol - This is the Equivalent Gas Volume. This only appears for products that are Table E. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Summed Comp Volume - This is the Sum of Component Volumes, excluding PPAs. It includes CPAs.
  • Adj Summed Comp Volume - This is the Adjusted Sum of Component Volumes. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Eqv Energy - This is the Equivalent Gas Energy. This only appears for products that are Table E. It includes PPAs and CPAs.
  • Completion - Indicates whether all data is present for a record. When viewing data for a location, if any of the members is missing data for the time frame indicated by the effective date, the status will be marked as "Incomplete".
  • GMS Date - This is the date that the data was written to the database.
