docs.title: PPA - Meas Tab
docs.text:
The PPA - Meas tab shows Prior Period Adjustments, if any were made.

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - The date for which the data is applicable.  This is dependent on contract day, contract hour and resolution.  For hourly resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for.  For daily resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day.  For monthly resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Code - This column will display whether or not any of the activity codes enabled under System Rollup Configuration are present for the device for a given period. The column will be highlighted an amber color if it is populated by anything and the code associated with the activity record(s) will appear. Right-clicking on a row will display the code and the associated trigger at the bottom of the context menu.
  • Closed Volume - The volume reported for the meter or location at closing for the specified time.
  • PPA Volume - The adjusted change in volume recorded for a meter or location after it has been closed.
  • Adjusted Total Volume - The total PPA volume plus rollup volume. The current volume reported for the meter or location for the specified time. This is the value after all adjustments have been applied to the closed volume.
  • PPA Energy - The change in energy recorded for a meter or location after it has been closed.
  • Adjusted Total Energy - The current energy reported for the meter or location for the specified time. This is the value after all adjustments have been applied to the closed energy. The total PPA Energy plus rollup energy.
  • Closed Mass - The mass reported for the meter or location at closing for the specified time.
  • PPA Mass - The adjusted change in mass recorded for a meter or location after it has been closed.
  • Adjusted Total Mass - The current mass reported for the meter or location for the specified time. This is the value after all adjustments have been applied to the closed mass.
  • Completion Status - Indicates whether or not there is missing data.  If there is no missing data for the time span, the completion status will be complete; otherwise, the completion status will be incomplete.
  • GMS Date - The date that the data was written to the database.

docs.title: Standard Tab
docs.text:
The Standard tab shows data calculated at base conditions based on the system-wide base conditions entered in System Factors.

The following items are available on this tab:

  • Effective Date - This is the date for which the data is applicable. This is dependent on contract day, contract hour and resolution. For hourly resolution, the effective date will be the day and hour the data is effective for. For daily resolution, the effective date will be at the contract hour for the given day. For monthly resolution, the effective date will be at the contract day and hour for the given month.
  • Activity Code - This column will display whether or not any of the activity codes enabled under System Rollup Configuration are present for the device for a given period. The column will be highlighted an amber color if it is populated by anything and the code associated with the activity record(s) will appear. Right-clicking on a row will display the code and the associated trigger at the bottom of the context menu.
  • Volume - This is the total volume including PPAs for the meter or location for the stated time span.
  • Energy - This is the energy reported by the meter for the stated time span.
  • Mass - This is the mass reported by the meter for the stated time span.
  • Extension or Raw Volume - The Extension is reported for AGA-3 meters. Raw Volume is reported for AGA-7 meters.
  • Flow Time - This is the time (hours, min, sec) where there was flow for the stated time span.
  • Differential Pressure or Pulses - Differential Pressure is displayed for AGA-3 meters, while Total Pulses or Frequency are shown for AGA-7 meters.
  • Pressure - This is the average static pressure for the meter or location at the given time.
  • Temperature - This is the average flowing temperature for a meter or location at the given time.
  • Completion Status - Indicates whether or not there is missing data. If there is no missing data for the time span, the completion status will be complete; otherwise, the completion status will be incomplete.
  • GMS Date - This is the date that data was written to the database.

docs.title: Source Analysis Rollups
docs.text:
The Source Analysis Rollups viewer summarizes gas or liquid quality data to hourly, daily and monthly resolutions for a wide selection of time frames. By default, the viewing parameters are daily resolution and previous contract month on a single source. Data will only be visible if the source has Enabled Rollups checked on the Main tab in the Quality Source editor and Type is set to Chromatograph on the Characteristic tab.

To access the Source Analysis Rollups viewer: Go to **Open** \> **Rollup Viewers** \> **Source Analysis Rollups**. You may view a single source or a list of sources. If you select a list, you can use the **Next** and **Previous** buttons to navigate through the list. - Click the **Show** button to identify where the source has data to view. - Click the **Open** button to open the appropriate Source Analysis Editor (liquid or gas) on the selected source. - Click the **Unrolled Data** button to display the Rollup Queue Viewer. - Click the **Refresh** button to update the display for the selected time frame. Print the graph by going to **File** \> **Print**.

docs.title: Analysis Overrides
docs.text:
Standalone samples are also used in FLOWCAL in an operation called Sample Override. The user can do a Sample Override on Meter Batches and Standalone Tickets. A meter or location can be assigned to have an LQ applied, but the user can choose to do a sample override and assign a specific standalone sample to a meter batch or a liquid inventory or tank location.

Apply Sample to a Batch

To perform a sample override on meter batch tickets, select one or more batches from the Volume Editor, right-click and hover over the Batch menu item, then select Sample Override. A Sample Assignment Window will appear where the user can choose between Source Quality analyses, or Sample Quality analyses. To apply a sample quality: 1. Select the **Sample Quality** radio button. 2. Choose a time frame that encompasses the sample to be applied. 3. Click **Refresh**. 4. Check the **Selection** checkbox for the sample to apply. 5. Choose an edit reason. 6. Choose whether to apply the sample as C6+, C7+, C8+, C9+ or C10+. 7. Select an Apply Density value from an LQ sample (API Degrees, Absolute Density, or Relative Density) to be used in the apply process for tickets (not available for meters). 8. Click **OK**.

Apply Sample to a Standalone Ticket

The same sample override operation can also be performed on standalone tickets: 1. Select one or more tickets from the Ticket Search or Ticket Editor window. 2. Right-click and select **Attach Analysis**. 3. Select the **Sample Quality** radio button. 4. Choose a time frame that encompasses the sample to be applied. 5. Click **Refresh**. 6. Check the **Selection** checkbox for the sample to apply. 7. Choose an edit reason. 8. Choose whether to apply the sample as C6+, C7+, C8+, C9+ or C10+. 9. Select an Apply Density value from an LQ sample (API Degrees, Absolute Density, or Relative Density) to be used in the apply process for tickets (not available for meters). 10. Click **OK**.

docs.title: Sample Analysis Editor
docs.text:
The Sample Analysis Editor contains a detailed layout for hydrocarbon and non-hydrocarbon analysis samples. The Sample Analysis Editor includes a Mole %, Mass %, and LV % component breakdown for hydrocarbon sources, and a NHC Mole %, NHC Mass %, and NHC LV % component breakdown for non-hydrocarbon sources.

For hydrocarbon samples, users can enter Mole %, Mass %, or LV % values, and FLOWCAL will then calculate other properties, such as densities in different units (top right), component Mole %, Mass %, and/or LV %. All calculations are performed based on the Characteristics. Calculations will not occur for non-hydrocarbon sample analysis.

Users can also set a hydrocarbon or non-hydrocarbon liquids product designation for the sample, which is used during LQ apply operations to ensure that like products are applied between the product in the sample and the product in the meter data or batch. FLOWCAL will not perform a sample apply for disparate products. Options on the sample analysis editor will vary depending on the product fluid service (hydrocarbon or non-hydrocarbon). The Sample Analysis Editor grid will not change if you are viewing a non-hydrocarbon sample.

To enter a new sample source analysis: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Sample Analysis**. 2. Click the **New Detail** button at the bottom of the **Sample Quality Editor**. 3. Click **Edit**. 4. Enter the sample date. 5. Enter the Sample IDThe Sample ID is unique across all standalone samples in a FLOWCAL database. This is in contrast to liquid quality source samples, whose unique identification is the LQ number and sample date. The Sample ID can contain up to 25 characters and is required for all standalone samples.. 6. Enter the Quality information. 7. Click **Save**. | | | | |----|----|----| | Hydrocarbon Sample Interface |   | Non-Hydrocarbon Sample Interface | | |   | |

docs.title: Screen Details
docs.text:
Override Options

- **HC Property Override** - Allows users to select a given set of GPA TP-17 hydrocarbon properties to be used in calculations, including user-defined sets. - **Base Density Calc Method** - Allows users to override the default density calculation based on HC properties and GPA-2145 constants. Options are COSTALD, Modified TP-2, and REFPROP. This field is disabled for non-hydrocarbon sample analyses.

Base Density Calc Method (Hydrocarbon Samples Only)

Base Density Calc Method allows the user to override the default density calculation based on HC Properties and GPA-2145 constants. Options are COSTALD, Modified TP-2, and REFPROP. If a Product using Table-E (TP-27) or Table E Extended (TP-27 EXT) table is designated on the sample, the Base Density Calc Method will automatically be populated with the Default Base Density Calculation set on the Product. The user will still have the ability to manually select a Base Density Calc Method to be used for the sample density calculation. | Sample Density Calc Method Defined for Product? | Base Density Calc Method Defined? | Base Density Calculation Method Used | |:--:|:--:|----| | Y | N | Product default source base density calc | | Y | Y | Text file or manual entry record base density calc method | | N | Y | Text file or manual entry record base density calc method | | N | N | Default to current behavior - Use HC Properties |

C6+ Extended (Hydrocarbon Samples Only)

To access C6+ Extended: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis**. 2. Select **Gas Quality**. 3. Select **Source Analysis**. 4. Click **New Detail**. 5. Enter **To** and **From** dates. 6. Click the **C6+ Extended** button. The user may also specify the C6+ Component Breakdown for a given sample by clicking on the button. This feature allows the user to account for the presence of C7 through C*(n)* in a given sample that has mole percent components up to C6. To allow FLOWCAL to calculate an accurate density and molecular weight for the sample, the minimum data point set to populate is the Molar Mass and Absolute Density of the C6+ components. The default set of Extended Characteristics assumes that the C6 composition provided is only C6. A C6+ split can be defined for standalone samples by going to the System Factors Editor (Admin **→** System Options → System Factors) and specifying a split there.

Source Apply Considerations

For the Source Apply process, the meter or location and source must have the same unit set (US or SI). A "Unit Set Discrepancy" exception is generated if both the meter or location and the source are not in the same unit set. This exception is also generated if the temperature base and pressure base of the meter or location are not in the same unit set. FLOWCAL does not apply the purity sample from the product to any records where an LQ Assignment is set for the meter or location during the time frame of that record. This allows users to use the sample product in FLOWCAL as a purity and a non-purity product on a per meter or location basis. For example: Meter 1 will use Propane as a purity, so Meter 1 will not have a Quality Source assigned. The purity sample will automatically apply onto the records for that meter. Meter 2 will be used as a non-purity propane meter, so Meter 2 will have a LQ Source Assignment setup. The purity sample will not apply to any records during the duration of the assignment. A sample must be applied through either the Source Assignment, or a Sample Override If a density value is not found as per the Apply Density option, FLOWCAL uses the next available density. In other words, the process fails over to using a sample density value in the order depicted in the table below. An exception is generated if a density value is used that is not the first Apply Density choice. If no density value is found even after the fail over process, then another exception is generated alerting the user about the lack of a density value. | Apply Density Option | First Failover | Second Failover | |----------------------|------------------|------------------| | Relative Density | API Gravity | Absolute Density | | API Gravity | Relative Density | Absolute Density | | Absolute Density | Relative Density | API Gravity | Applying a source/sample performs as follows when applying density to tickets: - **For Observed Temperature:** - If the user chooses to apply density and the ticket it set to Absolute Density, the Observed Temperature is set to the Base Temperature of the Sample. - If the user chooses not to apply a density at all, the Observed Temperature is not modified. - **For Observed Pressure:** - If the user chooses to apply density and the ticket is set to Gauge Density, the Observed Pressure is set to 0.0. - If the user chooses to apply density and the ticket it set to Absolute Density, the Observed Pressure is set to the Base Pressure of the Sample. - If the user chooses not to apply a density at all, the Observed Pressure is not modified.

C+ Type “Apply Extended As” Rules

Standalone samples do not currently support anything other than C6+, so C6+ extended characteristics will always be applied with a standalone sample. Standalone samples also do not currently support having a full analysis, so the sample will always be applied as-is. In the Quality Source Analysis Editor, if the “Has Extended Analysis” option is selected, FLOWCAL will follow the "Apply Extended As" value defined under **Volume Editor** \> **Characteristic** \> **Batch Sample Override**. Example If a sample contains a full analysis (220 components) that goes out to C10, and the “Apply Extended As” option in any of the three places listed above is set to C6+, FLOWCAL will sum the values from C6 to C10 and apply the sum to C6. FLOWCAL will also apply the C6+ extended characteristics. If the “Has Extended Analysis” option is not selected, FLOWCAL will apply the sample as it is given on the source and will apply the extended characteristics for the highest component that has a value. If the highest component that has a value is less that C6, the C6+ extended characteristics will be applied.

docs.title: Sample Quality Editor
docs.text:
The Sample Quality Editor displays analysis samples in descending chronological order for a specified time frame. By default, the Sample Quality Editor displays the most recent month of samples.

To enter a new sample: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Sample Analyses**. 2. Click the **New Detail** button at the bottom of the **Sample Quality Editor** screen. This editor contains a detailed layout of a hydrocarbon analysis sample. 3. You can enter Mole %, Mass % or LV % and have FLOWCAL calculate the other properties for the sample such as densities in different units (top right), component Mole %, Mass % and/or LV % etc. All calculations are done according to the source characteristics. 4. You can also set a liquids product designation for the sample which in turn is used during LQ apply operations to make sure that like products are applied between the Product in the sample and the product in the meter data or batch. FLOWCAL will not do a sample apply of two disparate products.

Screen Details

The following tabs are available on the Sample Analysis Editor screen: - **Quality** - Specification of quality characteristics such as product, molar mass, relative density, etc. (Alt+Q) - **Mole %** - Sample breakdown or composition in Mole %. (Alt+M) - **Mass %** - Sample breakdown or composition in Mass %. (Alt+A) - **LV %** - Sample breakdown or composition in LV %. (Alt+L) - **C6+** - Specification of C6+ extended characteristics such as molar mass, absolute density, relative density, etc. (Alt+C) - **Sample** - Sample attributes such as sample pressure, temperature, atmospheric pressure, etc. (Alt+S) - **Custom** - User-defined fields. (Alt+U) - **Edit Reasons** - Edit reasons allows the user to see who changed a sample, when it was changed, and the reason for changing the sample. (Alt+E) HC Properties Override allows the user to select a given set of GPA TP-17 hydrocarbon properties to be used in calculations, including user-defined sets.

docs.title: Source Analysis
docs.text:
The Set Points calculator requires the Validation Set Points module. Without it, you can manually enter validation parameters in the Source Editor for each source.

FLOWCAL uses built-in validation set points to identify data anomalies. These set points are based on limits imposed by various calculation standards. They can also be added to meters and quality sources to flag data that is outside of normal operating boundaries.

Set points can be calculated for multiple sources at a time using the Validation Set Points calculator for Source Analysis, based on each source’s historical data. Validation set points are determined based on data in a specified date range and the percentage of data to be flagged. To ensure that valid set points are calculated, this should only be used once data has been reviewed and verified.

Validation set points are logged to the Validation History if the "Log Validation Set Points History" option is enabled in FLOWCAL Configuration. To view the set point history, open the Source Editor, select the Validations tab, and click Show History.

To access the Source Analysis Set Point Calculator: Go to **Review** \> **Set Points** \> **Source Analysis**.

Validation Set Points Details

The following items are available on the Validation Set Points screen: - **Source/Source List** - Select whether to analyze data for a source or a list of sources. - **Analyze From/To** - Specify a date range of data to analyze. - **Percent Flagged** - This field establishes where the set points will be calculated relative to the data used. The percentage of data to be flagged is defaulted to 0.001%, which means that based on historical data, 0.001% of the user's data should be flagged with an exception in the future. The closer this value is to zero, the closer the set points will be to the minimum and maximum data values for each parameter. When setting these set points for the first time, it is recommended that you use .001%, so that you are not overwhelmed with exceptions. - **Override Pre-Existing Values** - If this option is checked, the value calculated for the set point will be used in place of previously calculated values. If the option is not checked, values that were previously calculated or manually entered will not be overwritten. - **Run on Imports and Edits** - Check this option to activate the set points. - **Run Min/Run Max** - For each parameter, select whether to calculate the minimum or maximum values. - **Clear All** - Uncheck all parameters on the selected tab. - **Check All** - Check all parameters on the selected tab. - **Run** - Calculate and save the set points for every meter in the list, location, or close group. Go to the Validations tab in the Meter Editor to view the calculated set points.

docs.title: Analysis Tab
docs.text:
Use the Analysis sub-tab to configure validation settings for the meter analysis data.

Set Dead Band Factors

To prevent excessive exceptions resulting from set points that are too tight, you can specify a dead band. Click the **Set** button to access the Dead Band screen. The dead band calculation for Flowing Analysis is based on a percentage difference between the minimum and maximum values calculated. The dead band value entered in the Dead Band Factors screen is the fraction of the difference to be added to the maximum or subtracted from the minimum calculated values. To perform the calculation: 1. Calculate minimum and maximum values for the field (ethane, propane, helium, etc.) for the given percentage to be flagged. 2. If dead band values are to be ignored, no further calculations are needed, and the numbers in step 1 will be used; otherwise, determine the difference between the maximum value and the minimum value and multiply this difference by the appropriate dead band factor. This yields an amount to subtract from the minimum or add to the maximum from step 1. The offset for the minimum and maximum values must be greater than the minimum allowed dead band value. This is fixed for every parameter. 3. For each field, minimum and maximum values may exist. For example, ethane is not allowed to go below 0. If the number calculated in step 2 falls outside the boundaries established, the result is set to this value. Thus, if the ethane value fell below 0, 0 would be used instead. Example 1: Suppose that in step 1, the minimum and maximum values for ethane are calculated as 0.2 and 7.5, respectively. The difference is 7.3. Suppose that a dead band factor of 1.0 is used for the minimum, and a dead band factor of 0.1 is used for the maximum. Multiplying the difference by the appropriate dead band factor yields the following: 7.3 X 1.0 = 7.3 (minimum) 7.3 X 0.1 = .73 (maximum) Subtracting the numbers from the appropriate values for each yields the following: 0.2 - 7.3 = -7.1 (minimum) 7.5 + .73 = 8.23 (maximum) For ethane, 0 is the lowest value allowed, so 0 will be used instead of the calculated minimum (-7.1). The maximum allowed ethane value is 100. Since 8.23 is less than 100, that value will be used. Example 2: Suppose that in step 1, the minimum and maximum values for DP are calculated as 10.0 and 10.05, respectively. The difference is 0.05. Suppose that a dead band factor of 1.0 is used for the minimum, and a dead band factor of 0.1 is used for the maximum. Multiplying the difference by the appropriate dead band factor yields the following: 0.05 X 1.0 = 0.05 (minimum) 0.05 X 0.1 = 0.005 (maximum) The minimum offset for ethane is 0.02, so for the maximum, 0.021 would be used instead of 0.005. Subtracting the numbers from the appropriate values for each yields the following: 10.0 - 0.05 = 9.95 (minimum) 10.5 + 0.02 = 10.52 (maximum) These values fall within the minimum and maximum allowed values, so these values will be used. docs.title: Expert Systems Tab
docs.text:
Expert system validations use statistical analysis of historical data to identify uncharacteristic changes in a meter's data flow pattern. A valid range of lower and upper bounds is calculated using a running or weighted average of previous records. Specify the number of previous records used for this average using the field in the upper right corner of the Expert Systems tab.

If a value in a record being imported falls outside of this range, an exception will be generated.

If the specified date range does not contain values for the main data point (volume for volumetric calculation method; mass for mass calculation method), set points will not be calculated for the meter and will not be set in the Meter Editor. If values are not provided for the Average Count and Step fields, default values are used to calculate set points.

docs.title: Gas Meters
Liquid Meters
docs.text:
Set Dead Band Factors

To prevent excessive exceptions resulting from set points that are too tight, you can specify a dead band. Click the **Set** button to access the Dead Band screen. The dead band calculation for Expert Systems validations varies depending on whether percent difference or standard deviation is to be used for generation of exceptions. To perform the calculation: 1. In both cases, appropriate values are calculated for the field (DP, pressure, volume, etc.) for the given percentage to be flagged. 2. If dead band values are to be ignored, no further calculations are needed, and the numbers in step 1 will be used; otherwise, otherwise, one of the following methods will be used: - For **standard deviation**, the value calculated in step 1 is multiplied by 1 + the dead band factor entered. - For **percent difference**, the value calculated in step 1 is multiplied by the dead band factor entered. Example 1: In step 1, percent difference is used for DP, with a dead band factor of 1.2. A value of 52.4 is calculated. Multiplying 52.4 by 1.2 yields 62.88. That resulting value would be stored in the database. Example 2: In step 1, standard deviation is used for volume, with a dead band factor of 0.05. A value of 4.8 is calculated. Multiplying 4.8 by 1 + 0.05 yields 5.04. That resulting value would be stored in the database.

docs.title: Final Form Tab
Min/Max Sub-Tab
docs.text:
While other validation set points are calculated using periodic data, final form validations allow users to validate that hourly, daily, and monthly totals for volume, energy, mass, and net standard volume fall within defined set points.

The Set Point calculator for final form min/max validations requires that the user specify whether the set points should be run against measured conditions, standard conditions, or both.

docs.title: Expert Systems Sub-Tab
docs.text:
The final form expert systems validations apply expert system validations to hourly and daily totals for volume, energy, mass, and net standard volume.

The following options are available:

  • Comparison Type - Specified as percent difference or standard deviation. The set point calculator will calculate both, but when validating data, it will use the type specified here.
  • For percent difference, the set point calculated is the percentage difference between the average of the current record and records prior to the current record.
  • For standard deviations, the set point calculated is the number of standard deviations that can exist between the current record and the average without an exception being generated.
  • Data Window -The number of records prior to the record being analyzed, to be used for the average.
  • Average Method - Specified as running or weighted. A running average treats each record the same when calculating the average. A weighted average gives more weight to records closer to the current record when calculating the average.
  • Closed Data Only - If this option is checked, only closed data will be used in the calculation.

docs.title: Flowing Parameters Tab
General Sub-Tab
docs.text:
Use the Flowing Parameters sub-tab to define minimum and maximum limits on values for the flow variable (DP or pulses), static pressure, temperature, volume, energy NSV, mass, flow basis (extension, raw volume), volume correlation factor (VCF), speed of sound, and flow time.

If a liquid meter uses a volumetric measurement, NSV can be validated; otherwise, mass can be validated.

Do not create no-flow exceptions - Check this option to prevent validations from being run on meters with no flow.

docs.title: Ultrasonic 2 Sub-Tab
docs.text:
This tab is only available for ultrasonic meters. The following options are available:

  • Speed of Sound
  • Duration (Hours) - The time frame in hours that set point calculations are performed for. This field is required; values must be greater than or equal to 0. For the List/Location Set Point calculator, if the duration has already been set at the meter level, that value is used.
  • Percent Difference Allowed - The percent difference by which the set point calculations may vary. This field allows values between 0 and 100, and will accommodate two decimal places. This calculation is based on the Duration (Hours) value and the percentage of data to be flagged.
  • Variance Using - When performing the variance validation for speed of sound, the variance can be specified as a unit difference or a percent difference.
  • Profile
  • Baseline - A user-defined value that is the target value of the calculated profile. This field is required; values must be greater than or equal to 0 and can have up to four decimal places. For the List/Location Set Point Calculator, if the value has already been set at the meter level, that value is used.

  • Percent Difference Allowed - A comparison between the profile baseline and the calculated baseline. This is the percent of variance allowed before an exception is generated.

    Example

    <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Profile Pct Difference">

| Calculated Profile From UFM Periodic Data | Baseline | Percent Difference Allowed | Percent Difference Calculated/Baseline | Exception Generated? |
|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| 5.02 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((5.02/5.095)-1)\*100 = <span style="color: #008000; font-weight: bold;">-1.472%</span> | <span style="color: #008000; font-weight: bold;">No</span> |
| 6 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((6/5.095)-1)\*100 = <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">17.763%</span> | <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">Yes</span> |
| 4 | 5.095 | 1.7% | ((4/5.095)-1)\*100 = <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">21.492%</span> | <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">Yes</span> |



</div>

</div>
    • Symmetry
    • Baseline - A user-defined value that is the target value of the calculated symmetry.

    • Percent Difference Allowed - A comparison between the symmetry baseline and the calculated baseline. It is the percent of variance allowed before an exception is generated.

      Example

      <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example-Symmetry Pct Difference">

| Calculated Profile From UFM Periodic Data | Baseline | Percent Difference Allowed | Percent Difference Calculated/Baseline | Exception Generated? |
|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| 1.001 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((1.001/1.0001)-1)\*100 = <span style="color: #008000; font-weight: bold;">-0.089%</span> | <span style="color: #008000; font-weight: bold;">No</span> |
| 0.9 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((0.9/1.0001)-1)\*100 = <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">-10.009%</span> | <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">Yes</span> |
| 1.1 | 1.0001 | 1.25% | ((1.1/1.0001)-1)\*100 = <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">9.989%</span> | <span style="color: #ff0000; font-weight: bold;">Yes</span> |



</div>

</div>

      Calculation Sequence

      The set point calculations for ultrasonic meters occur in the following order: 1. The process does nothing if there is no data in the time frame selected. A warning will display indicating that there is no data. 2. A percent difference is calculated for each data point within the Analyze From/To date range. 3. The number of data points are multiplied by the percentage of data to be flagged. The value is then rounded down and the result is the number of data points that should exceed the set point. Example There are 110 data points and the percentage of data to be flagged is 5%. 110\*0.05 = 5.5, so 5 data points should exceed the set point. The calculated set point will be the next highest data point following the values that exceed the set point. Using the same example, since five data points should exceed the set point, the calculated set point will be the sixth highest data point in the set.

      Set Dead Band Factors

      To prevent excessive exceptions resulting from set points that are too tight, you can specify a dead band. Click the **Set** button to access the Dead Band screen. The dead band calculation for Flowing Parameters is based on a percentage difference between the minimum and maximum values calculated. The dead band value entered in the Dead Band Factors screen is the fraction of the difference to be added to the maximum or subtracted from the minimum calculated values. To perform the calculation: 1. Calculate minimum and maximum values for the field (DP, pressure, volume, energy, etc.) for the given percentage to be flagged. 2. If dead band values are to be ignored, no further calculations are needed, and the numbers in step 1 will be used; otherwise, determine the difference between the maximum value and the minimum value and multiply this difference by the appropriate dead band factor. This yields an amount to subtract from the minimum or add to the maximum from step 1. The offset for the minimum and maximum values must be greater than the minimum allowed dead band value. This is fixed for every parameter. 3. For each field, minimum and maximum values may exist. For example, DP is not allowed to go below 0. If the number calculated in step 2 falls outside the boundaries established, the result is set to this value. Thus, if the DP value fell below 0, 0 would be used instead. Example Example 1 Suppose that in step 1, the minimum and maximum values for DP are calculated as 38.759 and 85.099, respectively. The difference is 46.34. Suppose that a dead band factor of 1.0 is used for the minimum, and a dead band factor of 0.1 is used for the maximum. Multiplying the difference by the appropriate dead band factor yields the following: 46.34 X 1.0 = 46.34 (minimum) 46.34 X 0.1 = 4.634 (maximum) Subtracting the numbers from the appropriate values for each yields the following: 38.759 - 46.34 = -7.581 (minimum) 85.099 + 4.634 = 89.733 (maximum) For DP, 0 is the lowest value allowed, so 0 will be used instead of the calculated minimum (-7.581). The maximum allowed DP value is 1000. Since 89.733 is less than 1000, that value will be used. Example 2 Suppose that in step 1, the minimum and maximum values for DP are calculated as 10.0 and 10.5, respectively. The difference is 0.5. SSuppose that a dead band factor of 1.0 is used for the minimum, and a dead band factor of 0.1 is used for the maximum. Multiplying the difference by the appropriate dead band factor yields the following: 0.5 X 1.0 = 0.5 (minimum) 0.5 X 0.1 = 0.05 (maximum) The minimum offset for DP is 0.1, so for the maximum, 0.1 would be used instead of 0.05. Subtracting the numbers from the appropriate values for each yields the following: 10.0 - 0.5 = 9.5 (minimum) 10.5 + 0.1 = 10.6 (maximum) These values fall within the minimum and maximum allowed values, so these values will be used. Minimum Offset Values for Flowing Parameter Fields | Field | Minimum Offset | |:---------------------:|:--------------:| | Pulses | 0.1 | | Differential Pressure | 0.1 | | Raw Volume | 0.1 | | Extension | 0.1 | | Pressure | 1 | | Temperature | 1 | | Volume | 1 | | Energy | 1 | | VCF | 0.01 | Minimum and Maximum Allowed Values for Flowing Parameter Fields | Field | Minimum | Maximum | |:---------------------:|:-------:|:-------:| | Pulses | 0 | 1.8 E+8 | | Differential Pressure | 0 | 1000 | | Raw Volume | 0 | 1.0 E+8 | | Extension | 0.25 | 4500 | | Pressure | 0 | 20000 | | Temperature | -160 | 400 | | Volume | 0 | 1.0 E+8 | | Energy | 0 | 1.0 E+8 | | VCF | 0 | 2 |

docs.title: Validation Set Points
Meter List/Location
docs.text:
The Set Points calculator requires the Validation Set Points module. Without it, you can manually enter validation parameters on the Meter Editor Validation tab for each meter.

FLOWCAL uses built-in validation set points to identify data anomalies. These set points are based on limits imposed by various calculation standards. They can also be added to meters and quality sources to flag data that is outside of normal operating boundaries.

Set points can be calculated for multiple meters at a time using the Validation Set Points calculator for Lists, Locations, and Close Groups, based on each meter’s historical data. Validation set points are determined based on data in a specified date range and the percentage of data to be flagged. To ensure that valid set points are calculated, this should only be used once data has been reviewed and verified.

Validation set points are logged to the Validation History. You can view the set point history on the Validations tab of the Meter Editor.

To access the Validation Set Points screen: Go to **Review** \> **Set Points** \> **Meter List/Location**. Only data points applicable to the given meter type are displayed and calculated.

Validation Set Points Details

The following items are available on the Validation Set Points screen: - **System and Object Selector** - Select whether to analyze data for a list, location, or close group. - **Analyze From/To** - Specify a date range of data to analyze. - **Percentage of data to be flagged** - This field establishes where the set points will be calculated relative to the data used. The percentage of data to be flagged is defaulted to 0.001%, which means that based on historical data, 0.001% of the user's data should be flagged with an exception in the future. The closer this value is to zero, the closer the set points will be to the minimum and maximum data values for each parameter. When setting these set points for the first time, it is recommended that you use .001%, so that you are not overwhelmed with exceptions. - **Do Not Scale by Flow Time** - If this option is checked, data will not be scaled based on the flow time. Example If the volume was 15 for an hour, but the flow time was only 30 minutes, then validation set point calculations will still use 15 for the volume. If this option is not checked, then the volume will be scaled to one hour of flow time. Using the same example, the validation set point calculations will use 30 for the volume instead of 15. Scaling only applies to accumulated fields such as volume, energy, and pulse count; scaling cannot be applied to averaged fields such as pressure or differential pressure. - **Override Pre-Existing Values** - If this option is checked, the value calculated for the set point will be used in place of previously calculated values. If the option is not checked, values that were previously calculated or manually entered will not be overwritten. - **Run on Imports and Edits** - Check this option to activate the set points. - **Run Min/Run Max** - For each parameter, select whether to calculate the minimum or maximum values. - **Clear All** - Uncheck all parameters on the selected tab. - **Check All** - Check all parameters on the selected tab. - **Run** - Calculate and save the set points for every meter in the list, location, or close group. Go to the Validations tab in the Meter Editor to view the calculated set points.

docs.title: Single Run Tab
docs.text:
Single run validations are useful for meter data that should not experience large changes from one record to the next or from one day to the next.

The Set Point Calculator for single run validations requires you to specify whether the calculations should be run against the previous record or previous day, as well as whether to calculate the set points as a percent difference or as a unit difference.

The following options are available:

  • Prev Record - The set point calculation will be done by comparing each record within the specified date range to the prior record.

  • Prev Day - The set point calculation will be done by comparing each record within the specified date range to the prior record at the same time of day. Example If the current record being evaluated is March 10, 2015 10:00:00, it would be compared to March 9, 2015 10:00:00. When the previous day is selected, the difference between records will be calculated and used to calculate the set points.

  • Percent Difference - The set point calculated will be a percentage change between records.

  • Unit Difference - The set point calculated will be the numeric difference between records.

Set Dead Band Factors

To prevent excessive exceptions resulting from set points that are too tight, you can specify a dead band. Click the **Set** button to access the Dead Band screen. The dead band calculation for Single Run validations is calculated by multiplying the dead band factor provided by the calculated minimum or maximum value. To perform the calculation: 1. Calculate minimum and maximum values for the field (DP, pressure, volume, etc.) for the given percentage to be flagged. 2. If dead band values are to be ignored, no further calculations are needed, and the numbers in step 1 will be used; otherwise, determine the difference between the maximum value and the minimum value and multiply this difference by the appropriate dead band factor. This yields an amount to subtract from the minimum or add to the maximum from step 1. Example Suppose that in step 1, the minimum and maximum values for DP are calculated as 40.0 and 60.0, respectively. Suppose that a dead band factor of 1.2 is used for the minimum, and a dead band factor of 0.8 is used for the maximum. Multiplying the difference by the appropriate dead band factor yields the following: 40.0 X 1.2 = 48.0 (minimum) 60.0 X 0.8 = 48.0 (maximum) As the results show, entering value of less than 1.0 has the effect of decreasing the dead band.

docs.title: Annual Schedule Editor
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires Application Process – FLOWCAL Options privileges.

Use the Annual Schedule Editor to create schedules for an entire year. The Annual Schedule Editor allows you to:

  • Define specific batch dates for liquid meters - Some batches run on a schedule that varies from month to month and year to year. For example: A batch may run every Monday, unless Monday is a holiday or is close to the start of the month or end of the month (Meter Editor > Liquids tab > Schedules sub-tab > Monthly Schedule selection).
  • Print chart levels for scheduled chart routes for gas meters - A schedule is used to specify the on and off dates for the charts, which is used when printing the Bar Code Labels report (Meter Editor > Imports tab > Chart Change Schedule selection).
  • Define schedules for weekly location rollups - Location rollups can calculate weekly final form data for a location if the Calculate Weekly Totals option is enabled within System Configuration, and a weekly schedule is defined for a location. Weekly totals do not have to be seven days of data; this customized time span is defined using the Annual Schedule Editor (Location Editor > Info menu > Weekly Schedule selection).
To create an annual schedule: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Annual Schedule Editor** within the **Application** group. 3. Select a year. The year cannot be changed once you enter edit mode. Each year must be created and edited individually. 4. Click the **New** button. 5. Enter a schedule name. 6. Double-click the days you want to include in the schedule. Selected days will display with a yellow highlight. To de-select a day, double-click it again. 7. Click the **Save** button.

docs.title: Custom Fields
docs.text:
The Custom Fields screen allows an administrator to designate labels for custom fields available in screens throughout the FLOWCAL application, such as the Meter Editor, Source Analysis Editor, and Location Editor. Custom fields are also available for history records, such as flow data (periodic) and source analysis.

Custom fields accommodate data that is specific to a user’s company and that may not be standard in FLOWCAL.

Example In the Meter Editor, many fields on the Custom Fields tab can be edited, as well as other fields available on the General tab. To access the Custom Fields screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Custom Fields** within the **Application** group.

Administrators must have Application Process – FLOWCAL Options privileges, granted from the User or Group Access screen.

Button and Tab Details

The following options are available on the Custom Fields screen: - **Edit** - Enable edit mode and specify field names. - **Save** - Save changes to field names. - **Table** - Create drop-down values for custom field tabs where drop-downs are supported. - **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not save changes. - **Exit** - Exit the Custom Fields screen. Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-30 are text fields

Meter > General Tab

Visible from: Setup > Meter > Editor > General tab

Data format:  Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Field 1 – City; Custom Field 2 – County; Custom Field 3 – State; Custom Field 4 – County

Meter > Custom Fields Tab

Visible from: Setup > Meter > Editor > Custom Fields tab

Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-60 are text fields

Meter Characteristics

Visible from: Open > Volume Editor > Characteristic > Periodic or Daily tab > Custom Fields sub-tab

Data format: Edit fields and drop-downs; Custom Fields 1-30 are text fields

Meter Edit Approval

Visible from: Review > Approvals

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-4 are Yes/No (Y/N) fields

Meter Periodic Values

For meter periodic values, the administrator can also define the rollup action to be performed by the Meter Rollup service for the custom fields. If a rollup action is not defined, the Meter Rollup service will roll up the last available value by default. If a meter is configured as a helium meter (Meter Editor > General tab), the Meter Rollups service will always sum Custom Fields 1-5, regardless of the rollup action defined for those fields.

Note

Visible from: Right-clicking in various screens, such as Volume Editor, Exception Resolver, Meter Editor, Location Editor, Source Editor, and selecting Add or View Notes

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-4 are text fields

Ticket Periodic Values

Visible from: Open > Tickets > Ticket Editor > Custom Fields tab; or Open > Tickets > Ticket Search > Custom Fields tab

Data format: Edit fields only; Custom Fields 1-8 are text fields; Custom Fields 9-16 are numeric fields

Create Custom Field Labels

To create a custom field label: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **Custom Fields** within the **Application** group. 2. Select a tab and click **Edit**. 3. Click in the **Field Name** field and enter the label. 4. Click **Save**.

Create Custom Drop-Down Fields

To create a custom drop-down field: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **Custom Fields** within the **Application** group. 2. Select a tab and click **Edit**. 3. Click the **Use Drop-Down?** field to enable the option. 4. While the field name is selected, click **Table**. The associated database table and field name will display in the title bar. 5. Click **New**. 6. Enter the drop-down value in the **User Choice** field. 7. Click **Save**. 8. Repeat steps 5 through 7 for each drop-down value. 9. To edit or delete a drop-down value, select the item from the grid and click **Edit** or **Delete**. 10. Click **Exit** to return to the Custom Fields screen.

docs.title: Data Stream Editor
docs.text:
The Data Stream Editor serves as a reference for data collection (SCADA). The information on this screen displays on the Misc. tab of the Meter Editor. This data is informational only and does not trigger any other functionality.

To access the Data Stream Editor and create a new data stream: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Data Stream** within the **Application** group. The Data Stream Editor is also available from the General tab of the Gas or Liquid Quality Source Editor. 3. Click the **New** button to create a new data stream. 4. Enter the code and name at the bottom of the screen. Both of these fields are alphanumeric. Click the **Auto Generate Code** button to automatically increment the current largest code number by 1. 5. Click the **Save** button. Data streams cannot be deleted once they are saved.

docs.title: Edit Reason Editor
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires Application Process - FLOWCAL Options privileges.

In many FLOWCAL editors, you will need to select a reason for an edit before you can save the change. These edit reasons provide context when the reason for revising data (such as equipment failure or crude analysis data) is not obvious.

The Edit Reason Editor allows you to create custom edit reasons that are then available for selection throughout FLOWCAL.

Multiple users can access and edit this screen simultaneously; however, if multiple edits are made to an edit reason at the same time, only the latest set of changes will be saved.

To access the Edit Reason Editor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Edit Reason** within the **Application** group.

Edit Reason Editor Menu Details

Users must have at least **FLOWCAL Options - Can View** privileges to access these options. Additional privileges required for edit, disable/restore, and create functionalities are listed in the corresponding sections. The following options are available in the right-click menu of the Edit Reason Editor: - **Sort Ascending** - Sort notes by the selected column in ascending order. - **Sort Descending** - Sort notes by the selected column in descending order. - **Show Search Panel** – Launch the search panel to show edit reasons with a code or description that match specific criteria.

Create Edit Reasons

This functionality requires **Application Process - FLOWCAL Options - Can View**, **Can Edit**, and **Can Create** privileges. To create a new edit reason: 1. Click the **Add Edit Reason** button. 2. Enter a new edit reason and code. 3. In the Object Type drop-down menu, check the **Meters/Tickets**, **Sources/Samples**, or **Exceptions** checkboxes to make the edit reason available for those object types. 4. Click the **Done** button to save your changes. The Code, Edit Reason, and Object Type fields are all required. If you create an edit reason with a code that has already been assigned, you will not be able to save the edit reason until you enter a unique code. Edit reasons can be modified at any time; however, the code cannot be edited once it has been saved.

Disable/Enable Edit Reasons

This functionality requires **Application Process - FLOWCAL Options - Can View**, **Can Edit**, and **Can Delete** privileges. To disable an edit reason: 1. Select the edit reason to disable. 2. Click the **Delete** button. 3. When prompted to confirm disabling the edit reason, click **Yes**. Disabling edit reasons will hide them but will not delete them from the database. This allows the edit reasons to remain in the database for audit purposes. To enable edit reasons that have been disabled: 1. Click the **Show disabled edit reasons** checkbox. 2. Select the edit reasons that you want to enable. 3. Click the **Restore** button.

Sort Edit Reasons

To sort edit reasons: - Click any column heading in the grid to sort the edit reasons by that parameter. Click the up and down arrows in the column header to change the sort order from descending to ascending. By default, edit reasons are sorted by code number, in descending order. - Change the column order by selecting a column header and dragging and dropping the column to a new location.

Filter Edit Reasons

You can filter edit reasons by a single column or multiple columns. To filter edit reasons by a single column: 1. Hover over a column header until the filter icon displays. 2. Click the filter icon to open the Filter dialog box. 3. Click back on the grid to close the Filter dialog box. Use the filter bar at the bottom of the screen to view or edit the filter directly.

docs.title: Exception Description Editor
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires Application Process – FLOWCAL Options privileges.

Exceptions flag suspect data that has been imported or manually added to a meter, location, source, or ticket. Running validations for a meter after data has been added can also create exceptions.

Use the Exception Description Editor to update exception descriptions, set the severity level for an exception, or specify contacts to notify when an exception is generated.

To access the Exception Description Editor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Exception Description** within the **Application** group. 3. Select an exception and click **Edit**. 4. Edit the exception description data as needed. Only the description and severity are available for editing. 5. Click **Save**.

Exception Description Screen Details

The following items are available on the Exception Description Editor screen: - **Number** - Unique numeric identifier associated with the exception - **Description** - The actual exception text explaining the issue and cause - **Severity** - The priority level defined for the exception; severity levels can range from 1 to 5 (example: 1 could be a normal exception, whereas a 5 could be a critical exception) The Severity setting is application-wide and requires services to be restarted. Setting the severity to "0" will disable the exception for the entire application. Updating exception severity will generate system message 1201 "Exception severity changed". - **Object** - The type of device or object - **Notify** - Contact types to notify when the specified exceptions are generated Existing contact types can be defined for each exception. As exceptions are generated, the contact(s) specified for the device Contact Type will be alerted by email when the exception is generated. Example Jane Doe is defined as Contact Type - Analyst for Meter 5555 within the Meter Editor. In the Exception Description Editor, the Contact Type - Analyst has been configured for Exception Number 12. Anytime exception 12 is generated for Meter 5555, Jane Doe will receive an email alert. - **Edit Criteria button** - This button is only visible when the user selects exceptions 6501-6600. (See: Exception Criteria Editor) The "Disable Exception 'Ignore' when Severity \>" setting on the FLOWCAL Configuration screen can be used to prevent users from acknowledging exceptions with a severity level greater than the level specified. By default, all exceptions have a severity of 1. Setting the severity level of an exception to be greater than the severity level set in FLOWCAL Configuration prevents users from being able to acknowledge that exception. This is useful if there are certain exceptions that should always require user intervention to resolve the exception, rather than just acknowledging it, such as no product on a batch.

Exception Criteria Editor

When processing import data, FLOWCAL checks for string events, user string events or string alarms. If any are detected, FLOWCAL checks to see if any of the user-defined String Event and Alarm (SEA) exceptions (6501 - 6600) have a severity rating greater than 0 and are defined for the corresponding item. If so, the string field from the event or alarm is checked against the defined exception criteria. If it is met, an exception is generated and attached to the periodic record time frame that encompasses the alarm or event. Use the Exception Criteria Editor to define parameters that will trigger the generation of SEA exceptions. To access the Exception Criteria Editor and set criteria: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Exception Description** within the **Application** group. 3. Select an exception number from 6501 to 6600. 4. Click the **Edit Criteria** button. 5. Click **Edit**. 6. Enter the exception text in the **Description** field. 7. Select the type of criteria that will trigger the exception (example: "Event Contains:"). 8. Click **Add** to add a new criterion. 9. Enter the conditions that must be met for the exception to be generated. These definitions allow for operators AND, OR, or NOT, as well as wildcard operators. 10. Click the **Clear** button to remove all criteria if desired. 11. Click **Validate** for FLOWCAL to verify that your changes are correct. 12. Click **Save**.
