docs.title: FLOWCAL Configuration
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires Application Process – FLOWCAL Options permissions.

The FLOWCAL Configuration screen contains several application level options for the administrator to configure. While these settings are generally configured during installation, an administrator has the ability to modify these settings as needed. These options are effective for the entire application and cannot be configured for individual systems when licensed with the Multi-System Extension add-on.

FLOWCAL Configuration Screen Details

The following items are available on the FLOWCAL Configuration screen: - **Close Schedule Type** - Determines the type of close schedule to be utilized by the monthly close process. - Selecting List (Default) will limit the object drop-down in the Close Schedules screen to lists. - Selecting Close Group will limit the object drop-down in the Close Schedules screen to close groups. When "Close Group" is selected, and if the "Require on Meter Create" option is checked, a close group must be assigned when creating a new meter from the Meter Editor (or Meter Quick Create for gas meters); otherwise, the meter cannot be saved. Close groups are created in the Close Group Editor under the main Setup menu. Users can then add meters to a close group by selecting the preferred close group under the close group drop-down within the Meter Editor. - **GQ Apply Range** - This option is used in conjunction with the "Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited" option within the quality source assignment for gas meters only. By default, "No Limit" is selected, which enables a source assignment to look back as far as the beginning of time on a quality source when applying a sample. Unchecking the No Limit option and selecting a range (number of days, months, or years) limits how far back to look for a sample on the quality source during a source apply. If the end date of a sample is farther back in time from the start date of the record than the specified range, then the sample will not be applied. This will prevent applying an analysis that is older than the allowed time between samples. Checking the No Limit option or specifying a large (or long) time frame for the Range can result in performance issues due to the increased processing load that may be required. Example A company may be contractually obligated to pull samples at least once a year for all sample points. If the Range is set to 13 months to give field technicians a month’s grace period, then once the sample becomes 13 months old, FLOWCAL will stop applying it. - **Subtotal by Meter Direction** - When checked, location rollups total data by meter direction in addition to calculating the total gain or loss for the location. In the Location Final Form tables, this will generate in an extra record per meter direction. The results can be viewed in the Daily and Monthly Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Analysis viewers. - **Subtotal by Meter Class** - When "Subtotal by Meter Direction" is selected, the Subtotal by "Meter Class" option becomes enabled. When checked, location rollups subtotal data by meter class in addition to meter direction. In the Location Final Form tables, this will generate in an extra record per meter class for each meter direction. Totals by meter class and direction can be viewed in the Daily and Monthly Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Analysis viewers. Class is subordinate to direction. FLOWCAL ships with several pre-defined meter directions and classes, but you can define unique directions and classes. This allows for the creation of directions that conform to company standard naming conventions and allows you to classify the use of a meter. Example If you have a location with inlet and outlet meters all with class of Fuel, there will be a subtotal record in the Location Final Form table for Inlets\Fuels and Outlets\Fuels as well as a grand total for the Fuels class. - **Station Member Required** - When checked, station locations created in the Location Editor must have at least one meter member. - **Meter Association Required** - When checked, meters must be a member of a station location. - **Disable Exception “Acknowledge” When Severity \>** - Used to prevent users from ignoring exceptions with a severity greater than the one specified. This is useful if there are certain exceptions that should always require user intervention to resolve, rather than just acknowledging it. Exception severity is defined in the Exception Description Editor. By default, all exceptions have a severity of one. The maximum exception severity is 5. By leaving the level at 5 for this field, any exception can be ignored. - **Gas Loss Ticket Direction** - Gas loss tickets must have a base direction of Outlet, which is used to define the contribution when calculating location balances totals. The user can create user-defined directions in the Meter Direction Editor, but only directions with a base direction of Outlet will be available for selection. The direction is reflected on the gas loss ticket. - **DB Profile Name** - Oracle profiles control password complexity, expiration, re-use, and various quotas. By default, this is left blank and the Default Oracle profile is used. You can define a different Oracle profile that will be used for new FLOWCAL users by providing the profile name here. FLOWCAL will fail to operate properly if you specify a profile that does not exist in the Oracle database instance. - **Observed Density Tolerance** - FLOWCAL calculates observed density by multiplying the density meter factor (DMF) by the uncorrected density. All three values can be imported in a CFX or TFX file. If all three values are imported, FLOWCAL will calculate an observed density and compare it to the imported observed density. If the difference is more than the value defined for Observed Density Tolerance, an exception is generated. Entry is limited to a maximum of 1. - **Ticket Date Populates** - Tickets, for a product movement (ex. scales, meters, rail car) have three dates: Effective Date, Movement Start Date and Movement End Date. This option can help reduce analyst entry time and reduce errors by automatically copying the Effective Date to the Movement Start Date or End Date when a date is not provided. - If this option is set to "Movement Start Date", then when the Effective Date is entered, if the Movement Start Date is undefined, the Effective Date is copied to the Movement Start Date. - If it is set to "Movement End Date", then when the Effective Date is entered, if the Movement End Date is undefined, the Effective Date is copied to the Movement End Date. - If it is set to "Nothing", then entering the Effective Date does not populate the other two dates. - **Default Liquid Recalc Method** - This option presets all liquid data editors (e.g., Volume Editor, the Ticket Editor and Source Assignments) to a default recalculation method for editing data. However, you are still able to select a different recalculation from the default when editing data. Options are: - **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Recalculates volume and mass using the correlation factor. - **Correlation Factor** - Recalculates the correlation factor. - **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Recalculates volume and mass and sets the correlation factor to 1.

Ticket Options

Product movements such as truck loads and unloads as well as inventory measurements such as tank gauges can be imported. On import, the user can specify a multitude of fields for each ticket, such as the customer, the transporter, the shipper, the destination and the origin. These values may not exist in FLOWCAL for that field. This is common when tickets are being generated at remote sites. A driver may pull in and be unable to find the applicable customer. The driver may be able to create one in the terminal management software at the site. This value will then be fed to FLOWCAL on import. Should FLOWCAL create the shipper or import the ticket without the shipper on it and generate an exception? Ticket Options allow the user to tell FLOWCAL what to do in this situation. For the end user, there should be a discussion about how to handle when a new entity, such as new customer, imports into FLOWCAL. For some, having FLOWCAL create a customer could be convenient. For other companies, they may choose to generate a message or exception and manually create the new ticket item. Once these values are created, they cannot be removed from FLOWCAL without purging the ticket or meter data as they are then part of the audit trail. This would mean that the user could have Flow-Cal, FlowCal, FlowCAL and FLOWCAL for the same company. Once the product, shipper, customer, transporter, facility, destination or origin is in FLOWCAL, it is part of the audit trail, unless all data that references it is purged out. When the product is created, a system message will be created. The following items are available in Ticket Options: - **Create Revisions** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, ticket data is imported as a new revision if a record already exists with the same Host ID and Ticket ID. Host ID is the generator of the ticket and is defined in the import file. Ticket ID is unique per host and is defined in the import file. - **Create Products** - Applicable for tickets and batches. When checked, if a product is not recognized on import, the product is created. Product configuration information will be imported. If the full product configuration information is not available on import, then calculations will not occur. The product will need to be set up in FLOWCAL and then the applicable records will need to be recalculated with a manual edit. For customers who have a limited product set, this option is not normally recommended. - **Create Customers** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a customer does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the customer will be created in FLOWCAL. The new customer is created with a company number of ‘#AUTO_GENERATED#XXXXXX’ where XXXXXX is a unique number. The customer is then visible in the Company Editor. - **Create Shippers** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a shipper does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the shipper will be created in FLOWCAL. The new shipper is created with a company number of ‘#AUTO_GENERATED#XXXXXX’ where XXXXXX is a unique number. The shipper is then visible in the Company Editor with Shipper checked. If the shipper already exists in the Company Editor, but Shipper is not checked, then the Shipper field for that customer will be checked. - **Create Transporters** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a transporter does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the transporter will be created in FLOWCAL. The new transporter is created with a company number of ‘#AUTO_GENERATED#XXXXXX’ where XXXXXX is a unique number. The transporter is then visible in the Company Editor with Transporter checked. If the shipper already exists in the Company Editor, but Transporter is not checked, then the Transporter field for that customer will be checked. - **Create Destinations and Origins** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a destination or origin does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the destination or origin will be created in FLOWCAL. - **Create Facilities** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, if a From Facility or a To Facility does not exist in FLOWCAL on import, the facility will be created in FLOWCAL. The new facility is then visible in the Facility Editor. - **Use Ticket ID as BOL If Not Provided (At Import Only)** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, the BOL (Bill of Lading) on a ticket is set to match the Ticket ID on import, when a BOL is not provided. Note: Ticket ID is not visible to the user in FLOWCAL. It will be generated by the system that generates the import file and must be unique. The Ticket ID plus the unique name of the system makes each ticket unique in FLOWCAL. This allows FLOWCAL to determine when importing a ticket if the ticket has been imported before or if it is a revision. - **Use Ticket ID as Ticket Number (At Import Only)** - Applicable for tickets only. When checked, Ticket Number is set to match the Ticket ID on import. When not checked, the Ticket Number will follow the settings for the ‘Generate Ticket Number at’ option. - **Allow Entry of Uncorrected Density** - Uncorrected density can be imported for batch meters and meter tickets. When checked, you can manually enter or edit the uncorrected density. Typically, this is for companies who do not enter the DMF into their flow computers in the field and need FLOWCAL to calculate the corrected density. If you do not need to enter uncorrected density, leave this box unchecked to reduce the chance of another user entering a density value in the wrong field. - **Allow Edit of CTPL** - CTPL can be imported for batch meters and meter tickets and can also be calculated. When checked, you can manually enter or edit the Correction for Temperature and Pressure of the Liquid (CTPL). When this value is edited, the calculation of the Combined Correction Factor (CCF) becomes CCF = CTPL \* meter factor where meter factor is rounded per product discrimination rules. Correction for Temperature of the Liquid (CTL) and Correction for Pressure of the Liquid (CPL) will still be calculated as they normally would, but they will not be used in the calculation of the CCF. Check this option only if there is a need to override the imported or calculated CTPL. - **Use Rounded CTPL in CCF** - Applicable for tickets and meters. - API defines CCF to be calculated as follows: Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z). - When checked, CCF is calculated as follows: Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z),w). This option does not conform to API 12.2.2. - **Generate Ticket Number at** - You can determine when ticket numbers for batches or tickets are created. - **New** - When the batch is first created on import or manual entry. - **Save** - When the batch data is saved after import or manual entry. - **Close** - When the batch data is closed for the month. These options are used in conjunction to further determine when ticket numbers are created. - **Assign Ticket Number as Needed (Only if Missing)** – A ticket number is assigned to a batch or ticket on import or edit if one is not specified. - **Always Assign Ticket Numbers (Overwrite Existing)** – A ticket number is always assigned to a batch or ticket, replacing the imported value. This will ensure ticket numbers are unique. - **Do Not Assign Ticket Numbers** - Ticket number must be manually assigned or provided on import. - **Batch Number is Unique** - You can determine how ticket numbers for batches or tickets are created. - **Globally** - When selected, a unique value is used for each batch and ticket when FLOWCAL assigns a ticket number. This ensures that each ticket number is completely unique. The length can be controlled from the configuration file fcdebugoptions (contact Customer Support for additional information)  - **Per Meter** - When selected, ticket numbers are unique only by appending the meter number to the ticket number. For example, meter ABC and meter XYZ both have ticket numbers of 000001. Only by concatenating the meter number to the ticket number (e.g. ABC000001) is there a unique identifier. - **Allow User to Edit Ticket Number** - Applicable for tickets and batches. When checked, you can manually edit the ticket number when entering or editing a batch in the Volume Editor or when entering or editing a ticket in the Ticket Editor. - **Include CPA on Batch Ticket** - Applicable for batches only. Current period adjustments (CPA) are calculated for a batch when a prove is manually applied to a meter batch in the Volume Editor. The CPA is the change in mass or volume based on prove factor changes. When checked, the CPA amount will be displayed on printed tickets. If the printing of CPAs on tickets is not desired, then do not check this option. - **Show Off Spec on Batch Tickets** - Applicable to tickets only, and not to meter batches. When checked, if product specification validations fail for the ticket, printed tickets will show that the data is off spec and will print on the report which components are out of bounds, what the value is, and what the limit is. See additional information on the following reports: - [Ticket Detail](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#TicketDetail) and [Ticket Detail Allowables](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Meter-Location%20Reports.md#TicketDetailAllowables) - [Final Form Ticket](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Other%20Application%20Reports.md#FinalFormTicket) and [Final Form Ticket Allowed](../../Reports/Report%20Descriptions%20and%20Tips/Other%20Application%20Reports.md#FinalFormTicketAllowed) - **Use SPLC Code for Origins and Destinations** - Standard Point Location Codes (SPLC) are nine-digit codes used in North America by various shippers. Every location has an SPLC code defined by the location’s city, county (or parish) and state. When checked, an SPLC code can be entered into the Origin/Destination Editor along with city, county and state. The SPLC Code must be a number. When unchecked, then origins and destinations will be string fields (e.g., League City, TX) on tickets. Origins and destinations can be imported or manually entered. - **Enforce Tickets Received in Order** - Applicable for tickets. Ticket imports contain a sequence number associated to each ticket ID. When checked, FLOWCAL validates that each imported ticket has the next sequence number on import. The first ticket for a given ticket ID must have a sequence number of 0. The next ticket for that ticket ID must have a sequence number of 1. However, if the next ticket for a given ticket ID has a sequence number other than what is expected, the ticket is not imported, and an exception is generated.

Capacity Table Import

The Ticket Recalc Method is the default recalculation method that will be used when tank capacity tables and configuration options are edited. Users can choose an alternate method when editing the ticket. Options are: - **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Volumetric and mass quantities are recalculated using the correlation factors. - **Correlation Factor (CF)** - Correlation factors are recalculated; volumetric and mass quantities are left unchanged. - **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Correlation factors are forced to 1 and volumetric and mass quantities are then calculated. - **No Recalc** - Changes are saved and no recalculation takes place. This option is generally discouraged as this forces supporting data to be out of sync with the resulting quantities.

docs.title: Facility Editor
docs.text:
This functionality requires Application Process – FLOWCAL Options privileges and the Liquids or Gas add-on.

FLOWCAL allows users to specify "To" and "From" facilities on batches and rail tickets in order to track inventory values at each facility.

Use the Facility Editor to enter facility names that will then be available in areas throughout FLOWCAL, such as the Meter Editor (Liquids > Facilities tab or Integration tab) and Ticket Editor (Rail Car > Accounting tab).

To create a new facility: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Facility** within the **Liquids** group. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Enter a facility name at the bottom of the screen. 5. Enter a facility code if needed (required for facilities designated as "Integrated"). 6. Designate the facility as a "From", "To", or "Integrated" facility by clicking the **Is From**, **Is To**, or **Integrated** checkboxes. A facility can be designated as a "To" , "From", or "Integrated" facility. If you do not specify the "From" and "To" designations, the facility will be available in both the **From** and **To** drop-down boxes. If the facility is designated as an "Integrated" facility, it can be selected in the Meter Editor Integration tab used for Quorum Enterprise Integration (i.e., FLOWCAL to TIPS). Integrated facilities cannot be deleted if the facility is associated with an integrated meter. 7. Click the **Save** button. When the "Create Facilities" FLOWCAL Configuration option is enabled, facilities can be automatically created on ticket import (TFX) if a "From" facility or "To" facility is in the file that is not in FLOWCAL.

docs.title: Field Selection
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires Application Process - FLOWCAL Options privileges.

The Field Select screen allows administrators to limit the number of options that are available in certain FLOWCAL drop-down lists. This helps users find appropriate values and prevents users from selecting invalid values.

You can limit selection options for the following meter characteristic and analysis drop-down lists:

  • Calculation Method
  • Z Method
  • Water Vapor Technique
  • Water Vapor Method
  • Flowing Gas Condition
  • Reporting Condition
  • Heating Value Condition
  • Mass Calculation Method
  • Energy Calculation Method
To set the available options in a drop-down list: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Field Selection** in the **Application** group. 3. Use the drop-down field at the top of the screen to select the list that you want to limit. 4. Click **Edit**. 5. Check or uncheck the **Display** checkboxes for each selection option. By default, all items are set to display. 6. Click **Save**.

docs.title: HC Property Source Document Editor
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires Application Process - FLOWCAL Options privileges.

Use the HC Property Source Document Editor to list source documents containing the physical constants used for hydrocarbon components, such as water, CO, ethane and cyclopentane. The source may be a published standard, company literature or any other data source.

These source documents will be available for selection in the Source Document column of the Hydrocarbon Properties Editor.

To access the HC Property Source Document Editor and add a new source document: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **HC Property Source** within the **Application** group. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Enter the document name and click **Save**. To edit an existing source document: 1. Select the document name and click **Edit**. 2. Make the necessary changes and click **Save**.

docs.title: Import Driver Editor
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires Application Process - FLOWCAL Options privileges.

When creating a new meter using the Meter Editor or Meter Quick Create, you can specify an import driver based on the type of files that will be imported for the meter.

Example To import CFX files for a meter, you will need to install the Stndfx driver and set the meter to use this driver.

Use the Import Driver Editor to install import drivers that will then be available for selection when creating a new meter.

To add a new import driver: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Import Driver** within the **Application** group. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Click the **Load from Driver on Disk** button. 5. Click the desired driver, and **OK**. 6. Click **Save**. Click the **View Drivers on Disk** button to see all drivers available for installation, and drivers that have and have not been installed.

The Stndtfx and Stndpfx drivers cannot be loaded. These import drivers are automatically used by FLOWCAL when importing tickets or PROVEit files, respectively.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text:
• Additional Import Drivers
  • Configure Imports

docs.title: Import Rules Editor
docs.text:
Use the Import Rules Editor to create rules that reject the import of specific periodic records. If this option is configured, imported records with differential pressure, static pressure, or temperature values that are too high, too low, or missing will be rejected.

Conditional import rules work for all files types; however, they will not work with Transaction Queue data.

To access the Import Rule Editor and create a new import rule: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Import Rules Editor** within the **Application** group. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Enter a name and/or description for the new rule. 5. Specify the criteria for the import rules by making the appropriate selections from the drop-down lists and entering a value. For liquid data, Pressure and Temperature rules will apply to meter pressure and meter temperature. They will not apply to observed pressure and observed temperature. 6. If additional criteria are needed, click the **New Row** button. 7. Click the **Validate** button to check the rule syntax. 8. Click the **Save** button. Clicking the **Clear** button will remove all criteria, including name and description.

Applying an Import Rule

To apply an import rule to a meter: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Editor**. 2. Select a meter and click the **Edit** button. 3. Click the **Imports** tab. 4. In the Conditional Import Rules section, provide a rule in the **Reject if True** field. 5. Click the **Save** button. You can also use the Bulk Changes screen to apply an import rule to multiple meters using a location or list.

docs.title: Message Description Editor
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires Application Process - FLOWCAL Options privileges.

Messages form an organized audit trail of changes made to FLOWCAL settings, device creation and deletion, and process status changes.

Four types of messages are generated:

  • System
  • Location
  • Meter
  • Source

All messages can be viewed and acknowledged from the Message Viewer. Messages can also be configured for automatic notification by email. Use the Message Description Editor to view and edit the default configuration for a message, specifically the message class and priority, and to designate email notification recipients.

To access the Message Description Editor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Message Description** within the **Application** group. 3. Select the **System**, **Location**, **Meter**, or **Source** radio button to filter the grid by message type. 4. Select a message and click **Edit**. 5. Edit the class and priority designation as needed. 6. Click **Save**.

Message Description Screen Details

The following items are available on the Message Description Editor screen: - **Number** - Unique numeric identifier for the message. - **Class** - User defined for the client’s needs depending on their IT and business structure. The class level defined for the message; Class levels are Error, Warning, Information, and Security. Where a warning could be a normal exception, whereas an Error could be a critical exception. - **Priority** - Severity classification for events that have occurred. - **0** - Messages that are not to be written. Setting the priority level to zero will disable the message for the entire application. - **1–10** - Messages that are to be written with an initial status of "Logged". - **\> 10** - Messages that are to be written with an initial status of "Unacknowledged". These messages can then be acknowledged; "Logged" messages cannot. The Priority setting is application-wide and requires services to be restarted. - **Message** - The message description. This should only be altered for clarification; changing the description will not alter the underlying meaning or the way the message is generated. - **Data Usage** - Data points populated for the message selected. These can vary by message. - **Contact Name/D-List** - Existing contacts or distribution lists defined for each message (designated in the Notify field). The contacts specified will receive an email when the message is generated. Example Jane Doe is defined in the Notify field for message 6500. Any time message 6500 is generated, Jane Doe will receive an email alert.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text:
• Messages (Message Viewer)
  • Message Directory

docs.title: Meter Class Editor
docs.text:
Meter class indicates the overall "meter purpose" and is used to provide categories for grouping meters within viewers and reports. The Meter Class Editor allows users to create user-defined classes in a measurement system to label and categorize the use of meters. Examples of meter classes include: Sales, Receipt, Delivery, Transportation Gas, Fuel, Blow Down, Water Draw and Construction Loss.

To realize the full benefit of class subtotals, careful planning and coordination should be done with other departments that utilize FLOWCAL data.

Your organization will need to determine if meter class subtotaling is required prior to setup and configuration of balance locations. Some organizations meet the subtotaling requirements through the creation of sub-balances.

Enable subtotaling by meter class in the FLOWCAL Configuration screen.

To access the Meter Class Editor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Application** group, click **Meter Class**.

Reviewing Meter Classes

To edit or add a meter class: 1. Open the Meter Class Editor. 2. Select a meter class name from the list and click **Edit**. 3. To create a new class, click **New**. 4. To change or enter a meter class name, click in the name field and enter a new class name. 5. If necessary, specify an optional code for each class. 6. Click **Save**.

Deleting Meter Classes

To delete a meter class: 1. Open the Meter Class Editor. 2. Select the meter class to be deleted. 3. Click **Delete**. If a class is assigned to one or more meters or tickets (i.e., it is still in use on at least one meter or ticket), then it cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Meter Direction Editor
docs.text:
FLOWCAL ships with several pre-defined directions termed base directions, but the user can add their own custom directions via the Meter Direction Editor. These custom direction names allow for the creation of directions that conform to company standard naming conventions.

Custom Directions require a Base Direction of Inlet, Outlet, Throughput, Off System, or Both (In and Out). Directions are used by the location rollups process to determine the contribution of each location member. If enabled in FLOWCAL Options, location rollups subtotal location rollup values based on Meter Direction. These totals are then viewable by certain reports and in the Monthly and Daily Rollups, NGL Balance Viewer and the Recovery Analysis viewer.

Enable subtotaling by Meter Direction in the FLOWCAL Configuration screen.

To view or edit meter directions: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Application** group, click **Meter Direction**. ![](data:image/png;base64,)

Meter Direction Screen Details

The following items are available on the Meter Direction screen: 1. **Default Meter Directions** - Default directions are the basic meter directions that were used in FLOWCAL 7 that have been predefined in FLOWCAL. They cannot be modified or deleted. 2. **User-Defined Meter Directions** - Examples of user-defined directions are Receipt with a base direction of Inlet and Delivery with a base direction of Outlet. Once meter directions are defined, a direction can be assigned to a meter by editing meter characteristics. 3. **Reserved Directions** - Directions depicted in bold print have specific purposes and cannot be edited by a user. 4. **Relationship** - The **Relationship** button is used to set a relationship between Meter Directions and Meter Classes, and is only visible when the Subtotal by Meter Direction and Meter Class options are enabled in the [FLOWCAL Configuration](FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md) screen. (This concept is covered in greater detail in the Meter Class section.)

Creating Meter Directions

To create a new direction: 1. Launch the Meter Direction Editor. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter the direction details. 4. Click **Save**.

Editing Meter Directions

To edit an existing direction: 1. Launch the Meter Direction Editor. 2. select an meter direction name from the list and click **Edit**. If a direction is assigned to one or more meters, the direction name is the only attribute that can be changed. Directions that have a bold font cannot be edited. 3. To change or edit a meter direction name, click the **Name** field and enter a new direction name. 4. Select a base direction from the drop-down menu. The base direction determines how meter and ticket data is used in gain/loss calculations, and how a meter or ticket is added to a location. Only directions that have a base direction of "Inlet" or "Outlet" can be assigned to a standalone ticket. 5. Click **Save**.

Deleting Meter Directions

To delete a meter direction: 1. Launch the Meter Direction Editor. 2. Click on the meter direction to be deleted. 3. Click **Delete**. If a direction is assigned to one or more meters or tickets (i.e., it is still in use on at least one meter or ticket), it cannot be deleted.

docs.title: Pipeline Editor
docs.text:
Use the Pipeline Editor to create pipelines that are referenced by gas loss tickets.

To access the Pipeline Editor: Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Application** \> **Pipeline Editor**. To create a new pipeline: 1. Click **New**. 2. Fill out the required fields (Type and Name). 3. Complete the Actual Volume (optional). The Actual Volume for the pipeline can be filled out by manually entering the volume, or by clicking the calculator icon and filling out the form to calculate the actual volume based on the pipeline length, nominal diameter, and wall thickness. 4. Assign the pipeline to a location and a gas quality source (optional). Only balance locations can be selected. 5. Click **Save**. The username and GMS date will automatically update when a new pipeline is created or an existing pipeline is edited.

Pipeline names are not case-sensitive; the editor will format all pipeline names in all caps, regardless of how they are initially recorded. For example: The editor will recognize “MyObj” and “MYobj” as the same pipline names, assuming they are the same type. The name “MYOBJ” would then be available throughout the FLOWCAL application.

docs.title: Pressure Base Editor
docs.text:
The Pressure Base Editor allows you to enter the pressure base values that will be available for selection everywhere a Pressure Base drop-down list is available in FLOWCAL, such as the meter characteristics.

To access the Pressure Base Editor and enter a new value: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Pressure Base** within the **Application** group. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Enter the new value in the **Pressure Base** field at the bottom of the screen. 5. Click the **Save** button.

docs.title: Required Meter Fields
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires Application Process - FLOWCAL Options privileges.

The Required Fields screen allows administrators to configure specific fields so that populating them is required when a meter is created in the Meter Editor or through Meter Quick Create. If a user creates a meter with a tool, such as FcLoader, required Meter Editor fields may not be populated upon meter creation. However, the user will then be required to populate the required fields during subsequent edits in the Meter Editor. This does not affect edits in the Volume Editor.

If a field is designated as required, it will be highlighted in green, indicating that data is required before changes can be saved. If data is required, the field will be highlighted with green.

To access the Required Fields screen and select required fields: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Application** group, select **Required Meter Fields**. 3. Click **Edit**. 4. Select a category of fields to require (Meter Attributes or Meter Characteristics). Meter Characteristics fields correspond to the fields available on the Meter Quick Create screen, not the Volume Editor. 5. Select the **Group** for which you want to view available fields. 6. For each field that you want to require, click **Required**. 7. When your selections are complete, click **Save**. If you select a field that is not available on the Meter Quick Create screen, a warning message will display stating that if you do not disable the Meter Quick Create form, it will be possible to create meters without the required field populated. In this situation, a **Disable Meter Quick Create** checkbox will display at the bottom of the Required Fields screen. If necessary, select the **Disable Meter Quick Create** option.

docs.title: TESTit Integrated Configuration
docs.text:
The TESTit Integrated Configuration screen contains the options relating to FLOWCAL integrated with TESTit 3.

This functionality is only available with TESTit 3 Integrated. You must have TESTit Admin privileges to edit in this screen.

To access the TESTit Integrated Configuration screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **TESTit Integration Configuration** within the **Application** group.

TESTit Integrated Configuration Screen Details

The following items are available on the TESTit Integrated Configuration screen: #### Objects from TESTit - **Meters** - Configure how FLOWCAL manages meters from TESTit. Available options are: - **Ignore** - Ignore all "enable meter" requests from TESTit. - **Report Only** - Generate a system message (3005) indicating that an "enable meter" request has been received from TESTit. - **Enable Existing** - Enable the meter for TESTit if it exists in FLOWCAL. If the meter does not exist, generate a system message (3003) indicating that an "enable meter" request has been made for a non-existent meter. - **Create or Enable** - Automatically create, if necessary, and enable a new meter with a business status of "On". If successful, a system message (3004) is created, indicating that the meter was successfully enabled. - **Create Pending** - Automatically create, if necessary, and enable a new meter with a business status of "Pending New". - **PDF Reports** - Configure whether PDF test reports are brought over from TESTit. You cannot select which reports will be brought over; if this option is enabled, all reports associated with a given meter will be brought over and available to view in the Volume Editor. #### Test Point Data - **Apply Calibration Adjustments** - Specify whether meter tests from TESTit bypass the Review Test Report process and are automatically applied or sent for approval. - **Accept New Report Revisions** - Specify whether new TESTit test report revisions override previous revisions. This process rejects pending PPAs and recalculates the adjustment using the new test data. - **Cal Adj Gross Trip Point Pct** - Define a limit for individual transmitter errors on imported test reports to help flag potential erroneous data entry on test reports. Transmitter errors that exceed this trip point will generate an exception. - **Correction Time Limit (days)**\* - Enter a system default for the maximum number of days that can be adjusted per test. - **Calibration Adjustment Rule**\* - This read-only option is set to "Half Way Back" by default. You can select a different adjustment rule through the Contractual Limits Editor in Master Data Validation - **Min Calibration Adjustment Pct**\* - Set a minimum percentage by which volume/energy must change at the monthly level for a calibration adjustment to occur. - **Min Calibration Adjustment Unit Diff**\* - Set a minimum unit difference by which volume/energy must change at the monthly level for a calibration adjustment to occur. #### Test Report Review - **Show Individual Transmitter Corrections** – When checked, sets the default display mode for the Preview button on the [Review Test Report screen](../../Integration/TESTit%20Integrated/TESTit%20Manager/Test%20Report/Review%20Test%20Report.md). \* These options are used to define system-level settings. Individual meters can still be configured under the Contractual Limits section of Master Data Validation. Those meter-level settings take precedence over system-level settings.

docs.title: Tabular Display Configuration
docs.text:
Use the Tabular Display Config screen to control the tabular views in the Volume Editor. You can select the columns to display and change the display order.

To access the Tabular Display Config screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Application** group, select **Tabular Display Configuration**. 3. Select a fluid phase, meter type, and grid type (along with a data category) to view the available columns for that combination. 4. To change the data that is displayed in the tabular view, click **Edit** and then use the right and left arrow buttons to make a column visible or to hide a column. To change the display order, use the up and down arrow buttons. 5. The configuration that you define on the Tabular Display Config screen applies to all FLOWCAL  users. If you select **Can Show** or **Can Hide** for a column, you can change the display within the Volume Editor. The changes will only apply to that session.

docs.title: Temperature Base Editor
docs.text:
The Temperature Base Editor allows you to enter the temperature base values that will be available for selection everywhere a Temperature Base drop-down list is available in FLOWCAL, such as the meter characteristics.

To access the Pressure Base Editor and enter a new value: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Temperature Base** within the **Application** group. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Enter the new value in the **Temperature Base** field at the bottom of the screen. 5. Click the **Save** button.

docs.title: Data Archive Configuration
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires Data Archive Crypkey license and Application Process – Data Archive privileges.

Use the Data Archive Configuration screen to define automated archival process behavior.

To access the Data Archive Configuration screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Data Archive Configuration** within the **Application** group. 3. Click the **Edit** button. 4. Make any necessary changes and click **Save**. This screen is accessible from the production database only; it is not accessible from the archival database.

Data Archive Configuration Screen Details

The following items are available on the Data Archive Configuration screen: - **Enable Archiving** - Select this option to enable the automated archival process. - **Archive Data older than \# months** - This option defines how old data must be to be considered for auto archiving. Values can range from 1 to 120 months; 36 months is set by default. This value must be less than or equal to the value specified for the **Purge Data older than \# months** option. - **Begin Archiving on day \# of the month** - The archive process will only archive data when the calendar day is equal or greater than the specified day. Values can range from 1 to 20; 10 is set by default. - **Enable Purging** - Select this option to enable the automated purge process. (This option will only be available if you have selected the **Enable Archiving** option.) - **Purge Data older than \# months** - This option defines how old data must be to be considered for auto purging. Values can range from 1 to 120 months; 72 is set by default. This value must be greater than or equal to the value specified for the **Archive Data older than \# months** option. - **Pause archive/purge operations during business hours (weekdays only)** - Select this option to specify a range of hours to suspend operations during the week (Monday through Friday only). (This option will only be available if you have selected the **Enable Archiving** option.) - **Disable from \# to \#** - Values can range from 0 (12 AM) to 23 (11 PM); 4 to 19 is set by default.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: Data Archive Per Device Configuration

docs.title: Data Archive Per Device Configuration
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires Data Archive Crypkey license and Application Process – Data Archive privileges.

Use the Data Archive Per Device Configuration screen to enable or disable archive operations for meters and locations (individually or through lists/close groups), add notes, and view archival and restore history per object, list of objects, or measurement month.

To access the Data Archive Per Device Configuration screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Data Archive Per Device Configuration** within the **Application** group. This screen is accessible from the production database only; it is not accessible from the archival database.

docs.title: Screen Tabs
docs.text:
Setup

Use the Setup tab to enable archival functionality and add notes for individual meters and locations. The following items are available on the Setup tab: - **Enable archival for this device** - Select this option to enable archive/restore/purge operations for the selected object. By default, these operations are disabled for newly created meters and locations. - **Comments** - Add an optional comment for the selected object (up to 2,000 characters allowed). - **Apply to device’s children** - Select this option to apply the same settings to the immediate children of the selected object. - This option is always disabled for meters and always enabled for lists and close groups. - If this option is enabled for a location, the settings will be applied to the immediate child meters and locations of the parent location. You can use a list or close group to bulk enable/disable archive operations and add comments; however, the checkbox will display as unchecked and the comment field will be empty when these object types are selected. The changes will be saved on individual meters and locations.

History

The History tab displays archive, restore, and purge histories for the selected objects; it also allows manual restore, manual re-archive, and manual purge operations for selected records. The following items are available on the History tab: - **Item Number** - Meter or location number. - **Item Type** - Meter or location object type. - **Contract Month** - ID for the contract month of the selected object. - **Status** - Current status of the selected object and contract month. - **Time of Archive** - Time stamp of manual re-archive, if applicable. - **Time of Restore** - Time stamp of manual restore, if applicable. - **Time of Purge** - Time stamp of manual purge, if applicable. - **Archive Username** - User who initiated the manual re-archive process, if applicable. - **Restore Username** - User who initiated the manual restore process, if applicable. - **Error Message** - Any error message generated by the data archive service when processing the records. - **Restore** - Queue the selected records for restore, which moves archived data back to production database from archive database. This option is only available for records with status of "Archived", "Restore Failure", or "Purge Failure". Once an archived record is restored, the archive service will not queue the record to be archived again in the future; these items will need to be manually queued be re-archived. - **Re-Archive** - Queue the selected records for manual re-archive, which moves previous restored data from production database to archive database. This option is only available for records with status of "Archival Failure" or "Restore". - **Manual Purge** - Queue the selected records for purge, which deletes archived data from archive database permanently. This optional is only available for records with status of "Archived", "Restore Failure", or "Purge Failure". **IMPORTANT:** This operation is ****not reversible**;** once purged, the data cannot be recovered.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: Data Archive Configuration

docs.title: Data Archive Solution
docs.text:
This feature requires the Data Archive add-on and Application Process – Data Archive privileges.

The Data Archive solution allows for automated archival of data from a production database to an archive database, and the subsequent automated purge of archived data, following user-configured time spans. Options to manually restore, re-archive, and purge data are also available. FLOWCAL can run against the archival database in read-only mode for the purpose of running reports and viewing data.

An archive database consists of only four tables (FC_ARCHIVE_FLAG, FC_FFLCN_HOURLY, FC_FFMTR_HOURLY, and FC_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES). If custom columns are added to any of these tables, in either the production or archive database, or if columns or constraints are otherwise modified, the changes must be applied to both databases, or the archive service will fail.

Setup

To set up an archive database and link it to a production database: 1. Create a new database shell. 2. Go to the **\Setup\FcArchival** directory in the FLOWCAL installation folder. 3. Run the **archiveCreateDb.sql** script on the new archive database to create necessary tablespaces. 4. Run the **CreateArchToProdDbLink.sql** script on the archive database to create a database link to the production database. 5. Run the **CreateProdToArchDbLink.sql** script on the production database to create a database link to the archive database.

Data Archive Service Installation

Meter periodic data (FC_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES), final form meter hourly (FC_FFMTR_HOURLY), and final form location hourly (FC_FFLCN_HOURLY) data are transferred from the production database using the installed Data Archive service (FlowCal.Archival.Service.exe). The service also processes data restore, re-archive, and manual purge operations. To install the Archive service: 1. Make sure you have the appropriate permissions required to install services on the applicable server. 2. Go to the **\FlowCal.Archival.Service** directory in the FLOWCAL installation folder. 3. Right-click the **\_Install_Service.bat** file and select **Run as Administrator**.

Configuration

Once the databases are linked and service is installed and running, configure and enable the service through the Settings Manager. 1. Configure the Data Archive operations settings (see: [Data Archive Configuration](Data%20Archive%20Configuration.md)). 2. Enable archive operations for desired meters and locations (see: [Data Archive Per Device Configuration](Data%20Archive%20Per%20Device%20Configuration.md)).

View Archived Data

Once data has been archived based on the defined time span, you can view the archived data in the Volume Editor and Rollup Viewers by logging into the FLOWCAL archive database. You will access the archive database using your production database login credentials; however, to log on to the archive database for the first time, you will need to go through the password reset process. When an object is deleted, its associated archived data will be deleted as well.

Manual Restore/Re-archive/Purge

To view the archive history of an object, go to the [Data Archive Per Device Configuration](Data%20Archive%20Per%20Device%20Configuration.md) screen and click the **History** tab. This tab also allows users to manually restore, re-archive, and purge eligible data. The Toolbox purge cannot be used for an object if the selected measurement month contains archived data; the archived data must first be restored.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text:
• Data Archive Configuration
  • Data Archive Per Device Configuration

docs.title: CALCit Calculator
docs.text:
CALCit offers a wide selection of calculators for use with FLOWCAL data.

The Gas Volume and Plate Size calculators are included with CALCit Integrated. For information on how to obtain additional calculators, contact Customer Support.

To access CALCit: - Go to the Settings Manager, and select **CALCit** in the **Calculators** group; or - Go to the Volume Editor, right-click a meter, and select **Calculators**. Accessing CALCit from the Volume Editor will pre-populate the meter's characteristics in CALCit.

docs.title: Unit Conversion
docs.text:
The Unit Conversion Calculator converts values from one unit to a different unit (e.g., from degrees Fahrenheit to degrees Celsius).

To access the Unit Conversion Calculator:  1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Unit Conversion** in the **Calculators** group. To convert a value: 1. On the left side of the screen, enter the value you want to convert and select the current unit from the drop-down list. 2. On the right side of the screen, select the new unit from the drop-down list. 3. The value is converted and displayed automatically.

Unit Conversion Details

The following options are available in the Unit Conversion screen: - **All Units to US** - Set the units on the left side of the screen to U.S. units and the right side to metric units. - **All Units to Metric** - Set the units on the left side of the screen to metric units and the right side to U.S. units. - **Clear** - Clear all values. - **Close** - Close the screen.

docs.title: Company Manager
docs.text:
Company names and numbers are managed in the Company Manager. Companies (also referred to as "customers" throughout the FLOWCAL application) can be associated with:

  • Contacts for report scheduling (requires the Scheduled Reporting module)
  • Objects such as meters for generating queries or displaying on reports
  • Rail patterns used for rail tickets (requires the Liquids add-on)
  • Batches and Standalone Tickets via the Accounting tab (requires the Liquids add-on)
To access the Company Manager: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Company Manager** in the **Contacts** group. Accessing the Company Manager requires the **Contacts** privilege.

Company Manager Details

The following items are available on the Company Manager screen: - **Number** - Company number - **Name** - Company (customer) name which is displayed on other forms where names are available for selection - **New** - Create a new company - **Edit** - Edit a company - **Delete** - Delete a company Only companies that are not associated to meters or tickets can be deleted. - **Save** - Save changes - **Meters** - Select a Company Number or Name and click the Meters button to display a list of associated meters - **Cancel** - Cancel changes - **Edit** - Edit a company #### Liquids Only The following fields apply to Liquid tickets only and are optional. If the company is not given a label (shipper, transporter, railroad, etc.) the company is still visible wherever there is a customer drop-down. - **Shipper** - A company that sends goods - **Transporter** - A company that transports goods - **Railroad** - A railroad company - **Consignor Truck** - In a contract, the company sending a truck shipment to be delivered - **Consignee Truck** - In a contract, the company to which a truck shipment is to be delivered - **Consignor Rail** - In a contract, the company sending a rail shipment to be delivered - **Consignee Rail** - In a contract, the company to which a rail shipment is to be delivered There are ticket options available from the FLOWCAL Configuration screen that dictate how customers, shippers, or transporters are handled on import of TFX files for tickets. These companies can be auto created or generate a message or exception. Auto creating could lead to the same company being created multiple times, such as Flow-Cal, FlowCal, FlowCAL and FLOWCAL. The company number is the unique identifier.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: Create Companies

docs.title: Contact Manager
docs.text:
Contacts and associated contact information are managed in the Contact Manager, also referred to as the Address Book. Contacts can be used for:

  • Assigning an Auditor or Contact for Audits (requires the Audits Package module)
  • Distributing reports or exports via email (requires the Scheduled Reporting module)
  • Emailing exception details from the Exception Resolver
  • Configuring automatic email notifications for exceptions or messages
  • Email distribution lists
  • Sending ad-hoc emails from FLOWCAL
To access the Contact Manager: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Contact Manager** in the **Contacts** group. Accessing the Contact Manager requires the **Contacts** privilege.

Contact Manager Screen Details

The following items are available in the Contact Manager screen: - **Type Filter** - Filter between All (No Filter), FLOWCAL, or TESTit contacts for those contacts where Type is defined. - **Company Filter** - Filter by Company for those contacts where Company is defined. - **Company** - Select from the companies created within the Company Manager screen. - **Communication** - Select the down arrow button to choose from a standard list of labels, configurable per contact. - **E-mail** - An email address is required for report scheduling and other email features within FLOWCAL. Click the button to the right of the email address to create a new email using the user’s default email application (e.g., Outlook). - **Internet** - Click the button to the right of the internet address to connect to the address using the user’s default web browser. - **Print** - Click Print to preview the Company and Contacts report for the contact selected.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: Create Contacts

docs.title: Contact Type Editor
docs.text:
The Contact Type Editor is used to define the contact types that will be available in the Contact Type Selection screens for objects, such as Meters, Locations, Quality Sources, and Test Reports and Calibration Devices in TESTit Integrated V2.

Contact types are not supported for TESTit Integrated V3.

Contacts can be associated to Contact Types at the object level (e.g., meter, location, source), which enables the contact to receive automatic email notifications as exceptions or messages are generated.

Example You can create a contact type called "Analyst" and enable it for use with meters and locations. You can then go to the Meter Editor or Location Editor, select a meter/location, and open the Contact Type Selection screen from the Tools menu to see the "Analyst" contact type. The Quality Source Editor would not contain the "Analyst" contact type, as it was only configured for meters and locations in the Contact Type Editor. From the Contact Type Selection screen, you can assign a contact name to the "Analyst" contact type. Each meter/location can have a different contact name, as well as zero, one, or multiple contact names assigned. In the [Exception Description Editor](../Application/Exception%20Description%20Editor.md), you can define which exceptions or messages will trigger an automatic email to the assigned analysts using the Notify field. The contacts assigned for each meter or location will then be notified by email when exceptions or messages that are configured to notify are generated for the meter or location.

By default, FLOWCAL installs with two contact types, "Technician" and "Witness", which cannot be deleted. However, other contact types can be created manually from the Contact Type Editor or in bulk using FcLoader.

To access the Contact Type Editor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Contact Types** in the **Contacts** group. Accessing the Contact Type Editor requires the "Contacts" privilege.

Contact Type Editor Screen Details

The following options are available on the Contact Type Editor screen: - **Meter** - Contact type will be available in the Meter Editor. - **Location** - Contact type will be available in the Location Editor, Liquid Cavern Editor, and Comparison Location Editor. - **Quality Source** - Contact type will be available in Quality Source Editor. - **TESTit** - Contact type will be available in Test Reports (TESTit Integrated V2 only). - **Calibration Device** - Contact type will be available in Calibration Devices (TESTit Integrated V2 only).

docs.text:
