  • FcLoader

docs.title: Distribution Lists
docs.text:
Distribution lists allow users to maintain lists of email addresses and send messages to all list members simultaneously. Use the Distribution Lists Editor to group contacts into distribution lists.

Contacts can belong to multiple distribution lists.

To access the Distribution Lists Editor and create a new distribution list: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Distribution Lists** within the **Contacts** group. 3. Go to **File** \> **New**. 4. Enter a name for the distribution list and select an address book. 5. Click **Save**. You cannot save until you have specified a name and an address book. 6. Click the **Members** button. 7. Click the checkboxes next to contact names to include them in the distribution list. 8. When you have finished selecting contacts, click **OK**. You can repeat steps 6 through 8 as many times as needed. 9. Click **Save**. To delete a distribution list, go to **File** \> **Delete**. To add or remove members, select the distribution list and click the **Members** button, or go to **Edit** \> **Add/Remove Members**. To rename a distribution list or change the list information, select the distribution list and go to **Edit** \> **Rename/Change List Info**.

Menu Details

The following menu options are available in the Distribution List Editor: - **File** - **New** - Create new distribution list - **Delete** - Delete the selected distribution list - **Print** - Print a report of the selected distribution list and associated members - **Exit** - Close the Distribution List editor - **Edit** - **Add/Remove Members** - Add or remove members from selected distribution list This functionality is also available when you click the **Members** button. - **Rename/Change List Info** - Change the name of the selected distribution list.

docs.title: Country Editor
docs.text:
The Country Editor allows you to enter country names that you can then access in areas throughout FLOWCAL, such as the Meter Editor and Location Editor.

To access the Country Editor and modify country options: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Country Editor** in the **Geographic** group. 3. Select a country from the list and click the **Edit** button. 4. Update the country data at the bottom of the screen as needed. 5. Click the **Save** button. To create a new country: 1. Click the **New** button. 2. Enter the country data at the bottom of the screen. 3. Click the **Save** button. The country will now be available within FLOWCAL. Once created, countries cannot be deleted.

docs.title: County Editor
docs.text:
The County Editor allows you to enter county names that you can then access in areas throughout FLOWCAL, such as the Meter Editor and Location Editor.

To access the County Editor and modify county options: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **County Editor** in the **Geographic** group. 3. Select a county from the list and click the **Edit** button. 4. Update the county data at the bottom of the screen as needed. 5. Click the **Save** button. To create a new county: 1. Click the **New** button. 2. Enter the county data using the fields at the bottom of the screen. The code is generally the Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) county code, which is used by the United States government to uniquely identify states and counties. 3. Click the **Save** button. The county will now be available within FLOWCAL.

docs.title: Measurement Area Editor
docs.text:
The Measurement Area Editor allows you to enter a measurement area that you can then access in areas throughout FLOWCAL, such as the Meter Editor, Quality Source Editor, or Location Editor.

To access the Measurement Area Editor and modify measurement area options: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Measurement Area** in the **Geographic** group. 3. Select a measurement area from the list and click the **Edit** button. 4. Update the measurement area data at the bottom of the screen as needed. 5. Click the **Save** button. To add a new measurement area: 1. Click the **New** button. 2. Enter the measurement area data at the bottom of the screen. 3. Click the **Save** button. The measurement area will now be available within FLOWCAL. To delete a measurement area: 1. Select a measurement area and click the **Delete** button. 2. Select another measurement area to replace the one being deleted for all associated meters, locations, etc., or delete the measurement area without replacing it by selecting "\*Leave Blank". 3. Click **OK**.

docs.title: State Editor
docs.text:
The State Editor allows you to enter state names that you can then access in areas throughout FLOWCAL, such as the Meter Editor and Location Editor.

To access the State Editor and modify state options: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **State Editor** in the **Geographic** group. 3. Select a state from the list and click the **Edit** button. 4. Update the state data at the bottom of the screen as needed. 5. Click the **Save** button. To create a new state: 1. Click the **New** button. 2. Enter the state data at the bottom of the screen. 3. Click the **Save** button. The state will now be available within FLOWCAL.

docs.title: Time Zone Editor
docs.text:
The Time Zone Editor allows you to enter time zone names and GMT offset data that you can then access in areas throughout FLOWCAL, such as the Meter Editor.

To access the Time Zone Editor and modify time zone options: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Time Zone** in the **Geographic** group. 3. Select a time zone from the list and click the **Edit** button. 4. Update the time zone data at the bottom of the screen as needed. 5. Click the **Save** button. To add a new time zone: 1. Click the **New** button. 2. Enter the time zone data at the bottom of the screen. The GMT Offset value (required) must be a value between 12 and -12. 3. Click the **Save** button. The time zone will now be available within FLOWCAL. Once created, time zones cannot be deleted.

When the Time Zone Shift option is enabled for a meter or location, all dates and times will be adjusted by the offset amount defined for the selected time zone during data imports. (See: Date & Time Adjustments During Import and Import Options)

When the Time Zone Shift option is disabled for a meter or location, the offset is informational only. Time Zone Shift options are disabled by default.

docs.title: About FLOWCAL
docs.text: The About FLOWCAL screen contains information about your FLOWCAL installation, including version number, user and licensing information, database information, details about your modules and systems, and information about TESTit Integrated.

docs.title: Application Usage
docs.text: The Application Usage screen provides an overview of your specific data, including a breakdown of gas and liquid meters, locations, average tickets for the last 12 months, and quality sources.

docs.title: Data Sources
docs.text:
Data in the Application Usage screen is derived as follows:

Gas Meters

- **Active** - Gas meters with a status of Active for the current system date - **Inactive** - Gas meters with a status of Inactive for the current system date - **Physical** - Total active and inactive meters - **Calculated** - Total gas calculated meters - **Total Meters** - Sum of Physical and Calculated totals

Liquid Meters

- **Active** - Liquid meters with a status of Active for the current system date - **Inactive** - Liquid meters with a status of Inactive for the current system date - **Physical** - Total active and inactive meters - **Calculated** - Total liquid calculated meters - **Total Meters** - Sum of Physical and Calculated totals

Locations

- **Balances** - Total balance locations (created in the Location Editor) - **Liquid Caverns** - Total liquid caverns (created in the Liquid Cavern Editor) - **Comparisons** - Total comparison locations (created in the Comparison Editor) - **Inventories** - Total gas/liquid inventory locations (created in the Location Editor) and gas inventories (created in the Inventory Editor) - **Segments** - Total segment locations (created in the Location Editor) - **Stations** - Total station locations (created in the Location Editor) - **Tanks** - Total tanks (created in the Tank Editor)

Tickets

- **Attached Count** - Monthly average of tickets attached to a location over the last 12 months (does not include the current month) - **Standalone Count** - Monthly average of tickets not attached to a location over the last 12 months (does not include the current month)

Quality Sources

- **Gas Count** - Total GQ sources (created in the Gas Quality Source Editor) - **Liquid Count** - Total LQ sources (created in the Liquid Quality Source Editor)

docs.title: Batch Movement Reconciliation
docs.text:
Pipeline companies typically match meter batches to scheduled batch movements when scheduling batches to be injected into a pipeline at a given point (the receipt point). Pipeline operations will also schedule those same batches to come off the pipeline at a different point (the delivery point). These schedules can then be imported into FLOWCAL.

As the meter batches are imported or manually entered, FLOWCAL can then match the meter batches to the scheduled batch movement based on delivery and receipt point, and the time and amount of the batch. FLOWCAL will model a single batch movement between delivery and receipt points by comparing the batches of meter members within two locations based on product, origin, destination, start time (both origin and destination), and the batch size (configured as GSV, NSV, or mass).

A single batch movement will be associated to at least two meters in two locations.

The purpose of having two different locations is to create an association to a batch movement between two different FLOWCAL meters that exist physically at the delivery and receipt points. This gives FLOWCAL enough information to narrow down a batch product and match on criteria as it travels from one location in the pipeline (the origin), to the delivery point in the pipeline (the destination).

The delivery and receipt points being at the location level within FLOWCAL allows for multiple meters to be located where batches are being injected into or coming off the pipeline.

The meters located at the receipt and delivery points represent the start and end points (respectively) of the batch movement from the left to the right in the diagram. The area enclosed on the left is the Origin location to be configured and the area enclosed on the right is the Destination location to be configured.

Example The origin of a batch movement is Location 1 and the destination of the movement is Location 2. A scheduled batch movement is imported with a start and end date at the origin of 12/01/2018 09:00:00 – 12/01/12:00:00 for a batch size of GSV = 2000. The scheduled batch movement also defines the start and end date for the destination to be 12/1/2018 13:00:00 – 12/1/2018 16:00:00. Since the origin and destination of the batch movement correspond to Location 1 and Location 2, FLOWCAL will attempt to find batches within the meters on each of the locations that match the criteria defined on the batch movement schedule. The Batch Schedule Matching service will search through all meters within Location 1 to find a batch that matches the product, batch size, and origin start date from the schedule. Similarly, the Batch Schedule Matching service will search through all meters within Location 1 to find a batch that matches the product, batch size, and destination start date from the schedule.

Scheduled batch movements can be entered into FLOWCAL manually or imported from an Excel (.xls) file in the FLOWCAL-specified format. As batches are imported for meters with the Reconcile Batches option enabled, FLOWCAL will try to match each batch to a scheduled batch movement via the Batch Schedule Matching service (FcSrvBatchScheduleMatching.exe). If a batch is unable to be matched, exception 18205 will be generated and the queue entry will fail to be processed.

This method requires the Liquids add-on.

Manually Import a Scheduled Batch Movement

To import a scheduled batch movement manually: 1. Go to **Import** \> **Scheduled Batch Movement**. 2. Click the **Browse** button to find a .xls file or type the file path into the edit box. 3. Click **Import**. 4. When the import is complete, go to **Tools** \> **Batch Movement Reconciliation** to view the scheduled batch movements.

Automatically Import a Scheduled Batch Movement

To import a scheduled batch movement automatically, use the File Import service. Specify the folder to check for scheduled batch movements in the [Service Configuration](../Services/Service%20Configuration.md) screen within the Liquid Imports tab. Any .xls files in the specified folder or its sub-directories will be imported. If an imported meter batch cannot be matched to a scheduled batch movement, exceptions will be generated to alert the user.

Manually Enter Scheduled Batch Movements

To manually enter scheduled batch movements: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Liquids** \> **Batch Movement Reconciliation**. 2. Click **New**. The Scheduled Batch Movement Editor will open. 3. Define the criteria for the scheduled batch movement desired and click **Save**. 4. Click **Match** to manually associate batches to the schedule. (See: [Manually Associate Scheduled Batches](#Associate)) The product on the scheduled batch must match the product on the meter batch. For additional information on field definitions, see Scheduled Batch Movement File Format.

Batch Schedule Matching Service

Queue entries on the Batch Matching tab of the Service Queues will be processed by the FcSrvBatchScheduleMatching.exe service. FLOWCAL will then attempt to associate meter batches to the scheduled batch movements defined in the Batch Movement Reconciliation Viewer. If the service is unable to associate a batch to both the origin and destination specified on the scheduled batch movement, the queue entry status will be set to "Failed". If the service associates a batch to the origin and destination specified on the scheduled batch movement, the queue entry will be cleared from the list and the meter batches will now be associated to the scheduled batch movement.

Location Setup for Scheduled Batch Movements

To set up location information for scheduled batch movements, the following must be configured in the Location Editor (**Setup** \> **Location** \> **Editor** \> **Tools** \> **Info**): - The meter containing the batch, matching the origin within the schedule, must belong to the location that has the origin defined in Custom Field 1. - The meter containing the batch, matching the destination within the schedule, must belong to the location that has the destination defined in Custom Field 1. - Set the tolerance for the batch’s volume or mass and start time on the location, so that they fall within the range for the scheduled batch movement. - The total volume or mass for the actual meter batch must match the scheduled batch movement amount within the tolerance setup on the location. The tolerance is defined using the **Volume or Mass Must Be Within** value. - The start date and time of the actual meter batch must match the start time of the scheduled batch movement within the tolerance setup for the location. The tolerance is defined using the **Start Time Must Be Within** value.

Manually Associate Scheduled Batches

If a meter batch fails to be associated with a scheduled batch movement and does not fall within the scheduled batch movement tolerances defined in the [Location Editor](../../Locations/Location%20Editor/Location%20Editor.md), you can manually associate a meter batch to the scheduled batch movement. To manually associate a meter batch: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager** \> **Liquids** \> **Batch Movement Reconciliation**. 2. Specify the location, where the match should occur, and date range criteria that fits the schedule you want to modify. 3. Double-click the schedule to bring up the Batch Movement Association Editor. 4. Select **Batches Filtered**. 5. Change the filter criteria for origin date, destination date, and batch size to meet the criteria for the meter batch. 6. When meter batch appears, click **Edit**. 7. Right-click the batch and select **Associate**, then **Save**.

Scheduled Batch Movement File Format

The import file is an Excel (.xls) file with the following columns for each line of data. Blank lines in the file will be ignored. The first line in the file may be a header line, which will be ignored on import. Column Notes Shipper Name Up to 50 characters; must match a valid company within FLOWCAL that is marked as a shipper (Settings > Settings Manager > Contacts > Company Manager) Product ID or Commodity Code Must match a Product Code or Product Alias within FLOWCAL (Settings > Settings Manager > Liquids > Products) Batch Start Date and Time at Origin - Batch End Date and Time at Origin - Origin Up to 50 characters; must match exactly to a custom field 1 on a location within FLOWCAL (Setup > Location > Editor > Tools > Info) Destination Up to 50 characters; must match exactly to a custom field 1 on a location within FLOWCAL (Setup > Location > Editor > Tools > Info) Batch Size - Estimated Flow Rate - Estimated Arrival Date and Time at Destination - Movement ID Up to 50 characters; must be unique Comments Up to 500 characters Volume Type "G" - GSV; "N" - NSV; "M" - Mass

docs.title: Batch Schedule Editor
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires System Process – System Information privileges and the Liquids add-on.

Batch schedules can be assigned to a liquid meter to automatically create batches for meters that deliver batches on a known schedule, with known products. You can assign a different batch schedule for a meter on a month-by-month basis if the product flow changes, or if the day of the month that the batch starts on changes.

The use of a batch schedule can be helpful if batches are hand-keyed into the system, or if the import file does not contain the batch start/stop or the batch product information.

When batches are created from a schedule, each batch starts and ends at the contract hour set in meter characteristics on the day specified in the schedule.

The Batch Schedule Editor is used to create monthly schedules. To create an annual schedule, use the Annual Schedule Editor.

To create a monthly batch schedule: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Batch Schedule Editor** within the **Liquids** group. 3. Click the **New** button. 4. Enter a schedule name and description. 5. Double-click each day to include in the schedule. As days are selected, they will display in the grid to the right. Selected days will display with a yellow highlight. To de-select a day, double-click it again. 6. Click the down arrow for each day to define a product. 7. Click the **Save** button. Once created, the batch schedule can be assigned to a liquid meter in the Meter Editor (Liquids tab \> Schedules sub-tab).

For FLOWCAL to create batches based on a batch schedule, the Batch Scheduler utility (FcBatchScheduler.exe) must be run. If the the Batch Scheduler utility is run, but cannot create batches on a meter because it is locked by another process, such as meter rollups or a user performing edits, no messages will be generated. The utility should be run during off hours to minimize the chances of this happening and to minimize database access during peak hours. For additional details, see: Batch Scheduler Utility.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text:
• Meter Editor Liquids Tab
  • Batch Scheduler Utility

docs.title: Batch Scheduler Utility
docs.text:
The Batch Scheduler utility (FcBatchScheduler.exe) must be run to create batches for meters according to assigned batch schedules. The utility takes a year and month as arguments and creates scheduled batches for all meters for the respective measurement month according to the meter’s assigned schedule.

FcBatchScheduler.exe /month=\<YYYYmm>

Example Running the following command will create the scheduled batches for March 2024 for all meters that have a batch schedule assigned to them. C:\\ FcBatchScheduler.exe /month=202403

Running the utility can be automated by creating a script that calls the utility with the appropriate year/month argument. The argument must be dynamic to adjust the creation of batches for a new month. The script can be scheduled via Windows Scheduled Tasks on one the FLOWCAL application servers. The task must be programmed to run prior to the end of a given calendar month to create batches for the following month, and it should be scheduled to run multiple times in case one or meters are locked, and the batches were not created. A meter must have Meter Type and Calculation Method defined in the meter characteristic for the scheduled batches to be created. If you are using the Annual Schedule option, then your meter characteristic must also have a product.

Example - The current calendar month is February 2021 - The intent of running the utility during February is to create the expected batches for March 2021 - The script described above must then adjust the month plus one and run the following command: FcBatchScheduler.exe /month=202103

Running the utility can also be automated by creating a script that calls the utility with the number of days until start of the next month as an argument. The script can be scheduled via Windows Scheduled Tasks on one the FLOWCAL application servers. The task must be programmed to run prior to the end of a given calendar month to create batches for the following month, and it should be scheduled to run multiple times in case one or meters are locked, and the batches were not created. A meter must have Meter Type and Calculation Method defined in the meter characteristic for the scheduled batches to be created. If you are using the Annual Schedule option, then your meter characteristic must also have a product.

Example - The job is scheduled to run on the last day of the month every month to create batches for the next month - Run the following command: FcBatchScheduler.exe 1

docs.title: Origin & Destination Editor
docs.text:
FLOWCAL allows users to specify an Origin and a Destination on tickets. This information is typically passed from FLOWCAL to a downstream accounting system.

The Origin/Destination Editor allows users to enter label names for origins and destinations that can be used on tickets.

Example: If the user enters the label name "Houston", this name will show up in the drop-down box for Origin and/or Destination in the Ticket Editor, as well as on the printed ticket.

To add a new origin or destination: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Liquids** group, select **Origin and Destination Editor**. 3. Select a label name from the list and click New to create a new label name for an origin and/or destination and enter its information using the fields at the bottom of the screen. The Label Name field should be a Shipping Location relevant to the Customer. 4. You can also click **Edit** to modify an existing label name using the fields at the bottom of the screen. 5. Specify whether the label name may be used as an origin, a destination, or both. 6. Click **Save**.

docs.title: Origin/Destination by SPLC Code
docs.text:
FLOWCAL can be configured to require that Origins and Destinations be labeled and named by SPLC Code rather than just by text strings of the user's own choosing. In order for this requirement to become effective, the user must enable the Use SPLC Code for Origins and Destinations option under FLOWCAL Configuration.

The Standard Point Location Code (SPLC) is designed to provide each point originating freight and each point receiving freight in North America with a unique code number so constructed as to identify the point with its geographic location, using two digits to identify State, County and City and three digits to identify Sub-Code. Available SPLC codes can be found on the web at http://www.nmfta.org/pages/splc.aspx.

Example: If you enter an SPLC Code of "142000017", this code will show up in the drop down box for Origin and/or Destination in the Ticket Editor.

To add an SPLC code: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Liquids** group, select **Origin and Destination Editor**. 3. Click **New** to create a new SPLC Ccode for an origin and/or destination and enter its information using the fields at the bottom of the screen. 4. You can also select an SPLC code from the list and click **Edit** to modify an existing SPLC Code using the fields at the bottom of the screen. 5. Specify whether the SPLC code may be used as an origin, a destination, or both. 6. Click **Save**.

docs.title: Rail Pattern Editor
docs.text:
Rail patterns are datetime effective, allowing the user to set a route and characteristics on a rail pattern for a given period of time. The Rail Pattern Editor is used to create railroad patterns that can be set on tickets where the Transportation Method is set to Rail.

To access the Rail Pattern Editor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Liquids** group, **select Rail Pattern Editor**.

Rail Pattern Screen Details

- **Route Point** - A location along the rail. - **Shipper and Product**- Must be set in order to save the Rail Pattern. - **Shipper, Railroad, Consignee, and Consignor** - Can be created and edited in FLOWCAL’s Company Manager. - **From and To** - Can be created and edited in FLOWCAL’s Facility Editor. - **Origin and Destination** - Can be created and edited in FLOWCAL’s Origin and Destination Editor.

docs.text:
• Company Editor
  • Facility Editor
  • Origin & Destination Editor
  • Ticket Details

docs.title: Ticket Type Editor
docs.text:
TicketsA measurement of data at a single point in time. A ticket can have a start date and an end date, but FLOWCAL treats it as a single data point. can be standalone or they can be assigned to locations where the location represents a measurement point, such a lease automatic custody transfer (LACT), tickets generated while loading/unloading a vessel (ship), or measurement points such as flares or blowdowns.

You will need to define a ticket type when entering a ticket for liquid measurement in the Ticket Editor, Ticket Autofill Editor, or Gas Loss Ticket Editor, or when setting parameters in the Ticket Search screen. FLOWCAL accommodates several ticket types, which are configurable using the Ticket Type Editor.

To access the Ticket Type Editor and modify ticket types: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Ticket Type** within the **Liquids** group. 3. Select a ticket type and click the **Edit** button. To create a new ticket type: 1. Click the **New** button. 2. Enter the new ticket type name in the **Ticket Type** field.

docs.title: See also:
docs.text: Ticket Types

docs.title: Ticket Types
docs.text:
The following ticket types are supported in FLOWCAL:

Batch Meter

Batch Meter tickets represent meter-measured product flow and contain a continuous record of meter operation. To view batch data, select "Batch Meter" in the Ticket Type selector. If you double-click a batch record in the grid, the Volume Editor will open and display the month containing that batch.

Blow Down

Blow Down tickets serve to indicate the quantity of a product lost by atmospheric venting. These tickets use FLOWCAL's API 12.2 Liquid Volumetric calculation. The calculation uses a K-factor, meter factor, and DFM of 1.0.

Cavern Level

Cavern Level tickets specify the amount of product contained within a cavern (inventory) at a given point in time.

Flare

Flare tickets represent the amount of product burned off via flaring. These tickets use FLOWCAL's API 12.2 Liquid Volumetric calculation. The calculation uses a K-factor, meter factor, and DFM of 1.0.

Gauge Ticket

Gauge tickets specify the amount of product contained within a tank (inventory) at a given point in time. Enabling the Gauge ticket type in FLOWCAL requires the Liquids Inventory module. #### Upright cylindrical tank: The Floating Roof Correction field label will change to Floating Roof Adjustment if the "FRA Built Into Table" option is selected in the tank capacity table. #### Spherical tank:

Inventory Empty

Enabling the Inventory Empty ticket type in FLOWCAL requires the Liquids Inventory module. Inventory Empty tickets are created when an inventory empty operation is initiated for a liquid cavern; these tickets represent an event in which the entire inventory volume is reduced to 0. This is to match the calculated inventory in FLOWCAL to the actual reported empty from the field. A non-zero difference can result from measurement inaccuracies into and out of the tank or cavern. Inventory Empty tickets cannot be edited manually, and they can only be created from the Liquid Cavern Editor. The data displayed is automatically calculated once the empty operation is performed and can only be changed by modifying data that will change the inventory prior to the empty operation (i.e., inventory data that has an effective date prior to the empty operation). When this data is modified, the Inventory Empty ticket will automatically revise the data, creating prior period adjustment records as necessary. Inventory Empty tickets can only be closed by the [Meter Close service](../Services/All%20Services.md#MeterClose). Hydrocarbon Inventory Empty Ticket Non-Hydrocarbon Inventory Empty The Allowable field is dependent upon which fluid service is assigned to the liquid cavern. Net Allowable is only available for hydrocarbon caverns and Mass Allowable is only available for non-hydrocarbon. The fluid service of the cavern is driven off of the product selection.

Meter

Meter tickets measure product flow as indicated by a meter, similarly to Batch tickets. Unlike Batch tickets, however, Meter tickets represent one transaction at a given point in time. The meter type and product specified control the display of certain fields on the Main tab. The calculation method, meter type and product will all affect the values expected and returned.

Product Conversion

Product Conversion tickets indicate an amount of product converted into another product (performed at the location level). Product Conversion tickets may be created for tanks, liquid caverns, or standard locations, but require the following conditions to be met: - The product to be converted must be flowing within the location of interest at the time a conversion is specified. - The product to be converted must have a valid conversion product assigned to it within the product editor. - The data for the location where the conversion is to occur must be rolled up. Once these conditions are met, a Product Conversion ticket can be created by specifying the time of the conversion, the appropriate location, the product to convert from, the product to convert to, and the relevant measurement values for each product. When a Product Conversion ticket is saved, each side of the conversion will appear as a distinct ticket, but each half will remain associated with the other. Any change to the common data within one of the tickets will apply to both tickets. The "From" ticket will inherently have a direction of "Outlet" while the "To" ticket will have a direction of "Inlet". Product Conversion tickets can be set up to have the pressure gauge type of either "Gauge" or "Absolute".  The Pressure Measurement Type and the Atmospheric Pressure can still be edited on each Product Conversion ticket if the default values are different for the "From" ticket or the "To" ticket.

Rail Car

Rail Car tickets represent the amount of fluid in a rail car at a given point in time. The Level and Level Type fields function similarly to those seen for Tank Gauge and Tank Run tickets, except there is no capacity table from which to derive a volume. The total observed volume must be manually specified to calculate the gross standard volume and mass. The fields in the right column are informational for display on printed tickets. The CTL will be calculated from the density and temperature provided. You may also manually input a CTL value, and the manually entered value will be used to calculate gross standard volume.

Run Ticket

Run tickets define the change in inventory of a tank due to a specific movement event. #### Upright cylindrical tank: The Extended Detail button is only visible if the "Open and Close Values for All Values" option is selected under Tank Characteristics.

Scale

Scale tickets are used to quantify the intake or output of fluid indicated by a change in weight over the course of a transaction. By specifying the weight in and weight out values, FLOWCAL can calculate the net weight of the transaction. Along with the product's table type, the observed density, the observed temperature, and the net weight, FLOWCAL can calculate the gross standard volume. The net standard volume may be calculated using the gross standard volume and the S&W percent. The Weigh In, Weigh Out, Out Scale ID, and In Scale ID fields are used to specify the times at which the movement started and ended.

Vessel Tank

Vessel Tank tickets capture the load (or unload) movement associated with a single tank located on a vessel. Because vessels are transient, setting up a tank in FLOWCAL is not usually practical. Therefore, each Vessel Tank ticket completely specifies characteristics of the tank and calculations as well as the arrival and departure ullages and the load summary. Vessel Tank tickets can be attached to a location for balancing and accumulating inventory, but the ticket does not draw characteristic information from that location. Vessel Tank tickets do not support a capacity table. Calculations start with a given Total Observed Volume (TOV). Levels can be provided for informational purposes but do not affect the calculations. (See: [Vessel Tank Calculation Symbols](Vessel%20Tank%20Calculation%20Symbols.md) for a glossary of symbols associated with vessel tanks.) Vessel Tank tickets support two calculation methods. API 12.1.2 (2012) is a volumetric calculation in that it calculates the volume of liquid first, then the mass of liquid. See Diagram 1. Mass is an inferred mass calculation that calculates the mass of liquid first, then the volume of liquid. See Diagram 2. Vapor is always calculated as inferred mass, i.e., mass of vapor first, then volume of vapor. A prime feature of Vessel Tanks is the ability to validate third-party inspection reports. In practice, the inspector-provided reports, the arrival and departure ullages specifically, are brought in as vessel tank tickets. The ticket calculations are verified via correlation factors that are determined for each quantity. Vessel Tank tickets use a “Vessel” re-calc method for this purpose.

docs.title: Vessel Tank Calculation Symbols
Quantities
docs.text:
FW (Free Water Volume) - The water present in a tank that is not suspended in the liquid. Free water may include bottom sediments. Generally, FW is taken from the tank capacity table prior to any corrections, such as those for floating roof and the temperature of the tank shell.

GOV (Gross Observed Volume) - The total volume of all petroleum liquids plus entrained sediments and water at observed temperature and pressure. Tank shell corrections due to the temperature of the liquid and the tank pressure are applied. An adjustment for a floating roof may also be included.

GOV = [(TOV - FW) * CTSh(liq) *CPSh] ± \<FRA or FRC>

GSV (Gross Standard Volume) - The total volume of the petroleum liquids and entrained sediments and water, plus the volume of product vapor, stated at base temperature and pressure conditions.

GSV = VOL + VOV

MASS (Total Mass) - The total mass of the petroleum liquids and entrained sediments and water, plus the mass of product vapor.

MASS = MOL + MOV

MOL (Mass of Liquid) - The mass of the petroleum liquids plus entrained sediments and water.

Volumetric: MOL = VOL / Rho(base)(liq)

Inferred Mass: MOL = GOV * Rho(alt)(liq)

MOV (Mass of Vapor) - The mass of the product vapors in the vapor space.

MOV = VS * Rho(alt)(vap)

NVOL (Net Volume of Liquid) - The volume of petroleum liquids at to base temperature and pressure conditions.

NVOL = VOL * CSW

NSV (Net Standard Volume) - The total volume of the petroleum liquids plus the volume of product vapor, stated at base temperute and pressure conditions.

NSV = NVOL + VOV

SWV (Sediment & Water Volume) - The volume of entrained sediments and water (S&W) at base temperature and pressure conditions

SWV = VOL - NVOL

TOV (Total Observed Volume) - The total measured volume of all petroleum liquids, sediments and water (S&W), and free water (FW) at observed temperature and pressure. Generally, TOV is taken from the tank capacity table prior to any corrections, such as those for floating roof and the temperature of the tank shell.

UVS (Uncorrected Vapor Space) - The actual volume of space occupied by product vapors at observed temperature and pressure prior to any corrections.

UVS = Tank Capacity - TOV + Tank Dead Space

VOL (Volume of Liquid) - The volume of petroleum liquids plus entrained sediments and water corrected to base temperature and pressure conditions.

Volumetric: VOL = GOV * CTL * CPL

Inferred Mass: VOL = MOL / Rho(base)(liq)

VOV (Volume of Vapor) - The volume of product vapors in the vapor space corrected to base temperature and pressure conditions.

VOV = MOV / Rho(base)(vap)

VS (Vapor Space) - The volume of space occupied by product vapors at observed temperature and pressure and including corrections due to the temperature of the vapor and the tank pressure.

VS = UVS * CTSh(vap) * CPSh

docs.title: Densities
docs.text:
Rho(alt)(liq) (Alternate liquid density) - Density of product liquids at tank conditions.

Rho(alt)(vap) (Alternate vapor density) - Density of product vapors at tank conditions.

Rho(base)(liq) (Base liquid density) - Density of product liquid at base conditions.

Rho(base)(vap) (Base vapor density) - Density of product vapors at base conditions.

docs.title: Correction Factors
docs.text:
CTSh(liq) - Shell volume correction due to liquid temperature

CTSh(vap) - Shell volume correction due to vapor temperature

CPSh - Shell volume correction due to tank pressure

CSW - Liquid volume correction due to entrained sediments & water

CTL - Liquid volume correction due to temperature of the liquid

CPL - Liquid volume correction due to pressure of the liquid

docs.title: Characteristic Tab
docs.text:
The Characteristic tab under the Product Editor contains datetime effective fields which are used in the meter and ticket level calculations corresponding to the effective dates specified. This includes selecting which API table or calculation is to be used for calculating correction factors such as CTL and CPL.

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Characteristic tab: - **Table** - Under the Characteristics tab, select the API Table or calculation method for calculating the CTL, CPL, and CTPL. - **Secondary** - If Table is set to Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27), Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27-EXT), COSTALD, or Modified TP-2, a secondary table can be selected, as well as the Conditions under which the Secondary table will be used. - **Type** - If Table is set to Aromatics and Cyclohexane, then the user must also choose a Type, such as Benzene. - **Alpha** - If Table is set to Table C – Special Applications (1980) or Table C – Special Applications (2004) a value must be specified for alpha. - **Density Offset** - If Table or Secondary is set to Modified TP-2 is chosen, then an option for a Density Offset appears. This offset is added to the base density and flowing density calculated in relative density units. - **Base Density** - A value for the Base Density is optional, but may be defined. This value is used as the default during calculations when base density cannot be calculated due to a missing observed density. It is useful for products such as propane and ethane that have a known base density, but not so for a product like crude oil where the base density varies. If Aromatics is selected for Table, a base density and its corresponding units is automatically defined based on the selected Type, unless Type is set to Mixed Xylene, 300 to 350 Aromatics or 350 to 400 Aromatics. Also, select the base density units from the Base Density drop-down. A Base Density must be provided for the following tables: - Aromatics & Cyclohexane (2004) - Ethylene (1974) - Ethylene (2013) - Propylene (1974) - Water (2003) The Base Density field and Units field are not editable for the Water (2003) product table and for the Aromatics & Cyclohexane (2004) product table, except for Mixed Xylene, 300 to 350 Aromatics or 350 to 400 Aromatics. - **Base Temp** - Select the Base Temperature to be used for this product. The user is limited to 15°C, 20°C and 60°F as these are the only values supported by liquids calculation standards. The appropriate temperature base must be defined in the Temperature Base Editor (Settings Manager → Application → Temperature Base) before the user can select it in the Products Editor. - **Base Pressure** - Specify the Base Pressure for the product. The user is limited to 14.696 psi and 101.325 kPa as these are the only values supported by liquids calculation standards and by FLOWCAL. The appropriate pressure base must be defined in the Pressure Base Editor (Settings Manager→ Application → Pressure Base) before the user can select it in the Products Editor. - **EVP** - The user can specify a default EVP to be used in case one is not provided in the import and one cannot be calculated. It is useful for products such as propane and ethane that have a known EVP, but not so for a product like crude oil where the EVP varies. - **EVP Calc Method** - An EVP Calculation method can be specified for the following tables: - Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27) - Table E – Light Hydrocarbons (TP27-EXT) - COSTALD - Modified TP-2 If an EVP calculation method is not specified, TP-15 will be used by default - **Density Import Option** - FLOWCAL has 3 fields for importing observed density values into meters: - Observed Density, Corrected Density - Observed Density in Relative Density - Observed Density in API Degrees By default FLOWCAL reads from Observed Density, Corrected Density based on the Density Import option being set to Engineering Units. If you want FLOWCAL to import from one of the other 2 fields for observed density, then you specify that in the drop-down. Selecting Relative Density will cause FLOWCAL to read from Observed Density in Relative Density. Select API Degrees will cause FLOWCAL to read from Observed Density in API degrees. There is no failover where if the product is set to read from Observed Density in API Degrees and that field is empty we will look in the other 2 fields. Do not change this option unless you know that the system generating your meter import data is populating the specified field. If the Density Import Option is set to Engineering Units and units are specified in the drop-down, when FLOWCAL imports density, the observed density units in meter characteristics will be set to the units specified. If the Density Import Option is set to Relative Density, when FLOWCAL imports density, the observed density units in meter characteristics will be set to relative density. If the Density Import Option is set to API Degrees, when FLOWCAL imports density, the observed density units in meter characteristics will be set to API degrees. - **Purity Product Options** - Specify Purity Product Options as required for applying analysis to the product. The option to set a product to a purity product is on the Product tab. For details on choosing the Recalc Method, refer to [Recalc Methods](../../../Volume%20Editor/Recalculation%20Methods.md).

docs.title: Conversions Tab
docs.text:
The Conversions tab under the Product Editor contains non-datetime effective options and is available when the user selects a product name from the product tree.

Product conversion is the process of re-classifying a product as a another product. The Conversions Tab allows users to specify what product another product can be converted to when creating a product conversion ticket in the Ticket Editor or Ticket Search. If no valid products are specified for conversion to, then a product cannot be converted to any other product.

Example: An example of a product conversion is when two products follow each other in a pipeline. Where the two products meet there is an interface layer which may be reclassified as one of the two products or possibly as a slop product to be reprocessed. Another example is in a storage cavern. The cavern may have propane in it and off spec propane is added to it. The propane that was initially in the cavern may now need to be reprocessed and so it may be converted to demethanized mix.

Set up a Product Conversion

To convert from one product to another or reclassify a product as another product, the user needs to specify Valid Product Conversions. When creating a product conversion ticket, only products that have a Valid Product Conversion defined can be selected as the From product. Once the From product is selected, only products that are set up as a Valid Product Conversion for the selected product will be available to convert to. **Example:** The user may have three products set up in FLOWCAL: propane, Y-grade and crude oil. If the user's propane is off spec and it needs to be reprocessed, it would be valid to convert it to Y-grade, but converting it to crude oil would not be sensible. Similarly, crude oil cannot be converted to Y-grade or propane, so given those product choices, it would not be setup with any Valid Product Conversions. Limiting what products can be converted to reduces the opportunity for errors to be made by the user. To convert a product: 1. Select the product name to convert. 2. Select a product from the drop-down at the bottom of the Valid Product Conversion box. 3. Click **Add**.

Remove a Product Conversion

To remove a product conversion: 1. Highlight the product in the Valid Product Conversions box. 2. Click **Remove**.

docs.title: Discrimination Tab
docs.text:
The Discrimination tab under the Product Editor contains datetime effective settings and is available when the user selects a date range from the product tree. Here the user can specify the number of decimal digits to be displayed or allowed for data entry for any of the listed fields. These values also control the number of decimal places displayed on reports for these fields.

When these fields are viewed in the Volume Editor, Ticket Editor and Ticket Search, values will be displayed per the defined discrimination values. Data entry is also limited for fields based on the discrimination level.

If the Apply Discrimination in Calculations option is checked, values used in liquid calculations on meter batches and tickets are rounded per the discrimination on the product selected before any calculations are performed; otherwise, values are used at full precision

The discrimination level specified for meter factor defines where it will be rounded for use in the calculation of the CCF. This rounding occurs regardless of whether the Apply Discrimination in Calculations option is checked or not.

CCF = Round(meter factor,x) * Round(CTL,y) * Round(CPL,z)

where: x, y and z are discrimination levels defined in the Product editor for each field

The discrimination level specified for CCF defines where it will be rounded for use in the calculation of Gross Standard Volume (GSV) from Indicated Volume (IV). If the CCF discrimination is set to unused, GSV will be calculated from an unrounded CCF. This rounding occurs regardless of whether the Apply Discrimination in Calculations option is checked or not.

GSV = IV * Round(CCF, w)

Where: w is the discrimination level defined in the Product Editor for CCF

Volume discrimination levels define discrimination for all volumes, including IV, GSV, NSV, SWV, Theoretical Production, component volume, and component net allowable volumes.

docs.title: Info Tab
docs.text:
The Info tab under the Product Editor contains non-datetime effective information which allows users to specify an STCC Number (Standard Transportation Commodity Code), a DOT Hazard Classification, and Notes. Once added, these fields do not appear elsewhere in FLOWCAL, but they can be displayed on ticket reports. STCC Number and DOT Hazard are displayed on FLOWCAL's standard rail Bill of Lading (BOL).

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Info tab: - **STCC \#** - A Standard Transportation Commodity Code (STCC#) can be specified. This can be printed on tickets. The STCC# is required by the Department of Transportation to be on all Rail and Truck BOLs. The field is free form text and can be up to 8 characters. - **DOT Hazard** - A DOT Hazard class can be specified (such as UN1075, Propane). DOT Hazard classes can be setup in the DOT Hazard Editor. - **Notes** - Add notes in the Notes section as needed. Up to 1,000 characters can be stored for each product.

docs.title: Product Tab
docs.text:
The Product tab under the Product Editor contains non-datetime effective options and is available when users select a product name from the product tree.

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Product tab: - **Fluid Service** - Select a fluid service according to the product. Available options are: - Hydrocarbon (default) - Nonhydrocarbon Selecting "Nonhydrocarbon" will enable the Mass Allowable sub-tab under the Validations tab. - **Show Uncorrected Density** - Choose whether or not Uncorrected Density should appear on printed tickets. Uncorrected Density is the density before the Density Meter Factor (DMF) is applied. - **Show Observed Density** - Choose whether or not Observed Density should appear on printed tickets. - **Show Density Meter Factor** - Choose whether or not the Density Meter Factor should appear on printed tickets. - **Show Alkenes** - Choose whether or not the product is sampled for alkenes (ethylene, propylene, and butylenes). If alkenes and neopentane are disabled here, they will also be disabled for entry on Analysis Entry screens in the Volume Editor, Ticket Editor, Liquid Quality Source, and Standalone Samples when entering data for the given product. These fields will also be suppressed on printed tickets when analysis information is shown. On import of meter, ticket and quality source data, if values are provided for alkenes and neopentane, they will be imported, but an exception will be generated. - **Show Neopentane** - Choose whether the product is sampled for neopentane. If not enabled, neopentane will be disabled for the Analysis entry. - **Show -** Determine what to Show on a printed report. When printing a ticket for a product that uses Table E, COSTALD, TP-2 or REFPROP, FLOWCAL shows either the mass percent and component mass, the liquid volume percent and component volumes or both percentages as well as component mass and component volume. That is defined by the following choices: - **Use Meter’s Calc. Method** – If the component volumes are calculated using LV% applied to the NSV, then the report displays liquid volume % and component volume on the report. If component volumes are calculated by applying Mass% to the mass to get component mass and then component density is used to get the component volumes, then the report displays mass%, component mass, LV% and component volumes. - **Volume** – Always display liquid volume % and component volume on the report. - **Mass** – Always display mass % and component mass on the report. - **Sample Required for Batch Meter** - This option is used to ensure that Batch Meter data with the specified Product has an Analysis applied. If this option is enabled in the Product Editor and there is an LQ Assignment set up on that Meter, then any time data with that Product that is created or edited within the time frame of the LQ Assignment, FLOWCAL validates that there is an Analysis applied to that data. If there is not an Analysis on the Assignment during the data time frame and there is no Sample Override, then FLOWCAL generates exception 18200, LQA - Sample Not Found. Having an Analysis on the Assignment during the time frame, or having a Sample Override on that data keeps the exception from being generated. If the Purity Product is set up in the Product Editor with an Analysis attached, the Analysis applies to the data, but the exception is still not resolved. If an LQ Assignment is not set up on the Meter then FLOWCAL does not check whether an Analysis is applied to the data or not. The validation is always looking at the LQ Assignment for an Analysis. Even if the Meter data has an Analysis, if the Assignment does not contain an Analysis for the time frame or a Sample Override is not applied then the exception is still generated. - **Apply HYC** - When a sample density is provided, it may have been measured with a hydrometer. If the density is not at the base temperature, it needs to have a hydrometer correction applied when calculating base density. There are three options for hydrometer correction in the Product Editor: - **None** – No hydrometer correction is needed. The density is either at base temperature, the density is not from a measurement with a hydrometer or the density has already had hydrometer correction applied. - **Default Yes** – Typically a hydrometer correction needs to be calculated and applied as part of the base density calculation. - **Default No** – Typically a hydrometer correction does not need to be calculated and applied as part of the the base density calculation, but sometimes it will. The user has the option to select when to calculate and apply a hydrometer correction. - **Sample Required for Standalone Ticket** - This option is used to ensure that any Ticket with that Product has an Analysis. If this option is enabled in the Product Editor, then any Ticket that is created or edited with that Product is checked for an Analysis on that Ticket. If there is not an Analysis on the Ticket, then FLOWCAL generates exception 18200, "LQA - Sample Not Found". When FLOWCAL is validating that there is an Analysis on the Ticket, having an S&W%, Mole%, Mass%, or LV% is sufficient enough to keep the exception from being generated. The validation is not run for imported Standalone Tickets. - **Odorant Allowed** - Hydrocarbons such as propane that are sold for public use are odorized or stenched before being shipped. If a product has odorant added, check Odorant Allowed. This allows for specifying on truck and rail tickets that odorant was added, what the odorant was, and how much odorant was added. Enabling this option also enables the flag on the Accounting tab of the Ticket Editor. If you have a product such as crude oil that is never odorized, then you do not want to enable this option. For a product such as propane which may be odorized before leaving your facility, this option should be enabled. - **Generate Exceptions for Unavailable S & W % and CSW** - If an S&W value is expected for a product such as crude oil or NGL and the user wants to be alerted via an exception if one is not on the batch, then enable this option. - **Purity Product** - Setting up a product as a Purity Product has two implications. First, when calculating the sum of component volumes, this value is set to match the Net Standard Volume (NSV) and all component volumes are back calculated from this value using the liquid volume percentages for the sample. Second, the option to assign a default quality source becomes available. If no sample is available from a quality source for a batch, then the sample on the default quality source is used. The sample is also automatically applied to tickets with the product unless the ticket belongs to a location with an assigned quality source. This is useful for products such as propane where a sample is not always collected and a standard analysis is assumed. - **Max component to report** - Analysis on a sample can be done out to C10. When the component volumes are reported on a printed ticket, the product may dictate that everything above a certain component be reported as that component. For instance on propane, analysis may be taken out to C4 for accurate component balancing, but all component volumes will be reported as C3. Setting the max component to report to C3 will cause the component volume from iso-C4 and n-C4 to be reported as C3 component volume. FLOWCAL lumps these values together into a single value for viewing in the Components tab in the volume editor and the ticket editor and also for display on net Allowable ticket reports. Options for Max Component to Report are C2, C3, C3H6, iso-C4, n-C4, iso-C5, n-C5, C6, C7, and C8. If nothing is selected, then all component volumes are reported per the analysis. - **Min Component to Report** - Analysis on a sample may include lighter components such as C1 and C2. When the component volumes are reported on a printed ticket, the product may dictate that everything below a certain component be reported as that component. For instance on propane, analysis may include C2 for accurate component balancing, but all component volumes will be reported as C3. Setting the min component to report to C3 will cause the component volume from C2 to be reported as C3 component volume. FLOWCAL lumps these values together into a single value for viewing in the Components tab in the volume editor and the ticket editor and also for display on net Allowable ticket reports. Options for Min Component to Report are C1, C2, C3, iso-C4, n-C4, iso-C5, n-C5, and C6. If nothing is selected, then all component volumes are reported per the analysis. The rolling of components into a higher component is done after net allowable rules, if any are specified, have been applied. - **Roll Ethylene into C2** - When checked, any component volume calculated from ethylene in the analysis is reported as C2 component volume. When the min component to report to is higher than C2, then ethylene volume is rolled into the minimum component. This option is only available when the Min Component to Report is set to C1 or C2. - **Roll Propylene into C3** - When checked, any component volume calculated from propylene in the analysis is reported as C3 component volume. When the max component to report to is C2 or C3, then propylene volume is rolled into the maximum component. This option is only available when the Min Component to Report is set to C1, C2 or C3 and the Max Component to report is C4 or higher. - **Roll Butylenes into C4** - When checked, any component volume calculated from butylenes in the analysis is reported as C4 component volume. When the max component to report to is higher than C4, then butylenes volume is rolled into the minimum component. This option is only available when the Max Component to Report is set to C5, C6, C7 or C8.

Product Aliases

When setting up a product in FLOWCAL, the user must set a product code. This code is then used to map a product during import to a product in FLOWCAL. Potentially, each flow computer or data source has different codes for the same product. **Example:** The user may have one system where demethanized mix is set up with a code of Y, whereas in another system demethanized mix is set up with a code of YGRADE. To accommodate this, FLOWCAL allows specification of product Aliases. Demethanized mix could be set up with a product code of Y and an alias of YGRADE or vice versa. Managing product aliases: 1. To add an alias, click **New** below the Aliases section. 2. Type in the name of a unique product alias in pop-up box. Click **OK** to add it. 3. To remove an alias, highlight the Alias and click **Delete** below the Aliases section. 4. To modify an existing alias, highlight it and click **Edit** below the Aliases section. Each alias product ID can only belong to one product. An alias cannot be used on more than one product or be used as a product code on another product.

C+ Type “Apply Extended As” Rules

In the Quality Source Analysis Editor, if the “Has Extended Analysis” option is selected, FLOWCAL will follow the Apply Extended As value defined under Product \> Purity Product Options. Example If a sample contains a full analysis (220 components) that goes out to C10, and the “Apply Extended As” option in any of the three places listed above is set to C6+, FLOWCAL will sum the values from C6 to C10 and apply the sum to C6. FLOWCAL will also apply the C6+ extended characteristics. If the “Has Extended Analysis” option is not selected, FLOWCAL will apply the sample as it is given on the source and will apply the extended characteristics for the highest component that has a value. If the highest component that has a value is less that C6, the C6+ extended characteristics will be applied.

docs.title: Validations Tab
docs.text:
The Validations tab under the Product Editor contains datetime effective fields where the user can set up validation limits for Density, Correction Factors (CTL, CPL and CTPL), Product Specifications, Net Allowable, and Mass Allowable.

There are no default limits set for Product Specification, Net Allowable, or Mass Allowable fields.

Density

Here, users can specify the number of decimal places (discrimination level) that imported values for Density Factors will rounded to in order to verify that they are the same as the FLOWCAL calculated values. An exception is generated if the rounded import value does not match the FLOWCAL calculated value. The **Run on Imports and Edits** checkbox must be checked for the validation to occur. Density and Correction Factors contain default limits (set initially when FLOWCAL is installed) that may be modified. The limits dictate the number of decimal places displayed in FLOWCAL and on printed reports for each field. **Example:** Meter flowing density is imported in a CFX file and is also calculated by FLOWCAL from the observed density. If the imported value is in API Degrees and the Rounding Factor for API Degrees is set to one, then the imported value will be rounded to one decimal place before being compared to the FLOWCAL calculated value. The Primary Density Calc Method is available for products with a calculation table of Table-E (TP-27), Table-E Extended (TP-27 EXT), COSTALD, or Modified TP-2. The options are COSTALD and Modified TP-2. The selected Primary Density Calc Method will be used on meter batches to calculate a density based on the provided analysis at the observed density conditions. This density can be used to validate the observed density. When a sample is manually entered in an LQ source or as a standalone sample, then the sample follows the setup of Sample Density Calc. Method as the default calculation for the Base Density Calc Method. The user can manually override this default when entering or editing a sample. For Products using Table-E (TP-27) or Table-E Extended (TP-27 EXT), the user may choose to Use Relative Density from Analysis As Observed, if Observed Density is Missing and to Use Relative Density from Analysis In TP-15 Calc. instead of Observed Density. Standalone tickets using a Table E product follow the setup on the product for these two options. Meters follow the setup for these two options on the product, unless these options have a different setup at the meter level.

Correction Factors

Here the number of decimal places (discrimination level) may be specified for where rounding is done on CTL, CPL and CTPL for calculation of the Combined Correction Factor (CCF). CCF = Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z) **where:** x, y and z are discrimination levels defined in the Product Editor for each field If the **Use Rounded CTPL in CCF** application option is selected, then the precision specified here for CTPL will be used. In this case: CCF = Round(meter factor,x) \* Round(Round(CTL,y) \* Round(CPL,z),w) **where:** w, x, y and z are discrimination levels defined in the Product Editor for each field with w being the precision defined for CTPL

Product Spec

On the Product Spec. and Product Spec.2 sub-tabs, users can specify the minimum and maximum limits for components and other data points that are applied to liquid quality sources, liquid meters, and tickets. The Percent Type field specifies whether the limits are by: Mole %, Liquid Volume %, Mass %, or PPM. Limits for Product Spec.2 properties that do not have the percent type are by unit. [Exceptions 30009 - 30040](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/30000/30000-30999.md) and [exceptions 4800 - 4860](../../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/4000/4800-4899.md) are generated for records outside of the specified limits for the product. The **Run on Imports and Edits** option must be selected for the validation to occur.

Net Allowable

On the Net Allowable tab, users can specify net allowable limits per product. FLOWCAL calculates component volumes and component mass for meters and tickets based on the analysis applied. Once these have been calculated, net allowable limits are applied. Component volumes above the net allowable limits are removed from the net allowable component volumes. Net allowable component volumes can be viewed in the Volume Editor and the Ticket Editor, as well as on numerous Net Allowable reports. Limits that can be specified for Net Allowable amount are: - The volume of CO2 allowed as a percentage of ethane volume - The volume of nitrogen allowed as a percentage of total component volume - The volume of methane allowed can be specified as the minimum or the maximum of the following: - Percentage of total component volume less nitrogen and CO2 - Percentage of ethane - Percentage of ethane and heavier (C2 - C10). When specified, if the value of methane, nitrogen or CO2 exceeds the specified limits, the allowed amount is calculated and appears on batch reports and in various editors and rollup viewers. These are set based on product specifications for each customer’s company. Typically, there is no value in CO2 or nitrogen and the net allowable amounts for these two components is zero.

Mass Allowable

Mass Allowable calculations only apply to non-hydrocarbon components. The Mass Allowable tab is enabled when a non-hydrocarbon fluid service is selected on the Products tab. On the Mass Allowable tab, non-hydrocarbon components can be rolled into one another and maximum limits can be set for the component mass percent. If enabled, when component values are calculated for non-hydrocarbon components, FLOWCAL will roll specified components into one another and apply mass allowable limits. Once a component is rolled into another component, it cannot be rolled again and a max mass percent cannot be specified. Components also cannot roll into a component that is already rolled into something else. Example If hydrogen is rolled into helium: - The Max Mass % field for hydrogen will be disabled. - The component drop-down for helium will be disabled. If another component is then selected to roll into hydrogen: - A message will display, stating that there is an invalid selection, and the selection will not be saved. Warning pop-up message The **Run on Imports and Edits** option must be selected for the validation to occur.

docs.title: Product Editor
docs.text:
The Products Editor allows users to set up the productsTypes of fluid being measured, such as crude oil, natural gasoline, or propane that are to be measured in FLOWCAL. Setting up a product requires knowledge of which API table or calculation is to be used for calculating the correction for the temperature of the liquid (CTL) and the correction for the pressure of the liquid (CPL).

To access the Product Editor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Liquids** section, select **Products**.

Setting up a Product

To set up a product: 1. Launch the Product Editor and click **New**. A new product will be displayed in the product tree on the left of the form. You can expand the list to view the effective dates. Upon save of a newly created product, it will only have one time range for all of time, as shown above, and the dates cannot be edited while in New mode. 2. Enter a product name and a product code. The product code is used to match a product in FLOWCAL to a product that is imported into FLOWCAL. These fields are required and the values must be unique. 3. Click the button next to the Color label to select a color for the product. The color specified is displayed in the Volume Editor, on the Ticket Editor grid, and in the Ticket Search grid. Using different colors for different products makes it easier to see a change in product on multi-product screens. 4. Configure additional settings as appropriate under the 6 tabs in the Product Editor. 5. Click **Save**.

Editing a Product

The Product Editor also provides several other functional settings for products. These additional functions are available in the form area to the right of the Product Tree, organized by tabs. The date-effective options are available when the user selects a datetime effective range from the product tree. To edit a product: 1. Select a product name and the date range of interest for the product from the tree view. 2. Click **Edit**. Only saved products may be edited. Only products that are not associated with another item, such as a meter, a source, or a ticket, may be deleted. 3. The **From** and **To** date fields become editable as well as the characteristics for the product. Enter the required information. 4. Enter an effective date range and specifies the characteristics for the time range entered. 5. If necessary, configure additional settings under the **Validations** and **Discrimination** tabs. 6. Click **Save**.
