docs.title: Access Lists
docs.text:
Use the Access List Editor to give users access to specific meters, quality sources, and locations. First, create an access list that contains meters, quality sources, and locations, and then assign the users and groups that should have access to those items. You can assign users and user groups to multiple access lists.

You can grant users and user groups access to all meters, quality sources, and locations in User Access (Settings > Settings Manager > Users) and Group Access (Settings > Settings Manager > Groups).

To create an Access List: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Security** group, select **Access Lists**. 3. On the **Access Lists** tab, click **New**. 4. Provide a name for the access list and select the type of devices that you want to add to the list. 5. From the list of available members, select the members that you want to add and use the right arrow button to add them to the list. You can also click **Query** to populate the list using a query. Access lists are not dynamic, even if you use a query to populate the members. If you need to update a list, you must manually update it. To view the assigned access lists for a meter or quality source: 1. In the Access List Editor, click **New**. 2. Click **Lookup**. 3. Select whether to view meters or quality sources. 4. Select a list member to view the access lists for that member. Lookup is not available for locations. To add users and groups to an Access List: 1. On the **Access Lists** tab, select the access list that you want to modify and click **Edit**. 2. On the **Group and User Access** tab, select the available groups or users that you want to add to the access list and use the right arrow button to add them to the list. You can also click **Query** to populate the list using a query.

docs.title: Group Access
docs.text:
A FLOWCAL group is a list of users that receive all the privileges that have been granted to the group. A user can be a member of multiple groups so that they can gain access to additional meters and/or privileges. User access is determined by the access specified in the user permissions or their group permissions. If access is granted at either the group or the user level, the selected users will have the same access. You must log out and log back in to refresh your privileges.

User security should only be enabled within the User Access screen, not the Group Access screen. FLOWCAL relies on database roles to manipulate users at the database level. Database roles can only be granted to users and not groups.

To access the Group Access screen:  1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select groups in the security group. Administrators must have the **Application Process - User Security** privileges to manage user or group IDs.  

Group Access Screen Details

The following items are available on the Group Access screen: - **ID** - The security group name. - **AD Group** - Indicates the Windows Active Directory group associated with the FLOWCAL security group. Each FLOWCAL group can only map to a single AD group, but one AD group can be mapped to any number of FLOWCAL groups. - **System** - Privileges are configured for each group ID for each system. A group ID can have access to multiple systems. For example: A group ID can have view-only privileges on one system and edit privileges on another. Members of a group will only be able to see the systems the group has access to. Access to a system is given by an administrator using the System Manager. The default system is "ENTERPRISE," but there could be multiple systems to choose from such as "GAS" or "LIQUID". By selecting a system from the System drop-down box on the User or Group Access screens, security can be defined uniquely within each system for a user or group ID. This feature requires the Multi-System Extension module. - **Group May Access All Meters** - This option allows group members to select any meter within the system. This option only grants the ability to select meters; what the group members can do with the meter data is still restricted by the group’s privileges. - **Group May Access All Quality Sources** - This option allows group members to select any quality source within the system. This option only grants the ability to select quality sources; what the group can do with the quality source data is still restricted by the group’s privileges. - **Group May Access All Locations** - This option will allow the group members to select any location within the system. This option only grants the ability to select locations; what the group can do with the location data is still restricted by the group’s privileges. - **Edit Approval Limits** - Determines the maximum amount of total edits for volume and energy that members of a group can approve for a given month, for each meter. - **Custom Limit** - User-defined limits for the maximum PPA or edit the group can approve. - **System Limit** - Limits defined within System Configuration screen or System Manager. - **No Limit** - No approval limit restrictions are set for this group. The group must also have the Edit/PPA Approval - Can Approve privilege. - **Application Process** - Security options affect all processes across the application for all systems. - **System Process** - Security settings defined per system. - **Ticket Access** - Ticket statuses are only populated if the FLOWCAL configuration option to automatically finalize is enabled (this option is only available with FC 8.11.38 and earlier). If this option is enabled, ticket access can be restricted. - **Check All** - Grant all privileges for all application processes or system processes. - **Clear All** - Remove all privileges for all application processes or system processes. - **Refresh** - Reload the group ID from the database. - **New** - Create a new group ID. - **Edit** - Edit an existing group ID. - **Delete** - Delete a security group ID. - **Save** - Save changes. - **Cancel** - Cancel changes. - **Exit** - Exit the screen. - **Members** - Launch the Edit Group screen to add/remove members for the security group selected. - **Notes** - Add notes for a given security group ID.

Application Process Details

The following items are available in the Application Process section of the Group Access screen: - **Close Groups** - Grant access to create, edit, and delete close groups. - Data Archive - Grant access to view and edit data archive-related settings. - **FLOWCAL Options** - Grant access to several groupings within the Settings Manager screen (e.g. Services, Application Geographic, and Liquids). - **Personality** - Allow toggle between FLOWCAL and TESTit using the **Ctl+T** functionality. (Applicable to TESTit Integrated v2 only.) - **System** - Grant access to create, edit, and delete systems from the System Manager. - **TESTit Admin** - Grant access to the administrative features under the TESTit Manager menu ( TESTit Options, Data Map Editor, and some administrative menus under TESTit Scheduler). - **Ticket Autofill** - Grant access to set up defaults for ticket fields. - **User Security** - Grant access to User/Group Access within FLOWCAL.

System Process Details

The following items are available in the System Process section of the Group Access screen: - **Data Transfer** - Import and export privileges control access to the Data Transfer module within FcDataBoss. - **Meter Edit - Can Delete** - This privilege is commonly withheld from users that are limited to day-to-day processing. - **Purge - Historical Purge** - Historical purge privilege controls access to the Historical Purge module in FcDataBoss.

Run the User Roles and Privileges report to view the privileges for each user ID based on user and group permissions.

docs.title: System Manager
docs.text:
This feature requires the Multi-System Extension module.

In some cases, companies may require separation of assets, settings and security. For example: A company may choose to keep regulated assets separate from unregulated assets, or require divisions to manage objects and security of those objects independently. FLOWCAL systems allow for separate assets to be managed in one database, rather than requiring users to create multiple FLOWCAL databases.

Default Enterprise System

By default, FLOWCAL ships with one system called "Enterprise", where settings and user-, group-, and object-level security can be defined for the entire application.

User-Defined Systems

With the Multi-System Extension module, there is no limit on the number of systems that can be created. Furthermore, because security is defined within each system, a single user could have full access to one system and its objects, and no access or view-only access to another. Some FLOWCAL application settings, such as those in the FLOWCAL Configuration screen, affect all systems (e.g., Enterprise, System 2); other settings, such as those in the System Configuration screen, are specific to a system. If you have access to a system, you will see a system object selector in many of the screens throughout FLOWCAL. This drop-down will include all of the systems you have access to.

Create Systems

Systems can only be created from the System Manager. The system creation process typically proceeds as follows: Administrators must have **Application Process - System** privileges, granted from the User or Group Access screen, to create, edit, and delete systems. To create a new system: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**, and select **System Manager** within the **Security** group. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter a system name. 4. Enter a system code if needed (this data is optional and is not displayed elsewhere in the application). 5. Grant system access to the appropriate users and/or groups. 6. Assign one or more managers to the system. Each system must have at least one manager. A manager can add or remove user or group system access from the System Manager screen. 7. Click **Save**. The administrator can then grant users and/or groups access to the system from the User or Group Access screen. Meters, locations, source analyses, lists, and other objects can then be assigned to the system. (Each object can only belong to one system.) In the Settings Manager, the System group contains system-specific settings, whereas the Application group contains settings that are application-wide and affect all systems.

Edit Approval Limits

Edit approval limitsThe maximum amount by which volume, energy, gross standard volume, or mass values can be changed through manual edits without requiring approval. Manual edits that exceed this limit will need to be approved before the edits are applied. can be set on a per-system basis. These limits are set in the System Manager screen under the Options tab, or in the System Configuration screen under the PPA and Approval Options tab. After edit limits have been set, if a user tries to save an edit to meter data that is greater than the approval limit set for that system, a message will display informing the user of the exceeded amount, and the edit will have a status of "Pending". The limit applies to the total edit amount for the month. Example An edit approval limit for volume is set at 1000 units. An edit is then made to the volume amount that varies 950 units from the original amount. The variance of 950 is below the 1000-unit limit, so no approval is required. The volume is then edited by an additional 60 units. The total variance of the edits (950 + 60) now exceeds the 1000-unit limit, so the second edit of 60 units will require approval. The edit will need to be approved by a user or group with edit approval limits greater than the system-level limit of 1000 units (defined in System Manager or System Configuration).

docs.title: User Access
docs.text:
FLOWCAL IDs are used to control access to forms and functionality and to maintain an audit trail for changes.

Run the User Privileges report to view the privileges for each user ID based on user and group permissions.

An administrator can grant individual processes and privileges to control the type of access users have (this requires Application Process - User Security privileges).

When a FLOWCAL ID is created, a corresponding Oracle user account is created. The Oracle account is tightly controlled using roles. FLOWCAL IDs are created and maintained through the User Access screen.

During user creation, the user type must be designated as "Standard" or "Instant". Designating a user as "Instant" will enable the Instant Login feature for the user. This designation cannot be changed after the user has been created.

Users who are part of security groups can be granted additional privileges at the user level to increase access that may not be required for the group. User privileges will override the group privilege settings. You must log out and log back in to refresh your privileges.

To access the User Access screen:  1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select users in the security group.

User Access Screen Details

The following items are available on the User Access screen: - **Type** - Select **Instant** to enable the Instant Login feature for the user; otherwise, select **Standard**. This designation cannot be changed after the user is created. - **ID** - The ID that is logged during edits and throughout the audit trail in FLOWCAL. This is the username entered when logging into FLOWCAL. - **Name** - Informational field only; this data is not used elsewhere in the application. Some companies use a numeric ID, so the name is used to further identify the ID. - **Contact** - Create a contact for a user in FLOWCAL and associate the contact information with the user by selecting the contact name from the drop-down list. An option to email logged in users in FLOWCAL uses the email address defined for the associated contact. The contact must exist in the system prior to selection. This is not required and can be updated at a future date. - **System** - Privileges are configured for each ID for each system. An ID can have access to multiple systems. For example: An ID can have view-only access on one system and edit privileges on another system. Users will only be able to see the systems they have access to. Access to a system is provided by an administrator using the System Manager. The default system is "ENTERPRISE," but there could be additional systems to choose from such as "GAS" or "LIQUID". By selecting a system from the System drop-down box on the User or Group Access screens, security can be defined uniquely within each system for a user or group ID. This feature requires the Multi-System Extension module. - **Groups** - Displays the security groups associated with the ID. - **User May Access All Meters** - This option will allow a user to select any meter within the system. This option only grants the ability to select meters; what a user can do with the meter data is still restricted by the user's privileges. - **User May Access All Quality Sources** - This option will allow a user to select any quality source within the system. This option only grants the ability to select quality sources; what a user can do with the quality source data is still restricted by the user's privileges. - **User May Access All Locations** - This option will allow a user to select any location within the system. This option only grants the ability to select locations; what a user can do with the location data is still restricted by the user's privileges. - **Edit Approval Limits** - Determines the maximum amount of total edits for volume and energy that a user or group can approve for each meter, in a given month. - **Custom Limit** - User-defined limits for the maximum PPA or edit the user can approve. - **System Limit** - Limits defined within System Configuration screen or System Manager. - **No Limit** - No approval limit restrictions are set for the user. The ID must also have the Edit/PPA Approval - Can Approve privilege. - **Password Expires\*** - When this option is checked, the Expiration Frequency option is enabled. If enabled, the user will be warned of impending expiration 10 days in advance. Once the password has expired, the user will be forced to change it before access to FLOWCAL will be allowed. - **Expiration Frequency\*** - Specify the number of months to elapse before the ID expires and the user must change their password. This option is available when Password Expires is checked. - **Password Expires On\*** - Automatically shows the ID expiration date based on the specified expiration frequency. - **Edit Password\*** - When creating a new user or if an existing user forgets a password, the administrator can change the password for the user. The user will log in with the new password but will be immediately prompted to change the password. If the password is not edited, the default password for a new user is "NEWUSER". \*These options are not available for FLOWCAL Instant Login users. - **User Creation Date** - Datetime the ID was created. - **Last Logged on Date** - Datetime the ID last logged in to the current FLOWCAL database. - **Application Process** - Security options affect all processes across the application for all systems. - **System Process** - Security settings defined per system. - **Ticket Access** - If this option is enabled, ticket access can be restricted by ticket status. The "Finalized" ticket status is only populated if the "Automatically Finalize" FLOWCAL configuration option is enabled. The "Automatically Finalize" option is only available with FLOWCAL 8.11.38 and earlier versions. - **Check All** - Grant all privileges for all application processes or system processes. - **Clear All** - Remove all privileges for all application processes or system processes. - **Refresh** - Reload the ID from the database. - **New** - Create a new ID. - **Edit** - Edit an existing ID. - **Enable / Disable** - Enable or disable an ID. IDs cannot be deleted in FLOWCAL to maintain the existing audit trail. However, the ID can be disabled to prohibit the user from logging in. To view disabled IDs, while in view mode, right-click the ID drop-down and select **Show Disabled Users**. A user in Oracle may be removed, if desired, after the corresponding ID has been disabled in FLOWCAL. - **Save** - Save changes. - **Cancel** - Cancel changes. - **Exit** - Exit the screen. - **Settings** - Each ID has a set of user preferences, such as a preferred location and default system. Click this button to access the [User Preferences](../User%20Settings/User%20Preferences.md) screen. - **Notes** - Add notes to a given ID.

Application Process Details

The following items are available in the Application Process section of the User Access screen: - **Close Groups** - Grant access to create, edit, and delete close groups. - **Data Archive** - Grant access to view and edit data archive-related settings. - **FLOWCAL Options** - Grant access to several groupings within the Settings Manager screen (Services, Application Geographic, and Liquids). - **Personality** - Allow toggle between FLOWCAL and TESTit using the **Ctl+T** functionality. (Applicable to TESTit Integrated v2 only.) - **System** - Grant access to create, edit, and delete systems from the System Manager. - **TESTit Admin** - Grant access to the administrative features under the TESTit Manager menu (TESTit Options, Data Map Editor, and some administrative menus under TESTit Scheduler). - **Ticket Autofill** - Grant access to set up default values for ticket fields. - **User Security** - Grant access to User/Group Access within FLOWCAL.

System Process Details

The following items are available in the System Process section of the User Access screen: - **Data Transfer** - Import and export privileges control access to the Data Transfer module within FcDataBoss. - **Meter Edit - Can Delete** - This privilege is commonly withheld from users that are limited to day-to-day processing. - **Purge - Historical Purge** - Historical purge privilege controls access to the Historical Purge module in FcDataBoss.

docs.title: All Services
docs.text:
Audit Service (FcSrvAudit.exe)

Enables users to automatically monitor check to sales meters and flag for unacceptable user-defined differences - on a spot basis or over a user-defined period. Audits are configured in Meter Editor and utilize a host of user-defined parameters for identifying suspect volume and energy discrepancies. Audits also generate all the necessary third-party correspondence while tracking each audit’s current and historical status. Provides the foundation for an effective measurement audit group/department. **Requirements:** Audit Package Module See: [Audits](../../Tools/Audits.md)

Auto Estimate Service (FcSrvAutoEstimate.exe)

Based on the settings with Meter Editor, the service will automatically recognize that data is missing and calculate estimated data for the meter based on historical data from that meter. The estimated data can be automatically replaced with actual data when it becomes available. Auto Estimates will also create data for balance purposes where no actual meter exists. By default, the Auto Estimate services will start at: - 12:00 am - 4:00 am - 10:00 am - 12:00 pm - 6:00 pm **Requirements:** Service to Auto Estimate Missing Data Module See: [Meter Editor](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Meter%20Editor.md)

Auto Rescan Service (FcSrvAutoRescan.exe)

Scans for missing records and queues SCADA to poll the meter for the missing data See: [Meter Editor](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Meter%20Editor.md)

Batch Schedule Matching Service (FcSrvBatchScheduleMatching.exe)

Matches scheduled batches with imported batches Associates meter batches to the scheduled batch movements defined in the Batch Movement Reconciliation Viewer. Processes Queue entries on the Batch Matching tab of the Service Queues. **Requirements:** Liquids Add-in See: [Scheduled Batch Movement](../../Imports/Scheduled%20Batch%20Movement/Scheduled%20Batch%20Movement.md)

Calculated Meter Service (FcSrvCalcMtrRollup.exe)

Calculates hourly, daily, and monthly data for a calculated meter based on member data in final form tables. The resulting data is used in the final form tables and can be seen in the Rollup Viewer. The same final form data is also used in reports and exports. See: [Calculated Meter Rollup Process](../../Calculated%20Meter%20Editor/Formulas/Calculated%20Meter%20Rollup%20Process.md)

Data Archive Service (FlowCal.Archival.Service.exe)

Transfers meter periodic data (FC_METER_PERIODIC_VALUES), final form meter hourly (FC_FFMTR_HOURLY), and final form location hourly (FC_FFLCN_HOURLY) data from production database to an archive database. The service also processes data restore, re-archive, and manual purge operations. **Requirements:** Data Archive Add-on See: [Data Archive Solution](../Application/Data%20Archive/Data%20Archive%20Solution.md)

File Import Service (FcSrvFileImport.exe)

Automatically imports a variety of different file formats such as CFX, meter text files, source analysis text files, etc. Requires the service log on use a network account with elevated privileges, configured in Microsoft’s Services console (refer to the Service Security section).

HCDP Service (FcSrvHCDPQueueProcessor.exe)

Calculates the hydrocarbon dew point (HCDP) and cricondentherm (CCT) of a GQ source analysis. The calculation uses the unmodified Peng-Robinson equation of state. Input sample pressure and sample temperature (GQ Source Analysis detail \> Sample tab) must be in units of psi and degrees Fahrenheit, respectively, and results are in degrees Fahrenheit. Option for HCDP must be enabled within Gas Quality Source Editor. **Requirements:** Source Analysis Module

TESTit 3 Integrated FLOWCAL Service (FlowCal.Enterprise.Integration.Service.exe)

FLOWCAL service responsible for publishing and handling TESTit Integrated related information; this includes pushing meter and list updates as well as receiving PDF, test point data and meter characteristic information from TESTit v3 to FLOWCAL. **Requirements:** TESTit v3 Integrated Only

TESTit 3 Integrated List Service (FlowCal.Enterprise.Integration.List.Polling.Service.exe)

FLOWCAL service responsible for polling dynamic list updates for TESTit v3 Integrated and publishing that information, for TESTit enabled lists. **Requirements:** TESTit v3 Integrated Only

TESTit 3 Integrated TESTit Service (FlowCal.FieldApplications.Integration.Service.exe)

TESTit service (starting with TI 3.3) responsible for publishing and handling TESTit Integrated related information. This includes pushing test point data and meter characteristic updates as well as receiving meter and list information from FLOWCAL to TESTit. **Requirements:** TESTit v3 Integrated Only

Line Fill Service (Flowcal.LineFill.Service.exe)

Calculates liquid component line fill on a pipe segment. Located in the NGLLineFill subdirectory of the FLOWAL install folder and is a Microsoft .NET service. It must be installed and uninstalled using the \_installService.cmd and \_uninstallService.cmd in the NGLLineFill subdirectory. It cannot be installed or uninstalled like the other FLOWCAL (non-Microsoft .NET) services.

List Members API service (FcSrvListMembersAPI.exe)

TESTit 3 Integrated service responsible for obtaining members from a list when purging or exporting a list; also used to manage list synchronization between FLOWCAL and TESTit. **Requirements:** TESTit V3 Integrated Only

Live Oil Service (FlowCal.LiveOil.Service.exe)

Processes and writes periodic data to dead oil and flash gas meters when they have an active relationship with a live oil meter in FLOWCAL. **Requirements:** Liquids System and Live Oil Management add-on See: [Live Oil Management](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Tools%20Menu.md) and [Live Oil Service](Live%20Oil%20Service.md)

Location Close Service (FcSrvLcnCloseData.exe)

Closes a contract month for a location and tickets associated with the location. **Requirements:** Monthly Close Functions and Service Module

Location Rollup Service (FcSrvLcnRollup.exe)

Used to calculate hourly, daily, and monthly data for locations from meter data. The resulting data is used in the final form tables and can be seen in the Rollup Viewer. The same final form data is also used in reports and exports. This service also calls for location validations to be performed.

Location Rollup Service (Station Locations) (FcSrvLcnRollupStation.exe)

Ensures that "Station" locations are prioritized to roll up before any other type of location; the standard location rollup service (FcSrvLcnRollup.exe) can be copied and renamed multiple times depending on need; each instance of the service must have a unique name by appending an integer at the end of the name.

Meter Close Service (FcSrvCloseData.exe)

Closes a contract month for a meter and tickets that have effective dates in the contract month, based on a close schedule. For any location on the list or the close group on a close schedule, meter and ticket members of the location are closed. Closing a contract month prevents editing of the meter or ticket data. Subsequent changes to a meter's or ticket's data for the closed contract month will generate a prior period adjustment (PPA). A child dead oil or flash gas meter will not close if a Live Oil service queue entry exists for the meter. **Requirements:** Monthly Close Functions

Meter Rollup Service (FcSrvMtrRollup.exe)

Used to calculate hourly, daily, and monthly data for meters from meter periodic values. The resulting data is used in the final form tables and can be seen in the Rollup Viewer. The same final form data is also used in reports and exports. For Meter Characteristic and Analysis Data meeting a certain criteria, the Meter Rollup service will condense datetime effective records to help maintain database stability and performance. Users can also initiate this process manually for meters using the [FLOWCAL Data Condenser utility](../../Admin%20Options/FcDataCondenser.md).

Quorum Enterprise Integration FLOWCAL Service (FLOWCAL.Integration.Events.Service)

Quorum Enterprise Integration (QEI) allows FLOWCAL data to be shared seamlessly with other applications within the Quorum Software ecosystem. This event-driven data sharing sends data to a central Integration Platform, where it can then be sent on to other Quorum applications. Currently, applications that support integration with FLOWCAL are: - QPTM - TIPS FLOWCAL supports sending header information, quantities and sample data for meters and calculated meters.

Report Scheduling Service (FcSrvReports.exe)

Runs reports and exports using report schedules defined by the user. Output can be printed, emailed, or saved to a network location. Requires the service log on use a network account with elevated privileges, configured in Microsoft’s Services console. Also requires a company email account that will be used to email reports/exports (refer to the Service Security section). **Requirements:** Scheduled Reporting Module See: [Configure Report/Export Scheduling](../../Admin%20Options/Configure%20Report-Export%20Scheduling.md)

Source Apply Service (FcSrvGqTrans.exe)

Applies GQ and LQ source analysis data to meter data and standalone ticket data (data edits and imports will queue a source analysis apply). **Requirements:** Source Analysis Module

Source Rollup Service (FcSrvGqAnlRollup.exe)

All source quality samples are stored at the data resolution they are generated (4-minute, hourly, daily, monthly, quarterly, etc.). The quality samples are averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. This could be useful for users handling daily and weekly chromatographs that need to report averages for a period. When the source quality type is "Chromatograph" or "RTU Average", the quality samples are weight-averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. Sample pressure and pample temperature value are not rolled up for chromatographs. If the type is "Gas Analysis", the quality is copied directly to the rollup tables. Requires the Enable Rollups option checked within the Gas Quality Source Editor. Feature is not currently supported for Liquid Sources. **Requirements:** Source Analysis Module

TESTit Analysis Sync Service (FcSrvTESTitAnalysisSync.exe)

Sends the current gas meter analysis in FLOWCAL to the corresponding gas analysis database table in TESTit for use in test reports. Meters need to be enabled for TESTit and rolled up for their analysis data to be copied to TESTit. Meter analysis data that is a part of auto estimated records is not copied by this service. The service is installed in the same manner that any other FLOWCAL service is installed. Once installed, it is started from the Windows Service Monitor and runs at 7:00 AM every day by default. **Requirements:** TESTit Integrated (2.14.2 and above or 3.3 and above)

TESTit Calibration Apply Service (FcSrvTESTitCalAdjApply.exe)

Processes TESTit test reports and applies calibration adjustments if the TESTit imports are configured for Auto Calibration Adjustments. **Requirements:** TESTit Integrated (v2 and v3)

TESTit Export Scheduler Service (FcSrvTESTitExportScheduler.exe)

Automatically processes scheduled TESTit export jobs via TSX files. **Requirements:** TESTit v2 Integrated Only

TESTit Import Service (FcSrvTESTitSchedulerImport.exe)

Automatically imports TESTit TSX files from a designated file location. **Requirements:** TESTit v2 Integrated Only

Transaction Queue Service (FcSrvTrans.exe)

Processes import records from the transaction queue tables. **Requirements:** Online Transaction Processing Module See: [Transaction Queue](Transaction%20Queue.md)

Transaction Queue Service (Positive Displacement) (FcSrvTransPD.exe)

The Transaction Queue service (Positive Displacement) (FcSrvTransPD.exe) is a copy of the standard Transaction Queue service (FcSrvTrans.exe). Its purpose is to only import transactions created by the Import \> Manual Entry \> Positive Displacement data entry screens. The objective is to import PD entry transactions as soon as possible regardless of how long the transaction queue is or whether the PD transactions were created after all waiting transactions. Transactions created by the PD UIs are written to the FC_TRANSACTION_QUEUE table with a write_timestamp equal to beginning of time (63093600, 1/1/1972 00:00:00:00) and the service will only import transactions whose write_timestamp is equal to beginning of time. PD entry transaction will also be imported by the standard Transaction Queue service (FcSrvTrans.exe). Since the PD entry transactions are created with the beginning of time write_timestamp, the service will process them before processing standard transactions.

docs.title: Live Oil Members Tab
docs.text:
This feature requires the Liquids system and the Live Oil Management add-on.

If a liquid meter is designated as a Live Oil meter and has a child meter (Dead Oil or Flash Gas) associated with it, the Live Oil service will perform calculations and/or transformations on the Live Oil data. This processed data will then be applied to the child meters as a data edit.

The Live Oil Members tab displays information for Live Oil member meter entries that have not been processed. Entries that have not been attempted will display a status of "Ready". Entries that did not process successfully will display a status of "Failed".

A child dead oil or flash gas meter cannot be opened or closed if a Live Oil service queue entry exists for the meter.

Screen Details

##### Columns - **Meter Number** - Displays the meter number for the dead oil or flash gas child meter. - **Meter Type** - The meter type of the child meter (Dead Oil or Flash Gas). - **Status** - **Ready** - Data for the live oil meter has been queued for processing, but the Live Oil service has not processed it yet. - **Failed** - The Live Oil service tried to process data for this meter, but an error occurred. More information about the reason for the failure can be found in the log files. - **First Date** - The first date for which data will be applied to the child meter. - **Last Date** - The last date for which data will be applied to the child meter. - **Queue Date** - The date on which the Live Oil data was queued to be processed. - **Parent Meter** - Displays the meter number for the Live Oil parent meter. - **Process Start** - For failed entries, the datetime that the service began processing the queue entry. - **Process Finish** - For failed entries, the datetime that the service finished processing the queue entry. - **Service Number** - For failed entries, the installed instance of the service that processed the queue entry. ##### Buttons - **Queue** - Change the status of a record to "In Queue". The Live Oil service will attempt to process the data again. - **Refresh** - Refresh the display to check the status of the Live Oil meter processing (display does not refresh automatically). - **Exit** - Close the screen.

docs.title: Queue Data Tab
docs.text:
The following object processing options are available on the Queue Data tab:

  • Object Selector - Use the Object Selector at the top to select the object to queue. Alternately, the radio buttons on the left can be used to select the type of object.

  • Action Selector - This unlabeled group box in the lower left provides a choice of actions that can be applied to the selected object.

  • Rollup - Select this option to create a rollup queue entry. For sources, a notification message will display if the selected source has not been enabled for rollups. Rollup queues are processed by Meter Rollup, Location Rollup, Source Rollup, and Calculated Meter services. This option is always enabled and selected by default.

  • Roll Data For - These options are only available for lists or locations; they are disabled for meters, sources, and source lists.

    • For list objects, the following selections are available:
    • Meters and locations in this list only. This option will only queue the immediate members of the list. It will not queue entries for meters or locations nested within locations in the list.
    • All meters in this list and member locations. This option will queue immediate meters in the list and iteratively examine nested locations for meter-type members. Ultimately, only the lowest level meters will be queued.
    • Lowest-level locations only. This option will iteratively examine nested locations for location-type members. Ultimately, only the lowest level locations will be queued.
    • For location objects, the following selections are available:
    • This location only. This option will only queue the selected location.
    • Top-level member meters and locations in this location only. This option will only queue the immediate members of the location. It will not queue entries for meters or locations nested within the selected.
    • All meters in this location and member locations. This option will queue the immediate meter members of the selected location and iteratively examine nested locations for meter-type members. Ultimately, only the lowest level meters will be queued.
    • Lowest-level locations only. This option will iteratively examine nested locations for location-type members. Ultimately, only the lowest level locations will be queued.

    View Flowcharts

    <div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Flowcharts">


    </div>

    • Check for Data Within the Range - Select this option to only queue periods in which data exists. When this option is not selected, the entire period will be queued for rollup, even when data does not exist.

    • HCDP Calc - Select this option for a source or source list to create an HCDP queue entry. A notification message will display if the selected source has not been enabled for hydrocarbon dew point or cricondentherm calculations. The HCDP queue is processed by the HCDP service (FcSrvHCDPQueueProcessor.exe).

    This feature requires the Source Analysis module.

    • Queue Location - Queues a location to close a selected month/year. The Location Close queue is processed by the Location Close service (FcSrvLcnCloseData.exe).

    • Batch Matching - As batches are imported for meters with the Reconcile Batches option enabled (Meter Editor > Liquids tab), FLOWCAL will try to match each batch to a scheduled batch movement. The Batch Matching queue is processed by the Batch Scheduling Matching service (FcSrvBatchScheduleMatching.exe).

    This feature requires the Liquids add-on.

    • Source Apply – This option queues sources to be applied to meters. The Source apply queue is processed by the Source Apply service (FcSrvGQTrans.exe)

    This feature requires the Source Analysis module.

docs.title: Service Configuration
docs.text:
Use the Service Configuration screen to set up FLOWCAL services that you installed on the application server(s). Available options vary based on the modules you purchased.

Before you begin service configuration, you must create a FLOWCAL service account within the application. Most companies create a user name called "FCSRV" to easily identify it. The service account should be an administrator account with permissions.

To access the Service Configuration screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **Services** group, select **Service Configuration**.

Service Login

All services use the same user name, password, and database information. To specify these credentials, you must be on the server where you installed the services. FLOWCAL writes the information to the registry, so it must be encrypted on the server where the services will run. If you update the service login information, you must restart the services.

Text File Imports

The following options are available for importing text files for meters and sources: - **Auto Create** - Select this option to create a new source analysis or meter number for any unidentified source analysis or meter number found in the text file and import the data. If you do not select this option, FLOWCAL discards the unidentified data. - **Use Field As Import ID** - Select this option to automatically select the **Source Analysis number field is Import ID** or **Meter number field is Import ID** option during manual imports of source analysis or meter text files. If FLOWCAL finds a match, it imports the data into the corresponding source analysis or meter. If FLOWCAL does not find a match, it does not import the data. - **Neither** - Select this option if you do not want to store imported data for meters and source analyses if the meter or source does not exist in the database, and you do not want to store the data under any alternate ID.

Transaction Queue Options

The following options are available for transaction queue processing: - **Auto Create Meters** - Select this option to automatically create meters during transaction queue processing if they do not already exist and the transaction queue receives data for them. If you do not select this option, FLOWCAL discards the data. - **Auto Create Sources** - Select this option to automatically create sources during transaction queue processing if they do not already exist and the transaction queue receives data for them. If you do not select this option, FLOWCAL discards the data. - **Check Meter Import ID First** - Select this option if you want FLOWCAL to attempt to correlate the meter number field from the Transaction Queue table to the **Meter Import ID** field first. If FLOWCAL finds a match, it imports the data into the corresponding meter. If FLOWCAL does not find a match, it uses the meter number field to correlate the data. - **Check Source Import ID First** - Select this option if you want FLOWCAL to attempt to correlate the source number field from the Transaction Queue table to the **Source Import ID** field first. If FLOWCAL finds a match, it imports the data into the corresponding source. If FLOWCAL does not find a match, it uses the source number field to correlate the data. - **Allow Duplicate Source Import IDs** - Select this option to allow the same source quality to be imported to multiple sources per the defined Import ID.

Service Installations

The following fields specify information for installing services: - **Service Count** - The number of instances of a service to run. FLOWCAL uses this information to divide the work across multiple services. Specify the maximum number you plan to run for any given service. For example, if you have two instances of the Meter Rollup service, two instances of the Location Rollup service, and only one instance of the other services, specify "2." - **Services Host Computer** - The default server name that the Service Monitor will use.

Services

The following options are available for configuring FLOWCAL services: - **Interval** - The length of time for which the service will sleep before running again. If you leave this value as 0, the service will sleep for one minute. This allows multiple services to share the CPU. The interval value for the Live Oil service will default to 10 minutes when set to 0. - **Port** - The port that the Service Monitor uses to communicate with the service. This should be unique for every service. When running multiple copies of a service, such as FcSrvMtrRollup and FcSrvMtrRollup2, the second service will use a port one increment larger than the one shown on the editor. - **Include `n` prior months** - The number of prior months that FLOWCAL should examine for audits (Audit service only). - **Include `n` prior days** - The number of prior days that FLOWCAL should examine when calculating liquid component line fill (LineFill service only).

Roll Options

Use these options to limit how far back in time FLOWCAL queues rollups for meters, calculated meters, and locations. Limiting the amount of time eliminates unnecessary data from the rollup process.

File Imports Tab

Use the **File Imports** tab to configure the following settings for the File Import service: - **Folder to Check** - The directory from which the service imports files. - **After every run pause for `n` sec.** - The time interval at which FLOWCAL polls the directory for new information to process. If you do not specify a value, FLOWCAL polls the directory every 60 seconds. - **Log Processed Files** - Select this option if you want the File Import service to generate a log file entry for every file that it processes. This is useful when researching issues with file imports. If you are not researching an issue, enabling this option is not recommended as the log file grows rapidly. - **Port Number** - The port that the Service Monitor uses to communicate with the service. This will be unique for every service. When running multiple copies of a service, the second service will use a port one increment larger than the one shown in the editor. - **Number of Retries** - The number of additional attempts that will be tried if the file fails to import on the first attempt. Windows has a hard-coded limit of 260 characters for file paths; file paths longer than this will not work. Importing files from a local install allows for using drive letters for network file paths; however, Citrix resolves the actual network location, which can cause the number of characters in a file path to exceed this limit.

docs.title: Service Monitor
docs.text:
Use the Service Monitor to view the status and activity for services running in FLOWCAL. Current activity for the selected service displays in the scrollable window.

To access the Service Monitor: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **Service Monitor** in the **Services** group.

Service Monitor Screen Details

#### Service Status **Green** - The service is currently awake, running, and processing requests on the host machine. Messages are displayed on the screen. **Yellow** - The service is running but is currently idle or waiting for the next cycle. **Red** - The service is not running or a connection to the service could not be established (the service may not have been started). #### Buttons - **Edit Host** - If the service you are monitoring is not running on your local machine, change the host being monitored to the IP address of the machine where the service is running. - **Connect All Services** - Click to restart the Service Monitor. This is often used in conjunction with the Edit Host function when pointing to a new host machine. - **Connect to Port \# / Disconnect** - If there are multiple copies of the selected service running on the specified host, click the **Disconnect** button to stop monitoring the copy running on the designated port. Enter the appropriate port corresponding to the copy you want to monitor and then click the **Connect to Port \#** button to restart the Service Monitor. To monitor a duplicate service, add the service number to the base port number. (Example: FcSrvMtrRollups is port 5001, so FcSrvMtrRollups2 would be 5002.)

docs.title: Service Queues
docs.text:
Use the Service Queues screen to monitor services within FLOWCAL. The Service Queues screen provides details about meters, locations, or quality sources that have not rolled yet, source analyses that have not applied yet, locations that have not closed yet, and pending HCDP calculations.

You can also use the Service Queues screen to force a re-roll of data for meters, locations, or quality sources, either individually, in a location or list. The data to be rolled up can be for all of time or just for a certain date range.

To access the Service Queues screen: - Go to the Settings Manager, and select the **Service Queues** link within the **Services** group; or - Click **Unrolled Data** in the Rollups Viewer. When you access the Service Queues screen from the Rollups Viewer, you will not be able to queue data for rolling; you will only be able to view data that has not been rolled yet. If a record in queue becomes postponed, select it and click the **Queue** button. If the record continues to be postponed, you could be running out of table space or there may be a data issue. In this case, contact Customer Support.

Service Queue Screen Details

The following tabs are available on the Service Queues screen: - **Queue Data** - Re-roll a list, location, meter, source, or source list for all of time or for a datetime range. Queue a location to be closed for a specific month. Queue meters for the batch matching service for all of time or for a datetime range. - **Unrolled Meters** - View unrolled meters in the queue. You can also see any items that have been postponed, held, or ignored. The queue should remain empty until the next import process is run, and will populate during data processing such as imports and edits. - **Unrolled Locations** - View unrolled locations in the queue. - **Unrolled Source Analysis** - View unrolled source analysis data in the queue. If you have configured source analysis data to be rolled in the Gas Quality Source Editor or the Liquid Quality Source Editor, it will display in this window when it is queued to roll up, and then follow the same process as unrolled meters. This feature requires the **Source Analysis** module. - **Unprocessed HCDP** - View source analysis data that does not have a calculated hydrocarbon dewpoint (HCDP). Any sources that have been set up to automatically calculate HCDP or cricondentherm will display in this window when records require recalculation. The HCDP service checks the queue for unprocessed records once per hour. This setting is not configurable. - **Unprocessed Analysis Apply** - View source analysis data that has not been applied to assigned meters or locations. When a new source or online chromatograph record is imported or an existing one is edited, it will display here. This feature requires the **Source Analysis** module. - **Location Close** - After meters and tickets are closed, any locations that the meter or ticket is a member of will display in this queue. Additionally, once a location is closed by the Location Close service, any parent locations will display here. This feature requires the **Monthly Close and Systems Balance** module. - **Batch Matching** - As batches are imported for meters with the [Reconcile Batches](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Liquids%20Tab.md) option enabled, FLOWCAL will try to match each batch to a scheduled batch movement. (See: [Scheduled Batch Movement](../../Imports/Scheduled%20Batch%20Movement/Scheduled%20Batch%20Movement.md)) This feature requires the **Liquids** add-on. - **Live Oil** - If a Live Oil meter has any Dead Oil or Flash Gas meters associated with it, the service will perform calculations or transformations on the Live Oil data and apply it to the child meters. (See: [Live Oil Info](Live%20Oil%20Tab.md)) This feature requires the **Liquids** add-on and the **Live Oil Management** module. - **Data Archive** - View meter and location records with pending archive/restore/purge operations.

docs.title: Transaction Queue
docs.text:
This feature requires the Online Transaction Processing module.

The Transaction Queue service is an alternative to file imports and can be used to import data into FLOWCAL on a near real-time basis.

Example An external SCADA system could create data entries within the Transaction Queue tables where the Transaction Queue service would read unprocessed entries. The service would then proceed through the list, performing validations and calculations, and storing the resulting information in FLOWCAL. Processed entries are marked as successfully or unsuccessfully processed; they are not deleted.

You can use the Transaction Queue screen to see meters, tickets, or source analyses that have not been processed or have failed. You can also force a re-queue of transaction data for meters, locations, source analyses, either individually or in a location or list. You can also force the re-queue of tickets in a location by location. The data can be re-queued for all of time or within a specified date range.

Additional Transaction Queue options can be configured from the Service Configuration screen.

To access the Transaction Queue screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manger** 2. Select **Transaction Queue** within the **Services** group. The **Queue** button is only enabled if you select the **Failed Data** tab.

Transaction Queue Screen Details

#### Tabs The following tabs are available in the Transaction Queue screen: - **Data Requeue** - Re-queue meters, tickets (by location), or sources using a datetime range or for all data (all of time). - **Unprocessed Data** - View records waiting to be processed by the Transaction Queue service. - **Failed Data** - View records that have been processed by the Transaction Queue service and failed. - **Processed Data** - View records that have been processed successfully by the Transaction Queue service. #### Columns The following columns are available in the Transaction Queue screen: - **Source ID** - Displays the meter number, location number for tickets, or source number. - **Transaction Type** - Displays the type of record to be processed. | Type | Code | |---------------------------------------------|:----:| | Meter Event | 1 | | Meter Alarm | 2 | | Meter Periodic | 3 | | Meter Configuration | 4 | | Quality Source Periodic | 5 | | Standalone Sample Analysis (Liquid Only) | 8 | | Ultrasonic Periodic (Gas Only) | 10 | | Meter Batch (Liquid Only) | 11 | | Meter Alternate Periodic (Liquid Only) | 12 | | Ticket - Meter (Liquid Only) | 14 | | Ticket - Tank Gauge/Inventory (Liquid Only) | 15 | | Ticket - Tank Run (Liquid Only) | 16 | | Ticket - Scale (Liquid Only) | 17 | | Ticket - Rail Car (Liquid Only) | 18 | - **From** - The start time for which the record is effective. - **To** - The end time for which the record is effective. - **Unavailable Code** - Status of the entry. Entry is created with a code of 0 upon insert, indicating that the record has not been processed. The status code will change when the entry has been processed. | Status | Code | |-----------------------------------|:----:| | Unprocessed | 0 | | Processed successfully | 1-9 | | Unable to save meter data | 10 | | Meter calculation method mismatch | 94 | | Meter out of service | 95 | | Time frame is closed | 96 | | Unable to save source data | 97 | | Meter or source does not exist | 98 | | Invalid timestamp | 99 | - **Min Read Date** - The minimum read date is when the data was processed by the Transaction Queue service. - **Max Read Date** - The maximum read date is when the data was processed by the Transaction Queue service. - **Min Write Date** - Minimum insertion dates that reflect when the data was written to the Transaction Queue tables. - **Max Write Date** - Maximum insertion dates that reflect when the data was written to the Transaction Queue tables.

docs.title: Unrolled Locations Tab
docs.text:
As data is imported or edited within FLOWCAL, the data is queued to roll. Meter rollups will queue the appropriate location rollups, if any, after rolling meter data. These will display on the Unrolled Locations tab.

The rollup service calculates hourly, daily, and monthly data for meters and locations from the periodic values. The resulting data is used for reporting purposes and can be viewed within one of the rollup viewers or by running a report or export.

The Unrolled Locations tab displays data for locations that have not rolled or were not rolled successfully. Data that did not roll successfully will display with a status of "Postponed".

To remove warnings about data failing to roll when running reports, select the desired locations and click the Ignore button. The data will refresh and the selected locations will have a status of "Ignored" and will not be re-rolled. If the problem that caused rollup failure has been corrected, select the desired locations and click the Queue button. The data will refresh and the selected location will have a status of "In Queue". You may then try the rollup again.

Screen Details

#### Columns - **Location Number** - Displays the location number. - **Location Name** - Displays the location name. - **Start Date** - The first date for which data will be rolled for the location. - **End Date** - The last date for which data will be rolled for the location. - **Status** - **Ignored** - Data for the location was queued for rolling, but failed. Someone selected the data and clicked the **Ignore** button. It will not be re-rolled until it has a status of "In Queue". - **In Queue** - Data for the location has been placed in the queue, but the rollups service has not rolled it yet. Clicking **Queue** or the **Ignore** button on "In Queue" data will have no effect. - **Postponed** - The rollups service tried to roll data for this location, but an error occurred. More information about the reason for the failure can be found in the log files. - **GMS Date** - The date on which the data was queued to be rolled. #### Buttons - **On Demand** - Set a location to roll on demand within the Location Editor. This queues the data for rollup, but the rollup will not process until it is initiated from the Unrolled Locations tab of the Service Queues. When a location is set to roll on demand, clicking the **On Demand** button makes these records visible from the Unrolled Locations tab and updates the status of these entries to "In Queue". - **Hold** - Put a record in the queue on hold. The records will not be processed until you change the status back to "In Queue". - **Ignore** - Ignore locations that were postponed. - **Queue** - Change the status of a record to "In Queue". Rollups will try to re-roll the data. - **Refresh** - Refresh the display to check the status of rollups (display does not refresh automatically). - **Exit** - Close the screen.

docs.title: Unrolled Meters Tab
docs.text:
As data is imported or edited within FLOWCAL, the data is queued to roll. The rollup service calculates hourly, daily, and monthly data for meters and locations from the periodic values. The resulting data is used for reporting and can be viewed within one of the rollup viewers or by running a report or export.

The Unrolled Meters tab displays data for meters that have not rolled or were not rolled successfully. Data that did not roll successfully will display with a status of "Postponed".

To remove warnings about data failing to roll when running reports, select the desired meters and click the Ignore button. The data will refresh and the meters will have a status of "Ignored" and will not be re-rolled. If the problem that caused rollup failure has been corrected, select the desired meters and click the Queue button. The data will refresh and the selected meters will have a status of "In Queue". You can then try the rollup again.

Screen Details

#### Columns - **Meter Number** - Displays the meter number. - **Meter Name** - Displays the meter name. - **Start Date** - The first date for which data will be rolled for the meter. - **End Date** - The last date for which data will be rolled for the meter. - **Status** - **Ignored** - Data for the meter was queued for rolling but failed. The data was then set to be ignored.It will not be re-rolled until it has a status of "In Queue". - **In Queue** - Data for the meter has been placed in the queue, but the rollups service has not rolled it yet. Clicking **Queue** or clicking the **Ignore** button on "In Queue" data will have no effect. - **Postponed** - The rollups service tried to roll data for this meter, but an error occurred. More information about the reason for the failure can be found in the log files. - **GMS Date** - The date on which the data was queued to be rolled. #### Buttons - **Hold** - Put records in the queue on hold. The records will not be processed until the status is changed back to "In Queue". - **Ignore** - Ignore meters that were postponed. - **Queue** - Change the status of a record to "In Queue". Rollups will try to re-roll the data. - **Refresh** - Refresh the display to check the status of rollups (display does not refresh automatically). - **Exit** - Close the screen.

docs.title: Rollup Configuration
docs.text:
Use the System Rollup Configuration screen to specify system-level default settings that are related to rollup calculations and services.

To access the System Rollup Configuration screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **System** group, select **Rollup Configuration**.

The following options are available:

  • For Location Reports Print - Select the information to include in the heading for location-based reports.

  • Pressure Printing Option - Select the pressure value to include in reports.

  • Volume, Energy - For gas only, specify the default number of decimals on the rollup viewers and Standard Reports screen.

  • Gas Avg. - Select the averaging technique to use for the displayed values. The default technique is Flow Weighted, Linear, but you can choose to use Time Weighted, Linear.

  • Gas Rounding - Select the carry/borrow method to use when rolling up periodic values to hourly, daily, and monthly totals.

If you select Daily, FLOWCAL rounds up or down the daily total and then totals integer days for the month.

If you select Monthly, FLOWCAL applies the carry/borrow functionality throughout the month.

  • Liq. Avg. - Select the averaging technique to use for liquids.

  • Balance Arithmetic - Select the numerator and denominator for balance calculations.

  • Activity Codes - Select the activities that you want to include in reports that are related to periodic meter data. Available activity codes are:

  • 01 – Events
  • 02 – Alarms
  • 03 – Characteristic Change
  • 04 – Analysis Change
  • 05 – Edited Data
  • 06 – Estimated Data
  • 07 – Inactive Meter
  • 08 – New Meter
  • 09 – Meter Re-Connect
  • 10 – Meter Calibration
  • 11 – Trouble Ticket
  • 12 – Calculated Meter

  • 13 – Check Meter Exists

  • Reports - Select the company logo to use in reports.

Dimensions for the large logo are 0.75"h x 3"w (72 pixels x 288 pixels). Dimensions for the small logo are 0.38"h x 1.5"w (36 pixels x 144 pixels). Preferred image file formats are JPG, PNG, and BMP.

docs.title: System Factors
docs.text:
Use the System Factors screen to specify default settings for systems that you define in FLOWCAL. These settings are datetime effective. If multiple records exist in the database, use the buttons below the Effective Date and Eff. End Date fields to scroll through the records.

To access the System Factors screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the **System** group, select **System Factors**.

Calculation and Reporting Options

The following options specify how FLOWCAL calculates certain values for analysis and reporting: - **Heating Value Condition** - The heating value condition under which FLOWCAL analyzes gas stream samples. - **Base Pressure** - The base pressure that FLOWCAL uses to calculate standard values. - **Base Temperature** - The base temperature that FLOWCAL uses to calculate standard values. - **Density of Air** - The base air density and measurement unit that FLOWCAL uses to calculate standard values. - **Density of Water** - The base water density and measurement unit that FLOWCAL uses to calculate standard values. - **Company Name** - Company name will display in the top right corner of Crystal reports. (See [Report Display Options](../../Reports/Report%20Display%20Options.md) for display precedence.) - **Liquid Rounding** - If you select **Yes**, FLOWCAL applies a carry/borrow method to liquid meters when allocating batch, monthly, or daily accumulated values down to the periodics. This ensures that the sum of periodics corresponds correctly with the batch, monthly, or daily values when rolling back up from the periodics. This applies to imports and edits at the batch, monthly, and daily resolution. - **Component Totals \[Hi Limit\]** - The default maximum set point for meter analysis data. [Meter exception 106](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/0-999/100-199.md) will be generated if the component total falls above maximum limit. - **Component Totals \[Lo Limit\]** - The default minimum set point for meter analysis data. [Meter exception 105](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/0-999/100-199.md) will be generated if the component total falls below the minimum limit. - **Contract Hour** - If not specified at the meter level, the contract hour that FLOWCAL applies to meters and uses in reports.

C6+ Split Options

C6+ splits provide for the C6+ properties to be calculated from a fixed ratio of pure component (C6 through C10) properties. This fixed split ratio is used by meters when applying the GPA-2172 corrections when the meter is not assigned to a quality source.

Ticket Options

The following options specify the default configuration for Conversion tickets: - **Pressure Gauge** - The pressure that FLOWCAL uses to calculate correction factors. - **Atmospheric Pressure** - If FLOWCAL uses gauge pressure to calculate correction factors, the atmospheric pressure and measurement unit to use in the calculation.

Additional Options

You can specify the following additional options: - **Dry Gas Max Water** - The maximum allowable water-vapor content for dry gas samples. - **Ignore Standalone Samples with Duplicate IDs** - If you select **Yes**, FLOWCAL ignores a standalone sample with the same ID as an existing sample during imports.

docs.title: Unit Assignment
docs.text:
Use the System Unit Assignment screen to view the default units that FLOWCAL uses for meter calculations if you do not define units at the meter level. Most meters do not have units defined at the meter level. FLOWCAL also uses the system units to calculate standard conditions.

Unit assignments are datetime effective. If multiple records exist in the database, use the buttons below the Edit Effective From and Effective To fields to scroll through the records.

You cannot edit historical values, but you can create a new set of units.

System units are useful in balancing and reporting. If gas meter 1 reports volume to FLOWCAL in hundred cubic feet (Ccf) while the remaining meters report in thousand cubic feet (Mcf), FLOWCAL calculates the volume for gas meter 1 in both Ccf and Mcf and stores both values in the database for more accurate calculations.

To access the System Unit Assignment screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. In the System group, select **Unit Assignment**.

docs.title: Approvals Tab
docs.text:
The Approvals tab contains several system-specific options for configuring prior period adjustments (PPAs).

Example You can require that PPAs or edits above a threshold are approved before they are applied. This means that instead of an edit applying automatically after editing data, the edit would require approval by designated users with approval privileges.

The Approvals tab contains the following options:

PPA Options

- **Drop-Down Menu** > - **PPAs not Allowed** – PPAs are not allowed on closed data. > - **Apply Immediate** – When you save an edit, the PPA is applied immediately without requiring approval. When this option is selected, the Allow Auto PPAs option must be checked to enable use of the [Create PPAs](../../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Calculations%20Tab.md#CreatePPAs) options in the Meter Editor. > - **Approval Required** – Each PPA is stored in a holding bin until it is approved by one or more designated users belonging to a group. Once approved, the PPA is finalized and applied. > > > When this option is selected, the Allow Auto PPAs option is automatically set to "Yes". The [Create PPAs](../../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Calculations%20Tab.md#CreatePPAs) options in the Meter Editor must be checked to allow PPAs to be created for each meter. > > > > Approval groups are designated in the Edit Approvals section. - **Allow Auto PPAs** - Allow re-imports of data (if the [Create Revisions](../../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Imports%20Tab.md#CreateRevisions) option is enabled in Meter Editor), edits of source assignment data, imports of test reports, etc. to edit meter data and create corresponding PPAs, based on the [Create PPAs](../../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Calculations%20Tab.md#CreatePPAs) options in the Meter Editor. If this option is not enabled, closed data can only be edited within the Volume Editor or PPA Editor. This option is only active when the "Apply Immediate" option is selected. - **Set Accounting Month To** - **Business Month** (default) - The first open month after the last closed month. If the last month closed is April and the current date is July 10, the PPA is accounted for in the business month of May (last month after close in April). - **Production Month** - The measurement month during which a gas or liquid product flowed. Example In July, an edit is made to closed data for a flow that occurred in January. In this case, January is the production month; July is the accounting month. - **Allow Edit** - Choose which month to have the PPA accounted for. - **Show Total on GVS Report** - You can determine whether to show the accounted for information on the Meter Gas Volume Statement by checking or not checking this option. - **Enable Daily PPA Accounting** - By default, PPA accounting information stored in the database only contains the net change of PPAs for the entire month regardless of what data is actually edited. When this option is enabled, daily PPA accounting information is also stored as PPAs are performed. The daily PPA accounting information is not displayed on any screen but is available in the database for custom exports as needed. Example Editing an hour on the 1st, 5th, and 15th of the month with a change of 10 to the volume for each edit will generate a record for the month with a net change of 30. While this tracks the monthly change, it does not track each daily change within the month. With the "Enabled Daily PPA Accounting" option enabled, the information stored will reflect the daily PPA changes by generating three records, one for the 1st, 5th, and 15th, with each record showing a net change of 10. - **Account for Liquid PPAs in Business Month at Location Level** - When this option is enabled, if there is a PPA on a meter or a ticket, FLOWCAL determines which locations the meter or ticket feeds directly into. For each location, a reversal entry will be created for the amount of the PPA with the reverse sign. Another entry is created or accounted for in the current business month. The current business month is defined as follows: - If the first open month is the current calendar month, the entry will be created with today’s date. - If the first open month is a prior calendar month, then the entry will be created on the last day of that month. For PPA totals to be rolled up correctly, users must have flow data on the date where the PPA is to be accounted for. It is assumed that there is not more than one open month between closed months and the current month. This option is applicable to liquid meters only.

Edit Approvals

When the PPA options are set to "Approval Required", you will use these options to designate one or more approval groups. Each drop-down box contains groups with Edit Approval privileges. Click the plus sign to add the selected group to approval group 1 through 3. Click the minus sign to remove groups that have been added previously. If groups are only added to group 1, a PPA requires one level of approval. If groups are added to group 1 and group 2, two levels of approvals are required. If groups are added to groups 1, 2, and 3, three levels of approvals are required. Approvals can be provided in any order (e.g., members from group 2 can provide approval before members of group 1), but at least one person from each set of groups must approve the PPA before it is applied. Example In this system, a group called "Editors" has an approval limit of 500 mcf. Another group called "Supervisors" has an unlimited approval limit. If both are added to the first approval section, a single approval is needed for an edit, and a member from either group could provide that approval. If the PPA for a given month is 600 mcf (exceeding the Editors group limit of 500 mcf), users in the Editors group could not approve the edit, but a user from the Supervisors group could approve it.
