docs.title: General Tab
docs.text:
The General tab contains the following options:

  • Allow free-form Edit Reason Entry - When enabled, you can enter custom edit reasons when editing data; otherwise, you must select from pre-defined edit reasons. (See: Edit Reason Editor)

  • Require Edit Reason for Exceptions - When enabled, you must select an edit reason when updating the status of an exception from the Exception Resolver.

Updating an exception’s status from any screen other than the Exception Resolver will not prompt for an edit reason; however, a default edit reason is generated automatically.

  • Validate When Exception(s) Acknowledged - When enabled, validations are run if an exception status is changed to or from "Acknowledged", "Pending", or "Unresolved" in the Exception Resolver. This enables the application to maintain an accurate count of exceptions for each meter periodic in the final form tables.

This requires additional processing time, so if this count is not needed, do not enable this option.

  • Do Not Close if Missing Data - When enabled, meters that have missing data cannot be closed when the meter is in an active state. A meter is considered to be missing data if the completion status on the meter’s final form monthly record is “Incomplete”, or if there is no final form monthly record rolled up.

  • Do Not Close if Pending Exceptions - When enabled, meters and tickets with unresolved or pending exceptions cannot be closed.

  • Update GMS Date on Close - When enabled, the close process updates the GMS DateThe gas measurement system day on which a database record was created or last modified in the final form tables when data is closed. This option may not always be desirable since the data (volume, energy, etc.) did not actually change.

  • Allow Closed Meters to be Reopened - When enabled, meters that have been closed can be re-opened if no prior period adjustments (PPAs) have been applied. If you want to require a PPA rather than allow meters to be re-opened, do not enable this option.

  • Allow Import Against Inactive Meters - When enabled, you can import data for an inactive meter. FLOWCAL will generate Exception 17003, and the data will not be rolled up. You must then determine if the data is valid and decide whether to set the status to Active for the associated time frame.

  • Allow Import Against Disconnected Meters - When enabled, you can import data for a disconnected meter. FLOWCAL will generate Exception 17004, and the data will not be rolled up. You must then determine if the data is valid and decide whether to set the status to Active for the associated time frame.

  • Inhibit Source Analysis with Exceptions - When enabled, analysis records with exceptions will be inhibited and not used for source apply operations. These exceptions are triggered on records that fall outside of the validation set points specified in the Quality Source Editors.

  • Do Not Extend Source Analysis on Import - When enabled, if a source analysis record does not contain an end date on import, the end date will end at the start of the next source analysis record. If disabled(default), the end date will extend to the end of time, overwriting existing records.

  • Source Assignments Required - When enabled, exception 55 will be generated for any meter that does not include a source assignment for dates after the first flow date (as provided on the Misc. tab of the Meter Editor). When an assignment is created, the exception is automatically resolved.

The meter must have an assignment for all of time, so the first assignment will cover all of time, regardless of what is selected for the duration. You can then split the assignment as long as there is an assignment that covers all of time.

Time periods during which the meter status is non-existent do not require a source assignment.

  • Skip Assign for Ext Vol Meters - When enabled, source assignments are not required for meters designated as External Volume in the Meter Editor. (This option is used in conjunction with the Source Assignments Required option.)

  • Use Calculated Results for Samples - When enabled, imported values for standalone sample mix properties (e.g., relative density, molar mass) will be discarded and replaced with calculated values.

  • Default Rail Car Level

    This feature requires the **Liquids** add-on. When entering a rail car ticket in the Ticket Editor, there is a field for the level on the car that the loaders are trying to hit. Use these fields to specify a default level and associated units, rather than manually entering this value each time. (Applicable to rail car tickets only.)

    • TESTit Integration

      This feature requires TESTit 2 Integrated. - **Allow Reschedule of Analysis Samples** - When enabled, a TESTit sample test is scheduled or rescheduled when source analysis records are inhibited due to exceptions generated when data falls outside of the validation boundaries. - **TESTit Analysis Sample Task** - Specify the task type to schedule (used in conjunction with the Allow Reschedule of Analysis Samples option).

      • Flow Time Edits

        Specify whether the Volume Editor will display meter flow time as a percentage or as a clock time. For percentage of flow, the amount of time represented by a percentage is dependent on the data resolution set in the meter's characteristics. For example: If the data resolution is hourly, 100% corresponds to one hour. If the data resolution is daily, 100% corresponds to one day.

        • Flow Time Calculation Method

          - **Simple (0 or 100%)** - If the differential pressure is greater than 0 or volume is greater than 0, flow time is assumed to be the full duration of the record; otherwise, flow time is assumed to be 0. - **Extension/Sqrt(DP\*SP)** - Static pressure is in psia; differential pressure is pressure in inches of water. - **Extention/Sqrt(DP\*SP\*1/T)** - Static pressure is in psia; differential pressure is pressure in inches of water; temperature is in Rankine.

          • Mol % Normalization

            Source analyses can be enabled to normalize imported samples if the total mole percent is not 100% but is within a minimum and maximum value. The Mol % Normalization option is enabled within Validations in Quality Source Editor, by choosing to use System or Source Quality limits. If System or Source Quality is selected, but min/max limits are not specified, these system-level limits will be used.

            • Pulses Display

              - **Pulses Display/(Decimals)** - The number of decimal places to display for pulses (up to four decimals). - **Days Past End Date (Days)** - The number of days into the future (past the current date) that positive displacement data can be manually entered on the Positive Displacement Entry screens.

              • Exception Values

                - **Pct. Flow in 1 Hour (%)** - For orifice and cone meters, if the flow time (as a percentage of an hour) is greater than this value, an exception is generated (default value is 100.09%). - **Pct. Flow in 1 Day (%)** - For orifice and cone meters, if the total flow time in the day (as a percentage of an hour) is greater than this value, an exception is generated. For a full day of flow, 2400 would be the expected value (default value is 2400.20%). - **Low Flow Cut-Off** - If an orifice or cone meter does not have a low flow cutoff at the meter level, this value is used (default value is 0.00). - **Beta Ratio MIN** - If the beta ratio (orifice or cone diameter/tube diameter) is less than this value, an exception is generated (default value is 0.10). - **Beta Ration MAX** - If the beta ratio (orifice or cone diameter/tube diameter) is greater than this value, an exception is generated (default value is 0.75). - **MIN Pressure** - If the static pressure in psia or kPa is below this value, an exception is generated (default value is 1.00). - **Weekly Resolution (Days)** - Used for orifice chart meters as the maximum length of a record for meters with weekly resolution specified in meter characteristics. - **Monthly Resolution (Days)** - Used for orifice chart meters as the maximum length of a record for meters with monthly resolution specified in meter characteristics.

                • External Volume Import

                  - **Input conditions must match database** - When enabled, you must enter the pressure base, heating value condition, data span, and data resolution on the initial selection window when navigating to Manual Entry \> Meter Input. If these values do not match what is in the database, you will not be allowed to continue. - **Can enter data for any meter** - When enabled, you can enter external volume data for any meter, regardless of whether the meter is identified as external volume in the Meter Editor. When this option is disabled, you can only enter data for meters that are flagged as external volume. - **Allow overwrite of existing data** - When enabled, existing data will be overwritten with new data. The new data will go in as original data (revision 0) and the previously imported data will be removed. This is for meters that: - Are marked as "External Volume" in the Meter Editor. - Contain data that was previously imported and has no edits (including source apply and auto edits). This option is intended for third-party measurement where the third party providing the data makes edits to the data, an audit trail is not required, and only the final answer reported by the third party is needed. When this option is enabled and Create Revisions set to "No", overwriting data will become revision 0. If Creation Revisions set to "Yes", overwriting data will increment the revision number. When this option is not enabled, you will not be able to import into a month that already has data. The import process window will display “No new history found”. For non-external volume meters, once data is imported, FLOWCAL does not overwrite the data on import. - **Season starts on** - External volume meters can have default temperature values set up for the different seasons when data is entered manually, as well as year-round defaults for static pressure and heating value. The start of each season must be defined so the appropriate values are applied when editing the data. The start of the season is set from the [External Volume Default Values Editor](../../../Imports/Manual%20Entry/External%20Volume%20Default%20Values%20Editor.md). See also: [Manual Meter Input](../../../Imports/Manual%20Entry/Manual%20Meter%20Input.md)

                  • GPS Ranges

                    Use these options to define limits to represent geographic boundaries. If latitude and longitude values that are outside of these system limits are entered in the Meter Editor, a message will display.

                    • Location Rollups

                      These options can increase the size of your database. - **Calculate Weekly Totals** - When enabled, if a weekly schedule is assigned to a location in the Location Editor, Location Rollups will total values based on the weekly schedule, as well as calculating hourly, daily, and monthly totals. Location Rollups do not calculate weekly totals by default. A weekly schedule can be assigned to a location, tank, inventory, liquid cavern or comparison. These options allow for Location Rollups to calculate values that span multiple days, but less than a month per the defined schedule. Although referred to as Weekly Totals, the span does not have to be for a week. The customized time span can be defined in the Annual Schedule Editor.

                      • Location Comments

                        Location comments are also known as location edit reasons. When a given location type (i.e. Balance, Inventory, Segment, or Station) is checked, you will be prompted for an edit reason when modifying the respective location type in the Location Editor.

                        • Additional Saturation Values

                          Contact Support before enabling this option. Turning on this functionality will greatly increase the size of your database. Saturation conditions are the amount of water vapor in the gas at various conditions, ranging from dry to saturated. Volume and energy at additional saturation conditions can be calculated and stored in the final form tables. When enabled, volume and energy is calculated at the respective saturation condition(s). - Dry Condition - Saturated @ Flowing - Saturated @ Base - Partially Saturated This information only exists in the database and does not get reported.

docs.title: Thresholds Tab
docs.text:
When the PPA options on the Approvals tab are set to "Approval Required", all PPAs must be approved before being applied. You can use the Thresholds tab to set limits so that approvals are required for edits to open months as well. When these limits are exceeded, approval is required before the edit can be applied.

Edits on open data that do not exceed the specified limits will apply immediately.

The Thresholds tab contains the following options:

PPA Thresholds

These parameters designate system-level minimum thresholds for PPAs when PPAs require approval. A PPA will be set to "Pending" if the PPA amount is equal to or greater than the Unit Diff. and the Percent Diff. values. Otherwise, the PPA will be rejected automatically and a meter message (number 705) will be logged. The rejected PPA can then be manually unrejected and approved from the [Edit Approvals](../../../Edit%20Approvals/Edit%20Approvals.md) screen. FLOWCAL will first look to see if thresholds have been set at the meter level under Operational and Contractual Limits. If meter-level thresholds have not been set, system-level thresholds will be enforced. Gas meters will validate against the Gas Volume and Energy thresholds. Liquid meters will validate against the Mass, GSV and Summed Vol. thresholds. The thresholds will only be enforced if the "Approval Required" PPA Option is selected in System Configuration. VCF edits, which are sometimes used to correct data values shown on final reports, do not alter volume but are still saved as PPAs. Such PPAs will be automatically rejected if the thresholds have been set and will need special attention by the user. Operational and Contractual limits require FLOWCAL Enterprise or the Master Characteristics module.

Monthly Edit Limits (Gas)*

This is the limit at which accumulated edits made to gas volume or energy data for a gas meter during an open month require approval. Quality source apply and auto edits are not considered during calculation if edits have exceeded the edit approval limit. Example If the edit limit is 1,000 units, an edit of 950 units will not require approval. However, if a subsequent edit of 60 units is made, the total edit amount exceeds the 1,000-unit limit (950 + 60 = 1010), so the edit of 60 units would require approval. This prevents original quantities from being altered non-typically without manager review.

Monthly Edit Limits (Liquids)*

This is the limit at which accumulated edits made to GSV or mass data for a liquid meter during an open month require approval. Quality source apply and auto edits are not considered during calculation if edits have exceeded the edit approval limit. Example If the edit limit is 1,000 units, an edit of 950 units will not require approval. However, if a subsequent edit of 60 units is made, the total edit amount exceeds the 1,000-unit limit (950 + 60 = 1010), so the edit of 60 units would require approval. This prevents original quantities from being altered non-typically without manager review.

Calibration Adjustments - Gross Trip Point %

This is the allowable limit of error per transmitter in a TESTit test report. If the error for a particular transmitter exceeds this limit, an exception will be generated. This process is especially helpful in flagging potential erroneous data on test reports. This feature requires TESTit 2 Integrated.

Max PPA Time Frame

This is the system-level maximum time frame beyond which PPAs will automatically be rejected. Example The threshold has been set to six months. In August 2018, a PPA is made to the closed production month of January 2018. The difference between the production month and the current business month is seven months, which is greater than the threshold, so the PPA will be rejected automatically.

docs.title: System Configuration
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires System Information - Can View permissions.

FLOWCAL ships with a single system called ENTERPRISE. If the Multi-System Extension add-on has been purchased, additional systems can be created.

An example of systems may be different drilling basins. You may only need access to the information for certain drilling basins, not all basins. Additionally, it can be desirable to have liquids in one system and gas in a different system. Options for each system can be configured individually.

While an administrator will set these fields during implementation, analysts benefit from understanding the options by knowing what functionality is available that may or may not have been incorporated in the setup.

docs.title: Screen Tabs
docs.text:
Three tabs containing various options are available within the System Configuration screen:

  • General Tab
  • Approvals Tab
  • Thresholds Tab

docs.title: User Preferences
docs.text:
Users can configure personalized settings that are used throughout the application. For example: If you set a default system, then when you access a screen that requires a system selection, the System field will already be populated with the default system you specified.

Settings are specific to each user.

To access the User Preferences screen: 1. Go to **Settings** \> **Settings Manager**. 2. Select **User Preferences** in the **User Settings** group.

User Preferences Screen Details

The following items are available on the User Preferences screen: - **Message Path** - The location of import messages created during the manual import process. Click the **Browse** button to select a folder where the file will be saved (example: D:\Flow-Cal\Logfiles). Each time a location or list is imported, a file is created with the list or location name and a .txt file extension. If you do not define a message path, the import messages will not be stored in a permanent file. - **Graph Centric** - If enabled, the Volume Editor will automatically display the data in graphical form instead of in a tabular grid. You can also switch between tabular and graphical mode from the Volume Editor **File** menu. - **Batch Import Mismatch Pause** - If enabled, a manual list or location import will pause if a meter number in the CFX import file does not match the FLOWCAL meter number it is being imported into. During this pause, you can review the discrepancy and elect to cancel or continue the import. (This feature only applies to manual import of CFX files.) - **Volume Editor Auto Open** - If enabled, FLOWCAL will remember the value of the Auto option in the Volume Editor for the duration of your FLOWCAL session. This option is enabled by default. - **Remember UI Filter Values** - If enabled, FLOWCAL will remember your filter settings in the Exception Resolver, Meter/Location Rollups Viewer, Volume Editor, and Standard Reports for the duration of your FLOWCAL session. Area Filters Remembered Exception Resolver
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Date range type and selection
  • Type filters, time filter, status filters, sort by, severity filter, and max rows
Meter/Location Rollups Viewer
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Date range type and selection
  • Data resolution, options, by location, by meter, revision, quantity, closed, conditions, net allowable and inventory
Volume Editor
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Object number (meter number is not remembered)
  • Auto
  • Month and year
  • FLOWCAL explorer (pinned or unpinned)
Standard Reports
  • Object selector for object type (meter, location, list, or close group)
  • Date range type and selection
  • Report list selection, level, resolution, volume/energy, revision, and number of decimals
- **Hide Virtual Batches** - If enabled, virtual batches will be hidden. - **Virtual Batch Hide Duration** - If the Hide Virtual Batches option is enabled, you can specify a minimum batch length to hide. This allows users to hide short gaps, but show longer gaps where data may be missing. The time period is denoted in hours, minutes and seconds, defaulted to 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 0 seconds. - If you leave the default value at 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 0 seconds, all virtual batches are hidden. - If you change the value to 0 hours, 0 minutes, and 5 seconds, only virtual batches less than or equal to five seconds in length are hidden, but virtual batches greater than five seconds in length are shown. - **Default System** - Selecting a default system automatically populates the System drop-down field on any FLOWCAL screen that requires a system to be specified. - **Notes Visibility** - This designation sets the default visibility for notes that a user creates. Options are: - **Everyone** - Anyone in the FLOWCAL application can see the note and it can be printed on reports such as Batch Ticket. - **Internal** - Anyone in the FLOWCAL application can see the note and it can be printed on reports such as Batch Ticket when the option to print internal notes is enabled. - **Private** - Only the person who entered the note can see it in FLOWCAL. It will not be printed on any reports. - **Preferred Location** - Selecting a preferred location makes the selected location the default location when entering the Location Tree Editor. - **Default Personality** (TESTit 2 Integrated only) - Defines the default application personality to be used upon initial login. - **Default Fluid Phase** - Defines the default fluid phase (gas or liquid) to be used upon creation of a new meter, location, or source analysis.

docs.title: Gas Quality Source Editor

docs.title: Characteristic Tab
docs.text:
The Characteristic tab is used to configure and manage the behavior and functionality for how FLOWCAL acts on quality samples as it pertains to imports, calculations, rollups, and other aspects. The characteristics are datetime effective and can be modified as needed to properly handle changes in quality sampling.

Characteristic 1 Sub-Tab

The Characteristics 1 sub-tab contains the following items: - **Status** - Current status of the quality source; may be "In Service", "Temporarily Out", or "Permanently Out". Source message 302 ("Source status changed") is generated when users update this field. - **Type** - See: [About Sources](../../Sources/About%20Sources.md) - **Sample Analysis** - Used if quality samples are spot samples or composite lab samples. - **Chromatograph** - Used if quality samples come from an online chromatograph. The type must be set to Chromatograph for the gas quality source hourly and daily reports to be run. When the "Enable Rollups" option is checked, and the type is "Chromatograph" or "RTU Average", the quality samples are averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. Sample pressure and sample temperature are not rolled up for chromatographs. If the type is "Gas Analysis", the quality is copied directly to the rollup tables. - **C6+ Split** - C6+ splits provide for the C(n)+ properties to be calculated from a fixed ratio of pure component (C6 through C10) properties. You can specify how a C6+ value is to be split for calculating HCDP, CCT, gravity, heating value, and liquid content (GPMs). - **C7+ Split** - C7+ splits provide for the C(n)+properties to be calculated from a fixed ratio of pure component (C7 through C10) properties. You can specify how a C7+ value is to be split for calculating HCDP, CCT, gravity, heating value, and liquid content (GPMs). - **Contract Day/Hour** - Contract day and hour can be specified if a source is enabled for rollups. These are used to calculate logical measurement months and measurement days for source rollup purposes. - **Pressure Base** - Default sample pressure base. - **Temperature Base** - Default sample temperature base. - **Atm. Pressure** - Default atmospheric pressure. - **Z Method** - Calculation method for gas compressibility. This applies to gas quality sources only. Available options are: - AGA-8 Detail (1992) - AGA-8 Details (2017) - AGA-8 GERG (2017) - Fpv = 1.0 If you do not select a Z-method from the drop-down, FLOWCAL will default to AGA-8 Detail (1992). - **Replace Imported Values with Calculated Results** - By default, FLOWCAL will calculate all possible sample properties from the imported components’ mole percent. FLOWCAL will save the calculated value for any property not provided in the import file. When this option is enabled, FLOWCAL will also replace the properties that have been included in the import file, such as molar mass, densities, Wobbe index, and heating values. - **Component Characterization Method** - Determines how the C(n)+ fluid properties are calculated when a sample is only analyzed to C6 (or to C7, C8, etc.). Enabling the "Use Extended Characteristics" option allows the C(n)+ properties to be calculated from a full characterization of the C(n)+ portion of the sample. This can be imported via text file or manually entered. Manual entry is only supported for C6+ properties. - **Characterization Date** - Records of the C6+ characterization effective date of the extended characteristics; this is a read-only field. Characteristic records may be split in time for any of various reasons. Each split will have its own effective date. The characterization date only changes when the extended characteristics change. BLM requires either a C9 analysis or a C6+ characterization when the C6 component exceeds 0.5 mole percent. If a characterization is used, it must be updated at intervals that depend on the FMP's volume tier. FLOWCAL uses this characterization date to know the "age" of the current characterization and to provide a warning (in the form of an exception) when the interval date is approaching. The value is generally equal to the source characteristic's effective date (also visible on that screen) but there are manual entry and "out-of-order" import scenarios that will cause that date to differ. It may be considered an FYI value as it is FLOWCAL's best attempt to notify the user as noted above and is not a BLM-required reporting field. - **Reason** - An edit reason must be entered when a new source is created, or a source is edited. - **User Name** - User that made the most recent change to the source.

Characteristic 2 Sub-Tab

The Characteristics 2 sub-tab contains the following items: - **Custom Fields** - Ten custom fields are available. The first five are numeric and the next five are alphanumeric with a 50-character limit. The labels can be user-defined by the administrator (see also Custom Fields). - **Associated GQ Source, Sample Interval, and Instrument Inspection** - This feature is no longer supported and is not tied to any functionality. - **Notes** - These notes are associated to the source characteristic record. The notes stored on the Characteristic 2 tab are only available from the Gas Quality Source Editor. Right-click the top of the Gas Quality Source Editor screen to add or view notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Source Analysis Rollup Viewer).

Ext Combinations Sub-Tab

Use the Ext (Extended) Combinations tab to view the imported, calculated, or edited values of each possible C(n)+ combination, whether based on an analysis of the C(n)+ portion of the sample or a defined component C6+/C7+ split fixed ratio.

The following items are available on the Gas Quality Source Editor File menu:

  • New - Creates a new source.
  • Delete - Delete the selected source.

docs.title: Full Wellstream Factor
docs.text:
In FLOWCAL, as in wide industry practice, full wellstream factor (Fws) is a term used to indicate the fraction of the measured wellhead production that is natural gas. It is a direct multiplier of the metered well volume, and it is never greater than 1.0000.

Technically, full wellstream is the whole volume produced from a well. It is common for wells to produce a mix of natural gas, condensate and water. It is best to separate these products and to meter them individually but often this is not practical or economical. Therefore, a procedure is periodically conducted to determine the fractional content of each part. In this process, a test separator is used to separate the well production into the three products for some period of time. The separated contents are each measured and fractions of the whole for each part are determined from this data. The portion that is natural gas is called the natural gas gross withdrawal (U.S. EIA).

Subsequent to the test procedure, the produced gas portion (i.e., the natural gas gross withdrawal) can be calculated by multiplying the metered well volume by the gas fraction.

In FLOWCAL meters, there are two references to full wellstream:

  • In Meter Analysis, there is a full wellstream factor. This may be imported from the flow computer (as original data), edited locally or copied from a Source Analysis.
  • In Meter Characteristics, there is a Yes/No flag that indicates whether the flow computer applied a full wellstream factor to the volume imported by FLOWCAL. If yes, FLOWCAL applies the analysis full wellstream factor to the FLOWCAL-calculated import volume prior to calculating the VCF. On edit recalcs, without regard to the flag, the full wellstream factor is applied to the FLOWCAL-calculated volume along with the VCF.

The meter analysis full wellstream factor and the meter characteristic full wellstream flag are both importable via CFX.

The BLM does not permit the use of full wellstream factor calculations.

docs.title: Gas Quality Source Editor
docs.text:
This feature requires the Source Analysis module.

The Gas Quality Source Editor is used to create, edit, or delete a gas quality source. A gas quality source is used to gather analysis information which a user can then apply to one or more meters. Typically, the user receives a lab analysis and imports or hand keys the analysis information into a gas quality source.

With a gas quality source, you can also take analysis data from a meter, pass it to a gas quality source, and then apply it to one or more meters. For example, a meter is supplied analysis data from an online gas chromatograph. The analysis gets imported into FLOWCAL via the meter import and is then fed to a gas quality source, which is ultimately applied to one or more meters.

To access the Gas Quality Source Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Gas Quality**.

Gas Quality Source Editor Screen Details

The following items are available on the Gas Quality Source Editor screen: - **New** - Create a new source. - **Edit** - Enable Edit mode - **Delete** - Delete the selected source. Gas sources can only be deleted from the Gas Quality Source Editor - **Save** - Save changes; enabled only when in New or Edit mode - **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not changes; enabled only when in New or Edit mode - **Copy** - Copy the selected source and generates a new source, maintaining the general information from the original source - **Exit** - Exit the screen.

docs.title: Main Tab
docs.text:
The Main tab in the Gas Quality Source Editor shows basic information about the source, such as the measurement area, import ID, and analysis type. The fields that are shaded in gray such as System Name, Analysis Type, and Source Meter Number are read-only.

By default, the only fields required to save a new source are Source Number and Reason.

Data Field Details

The following items are available on the Main tab of the Gas Quality Source Editor: - **System Name** - Displays the name of the system the source belongs to - **Import ID** - If applicable, enter the Import ID. This is used if importing data from a third party and the source number in the file is different than the source number that is setup in FLOWCAL. This will tell FLOWCAL what source to import the data to. It can be used with text file imports or Transaction Queue. - **Analysis Type** - Read-only field that is set to gas when the source is created - **TESTit Enable** - This field by default is set to No when a source is created. You can update this field to Yes for this source to be utilized with TESTit Integrated. If you do not have TESTit Integrated, this field is hidden. This feature is supported by TESTit v2 Integrated only. Once this field is set to Yes, it cannot be changed due to the audit trail and the ability to link TESTit tasks to this source. Test reports are available through the Tools \> Test Reports menu on the Gas Quality Source Editor. - **FWS** - See: [Full Wellstream Factor](Full%20Wellstream%20Factor.md) - **Default Analysis** - On startup of a new well the user may assign the meter to a default gas quality source until the first samples are collected and verified. Assigning a meter to a default source (a source with this flag set) generates exception 56 on the meter at the start of the assignment indicating that the meter is using a default analysis. Later, the meter is reassigned to a real source and the exception is cleared. If the user chooses to enter non-default analysis into the source and change the Default Analysis flag to No, the user will need to manually ignore the exception. - **Enable HCDP** - If checked, FLOWCAL will calculate the hydrocarbon dew point. Sample pressure, sample temperature, absolute or gauge, and atmospheric pressure must be provided for the calculation as well as the sample composition. HCDP is the temperature at a given pressure at which hydrocarbons will start to condense out. The calculation methods used are Sandler-Clark or Lomic. Lomic requires a separate license. The HCDP service (FcSrvHCDPQueueProcessor.exe) must be installed and running for these calculations to be done. - **Enable CCT** - If checked, FLOWCAL will calculate the cricondentherm. Mole percents are required for this calculation. Cricondentherm is the highest temperature at any pressure at which hydrocarbons will condense out. The HCDP service (FcSrvHCDPQueueProcessor.exe) must be installed and running for these calculations to be done. - **Enable Rollups** - All quality samples are stored at the data resolution they are generated (4-minute, hourly, daily, monthly, quarterly, etc.). When Enable Rollups is checked, and the Type is Chromatograph or RTU Average, the quality samples are averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. This could be useful for users handling daily and weekly chromatographs that need to report averages for a period. If the Type is Gas Analysis, the quality is copied directly to the rollup tables. The rollups service (FcSrvGQAnlRollup.exe) must be installed and running. To view the result of the source rollups, go to Open \> Rollup Viewers \> Source Analysis Rollups. - **Save Hourly Rollups** - If checked, the hourly rollup data will be saved to the database; otherwise, it is calculated on rollup, but discarded, saving database space. - **Replace Original Only** - When checked, during imports of quality samples, only the revision zero or original data is replaced. Edits to the data are retained and are used when a sample is applied. - **Remove Overlapping Edits** - When checked (default), during imports of quality samples, existing samples are replaced. Any edits that overlap the imported data are truncated to end where the new analysis begins and resume after it ends. - **Snap Before/Snap After**\* - If the effective date of a record (especially a chromatograph hourly record) is provided and is not exactly at the top of the hour (ex: 08:00:05) but is within the range specified before and after the hour, it will "snap" to the top of the hour (ex: 08:00:05 would be snapped to 08:00:00). (See: [Snap Before/Snap After Details](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Snap%20Before-Snap%20After.md)) - **Date Rule**\* - Used to specify rules for setting the effective date on analysis during the import process when an effective date is not provided, or the Override Effective Date on Import is enabled. - **Override Effective Date on Import** - Used in conjunction with the Date Rule. If an effective date is provided on import, this option must be checked to override the date and apply the Date Rule specified. Otherwise, the effective date provided on import will be used. - **Time Rule**\* - Used in conjunction with the Date Rule option, the Time Rule will define what hour to use for the override. When using the Date Rule, a time of midnight will be used by default unless a Time Rule is specified. - **Measurement Area** - Select a measurement area from the drop-down or, with the correct privileges, click the New button to create a new Measurement Area. Measurement areas are managed from the Measurement Area Editor. - **Data Stream** - Informational field used to denote a data collection system or source - **Source Meter Number** - A read-only field that displays the meter number that the source is receiving analysis from. This would be used if sending Online GC data from a meter to a source. - **Custom Fields** - User-definable fields that can be used to accommodate company-specific information, such as division or field technician. All the labels are user-defined and are managed from the Custom Fields screen within the Settings Manager. Fields 1–5 are numeric and 6–10 are alphanumeric. ..\* The Date Rule and Time Rule options are only supported for file imports, not Transaction Queue; however, the Snap Before and Snap After options are supported by both.

docs.title: Service Tab
docs.text:
The Service tab is used for configuring the source for SCADA Request if gas quality data is missing. The SCADA Request service (FcSrvAutoRescan.exe) will look for missing data within the time frame configured on the Service tab. If data is missing, information about the missing data will be written to the SCADA Request table in the database so that the SCADA system can read and attempt to rescan the data.

Data Field Details

The following items are available on the Service tab: - **Rescan Data** - When set to "Yes", the SCADA Request service is enabled for the source. The Auto Rescan service (FcSrvAutoRescan.exe) must be installed and running. - **Log Rescan in Exceptions Log** - When set to ‘Yes’, an exception will be generated when data is missing, and a request has been written to the database for the SCADA system to rescan the data. - **Rescan Frequency** - Determines if the service should rescan at an hourly or daily frequency. - **Time Elapsed Before Considered for Rescan** - Amount of time (days or hours) the service waits until it rescans for missing data. Valid values are 0 to 30 (for days) and 0 to 23 (for hours). Data is considered missing if it is older than the values entered. - **Number of Prior Days Considered** - The time frame for which the service processes data. Specifies the number of days prior to the current date that the service will scan for missing data. Valid values are 1 to 60. For example: If you enter 60, the service will not examine data that is more than 60 days old. - **Daily Rescan Hour** - When Rescan Frequency is set to Daily, this value determines what time of the day to process data.

docs.title: Source Analysis Tab
docs.text:
After importing data, the user can view the data through the Gas Quality Source Editor on the Source Analysis tab. The Source Analysis tab will contain the history of all gas quality data that has been imported in a grid view.

There are several sub-tabs that allow easy access to view Quality, Mole %, Mass%, Condensates, Sample/Sulfur, Custom Fields, as well as any Edit Reasons associated with a record.

A Gas Analysis type will display three years of historical samples on the Source Analysis grid by default, and RTU Average and Chromatograph types will default to the current month of samples. The display can be altered to show current records (default view), original records and all revisions of records:

  • Show Original – This option shows the original data that was imported (Rev. 0 records)
  • Show All – This option shows the original data that was imported as well as all revisions that have been done to the data. When applying gas quality, FLOWCAL applies the record that has the highest revision number to the meter data.
  • Show Current – This is the default. This shows the most current gas quality record that is being applied to the meter.

The grid view will highlight data according to different conditions. If exceptions exist, the effective date background will be highlighted yellow to alert the user. If inhibited, the effective date will be in red font.

Values displayed in blue indicate that the data has been edited. Values displayed in green indicate that the data has been calculated by FLOWCAL. Values highlighted yellow indicate that an exception is available for that data.

docs.title: Context Menu
docs.text:
Selecting or highlighting a record allows the user to right-click and bring up the context menu. The context menu allows the Inhibit/uninhibit of records, and adding/viewing notes.

Users cannot create a new source while on this tab; they must go to any of the other tabs.

docs.title: Analysis Details
docs.text:
Click the New button or the Open Detail button to access the following analysis details.

C6+ Extended

If a source analysis is set to "Use Extended Characteristics" on the Characteristic tab, you must also specify the extended characteristics for a given sample by clicking the C6+ button. This feature allows the user to account for the presence of C7 through C(n) in each sample that is providing a C6+ value for C6. The From date will default to the Characterization Date from the Characteristic tab. If no extended characteristics are provided, the default set of Extended Characteristics assumes that the C6 composition provided is only C6. You can also specify extended characteristics by importing an extended characteristic from a source text file or by importing an extended analysis, which will calculate extended characteristics.

Full Analysis

It is also possible to have what is known as a full extended analysis or a TP-17 for a sample. A full analysis can be entered by clicking the **Full Analysis** button. The user can then enter a detailed analysis that encompasses beyond the customary C1-C10 components. While manual entry is possible, a full extended analysis sample will typically be imported via text file given the significant number of data values. Given the large number of fields on this screen, FLOWCAL has provided some options to help filter the data. By default, all components are shown in the grid. By selecting one of the radio buttons in the Show box, the user can narrow down the values displayed based on the Cn composition (C5 – C6, C7, C8, C9, C10 – C15). The user can also filter by those components with non-zero values or that have a value, regardless of whether it’s zero or higher.

Sample Tab

The Sample tab contains fields relevant to the conditions and methodology of the sampling and the analysis of the sample. The information on this tab is referential and will not affect the calculations in any way. Some reports will use the information. The Sample tab has separate sub-tabs for Sample and Analysis. - The **Sample** fields will contain information on the sample itself such as the ambient temperature of the air at the time of the sample and if the bottle was cleaned. - The **Analysis** fields will contain information on the analysis process such as instrumentation and laboratory name. All fields may be imported via source text file or Transaction Queue.

docs.title: Tools Menu
docs.text:
The following options are available on the Gas Quality Source Editor Tools menu:

  • HC Properties - Launch the Hydrocarbon Property Timeframe Editor.

  • User Access - Display users and groups with access to the selected source.

User/group access to sources is only relevant for companies that maintain object-level security. Most companies do not restrict access on a per-source basis.

  • Test Reports - When the TESTit Enable field is set to Yes on the Main tab of the Gas Quality Source Editor, test reports for the selected source can be viewed by selecting the Test Reports menu.

TESTit v2 Integrated only.

  • Notes - These notes are associated to the selected gas quality source and can be edited while in Edit mode.

The notes stored here are only available from the Gas Quality Source Editor. Right-click the top of the Source Quality Source Editor screen to add or view notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Source Analysis Rollup Viewer).

  • Contact Selection - See: Create Contact Types

  • GQ-GQ Association - The GQ-GQ Association menu is only available when in new mode. This feature is used to reduce the need for extended characteristics runs by associating one source with extended characteristics to other sources that may not have extended characteristics. By creating the association, each associated source receives a copy the characteristics. Go to Setup > Source Analysis > Source Associations to make changes once the source has been created.

docs.title: Validations Menu
docs.text:
Validations will be run automatically on imports and edits when validations are enabled. Each validation tab is enabled individually by checking the option to Enable. Enabled validations can also be run manually from the Review > Run Validations menu.

All exceptions generated can be viewed from the Exception Resolver.

This feature requires the Source Analysis module.

The Show History button allows users to view the history of validation set points across all tabs. This includes what changes, who made the change, and when. The button is available when the Log Validation Set Point History option is checked within FLOWCAL Configuration.

The following tabs are available in the Validations menu:

  • Min/Max - Min/Max performs a comparison of all the minimum and maximum values for each of the components. If Enabled Min/Max is checked, the values entered for all the analysis components will be validated during import and if the value is out of range then an exception will be generated.
  • Radical Change - Radical Change is a comparison of the current analysis to the previous analysis based on percent or unit difference. If the Enabled Radical Change is checked, the values entered for all the analysis components will be validated during import. If the difference between the current analysis and the previous analysis exceeds the limit set, then an exception will be generated.
  • Frozen Value - Frozen Value performs a comparison of selected parameters to prior records to recognize an interruption in a live data feed. This filter is user configurable as to the number of repeated records and which parameters to consider, as well as a limit. This is especially useful with online chromatograph data to identify if a gas chromatograph was left in calibration mode or if SCADA is not being updated with new values.
  • Expert System - Expert System employs statistical analysis to perform historical data review to identify uncharacteristic changes in gas quality source data. This function provides the user with numerous configurable set points that allow the user to customize a validation to each individual gas quality source. The data is validated to make sure a given data point is within a user-defined number of standard deviations from the prior set of samples.
  • Variance - Variance validations compare the GPMs provided by the lab against the GPMs that FLOWCAL calculates. If the difference is outside the limits established, then an exception will be generated.

docs.title: Hydrocarbon Properties
docs.text:
Accessing this form requires System Process – System Information privileges.

Use the Hydrocarbon Properties (HC) Editor to specify physical constants for various analytical properties of hydrocarbon components such as water, CO, ethane and cyclopentane. You can also specify the source of each set of constants. These values are used in quality source calculations for determining values such as liquid volume %, heating value, mass % and density. They are also used for calculating component volumes and component mass on meters and tickets.

FLOWCAL allows the creation and editing of sets of constants as new standards are published. New records may also be required if a contract calls for a value outside of the published standards which needs to be used in calculations.

By default, a set of constants labeled "US Units 2003" is applied to all meters and liquid quality sources in a system from the beginning of time to 01/01/2009 00:00:00. A set of constants labeled "US Units 2009" is applied from 01/01/2009 00:00:00 to 01/01/2017 00:00:00. A set of constants labeled “US Units 2016” is applied from 01/01/2017 00:00:00 until the end of time.

Base pressure and base temperature at which the values were measured are also given, as is the gas constant and the source document from which the constants were taken.

Each set of physical constants can be assigned to a meter, a ticket or to a quality source for a given date and time range.

#### Distribution Notes for GPA 2145-16 GPA 2145-16 is the source document for most of the values for the two FLOWCAL default sets, US Units 2016 and SI Units 2016 at 15C. - The heating value of water has been omitted because water does not contribute to combustion. - The heating value of hydrogen sulfide has been omitted because it is not a saleable component of the gas/liquid product. - Liquid densities for ethylene published in the current revision are given for the liquid state at the normal boiling point, not at 60°F/15°C. GPA is discussing an appropriate density that can be used at these standard temperatures. - All properties for butylenes have been omitted. FLOWCAL has not previously included these properties. If butylene values were previously entered in FLOWCAL, they will need to be added to the current template as well. - Any of the above properties can be added manually via the Hydrocarbon Properties editor. - These sets do not include the 25 new published components. To create a new set of constants in the Hydrocarbon Properties Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Hydrocarbon Properties**. 2. Select **File** \> **New**. The characteristics defined for the set of constants selected prior to choosing New will be carried over to a new configuration by default. 3. Enter a label. 4. Make changes as applicable. 5. Click **Save**. Once created, the Hydrocarbon Properties configuration can be edited as needed, but it cannot be deleted.

Hydrocarbon Properties Editor Details

The following items are available in the Hydrocarbon Properties Editor: - **Label** - Contains a list of existing Hydrocarbon Properties configurations. - **Base Pressure/Temperature** - The base temperature and pressure associated with the extended characteristics defined by a Hydrocarbon Properties configuration are displayed and may be edited. - **Constants (Density of Water, Density of Air, Univ. Gas Constant)** - This is where the constants may be defined for the density of water, density of air, and the Universal Gas Constant used in the derivation of the extended characteristics for each component. The density of water defined here is not used in the calculation standards such as Table A. Each one uses the density of water defined by the standard to calculate the correct results as prescribed by the standard - **Compounds** - Applicable standards. Allows for different characteristic values to be set up per component based on TP-17 characteristic values. - **Columns** - Extended component characteristics. Several characteristics are displayed for each component: - Component name (read-only) - Source document from which the characteristics were derived The source may be a published standard, company literature or any other data source. Once the source for the data is entered in the HC Property Source Document Editor, it can be used for specifying the source document on the Hydrocarbon Properties Editor. - Molar mass (g/mol) - Relative density as an ideal gas - Absolute density as a liquid (in lbm/gal or Kg/m3) - Volume ratio (in ft3/gal) - Gross heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/ft3 or MJ/m3) - Gross heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/gal) - Gross heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/lbm or MJ/Kg) - Gross heating value of fuel as a liquid (in Btu/gal or MJ/m3) - Gross heating value of fuel as a liquid (in Btu/lbm or MJ/Kg) - Net heating value of fuel as an ideal gas (in Btu/ft3 or MJ/m3) - Vapor pressure (in psia or kPa) - Heat of vaporization (in Btu/lb or KJ/kgm) - Critical temperature (in °F or °C) - Critical pressure (in psia or kPa) - Normal boiling point (in °F at 14.696 psia or K at 101.325 kPa) - Characteristic volume (ft3/lb-mol or m3/kmol) - Acentric factor - **Show** - The selection made here determines which class of components is displayed in the grid, allowing for components to be more easily viewed or edited. - **Find** - Perform quick value and text searches within the HC Properties data table grid. For example: You can search for a value, such as 58.122, or for text, such as "Ethane". To activate the find functionality, press **Ctrl+F** or go to **File** \> **Find**.

Tool Menu Details

The following options are available in the Tools menu: - **Change Decimal Positions** - Specify the discrimination for each characteristic in a given configuration. Each applicable standard has separate settings, and the settings which the editor controls are determined by which standard was selected when the form was opened. You must be in edit mode to change the discrimination, and the number of decimals specified for a characteristic determines the number of decimals to which its values are displayed and editable on the main form. - **Manage Source Documents** - Open the [Hydrocarbon Property Source Editor](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/HC%20Property%20Source%20Document%20Editor.md). - **System HC Properties** - Launch the [Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor](Hydrocarbon%20Property%20Time%20Frame%20Editor.md).

docs.title: Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor
docs.text:
The Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor is where the Hydrocarbon Properties that have been created in FLOWCAL may be specified on a datetime effective, per-system basis. By default, all systems use the pre-set US Units 1972 configuration for all dates between 1/1/1972 00:00:00 and 1/1/2009 00:00:00, after which the pre-set US Units 2009 configuration is used. SI Units 2009 is also available if needed.

The dates for which each default configuration applies may be modified for each system, or custom configurations may be defined and named for any system and time frame as needed. The user can edit these values or create new records as new standards are published. New records may also be required if a contract calls for a value outside of the published standards, which needs to be used in calculations.

There are three ways to access the Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor:

  • When defining HC properties for an individual source, select Tools > HC Properties from the Gas Quality Source Editor; or
  • When defining HC properties for an individual meter, select Tools > HC Properties from the Meter Editor; or
  • When defining HC properties for the system, go to Setup > Source Analysis > Hydrocarbon Properties and select the Tools > System HC Properties menu.

Create a New Record

To create a record: 1. Click **New** on the Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor. 2. Specify a Start/End Date and Hydrocarbon Property record. 3. Click **Save**. Existing records will be shortened and removed as needed to accommodate the changes. There are no gaps between time frames. A record is created in between non-adjacent time frames using the same set of units from the time frame preceding it.

Modify an Existing Time Frame

To modify a time frame: 1. Select a row in the Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor and click **Edit**. 2. Adjust the Start/End Date and change the selected Hydrocarbon Properties as appropriate and click Save. Note that if the user shortens the time frame on either end, the editor will leave behind a record with the original entry so that there is not a point in time without an assigned Hydrocarbon Property record. Similarly, if the user extends a record, it will shorten and remove other records as needed. There are no gaps between time frames. A record is created in between non-adjacent time frames using the same set of units from the time frame preceding it.

docs.title: Characteristic Tab
docs.text:
The Characteristic tab is used to configure and manage the behavior and functionality for how FLOWCAL acts on quality samples as it pertains to imports, calculations, rollups, and other aspects. The characteristics are datetime effective and can be modified as needed to properly handle changes in quality sampling.

Characteristic 1 Sub-Tab

The Characteristics 1 sub-tab contains the following items: - **Status** - Current status of the quality source; may be "In Service", "Temporarily Out" or "Permanently Out" Source message 302 “Source Status Changed” is generated when this field is updated. - **Type** - See: [About Sources](../../Sources/About%20Sources.md) - **Sample Analysis** - Used if quality samples are spot samples or composite lab samples - **Chromatograph** - Used if quality samples come from an online chromatograph. The type must be set to Chromatograph for the liquid quality source hourly and daily reports to be run. When Enable Rollups is checked, and the Type is Chromatograph or RTU Average, the quality samples are averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. If the Type is Liquid Analysis, the quality is copied directly to the rollup tables. - **C6+ Split** - C6+ splits provide for the C(n)+ properties to be calculated from a fixed ratio of pure component (C6 through C10) properties. You can specify how C6 data is to be split for calculating HCDP, CCT, gravity, heating value and GPMs. - **C7+ Split** - C7+ splits provide for the C(n)+properties to be calculated from a fixed ratio of pure component (C7 through C10) properties. You can specify how C7 data is to be split for calculating HCDP, CCT, gravity, heating value and GPMs. - **Contract Day/Hour** - Contract day and hour can be specified if source is enabled for rollups. Used to calculate logical measurement month and measurement day for source data rollup purposes. - **Pressure Base** - Default sample pressure base. - **Temperature Base** - Default sample temperature base. - **Atm. Pressure** - Default atmospheric pressure. - **Product** - Default product of the analysis. This can impact the meter apply process wherein the analysis product and the meter product must match. - **Replace Imported Values with Calculated Results** - By default, FLOWCAL will calculate all possible sample properties from the imported components’ mole percent. FLOWCAL will save the calculated value for any property not provided in the import file. When this option is enabled, FLOWCAL will also replace the properties that have been included in the import file, such as molar mass, densities, Wobbe index, GPMs, and heating values. - **Component Characterization Method** - Determines how the C(n)+ fluid properties are calculated when a sample is only analyzed to C6 (or to C7, C8, etc.). Enabling the "Use Extended Characteristics" option allows the C(n)+ properties to be calculated from a full characterization of the C(n)+ portion of the sample. This can be imported via text file or manually entered. (See: Ext Combinations Sub-tab below) - **Characterization Date** - Enables tracking of the C6+ characterization effective date; read-only field. BLM requires either a C9 analysis or a C6+ characterization when the C6 component exceeds 0.5 mole percent. If a characterization is used, it must be updated at intervals that depend on the FMP's volume tier. FLOWCAL uses this characterization date to know the "age" of the current characterization and provide a warning (in the form of an exception) when the interval date is approaching. The value is generally equal to the source characteristic's effective date (also visible on that screen) but there are some manual entry and "out-of-order" import scenarios that will cause the date to differ. It may be considered an FYI value as it is FLOWCAL's best attempt to notify the user as noted above and is not a BLM-required reporting field. - **Reason** - An edit reason must be entered when a new source is created, or a source is edited. - **User Name** - User that made the most recent change to the source.

Characteristic 2 Sub-Tab

The Characteristics 2 sub-tab contains the following items: - **Custom Fields** - Ten custom fields are available. The first five are numeric and the next five are alphanumeric with a 50-character limit. The labels can be user-defined by the administrator (see also Custom Fields). - **Notes** - These notes are associated to the source characteristic record. The notes stored on the Characteristic 2 tab are only available from the Liquid Quality Source Editor. Right-click the top of the Liquid Quality Source Editor screen to add or view notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Source Analysis Rollup Viewer).

Ext Combinations Sub-Tab

Use the Ext (Extended) Combinations tab to view the imported, calculated, or edited values of each possible C(n)+ combination, whether based on an analysis of the C(n)+ portion of the sample or a defined component C6+/C7+ split fixed ratio.

The Liquid Quality Source Editor is used to create, edit, or delete a liquid quality source and to manage its associated liquid analyses data. (See: Liquid Quality Source Overview)

To access the Liquid Quality Source Editor: Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Liquid Quality**.

Liquid sources can only be deleted from the Liquid Quality Source Editor - **Save** - Save changes; enabled only when in new or edit mode - **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not changes; enabled only when in new or edit mode - **Copy** - Copy the selected source and generates a new source, maintaining the general information from the original source - **Exit** - Exit the screen

docs.title: Liquid Quality Source Overview
docs.text:
A liquid quality source is used to organize, validate and calculate liquid analysis information which can then be applied to one or more meters as identified by meter-to source assignments. Typically, a laboratory performs the analysis and provides a source text file which can be imported into a liquid quality source, or a printed/pdf lab report that can be hand-keyed into the source.

Analyses imported into a meter can be “sent” to an assigned source where the configured validations and calculation will take place. Subsequently, these analyses can be applied to additional meters as described above.

docs.title: Main Tab
docs.text:
The Main tab in the Liquid Quality Source Editor shows basic information about the source, such as the measurement area, import ID, analysis type, and fluid service. The fields that are shaded in gray such as System Name, Analysis Type, and Source Meter Number are read-only.

By default, the only fields required to save a new source are Source Number and Reason.

Data Field Details

The following items are available on the Main tab of the Liquid Quality Source Editor: - **System Name** - Displays the name of the system the source belongs to. - **Import ID** - If applicable, enter the Import ID. This is used if importing data from a third party and the source number in the file is different than the source number that is setup in FLOWCAL. This will tell FLOWCAL what source to import the data to. It can be used with text file imports or Transaction Queue. - **Analysis Type** - Read-only field that is set to liquid when the source is created. - **Fluid Service** - This field is only editable when users are creating a new source. The fluid service is set to "Hydrocarbon" by default; if "Nonhydrocarbon" is selected, the Nonhydrocarbon Liquid Source Analysis detail will display. After a source has been created, this field is read-only. - **TESTit Enable** - This field by default is set to No when a source is created. You can update this field to Yes for this source to be utilized with TESTit Integrated. If you do not have TESTit Integrated, this field is hidden. This feature is supported by TESTit v2 Integrated only. Once this field is set to Yes, it cannot be changed due to the audit trail and the ability to link TESTit tasks to this source. Test reports are available through the Tools \> Test Reports menu on the Liquid Quality Source Editor. - **Enable Rollups** - All quality samples are stored at the data resolution they are generated (4-minute, hourly, daily, monthly, quarterly, etc.). When Enable Rollups is checked, and the Type is Chromatograph or RTU Average, the quality samples are averaged and rolled up into daily and monthly averages. This could be useful for users handling daily and weekly chromatographs that need to report averages for a period. If the Type is Liquid Analysis, the quality is copied directly to the rollup tables. The rollups service (FcSrvGQAnlRollup.exe) must be installed and running. To view the result of the source rollups, go to Open \> Rollup Viewers \> Source Analysis Rollups. - **Save Hourly Rollups** - If checked, the hourly rollup data will be saved to the database; otherwise, it is calculated on rollup, but discarded, saving database space. - **Replace Original Only** - When checked, during imports of quality samples, only the revision zero or original data is replaced. Edits to the data are retained and are used when a sample is applied. - **Remove Overlapping Edits** - When checked (default), during imports of quality samples, existing samples are replaced. Any edits that overlap the imported data are truncated to end where the new analysis begins and resume after it ends. - **Ignore Duplicate Dates** - When this option is enabled, any quality source sample with the same source and sample date as an existing sample is not imported. When attempting to import a duplicate liquid sample through the file import service, the duplicate sample is ignored, the import is treated as successful, and a source message is generated to alert the user. When attempting to manually import, a message is generated on screen to alert the user that the sample was not imported as well as generating a source message. - **Measurement Area** - Select a measurement area from the drop-down or, with the correct privileges, click the New button to create a new Measurement Area. Measurement areas are managed from the Measurement Area Editor. - **Data Stream** - Informational field used to denote a data collection system or source - **Source Meter Number** - A read-only field that displays the meter number that the source is receiving analysis from. This would be used if sending Online GC data from a meter to a source. - **Custom Fields** - User-definable fields that can be used to accommodate company-specific information, such as division or field technician. All the labels are user-defined and are managed from the Custom Fields screen within the Settings Manager. Fields 1–5 are numeric and 6–10 are alphanumeric. - **Liquid Analysis Comparison** - Allows a user to compare analysis samples to another liquid quality source. This is useful if multiple samples are collected and sent to different labs for analysis. On import, an exception will be generated that the comparison failed. The user can go to the Source Analysis tab and right-click on the grid to select Compare from the context menu and re-run the comparison.

docs.title: Service Tab
docs.text:
The Service tab is used for configuring the source for SCADA Request if liquid quality data is missing. The SCADA Request service (FcSrvAutoRescan.exe) will look for missing data within the time frame configured on the Service tab. If data is missing, information about the missing data will be written to the SCADA Request table in the database so that the SCADA system can read and attempt to rescan the data.

Data Field Details

The following items are available on the Service tab: - **Rescan Data** - When set to "Yes", the SCADA Request service is enabled for the source. The Auto Rescan service (FcSrvAutoRescan.exe) must be installed and running. - **Log Rescan in Exceptions Log** - When set to "Yes", an exception will be generated when data is missing, and a request has been written to the database for the SCADA system to rescan the data. - **Rescan Frequency** - Determines if the service should rescan at an hourly or daily frequency. - **Time Elapsed Before Considered for Rescan** - Amount of time (days or hours) the service waits until it rescans for missing data. Valid values are 0 to 30 (for days) and 0 to 23 (for hours). Data is considered missing if it is older than the values entered. - **Number of Prior Days Considered** - The time frame for which the service processes data. Specifies the number of days prior to the current date that the service will scan for missing data. Valid values are 1 to 60. For example: If you enter 60, the service will not examine data that is more than 60 days old. - **Daily Rescan Hour** - When Rescan Frequency is set to Daily, this value determines what time of the day to process data.

docs.title: Source Analysis Tab - Source Analysis Detail Screen
docs.text:
The Source Analysis Detail screen is available when you double-click a Source Analysis grid row.

The source analysis detail grid will change based on the fluid service selection.

Hydrocarbon Sources

Base Information - **Sample Date** - Date/time that the sample was drawn. This required field is used to determine which meter batch this sample applies to. - **Product** - The hydrocarbon product name of the sampled liquid. If provided, this analysis will only be applied to meter batches with the same product designation. - **Base Density Calc Method** - The method used to calculate base densities for this analysis (HC Properties, COSTALD, TP-2, REFPROP). HC Properties is the default method, which uses the constants given in GPA-2145. If the designated product is configured to use Table E (TP-27) or Table E Extended (TP-27 EXT), then “Base Density Calc Method” will automatically populate with the “Sample Density Calc. Method” set on the Product. The user can always select any option. The following table depicts the order of precedence used to set the “Base Density Calc Method”: | Product with Sample Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit | Base Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit | Base Density Calc Method Used | |:--:|:--:|:---| | Yes | No | Default Base Density from the Product | | Yes | Yes | Base Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit | | No | Yes | Base Density Calc Method Defined on Import/Edit | | No | No | Use HC Properties | - **Pressure Base** - Pressure base of the stated mix properties. - **Temperature Base** - Temperature base of the stated mix properties. - **Set Relative Density by Range** - Specialty option that should only be used in consultation with Quorum. - **Inhibited** - Indication that this analysis is inhibited. An inhibited analysis will not be applied to meters and will not be included in any averages. It is an inactive analysis. - **Has Extended Analysis** - Indication that this is an extended analysis. Extended analyses may include up to 200 components. FLOWCAL uses extended analyses to calculate and update the extended combinations as shown in the Characteristics tab of the Liquid Analysis Editor. Mix Properties - **Molar Mass** - **Abs. Dens. (in vac., lbm/gal)** - **Abs. Dens. (in air, lbm/gal)** - **Relative Density** - **API Gravity** - **Volume Ratio** - **Viscosity** - **Vapor Pressure** Data Tabs - **Mole %** - Displays component mole percentages. - **Mass %** - Displays component mass percentages. - **LV%** - Displays component liquid volume percentages. - **Sulfurs** – Displays sulfur content in ppm. - **Additional** – Provides fields for various mixture attributes including S&W amount, shrink and flash factors, and product specification limits. - **Extended Analysis** - For source analysis records that have full analysis, mole % provided for the individual components in aromatics and BTEX groups are summed and displayed. These fields are read-only. - **Aromatics** - BTEX and their derivatives. There are total 43 aromatics compounds in the full analysis supported by FLOWCAL. - Benzene - Ethylbenzene - Toulene - Xylenes (m-Xylene, p-Xylene, o-Xylene) - **Product Spec** - Users can manually enter percentages for these special interest components: Aromatics, Olefins, Carbon Monoxide, Hydrogen, Water, and Hydrogen Sulfide. - **Aromatics** - These fields are independent from the individual components that are part of the extended analysis. These fields are edited by users, not calculated by FLOWCAL. - **Olefins** - These read-only fields display the summation of Ethylene, Propylene, and Butylenes. - **H2S** - H2S content, expressed in percentage. - **Sample** - The Sample tab contains fields relevant to the conditions and methodology of the sampling and the lab’s analysis of the sample. The Sample tab contains data on two sub-tabs: - **Sample Sub-Tab** - Contains information to identify the sample and the conditions existing at the time the sample was drawn. The following densities, determined at sample conditions at the time of the sample draw, are supported: - Absolute Density (in vacuum) - Absolute Density (in air) - Relative Density - API Gravity If any of these densities are provided, the sample temperature, pressure and gauge/absolute indicator are required and exceptions 3501 to 3503 may be generated if these fields are missing. Atmospheric pressure (exception 3504) is required if ‘Gauge’ is indicated. A sample density may be selected to be applied to a meter or ticket via the Source Assignment editor. -  **Analysis Sub-Tab** - Contains information on the analysis process such the name of the chemist performing the analysis and the instrumentation used. - **Custom** – Eleven custom fields that users can label and used in any fashion. Buttons - **C6+ Extended** - **View mode** - This button shows the current C6+ properties from the Source’s characteristic - **Edit/New mode** - This button allows entry of C6+ properties as listed on a lab report. C6+ properties are required when a source analysis is set to "Use Extended Characteristics" on the Characteristic tab - **Calculate** – Runs calculations for the current analysis. - If the current analysis is an extended analysis, calculate extended combinations. - Starting with mole %, calculate mass %, LV% and mix properties. - Missing and previously calculated values will be replaced. Imported and manually edited values will not be replaced. - **Normalize** – Proportionately normalizes the current mole percent analysis to 100% and initiates calculations. - **Exceptions** – Displays unresolved exceptions - **Full Analysis** – Opens the Extended Analysis Detail screen. A full or extended analysis is a detailed analysis that includes components between and beyond the customary C1 – C10 components. FLOWCAL supports approximately 200 compounds as defined in GPA TP-17 (1998). Given the large number of fields on this screen, FLOWCAL has provided some options to help filter the data. By default, all components are shown in the grid. By selecting one of the radio buttons in the Show box, the user can narrow down the values displayed to the compounds included in a carbon group (C5 – C6, C7, C8, C9, C10 – C15) based on elution order. That is, selecting C7 will filter and display those compounds that elute after hexane (C6), up to and including heptane (C7). - **New** - **Edit** - **Exit** - **Print** Edit Reason - **Reason** - The reason provided for the latest edit - **User Name** - The name of the user who made the edit

For Non-Hydrocarbon Sources

Base Information - **Sample Date** - Date/time that the sample was drawn. This required field is used to determine which meter batch this sample applies to. - **Product** - The nonhydrocarbon product name of the sampled liquid. If provided, this analysis will only be applied to meter batches with the same product designation. - **Base Density Calc Method** – This option will be disabled in the liquid quality source analysis editor for non-hydrocarbon products. - **Pressure Base** - Pressure base of the stated mix properties. - **Temperature Base** - Temperature base of the stated mix properties. - **Inhibited** - Indication that this analysis is inhibited. An inhibited analysis will not be applied to meters and will not be included in any averages. It is an inactive analysis. Mix Properties - **Molar Mass** - **Abs. Dens. (in vac., lbm/gal)** - **Abs. Dens. (in air, lbm/gal)** - **Relative Density** - **API Gravity** - **Volume Ratio** - **Viscosity** - **Vapor Pressure** Data Tabs - **NHC Mole %** - Displays non-hydrocarbon component mole percentages. - **NHC Mass %** - Displays non-hydrocarbon component mass percentages. - **NHC LV%** - Displays non-hydrocarbon component liquid volume percentages. - **Sample** - The Sample tab contains fields relevant to the conditions and methodology of the sampling and the lab’s analysis of the sample. The Sample tab contains data on two sub-tabs: - **Sample Sub-Tab** - Contains information to identify the sample and the conditions existing at the time the sample was drawn. -  **Analysis Sub-Tab** - Contains information on the analysis process, such the name of the chemist performing the analysis and the instrumentation used. - **Custom** – Eleven custom fields that users can label and used in any fashion. Buttons For non-hydrocarbon analysis, calculations will not occur. - **Normalize** – This option is disabled for non-hydrocarbon products. - **Exceptions** – Displays unresolved exceptions. - **Full Analysis** – This option is disabled for non-hydrocarbon products. - **New** - **Edit** - **Exit** - **Print** Edit Reason - **Reason** - The reason provided for the latest edit. - **User Name** - The name of the user who made the edit.
