docs.title: Source Analysis Tab
docs.text:
Users cannot create new sources from this tab.

The Source Analysis tab displays a range of historic liquid quality data in a grid view. The “From” and “To” date selectors control the range of data displayed. The display can be altered to show current record revisions (default view) or the original record revisions:

  • Show Original – This option shows the original data that was imported (Rev. 0 records)
  • Show Current (default) – This shows the most current liquid quality record

Analysis information is grouped under the following sub-tabs:

  • Properties - The aggregate properties of the analysis and their base conditions
  • Mole % - Component mole percent values
  • Mass % - Component mass percent values
  • LV% - Component liquid volume percent values
  • Sample - Sample tag and analyzer details and comments
  • Custom - User-defined, custom fields
  • Edit Reasons - Edit reasons and codes, and the user that made the edits

The analysis grids highlight data according to different conditions. If an analysis record is inhibited, the effective date will be in red font. Any values in the grid that appear ‘blue’ indicate that the data has been edited. Any values that appear ‘green’ indicate that the data has been calculated by FLOWCAL. Any values that are highlighted ‘yellow’ indicate an exception existing for that value. Additionally, if any unresolved exception exists, the effective date background will be highlighted yellow.

Double-click a Source Analysis grid row to access the Source Analysis Detail screen.

Button Details

The following buttons are available from the Source Analysis tab: - **Exceptions** - Shows a brief summary of unresolved exceptions for the displayed time period - **New Detail** - Opens the Detail screen in New mode, ready for user input. (This button is not available when the “Show Original” option is selected) - **Open Detail** - Opens the Detail screen in read mode, providing a form view of the currently selected record - **Exit** - Closes the editor

Right-Click Menu Options

Select or highlight one or more rows in the data grid and right-click to access options in the context menu. - **Compare** - Opens the analysis comparison screen, which allows repeatability of two analyses per GPA 2177-03. On this screen, you can select a liquid quality source to compare to and use the navigation arrows on the top right to select a comparison sample. Clicking Compare at the bottom of the screen will calculate the differences for each component. You can also right-click on the grid and copy everything to the clipboard. - **Graph** - This feature has been disabled. - **Inhibit** - Inhibits the currently selected analyses. An inhibited analysis is not applied to any meters and is not included in any averages. It is an inactive analysis. - **Uninhibit** - Uninhibits the currently selected analyses. - **Add User Note** - Opens the user note dialog in Add mode with the date range pre-selected to the dates/times currently highlighted on the analysis grid. - **View User Note** - Opens the user note dialog in View mode.

docs.title: Tools Menu
docs.text:
The following options are available on the Liquid Quality Source Editor Tools menu:

  • HC Properties - Launch the Hydrocarbon Property Time Frame Editor.

  • User Access - Display users and groups with access to the selected source.

User/group access to sources is only relevant for companies that maintain object-level security. Most companies do not restrict access on a per-source basis.

  • Test Reports - When the TESTit Enable field is set to Yes on the Main tab of the Liquid Quality Source Editor, test reports for the selected source can be viewed by selecting the Test Reports menu.

TESTit 2 Integrated only.

  • Notes - These notes are associated to the selected liquid quality source and can be edited while in edit mode.

The notes stored here are only available from the Liquid Quality Source Editor. Right-click the top of the Source Quality Source Editor screen to add or view notes that can be accessed throughout the application (e.g., from the Source Analysis Rollup Viewer).

  • Contact Selection - See: Create Contact Types

  • GQ-GQ Association - The GQ-GQ Association menu is only available when in new mode. This feature is used to reduce the need for extended analyses runs by associating one source with an extended analysis to other sources that may not have an extended analysis. By creating the association, each associated source receives a copy the characteristics. Go to Setup > Source Analysis > Source Associations to make changes once the source has been created.

docs.title: Liquid Quality Source Editor

docs.title: Validations Menu
docs.text:
Validations will be run automatically on imports and edits when validations are enabled. Each validation tab is enabled individually by checking the option to Enable. Enabled validations can also be run manually from the Review > Run Validations menu.

All exceptions generated can be viewed from the Exception Resolver.

This feature requires the Source Analysis module.

The Show History button allows users to view the history of validation set points across all tabs. This includes what changes, who made the change, and when. The button is available when the Log Validation Set Point History option is checked within FLOWCAL Configuration.

The following tabs are available in the Validations menu:

  • Min/Max - Min/Max performs a comparison of all the minimum and maximum values for each of the components. If Enable Min/Max is checked, the values entered for all the analysis components will be validated during import and if the value is out of range then an exception will be generated.

Mol % Normalization

Source Analysis can be enabled to normalize imported samples if the total mole percent is not 100% but is within a minimum and maximum value. The following options are available for Mole % Normalization: - **System** – When selected in the Source Editor, FLOWCAL will use the System Configuration limits for Mole % Normalization. This will enable the user to manage limits for all sources. - **Source Quality** – When selected, the local source limits are used. This will enable the user to place custom normalization per source. - **No Normalization** – When selected, normalization will not occur for any source. Exceptions will not be written if this option is enabled. If the analysis total is outside the normalization range, the analysis will NOT be normalized. Only analysis totals within the range will be normalized. If the normalization does not occur, [exception 3719 or 3720](../../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/3000/3700-3799.md) will be written. The Mole % Normalization Minimum and Maximum values shown in the Quality tab for Source Validations are read only. These values are configuration within System Configuration or the Liquid Quality Source.

  • Radical Change - Radical Change is a comparison of the current analysis to the previous analysis based on percent or unit difference. If the Enabled Radical Change is checked, the values entered for all the analysis components will be validated during import. If the difference between the current analysis and the previous analysis exceeds the limit set, then an exception will be generated.

  • Frozen Value - Frozen Value performs a comparison of selected parameters to prior records to recognize an interruption in a live data feed. This filter is user configurable as to the number of repeated records and which parameters to consider, as well as a limit. This is especially useful with online chromatograph data to identify if a liquid chromatograph was left in calibration mode or if SCADA is not being updated with new values.

  • Expert System - Expert System employs statistical analysis to perform historical data review to identify uncharacteristic changes in liquid quality source data. This function provides the user with numerous configurable set points that allow the user to customize a validation to each individual liquid quality source. The data is validated to make sure a given data point is within a user-defined number of standard deviations from the prior set of samples.

  • Variance - Variance validations compare the GPMs provided by the lab against the GPMs that FLOWCAL calculates. If the difference is outside the limits established, then an exception will be generated.

docs.title: Quality Assignment Editor
Configuring Assignments
docs.text:
The options available when configuring assignments vary slightly between gas and liquid, and between meters and locations. The New and Edit functions will open the appropriate detail screen based on the selected object. Meters will open to the detail corresponding to the meter’s fluid phase; locations open to a detail tailored for liquid tickets.

Gas Meter Assignment Details

The following options are available on the gas meter assignment details screen: - **Assignment** - The meter object selector will be populated from the previous screen. The source object selector will only display gas sources for gas meters. - **Duration** - Assignments are date-effective. - **Apply GQ At** - The earliest meter flow data date/time to which the analysis should be applied. - **Effective Date/Time** - Applies to the flow data record whose effective date/time matches the source analysis record. This is typical for online chromatographs. - **Start of Current Day** - Applies the source record back to the first hour of the current day. "Current day" refers to the date of the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract hour. If there are multiple analyses in a measurement day, the last one will be used. - **Start of Current Month** - Applies the source record back to the first hour of the current month. "Current month" refers to the date of the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract day and hour. If there are multiple analyses in a contract month, the last one will be used. - **Start of Next Day** - Applies the source record to the first hour of the next day. "Next day" is relative to the date of the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract hour. if there are multiple analyses in a measurement day, the last one will be used. - **Start of Next Month** - Applies the source record to the first hour of the next month. "Next month" is relative to the analysis record being applied including consideration of the meter’s contract day and hour. If there are multiple analyses in a measurement month, the last one will be used. - **Apply Extended As** - Dictates how a full or extended analysis (potentially 200+ components) is totaled for application to a meter. This only applies to source analyses designated as full analyses in the source detail. - **Saturation** - The water vapor saturation condition of the heating value that is to be applied. - **Meter Condition** - Choose the heating value that matches the meter’s current heating value saturation. - **Dry Condition** - Apply the source’s dry heating value and alter the meter’s condition to dry. - **Wet Condition** - Apply the source’s wet heating value and alter the meter’s condition to wet. - **As Delivered Condition** - Apply the source’s as-delivered heating value and alter the meter’s condition to as-delivered. - **Recalc. Method** - The calculation methodology to be used on the meter. - **Volume** - Recalculates the meter’s volume and energy using the applied relative density, VCF, and heating value. - **VCF** - Recalculates the meter’s VCF using the applied relative density, leaving the volume unchanged. By default, the energy will not be recalculated. - **Vol, Set VCF = 1** - Recalculates the meter’s volume and energy using the applied relative density and heating value and resetting the VCF to 1. - **Enable Assignment** - Enables the source apply to proceed. This option is enabled by default on new assignments. It is only disabled in specific circumstances. - **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** - Enables the application of a prior analysis when the analyses that should be available for a given meter date/time is missing or marked as inhibited. - **Copy Liquid Content** - Enables the copy of the source’s liquid content values (GPMs) to the meter. - **Copy ASD Heating Value** - Enables the copy of the source’s as delivered heating value to the meter.

Liquid Meter Assignment Details

The following options are available on the liquid meter assignment detail screen: - **Assignment** - The meter object selector will be populated from the previous screen. The source object selector will only display liquid sources for liquid meters. If a non-hydrocarbon meter is selected, the source object selector will only display non-hydrocarbon sources. - **Duration** - Assignments are date-effective. All assignment options will be effective only for the meter data that occurs within the effective date span of the assignment. - **Apply Sample At** - The flow data date/time to which the analysis should be applied. - **End of Batch** - Apply the sample, whose sample date is within tolerance of the batch end date, to entire batch. Tolerance is specified in the on the [Liquids > Setup tab](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Liquids%20Tab.md) of the Meter Editor. - **Effective Date/Time** - Applies to the flow data record whose effective date/time matches the source analysis record. This is typical for online chromatographs. - **Apply Extended As**\* - Dictates how a full or extended analysis (potentially 200+ components) is totaled for application to a meter. This only applies to source analyses designated as full analyses in the source detail. - **Apply Density**\* - Signifies if the meter quantities will be recalculated using the source density. In all cases, the analysis information will be copied to the meter and used to calculate component masses, component volumes, and summed volume. - **Do Not Apply** - The flow data quantities gross standard volume, net standard volume and total mass will not be altered when the analysis is copied to the meter. Only the component quantities and summed volume are calculated. - **Base Relative Density** - The source’s base relative density will be copied to the meter’s observed density and the meter’s observed temperature will be set to the product base temperature and the observed pressure will be set to 0 gauge pressure or the product EVP. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Base API Gravity** - The source’s base API gravity will be copied to the meter’s observed density and the meter’s observed temperature will be set to the product base temperature and the observed pressure will be set to 0 gauge pressure or the product EVP. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Base Density (in vac.)** - The source’s base absolute density in vacuo will be converted to meter density units and copied to the meter’s observed density, the meter’s observed temperature will be set to the product base temperature and the observed pressure will be set to 0 gauge pressure or the product EVP. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Sample Relative Density** - The source’s sample relative density, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the meter’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Sample API Gravity** - The source’s sample API gravity, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the meter’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Sample Density (in vac.)** - The source’s sample absolute density in vacuo, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the meter’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Recalc. Method** - The calculation methodology to be used on the meter. - **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Recalculates the meter’s gross standard volume, net standard volume and mass using the applied density and VCF. This is the most common method. - **Correlation Factor (CF)** - Recalculates the meter’s correlation factors using the applied density, leaving the volume and mass quantities unchanged. - **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Recalculates the meter’s volume and mass quantities using the applied density and resetting the correlation factors to 1. - **Enable Assignment** - Enables the source apply to proceed. This option is enabled by default on new assignments. It is only disabled in specific circumstances. - **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** - Enables the application of a prior analysis when the analyses that should be available for a given meter date/time is missing or marked as inhibited. - **Apply Back to Prior Sample** - Enables the application of a sample to multiple batches beginning from the prior sample’s effective date. This is useful when samples are not retrieved for every batch, such as daily batches. - **Apply Back Within Sample Month Only** - Limits the prior sample application to the current month. This can prevent PPAs from being created. This option can only be enabled when **Apply Back to Prior Sample** option is enabled. - **Use First Sample** - Enables use of the first sample, by chronological sample date, on an End of Batch assignment with [sample tolerance](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Liquids%20Tab.md) set. By default, the last sample is used when there are multiple samples within the sample tolerance. \*Options are disabled for non-hydrocarbon meters. **See also:** [Liquid Meter Assignment - Options Details](Liquid%20Meter%20Assignment%20Ops%20Dets.md)

Location Assignment Details

The following options are available on the location assignment detail screen: - **Assignment** - The location object selector will be populated from the previous screen. The source object selector will only display liquid sources. - **Duration** - Assignments are date-effective. - **Apply Sample At** - The date/time to which the analysis should be applied. - **Effective Date/Time** - Applies the analysis to tickets whose effective date/time matches the sample date/time. When used in conjunction with the **Use Prior…** option, all future tickets will use the same analysis until a new sample is received. - **Start of Current Day** - The analysis date/time is adjusted to the start of the day (contract hour) and applied to tickets whose effective date/time matches the adjusted sample date/time. When used in conjunction with the **Use Prior…** option, all tickets in the current day and those in the future will use the same analysis until a new sample is received. - **Start of Current Month** - The analysis date/time is adjusted to the start of the current month (contract day, contract hour) and applied to tickets whose effective date/time matches the adjusted sample date/time. When used in conjunction with the **Use Prior…** option, all tickets in the current month and those in the future will use the same analysis until a new sample is received. - **Apply Extended As** - Dictates how a full or extended analysis (potentially 200+ components) is totaled for application to a ticket. This only applies to source analyses designated as full analyses in the source detail. - **Apply Density** - Signifies if the ticket quantities will be recalculated using the source density. In all cases, the analysis information will be copied to the ticket and used to calculate component masses, component volumes, and summed volume. - **Do Not Apply** - The flow data quantities gross standard volume, net standard volume, and total mass will not be altered when the analysis is copied to the ticket. Only the component quantities and summed volume are calculated. - **Base Relative Density** - The source’s base relative density will be copied to the ticket’s observed density and the ticket’s observed temperature and pressure will be set to base temperature and base pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Base API Gravity** - The source’s base API gravity will be copied to the ticket’s observed density and the ticket’s observed temperature and pressure will be set to base temperature and base pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Base Density (in vac.)** - The source’s base absolute density in vacuo will be converted to ticket density units and copied to the ticket’s observed density, and the ticket’s observed temperature and pressure will be set to base temperature and base pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Sample Relative Density** - The source’s sample relative density, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the ticket’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Sample API Gravity** - The source’s sample API gravity, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the ticket’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Sample Density (in vac.)** - The source’s sample absolute density in vacuo, sample temperature, and sample pressure will be copied to the ticket’s observed density, observed temperature, and observed pressure, respectively. Calculation of the flow data quantities will be initiated. - **Recalc. Method** - The calculation methodology to be used on the ticket. - **Vol. and Mass, Use CF** - Recalculates the ticket’s gross standard volume, net standard volume, and mass using the applied density and VCF. This is the most common method. - **Correlation Factor (CF)** - Recalculates the ticket’s correlation factors using the applied density, leaving the volume and mass quantities unchanged. - **Vol. and Mass, Set CF = 1** - Recalculates the ticket’s volume and mass quantities using the applied density and resetting the correlation factors to 1. - **Enable Assignment** - Enables the source apply to proceed. This option is enabled by default on new assignments. It is only disabled in specific circumstances. - **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** - Enables the application of a prior analysis when the analyses that should be available for a given ticket date/time is missing or marked as inhibited.

docs.title: Quality Assignment Editor
Liquid Meter Assignment - Options Details
docs.text:
These selections in the Options groupbox will determine which sample of the source is applied to meter data. (See also: Configuring Assignments)

Apply Sample At

Users can elect to apply samples at the end of a batch or at the effective date/time. ### End of Batch When applied at the end of a batch, a sample with a sample date that matches the end effective date of the batch is applied to the entire batch. Example A sample with a sample date of 01/13/2023 09:00 is applied to the entirety of a batch dated 01/01/2023 09:00 – 01/13/2023 09:00. ##### Sample Tolerance End-of-batch assignments are subject to sample tolerance limits that are configured on the [Liquids tab of the Meter Editor](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Liquids%20Tab.md). When a sample tolerance is set, a sample with a date that is outside of the tolerance will not be applied. ##### Use First Sample The Use First Sample option is available for end-of-batch assignments with a sample tolerance set. When this option is enabled, if there are multiple samples that fall within the sample tolerance of the end of the batch, the earliest sample will be used. By default, FLOWCAL will use the latest chronological sample that meets all specified criteria. Example A meter has a sample tolerance of one hour before and after the end of the batch. The meter has one batch: | Effective Date | Effective Date End | |--------------------|---------------------| | 11/30/2023 9:00:00 | 11/30/2023 12:00:00 | The liquid quality source has four samples: | Sample Date | |---------------------| | 11/29/2023 00:00:00 | | 11/30/2023 11:45:00 | | 11/30/2023 12:00:00 | | 11/30/2023 12:00:01 | Samples are applied as follows, based on configuration options: - End of batch assignment, with no other option enabled: | Batch | Sample Applied | |-----------------------------|---------------------| | 11/30/2023 9:00:00-12:00:00 | 11/30/2023 12:00:01 | - End of batch assignment, with **Use First Sample** option enabled: | Batch | Sample Applied | |-----------------------------|---------------------| | 11/30/2023 9:00:00-12:00:00 | 11/30/2023 11:45:00 | - End of batch assignment, with **Use Prior** option enabled: | Batch | Sample Applied | |-----------------------------|---------------------| | 11/30/2023 9:00:00-12:00:00 | 11/30/2023 12:00:01 | - End of batch assignment, with **Use Prior** and **Use First Sample** options enabled: | Batch | Sample Applied | |-----------------------------|---------------------| | 11/30/2023 9:00:00-12:00:00 | 11/30/2023 11:45:00 | ### Effective Date/Time When a sample is applied at the effective date/time, the sample will apply only to the periodic record with an effective date that matches the sample date.

Use Prior When Current Is Missing or Inhibited

When the **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** option is enabled, if there is no sample with a sample date matching the batch end date or a periodic record effective date, then the latest sample before the end of batch or periodic record applies. Example There are batches that start at 09:00 every four days and end at the start of the next batch (notated on the calendar in blue) and weekly samples as designated by the table to the right. Assignment options are set to apply sample at the end of batch with only the **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** option enabled. With this configuration, when there is no sample with the sample date matching the batch end date, batches are applied with the prior sample: | Batch | Sample Applied | |--------------------------|----------------| | B1 (4/1 9:00-4/5 9:00) | A (4/1 9:00) | | B2 (4/5 9:00-4/9 9:00) | B (4/8 9:00) | | B3 (4/9 9:00-4/13 9:00) | B (4/8 9:00) | | B4 (4/13 9:00-4/17 9:00) | C (4/15 9:00) | | B5 (4/17 9:00-4/21 9:00) | C (4/15 9:00) | | B6 (4/21 9:00-4/25 9:00) | D (4/22 9:00) | | B7 (4/25 9:00-4/29 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | | B8 (4/29 9:00-5/1 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) |

Apply Back to Prior Sample

When the Apply Back to Prior Sample option is enabled, a sample will apply to the batch or periodic record according to the Apply Sample At option set (End of Batch or Effective Date/Time) and to any previous batch or periodic records, stopping at the sample date of the prior sample. Enabling this option allows for a further condition, Apply Back Within Sample Month, to be applied. This secondary condition limits the application of samples to the month of the sample date. Example #### Example 1 There are batches that start at 09:00 every four days and end at the start of the next batch (notated on the calendar in blue) and weekly samples as designated by the table to the right. The assignment is set to apply sample at End of Batch and only the Apply Back to Prior Sample option enabled. Sample A is not applied to any batches during the month of April, as the earliest batch (B1) has a batch end date of 04/05 09:00 which is later than Sample A’s sample date. Instead, Sample B is applied to this batch as it is the next available sample that can be applied back. The last batch B8 does not have any sample applied as no sample has a sample date that matches or is later than the batch end date. | Batch | Sample Applied | |--------------------------|----------------| | B1 (4/1 9:00-4/5 9:00) | B (4/8 9:00) | | B2 (4/5 9:00-4/9 9:00) | C (4/15 09:00) | | B3 (4/9 9:00-4/13 9:00) | C (4/15 9:00) | | B4 (4/13 9:00-4/17 9:00) | D (4/22 9:00) | | B5 (4/17 9:00-4/21 9:00) | D (4/22 9:00) | | B6 (4/21 9:00-4/25 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | | B7 (4/25 9:00-4/29 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | | B8 (4/29 9:00-5/1 9:00) | \- | #### Example 2 The assignment is set to apply the sample at effective date/time and only the **Apply Back to Prior Sample** option is enabled. With only one periodic record having a corresponding effective date/time to Sample A, the sample is only applied to the periodic record beginning at 04/01 09:00 and ending at 04/01 10:00. The subsequent periodic records have Sample B applied until 04/08 10:00, the first record with an effective date/time that occurs after Sample B’s sample date. Applying sample at effective date/time is best suited to users with a stronger focus on periodic records rather than batch records.

Enabling Both Use Prior and Apply Back

When both the **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** and **Apply Back to Prior Sample** options are enabled, samples that would be applied under Apply Back to Prior Sample have precedence. Example #### Example 1 There are batches that start at 09:00 every four days and end at the start of the next batch (notated on the calendar in blue) and weekly samples as designated by the table to the right. ![](data:image/png;base64,) The assignment is set to apply sample at the end of batch and both **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** and the **Apply Back to Prior Sample** options are enabled. For the batch B1, the Sample B that applies back takes precedence over the sample A that is prior to the batch end date. | Batch | Sample Applied | |--------------------------|----------------| | B1 (4/1 9:00-4/5 9:00) | B (4/8 9:00) | | B2 (4/5 9:00-4/9 9:00) | C (4/15 09:00) | | B3 (4/9 9:00-4/13 9:00) | C (4/15 9:00) | | B4 (4/13 9:00-4/17 9:00) | D (4/22 9:00) | | B5 (4/17 9:00-4/21 9:00) | D (4/22 9:00) | | B6 (4/21 9:00-4/25 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | | B7 (4/25 9:00-4/29 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | | B8 (4/29 9:00-5/1 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | #### Example 2 The assignment is set to apply sample at Effective Date/Time and both Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited and the Apply Back to Prior Sample options are enabled. The periodic record with 04/01 09:00 effective date will be applied with the Sample A since the Sample Date matches. For the next periodic record at 04/01 10:00, there is no sample with a Sample Date matching the effective date. Although Sample A (4/1 09:00) is a prior sample and could be applied, the Apply Back to Prior Sample option has precedence and Sample B (4/8 09:00) is applied back to this periodic record.

Use Prior and Apply Back - With Sample Tolerance

Example There are batches that start at 09:00 every four days and end at the start of the next batch (notated on the calendar in blue) and weekly samples as designated by the table to the right. ![](data:image/png;base64,) Assignment is set to apply sample at the end of batch and both **Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited** and the **Apply Back to Prior Sample** options are enabled. There is a sample tolerance set for 1 day before the end of batch and 1 day after the end of batch. ![](data:image/png;base64,) ![](data:image/png;base64,) The logic for sample application assumes that Apply Back to Prior Sample option has precedence over Use Prior When Current is Missing or Inhibited option. Note that for Batch 5 (4/17 09:00 – 4/22 09:00), there is no sample with a sample date matching the End of Batch date (4/21 09:00). Because of this, sample application would first look for a sample to apply back to this batch. With the Sample Tolerance set to 1 day in either direction, Sample D (4/22 9:00) can be applied. \*end of batch only | Batch | Sample Applied | |--------------------------|----------------| | B1 (4/1 9:00-4/5 9:00) | B (4/8 9:00) | | B2 (4/5 9:00-4/9 9:00) | B (4/8 9:00) | | B3 (4/9 9:00-4/13 9:00) | C (4/15 9:00) | | B4 (4/13 9:00-4/17 9:00) | D (4/22 9:00) | | B5 (4/17 9:00-4/21 9:00) | D (4/22 9:00) | | B6 (4/21 9:00-4/25 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | | B7 (4/25 9:00-4/29 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) | | B8 (4/29 9:00-5/1 9:00) | E (4/29 9:00) |

docs.title: Quality Assignment Editor
docs.text:
The Quality Assignment Editor is used to view, create, and maintain source-to-meter and source-to-location assignments. An assignment causes source analysis data to be applied to the assigned meters and to tickets of assigned locations.

The editor is also used to configure the “Send To” capability that allows meter or location analysis data to be sent to a source. Sending location data is the implementation of a calculated source since the location will be the volume weighted average of its members’ analyses.

To access the Quality Assignment Editor: - Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Quality Assignments**; or - Click the **Quality Assignments** shortcut tile .

Quality Assignment Editor Screen Details

The standard **object selector** allows users to select meters, locations, lists, sources and source lists. - If you select "Meter", existing assignments for the meter will display. - If you select "Location", the following options will display: - **By Meter** - The location will be treated as a list of meters. Only immediate meter members of the location are available. Use the navigation buttons to scroll through the list; the currently selected meter displays in the title bar of the window. Meter assignments are maintained individually. Source assignments can be set for multiple meters using [Bulk Changes](../../Tools/Bulk%20Changes.md). - **By Location** - The location will be treated as a list of locations. The selected location and all locations below it in the hierarchy are available. Use the navigation buttons to scroll through the available locations; the currently selected location displays in the title bar of the window. - If you select "List", the following options will display: - **By Meter** - A scrollable list of all of the list’s member meters and all the meters of each location hierarchy will display. Use the navigation buttons to scroll through the available meters; the currently selected meter displays in the title bar of the window. - **By Location** - The selected location and the locations in the hierarchy will display. Use the navigation buttons to scroll through the available locations; the currently selected location displays in the title bar of the window. - If you select "Source", existing assignments for the source will display. - If you select "Source List", a scrollable list of sources will display. Use the navigation buttons to scroll through the available sources; the currently selected source displays in the title bar of the window. The **assignment grid** displays details about the assignment, including meter, source, and effective dates. The **Send To group box** contains configuration options for sending meter or location data to a source. The **assignment configuration buttons** provide functionality options including creating, editing, or deleting an assignment.

docs.title: Quality Assignment Editor
Send To Functionality Configuration
docs.text:
The Send To functionality provides for the transfer of analysis data from a meter or location to a quality source. This is useful for propagating an analysis to many meters (‘chromatograph zoning’).

Meter Send To

The meter "Send To" configuration is available when the object type is **Meter** or when the **By Meter** radio button is selected. Click the **Edit** button within the "Send To" group box to alter the configuration. - **Feed Raw Data -** When this option is enabled, each periodic analysis record contained in a meter's import file will be sent to the source. This is common when a chromatograph is connected to the flow computer. Subsequent edits of analyses records on the meter will not be sent to the source. When this option is not enabled, the meter’s analysis records will be replicated in the source. This is common when a fixed lab analysis is entered into the flow computer because it prevents redundant periodic records from being sent to the source. Subsequent edits of analyses data on the meter will be sent to the source. Once configured, the meter analyses will be sent to the specified source when data is imported or edited (except as noted in [Configuring Assignments](Configuring%20Assignments.md)). The effective start and end date of the source analysis record will match the meter analysis start and end date. When meter analysis for a gas meter is sent to a source, if the heating value saturation condition is not specified in the meter, then the composition will be used to calculate the Dry, Saturated, and As Delivered heating values. If the heating value saturation is specified, then the heating value from the meter will be applied to the corresponding real heating value in GQ Source and used to calculate the other real heating values. If a gas meter has a heating value saturation condition, then the heating value from the meter will populate that heating value in the source and used to calculate the other two heating values. For example: If the meter has a heating value of 1,010 and a heating value saturation of "Dry", then the GQ source will be given a dry heating value of 1,010, and the "Saturated (Wet)" and "As Delivered" heating values will be calculated from this value; otherwise, the "Dry", "Saturated", and "As Delivered" heating values will be calculated from the composition.

Location Send To

The location "Send To" configuration is available whenever the object type is **Location** or **List** and the **By Location** radio button is selected. Click the **Edit** button within the "Send To" group box to alter the configuration. - **Data Resolution** - The data resolution of the records to be sent to the source. Options are **Monthly**, **Daily**, and **Hourly**. - **Include End Date** - The option allows users to decide whether the monthly analysis being sent to the source ends at the end of the month or extends to the end of time. Hourly and daily resolutions always include the end date. This option is only available when the "send to" source is a gas quality source and the data resolution is monthly. Once configured, the location analyses will be sent to the specified source when the location is rolled up and is flagged as "Complete" (except as noted in [Configuring Assignments](Configuring%20Assignments.md)). The effective date of the sent records will be set as the effective date and sample date of the source records.

docs.title: About Sources
docs.text:
Sources represent flowing product composition at strategic points in a pipeline. Product samples may be drawn into a sample cylinder for local or lab analysis, or continuously drawn and analyzed by an online chromatograph. In FLOWCAL, these types of sources are called "sample analysis" and "chromatograph" sources.

In FLOWCAL Gas, an online chromatograph may be connected to the EFM, which will perform weighted averaging of the analyses. This is called "RTU average".

docs.title: Source Types
docs.text:
Sample Analysis

Sample analyses, or samples, are drawn locally either on a periodic "spot" basis or on a continuous "composite" basis. Sample frequencies typically range from monthly to annual.

Chromatograph

Online chromatographs are connected to the pipeline and continuously flow a small amount of product through a transfer line. The transfer line may either vent to atmosphere or be returned to a low pressure section of the pipeline. The chromatograph draws a sample from transfer line and analyzes it, which usually takes 2 to 6 minutes. The chromatograph controller will usually create hourly averages of components and properties from the individual analyses.

RTU Average (Gas Quality Only)

"RTU average" is a FLOWCAL-specific term that describes an online chromatograph (or other device) connected to the flow computer. RTU averages differ from chromatographs in two key ways. First, the flow computer will create weighted averages (based on flow rate or flow time), whereas the chromatograph can only create simple averages. Second, depending on the equipment in use, the analysis of an RTU average may be incomplete. Properties such as relative density and heating value, and components such as CO2 and N2, may be the only available variables.

docs.title: Create & Delete Sources
docs.text:
Gas or liquid sources can be created in FLOWCAL manually or automatically via file imports. Following a new implementation of FLOWCAL, merger, or other type of data acquisition, many sources may need to be created in bulk. Other times, analysts may need to create a handful of sources periodically.

This feature requires the Source Analysis module.

Manually Creating Sources

In FLOWCAL, you can manually create sources from the Quality Source Editor screen. To create a **gas** quality source: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Gas Quality** and click the **New** button, or go to **File** \> **New** from the Gas Quality Source Editor menu. 2. Populate required data fields (highlighted in green). These fields must be populated before you can save the source record. By default, the only required field to save a new gas quality source is Source Number and Reason. Additional fields may be required based on how FLOWCAL options are configured. 1. Enter any additional source information and click **Save**. To create a **liquid** quality source: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Liquid Quality** and click the **New** button, or go to **File** \> **New** from the Liquid Quality Source Editor menu. 2. Populate required data fields (highlighted in green). These fields must be populated before you can save the source record. By default, the only required field to save a new gas quality source is Source Number and Reason. Additional fields may be required based on how FLOWCAL options are configured. 1. Enter any additional source information and click **Save**.

Automatically Creating Sources

The “Auto Create Sources” options allow you to automatically create sources during data import using Quorum’s proprietary source text file format or Transaction Queue. These options must be configured under the Service Configuration screen. - **Text Files** - When the “Auto Create” option for Sources is enabled, sources imported by text file using the Import \> Source Analysis Text File screen will be created automatically if they do not already exist. (See: [Import Source Analysis Text File](../Imports/Import%20Source%20Analysis%20Text%20File.md)) You can also use the File Import service to automatically import source text files and create sources. - **TESTit Integrated** - Sources can also be created automatically using TESTit Integrated. This feature requires TESTit Integrated. - **T3** - This feature is not supported with TESTit V3 Integrated. - **T2** - When you set the Update column to Create for GQSource on the Data Map Editor, sources will be created automatically when test reports are imported.

Bulk Creating Sources

A new FLOWCAL implementation or data acquisition can require the creation of hundreds or thousands of sources. The FcLoader utility is available for creating sources in bulk. FcLoader ships with FLOWCAL and is located in the installation folder. A signed non-disclosure agreement (NDA) must be on file to receive the source text file, FcLoader, and Transaction Queue file formats. Contact Customer Support to obtain the appropriate NDA.

Copying Sources

You can also create a source by making a copy of an existing source. Users will often create a set of default sources to use as the basis for new sources, so that certain settings or custom fields are automatically specified in the new source. You can copy an existing source through the Gas or Liquid Quality Source Editor. To copy a source from the Gas or Liquid Quality Source Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Gas Quality** or **Liquid Quality** and click **New**. 2. Click the **Copy** button and select the source to copy from the list. 3. Enter a source number and name. 4. Make any required edits and click **Save**.

Deleting Sources

Sources can only be deleted from the Quality Source Editor. Deleting a source requires the “Quality Source Edit – Can Delete” privilege. To delete a source: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Gas Quality** or **Liquid Quality**, and select a source to delete using the Source drop-down. 2. Click the **Delete** button. 3. When prompted, confirm the deletion. When a source is deleted, FLOWCAL will generate a message logging the deletion (available in the Message Viewer).

docs.title: Edit Source Data
docs.text: Once a source has been created in FLOWCAL, you can make edits to the general source information or other data, such as the source analysis.

docs.title: General Information
docs.text:
General source information, such as custom fields, validations, and other options, can be edited from the Quality Source Editor.

You can make the same edit across several sources from the Bulk Changes screen.

To edit a source from the Quality Source Editor: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Source Analysis** \> **Gas Quality** or **Liquid Quality** and select a source using the Source drop-down. 2. Click the **Edit** button. 3. Populate required fields (highlighted in green). These fields must be populated before you can save your changes. By default, Source Number and Reason are required fields; however, additional fields may be required based on how FLOWCAL options are configured. 1. Enter any additional source information and click **Save**.

docs.text: Source data can be edited in the Quality Source Editor by selecting the Source Analysis tab and clicking the New Detail button.

docs.title: Import Source Data
docs.text: Several options are available for importing quality source data, varying based on data type and import format.

docs.title: General Data
docs.text:
General source attributes, characteristics, and validations as seen in the Quality Source Editor can be populated using the following methods:

  • Manual entry through the Quality Source Editor
  • Bulk edits through the Bulk Changes screen
  • Bulk imports using the FcLoader utility

docs.title: Source Analysis Data
docs.text:
Source analysis can be imported using the following methods:

  • Manual or automatic file imports (such as source text files or imported with meter data)
  • Manual data entry
  • Transaction Queue import

docs.title: Manual File Imports
docs.text:
• Source Text Files - When a lab supplies analysis data in Quroum’s Source Text File format, the files can be manually imported from the Import > Source Analysis Text File menu. Once imported, the data is applied to all assigned meters. (See: Import Source Analysis Text File)

  • Import with Meter Data - When analysis data is supplied with the meter data, such as in a CFX file, the meter/source assignment can be configured to send the analysis from the meter to the source where it can then be applied to other assigned meters.

Most files imported into FLOWCAL are in Quorum’s proprietary file format. A signed non-disclosure agreement (NDA) must be on file to receive these file formats. Contact Customer Support to obtain the appropriate NDA.

docs.title: Automatic File Imports
docs.text: The File Import service is a Windows service that can be installed on the application server where FLOWCAL is installed. The service automatically processes import files based on the file path specified within FLOWCAL. The service can be used to import different file types, such as source analysis text files and CFX files.

docs.title: Manual Data Entry
docs.text: Source data can be entered manually in the Quality Source Editor by selecting the Source Analysis tab and clicking the New Detail button.

docs.title: Transaction Queue
docs.text:
Transaction Queue provides an alternative to file imports and can be used to import online chromatograph data into FLOWCAL on a near real-time basis. The data is written to the database from SCADA or other intermediate solution. The Transaction Queue service monitors the Transaction Queue tables and imports the data into the appropriate source. The source data is then queued to be applied to all assigned meters.

Contact Customer Support for additional information about Transaction Queue.

This feature requires the Online Transaction Processing module.

docs.title: View Source Data
docs.text: Once a source has been created in FLOWCAL, you can view general information about the source or other source data, such as analysis.

docs.title: General Information
docs.text: General source information, such as custom fields, validations and other options, are viewable from the Quality Source Editor.

docs.title: Source Analysis
docs.text: Source analysis records can be viewed and edited from the Quality Source Editor. When enabled, this data is rolled up into hourly, daily, and monthly records, which can then be seen from the Source Analysis Rollups Viewer. This rolled data is primarily used for reporting externally and internally to other departments and downstream systems.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
You can enter a sample Mole % or Mass %, and then have FLOWCAL calculate the other properties for the sample such as densities in different units, component Mass %, etc. All calculations are done according to the configuration in the Characteristics 1 tab for C6+/C7+ fixed ratio splits or Extended Characteristics. If set up accordingly, GPMs can be calculated using GPA 2172.

Calculations occur on import and edit and are saved only if the current values are missing or were previously calculated. If hand keying gas quality data, you must click the Calculate button.

docs.title: Tank Editor - Tools
docs.text:
<< Back to Tank Editor

The following options are available on the Tank Editor Tools menu:

Contact Selections

Users can assign contacts to tanks, similarly to meters, locations, and quality sources. Assigning contacts to tanks allows for notifications based on messages and exceptions. Typically, these will be generated when importing TFX files with gauge tickets and tank run tickets.

Ticket Validations

This option allows users to attach validation templates to a tank to validate attached tickets. See [Ticket Validations](../Locations/Location%20Editor/Tools%20-%20Ticket%20Validations.md) for additional information.

Info

The Info screen contains the following items: - **Fluid Phase** - The fluid phase of a tank is always "Liquid". - **Requires Close Approval** - Tanks that require close approval have to satisfy a set of conditions before they can be closed, and are closed manually in Location Close Approval. - **Weekly Schedule** - This drop-down will list schedules created using the [Annual Schedule Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Application/Annual%20Schedule%20Editor.md). Location rollups will calculate totals for the tank according to the date spans defined by the schedule selected here. **Tip:** Checking the Calculate Weekly Totals option in System Configuration will make the Weekly Schedule option visible for the locations, tanks, and caverns in that system. - **Ticket Import** - Ticket import options are used to enable adjustment of ticket dates for daylight savings time or for time zone. When these options are enabled, dates on all tickets that are imported into the location via TFX or FLOWCAL text file format are adjusted. (See: [Date and Time Adjustments During Import](../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Date%20and%20Time%20Adjustments%20During%20Import.md)) - **Time Zone Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times are adjusted by the offset amount defined for the selected time zone. (Time zones are created using the [Time Zone Editor](../Settings%20Manager/Geographic/Time%20Zone%20Editor.md).) For these purposes the time zone offset is to be user-configured based on the offset from the company's standard business time zone rather than offsets from UTC. - **DST Shift** - When enabled, all dates and times occurring during daylight saving time are shifted forward one hour. All dates and times that occur outside of daylight saving time are imported. - **Time Zone** - This read-only field displays the current time zone of the location.

Product Conversion

Product conversion tickets can be entered if the contents of a tank need to be converted from one product to another. When entering a Product Conversion ticket, only products that have been set up in the Product Editor with a product to be converted to can be converted. Only products that have a non-zero inventory in the tank at the effective date of the conversion ticket can be selected. To generate a product conversion ticket: Go to **Tools** \> **Product Conversion** in the Tank Editor. When creating a ticket from this screen, the location field will be locked to the selected tank.

Tank Empty

If a tank is empty, but due to measurement inaccuracies, FLOWCAL does not have the tank inventory at zero, an Inventory Empty ticket can be created. When this is done, a ticket will be assigned to the tank that backs out any volume in the tank. If the calculated volume in the tank is negative, then the direction of the ticket will be adjusted to account for this. To generate an inventory empty ticket: Go to **Tools** \> **Tank Empty** in the Tank Editor. The Inventory Empty screen will display, requesting date information and advanced empty settings. After initializing and confirming the empty, an inventory empty ticket will be generated and the tank's inventory level will be zeroed out at the specified time.

Capacity Table

A capacity table (strapping table, calibration table) is generated by the company that performs the field determination of how much volume a tank holds at specified tank levels. A capacity table in FLOWCAL consists of datetime effective settings for tank dimensions and calculation specifics, such as level resolution and floating roof weight, and the volume/level information. FLOWCAL capacity tables are identified by name and a tank may have more than one capacity table. Each named capacity table is a distinct set of the date effective data described above. Some example reasons for having multiple capacity tables on a tank include separate tables for high leg and low leg roof configurations, and alternate tables that depend on product density. Once the tank has been created, one or more named capacity tables can be added using the Capacity Table editor or the Capacity Table import. ##### Capacity Table Editor If the tank does not already have a capacity table, the capacity table editor will open in “New Table” mode; otherwise, the user will be able to edit an existing capacity table or create a new one. The **New** button in the Capacity Table Editor includes a drop-down menu with the following options: - **Table** - Creates a new named table. This operation is used to create an alternate capacity table with its own set of setup and volume/level information. - **Data** - Data creates new set of date effective data for the currently selected named table. This operation is used to add new tank calibration data or to alter the table setup information. To create a new named capacity table: 1. Launch the Tank Editor and go to **Tools** \> **Capacity Table**. 2. Select **Table** from the **New** button drop-down. To create a new data effective data set on an existing named capacity table: 1. Launch the Tank Editor and go to **Tools** \> **Capacity Table**. 2. Select the desired capacity table (field 1). 3. Select **Data** from the **New** button drop-down. To edit an existing date effective data set: 1. Launch the Tank Editor and go to **Tools** \> **Capacity Table**. 2. Select the desired capacity table (field 1). 3. Select the desired effective date (field 2). ##### Capacity Table Setup Tab 1. If in new mode, set the start and end dates. 2. Set the reference temperature. The units are based on the temperature units for the tank set in [Tank Units & Options](Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Units-Options%20Tab.md). 3. Indicate if a shell temperature correction (CTSh) needs to be applied. 4. Indicate if the CTSh is built into the capacity table. 5. If the tank has a floating roof (upright cylindrical tanks only): 1. Enter a value for the leg height at the time of calibration. An exception will be written when the innage or outage level is below leg height. 2. Enter the data for the floating roof adjustment (FRA). Different options are available depending on whether the FRA Built Into Table option is enabled. FRA/FRC will not apply to the tank volume if the product level is below the configured tank leg height. 6. If Enable Vapor Space Calculations is selected, the vapor space will be evaluated for corresponding tickets, and entering values into dead space will account for the dead space of the tank when evaluating the total vapor present in the tank. The required fields in the Capacity Table editor are highlighted in green. You will not be allowed to save until all required fields are populated. These fields will vary based on tank type. 7. Select whether the capacity table to be entered is Innage or Outage. Innage measurement is relative to the bottom of the tank. Outage (aka Ullage) measurement is relative to a level at the top of the tank. 8. Select how the data for the capacity table will be entered. If the capacity table to be entered has the tank volume at each level, select Volume and Level. If the capacity table to be entered has the volume for each increment in each section along with the number of increments in the section, select Increments per Zone/Volume per Increment. If the user chooses Increments per Zone/Volume per Increment, FLOWCAL will calculate the volume at each level when the capacity table is saved. The user can also switch between Table Entry Type options while entering the capacity table, but FLOWCAL will set the increments per zone to one and recalculate the volume per zone when the option Volume and Level is selected. 9. Select **Table Resolution Entry**. This impacts data entry on the capacity table Data tab and entry of open, close, and gauge levels on tickets. Options vary based on the level units set on the tank: - **Feet** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet - **Inches** - Enter capacity table values as whole inches - **1/2 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–11/2 inches - **1/4 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–31/4 inches - **1/8 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–71/8 inches - **1/16 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–151/16 inches - **1/32 inch** - Enter capacity table values as whole feet, whole inches and 0–311/32 inches - **0.1 Foot** - Enter capacity table values as tenths of a foot; ex.: 10.1 - **0.01 Foot** - Enter capacity table values as hundredths of a foot; ex.: 10.13 10. Click the **Save** button. ##### Capacity Table Data Tab To add capacity table data: 1. Right-click on an existing row and choose **Insert Row Above** or **Insert Row Below**. A row will be added. 2. Enter data for each cell. 3. Click **Save**. 4. To delete a row from the grid, right-click on an existing row and choose **Delete Row**. The highlighted row will be removed.

docs.title: Tank Editor
docs.text:
This feature requires the Liquids Inventory module.

FLOWCAL supports the creation of upright cylindrical, horizontal, and spherical tanks, as well as editing tank characteristics and tank data in the Tank Editor. Capacity (strapping) tables can be manually entered or imported from a text file so that FLOWCAL can perform volume calculations based on reported levels. The tank inventory can be calculated and tracked based on meter measurement into and out of the tank, tank gauges and tank run tickets.

One of the most important pieces of liquids measurement is calculating and validating tank volumes for tank gauges and tank movements. This in turn allows for accurate GainLoss calculation as these tanks can be used in balance locations and calculating inventory.

docs.title: BLM Tab
docs.text:
The BLM tab contains BLM-specific data points. The options on this tab determine how FLOWCAL handles verifications and reports generated for this tank.

To enable to BLM data points, set the BLM Property identifier to "Yes". The following items will then be available on the BLM tab:

  • FMP Number* - A BLM-approved facility measurement point (FMP) where oil or gas produced from a Federal or Indian lease, unit PA, or CA is measured and the measurement affects the calculation of the volume or quality of production on which royalty is owed; required field if BLM Property identifier is set to "Yes"

  • Lease Number* - The number assigned to the lease location where the production occurs

  • CA Number* - Communitization agreement (CA) number identifying an agreement to combine a lease or a portion of a lease with other tracts for purposes of cooperative development and operations, when the initial lease cannot be independently developed and operated in accordance with established well spacing or well development programs

  • PA Number - Participating area (PA) number representing a combined portion of the unitized area that BLM determines to be reasonably proven to produce geothermal resources or that supports production in commercial quantities, such as pressure support from injection wells; the size and configuration of all participating areas and revisions are not effective until BLM approves them

  • FMP Tier* - A volume rate designation for this tank; higher volume rates have more stringent operating requirements

Designations for tanks are as follows:

  • High Volume: ≥ 30,000 bbl/month (default selection)
  • Low Volume: \< 30,000 bbl/month

The averaging period refers to the previous 12 months or the life of the tank, whichever is shorter. For FMPs that measure production from a newly drilled well, the averaging period excludes production from that well that occurred in or before the first full month of production.

* FMP Number, Lease Number, CA Number, and FMP Tier are shown on select reports designed specifically for BLM reporting requirements.

docs.title: Tank Editor - Configuration
docs.text: << Back | Main | Characteristics | Units & Options | Site | BLM

docs.title: Characteristics Tab
docs.text:
The options on this tab are date effective based on the From and To dates shown.

The following options are available on the Characteristics tab:

  • Status - Set to Active, Inactive, Long-Term Monitoring, or Plugged and Abandoned. The status is datetime effective. If the status is anything other than Active and location rollups calculates a change in inventory, an exception (20006 INV – Total changed when inventory was not active) will be generated to alert the user.
  • Capacity Table - Indicates the active capacity table for this tank. New tickets will default to using this table for calculations.
  • Data Entry Mode - Applies to Tank Run Tickets. Specify whether to enter open and close values for only tank levels (common for movements on field production tanks), or for all data points.
  • Volume Calc Method - Specifies the calculation sequence used for each tank type
  • Component Calc Method - Three options available
  • Net Mass - Net mass and mass fraction are used to calculate component mass which is then converted to component volume using component densities.
  • Net Standard Volume - Net Standard Volume and liquid volume fraction are used to calculate component volume.
  • Follow Product - If the product is a purity product then FLOWCAL will calculate components using Net Standard Volume and liquid volume fraction. If the product is not a purity product then FLOWCAL will use net mass and mass fraction to calculate components.
  • Run Ticket Span - Determines how run tickets are treated during the rollup process. This option ensures that run tickets are rolled into the desired hour, day and month.
  • Time Leads - The run ticket's effective date represents the start time of the run (example: A run ticket movement effective 4/01/2021 @7:00 (contract hour = 7) will be rolled into the measurement day 4/01/2021)
  • Time Trails - The run ticket's effective date represents the end time of the run (example: A run ticket movement effective 4/01/2021 @7:00 (contract hour = 7) will be rolled into the measurement day 3/31/2021)

docs.title: Tank Editor - Configuration
docs.text: << Back | Main | Characteristics | Units & Options | Site | BLM

docs.title: Main Tab
docs.text:
The following options are available on the Main tab:

  • Tank Type - Options for this field are Production Tank (upright cylindrical), Product Tank (upright cylindrical), Horizontal Tank, or Spherical Tank.
  • Roof Type - If the tank type is specified as either "Production Tank" or "Product Tank", a Roof Type field will become available. Options for this field are "Fixed Roof", "Floating Roof", or "No Roof".
  • Construction Material - The construction material is used when calculating the liquid and vapor temperature corrections of the tank.
  • Tank is Insulated - If the tank is insulated, the tank shell temperature correction (CTSh) will be calculated using only the liquid temperature. If the tank is not insulated, the CTSh will be calculated using the liquid temperature and the ambient temperature as per API.
  • Nominal Tank Capacity - This is the maximum capacity of the tank. For reference only; it is not used in any calculation
  • Reference Meter - A reference meter is required upon creation of a new tank. The contract day and hour from the reference meter will be used to calculate the rollup IDs for the tank tickets.
  • Injection Point - A previously defined station location in FLOWCAL that will act as the inlet to the tank. Optional.
  • Withdrawal Point - A previously defined station location in FLOWCAL that will act as the outlet to the tank. Optional.

docs.title: Tank Editor - Configuration
docs.text: << Back | Main | Characteristics | Units & Options | Site | BLM

docs.title: Site Tab
docs.text:
The Site tab contains the legal description and information about the location of the tank.

The following data fields are available on the Site tab:

  • City - Indicates the city the tank is located in; up to 20 characters.
  • County - The county the tank is located in; drop-down options are defined in the County Editor.
  • State - The state the tank is located in; drop-down options are defined in the State Editor.
  • Country - The country the tank is located in; drop-down options are defined in the Country Editor.
  • Time Zone - The time zone of the tank location; drop-down options are defined in the Time Zone Editor.
  • Section - The basic unit of a township and range; each section refers to an area of a square mile; up to three characters.

  • Quarter - Each section is divided into quarter sections, which are each further divided into quarter sections, for a total of 16 parts per section; up to 25 characters. **For example:** "NW 1/4 of the SE 1/4" would refer to the most northwestern quarter of the southeastern quarter.

  • Township - A measure of the distance north or south from the baseline, six miles in length; up to four characters.

  • Range - A measure of the distance east or west from the principal meridian, six miles in length; up to four characters.
  • Meridian - A geographical north to south reference point; up to 25 characters.
  • Latitude - A geographic coordinate specifying a north-south location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Equator; up to 12 characters.
  • Longitude - A geographic coordinate specifying an east-west location on the Earth’s surface, measured from the Prime Meridian; up to 12 characters.
  • Valid Products - If enabled, valid products allow for the validation of the product on all incoming tickets or flow data from injection and withdrawal points. It also limits the products that a user may choose from when manually entering a ticket. By setting a product as the Default, when a ticket is manually entered on a tank, the ticket will be initialized to have this product.

docs.title: Tank Editor - Configuration
docs.text: << Back | Main | Characteristics | Units & Options | Site | BLM

docs.title: Units & Options Tab
docs.text:
The following options are available on the Units & Options tab:

Tank Units

Units of measure for tanks are defined on the Units & Options tab of the Tank Editor. The units apply to all tank tickets. Available unit options are:

  • Tank Level
  • Density
  • Pressure
  • Temperature
  • Volume
  • Mass

The tank level units are dependent on values that will be imported from TFX files. If the TFX files have levels measured in feet, the level units must be set to feet in the Tank Editor.

Manual Entry

Use Prior Ticket Values (Yes/No) - When manually creating a gauge or run ticket, this option will cause the fields in the table below to be pre-populated in the new ticket with values from the most recent prior ticket. The most recent prior ticket may be a gauge or a run ticket and is determined as the latter of the gauge ticket effective date, the run ticket effective date, and the run ticket movement end date.

Fields populated with prior values:

Gauge Ticket Run Ticket Product Product Observed Density Open Observed Density Observed Temperature Open Observed Temperature Observed Pressure Open Observed Pressure Liquid Temperature Open Liquid Temperature Tank Pressure Open Tank Pressure

Run Splitting

  • Split Run Tickets on Import/Edit (Yes/No) - If enabled, this option will cause a run ticket to be split at the contract hour if the following conditions are true:
  • The run ticket spans a gauge ticket; and

  • The gauge ticket is effective at the contract hour (or within a tolerance limit, as described below).

  • Populate New Ticket with (Gauge Values/Run Values) - When a run ticket is split by this process, the closing values of the first split piece and the open values of the second split piece must be filled with data. This option determines the source of that data. The data will be taken from either the gauge ticket that was encompassed by the run ticket or from the run ticket’s open values.

Levels are always taken from the gauge ticket.

The choice between using the gauge ticket’s or the run ticket’s data is a matter of completeness. Throughout the month, the available daily gauges may be in complete as to recording or collecting data required for a run ticket. For example: It may be that an observed density is not recorded. In those cases, it is better to use the run ticket information, which is more likely to be complete.

In either case, a month-end gauge ticket will always be used for a split record.

  • Contract Hour Tolerance - This value (in seconds) is used to determine if a gauge ticket with an effective date near the contract hour can be used for the run splitting process. A gauge within plus or minus this number of seconds will be considered as the contract hour gauge reading and will be used.

docs.text: The Daily tab displays daily movement data.

docs.title: Gauging Tab
docs.text:
The Gauging tab displays the gauge levels associated with gauge tickets or run tickets currently attached to the tank for the specified time period. Double-click record to open the associated ticket for viewing or editing.

Gauge tickets can be created and deleted from the Gauging tab.

To enter a gauge ticket: 1. Navigate to the Tank Editor and select a tank. 2. Click the **Gauging** tab 3. Right-click the grid and select **New Tank Level**. 4. Navigate to the Ticket Editor and select **Tank Gauge**. 5. Right-click the grid and select **New Ticket**. 6. Navigate to the **Ticket Search**. 7. Right-click the grid and select **New Ticket** \> **Tank Gauge**. 8. Edit the date as appropriate. 9. Select the product from the list. If the tank has been set up with a list of valid products, only those will appear in the drop-down. If a default product was specified, it will be pre-selected in the drop-down. 10. Enter tank gauging information. Data points are different for each tank type. Upright Cylindrical Tank Gauge Tickets If a CTSh is to be calculated, ambient temperature is required, and the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Apply Shell Temperature Correction, CTSh’ enabled. If the option to calculate CTSh is not enabled, or FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CTSh, then a value of one is assumed. S&W % is not required. If S&W % is not specified, zero is assumed. Free Water is not required. If Free Water is not specified, zero is assumed. If CTSh, FRA, or CTL is provided on import, these values will be stored into revision 0, but the calculations will use the FLOWCAL calculated CTSh, FRA, or CTL; however, if a user manually enters CTSh, FRA, or CTL, then FLOWCAL will use the manually entered values in the calculations. Horizontal Tank Gauge Tickets If a Correction for Shell Temperature is to be calculated, the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Use Steel Temperature Correction (CTS) for Calculations’ enabled. If the option to calculate CTS is not enabled, or FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CTS, then a value of one is assumed. If CTS or CTL is provided on import, these values will be stored into revision 0, but the calculations will use the FLOWCAL calculated CTS or CTL; however, if a user manually enters CTS or CTL, then FLOWCAL will use the manually entered values in the calculations. In order to calculate Vapor Density, observed density, observed temperature, and analysis are needed. Spherical Tank Gauge Tickets If a CTS liquid/CTS vapor is to be calculated, tank construction material and liquid/vapor temperature are needed, and the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Use Steel Temperature Correction (CTS) for Calculations’ enabled. If the option to use CTS is not enabled, then a value of one is assumed. If the option to use CTS is enabled and FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CTS, CTS is not calculated. If a CPS is to be calculated, tank construction material, thickness of tank shell, and tank pressure are needed, and the Capacity Table must have the option ‘Use Steel Pressure Correction (CPS) for Calculations’ enabled. If the option to use CPS is not enabled, then a value of one is assumed. If the option to use CTS is enabled and FLOWCAL does not have the data needed to calculate CPS, CPS is not calculated. Spherical tank does not support sediment and water. Even if S&W% is provided on analysis, 0% sediment and water is assumed for calculation. In order to calculate Vapor Density, observed density, observed temperature, observed pressure, and analysis are needed. If CTS liquid, CTS vapor, or CTL is provided on import, these values will be stored into revision 0, but the calculations will use the FLOWCAL calculated CTS liquid, CTS vapor, or CTL; however, if a user manually enters CTS liquid, CTS vapor, or CTL, then FLOWCAL will use the manually entered values in the calculations. 11. Click **Calculate** to see the results. 12. Enter data on the **Accounting**, **Analysis**, **Components**, and **Custom Fields** tabs as needed. 13. Select an edit reason. 14. Click **Save**. Data will calculate and save to the database. 15. Click **Exit**.

docs.title: Tank Editor - Flow Data
