docs.title: Tickets Tab
docs.text:
The Tickets tab displays movement associated with run tickets. Double-click record to open the associated ticket for viewing or editing.

Run tickets can be created and deleted directly from the Tickets tab.

To enter a run ticket: 1. Open the Ticket Detail form for a run ticket. Three options are available: - Navigate to the Tank Editor and select a tank. Click the **Tickets** tab, right-click the grid, and select **New Tank Level**. - Navigate to the Ticket Editor and select **Tank Gauge**. Right-click the grid, and select **New Ticket**. - Navigate to the Ticket Search. Right-click the grid, and select **New Ticket** \> **Tank Run**. 2. Edit the date as needed. The ticket will follow tank characteristics for the time span that contains the effective date of the ticket. This will determine the status, component calculation, and data entry mode. (See: [Tank Characteristics](../Configuration/Tank%20Editor_Config%20-%20Characteristics%20Tab.md)) 3. Define the inventory movement time frame using the **Movement Start Date** and **Movement End Date** fields. 4. Select a product from the list. If the tank has been set up with a list of valid products, only those will appear in the drop-down. If a default product was specified, it will be pre-selected. 5. Click the browse buttons next to the **Direction** and **Class** fields to select these values. 6. Enter appropriate tank run information. Data points will differ for each tank type. The data to be entered and the calculation methods will vary based on the data entry mode for the tank. Open and Close Values for Level Only The Open Level and Close Level values specify the depth of the fluid within the tank at the start and end of the movement, respectively. Both need to be provided for the movement volume and mass to be calculated. Values required for each calculation step are identical to those required for the tank gauge ticket for each respective tank type. For details, see Entering Gauge Tickets. Upright Cylindrical Tank Run Tickets Horizontal Tank Run Tickets Open and Close Values for All Levels The Open and Close set of values specify conditions and quantities of the fluid in the tank at the start and end of the movement, respectively. Open level and open parameters need to be provided for the open volume and mass to be calculated. Close level and close parameters need to be provided for the close volume and mass to be calculated. Delta volume and mass are calculated when both corresponding open and close values are available. - **Required values for calculation** - Values required for each calculation step in the open set and close set are identical to those required for the tank gauge ticket for each respective tank type. For details, see Entering Gauge Tickets. - **Extended detail form** - Given the large number of data points that are involved in the complete calculation of open, close and delta set of quantities, the run ticket form only displays the minimal set of required values for calculation. The extended detail form can be used to view, edit, and calculate the complete set of values for the given tank type. Upright Cylindrical Tank Run Tickets Click the **Extended Detail** button at the bottom to open the extended detail form. If the ticket detail is in view mode, the extended detail will open in view mode where data can only be viewed. If the ticket detail is in edit mode, the extended detail will open in edit mode. The user will be able to edit data and use calculate button to trigger calculation and check results in detail. Edits made in the ticket detail or in the extended detail are synched to the other form. Horizontal Tank Run Tickets Click the **Extended Detail** button at the bottom to open the extended detail form. If the ticket detail is in view mode, the extended detail will open in view mode where data can only be viewed. If the ticket detail is in edit mode, the extended detail will open in edit mode. The user will be able to edit data and use calculate button to trigger calculation and check results in detail. Edits made in the ticket detail or in the extended detail are synched to the other form. Spherical Tank Run Tickets For spherical tank run tickets, observed and measurement conditions for both the start and end of the movement are also to be entered in separate open and close fields. The open conditions are needed to calculate the volume at the open of the movement, and the close conditions are needed to calculate the volume at the end of the movement. All fields on the run ticket detail need to be populated to calculate the Total NSV and Total Mass of the movement. If FLOWCAL does not have data needed to calculate either the open or the close volume amount, FLOWCAL will not be able to calculate the NSV and mass of the movement displayed in the run ticket detail. Not all data points are displayed and editable. More data points for a spherical tank run ticket can be viewed in the Ticket Editor or the Ticket Search grids. 7. Click **Calculate** to see the results. 8. Enter data on the **Accounting**, **Analysis**, **Components**, and **Custom Fields** tabs as needed. 9. Click the browse button to select a value for the **Direction** field. 10. Click the browse button to select a value for the **Class** field. 11. Select an edit reason. 12. Click **Save**. 13. When the data is complete, click **Exit**.

docs.title: Gas Loss Tickets
docs.text:
The Gas Loss Ticket Viewer is used for viewing and creating Gas Loss ticket data. Gas loss tickets are used to account for unmeasured gas volumes such as from the blowdown of a line. You can view and edit Gas Loss tickets in the Gas Loss Ticket Editor as well as Ticket Search.

To access the Gas Loss Ticket Viewer and view Gas Loss tickets: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Tickets** \> **Gas Loss Tickets**. 2. Specify a date range and click **Refresh**. All saved Gas Loss tickets will display. 3. Double-click a ticket entry to view the ticket details.

Add a Gas Loss Ticket

To create a Gas Loss ticket: 1. Refresh the Gas Loss Ticket Viewer. 2. Right-click anywhere on the grid and select **New Ticket**. 3. Enter the date and time for the ticket. This will dictate when it is included in balances as well as what month it is in for month end closing.. 4. Select a ticket type from the **Type** drop-down menu. 5. Depending on the type that you select, you must select a mainline, a mainline and a lateral, or a mainline and a compressor. These must be created in the Pipeline Editor before the Gas Loss ticket is created. 6. Select a meter class (required if the [Subtotal by Meter Class option](../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#SubtotalClass) is enabled). A default value for this data point be configured on the [FLOWCAL Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md) screen. All gas loss tickets are assigned with a direction as specified in [FLOWCAL Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#GasLossTicket). 7. Select a calculation method. Available options are: - **Manual** – This is the default calculation method. When this option is selected, you must enter an actual volume. The volume must be at base conditions as no calculations are done on the volume. - **Blowdown** – When this option is selected, the actual volume will be populated from the selected mainline, lateral, or compressor, depending on the ticket type. You will then need to enter the pressure and temperature of the gas at the start and end of the blowdown, whether the pressure measurement is gauge or absolute, and the atmospheric pressure for gauge measurements. From this, FLOWCAL will calculate the amount of gas loss at base conditions. - **Pinched Valve** – When this option is selected, you must specify the valve information, starting and ending pressure, elapsed time for the valve to be open, whether the pressure measurement is gauge or absolute, and the atmospheric pressure for gauge measurements. From this, FLOWCAL will calculate the amount of gas loss at base conditions. If a gas quality source for the Gas Loss ticket is selected at the bottom of the Gas Loss Ticket Editor, and it has a sample that encompasses the Gas Loss ticket, it will be used to calculate the energy; otherwise, you must manually enter an energy value or leave the Energy field blank. Analysis information can be viewed on the Analyses tab. Once the ticket is saved, the calculation method cannot be changed. 8. Location will be set based on the setup of the selected mainline, lateral, or compressor. This dictates what balance the gas loss ticket will go into, if any. Users may override this. 9. Select an edit reason from the drop-down menu and click **Save**. 10. Click **Edit** to make revisions to the data at any time. The location rollup process totals the appropriate values associated with gas loss tickets. The source analysis apply routine implements a gas quality source for a gas loss ticket upon saving the gas loss ticket. If the calculation method is "Blowdown", the calculated volume is based on the compressibility values determined using the applied gas quality Z method. Calculated energy is based on the applied gas quality dry heating value.

Add a Ticket Note

If a ticket includes a note, note icon next to the ticket will be yellow. The icon will be gray if no note is attached. Right-click the note icon to access options for viewing or adding notes.

Close a Ticket

To close a Gas Loss ticket in the Gas Loss Ticket Editor: 1. Refresh the Gas Loss Ticket Viewer. 2. Select one or more Gas Loss tickets. Exceptions on each ticket must have been acknowledged or resolved before the ticket can be closed. 3. Right click on the grid and select **Close Ticket**. Once a ticket has been closed, the closed values display on the Close Data tab.

docs.title: Ticket Autofill Editor
docs.text:
Users can specify default values for each field by ticket type (excluding Product Conversion, Inventory Empty, Batch Meter, and Custom Ticket types). Users can also specify autofill criteria or default options for each field on tickets on the Flow Data (Main), Accounting, Units, Custom Fields, Configuration, and Analysis tabs. Multiple autofill profiles can be created, and a default profile can be set for a specific ticket type.

If a profile is set as the default, then each ticket created of the same ticket type will automatically be populated with the values specified on the Autofill profile.

To access the Ticket Autofill Editor and create a new autofill profile: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Ticket Autofill Editor**. 2. Click **New**. 3. Enter the name of the profile. 4. Select a ticket type and group. 5. Populate the fields with values that will be automatically filled upon ticket creation. 6. Check **Set As Ticket Type Default** if the profile will be the default profile. 7. Click **Save**.

docs.title: Ticket Editor
docs.text:
Use the Ticket Editor to view, create and edit standalone tickets and view batch data.

Three ticket types are available in FLOWCAL:

  • Meter batch tickets
  • Tickets associated with a location
  • Standalone tickets

Standalone tickets can be applied to a location directly. These can be used for blowdowns where there is not a measurement point or trucks being loaded from a tank among other things.

To view and edit tickets: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Tickets** \> **Ticket Editor**. 2. Select a date range and click **Open**. All tickets for the selected time frame will display. - Double-click a location or standalone ticket to access the [Ticket Details](Ticket%20Details/Ticket%20Details%20Editor.md) screen. - Double-click a batch ticket to access the [Batch Details](../Volume%20Editor/Batch%20Tab.md#BatchDetail) screen, or right-click a batch ticket to access the [Volume Editor](../Volume%20Editor/Volume%20Editor.md). If you access the Batch Details screen from the Ticket Editor, and then edit the batch data, the edit will only apply to that batch and its selected underlying periodics. Because of this, the effective dates for flow data, characteristics and analysis are read-only.

Ticket Editor Screen Details

The following items are available on the Ticket Editor screen: - **Date/Time Span Selector** - Limit the tickets returned by the search to those with an effective date in the specified range. Click the refresh button to reload the tickets within that range to view the most current data. - **Ticket Type Selector** - Select the type of tickets to view. Select Batch Meter to view batch data for all of the pipeline meters. Select Undefined tp view custom ticket types or ticket types that were not recognized during TFX import. Tank Run, Tank Gauge Level, and Inventory Empty Ticket Types require a license for the Liquids Inventory Module. - **Grid** - Displays data for tickets that fit the specified date and type criteria. Changes made to ticket details will be reflected in the grid automatically. Refresh the view to see changes made by other users or processes. - **Data Type tabs** - Sub-categories of ticket information. All tickets have the following tabs: Measurement, Analyses, Accounting, Components, Net Allowable, Custom Fields, and Close Data. Meter tickets also have a Configuration tab. Click the arrow buttons to the far right to access tabs that may be cut off or hidden. ##### Right-Click Menu Options - **New Ticket** - Creates a new Ticket of the Type currently selected. If this option is selected and a Default Autofill Profile has been set for that Ticket Type, then the ticket is automatically populated with the default fields for the default profile. - **New From Profile** - When this option is hovered over, a sub-menu displays the Profile Name of all Autofill Profiles for the corresponding Ticket Type. Once an Autofill Profile is selected, a new ticket is automatically populated with the default values for that profile. (See: [Ticket Autofill Editor](Ticket%20Autofill%20Editor.md)) - **Delete Ticket** - This option allows the user to delete the selected ticket. Closed tickets cannot be deleted from within the Ticket Editor or Ticket Search screens as they have already been processed. - **Attach Analysis** - This option allows the user to attach a standalone sample or source analysis to a ticket.

Edit to Original

Right-click a ticket and select Edit to Original to reapply the original data to the ticket. This edit will display as a new revision, but will contain only the original data. This process can be applied to multiple tickets; any tickets that cannot be updated will be flagged.

Prior Period Adjustments

A PPA is automatically created when a new ticket is attached to a location and the effective date occurs in a measurement month when the location is closed. If a PPA is automatically created during import, a location-level message is generated. If the System PPA option is set to "Not Allowed", the ticket will not import, and a location-level message is generated.

docs.title: Ticket Search
docs.text:
Users can search for tickets using the Ticket Search screen. Companies can accumulate thousands of tickets, making it difficult to find specific tickets. The Ticket Search screen is configured to select either one, or many filters to narrow down a search. This screen also allows for multiple searches from within the same screen.

Ticket Search lets users find tickets based on one or more of the following criteria: product, ticket type, time frame and location the ticket is attached to. Users can create multiple searches by adding additional tabs to the UI.

To open Ticket Search: Go to **Open** \> **Tickets** \> **Ticket Search**.

Any edits made to the Batch Detail opened from the Ticket Search screen only performs an edit to that batch and its selected underlying periodics. Because of this, the effective dates for Flow Data, Characteristics and Analysis are read-only in this view. Additionally, since FLOWCAL is only aware of the data in the batch being edited, when a PPA is performed the percent change values displayed at save time are for the batch only.

Ticket Search Screen Details

The following items are available on the Ticket Search screen: - **Master search tab** - By creating new tabs using the button, the conditions and results of multiple searches can be simultaneously maintained, allowing the user to find tickets that meet various criteria without having to continually change the query and lose the prior search. - **Current search conditions** - This section displays the selected search criteria. Users can remove search criteria by right-clicking a search condition and selecting **Remove Filter**. - **Search criteria** - Here, the user can use the drop-down to specify a data point to filter by. The user may then enter the actual criteria to filter the search below. To add new search criteria all the user needs to do is change the option in the drop-down menu, FLOWCAL will automatically add the selection to the current search conditions box. When searching by ticket type, the following ticket types will only be available when licensed for the Liquids Inventory module: Cavern Level, Tank Gauge, Tank Run, and Inventory Empty. - **Refresh** - This will cause the current search conditions to be run, refreshing the grid with the most up to date data for all tickets that meet the search criteria. - **Data navigation type** - These tabs separate ticket data into distinct sections that allow for easier viewing of related information. - **Ticket search grid** - This is where all tickets and batches that meet the conditions specified by the user’s search are displayed. The user may open the Ticket Editor Detail for a given ticket by double-clicking on it in the grid. The Batch Details screen can be opened to view batch data by double-clicking on a batch. A right-click option on batches called Open Volume Editor is also available to allow the user to open the Volume Editor for the meter and month of the Batch Ticket selected. FLOWCAL will only display up to 10,000 tickets. If the search criteria will compile more than 10,000 tickets, the message "(Truncated)" will display in the status bar at the bottom of the screen, followed by the number of tickets displayed on that tab. - **Right-click menu options** - The functions available in the right-click options menu are **New Ticket** and **New from Profile**. These options function the same as their counterpart options found in the right-click menu in the Ticket Editor. [Ticket Editor](Ticket%20Editor.md). Right-clicking anywhere on the grid and selecting **New Ticket** will open a blank ticket editor detail from which a new ticket may be created. Unlike creating a ticket through the Ticket Editor, the ticket type must be specified when creating a new ticket, and tickets of all types (other than Inventory Empty) may be created here. As with the Ticket Editor, batch data can be viewed from the Ticket Search form. When a user hovers over the **New From Profile** option, a sub-menu displays a list of available Ticket Types from where you can then choose the Profile Name from all Autofill Profiles for the corresponding Ticket Type. Once an Autofill Profile is selected, a new ticket is automatically populated with the default values for that profile. (See: [Ticket Autofill Editor](Ticket%20Autofill%20Editor.md))

docs.title: Accounting Tab
docs.text:
The Accounting tab contains non-measurement data that is often used by accounting processes such as the BOL, shipper, and odorant. The fields can vary by ticket type and by transport method. For instance: a Tank Gauge ticket will not include a shipper or transporter, whereas most other ticket types will.

Rail Patterns

Rail patterns can be used on rail tickets when the shipper for a rail pattern matches the shipper selected for a given ticket. All rail patterns with matching shippers are listed as a choice in the rail pattern drop-down field in the Ticket Editor. To select a rail pattern, you must first select a shipper that corresponds to a shipper on a rail pattern. Once you select a rail pattern, the following data points will be copied from the rail pattern onto the ticket: - All Characteristic and Route fields - From and To facilities - Location, product, class, and direction

BLM Oil Fields

In furtherance of Bureau of Land Management regulation 3174.12 (a), the following fields have been added to Meter, Tank Run, and Tank Gauge Tickets. Accounting Tab (Meter Ticket) Accounting Tab (Tank Run Ticket) The following options are available on the Accounting tab: - **Operator** – Name of the operating company. Name must be previously defined in Company Manager. - **Seal 1 Off/On** – Values that must match the previous and successive tickets associated with a location or tank. - **Seal 2 Off/On** - Values that must match the previous and successive tickets associated with a location or tank. - **Witness** – Name of the purchaser’s representative. Must be a previously defined contact under Contact Manager. - **Gauger** - Only found of Tank Run and Tank Gauge tickets. Name of the person performing the gauging. Must be a previously defined contact under Contact Manager.

docs.title: Analysis Tab
docs.text: The Analysis tab displays different component breakdown data depending on whether the meter is a hydrocarbon or non-hydrocarbon meter. The tab also displays sample data, such as sample date, absolute density, and molar mass.

docs.title: Hydrocarbon Meters
docs.text: For hydrocarbon meters, the tab displays the component breakdown for Mole %, Mass % and Liquid Volume % as well as extended characterization values for samples with a C6+, C7+, C8+, C9+, or C10+.

docs.title: Non-Hydrocarbon Meters
docs.text: For non-hydrocarbon meters, the tab displays the non-hydrocarbon component breakdown for NHC Mass%, NHC Mole %, and NHC Liquid Volume %.

docs.title: Components Tab
docs.text: Once a valid product has been selected for a ticket, component values will be available for use under the Ticket Editor detail Components tab.

docs.title: Hydrocarbon Products
docs.text:
For hydrocarbon products, the Components tab displays data for Component Mass, Component Volume and Net Allowable Volume for CO2, N2 and C1 – C10.

Each Component field in the Net Allowable column is read-only if that Component is being rolled into another Component based on the settings of the Min/Max Component to Report options in the Product Editor.

Example If the Min Component to Report is set to C3, and the Max Component to Report is set to C3, then all components above and below C3 are set to read-only. In this case, the only row that is enabled in the Net Allowable column is C3.

docs.title: Non-Hydrocarbon Products
docs.text:
For non-hydrocarbon products, the NHC Components tab displays data for Component Mass and Component Mass Allowable.

Negative values may be entered for any component in order to enter a customer balance that is for custody.

The Configuration tab is used to define Meter Configuration data such as the Meter Type, Calculation Method and Atmospheric Pressure.

Similar to Batch Meters, Meter Tickets must also be configured in order for calculations to take place. The Configuration tab on the Ticket Detail screen for Meter Tickets contains all of the same configuration fields that are provided on the Characteristics Meter Tab in the Volume Editor.

For linear meters, if the "Pressure Compensated" option is set to "Yes", the "Meter Factor" label will change to "Comp Meter Factor".

This tab is only available for meter tickets.

docs.title: Ticket Details Editor
docs.text:
The Ticket Editor is used for entering data for a ticket that is not assigned to a meter. All fields with a green background such as Date, Device Number, and Product must be populated prior to saving data.

When a ticket is initially created or is opened from the Ticket Editor or Ticket Search screen, the Ticket Editor Detail is displayed. The appearance of this form differs between ticket types, but most sections (segregated by tabs) are shared between ticket types.

To edit ticket details: 1. Double-click a ticket in the [Ticket Editor](../Ticket%20Editor.md). The Ticket Details Editor window will display. 2. Complete all required data. 3. Enter the ticket number to be used for this ticket. A **Regenerate Ticket Number** button is located next to the Ticket Number entry field when the [Generate Ticket Number At](../../Settings%20Manager/Application/FLOWCAL%20Configuration.md#Generate) configuration option is set to "Save". 4. Select a ticket type. Onscreen options will vary by ticket type. If ticket creation has been initiated from the Ticket Editor, the ticket type will reflect the ticket type section that was open when the ticket was created. 5. If the device type is set to "Location", you will need to select a location to assign the ticket to. If this is not known or there is not one, set the device type to "Standalone". 6. Complete all applicable fields. 7. When you are ready to save, select an edit reason and click **Save**. 8. If you need to make changes to the data, click **Edit**.

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Ticket Details Editor screen: - **Date** - This is the ticket's effective date and determines when the measurement specified by the ticket will be accounted for. - **Ticket Number** - This field serves as a means of identifying and tracking a ticket. Depending on the options set under the FLOWCAL application options, this identifier may be automatically generated by FLOWCAL, brought in by import, or manually entered. - **GMS Date** - This field stores the date and time at which the latest revision of a ticket was generated. - **Revision** - Whenever an edit is made to a ticket, a revision is generated, and it is here that the current revision number of a ticket is indicated. Clicking Show Revisions will bring up a screen showing the results for each revision of the ticket. - **Status** - This field displays a ticket's current status. The status will be either "Empty" or "Closed". - **Ticket Type** - This field displays the ticket type of a selected ticket. Once a ticket has been created, its type cannot be changed. The type may only be explicitly chosen when a ticket is created using the Ticket Search form; within the ticket editor, a ticket's type is determined by the tab from which its creation was initiated. - **Product** - A product associated with a ticket's measurement must be specified when the ticket is created. - **Device Type** - The user may specify whether a ticket belongs to a Location or if it is Standalone and associated with no location. If a ticket is attached to a location, its measured values will be accounted for within that location. Certain ticket-types (such as Tank Run and Tank Gauge) cannot be created as Standalone. - **Device Number** - The displays the Device Number associated with a ticket. For location-attached tickets, this field will display the Location Number of the location to which the ticket belongs. - **Class & Direction** - These fields serve to classify the type of measurement represented by a ticket. If the Subtotal by Direction or Subtotal by Class options have been set under the FLOWCAL Application Options, the class and direction specified for a ticket will determine how the ticket's data will be accounted for within a location with respect to the other members of that location. - **Rejected** - When loading product onto a rail car or a truck, there may be times when the vehicle cannot be loaded. For instance, a rail car may not meet requirements and must be returned or the water is too high when the crude is checked for S&W content. In these cases, there may still need to be a ticket as there may be fees associated with the problem rail car or load. Flagging a ticket as rejected causes the volumes and mass to be set to zero, but alerts accounting that there was a ticket and that fees may be billed. - **Calculate** - Perform calculations using the data provided and generate or resolve exceptions accordingly. This provides an opportunity to review the results of edits before the edits are actually saved. Use the Recalc. option to specify whether the existing correlation factor (CF) will be applied when calculations are performed, or if the CF itself will be recalculated using the current data. - **Save** - Save data and perform the calculation routine, similarly to when you click Calculate. If the calculation cannot be completed due to missing data, the save will not complete and a message indicating the error will display on the lower left side of the form. - **Delete** - Delete the selected ticket. - **Print** - Generate a report of the ticket details. The report type will vary based on the ticket type. This button is only enabled when you are in View mode. - **Show Revisions** - View a grid displaying the measurement values for prior revisions as well as any reversals that exist.

docs.title: Ticket Validation Template Editor
docs.text:
FLOWCAL supports the creation of validations for liquid tickets through the Ticket Validation Template Editor. Templates are created for different ticket types and these validations templates are then attached to a location. Once attached to a location the validations will be run on all tickets that are members of that location.

The following validation types are available in the Ticket Validation Template Editor:

  • Required Field – If a data point is specified as a required field, an exception will be generated for any ticket that does not have a value for that field.

  • Min/Max – If a value lies outside the minimum and maximum values specified, an exception will be generated.

  • Calculation Variance - User-provided expected maximum variance between measured and calculated results for the data point. If the variance exceeds the validation set point, an exception will be generated.

  • Sequential Check - Given an expected sequence of values, if a current value does not match the prior value, an exception will be generated.

For the Gauge & Run ticket type, sequential validation of level and seal values are available in Prior Ticket group box.

For the validation process to consider a pair of tickets to be in sequence, the following conditions need to be met:

  • Tickets must belong to the same location.

  • Tickets much have the same Accounting > Meter ID value.

    Two tickets having null Meter ID values are considered to have the same Meter ID.

Missing value is not considered to be out of sequence. For example: Exception 11852 “TKT – Indicated Volume start index is out of sequence” is not generated for a meter ticket that does not have an IV Start Index value, even if the validation is enabled in the template.

Create a Template

To create a new validation template: 1. Click **New**. 2. Type in the name of the new validation template. The name of the template must be unique. 3. Select the ticket type from the drop-down list. 4. Optionally select a product from the drop-down list. If left blank, the template will be applied to all tickets regardless of the ticket product. 5. Specify the points that will be validated by this template. 6. Click **Save**. After creating a validation template, that template can be attached to a location. In order for the validations to be run the template must be attached to a location that contains the tickets that will be validated.

Modify a Template

To modify a validation template: 1. Select the template to be edited from the drop-down menu. 2. Click **Edit**. 3. Make changes to the validation template. 4. Click **Save**.

Delete a Template

To delete a validation template: 1. Select the template to be deleted from the drop-down menu. 2. Click **Delete**. Once a validation template has been deleted it cannot be retrieved.

docs.title: Ticket Validation Templates
docs.text: Validation templates are used to configure validations for tickets. Once created, these templates can be attached to a location and used to validate all tickets within that location. The validations that are available to run differ for each ticket type.

docs.title: Validation Process
docs.text:
Once a validation template has been added to Ticket Validations in the Location Editor then the tickets that are under that location will be validated. The validation process will run when under the following conditions:

  • A ticket is imported into FLOWCAL and is assigned to a location that has validation templates assigned to it.
  • A ticket is manually created and is assigned to a location that has validation templates assigned to it.
  • A ticket is edited that is assigned to a location with validation templates.
  • A change is made in the Ticket Validation window.

If multiple validation templates are attached to a single location the order of the validations will be determined by the order in which they are listed in the Ticket Validations window.

Validation templates that have a product specified will only be run against tickets that contain that same product. If there is no product specified, the template will be run against all tickets with a matching ticket type.

Example In this example, the meter ticket that contains crude oil will be validated by the Meter Ticket template and the Meter Ticket – Crude Oil template. The order these validations are run in is determined by the order in which the templates appear in the [Ticket Validations](../../Locations/Location%20Editor/Tools%20-%20Ticket%20Validations.md) window. If an incoming ticket does not meet the criteria of the validation templates that are attached to the location, no validations will be run for that ticket.

docs.title: Audits
docs.text:
Audits allow users to define criteria for meters to be flagged for audit on a meter by meter basis. The criteria can be based on:

  • Time (monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually)
  • Volume or energy change from one month to the next
  • Total volume or energy for the month
  • Difference in volume or energy for a check to sales relationship (meter or check location)

Before starting, consider the following questions:

  • Is this for volume recovery or a second layer of data validation?
  • Will individual analysts or a small group manage the setup and review?
  • Is there a current list of ins and outs for gathering systems or one-to-one relationships for checks on sales meters?
  • Will this roll out to one geographic area or one-to-one relationships first?

This feature requires the Audit Package module.

Configuring a Meter to Audit

A meter’s audit criteria can be set up within the Meter Editor \> Audits tab, to validate potential discrepancies with an Audit, Custody, or Check Meter. Audits can be performed based on volume/energy differences or using a time criteria. To configure a meter to audit based on volume/energy values: 1. Go to **Setup** \> **Meter Editor**. 2. Select a meter to audit and click **Edit**. 3. Select the **Audits** tab. 4. Select the Audit Meter the user will be doing the audit work in. The Audit Meter is for informational purposes only and will not generate audits. 5. Select a Check Meter or location to compare with. 6. Select the Auditor from the user list that will be primarily perform audits of the meter. 7. Select the Contact who will be contacted for information on the meter. 8. Select Volume or Energy limit. 9. Enter a value for the Monthly change greater than field. 10. Enter a value for the Check meter differs by field. You can audit on any one of the available parameters or a combination. If Frequency is selected, audits will be created at the frequency regardless of any other criteria. The user will need to select a month/year to begin the frequency validation. Only monthly volumes are considered, not daily. Audits will not automatically kick-out if the data is incomplete for the month.  

Viewing or Editing an Audit

Audits that have been flagged by the Audit service can be viewed from the Audit Tracker screen. Users can also create an audit manually from the Audit Tracker. From the Audit Tracker the user can walk through the audit process, starting from identifying the problem, to requesting data from a third party, or requesting an adjustment, to closing out the audit. To access the Audit Tracker and view audits: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Audits**. 2. Filter by meter, list, or location, contact, auditor, customer, result, or status. 3. Click **Refresh**. Audits are created with a default status of ‘Need to Request Data’. 4. Double-click the record to make edits in the Audit Detail screen. For example, edit the Auditor, Audit Status, Note, or Problem Found. Notes can be used to detail findings and document action items and results. The Problem Found can be populated when an audit is resolved. #### Audit Tracker Data Field Details - **Detail View** - Double clicking a record within Audit Tracker or selecting the Detail View button will open the Audit Detail screen. - **New Audit** - Manually create an audit - **Refresh** - Refresh screen - **Print** - Preview the full audit package for the audit selected, which includes the Audit Reconciliation Request, GVS Daily, Audit Data Request Letter, and Audit Summary reports. - **Exit** - Exit screen

Audit Detail

Double clicking a record within Audit Tracker or selecting the **Detail View** button will open the Audit Detail screen. This screen shows: - The meter flagged for audit - The month being audited - Why it was flagged - Who the assigned auditor is - Who the primary contact is - The status of the audit - Volume and energy for the meter being audited, the check meter/location and the audit meter #### Data Field Details - **Audit Criteria** - Click the button to see the full audit criteria as specified in the Meter Editor - **Status History** - Click the button to view the dates for different steps in the progression of the audit - **Problem Found - Select** - Click Select to select, edit, or create a Problem Code and Description. Once a problem is found, choose a Problem Found for the audit. - **Letter** - Print or send a letter requesting data to the contact. See: Letter Selection - **Save** - Save changes - **Custom** - View or edit the 15 custom fields associated to the audit. The labels for these fields can be customized within the User-Defined Labels screen under the Settings Manager. There is an Audits tab that will allow changing the labels. Users must have System Information privilege to access the editor. - **Exit** - Exit form - **Print** - At any step in the process, the user can click Print to preview the Audit Detail report. The report will show information from the audit and as the audit progresses and more information is available, will reflect changes to the audit.

Letter Selection

Once the audit work has determined the problem, the user can send a letter from FLOWCAL requesting an adjustment. Clicking the Letter button on the Audit Detail screen will open the Letter Selection screen. ##### Data Field Details - **Letters for Need to Request Data** - Letter to request data or an adjustment After requesting data, the user can change the Audit Status to Data Requested. Once data is received, work can be done in the audit meter to determine the reason for the difference. Once the Audit Status has changed from Data Requested, the Request Adjustment option is available for selection. - **Contact Methods** - The contact selected on the Audits tab within Meter Editor will be displayed. - **Print** - Generate a local print of the letter - **Email** - If the contact has an email address defined, it will be displayed. - **Preview** - Preview the letter requesting data

docs.title: Bulk Changes
docs.text:
Accessing this screen requires System Information, Meter Edit, and List Edit or Location Edit system process privileges.

Use the Bulk Changes tool to make changes (such as plate diameter or meter direction) to multiple meters, quality sources, or locations at the same time.

To apply bulk changes: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Bulk Changes**. 2. Select a list, location or source list. 3. Select a category. Options in the drop-down menu will vary based on the type of list you selected. 4. Select a group. Options will vary based on the category you selected. 5. Click **Edit** to enable the fields for editing. 6. To change a field value, select **\** and specify the new value or select a value from the drop-down list, if available. To clear a field value, select **\**. If you select **\** and do not specify a value, no action is taken. 7. Select the date range for which the changes will be applicable, if the fields are datetime effective. For fields that are not datetime effective, such as fields on the Meter Editor, the date range will be ignored. 8. Select the reason for the change, if prompted, and click **Apply**. The progress of the changes will display. When all changes have been successfully applied, the status will change to "Complete".

docs.title: Data Reconciliation
docs.text:
When FLOWCAL is upgraded from Version 7 to Version 8, data values must be migrated from the old Version 7 database to a new Version 8 database. After this migration process has been performed, differences in the calculated rollup values may occur.

This could be caused by any number of reasons:

  • A rounding effect due to differences between Version 7 and Version 8 in the number of decimal digits values are stored with.
  • Values that were rolled and totaled up incorrectly in Version 7 which are now summed correctly in Version 8.

The upgrade to Version 8 should be complete before the user begins the process of accepting or ignoring these differences between Version 7 and Version 8 rolled up values. These differences can then be evaluated and accepted or ignored as appropriate to each case.

Until these differences are accepted or ignored, the rollup services will continue to use the original values, regardless of any differences calculated during the migration.

To access the Data Reconciliation tool: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Data Reconciliation**. 2. Choose a meter, location, list, or close group. 3. Double-click a row to bring up detailed daily information about that row (or month) in a new tab. A reason (or reasons) for the selected difference will display. A reason (or reasons) for the selected difference will be displayed. 4. Click the blue up or down arrow buttons to move back and forth through the data for the meters (or locations) in the list. Differences can be accepted or ignored for each individual data row. When a difference is rejected, the data remains as it was prior to the migration. When a difference is accepted, a PPA is created instantly. Once a PPA is accepted, it cannot be rejected. 5. Select the **Data** tab to go back to the full overview display. Double-click another data row or select multiple rows and click the **Open** button to display each meter in its own tab and easily compare the results.

docs.title: Email
docs.text:
You can send emails from within the FLOWCAL application.

Make sure you have configured the settings in the Email section of the Report Scheduler Configuration (Reports > Report Scheduler > Configuration).

To send an email from FLOWCAL: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Email**. 2. Click the **To** button to select a recipient. 3. Enter a subject. 4. Click the **Attachment** button to attach a file, if necessary. 5. Enter your message, and click the **Send** button.

docs.title: Graph Tool
docs.text:
Accessing this feature requires Meter Edit system process privileges.

The Graph Tool allows you to view meter and location data graphically.

To create a graph: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Graph Tool**. 2. Click **Select Parameters**. 3. Select whether to graph data for meters or locations, and then select the meter or location for which you want to graph data. 4. Select whether to graph **Process** parameters (flow data) or **Component** parameters (analysis). To select from all available parameters, select **All**. 5. If you want to change the plot line color for a parameter, right-click the color and choose from the available colors. 6. Select the parameters that you want to graph, or click **Check All** to select all of the parameters in the list. 7. Click **Insert**. FLOWCAL lists the parameters that you selected on the right side of the screen. 8. When you are satisfied with the list of parameters to be plotted, click **OK**. 9. The name of the meter or location and the selected parameters display on the left side of the Graph Tool. When the Traces option (top menu) is set to "On", the Trace checkboxes can be used to trace the plot line. The exact date and values are displayed above the graph as the line is traced. 10. Select the date range and data resolution to plot, and then click **Plot**. FLOWCAL displays the data in graphical and tabular format. To zoom in on the graph, click and drag in an area of the graph. To zoom out, double-click the graph. 11. To export the data to an Excel spreadsheet, right-click the table and select **Export to Excel**. Additional options for formatting the graph (such as changing the scale and selecting a gradient) are available from the menus at the top of the screen.

docs.title: Query Editor
docs.text:
The Query Editor allows a user to create a query to run against the FLOWCAL database. The user can also edit an existing query and create a new query based on an existing query. Queries can be used for filtering out objects (e.g., meters, locations, sources) and as the basis for Dynamic Lists.

A query can be executed for all meters, a meter list, a location, all source analyses, or a source analysis list. The query will run for all dates by default, but can be applied to a specific date range.

To access the Query Editor:  - Go to **Tools** \> **Query Editor**; or - Click the **Query** button in the List Editor when creating a dynamic list. For a list of possible values for the most commonly used tables and fields, see the [Query Cheat Sheet](Query%20Cheat%20Sheet.md).

Query Editor Screen Details

The following items are available on the Query Editor screen: - **Query Name** - Click the drop-down to select an existing query. Queries for all object types (e.g., meter, location, source) will be listed. - **Meters, Locations, Sources** - Reflects the object type associated with the Query Name selected. - **SQL** - Show the SQL compiled based on the query options selected. - **New** - Create a new query. - **Copy** - Create a copy of a selected query. - **Edit** - Edit an existing query. - **Run** - Run an existing query. A Query Results screen will appear showing the results of the query. - **Delete** - Delete a query. - **OK** - Exit the form. - **Cancel** - Cancel edits and do not save changes.

Query Editor Tab Details

The Query Editor includes three sub-tabs: - **Criteria** - Displays the tables/columns, operands, values, dates, etc. used as the criteria for the query. Up to 15 criteria are supported. Sub-Tab Details - **Table** - Used to filter the type of data to query for. The Table drop-down is populated based on the query object type selected (e.g. Meters, Locations, Sources). - **Field** - Used to select the field to query against. The Field drop-down is populated based on the Table selected. - **Operand** - Used to select the operand to use in the criteria (e.g. \<, \>, =, \<\>). The Query Editor supports Match and Skip operators for Equal and Not Equal using exact numbers or strings. - **Value** - Contains the values to query for. Wild card characters of "\*" and "%” are also supported. - **\*** - The "\*" column indicates whether the Value is case sensitive - checked means exact value, unchecked means that case does not matter. For numeric values such as pressure base, unchecking the field will cause FLOWCAL to round the value to the number of decimal places specified. - **And/Or** - Used to include more than one criterion in the query. When And is used, the value must meet both criteria to be true. When Or is used, the value must meet one or the other to be true. - **For All Date, Date/Time, Data Set Dates** - The query will run for all dates by default, but can be applied to a specific date range. - **Sort By** - The query results will return in order by object number, such as meter number. Use the Sort By tab to select one or more fields to sort the results by. - **Selection Pool** - By default, the query will run against all objects. To limit the query pool, select an option from the Selection Pool. For example, for a meter query, the user can select a list of meters to run the query against.

View Query Results

You can view the results of a selected query or a query as it is being created. To view query results: 1. From the Query Editor, click the **Run** button. The Query Results screen will open with the results. 2. Click **OK** to close.

Print Query Results

You can print query results for a selected query or a query as it is being created. To print query results: 1. From the Query Editor, click the **Run** button. The Query Results screen will open with the results. 2. Click the **Select All** button to select all the objects returned in the query results. All objects appearing on the right side of the form will be printed. 3. Click the **Print** button to see the report displaying the query and the query results. The report always prints the selected objects ordered by their unique identifier (meter number, quality source number, or location number). It does not use the Sort By criteria specified in the report.

docs.title: Reference Fluid Properties (REFPROP)
docs.text:
REFPROP is only used by FLOWCAL liquids. It is not used as a part of FLOWCAL gas.

Reference Fluid Properties (REFPROP), a program developed by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), calculates the thermodynamic and transport properties of industrially important fluids and their mixtures.

The calculation table is referred to as "REFPROP (NIST 23)" in the Product Editor and as "REFPROP" in the LQ Source Analysis editor.

docs.title: Licensing
docs.text: Customers must purchase their own license to utilize this calculation table in FLOWCAL. It is not shipped with FLOWCAL. If a user selects to use REFPROP in FLOWCAL, but does not have the DLL installed, no calculations will occur.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
To install REFPROP:

  1. Purchase REFPROP from NIST.
  2. Copy the refprop.dll and the FLUIDS folder from the REFPROP installation into the Mathlibs folder everywhere FLOWCAL is installed.
  3. In FLOWCAL, select "REFPROP (NIST 23)" in the Product Editor or "REFPROP" on the LQ Source Analysis tab.

docs.title: Tracking
docs.text:
Bar coded charts can be tracked electronically to quickly determine where charts are in an office. There are eight customizable stages of the chart progression. At each stage, a chart can be "wanded" to record the date of that event. For example: As charts are received via mail delivery, each one is "wanded" into the system as received.

To access the Chart Tracking screen: Go to **Tools** \> **Charts** \> **Tracking**.

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Several chart reports are available within FLOWCAL:

  • Bar Code Labels
  • Chart Batch Contents
  • Chart Tracking Status
  • Operator Statistics Detail
  • Operator Statistics Summary
To access the Chart Reports screen: Go to **Tools** \> **Charts** \> **Reports**.

Chart Report Details

The following options are available in the Chart Reports screen: - **Reprint Labels** - Print labels that have been printed previously. - **Show All Lists** - By default, lists are filtered by ordered lists, unless this option is checked. The List drop-down only contains ordered lists; this function does not support static or dynamic lists. - **Collation** - **By Date** – When running a report for an ordered list of meters from January 2017 through December 2017, the report will run all meters for January, then all meters for February, through December. - **By Meter** – When running report for an ordered list of meters from January 2017 through December 2017, the report will run data for the first meter from January through December, then data for the second meter from January through December, until the last meter has been processed.

docs.title: Bar Code Labels
docs.text:
Chart labels can be created for scheduled chart routes. A schedule is used to specify the on and off dates for the charts. The rotation is used if a schedule has not been assigned to the meter.

The report uses an ordered list so that labels are printed in route order. When running the Bar Code Labels report, please note that labels print from the start of the first month and year selected through the end of the last month and year selected.

To print the bar code labels, you must purchase and install the IDAutomationC128M.ttf font.

To set up a meter for printing bar code labels: 1. Create a schedule through the Annual Schedule Editor. 2. Assign the schedule to one or more meters through the Meter Editor. 3. Specify the meter characteristics through the Volume Editor. 4. Create an ordered list of meters.

Creating and Assigning Annual Schedules

Annual schedules can be created via the Annual Schedule Editor. Once a schedule is created, assign it to one or more meters by selecting the schedule from the Chart Change Schedule drop-down box on the Reports tab of the Meter Editor.

Meter Characteristics Setup for Bar Code Labels

To configure the meter characteristics: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor**. 2. Select a meter and select **Characteristics**. 3. Double-click the appropriate characteristic record. 4. On the Meter tab, select "Chart" from the **Chart** drop-down list. 5. Set the rotation. 6. Set the chart type to either **two pen**, **two pen with temperature** (will print two labels for each pull date), or **three pen**. 7. Set the orifice plate size. 8. Set the ranges for differential pressure, pressure, and temperature. 9. Click the **Save** button.

Running the Report

To run the Bar Code Labels report: 1. Go to **Charts** \> **Reports**. 2. Select **Bar Code Labels** as the report to run. 3. Select a system. 4. Select an ordered list from the drop-down list. 5. Specify a month range. 6. Select a collation option. > - **By Date** - Collates by schedule date, printing labels for all meters for the date, then moving to the next schedule date > - **By Meter** - Collates by meter, printing labels for all schedule dates for the meter, then moving to the next meter 1. Click the **Print** button.

docs.title: Applying a Master Allocation
docs.text:
After Master Allocation associations are created, the Master Allocation must be manually triggered to redistribute the volumes via the Master Allocation screen.

To apply a Master Allocation: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Master Allocation** \> **Allocation**. 2. Select a master allocation meter\location number or name and a contract month that you want allocated. 3. Click **OK**. When the process completes, the status window will display the following message, “Master meter/location allocation process completed”. If the allocation process fails to complete, an error message will display. The allocation process will not complete if there are any unresolved exceptions for any meter members of the master meter or location within the specified time frame.

docs.title: Gas Calculation Method
docs.text:
When calculating allocation values for a master meter, the balance arithmetic used is based on the base direction of the master.

For master meters with an inlet base direction:

Inlet Meter = Inlet Meters – Outlet Meters

For master meters with an outlet base direction:

Outlet Meter = Outlet Meters – Inlet Meters

Example 1 - Gas Allocation

A master meter has three meter members (Meter 1 \[inlet\], Meter 2 \[outlet\], and Meter 3 \[outlet\]). The master meter has direction set to outlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used: Outlet Meter = Outlet Meters – Inlet Meters For Volume: The master total volume differs from the member total volume. Difference = Master Total Volume – Member Total Volume 300 - 245 = 55 This difference must be allocated proportionally across member meters. Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total) > | Meter | Allocation | > |:-----:|:--------------------------------:| > | 1 | 55 \* (-360 / 245) = **- 80.82** | > | 2 | 55 \* (195 / 245) = **43.78** | > | 3 | 55 \* (410 / 245) = **92.04** | The allocation will then be added to each member’s volume to create a revised allocated volume per meter. > | Meter | Original Volume | Allocation | Revised Volume | > |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:| > | 1 | -360 | -80.82 | -440.82 | > | 2 | 195 | 43.78 | 238.78 | > | 3 | 410 | 92.04 | 502.04 | > | Total | 245 | N/A | 300 | The revised member total volume now equals the master total volume. Energy and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

Example 2 - Gas Allocation with Keep Whole

A master meter has three meter members (Meter 1 \[inlet\], Meter 2 \[outlet\], and Meter 3 \[outlet\]). The master meter has direction set to outlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used: Outlet Meter = Outlet Meters – Inlet Meters Meter 2 will be "kept whole", indicating that the volume, energy, and mass for that meter will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit. For Volume: The volume of the kept whole meter will be subtracted from the master total to create a new master total for allocation. New Master Total Volume = Master Total Volume - Kept Whole Volume 300 - 195 = 105 The total volume for the three member meters is 245. The volume of the kept whole meter will be subtracted from the total volume of the meter members to create a new member total volume. New Member Total Volume = Member Total Volume - Kept Whole Volume 245 - 155 = 50 The new master total volume differs from the new member total volume. Difference = New Master Total Volume – New Member Total Volume 105 - 50 = 55 This difference must be allocated proportionally across the two member meters that are not being kept whole. Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total) > | Meter | Allocation | > |:-----:|:----------------------------:| > | 1 | 55 \* (-360 / 50) = **-396** | > | 2 | N/A (kept whole) | > | 3 | 55 \* (410 / 50) = **451** | The allocation will then be added to each member’s volume to create a revised allocated volume per meter. > | Meter | Original Volume | Allocation | Revised Volume | > |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:| > | 1 | -360 | -396 | -756 | > | 2 | 195 | 0 | 195 | > | 3 | 410 | 451 | 861 | > | Total | 245 | N/A | 300 | The revised member total volume now equals the master total. Energy and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

docs.title: Liquid Allocation
docs.text:
The allocation process for liquid meters ensures that, for each day, values are available for GSV, NSV, mass, components, and net allowable, and that availability is consistent between each master and member meter. For the allocation process to occur, all meters within the allocation must have the same data values for the time frame selected; otherwise, an exception will be generated.

To set up a master location (liquid): 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Master Allocation** \> **Setup**. 2. Click the **Liquid** radio button. 3. Click **New**. 4. Select a liquid location to become the master location. The master location can only contain meter members, and must have a base direction of either inlet or outlet. Locations with a different direction will not be available in the drop-down list. 5. Select the date range for the allocation. 6. Use the Available Meters list to locate meters to include in the allocation. Double-click a meter to move it to the Meter Members list, or select multiple meters and click the right arrow button. 7. Indicate the meters that you want to keep wholeVolume, energy, and mass for meters that are "kept whole" in the allocation process will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit. during the allocation process. If a direction has not been defined for a meter in Meter Characteristics, you will be prompted to select a direction. Meters without an assigned direction will be highlighted with a red and white border.

docs.title: Liquid Calculation Method
docs.text:
When calculating allocation values for a master location, the balance arithmetic used is based on the base direction of the master.

For master locations with an inlet base direction:

Inlet Location= Inlet Meters – Outlet Meters

For master locations with an outlet base direction:

Outlet Location = Outlet Meters – Inlet Meters

Direction refers to the direction of the master location as defined in the Location Editor.

Example 1 - Liquid Allocation

A master location has three meter members (Meter 1 \[outlet\], Meter 2 \[inlet\], and Meter 3 \[outlet\]). The master location has direction set to outlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used: Outlet Location = Outlet Meters – Inlet Meters For Volume: The master total volume differs from the member total volume. Difference = Master Total Volume – Member Total Volume 560 - 575 = -15 This difference must be allocated proportionally across member meters. Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total) > | Meter | Allocation | > |:-----:|:--------------------------------:| > | 1 | -15 \* (360 / 575) = **- 9.39** | > | 2 | -15 \* (-195 / 575) = **5.09** | > | 3 | -15 \* (410 / 575) = **- 10.70** | The allocation will then be added to each member’s volume to create a revised allocated volume per meter. > | Meter | Original Volume | Allocation | Revised Volume | > |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:| > | 1 | 360 | -9.39 | 350.61 | > | 2 | -195 | 5.09 | 189.91 | > | 3 | 410 | -10.70 | 399.30 | > | Total | 575 | N/A | 560 | The revised member total volume now equals the master total volume. Energy and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

Example 2 - Liquid Allocation with Keep Whole

A master location has three meter members (Meter 1 \[outlet\], Meter 2 \[inlet\], and Meter 3 \[outlet\]). The master location has direction set to inlet, so the following balance arithmetic will be used: Inlet Location= Inlet Meters – Outlet Meters Meter 3 will be "kept whole", indicating that the volume, energy, and mass for that meter will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit. For Energy: The energy of the kept whole meter will be subtracted from the master total to create a new master total for allocation. New Master Total Energy = Master Total Energy - Kept Whole Energy 765 - 115 = 650 The energy for the kept whole meter will not be included in the member meter total. Without Meter 3, the meter member total energy is 780. 1380 - 600 = 780 The new master total energy differs from the new member total energy. Difference = New Master Total Energy – New Member Total Energy 650 - 780 = -130 This difference must be allocated proportionally across the two member meters that are not being kept whole. Allocation = Difference \* (Individual Meter / Member Total) > | Meter | Allocation | > |:-----:|:--------------------------------:| > | 1 | -130 \* (-600 / 780) = **100** | > | 2 | -130 \* (1380 / 780) = **- 230** | > | 3 | N/A (kept whole) | The allocation will then be added to each member’s energy to create a revised allocated energy per meter. > | Meter | Original Energy | Allocation | Revised Energy | > |:-----:|:---------------:|:----------:|:--------------:| > | 1 | -600 | 100 | -500 | > | 2 | 1380 | -230 | 1150 | > | 3 | 115 | 0 | 115 | > | Total | 895 | N/A | 765 | The revised member total energy now equals the master total. Volume and mass are allocated in the same manner. This may cause a disconnect between the meter’s heating value and the energy/volume ratio and/or energy/mass ratio.

docs.title: Master Allocation Setup
docs.text:
Use the Master Allocation Setup screen to configure the associations between a master and its member wells (meters) that will be used in the allocation process.

Master Allocation requires Master Allocation and Meter or Location Edit system process privileges.

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Master Allocation Setup screen: - **Gas, Liquid** – The fluid phase for the master allocation meter (gas) or location (liquid). - **System and Meter/Location** – Master meter or location. - **From/To** – Applicable date and time range. - **Delete** – Delete an association for the specified time frame. - **Direction** – Direction of master meter (gas). Master locations will use the direction that has been defined for the location within the [Location Editor](../../Locations/Location%20Editor/Location%20Editor.md). - **Energy Alloc Method** – The method of allocation for the selected meter or location. Available options are: - **Allocated** – Allocate the energy directly from the master to its members. - **Calculated** – Recalculate the energy after a master volume has been allocated to its members. The Direction and Energy Alloc Method options are only available for gas master allocations. ##### Grid Details - **Number** – Meter number. - **Name** – Meter name. - **Direction** – Meter direction. - **KW (Keep Whole)** – Indicates whether a meter member will be kept wholeVolume, energy, and mass for meters that are "kept whole" in the allocation process will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit. during the allocation process. Outlet meters are highlighted in blue; inlet meters are highlighted in red. ##### Button Details - **Refresh** – Refresh the screen. - **Delete** – Delete the master meter or location and its relationships for all of time. - **Edit** – Edit an existing master allocation meter or location. - **New** – Create a new master allocation meter or location. - **Exit** – Exit the screen.

docs.title: Master Allocation
docs.text:
The Master Allocation process allows you to create a master meter (gas) or location (liquid) that will redistribute volumes back to wellheads based on the volume at a master level.

Theoretically, the master meter or location volume will be equivalent to the difference of volume between its outlet and inlet meter members. For instances where this is not the case, an allocation calculation is performed to distribute the surplus or deficit back to its member meters.

After Master Allocation associations are created, the Master Allocation must be manually triggered to redistribute the volumes. For gas allocations, the daily rollup records are updated and then rolled to the monthly level. For liquid allocations, periodic data is edited and queued to rollup.
