docs.title: Purge Meter Data
docs.text:
Use the Meter Purge screen to delete data from the database for meters in a list, or for individual meters. Purging will delete data from the following tables: periodic, batch, analysis, characteristics, events, edit reasons, alarms, exceptions, and final form data (hourly, daily, monthly).

After the data has been purged, the data will automatically be queued to rollup.

This is a very powerful utility that should be used carefully. A lot of important data can be deleted easily, especially if you purge data using the "All Date/Time" option. For this reason, you can only access Meter Purge if you have Purge > Open Meter Data privileges on at least one system.

To access the Meter Purge screen: - Go to **Tools** \> **Purge** \> **Meter Data**; or - Right-click an item in the Volume Editor and select **Purge**. The Meter Purge access from the Volume Editor is only available on the periodic, daily, monthly and batch tabs. When accessed from the Volume Editor, the form will pre-populate with the system, meter number, meter name, and selected date.

Meter Purge Details

The following options are available on the Meter Purge screen: - **System and Meter/List** - Select a system and the meter or list of meters. - **Date Range** - Perform the purge for a contract month, contract day(s), date/time range, or all date/time. When “All Date/Time” is selected, FLOWCAL will populate the characteristic record with the latest available record for all of time. When “Date/Time Range” is selected, and the From and To time are set to beginning of time and end of time, FLOWCAL will populate the characteristic record with the first available record for all of time. - **Keep Original Data** - Keep original data and only delete the edits. If you need to delete all data and re-import it, do not select this option. If you select this option, the Apply Autoedits and Apply Source options will also be available. This function requires **Purge** \> **Open Meter Data** privileges. - **Apply Autoedits** - Apply auto edits automatically after purging edits. - **Apply Source** - Apply the source analysis automatically after purging edits. - **Purge PPA(s)** - Purge prior period adjustments only. This function requires **Purge** \> **PPA Meter Data** privileges. - **Rescan** - Sends the purge time frame to SCADA request. - **Keep Original Batch Configuration** - Keep the imported batch time frame(s).

docs.title: Purge Source Analysis Data
docs.text:
Use the Source Analysis Purge screen to delete data from the database for sources in a list, or for individual sources.

This is a very powerful utility that should be used carefully. A lot of important data can be deleted easily, especially if you purge data using the "All Date/Time" option. For this reason, you can only access Source Analysis Purge if you have Purge > Source Analysis privileges on at least one system.

To access the Source Analysis Purge screen: Go to **Tools** \> **Purge** \> **Source Analysis Data**.

Source Analysis Purge Details

The following options are available on the Source Analysis Purge screen: - **Date Range** - Perform the purge for a date range or all date/time. - **Keep Original Data** - Keep original data and only delete the edits. If you need to delete all data and re-import it, do not select this option.

docs.title: Demand Scan
docs.text:
FLOWCAL's SCADA request process provides a tool to ask the SCADA system to perform the specific task of retrieving missing data for a specific time frame by meter, location, list, close group, source list, or source. Entries will be created in the database table FC_SCADA_REQUEST for each meter or source that is queued. Your SCADA system must be able to read from the FC_SCADA_REQUEST table.

To run the SCADA Request Demand Scan tool: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **SCADA** \> **Demand Scan**. 2. Select the type of data to scan, such as meters or quality sources. 3. Select the meter, location, list, source, source list or close group that the user wishes to request a SCADA scan for from the drop-down selection list or from the tree view. 4. Specify the desired time frame for the SCADA scan. 5. Select the start and end dates for the time frame. Specify the hour next to the **From** and **To** fields if the scan is being run for a date/time range. 6. Click the **Run** button. If the request was successful, a message will display confirming that the request has been submitted. You can view these entries in the [SCADA Request Viewer](Request%20Viewer.md).

docs.title: Quality Download
docs.text:
FLOWCAL's SCADA request process provides a tool to download quality source data to a meter in the field via the SCADA system. This task may be requested by meter, list, or close group.

The following requirements must be met:

  1. The SCADA system must be able to read from the FC_SCADA_REQUEST table.
  2. Each meter must have a quality source assigned to it.
  3. Each meter must be configured for the data to be downloaded on the Services > Quality Download tab in the Meter Editor.
To access the SCADA Request Quality Download and edit an existing request: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **SCADA** \> **Quality Download**. 2. Select the appropriate name from the drop-down list, and go to **File** \> **Edit**. To create a new request: 1. Go to **File** \> **New**. 2. Enter the new request name. 3. Select the data type (meter, list or close group) and choose the desired meter, list, or close group from the drop-down list or tree view. The Force All Meters option allows users to force quality download requests to be processed for all meters for the selected request. 4. Make any necessary changes to the request setup. 5. Click **Save**.

Run a Quality Download Request

To run a quality download request: 1. Select the name from the drop-down list. 2. Click the **Run Now** button to make the request for the selected quality download. 3. Click the **Messages** tab to see if the request was successful or if any errors occurred.

Delete a Quality Download Request

To delete a quality download request: 1. Select the name to be deleted from the drop-down list selection. 2. Go to the **File** menu and click **Delete**. If the selected request is currently being edited by another user, the user will be presented with an error message letting the user know that the Request could not be deleted. 3. When prompted, confirm the deletion. Click **Yes** to continue with the delete operation; click **No** to cancel the operation.

docs.title: Request Viewer
docs.text:
FLOWCAL's SCADA request process provides a tool to ask the SCADASupervisory Control and Data Acquisitionsystem to perform specific tasks such as retrieving missing data from a meter or a source in the field (a scan), downloading gas quality data or characteristics from FLOWCAL to a meter in the field.

The SCADA Request Viewer shows the status of these tasks for meters and source analyses. These requests are stored in the SCADA Request table within the database and may be reviewed by meter, location, list, close group, source list, or source. The search results may also be filtered using various criteria.

To view current SCADA requests: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **SCADA** \> **Request Viewer**. 2. Select the type of data the user would like to view from the selector in the **Type Filters** area. 3. After the appropriate type has been chosen, select the meter, list or any other data ID that the user would like to view SCADA requests for from the appropriate drop-down menus in the **Type Filters** area. 4. After the desired data type has been selected, select the time filter from the **Time Filter** area, which can be **None**, **Effective Date** of the request or the **Initial Request Date**. If necessary, the user can then change the date range used for the effective date or the initial request date. The Effective Date option is only available when the request type is set to "Scan". 5. The **Status Filters** area displays the color codes the user will find in the tabular view of requests and allows the user to select what request states the user wants to view. 6. Select the request type (**Scan**, **Quality**, or **Characteristics**), which will display the type of request the user desires to view for the selected data type and time frame. 7. Click the **Refresh** button at the bottom of the form. The results and related information will display. 8. To run another request, change the desired filters and click the **Refresh** button again. Use options at the bottom of the form to format the results and limit the number of rows that will be returned.

docs.title: Queue Live Oil Child Meters
docs.text:
Service queue entries can be generated using the Queue Live Oil Child Meters option in the Toolbox.

Running this option for a live oil meter will generate queue entries for each active associated child meter. Selecting a single child meter in the Toolbox will generate a queue entry only for that specific child meter.

docs.title: Run Duration Fix Utility
docs.text:
The Duration Fix utility addresses situations that cannot be fixed or addressed by normal data processing or editing in FLOWCAL, specifically gaps and overlaps in meter and source characteristics and analysis. The utility addresses issues in the revision zero records and the latest or current revision records.

Duration Fix is normally run under the suggestion of your Customer Support representative when an abnormal situation may point to possible gaps or overlaps in characteristic and analysis data. Running Duration Fix on a good data set is harmless and poses no risk to data integrity.

Duration Fix checks the continuity of characteristics and analysis for meters and sources and identifies gaps and overlaps for the following data:

  • Meters
  • Characteristics
  • Analysis
  • Quality Sources
  • Characteristics
  • Analysis
  • Extended Analysis

The utility will run for all of time to ensure that all gaps and overlaps are addressed.

Gaps

Gaps are missing portions of data in characteristic or analysis records. They are fixed by moving the effective end date of the earlier record forward to meet the effective start date of the later record, removing the gap in data.

Overlaps

Overlaps are when the effective end date of a previous record is greater than the effective start date of the next record. Duration Fix addresses overlaps by moving the effective end date of the earlier record back to the effective start date of the next record. This creates a continuous record with no gaps or overlaps. To run the Duration Fix utility: 1. Go to **Tools** \> **Toolbox**. 2. Select a meter, meter list, location, close group, source, or source list. 3. Select the **Run Duration Fix Utility** radio button. 4. Click the **Run** button. To run the Duration Fix standalone utility: 1. Launch the utility from the FLOWCAL installation directory (e.g., **C:\\FLOWCAL install folder\]\Tools\DurationFix.exe**). 2. When the login screen displays, enter your FLOWCAL username and password and click the **Login** button. 3. When the utility screen displays, select a meter, meter list, location, close group, source, or source list and click **Run**. The utility will process each meter for all date time, as per the selected options, to log or fix gaps and overlaps. Selecting the "Log" option scans the data to identify and report gaps and overlaps; problems in the data are displayed on the utility screen and no fixes are performed.

docs.title: Run Validations
docs.text: Use this option to perform data validations for an object or list of objects on demand, for a specific time frame. (See: Toolbox)

docs.title: Toolbox
docs.text:
The Toolbox comprises a set of tools that can be used to perform various tasks from applying analysis to performing data validations on demand.

Some Toolbox operations are not intended for use on closed data. If attempted, FLOWCAL will display a message stating that an operation is not allowed on closed data.

To access the Toolbox screen:  Go to **Tools** \> **Toolbox**.

Toolbox Details

The following options are available on the Toolbox screen: - **Date Type** - Select a span of time, such as contract month, contract day(s), or date/time range. - **Recalc Rollup IDs** - This function should only be run at the request of Customer Support. - **Run Validations** - Run the configured validations for meters, locations and/or sources, for the selected time frame. The objects validated depend on the selected object type as follows: Object Type Selected   Validation Meter Current meter ü Location Current location ü Meter members of location ü Location members of location û Meter members of location members ü Location members of location members û List Meter members ü Location members û Close Group Meter members ü Location members û Source Current source ü Source List Source members ü - **Apply Defined Auto Edits** - Apply auto edits that are assigned to a meter. - **Apply This Auto Edit** - Apply the auto edit selected from the drop-down list. You may also apply multiple auto edits. - **Force Recalc of** - Force a recalculation of the volume or VCF due to edits that did not trigger a recalculation. - **Accept Auto Estimates** - Accept auto estimated data to allow the assigned source analysis to be applied. - **Apply Source Analysis to Meters** - Apply source analysis to a single meter or multiple meters based on the source assignment. - **Load Source Analysis from Meter** - Push an analysis from a meter to a source. - **Run Duration Fix Utility** - Normally run under the suggestion of your Customer Support representative when an abnormal situation may point to possible gaps or overlaps in characteristic and analysis data. This utility addresses situations that cannot be fixed or addressed by normal data processing or editing in FLOWCAL, and addresses issues in the revision zero records and the latest or current revision records. (See: [Duration Fix Utility](Run%20Duration%20Fix%20Utility.md)) - **Calculate FMP Tier** - Recalculate the FMP volume tier. This only applies to meters for which the BLM Property designation is set to "Yes". (See: [FMP Tier Calculation](../../BLM/FMP%20Tier%20Calculation.md)) - **Queue Live Oil Child Meters** - Queue to send data from a live oil meter to any associated dead oil or flash gas child meters. (See: [Live Oil Management](../../Meters/Meter%20Editor/Tools%20Menu.md)) This only applies to meters that are designated as live oil and have an active relationship to at least one child meter.

docs.title: Alternate Periodic Tab
docs.text:
The Import Alternate Periodics option on the Imports tab of the Meter Editor allows you to store data with an alternate periodic resolution. For example: You could use one set of data (e.g., hourly) for measurement calculations, but still bring in and view data at a different resolution (e.g., daily).

If Import Alternate Periodics option is enabled, FLOWCAL will import data in the Alternate Periodic data section of the CFX file if it is provided. The Volume Editor will display this Alternate Periodic tab when Flow Data records are selected. You can then double-click a row to access a detailed view of the data, but the data will not be editable.

docs.title: Volume Editor
Analysis Editor

Use the Analysis Editor to maintain a meter’s analysis components and properties. If a meter has a source assignment, the Analysis Editor will automatically open when you click the Edit button.

To access the Analysis Editor: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor**. 2. Select a meter. 3. Click the **Analysis** radio button. 4. Adjust the date range as needed. 5. Double-click a row on the grid.

When the assigned Source Analysis is configured to use splits, the C6+ and C7+ splits are applied and shown in the analysis detail view.

When the assigned Source Analysis is configured to use extended characterizations, the related C+ properties are applied and shown in the analysis detail view.

docs.title: Batch Tab
docs.text:
This tab is only available for liquid meters.

The Volume Editor Batch tab shows the volume of liquid product passed through a meter over a specific period of time. Data can be edited at the batch level for Characteristics, Analysis, and Flow Data. If there is no batch present for the time frame specified, a batch will be created. Once a batch is created, editing the Start and End Date on batches is prohibited. You must split the batch in order to alter the dates.

If the edited batch time frame overlaps the time frame for a batch that is imported later, that batch will not be imported.

When editing a batch record, you can easily see on the Flow Data tab whether a batch exists. If there is not an existing batch for the time frame, a "V" (virtual batch) will display in the columns next to the start date. There is not an indicator on the other tabs such as Characteristic or Analysis.

By default, the batch total record is calculated from the sum of the periodic records within the batch.

Right-Click Menu Options

The following options are available on the Batch tab: - **Span Edit** – Allows you to edit multiple records at once. - **Purge** – Opens the Meter Purge screen with the meter and selected month pre-populated. To initiate a meter purge: 1. Modify the selections or proceed with the pre-populated selections. 2. Click the **Purge** button. When the purge is complete, the Volume Editor will refresh. Accessing this feature requires **Purge** privileges. - **Edit to Original** – Edit data to the original values. The Edit to Original function re-imports the original (revision 0) data of a record. This new import then contains the same data as revision 0. This allows users to edit the original data as if it were imported, saving all prior revisions as an audit trail. If revision 0 exists, and the current revision is greater than 0, the Edit to Original process will complete. If a record within the selected range cannot be edited back to original, a pop-up will display, indicating that there were records that could not be edited to the original data, and the dates of those records will display in red. That color will reset if the Volume Editor grid is refreshed. This option is not available for line pack meters. Process Logic FLOWCAL adheres to the following conventions when users choose to edit to original data: - If a user chooses to edit to original, and the meter or ticket contains *only* an original (revision 0) record, no action will be taken for that record. This will not be considered a failure or included in the list of tickets that could not be updated. - For liquid meters: - If a user chooses to edit to original on the Batch tab, the revision 0 batch (if it exists) will be promoted to current and will be allocated to the underlying periodic records. This is independent of whether the data is master, batch, or periodic. - If a user chooses to edit to original on the Periodic tab, the revision 0 batch (if it exists) will be promoted to current. The batch will be recalculated from the underlying periodics. This is independent of whether the data is master, batch, or periodic. - **Batch** - **Prove Adjustment** – Used when manually creating a prove adjustment on a batch to adjust prior and current adjustments for meter factor, K-factor, and density meter factor values. This option is not available for line pack meters. - **Ticket** – Prints the meter batch ticket for the selected batch. If multiple batches are selected, this option is disabled. Because reports run off data saved in the database, this menu option is disabled if you have any unsaved changes. - **Ticket with Internal Notes** – Prints the Meter Batch Ticket report and includes notes that are marked as internal. - **Split - Simple** – When this option is selected, you can select a batch and specify where in the batch the split should occur. Two batches are then created from that single batch (i.e., a simplistic batch split). The two new batches are calculated from the sum of the original periodic records that fall within each batch time frame. The screen that comes up for this option has two modes: Slider Entry and Free-Form Entry. When you edit using the Free-Form Entry option, you must also select if the data should be allocated "pro-rata" or "straight line". For both cases, the batch number for the second batch can be manually entered. This functionality is available for meters with both daily and hourly data. This option is available when a single batch is selected. - **Split - Advanced** – Allows you to perform a more advanced batch splitting action. When this option is selected, you can edit any flowing parameters, as well as meter factor and DMF, on the new batch. First, edit the left side of the batch, choosing the date of the split. After completing the edit of the first batch, enter data for the second batch. You'll have the option of doing "pro-rata" or "straight line" data allocation upon saving. This option is available when a single batch is selected, and you have saved pending edits. This option is not available for line pack meters. - **Split - Periodic** – When this option is selected, you'll first specify the date and time for the batch split, and then specify flowing parameters, such as mass, GSV and NSV, for each portion of the record being split. After these values are specified, new batch totals are calculated from the split periodic records and the other periodic records that fall within the batch time frames. This option is not available for line pack meters. - **Merge** – This option joins two batches. The resulting batch will have the same batch number as the batch with the earliest time stamp before the split. This option is available when two adjacent batches with the same product are selected. - **Sample Override** – Allows you to select either a standalone sample or a sample from a quality source as the sample to be used for the selected batches. The product on the first of the selected batches is used to determine which samples are valid. If a quality source is assigned to the meter, the override sample is used on the batch instead of the quality sample. Once the sample override is applied, any updates to the sample are applied to the batch by the GQ Apply service. Different samples can be selected as override samples at different times if desired. Only samples with a product that matches the product on the batch, or that do not have a product can be selected. When applied, a volume recalculation is performed using the correlation factor. (See: [Recalculation Methods](Recalculation%20Methods.md)) - **Quick Sum** – When this option is enabled, the monthly sum quick view is replaced to display the sum or average of selected rows in the Volume Editor. - **Monthly Sum** – When this option is enabled, a quick view of the monthly sum is displayed at the bottom of the Volume Editor screen. - **Add Note** – Allows you to add notes to any record in the Volume Editor. - **View Notes** – Allows you to view notes for any record in the Volume Editor. - **Prove Reports** – When a PFX file is imported, it can contain a PDF of the prove report. (This option is not available for line pack meters.) - If the prove report is imported into FLOWCAL via PFX file, the report will be available under Reports \> Prove Reports. An "R" will display in the character column next to the batch to which the prove report is applied, and the MF will be updated accordingly - If the prove report is imported through TESTit, the report will be available under Reports \> Test Reports. An "R" will display in the character column next to the batch to which the prove report is applied, but the MF will *not* be updated. Prove reports imported through TESTit will not trigger Master Characteristic validations. - **Edit Columns** – Allows a you to change the columns displayed in the Volume Editor. - **Accept ACBI** – If periodic data that does not already have batches is imported, FLOWCAL will create an ACBIAutomatically Created Batch Upon Import on the batch tab in the Volume Editor. The Accept ACBI option is visible when you select a highlighted row in the Volume Editor that is an ACBI. When you accept an ACBI batch: - The most current revision of the batch will no longer show as “ACBI” (the original revision will still show as “ACBI”) - An edit reason of "ACBI Batch accepted" will be applied to that revision. - The revision number will be incremented. - All future edits will increment the batch revision; with ACBI batches, revision will always remain revision 1.

Batch Detail Window

To access the Batch Detail window: Double-click a given row on the Batch tab. The following tabs are available in the Batch Detail window: | | | |----|----| | Hydrocarbon Meters | Non-Hydrocarbon Meters | | | | All of the flow data for the selected batch is viewable from the Flow Data tab. The **From** and **To** dates at the top show the beginning and end times for the selected batch. Field Hydrocarbon Non-Hydrocarbon Base Information Product • • Uncorrected Density • Observed Density • Observed Temperature • Observed Pressure • Observed Eq Vapor Press • Pressure Temperature Information Meter Temperature • • Meter Pressure • • Eq Vapor Pressure • Factor Information MF • • DMF • • Calculated Information Base Density • • Meter Density • • CTPL • • CTL • • CPL • • KF • • CCF • • CSW • Volume Information Mass • • Mass Allowable • Indicated Vol. • Gross Standard • Net Standard* • Summed Vol. • Net Allowable • S&W% • S&W volume • Theoretical Prod. • ##### Custom Fields There are 20 batch-specific custom fields that can be imported into FLOWCAL via CFX, text field, or Transaction Queue import. ##### Accounting The Accounting tab allows the user to set the following options: - **Shipper/Outside Shipper** – A company that is sending the product. Company must already exist and be specified as a shipper in Company Manager - **From/To Facility** – Used to track inventory. Facility must be previously defined under Settings Manager \> Liquids \> Facilities - **Customer Ticket ID** – Unique identification of batch provided by customer. - **Witness** – Name of purchaser’s representative. Must be a previously defined contact under Contact Manager - **Operator** – Name of operating company. Name must be previously defined in Company Manager. - **Seal 1 Off/On** – Values that must match the previous and successive batches associated with the meter - **Seal 2 Off/On** - Values that must match the previous and successive batches associated with the meter ##### Components Component level data for the select batch can be viewed here. Values will display in units specified under the **Meter Characteristic** \> **Units tab** \> **Component Volume**.

docs.title: Cell Editing - Volume & Mass
docs.text:
When cell editing volume and mass quantities in the FLOWCAL Volume Editor, the values are tracked with two columns: A Closed column and an Adjusted Total column, which includes PPAs.

The Closed column tracks the volume or mass until the meter goes through the month-end close process. Once the meter is closed, the value in the Closed column will no longer change in the database. The value in the Adjusted Total column will match the corresponding value in the Close column through the close. If adjustments are made to the data once the meter is closed, the value will be updated in the Adjusted Total column.

Each of these columns can be displayed in the tabular view of the Volume Editor.

While in cell edit mode in the Volume Editor, only one of these columns will be editable for a given quantity such as mass, net standard volume (NSV), and gross standard volume (GSV).

The following tables explain which column is editable for each quantity while in cell edit mode.

docs.title: Copy & Paste Flow Data
docs.text:
The copy/paste functionality is used to copy existing flow data into other records. This can include time frames of missing data or time frames where certain parameters are out of normal bounds and the user wants to replace that "bad" data with "good" data from another time period.

To copy and paste flow data:

  1. Highlight the row(s) to be copied.

  2. Right-click and select Copy from Selected Date/Time.

  3. Highlight the row(s) where the copied data is to be pasted. To select a disjointed selection of rows, press and hold the Ctrl key while clicking the rows to paste into.

    The rows will appear highlighted in green if the number of rows selected for pasting equals the number of rows that were copied. (This only applies to a contiguous selection of rows.)

  4. Right-click and select Paste to Selected Date/Time.

  5. A window will display where you can select data points and quantities to be pasted in the selected rows. Options include:

    • Paste Rows – This option allows you to paste the exact data from the copied rows. This option is only enabled if the number of rows selected for pasting is equal to the number of rows that were copied.
    • Paste Average – The flow data from the copied rows is averaged and those values are pasted in each row the selected time frame.
    • Paste Average, Fill Missing Rows Only – The flow data from the copied rows is averaged and those values are pasted only in the rows that are missing data in the selected time frame.
    • Exclude Zero Volume Rows from Average – Only available if Paste Average or Paste Average, Missing Rows Only is selected. Will exclude from the averages any data in the copied time frame that has no volume.
    Gas Options Liquid Options

|

|

Copy/Paste Between Two Meters

It is possible to copy data from one meter and paste into another meter of the same fluid phase and data resolution. 1. Highlight the row(s) to be copied. 2. Right-click and select **Copy from Selected Date/Time**. 3. Open the new meter that the data will be pasted into. This can be done by opening a new Volume Editor window or by simply navigating to the meter through the same instance of the Volume Editor. 4. When pasting to a second meter, two paste options are available: - **Paste to Selected Date/Time** – Copied data will be pasted into the date/time that has been selected by the user. 1. Highlight the row(s) where the copied data is to be pasted. To select non-consecutive rows, press and hold the **Ctrl** key while clicking the rows that you want to paste in. 2. Right-click and select **Paste to Selected Date/Time**. - **Paste to Copied Date/Time** – Copied data will be pasted into the corresponding date/time in the new meter. 1. Right-click and select **Paste to Copied Date/Time**. The current row selection, if any, will be ignored. If the calculation table and/or meter calculation of the meter where the data was copied does not match that of the meter where the data will be pasted, a warning will display. To continue with the paste operation, click **OK **when prompted.

Pasting Data into Split Records

When flow data is pasted into a time frame that contains split periodic records the quantity data points will be allocated pro rata into each split record based on the duration of each record. Quantity Data Points Gas
  • Flow Time
  • Volume
  • Energy
  • Mass
  • Raw Volume
  • Pulses
Liquid
  • Summed Volume
  • Net Allowable
  • Mass
  • IV
  • GSV
  • SWV
  • NSV
  • Pulses
Example Copy the following row of data: | Date/Time | Flow Time (Hours) | Volume (Mcf) | |---------------------|-------------------|--------------| | 08/01/2020 09:00:00 | 20 | 3421 | Paste the record into the following time frame that includes split periodic records: - 08/05/2020 09:00:00 - 08/05/2020 14:00:00 - 08/05/2020 20:00:00 FLOWCAL will use the weighted duration of the split records to correctly allocate the quantities in a pro rata fashion.

Pro Rata Allocation to Split Records during Paste Operation

Data Resolution: Daily (24 hours)

Date/Time Record Duration Allocated Flow Time (copied flow time * duration ratio) Allocated Volume (copied volume * duration ratio) 08/05/2020 09:00:00 5:00:00

20 * 5 / 24 = 4.16…

= 04:10:00

3421 * 5 / 24 = 712.708 08/05/2020 14:00:00 12:00:00

20 * 12 /24 = 10

= 10:00:00

3421 * 12 / 24 = 1710.500 08/06/2020 02:00:00 7:00:00

20 * 7 / 24 = 5.83…

= 5:50:00

3421 * 7 / 24 = 997.792

Copying Split Periodic Data

When a copied selection contains split periodic records the record values will be summed and averaged, as applicable, into a single record representing the full resolution time period; e.g., 1 hour. Example The following data contains a split record at 05/07/2020 09:00:00. The split record quantities are summed to produce totals for the resolution time period. The process variables are averaged per the system gas or liquid averaging option (Settings \> (System) \> Rollup Configuration). Effective Date Volume Total Volume Per Period 05/07/2020 08:00:00 1350 1350 05/07/2020 09:00:00 650 1497 05/07/2020 09:25:00 725 05/07/2020 09:48:00 122 05/07/2020 10:00:00 1425 1425 Average to Be Pasted 1424 The selection for the Copy operation will automatically include all split records to calculate a complete periodic. Using the example above, if the user selects 05/07/2020 08:00:00 through 05/07/2020 09:25:00 and selects the Copy operation, the process will automatically include the 05/07/2020 09:48:00 record and use all three split records to calculate a sum for the 09:00:00 period.

The Grid Legend contains an overview of color and alarm state codes used in the Volume Editor.

The character codes are set per flow data (periodic) record. The information displayed on the Daily and Monthly tab is from meter rollups; therefore, character codes are only displayed on the Flow Data Periodic tab and not on the daily or monthly tabs. However, color codes are available from all three display tabs (Periodic, Daily, and Monthly).

To access the Grid Legend: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor**. 2. Click the **View** menu. 3. Select **Grid Legend**.

The following color codes help identify processes performed by the application services and/or users.

docs.title: Periodic Tab
docs.text:
The Periodic tab displays flow data records according to the data resolution configured in the Meter Characteristics screen. Typical data resolutions are 15-minute, hourly, and daily data.

Right-Click Menu Options

The following options are available for periodic data: - **Span Edit** – Allows you to edit multiple records simultaneously. - **Purge** – Opens the Meter Purge screen with the meter and selected month pre-populated. To initiate a meter purge: 1. Modify the selections or proceed with the pre-populated selections. 2. Click the **Purge** button. When the purge is complete, the Volume Editor will refresh. Accessing this feature requires **Purge** privileges. - **Edit to Original** – Edit data to the original values. The Edit to Original function re-imports the original (revision 0) data of a record. This new import then contains the same data as revision 0. This allows users to edit the original data as if it were imported, saving all prior revisions as an audit trail. If revision 0 exists, and the current revision is greater than 0, the Edit to Original process will complete. If a record within the selected range cannot be edited back to original, a pop-up will display, indicating that there were records that could not be edited to the original data, and the dates of those records will display in red. That color will reset if the Volume Editor grid is refreshed. This option is not available for line pack meters. Process Logic FLOWCAL adheres to the following conventions when users choose to edit to original data: - If a user chooses to edit to original, and the meter or ticket contains *only* an original (revision 0) record, no action will be taken for that record. This will not be considered a failure or included in the list of tickets that could not be updated. - For liquid meters: - If a user chooses to edit to original on the Batch tab, the revision 0 batch (if it exists) will be promoted to current and will be allocated to the underlying periodic records. This is independent of whether the data is master, batch, or periodic. - If a user chooses to edit to original on the Periodic tab, the revision 0 batch (if it exists) will be promoted to current. The batch will be recalculated from the underlying periodics. This is independent of whether the data is master, batch, or periodic. - **Range Average** – Used to edit a specific range of data by using an average of data before or after the specified time frame. Fields available for Range Average will vary based on meter type and calculation method. When the **Exclude Zero Volume Rows from Average** option is enabled, zero volumes that appear in the specified time frame will not be included in the average. | | | |----|----| | Range Average | Range Average - Gas | | | | - **Split Periodic** – Allows user to create a new or missing periodic record that starts at the top of the period (15-minute, hour, day, month). You can specify a date to split the periodic record. No calculations occur at the time of split, but you can provide totals after the split. - **Quick Sum\*** – When this option is enabled, the monthly sum quick view is replaced to display the sum or average of selected rows in the Volume Editor. - **Monthly Sum\*** - When this option is enabled, a quick view of the monthly sum is displayed at the bottom of the Volume Editor screen. \* For non-line pack meters, averages calculated by quick sum or monthly sum follow the settings in [Rollup Configuration](../Settings%20Manager/System/Rollup%20Configuration.md). For line pack meters, averages are calculated by quick sum or monthly sum with respect to the inventory volume. - **Calculations** – When this option is enabled, the Spot Volume Calculator and Plate Size Calculator become available in the Volume Editor. You can use shortcut keys to launch the Spot Volume Calculator and Plate Size Calculator directly from the Volume Editor. Access the right-click menu and scroll down to Calculators, then press **V** to launch the Spot Volume Calculator or **P** to launch the Plate Size Calculator. (This option is only available for gas orifice meters with a CALCit license.) - **Copy from / Paste to Selected Date/Time** – Allows you to copy existing flow data into other records. (See: [Copy & Paste Flow Data](Copy-Paste%20Flow%20Data.md)) - **Add Note/Attachment** – Allows you to add notes or attachments to any record in the Volume Editor. - **View Note/Attachment** – Allows you to view notes or attachments for any record in the Volume Editor. - **Task Reports** – Displays all reports for the time frame via the PDF reader on your PC. An "R" displays in the first column of the Volume Editor for any records that contain TESTit reports. This option is only available with TESTit 3 Integrated. - **Prove Reports** – When a PFX file is imported, it can contain a PDF of the prove report. - **Edit Columns** – Allows you to change the columns displayed in the Volume Editor.

docs.title: Recalculation Methods
docs.text:
There are several Recalc Methods available to choose from for both gas and liquid meters:

For Gas Meters

##### Vol Use VCF The basic volume calculation. After volume is calculated, the Volume Correlation Factor is applied. If VCF is not defined, the re-calculation fails. Exception 71 (No Correlation Factor. Unable to calculate volume) is generated. Once a valid VCF exists, exception 71 will be resolved. ##### VCF The basic VCF calculation. After volume is calculated, the VCF is calculated using the newly calculated volume against the current existing volume. If there is no current existing volume and a new volume cannot be calculated the calculation fails. ##### Vol, Set VCF=1 For Gas meters only. VCF is set to 1 if a volume is calculated, otherwise the calculation fails. ##### Vol, Use VCF or Set VCF=1 For Gas meters only. If VCF is defined, it is used, otherwise, VCF is set to 1 if a volume is calculated. ##### Volume, From Extension For Gas meters only. Calculates volume using extension as the starting point instead of DP. (Actually it ratios DP out of the extension and then goes forward with the normal calculation using that). Extension is only applicable to orifice and cone meters. If this Recalc Method is selected for any other meter type, FLOWCAL will recalculate as if the user had selected Vol Use VCF.

For Gas Quality

##### Vol Use VCF Source Analysis will not be applied to meter analysis applicable to periodic data where the VCF is not defined. Exception 70 will be generated (No Correlation Factor. Unable to apply source analysis). Where VCF is defined source analysis will be applied and volumes re-calculated. ##### VCF Source Analysis will be applied to any applicable meter analysis regardless of periodic data VCF status. If a current volume exists and a new volume can be calculated, VCF will be calculated. Typically when applying analysis you want to recalc volume. Only choose VCF if you want the analysis applied for reporting purposes, but want to keep the volume from the meter.   If you choose to recalculate VCF, you have the option to also have energy recalculated based on the applied heating value. ##### Vol, Set VCF=1 If VCF is not defined, it will be set to 1 for calculations.

For Liquid Meters

##### Vol and Mass, Use CF The usual recalculation method that incorporates a correlation factor. Correlation factors (CF) account for the pressure, temperature and density averaging discrepancies exhibited between the one second EFM calculations and a recalculation using hourly or batch averages. CFs permit an exact recalculation of the EFM ticket, provide a validation of the original data and enables more accurate recalculations of edited data. After volume and mass are calculated, the Correlation Factor is applied. If CF is not defined, the re-calculation fails. Exception 71 (No Correlation Factor. Unable to calculate volume) is generated. Once a valid CF exists, exception 71 will be resolved. ##### Correlation Factor (CF) Calculates new CFs for a record and does not alter the volumes or mass. This is frequently used where it is desired to keep EFM data unchanged but to utilize an analysis to calculate component volume, component mass and gas equivalent values. ##### Vol and Mass, Set CF = 1 For liquid meters only. This method allows the user to recalculate data using a correlation factor of 1.0, meaning the recalculation is directly off of the metered 'IV' or Mass quantity and process variable averages. This produces a ticket that your trading partner can verify via manual calculation.

For Liquid Quality

##### Vol and Mass, Use CF Where CFs are defined, source analysis will be applied and volumes and mass re-calculated using the correlation factors. When CFs are not defined, a CF of 1.0 will be used in the calculation of volume and mass. ##### Correlation Factor (CF) Source Analysis will be applied to any applicable meter analysis regardless of periodic data VCF status. If a current volume exists and a new volume can be calculated, VCF will be calculated. Typically when applying analysis you want to recalc volume.  Only choose VCF if you want the analysis applied for reporting purposes, but want to keep the volume from the meter.   If you choose to recalculate VCF, you have the option to also have energy recalculated based on the applied heating value. ##### Vol and Mass, Set CF = 1 For liquid meters only. This method allows the user to recalculate data using a correlation factor of 1.0, meaning the recalculation is directly off of the metered 'IV' or Mass quantity and process variable averages. This produces a ticket that your trading partner can verify via manual calculation.

docs.title: Volume Editor
docs.text:
Accessing the Volume Editor requires System Process – Meter Edit – Can View privileges. For additional details about Volume Editor access, see: Volume Editor Access Privileges.

Use the Volume Editor to view and edit flow data, meter characteristics, and meter analysis for meters. Meters can be selected by list, location, or close group. You can view the data on a batch, periodic, daily, or monthly basis.

To view meter data in the Volume Editor: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor**. 2. Select a meter, location, list, or close group. When a location, list or close group is selected, the meter number with focus is displayed in the title bar at the top left of the screen. 3. Select a data type (e.g., Flow Data). 4. Select the month and year for the data you want to view.

The following items are available on the Volume Editor screen:

Screen Menus

### Data - **Rollup Viewer Graph** – Graph time frame where data exists for the selected meter. - **Graphical Editor** – Edit periodic flow data. - **Graph UFM** – Graph changes in ultrasonic data before and after selected month. - **Run Validation** – Perform validations on the meter. - **Split Periodic** – Create a new or missing periodic record that starts at the top of the time period (15-minute, hour, day, month). You can specify a date to split the periodic record. No calculations occur at the time of split, but you can provide totals after the split. - **Export to Excel** – Export data for specific month to an excel spreadsheet. - **Recalc** – Recalculate data after changes are made. - **Save** – Save changes to data. - **Refresh** – Reload the meter, source, or location from the database. - **Locate** – Locate a subsequent record with specific criteria such as PPA pending or missing data. - **Goto** – Locate records with specific data such as missing data or alarms for a specific month. ### Report - **Standard Report** – Open the Reports screen with the meter pre-populated. - **Exports** – Export data for selected time frame. - **Test Report** – Open the TESTit Report Viewer for selected time frame. - **Prove Reports** – Open a PDF of the prove report for a record (liquid meters only). ### Set-Up - **Meter Editor** – Open the Meter Editor with the meter pre-populated. - **Source Analysis** – Open the Quality Source Editor with the assigned source pre-populated. - **Source Assignments** – Open the Quality Source Assignment Viewer with the meter number pre-populated. - **Close Dates** – Open the meter data Close Dates screen with the meter number pre-populated for all dates. - **Edit/PPA Approvals** – Open the PPA Approval Editor screen with the meter number pre-populated. - **PPA Editor** – Open the PPA Editor screen with the meter number pre-populated. - **Proving Adjustment** – Open the Liquid Prove Editor with the meter number pre-populated. ### Options - **Current Flow Data** – Display the most current revision of meter data. - **Original Flow Data** – Display imported data with no revisions. - **Cell Editing** – Edit flowing parameters (pressure, temperature, and indicated volume) for multiple records at a time. - **Row Editing** – Edit an entire data row for a single record or a span of time. - **Move selection after enter** - **Up/Down** – When selected, your cursor will move down when you press **Enter** when cell editing. - **Left/Right** – When selected, your cursor will move to the right when you press **Enter** when cell editing. ### View - **Grid Legend** – Open the tabular editor legend and display the overview of color codes and alarm state codes used in the Volume Editor. (See: [Grid Legend](Grid%20Legend.md)) - **Hide Grid Selection** – Enable or disable highlighted representation of a row or cell. - **Hide Virtual Batches** – Enable or disable virtual batches for which Mass and NSV are empty. This option is only available in Batch view, not in Periodic, Daily, or Monthly views.

Object Selector

- **System** - Contains a list of the FLOWCAL systems of which you are a member. - **Meter/Location/List/Close Group** - Displays the number of the selected object. If you select a list, location, or close group, the meter on display out of the meters contained in the selected object will be identified in the title bar. You will be able to navigate through and filter the set of meters using the options that display next to the Measurement Month selector. - **Show All** - Display all meters in the selected object. - **Skip Empty** - Skip all meters that do not contain data for the selected measurement month. - **Show Incomplete** - Toggle through meters that are missing data. If a single meter is selected, the most current month range will display. When opening a list, location, or close group, click the left and right arrows next to the date selector to explore available meters in the selected object. - **Name** – The name of the selected object.

Data Types

- **Flow Data** – View and edit flow data points for the meter, such as Differential Pressure, Static Pressure, Temperature, Volume, and Energy. - **Characteristic** – View and edit the characteristic information for the meter, such as Meter Type, Calc Method, Meter Direction, and Meter Class. - **Analysis** – View and edit analysis information for the meter, such as Mole %, Relative Density, Heating Value, and Viscosity. - **Equipment** – View and edit information for flow devices and transmitters. - **Components** – View and edit fluid parameters, such as Pulses, Observed Density, and Meter Temperature and Pressure (only available for liquid meters).

Measurement Month Selector

- **Month/Year** – Select the month and year for data you want to display. The measurement month is defined by the Contract Day and Contract Hour values specified for the meter. If the meter does not have a Contract Day and Contract Hour specified for the date range, the grid will use the contract day and hour specified for the system of the meter. - **Auto** – Check this option to automatically refresh the grid once a new selection has been made. If this option is not selected, click the **Open** button to refresh the grid when selecting a new object or measurement month. Settings for this option will be retained throughout your FLOWCAL session if the Volume Editor Auto Option is enabled in [User Preferences](../Settings%20Manager/User%20Settings/User%20Preferences.md). If the "Remember UI Filter Values" option is enabled (see: [User Preferences](../Settings%20Manager/User%20Settings/User%20Preferences.md)), the Volume Editor will retain the filter and date settings for the duration of the FLOWCAL session. The filter date settings for the last Volume Editor session to be closed are retained when multiple Volume Editors are opened. The filter settings will reset when you log out or close FLOWCAL.

Data Grids

Data Types Flow Data Characteristic Analysis Equipment Components* Tabs Batch* • • • - • Periodic • • • • • Daily • • • - • Monthly • - • - • Alternate Periodic‡ ° - - - - UFM Diagnostic‡ ° - - - - | | | |----|----| | \*Only supported for liquid meters | ‡Available for Flow Data depending on meter setup | For additional details, see: [Volume Editor Grid Tab Details](Batch%20Tab.md).

Product Filter

Filter the grid using the Product Name or Product Code drop-down options (only available for liquid meters). This feature is not enforced in the Characteristic - Periodic tab.

Details Screen

On any Volume Editor grid, a row represents the date span that begins at the Effective Date displayed in the first column. users can double-click a row to open the Detail screen that shows the details of various data types for the date span. ### Gas Meter Detail Detail screen opened from the Flow Data \> Periodic tab The GPA 2172 tab is supported only for gas meters. ### Liquid Meter Detail Detail screen opened from the Flow Data \> Batch tab The Components sub-tab is supported only for liquid meters. The Batch menu option and the Accounting sub-tab only display for Batch details (i.e., when the Detail form is opened from the Batch grids).

docs.title: Volume Editor
Event/Alarms Tab
docs.text:
Event and alarm records can be viewed on the Flow Data’s Detail Editor. Click the Event/Alarms tab and view all event and alarm records for the time frame.

To access the Event/Alarms tab: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor**. 2. Select a meter and time period. 3. Double-click a record. 4. Click the **Event/Alarms** tab.

Alarm States

The Alarm States column contains multiple sub-columns to indicate various alarm data. The first column displays differential pressure alarms and the second column for static pressure alarms. (See: [Grid Legend - Alarm States](../Grid%20Legend.md))

docs.title: Volume Editor
Exceptions Tab
docs.text:
Exceptions can be viewed on the Flow Data’s Detail Editor. The user will go to the Exceptions tab and view all applicable exceptions for the time frame.

To access the Exceptions tab: 1. Go to **Open** \> **Volume Editor**. 2. Select a meter and time period. 3. Double-click a record. 4. Click the **Exceptions** tab.

Screen Details

The following items are available on the Exceptions tab: - **Date** - Date of the record that the exception was generated for. - **Status** - A one or two character code indicating if the exception is Acknowledged(A), Pending (P), Resoluved by Late Data (RD), Resolved by User (RU) or Unresolved (U). Users can click on the funnel in the column header to filter which exception types are viewed. - **Category** - Whether exception was generated based on Flow Data, Characteristics, or Analysis. Users can click on the funnel in the column header to filter which exception categories are viewed. - **Number** - The exception number. - **Description** - The exception description

Editing Exceptions

When an edit of data is initiated from the Flow Data tab, the user can select the exceptions tab on the Detail Editor. Exceptions for the record are visible there. To edit an exception: 1. Click **Edit** at the top of the editor and then select one or more exceptions and click one of the three buttons at the bottom. 2. Once any changes are made, click **Apply**. 3. Enter an edit reason if needed.

docs.title: Measurement Glossary
docs.text:
• Absolute Pressure

    Atmospheric Pressure + Gauge Pressure

    • ACBI

      Automatically Created Batch Upon Import

      • AGA-7 Calculation Method

        American Gas Association method for calculating gas flow for a linear meter

        • Ambient Conditions

          The conditions (pressure, temperature, humidity, etc.) of the medium surrounding an object such as the case of a meter, instrument, transducer, etc.

          • Analysis Reports

            Analysis reports allow the user to identify analysis information that has been applied to a meter

            • AP0

              Atmospheric Pressure Zero

              • API Gravity

                A term used to express the relative density of petroleum liquids. API gravity is measured by a hydrometer instrument having a scale graduated in degrees API.

                • Application Process

                  The application process provides security options that affect all processes across the FLOWCAL application

                  • Atmospheric Pressure

                    The pressure exerted by the weight of the atmosphere at the meter’s location. At sea level, the pressure is approximately 14.7 psi (101 kpa), often referred to as 1 atmosphere

                    • Auto Rescan

                      Auto Rescan is a service that allows FLOWCAL check for missing data on meters and quality sources.

                      • Base Conditions

                        The conditions of temperature and pressure to which measured volumes are to be corrected. Defined in FLOWCAL as the system pressure and temperature base.

                        • Base Density

                          Determined from the density at flowing conditions by applying the density meter factor (DMF) to account for densitometer inaccuracies and then accounting for the temperature and pressure of the density measurement not being at base temperature and pressure

                          • Batch

                            Used in liquids only. Volume of liquid product pass through a meter over a period of time. Accumulations of records taken in either hourly, daily, 15 minute or possibly other data resolutions.

                            • Batch Meter

                              Used in liquids only. Batch meters represent meter measured product flow. It contains continuous records of a meter’s options.

                              • Batch Schedule

                                Set schedule for automatically creating batches for liquid meters that deliver batches on a known schedule

                                • Bill of Lading

                                  A document by which a carrier acknowledges having received in good order and condition (or the reverse) certain specified goods consigned to them by some particular shipper and binds them to deliver those good in similar condition to the consignees of the shippers.

                                  • Blow Down Ticket

                                    Blow down tickets serve to indicate the quantity of product lost by venting.

                                    • Business Month

                                      The business month is the first month after the last close. If the last month closed is April and the current date is June 10, the business month is May (last month after the close in April)

                                      • Capacity Table

                                        A table showing the capacities or volumes of a tank for various liquid levels measured from the reference gauge point; also known as a strapping table, tank capacity table or calibration table.

                                        • Cell Editing

                                          An option found in the Volume Editor that allows the user to edit more than one value for multiple records at a time in a spreadsheet-like format. This type of editing can only be done of flowing parameters (pressure, temperature, indicated volume, etc.).

                                          • CFX File

                                            A proprietary binary file format used to bring meter flow data and configuration information into FLOWCAL.

                                            • Close Group

                                              A date-effective group of meters that allows the user to close meters in bulk. Meters can only belong to one close group at a time.

                                              • Combined Correction Factor (CCF)

                                                Factor that can be multiplied against the indicated volume to get the Gross Standard Volume (GSV). This factor takes all factors that need to be applied to take the volume measurement at flowing conditions to get an accurate volume at base temperature and pressure.

                                                • Comparison Location

                                                  A location use to compare two measurement quantities (meters and/or locations).

                                                  • Compressibility

                                                    The ratio of actual volume of gas at a given temperature and pressure to the volume of gas when calculated by the ideal gas law.

                                                    • Compressor

                                                      a piece of equipment which helps transport product from one location to another by compressing the product entering the compressor and then discharging that product at a higher pressure. Discharging the pressurized product causes it to move down the pipeline.

                                                      • Consignee

                                                        Party (usually a seller) who delivers a consignment to a carrier for transporting to a consignee (usually a buyer) named in the transportation documents. Ownership (title) of goods remains with the consignor until the consignee pays for them in full.

                                                        • Contractual Limits

                                                          Regulatory requirements defined in a tariff and/or operational agreements, maintenance agreements, and standard operating procedures and include items such as test frequency and sample frequency.

                                                          • Correction for Pressure of the Liquid (CPL)

                                                            Factor calculated from the products calculation table. The correction to be applied to the indicated volume to correct from flowing pressure to base pressure.

                                                            • Correction for Sediment & Water (CSW)

                                                              Factor to account for part of the product being measured as sediment and water. CSW will be 1 for refined products such as propane and gasoline. CSW will be less than 1.0 for products such a crude oil.

                                                              • Correction for Temperature and Pressure of Liquid (CTPL)

                                                                Factor calculated based on the product’s calculation table or by multiplying CTL and CPL together. CTPL is the correction to be applied to the indicated volume to correct from flowing temperature and pressure to base temperature and pressure.

                                                                • Correction for Temperature of Liquid (CTL)

                                                                  Factor calculated based on product’s calculation table. The correction is applied to the indicated volume to correct from flowing temperature to the base temperature.

                                                                  • Corresponding States Liquid Density (COSTALD)

                                                                    COSTALD uses an equation of state to calculate density from composition.

                                                                    • Cricondentherm

                                                                      The highest temperature at any pressure at which hydrocarbons will condense out.

                                                                      • Current Period Adjustment

                                                                        Created on meter batches when a prove is entered in the Volume Editor prior to the month being closed

                                                                        • Datetime Effective

                                                                          Datetime effective records have a defined start date and time and a defined end date and time.

                                                                          • Density Meter Factor (DMF)

                                                                            Correction factor to take uncorrected density to a corrected observed density. The factor is calculated by using a pycnometer ball to calculate a fluid’s density and then dividing that density with the density reported by the online densitometer for the same measurement. This is also called pyc factor or densitometer factor.

                                                                            • Differential Pressure

                                                                              The drop in pressure measured across an orifice plate or a cone. The amount of pressure drop is used to calculate the volume of gas or liquid flowing through a pipe.

                                                                              • Dynamic List

                                                                                A list that is based on a query that the user creates. This list will automatically be built based on the query selected.

                                                                                • Edit Approval Limits

                                                                                  The maximum amount by which volume, energy, gross standard volume, or mass values can be changed through manual edits without requiring approval. Manual edits that exceed this limit will need to be approved before the edits are applied.

                                                                                  • Edit Limit

                                                                                    The maximum amount of change to volume, energy, GSV or mass that can be made by manual edits before edits require approval.

                                                                                    • Electronic Flow Measurement (EFM)

                                                                                      An electronic flow computer records the flowing parameters such as pressure, temperature and pulses and then calculates the volume.

                                                                                      • Equilibrium Vapor Pressure (EVP)

                                                                                        The pressure at a given temperature at which a fluid will transition from a liquid to a gas. Above the EVP the fluid is a liquid, below the EVP the fluid is a gas.

                                                                                        • Exception

                                                                                          A notification or flag created when suspect data for a meter, location or quality source is imported or added as an edit.

                                                                                          • Expert System

                                                                                            Functionality calculates Set Points and validates data based upon historical data using statistical analysis.

                                                                                            • GMS Date

                                                                                              The gas measurement system day on which a database record was created or last modified

                                                                                              • Inventory Location

                                                                                                Inventory locations, such as underground sotrage caverns, are used to track storage amounts. An initial amount is added to or subtracted from the inventory. The results can then be viewed and reported in FLOWCAL.

                                                                                                • Keep Whole

                                                                                                  Volume, energy, and mass for meters that are "kept whole" in the allocation process will not be adjusted to compensate for a surplus or deficit.

                                                                                                  • Products

                                                                                                    Types of fluid being measured, such as crude oil, natural gasoline, or propane

                                                                                                    • Sample ID

                                                                                                      The Sample ID is unique across all standalone samples in a FLOWCAL database. This is in contrast to liquid quality source samples, whose unique identification is the LQ number and sample date. The Sample ID can contain up to 25 characters and is required for all standalone samples.

                                                                                                      • SCADA

                                                                                                        Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition

                                                                                                        • Source

                                                                                                          The basis of gas or liquid quality analysis as defined by the user; a source could be a physical sample or online chromatograph; it is a representative sample either manually entered or imported into FLOWCAL and utilized to calculate volumes, mass, components, and gas equivalent values

                                                                                                          • TFX File

                                                                                                            A proprietary binary file format used to import volume and accounting information from run tickets and gauge tickets (pipelines, LACTs, trucks, rail cars, marine vessels, or tank tickets) into FLOWCAL.

                                                                                                            • Ticket

                                                                                                              A measurement of data at a single point in time. A ticket can have a start date and an end date, but FLOWCAL treats it as a single data point.

                                                                                                              • Useful Outlets/Inlets

                                                                                                                Useful outlets include sales stations, storage, and product flowing downstream. Non-useful outlets include fuel, flare, and blowdown.

                                                                                                                • WP0

                                                                                                                  Working Pressure Zero

docs.title: Deprecated as of 10.1.0.0
docs.text: The following items have been deprecated as of Version 10.1.0.0. If your company requires any of the following items, please contact Customer Support immediately.

docs.title: Location Rollups Viewers
docs.text:
With the release of the new Balance Explorer, the Daily Location Rollups, Monthly Location Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Balance Viewers will be removed.

Show Details

Reason

As part of our continued development of the new interface and user experience of FLOWCAL Enterprise, Flow-Cal is pleased to announce the launch of our new Balance Explorer. The Balance Explorer combines four key rollup viewers (Daily Location Rollups, Monthly Location Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Balance Viewers) into a single screen.

With the release of the new Balance Explorer, the Daily Location Rollups, Monthly Location Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Balance Viewers will be removed.

Replaced by Another Feature New Balance Explorer Items Affected The Daily Location Rollups, Monthly Location Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Balance Viewers. Installation Changes N/A Upgrade Changes N/A

docs.title: Location Close Approval from Exception Resolver
docs.text:
Selecting location exceptions now opens the Balance Explorer, at the request of the FLOWCAL user community.

Show Details

Reason Selecting a location exception in the Exception Resolver opens the Location Close Approval screen. With the launch of our new Balance Explorer, selecting location exceptions opens the Balance Explorer, at the request of the FLOWCAL user community. Replaced by Another Feature The Exception Resolver will now open the new Balance Explorer for location exceptions. Items Affected Selecting a location exception from the Exception Resolver will no longer open the Location Close Approval screen; however, the Location Close Approval screen can still be accessed from the main menu. Installation Changes N/A Upgrade Changes N/A

docs.title: All Lists Button in List Editor
docs.text:
This functionality is redundant to the List drop-down, so the button adds no value to the product.

Show Details

Reason

The All Lists button was designed to show all lists that exist in the application, regardless of a user's access privileges for the lists. The List drop-down already supports this functionality, so the button adds no value to the product.

Note that screens outside of the List Editor will continue to filter the drop-down to lists to which the logged in user has access.

Replaced by Another Feature No; the drop-down in the List Editor provides this functionality. Items Affected All Lists button in the List Editor Installation Changes N/A Upgrade Changes N/A

docs.title: Import Drivers
docs.text:
LQTicket.dll has been removed from the installer.

Show Details

Reason Custom import drivers are not included in the general install set. For this reason, LQTicket.dll has been removed from the installer. Replaced by Another Feature Yes, the FLOWCAL now supports a standard text file format for importing liquid data. Items Affected LQTicket.dll import driver Installation Changes Driver listed will not be present Upgrade Changes Customers must confirm if import driver is in use before upgrading. If your company is using this driver, please contact Flow-Cal Support.

docs.title: Reconcile and Final Columns
docs.text:
The custom Reconcile Volume option was previously removed from the FLOWCAL Configuration screen. The underlying functionality has now been removed as well.

Show Details

Reason This customer-specific feature was no longer supported in a previous version. This release included work to remove the underlying functionality. As part of this change, there are fields and columns that will no longer be available. Replaced by Another Feature No Items Affected

Reconciled and Final columns are no longer available on the following screens:

  • Volume Editor
  • Tabular Display Config
  • Ticket Editor
  • Ticket Search
Installation Changes N/A Upgrade Changes N/A

docs.title: Item Deprecation
docs.text: Deprecated for Current Release | Future Deprecation | Deprecation History

docs.title: Slated for Deprecation (TBD)
Time Trails Data Span
docs.text:
The Data Span indicates when an interval of time is recorded within the beginning and ending time stamps. This is defined at the meter level by setting the Data Span field within the meter’s characteristics. FLOWCAL currently supports Time Trails and Time Leads data for gas meters and only supports Time Leads for liquids meters.

Show Details

Reason Supporting both Time Leads and Time Trails data spans complicates the measurement process and the FLOWCAL application. The Time Leads data span is more prevalent than Time Trails, and FLOWCAL users find it intuitive and easy to use. Replaced by Another Feature In a future release (TBD), FLOWCAL will normalize Time Trails data to Time Leads data as a standard, ultimately moving to a Time Leads-only system for gas data to match what is currently in place for liquids data. Items Affected The field applies to the meter level; users set the Data Span field within the meter’s characteristics. Installation Changes N/A Upgrade Changes A FAB-8 working group invitation to discuss Time Trails deprecation will be forthcoming.

docs.title: Standard and System Values Labels
docs.text:
Secondary units will be renamed to "Alternate" units for both gas and liquids data. All fields that refer to either "System" units or "Standard" units will be renamed to "Alternate" units.

Show Details

Reason Currently, the terminology for the secondary set of units is inconsistent between liquids and gas data. For liquids, the secondary units are called "System" units. For gas, the secondary units are called "Standard" units. The secondary units need to be made consistent for liquids and gas data. Replaced by Another Feature "Standard" and "System" labels will be renamed to "Alternate". Items Affected Labels located throughout FLOWCAL, such as the Meter/Location Rollup Viewer. Installation Changes N/A Upgrade Changes N/A

docs.title: [ALL] Drop-Down Option
docs.text:
The [ALL] option will be removed from the object selector for all new screens.

Show details

Reason As new screens are introduced, the object selector will no longer include the [ALL] option in order to prevent users from unintentionally loading an excessive amount of data and reduce code complexity. Replaced by Another Feature No; however, users can create a list containing all objects such as meters, sources, or locations, to perform the same function. Items Affected Object selectors on all new screens Installation Changes N/A Upgrade Changes N/A

docs.title: New Feature Archive
Version 10.1.1.0
docs.text:
• Balance Explorer - The new Balance Explorer combines several legacy rollup viewers: Daily Location Rollups, Monthly Location Rollups, NGL Balance, and Recovery Analysis Viewer.
  • Transaction Queue for Liquids - The Transaction Queue service now includes functionality for liquids data in addition to gas data.
  • Density at Flowing Conditions (Liquid Sources) - The liquid source analysis import, editing, and apply processes have been enhanced to support liquid densities at sample conditions.

docs.title: Version 10.0.3.0
docs.text:
• Live Oil Management Add-on - The Live Oil Management form enables the ability to designate a liquid meter as a live oil meter. This form also allows dead oil and flash gas meters to be created and linked to a live oil meter.
  • New Location Volume Statement Reports - Four liquid versions of the Location Volume Statement report have been added that compile component composition, flow parameters and liquid quantities such as mass, GSV, NSV, and sediment and water for selected locations.

docs.title: Version 10.0.2.0
docs.text:
• Original Meter Factor Validation - Meter factor and K-factor validations compare a meter characteristic value to a specified baseline range.
  • PPA Thresholds - FLOWCAL now supports a set of minimum thresholds below which PPAs will be automatically rejected.
  • Location Validations - Location validations help ensure that values fall within specified set points.
  • Exception Resolver - The Exception Resolver now includes user settings, edit reason and note capabilities, and an object explorer view.

docs.title: Version 10.0.1.0
docs.text:
• New Exception Resolver - The Exception Resolver has been redesigned to align with FLOWCAL's updated UI standards and further our efforts to provide an optimal user experience.
  • Calculated Meter Enhancements - Functionality to support formulas is now available for calculated meters. This added flexibility allows users to define and expand arithmetic operators using conditional statements and defined criteria.
  • FMP Volume Tier, Heating Value Uncertainty (BLM Compliance Updates) - Calculation functionality is now available for FMP Volume Tier and Heating Value Uncertainty. These capabilities help users maintain compliance with current BLM regulations.

docs.title: Version 10.0.0.0
docs.text:
• Main Screen & Menu Structure - Our new interface has been designed and organized with the user in mind.
  • Customizable Dashboard - The FLOWCAL Dashboard contains several tools to improve the user experience.
  • Bureau of Land Management (BLM) - FLOWCAL 10 can help ensure compliance with BLM regulations.
