docs.title: Definitions of Symbols
Definitions of Symbols
docs.text:
The information in this section has been duplicated from Section 4.2 of the API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards; Chapter 12.2 Part 3; First Edition; October 1998. Additional symbols not defined in Ch.12.2 have been added from the API Manual of Petroleum Measurement Standards; Chapter 5.6; First Edition; October 2002 to define mass proving symbols.

A combination of upper and lower case notation is used for symbols and formulas in this publication. Subscripted notation is often difficult to use in word-processed documents and therefore has not been used in this publication. Upper case notation is usually preferred for computer programming and other documents as appropriate.

Symbols have been defined to aid in clarity and specificity of the mathematical treatments. For example:

  • CTL = Correction for Temperature on the Liquid
  • GSV = Gross Standard Volume
  • CPS = Correction for Pressure on Steel.

In many cases, the symbols are followed by additional letters to help clarify meaning and application. Examples include:

  • “m” refers to the meter (as in CTLm)
  • “p” refers to the meter prover (as in GSVp)
  • “b” refers to base conditions (as in RHOb)
  • “obs” refers to observed conditions (as in RHOobs)
  • “avg” refers to the average (mean) of the readings [as in Tp(avg)]

Note: Additional letters may be in use as well.

docs.title: Core Features Quiz
docs.text:
Test your understanding of meters, product setup, locations, tickets, and rollup viewers.

What does a FLOCON filter do in FLOWCAL?

Attaches to a meter and captures its raw measurement data Stores historical PPA approval records Creates users and groups for security Rolls up ticket data into monthly reports

Which characteristics primarily determine how a meter's raw data is converted to flow?

Contract hour and day Pressure base and temperature base Group privilege level Ticket number

When creating a meter, what two meter types can be chosen at creation?

Coriolis meter or turbine meter Gas meter or liquid meter Batch meter or periodic meter Enterprise meter or local meter

Where do a liquid meter's pressure base and temperature base values typically come from?

They must always be entered manually They default from the product selected for the meter They come from the ticket They come from the assigned group's privilege level

What distinguishes batch data entry from periodic (e.g. hourly) data entry?

Batch data arrives at irregular intervals rather than a fixed period Batch data only applies to gas meters Periodic data cannot be hourly Batch data requires PPA approval before entry

What is the name of FLOWCAL's default system?

Standard Enterprise Core Primary

Can multiple meters belong to the same FLOWCAL location?

No, only one meter per location is allowed Yes, a single location can contain multiple meters Only if they are the same meter type Only after PPA approval

How does a FLOWCAL ticket differ from a meter's flowing data?

A ticket represents a single point-in-time record rather than continuous data A ticket only exists for gas meters A ticket replaces the need for a location A ticket is generated automatically every hour like periodic data

Why must fields like product and temperature be selected manually when creating a new ticket?

Because tickets are periodic and copy prior values automatically Because there is no periodic record for the ticket to draw values from Because tickets do not support products Because manual import always overrides ticket fields

What does the Roll Up Viewer show for a FLOWCAL location?

User group privilege levels How the location's meter data aggregates, e.g. at minute, super, and monthly levels PPA approval history Manual import error logs

docs.title: FLOWCAL Flashcards
docs.text:
An organizational boundary in FLOWCAL. Systems contain the locations used to model operations. An operational place within a system. A location can have one or more meters. A physical device that measures product volume and provides data to FLOWCAL. A point-in-time record whose values are entered manually rather than read from continuous meter data. A check that evaluates incoming data. Failed data creates an exception that must be resolved. Post-processing approval used for changes to data that has already been closed. The aggregation of detailed data into higher-level results used for analysis and reporting.

Continue with the Getting Started Quiz or the Visual Data Journey.

docs.title: Getting Started Quiz
docs.text:
Test your understanding of the FLOWCAL data journey.

How is access to FLOWCAL controlled?

Every user shares a single admin account Users are assigned to groups that carry distinct privilege levels Access is granted purely by IP-address allowlisting Access is controlled per-ticket rather than per-user

What happens when incoming meter data fails validation in FLOWCAL?

It is silently discarded It closes on an exception that must be resolved It is automatically approved through PPA It is rolled up as-is into reports

What is required to make a change (e.g. an equation change) to an already-closed meter?

No approval is needed since the meter is already closed The change must go through PPA approval The meter must be deleted and recreated A new group must be created for the change

docs.title: Visual Story: The FLOWCAL Data Journey
docs.text:
Step 1 · Overview The FLOWCAL Data Journey

From securing access with users and groups, to creating a liquid meter and its location, through validation, exceptions, PPA approval, imports, and rollups into reports — this is the path data takes through FLOWCAL.

Coriolis Turbine FLOCON Filter Step 2 · Meters Meter Fundamentals

A meter is the physical device that measures product volume. A FLOCON filter captures its raw data, and characteristics like meter type, pressure base, and temperature base determine how that raw data becomes flow.

product density pressure base temperature base meter factor = 1 contract hour/day Step 3 · Volume Editor Liquid Meter & Product Setup

Choosing a product (e.g. a Table E product) auto-fills the meter's pressure base and temperature base, meter factor defaults to one, and the contract hour/day setting controls whether data is entered periodically or in batches.

Enterprise (System) ↓ Location ↓ Meter A Meter B Step 4 · Locations Locations & Systems

FLOWCAL's default system is called enterprise, and customers can add other systems as needed. Within a system, a single location can have multiple meters attached to it.

TimeProductTempVolumeType Hr 1---periodic 1 ptmanualmanualmanualticket Step 5 · Tickets Tickets Overview

Unlike a meter's continuous hourly data, a ticket captures a single point in time — so its product, temperature, and similar fields are entered manually rather than drawn from a periodic record.

Minute Super Monthly Step 6 · Rollup Viewers Rollup Viewer Basics

Once a location has meters attached, the Roll Up Viewer shows how its data aggregates — from minute-level detail up through super and monthly totals.
